This enables systematic building and evaluation of end-to-end scientific AI systems under leakage-resistant protocols.

entry.title: Stream Recursion Model (SRM)

author.name: Asael Sorensen, Charles Brock, David Chamberlain, Jennifer Minnich, Matthew Hoffman, Ramyaa Ramyaa

entry.summary: The Stream Recursion Model modifies the Hierarchical Reasoning Model to organize computation into multiple interacting latent streams updated by recursive refinement, designed for mechanistic interpretability at scale. The structure enables direct analysis of stream dynamics, causal contributions, and routing behavior while maintaining competitive performance.

entry.title: CataOPD: Catalytic On-Policy Distillation for Large Language Model Reasoning

author.name: Wenjin Liu, Chenxi Wang, Jiapu Wang, Zhe Cui, Anh Tuan Luu, Haoran Luo

entry.summary: CataOPD treats the teacher as a catalyst rather than a target for LLM reasoning improvement, combining reinforcement learning with on-policy distillation: Self-Rescue Routing first seeks correct trajectories through additional on-policy self-sampling and only uses teacher intervention when all-failed groups occur, with verified student trajectories internalized into a catalyst-free policy. This addresses the complementary failure modes of RL (no positive signal without correct samples) and OPD (limited by student's reachable trajectories). It is a thoughtful contribution to the fast-moving area of reasoning post-training.

entry.title: An Agnostic Sample Compression Scheme for Squared Loss of Near-Linear Size in the Fat-Shattering Dimension

author.name: Guangjian Zhang

entry.summary: Constructs an agnostic sample compression scheme for squared loss with size O(fat(F, c-alpha) * log^3(2/alpha)), independent of sample size, for arbitrary real-valued function classes with noisy labels. This resolves, in the positive, an open problem posed by Attias, Hanneke, Kontorovich, and Sadigurschi at ICML 2024. It establishes that near-linear compression in the fat-shattering dimension is achievable even under agnostic noise.

entry.title: Exact Bayes Regret and Asymptotic Optimality in High-Dimensional Gaussian Bandits

author.name: Prakhar Singhvi (Abstract Math Institute), Yi Zou (Abstract Math Institute), Abhishek Bhattacharjee (Abstract Math Institute)

entry.summary: This theory paper derives exact normalized regret curves for Thompson sampling, greedy posterior selection, and scaled-covariance policies in high-dimensional Gaussian linear bandits where the horizon is proportional to dimension. It establishes a policy-uniform lower bound identifying the limiting optimal policy and proves L1 convergence of realized regret. This provides rigorous optimality characterizations for Bayesian sequential decision-making.

entry.title: ELF-REG: Scaling Continuous Diffusion Language Models to Reasoning Tasks

author.name: Zeyu Michael Li, William Xingxu Chen, Bingshuo Qian, Jiayin Liu, Xiang Cheng

entry.summary: ELF-REG scales fully continuous diffusion language models to mathematical reasoning and code generation by aligning intermediate denoiser features with a frozen autoregressive teacher (REPA plus regularization), jointly denoising a global representation with the response. ELF-REG-L reaches 55.96 percent pass@1 on GSM8K with parallel decoding of all response tokens.

entry.title: Temporal Taxation Compounds Under Post-Training Compression of Whisper Models

author.name: Srishti Ginjala, Eric Fosler-Lussier, Christopher W. Myers, Srinivasan Parthasarathy

entry.summary: This paper audits how post-training compression (quantization, pruning, distillation) redistributes error burden across demographic groups in the Whisper speech recognition family. It finds that 50% Wanda pruning of Whisper-large-v3 more than doubles the word-error-rate gap between worst- and best-served groups on Fair-Speech, framing the effect as a compounding 'temporal taxation' cost for affected users.

entry.title: COILD: An Indic-Centric Parallel Corpus and Benchmark for Machine Translation Across Indian Languages

author.name: Kshetrimayum Boynao Singh, Nitin Kumar Mishra, Palash Pratim Dutta, Atai Waris Khan, Aparna Kaushik, Avinash Kumar, Deeksha, Deepak Kumar, Saroj Kumar Jha, Saloka Sengupta, Anansa Roy, Umalatha Kannoth, Saifulla Samar, Meena Sharma, Manpreet Kaur, Jyoti Sharma, Ashwini Vaidya, Muralikrishna SN, Md Shad Akhtar, Poonam Bansal, Amita Dev, Sanasam Ranbir Singh, Samit Bhattacharya, Tanmoy Chakraborty, Asif Ekbal

entry.summary: Introduces COILD, an Indic-centric parallel corpus of over 1.16 million human-translated and human-verified sentence pairs spanning 20 Indian language pairs across four language families, built from original Indian-language sources rather than English-pivot content. It addresses a major resource gap for Indian-language machine translation and provides an evaluation benchmark that better captures linguistic and cultural diversity.

entry.title: Free the Language Model From the Vision Encoder: Semantic Serialization as a Perception Interface for Small Language Models

author.name: Cong Xu, Ravi Sankar

entry.summary: The paper studies an embodied scene QA interface where visual perception never enters the language model: a frozen perception stack detects and ranges objects, a deterministic semantic serializer compiles the scene state into decision-aligned text, and an unmodified text-only LLM answers. On an occlusion-audited campus-robot benchmark this serialized interface outperforms a zero-shot VLM whose language model is comparably sized. The work challenges the end-to-end VLM assumption that perception must be coupled to the LLM.

entry.title: Only What Was Seen: Observation-Gram Compaction of View-Dependent Appearance in 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Krzysztof Pietroszek

entry.summary: The paper introduces an observation-Gram matrix per Gaussian, accumulated from viewing directions and blending weights, as an exact first-order map from spherical-harmonic coefficient changes to image error. This distortion metric enables closed-form degree reduction, rate-distortion-optimal degree allocation, and matrix-weighted vector quantization for 3DGS compression.

entry.title: PROVE: Proof-guided Regime-aware Operator Verification for Hallucination Detection in Medical Visual Question Answering

author.name: Keyang Zhou, Siyi Li, Zhongnan Shi, Qichao Ying, Wei Tang, Zhenxing Qian

entry.summary: PROVE is a black-box hallucination detector for medical VQA that adapts its verification strategy to the evidential structure of each question, classifying questions into three verification regimes instead of applying uniform reliability checks. This reduces both missed overconfident errors and false alarms from over-verification.

entry.title: BeyondRetarget: Learning Executable Humanoid Motions Directly from Monocular Video

author.name: Tianyu Xiong, Yi Lu, Jinrui Wang, Ziqi Liang, Dandan Lei, Xiaoyang Zhou, Xiao-xiao Long, Qiu Shen, Xun Cao

entry.summary: BeyondRetarget learns executable humanoid motions directly from monocular human video, bypassing the standard pipeline of first estimating a human motion representation and then retargeting it to the robot, which suffers from morphology and DoF mismatches and error propagation. It offers a scalable route for humanoids to acquire demonstration motions from human videos. This is significant for scaling humanoid robot training data.

entry.title: Online Sim-to-Real Adaptation via Closed-Loop System Modeling

author.name: Yuhao Huang, Samuel A. Moore, Boyuan Chen

entry.summary: OSRAM adapts the reference commands fed to an existing controller rather than retraining policies or identifying raw dynamics, treating the deployed robot plus its policy as one closed-loop dynamical system whose task-level command-response behavior is learned online. This corrects residual sim-to-real tracking errors with substantially less data and computation than policy retraining or simulation finetuning.

entry.title: OREN-X: Octree Residual Network for Real-Time Multi-Modal Mapping

author.name: Zhirui Dai, Qihao Qian, Dinh Minh Nguyen, Quan-Dung Pham, Kiana Bronder, Carlos Nieto-Granda, Yiyu Chen, Quan Nguyen, Nikolay Atanasov

entry.summary: OREN-X is an online mapping system that uses a single octree data structure to jointly store geometric, radiance, and vision-language features, instead of maintaining separate representations per modality. This unified multi-modal field supports planning, rendering, relocalization, and open-vocabulary grounding while reducing memory and compute cost. The approach targets long-horizon general-purpose robot autonomy.

entry.title: Robo-Harness K1: Harnessing Robot-Use Agents via Perception Augmentation

author.name: Zexi Li, Yehang Zhang, Wenqian Li, Haojian Huang, Chenxu Wang, Shiyuan Deng, Yangkai Wei, Tianyi Zhang, Binghui Xie, Bohan Zhou, Yifan Chang, Kaiwen Zhou, Ying-Cong Chen, James Cheng, Yinchuan Li

entry.summary: Robo-Harness K1 is a robot-use agent framework that exposes perception as tools: the VLM agent queries calibrated depth, persistent visual anchors, spatial measurements, and grasp hypotheses, then selects generic motions based on returned evidence. This gives agents access to 3D geometry without changing model architecture or training depth encoders, avoiding the demonstration burden of VLA models and the fragility of RGB-only VLM control. The interface makes foundation-model manipulation more reliable.

entry.title: Res-HIL: Human-Guided Residual Reinforcement Learning for Sample-Efficient Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Mariia Iavorskaia, Christian Dietz, Sebastian Albrecht, Majid Khadiv

entry.summary: Res-HIL is a human-in-the-loop residual reinforcement learning framework that learns corrective actions on top of a frozen imitation policy for dexterous manipulation. Each human intervention yields two learning signals: direct supervision of the residual policy and reward shaping of prior autonomous behavior. This addresses a key weakness of imitation learning, whose policies fail outside the demonstration distribution.

entry.title: Faster Visuomotor Policy Learning on Action Manifolds via Riemannian MeanFlow

author.name: S. Talha Bukhari, Austin Garrett, Yi Wei, Ruiqi Ni, Zachary Kingston, Aniket Bera

entry.summary: This paper introduces the Riemannian MeanFlow Policy (RMFP), a visuomotor policy learning method that combines flow-matching-style multimodal action generation with one-step (few-step) sampling to avoid costly multi-step numerical integration during robot control. It explicitly accounts for the intrinsic geometry of robot action spaces by learning the flow map on the smooth manifold on which action sequences are defined. The result targets fast control rates needed for real-time robotic manipulation.

entry.title: Five frontier LLMs fact-checked the same 1,000 claims. They disagree on 63% of them.

author.name: David Yordanov

entry.summary: An empirical study giving five frontier LLMs the same 1,000 recent user-submitted claims to fact-check on a five-point verdict scale, finding disagreement on 63% of the 997 claims with usable verdicts and large (2+ category) divergences on 23%. High self-reported confidence (9-10 in 76% of answers) did not predict cross-model agreement, challenging the assumption that frontier models are interchangeable verifiers.

entry.title: Estimating suicide risk from text

author.name: Jennifer Michalowski | McGovern Institute for Brain Research

entry.summary: MIT McGovern Institute researchers developed a language-processing tool using a custom lexicon of words and phrases mapped to 49 suicide risk factors, which accurately predicts suicide risk from crisis-counselor text conversations according to a paper in the Journal of Psychopathology and Clinical Science. The tool is already clarifying which risk factors matter most during crises and could support clinical and crisis-line triage with further validation.

entry.title: DEEPO: Dual-Entropy Enhanced Policy Optimization for Hallucination in MLLMs

author.name: Yingxuan Zhuang, Miao Pan, Wangjie Gan, Jingxiao Yang, Fan Wang, Weiming Liu, Cheng Tan, Xuhong Zhang, Jintao Chen

entry.summary: DEEPO diagnoses two failure points in the correction chain of RL for multimodal LLMs: hard queries with high semantic entropy collapse group-relative advantages to zero, and confident-but-wrong tokens become gradient-invisible as distributions sharpen. The proposed Dual-Entropy Enhanced Policy Optimization targets both, injecting updates exactly where hallucination risk is highest. The gradient-vanishing analysis of overconfident wrong tokens is a particularly sharp insight.

entry.title: Advancing Model Research in AgentX: Long-Horizon Autonomy for Industrial Recommender Systems

author.name: Shuang Yang, Zijie Zhuang, Changxin Lao, Pengbo Xu, Hanwen Xu, Yusheng Huang, Han Gao, Guanchen Wang, Tianbao Ma, Linxun Chen, Peilin Song, Xuming Wang, Chen Li, Fan Wu, Tao Wang, Zibo Zhao, Xiangyu Wu, An Liu, Fei Pan, Peng Jiang, Chen Yang, Zhaojie Liu, Wenwu Ou

entry.summary: Presents AgentX-Model, a dual-agent framework for industrial recommendation research in which a Research Agent develops independently reviewed proposals from papers and experiments while a Model Agent conducts multi-round code-level investigations, feeding results back to select implementations and next experiments. It targets sustained autonomous model research at Kuaishou scale.

entry.title: PrivDrift: Auditing User-Secret Leakage Under Topic Drift in Active LLM Conversations

author.name: Luciano Maldonado

entry.summary: Introduces PrivDrift, a benchmark of 1,000 controlled multi-turn dialogues with seeded secrets, content-dense topic drift, and standardized extraction probes, auditing whether user-disclosed secrets remain recoverable in later prompts across three LLMs with extended context windows. Hybrid dialogue-level leakage remains substantial after topic shifts.

entry.title: A Living Benchmark for Information Retrieval from Electronic Health Records

author.name: Jordan L. Cahoon, Chloe O. Stanwyck, Sulaiman Somani, Philip Chung, Kevin R Keet, Kameron C. Black, Andrea T. Fisher, Sarita Khemani, Jerry Liu, Stephen Ma, Saloni K. Maharaj, Rita M. Pandya, Eduardo Perez-Guerrero, Priyanka Pillai, Lisa Shieh, David J. H. Wu, James Xie, James C. McAvoy, Teresa Nguyen, Jessica Tran, Lucy Yin, Bridget Lin, Alison Callahan, Jason A. Fries, Nigam H. Shah, Emily Alsentzer

entry.summary: The paper presents a scalable framework that automatically generates QA pairs from longitudinal EHR notes, validated by nineteen clinicians, yielding BRIE, a continuously maintainable benchmark for clinical information retrieval. Evaluation across nine LLMs and five inference strategies shows headroom remains for state-of-the-art models.

entry.title: PROOF: Profiling Reliability of Object-Level Facts in Large Language Models

author.name: Andrei Chetvergov, Mikhail Solovev, Timofei Sivoraksha, Stepan Ukolov, Valeriia Kuschenko, Alexander Evseev, Sergey Bolovtsov

entry.summary: Introduces PROOF, a profile-oriented factuality benchmark built from a frozen Wikidata snapshot into 18,486 multiple-choice questions with explicit I-don't-know options, no-correct-option traps, and nine controlled formulations per question, evaluated over 166,374 prompts per model deployment across 18 open-weight models. It moves beyond aggregate factuality scores to expose which relations models confuse and how answers survive decoding perturbations.

entry.title: Let Training Guide Selection: Online Synthetic Data Filtering via Real-Anchored Utility

author.name: Yanran Wu, Sana Lakdawala, Renzo Tassara Miller, Chongyang Bai, Sharath Ciddu, Shivendra Pratap Singh, Kungang Li, Sandeep Pandey, Chunwei Liu

entry.summary: Proposes FROST, an online framework that estimates the utility of synthetic training data through gradient feedback anchored in real data, calibrating batch utility against recent history to decide when filtering is needed and filtering only out-of-band batches, with no external verifier or held-out validation set. Experiments on image classification and LLM fine-tuning for text-to-SQL show it filters roughly 2x... more effectively than alternatives. It directly addresses the noise and distribution mismatch problem that limits synthetic data value.

entry.title: On the SoS Certifiability of Log-Concave Distributions

author.name: Aleksandr Storozhenko

entry.summary: Proves that for any isotropic log-concave distribution, a polynomial moment expression is a sum of squares for every even moment order, removing the dependence on the Poincare constant in a prior theorem of Kothari and Steinhardt and recovering optimal moment bounds. As a corollary it yields computationally efficient algorithms with dimension-free error guarantees for a broad range of high-dimensional statistical estimation problems. The proof uses stochastic localization to decompose the distribution into strongly log-concave components.

entry.title: JEV vs. LLMs as Rubric Judges: Cheaper, Faster, and Wrong in the Same Places

author.name: Delip Rao, Chris Callison-Burch

entry.summary: The paper evaluates whether Jev, a typed classifier returning probabilities over permitted answers without text generation, can replace LLM rubric judges across nine panels from seven benchmarks. Jev matches flash-tier LLM judges in most comparisons while costing 29-325 times less and running 30-220 times faster, and all judges share similar error patterns on graded criteria. This suggests lightweight classifiers could replace expensive LLM-as-judge pipelines in many settings.

entry.title: Looks the Same, Answers Differently: Flip-Direction Steering for Robust Vision-Language Reasoning

author.name: Yeonsung Jung, Joonhyun Jeong, Hoang Pham, Joowon Kim, Yoonsik Park, Viet Dac Lai, Eunho Yang

entry.summary: The paper documents answer flips — VLM reasoning that changes under imperceptible image perturbations as activation shifts accumulate across decoding steps — and proposes FlipDir, a training-free inference-time steering method. It estimates a low-rank flip-inducing activation subspace from contrastive pairs and steers hidden states during decoding with a margin-based gate. This improves robustness of visual reasoning without retraining.

entry.title: A Multimodal Dataset for Survival Prediction in Resected Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma

author.name: Anh-Tien Nguyen, Mawuko Tettey, Jacqueline Michelle Metsch, Teresa Zimmer, Niklas Ullrich, Mario Duker, Sandra Rungeling, Kirsten Reuter-Jessen, Tessa Rosenthal, Lena-Christin Conradi, Michael Ghadimi, Alexander Konig, Elisabeth Hessmann, Volker Ellenrieder, Philipp Strobel, Hanibal Bohnenberger, Anne-Christin Hauschild

entry.summary: This paper releases a retrospective cohort of 302 PDAC resection patients with 446 H&E whole-slide images, clinicopathological variables, targeted sequencing for 154 patients, and long-term survival outcomes (median follow-up 76 months). Benchmark experiments across fourteen survival-prediction configurations establish reference baselines.

entry.title: Know Your Body: A Harness for Direct and Self-Improving Robot Control with VLMs

author.name: Zeyu Lou, Yanhong Zeng, Yong Wang, Chenyang Si

entry.summary: KnowBody is a harness that makes action-relevant robot body relations explicit, queryable, and revisable for frozen-weight VLMs, initialized from one off-task trajectory and refined as new evidence arrives, with knowledge rechecked when body estimates are revised. Across 32 fixed-budget trials on four real-robot tasks it achieves 75 percent completion versus 25 percent for the native harness. It shows large gains from explicit embodied self-models without fine-tuning.

entry.title: ActGaze: Learning Action-Grounded Gaze through Counterfactual Visual Interventions for High-Precision Manipulation

author.name: Jinxuan Zhu, Jiaheng Wang, Chao Tang, Mengfan Wang, Hao Wei, Shengbao Li, Hong Yin, Yiwen Gao, Chenrui Tie, Tingguang Li

entry.summary: ActGaze improves high-precision VLA manipulation by focusing visual attention on task-relevant regions, deriving gaze supervision from the policy's own action objective via counterfactual visual interventions rather than external gaze labels. Real-robot experiments across four high-precision tasks demonstrate the approach.

entry.title: a recurrent llm is quite easy to interpret but complex to steer

author.name: nesiacel

entry.summary: Original mechanistic interpretability experiments on the recurrent Ouro-1.4b-thinking model, showing that standard tools (logit lenses, linear probes) apply broadly across loops, but Contrastive Activation Addition steering only works well when applied to the final loop, with the model apparently cleaning injected foreign concepts out of the residual stream before the last loop. The author flags possible safety implications for steering recurrent architectures.

entry.title: Sharp Limits for Honest Uncertainty in Hard-Budget Repeated Evaluation

author.name: Yezhou Cheng, Runjia Du, Zeming Liu, Qibai Chen, Hang Lyu, Yilan Wei, Yankai Zeng, Bojun Lin

entry.summary: This theory paper characterizes how many repeated evaluations are needed to certify narrow uncertainty bounds on benchmarks under a hard response budget, deriving optimal worst-case interval widths of order inverse-square-root in tasks and repeats, with and without task omission. It proves lower bounds covering adaptive policies and shows fixed random-subset designs attain the rates via disagreement certificates.

entry.title: SWE-Prometheus: Measuring Engineering Governance Improvements in Real-World Repositories

author.name: Jiajun Wu, Leixin Sun, Zihan Tan, Yitao Liu, Shuo Li, Jiaru Qian, Shanghaoran Quan, Chuangxin Zhao, Yangxu Liao, Yang Liu, Bin Chong, Guancheng Wan

entry.summary: SWE-Prometheus is a benchmark that evaluates coding agents on the broader task of improving repository engineering governance rather than just fixing pre-identified issues. Tasks provide a repository snapshot and an open-ended objective, requiring agents to identify risks, prioritize interventions, and verify changes across six governance dimensions, using paired evidence, clean-environment probes, behavior gates, and two independent teacher ratings. It covers 60 real-world repositories.

entry.title: Fair Like Us? Auditing LLM Alignment in Resource Allocation

author.name: Qishen Han, Hadi Hosseini, Joshua Kavner, Samarth Khanna, Sujoy Sikdar, Lirong Xia

entry.summary: The paper introduces a general method for evaluating fairness reasoning in LLMs, comparing first-person fairness judgments across a broad set of models against human responses on matched scenarios and elicitation conditions in resource-allocation problems. It finds LLMs tend to prefer certain distributional patterns and may violate key normative principles from formal fairness theories. The work connects LLM alignment with the distributive justice literature.

entry.title: ENDOPROMPT: Victim-Side Pseudo-References for Utility Degradation

author.name: Qingyu Wu, Zeyu Feng, Yongda Yu, Yuzhe Luo, Hua Cheng

entry.summary: Introduces ENDOPROMPT, a white-box attack that learns utility-degrading prompt prefixes from unlabeled instructions, using clean victim continuations as pseudo-references and local search plus preference fitting to distill a generator that produces one damaging prefix per request. It is evaluated across four instruction-tuned models and multiple benchmarks.

entry.title: Persistent Billable State: Denial-of-Wallet Attacks and Defenses in Tool-Calling LLM Agents

author.name: Jinqian Zhang (Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences, School of Cyber Security, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences), Haojun Xia (Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences, School of Cyber Security, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences), Shujiang Wu (Beihang University), Jingkun Yue (State Key Laboratory of Networking and Switching Technology, Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, Beijing, China), Xia Zhang (Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences, School of Cyber Security, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences), Zhangpei Cheng (Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences, School of Cyber Security, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences), Bibo Tu (Institute of Information Engineering, Chinese Academy of Sciences, School of Cyber Security, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences)

entry.summary: The paper identifies persistent billable state: when an agent runtime carries an external tool return into later model inputs, providers meter that content again, letting a malicious tool convert untrusted data into recurring victim-billed processing without credentials or local privilege. It formalizes this boundary, derives six denial-of-wallet attack vectors, and builds DOW-BENCH evaluated across six model families with defenses.

entry.title: Policy Complexity, Reaction Time, and Bounded Rationality in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: James Wu, Chris R. Sims

entry.summary: Derives MI-SARSA, an on-policy temporal-difference algorithm with mutual-information regularization that explicitly penalizes policy complexity, modeling resource-rational constraints like limited working memory. This produces a learning model in which state information is used selectively, matching reaction-time phenomena observed in biological agents.

entry.title: M$^2$PFN: End-to-End Disentangled Alignment for Generalizable Multimodal In-Context Learning in Alzheimer's Disease

author.name: Lujia Zhong, Shuo Huang, Jianwei Zhang, Xinyu Nie, Yonggang Shi

entry.summary: Extends the tabular foundation model TabPFN's in-context learning to multimodal Alzheimer's diagnosis by making TabPFN's transformer differentiable end-to-end and aligning image-derived features with its synthetic tabular priors. The framework targets cross-cohort generalization, a persistent weakness of imaging-plus-tabular diagnostic models.

entry.title: Less is More: Encoder-only Audio-Visual Segmentation

author.name: Ilpo Viertola, Vladimir Iashin, Sophie T\"otterstr\"om, Esa Rahtu

entry.summary: EASE strips decoder components from Transformer-based audio-visual segmentation models, showing an encoder-only design achieves state-of-the-art AVSS at up to 365 FPS, roughly 3x faster than prior models, training in under 11 GPU-hours. This demonstrates that audio-visual segmentation can be simpler and far more efficient than inherited image-segmentation designs.

entry.title: Deep learning of longitudinal visual fields predicts glaucoma progression rate and identifies fast progressors

author.name: Taiabur Rahman, Siddiqur Rahman, Muhammad Moniruzzaman, Ummay Kawsar, Sayedatunnessa Ratna, Shadman Siddique, Rafsan Siddique, Tausif Ahmad, Tahsin Ahmad, Golam Rabbani

entry.summary: GLAM is a deep learning model that ingests longitudinal Humphrey 24-2 visual field sequences with clinical features to predict glaucoma MD and VFI progression rates far earlier than the 6-10 tests over years required by standard regression. On 4,276 patient-eyes from an open-access dataset it achieves strong MD-rate prediction with aleatoric uncertainty, enabling earlier identification of fast progressors at risk of irreversible blindness.

entry.title: Who Put the I in AI? Provenance and the Admissibility of Machine Self-Report

author.name: Kristina \v{S}ekrst

entry.summary: Examines when LLM statements about their own minds can be treated as evidence, tracing the provenance of self-descriptions end to end across Pythia and OLMo 2 pretraining checkpoints and post-training stages. The paper shows that contradictory self-descriptions stem largely from question phrasing and situates machine self-report within an evidentiary framework.

entry.title: Understanding and Exploiting Initialization Anchoring Weakness in Feedback-Based Agent Planning

author.name: Chuanchao Zang, Jianing Wang, Wenyu Chen, Xiangtao Meng, Li Wang, Xinyu Gao, Peng Zhan, Zheng Li, Shanqing Guo

entry.summary: A round-wise analysis of four feedback-based agent planning mechanisms reveals an initialization anchoring weakness: the first feedback round corrects 46% of adversarial plan directions, but correction rates drop to 13% and 7% in subsequent rounds. The authors attribute this to plausible initial shifts, insufficient counterevidence, and persistence of accepted directions in accumulated trajectories, and propose a mitigation.

entry.title: Beyond Average Safety: Chance-Constrained LLM Fine-tuning

author.name: Taha Entesari, Mahyar Fazlyab

entry.summary: This work proposes a chance-constrained formulation for safety-preserving LLM fine-tuning that bounds the fraction of safety-critical prompts whose performance degrades beyond a threshold relative to a reference model, rather than controlling only average safety loss. The authors derive a differentiable majorization of the discontinuous violation indicator to make the constraint tractable, avoiding obscured rare but severe safety regressions. This addresses a genuine gap in how safety is measured during fine-tuning.

entry.title: World Action Agent: Harnessing VLMs for Robot Manipulation via World Action Rehearsal

author.name: Yehang Zhang, Haojian Huang, Yifan Chang, Jianchong Su, Bohan Zhou, Yingjie Xu, Wosong Chen, Tianhao Zhou, Chenxu Wang, Tianyi Zhang, Yangkai Wei, Wenqian Li, Shiyuan Deng, Yinchuan Li, Ying-Cong Chen, Zexi Li

entry.summary: World Action Agent is a multi-agent harness that lets vision-language models directly pilot robots within a visual action workspace, featuring automatically selected contact views and an action rehearsal mechanism where each action becomes an editable proposal previewed and revised against planning feedback, optionally via an Imagination Agent. This differs from prior systems that use VLMs only indirectly to predict constraints or write programs. The work represents a notable step in general-purpose VLM-driven robot manipulation.

entry.title: Accelerating Video Diffusion via Training-Free Trajectory Routing

author.name: Mustafa Munir, Huy Vu, Shreyas Misra, Rohit Jena, Sajad Norouzi, Ali Taghibakhshi, Anis Ahmad, Anjul Patney, Pavlo Molchanov, Nima Tajbakhsh

entry.summary: TRACK is a training-free heterogeneous denoising strategy for video diffusion that switches between compatible large and small models at selected steps, with switching determined by a calibration rollout comparing the small model's predictions against the large model's reference trajectory. This reduces average cost per denoising evaluation even under step distillation, where each remaining step is still expensive. The approach offers a practical, plug-in efficiency gain for video generation.

entry.title: RLVR landscapes for iterated multiplications can be benign: Insights from spin-glass theory

author.name: Noa Rubin, Zohar Ringel

entry.summary: The paper maps entropy-regularized RLVR over tabular policies onto an energy-based spin-glass model over deterministic policies, providing an upper bound and rigorous characterization of the optimization landscape for algorithmic tasks like iterated group and quasigroup multiplication. It shows theoretically and experimentally that for tasks with uncorrelated inputs the landscape is benign, with no trapping local minima.

entry.title: Downside-Controlled Online Forecast Combination under Delayed and Revised Outcomes

author.name: Minkyoung Kim, Hyunjung Byun, Yohan Lee, Beakcheol Jang

entry.summary: The paper proposes combining a frozen forecaster (e.g., a foundation model) with static and online correctors on the simplex, using only losses that mature after the horizon, to provide downside control: never much worse than the starting forecast. Across seven benchmarks and four base models, worst-case deterioration is 0.15% while gains reach 11.5%, and on European day-ahead load forecasting it lowers MSE in all seven zones where single correctors can raise MSE by up to 102%.

entry.title: ICE: Task-Aligned Clifford Latent Fields for Multimodal Graph Foundation Models

author.name: Xunkai Li, Xu Wang, Yinlin Zhu, Xiong Yongfu, Yi Liu, Rong-Hua Li, Guoren Wang

entry.summary: ICE (Interaction-aware Clifford Encoder) is a multimodal graph foundation model that uses Clifford algebra latent fields rather than fused Euclidean vectors, preserving entity semantics, neighborhood interaction state, and task-specific geometry across graphs combining entities, images, language, and relations. The paper motivates the design with an empirical study showing these requirements are inseparable. This is a notable step toward geometrically grounded multimodal graph foundation models.

entry.title: Bandit Multiclass PAC Learning: Corrected Lower Bounds, Exact Families, and a Confidence Direct-Sum Phenomenon

author.name: Guangjian Zhang

entry.summary: Corrects a published lower bound in realizable multiclass PAC learning with bandit feedback, exhibiting explicit classes with BDS dimension K-1 whose sample complexity is exponentially smaller and locating two gaps in the original proof, then repairs the theorem. It also identifies a new confidence direct-sum phenomenon. Correcting foundational learning-theoretic results matters for the field's understanding of optimal bandit sample complexity.

entry.title: HClimRep-Ocean: A Global Ocean Emulator on an Unstructured Mesh

author.name: Kacper Nowak, Aleksei Koldunov, Nikolay Koldunov, Savvas Melidonis, Ankit Patnala, Simon Grasse, Julius Polz, Christian Lessig, Martin Schultz, Thomas Jung

entry.summary: The paper presents HClimRep-Ocean, a machine-learning emulator for global ocean dynamics operating on unstructured meshes, addressing challenges that distinguish ocean modeling from its more mature atmospheric counterparts: mesoscale eddies at much smaller spatial scales, complex coastlines, narrow straits, and ice-covered boundaries. By working natively on unstructured meshes rather than regular grids, it targets a central gap in ML-based earth system modeling. This extends the rapid progress seen in ML weather forecasting toward ocean simulation.

entry.title: Exploiting answer-invariant redundancies in satellite imagery for efficient VLM inference on edge

author.name: Ishani Janveja, Davis Zhang, Seoyul Oh, Deepak Vasisht

entry.summary: The paper identifies answer-invariant token redundancy in satellite imagery and presents Rift, a two-stage system combining query-conditioned tile pruning with elastic prefill for onboard VLM inference. On LLaVA-1.5 7B running on Jetson AGX Orin it cuts energy by 78 percent and latency by 69 percent while raising accuracy from 45 to 73 percent.

entry.title: GridSFM: A Foundation Model for Solving AC Optimal Power Flow

author.name: Luke Bhan, Weiwei Yang, Margaret Capetz, Baosen Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces GridSFM, a 15-million-parameter physics-inspired graph neural network pretrained across 54 grid topologies of 500 to 4,000 buses, achieving 2.45% zero-shot generation-cost error on a held-out 10,000-bus case with no degradation as system size grows. Physics-informed fine-tuning based on Newton's method adapts the model to unseen grids up to 10,000 buses with only 100 solved instances, outperforming single-topology dedicated models.

entry.title: Likelihood Ranking doesn't Scale Like Prompting in LLMs

author.name: Alessandro Bondielli, Lucia Passaro, Davide Bacciu, Alessandro Lenci

entry.summary: Across 95 decoder-only LLMs (0.1B to 104B parameters) and 10 MCQA datasets, the authors show that likelihood ranking of declarative statements diverges systematically from prompted answering, with statement-likelihood accuracy scaling differently with model size. This challenges the assumption that likelihood-based and prompting-based evaluations probe the same capabilities.

entry.title: EnSiTa - A Trilingual Multi-Domain Parallel Dataset and Benchmark for Domain-Specific Machine Translation

author.name: Surangika Ranathunga, Nisansa de Silva, Aloka Fernando, Kavindu Warnakulasuriya, Isuru Wijesiri, Menan Velayuthan, Charitha Rathnayaka, Thivaharan Varatharajan, Sajeevi Silva, Piumi Kandanaarachchi, Uthayasanker Thayasivam

entry.summary: EnSiTa provides a trilingual multi-domain parallel dataset and benchmark for English, Sinhala, and Tamil, with human post-edited training data across seven domains and professionally translated test sets produced under multi-year quality control. The authors benchmark domain-specific MT across all six language directions using a from-scratch Transformer, NLLB-600M, and decoder-only LLMs. It is a significant resource contribution for low-resource language MT research.

entry.title: Reward-Tilted On-Policy Distillation for Acoustic Grounding in Audio-Language Models

author.name: Kaiyang Li, Shaobo Han, Yue Tian, Shihao Ji

entry.summary: The paper proposes RT-OPD, a variant of on-policy distillation that combats textual shortcuts in audio-language models by measuring how much a frozen teacher's next-token predictions change when audio input is added. This log-probability contrast defines a reward that reshapes the teacher distribution for reverse-KL distillation, emphasizing acoustic evidence. Experiments across two benchmarks show improved audio grounding in compact ALMs.

entry.title: Direction-Scale Decomposition in Action Representation: Rethinking What to Tokenize for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Yufei Duan, Hang Yin, Alberta Longhini, Chao Tang, Danica Kragic

entry.summary: The paper proposes Direction-Scale Decomposition (DSD), an action representation for discrete-token vision-language-action models that splits translation and rotation increments into direction and scale components before tokenization. This isolates motion direction from execution-speed sensitivity and dataset-specific normalization, evaluated with uniform binning and a B-spline-based BEAST tokenizer in simulation and real-world manipulation. DSD reveals geometric structure shared across demonstrations.

entry.title: AV-GRPO: Modality-Anchored Decoupling Diffusion Reinforcement Learning for Joint Audio-Video Generation

author.name: Zhiyu Xu, Weilong Yan, Yufei Shi, Shiyang Li, Yihao Liu, Kin-Man Lam, Yuewen Cao

entry.summary: AV-GRPO is a modality-anchored online diffusion RL framework for joint audio-video generation that decouples heterogeneous multimodal rewards to ease credit assignment and handles divergent modality dynamics in the two modality towers. It also introduces 5DAV to address synchronization reward comparability across paired samples.

entry.title: SplatLabel: Pseudo-Labelling through 4D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Nitya Nanvani, Andras Palffy, Holger Caesar

entry.summary: SplatLabel uses a 4D Gaussian representation with an explicit temporal manifold tracking trajectories and lifespans of 3D primitives to generate LiDAR semantic pseudo-labels with confidence and occupancy grids at arbitrary voxel resolutions. It handles dynamic environments without pre-annotated data or complex multi-model ensembles.

entry.title: OmniFabric: Coherent UV Space Texture Synthesis for 3D Garment Reconstruction

author.name: Ding-Jiun Huang, Yuanhao Wang, Cheng Zhang, Hugo Bertiche, Alexandru-Eugen Ichim, Thabo Beeler, Fernando De la Torre

entry.summary: OmniFabric synthesizes globally coherent texture maps directly in 2D sewing-pattern space from a single image, avoiding baked-in illumination and shadows so garments are usable for physical simulation and relighting. It combines an estimated 3D mesh with generative priors for production-ready 3D garment assets. This matters because texture synthesis is the main bottleneck in automated garment asset creation for digital content and fashion pipelines.

entry.title: Streaming-WAM: Action-Conditioned World-Action Model for Asynchronous Robot Manipulation

author.name: Xuyao Huang, Yixuan Wang, Zengyao Ye, Boyuan Zhao, Chenyang Yu, Haoran Wen, Zhijie Deng

entry.summary: Streaming-WAM couples action-conditioned world modeling with asynchronous robot control: at each streaming update, future visual prediction is conditioned on the latest observation plus committed actions that form the fixed prefix of the next action chunk. This lets the world model account for actions already in execution, reducing generation latency while keeping predictions consistent with scheduled motion.

entry.title: AdaHVLA: Adaptive Harnesses for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Execution

author.name: Junyi Tang, Jie Peng, Zezhen Ding, Yuan Shen, Tianlong Chen

entry.summary: AdaHVLA combines VLA models, which provide strong local control, with task harnesses that retain task history and track progress for long-horizon execution. The system adaptively refines code-based coordination policies from robot experience using a decoupled multiagent process that separates evidence analysis, harness revision, and behavioral assessment. Testable coordination hypotheses guide revisions, improving alignment between agent reasoning and VLA execution.

entry.title: Real-Time Force Regulation for Whole-Hand Dexterous Grasping

author.name: Sang Min Kim, Alexander Alexiev, Tzu-Yuan Lin, Sangbae Kim, Young Min Kim, Yonghyeon Lee

entry.summary: The paper presents a framework for real-time regulation of contact forces across dynamically changing whole-hand contacts during dexterous grasping. It estimates contacts on all hand links geometrically from a tracked object model and proprioception, without tactile sensing, and repeatedly recomputes desired force distributions under friction, actuator, and actuation-consistency constraints. This improves robustness of grasps against object motion and disturbances.

entry.title: Forecast-Dojo: Replayable Environments for Benchmarking and Training LLM Forecasting Agents

author.name: Liqin Ye, Haorui Wang, Fardin Ahmed, Rongzhi Zhang, Yuan He, Ziyuan Lin, Yanbin Yin, Jing Peng, Michael Galarnyk, Sudheer Chava, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: Forecast-Dojo is a replayable environment combining 1,568 resolved Polymarket events with 18.8M dated news articles, letting forecasting agents research events at successive historical dates and receive outcome-based feedback without waiting for resolution. Evaluating 12 models shows research tools lower Brier scores for all of them, with forecasts improving as dated evidence accumulates. It enables both benchmarking and training data collection for forecasting agents.

entry.title: Back to the Definition: Estimating Step-Level Advantages via Trajectory Graphs for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xincheng Yao, Haobo Fu, Weiming Liu, Chongyang Zhang

entry.summary: This paper shows that GRPO-style group-normalized advantages are systematically biased at the step level in agentic RL, since trajectory-level advantages miss the contribution of individual steps, including valuable steps inside failed trajectories. Revisiting the foundational RL definition, it estimates step-level advantages via trajectory graphs where the mean reward of multiple actions from the same state is treated as a credible estimate. A principled fix for a known weakness in agentic RL credit assignment.

entry.title: Direct Message Approximation (DMA): A Consistency-Based Framework for Tractable Approximate Inference on Factor Graphs

author.name: Ralf Herbrich, Rainer Schlosser, Jan Lemcke, Johann Ukrow, Anna Kazachkova, Nicolas Alder, Leonhard Hennicke, Theo Bardey, Nico Grimm, Luca Kleinschmidt, Philipp Kolbe, Cezary Kujath, Johanna Schlimme, Karl Matti Sch\"utz

entry.summary: Introduces Direct Message Approximation, which approximates factor-to-variable messages directly on factor graphs rather than the marginals, with a consistency condition and a proven master theorem bounding behavior for proper messages on arbitrary graphs. The framework addresses limitations of expectation propagation and variational message passing, including round-robin schedules and pathological messages at Dirac-delta factors.

entry.title: MorphIK: Morphology-Conditioned Neural Inverse Kinematics for Unknown Robots

author.name: Lennart Clasmeier, Jan Gerrit Habekost, Cornelius Weber, Stefan Wermter

entry.summary: Presents MorphIK, a transformer-encoded, flow-matching model that solves inverse kinematics for revolute-joint kinematic chains never seen in training, conditioned on robot morphology and target pose and trained purely on procedurally generated synthetic robots. It reaches roughly 5 cm precision on unseen real-world 6-9 DoF robots and serves as a strong prior for further optimization.

entry.title: Three Ways Classical Test Theory Misleads for LLM Judges

author.name: Louis Yiven Zhu

entry.summary: Shows that reliability statistics borrowed from classical test theory, such as KR-20 internal consistency, mean something different when applied to LLM judges because the judge setting rearranges the measurement design those statistics assume. Concrete numerical examples demonstrate that a fixed judge error rate can yield coefficients ranging from 0.01 to 0.68 depending only on how the item bank is designed. This is a timely methodological warning for the widespread practice of evaluating LLM-as-judge reliability with test-theory tools.

entry.title: Artificial Societies Benchmark: A Validation Framework for Synthetic Research

author.name: Edoardo Chidichimo, Min Jun Jung, Felix P. S. Wallis, James K. He

entry.summary: The Artificial Societies Benchmark provides eleven tests across internal, construct, and external validity to assess whether LLM-based synthetic survey populations support intended research analyses, comparing nine language models against twenty human sources. Key findings include that models answer too consistently, compress response distributions, and that strong fidelity in one domain does not transfer to others. This is a valuable calibration tool for the growing use of synthetic populations in social science.

entry.title: PlenoCI: Plenoptic CharacterIstics for View Dependence Aware Change Classification

author.name: Jason Lai, Chamuditha Jayanga Galappaththige, Niko Suenderhauf, Dimity Miller, Donald G. Dansereau

entry.summary: PlenoCI introduces plenoptic characteristics, a feature derived in closed form from 3D Gaussian Splatting representations that captures view-dependent visual structures while ignoring Lambertian textures. This yields change classification robust to the underconstrained nature of radiance-field reconstructions, where independent optimizations converge to different primitives even in unchanged regions. The method reports two orders of magnitude improvement in robustness metrics.

entry.title: Inverse Problems Conditioned on Observation Ensembles: Applications and Methods

author.name: Zhengyan Huan, Camila Pazos, Martin Klassen, Vincent Croft, Pierre-Hugues Beauchemin, Shuchin Aeron

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Ensemble-conditioned Inverse Problem (EIP), inverting for a whole ensemble distributed as the pushforward of a prior under a forward process, generalizing problems like high-energy-physics unfolding and full waveform inversion. The authors propose non-iterative inference-time posterior samplers built on a new class of conditional generative models called ensemble inverse generative models. This provides a unified statistical framework for several important inverse problems.

entry.title: Overtly misaligned trajectories score highly in RL.

author.name: Cleo Nardo

entry.summary: Cleo Nardo argues that current AI agents sometimes behave overtly, egregiously misaligned because such trajectories scored highly during RL training. The proposed explanation combines poor RL sample efficiency forcing reliance on script or LLM graders, poor generalization forcing thousands of synthetically generated training environments, and the resulting sloppiness of scaling RL without human oversight. The post suggests this failure mode is a distinct and underappreciated risk category compared to subtle misgeneralization.

entry.title: TW3Cast: A Frozen Router of Lightly Fine-Tuned Foundation Models for Time-Series Forecasting on GIFT-Eval, Selected Entirely on the Training Split

author.name: Nathan Thierry, Andre-Louis Rochet

entry.summary: TW3Cast reaches position 3 of 130 on the GIFT-Eval time-series benchmark using no agents or language models, only lightly fine-tuned public foundation models (Chronos-2, TiRex, Toto) selected by a lookup table frozen on the training split. It outperforms everything except the leaderboard's agentic multi-step systems. This is a compelling demonstration that simple, leakage-free expert selection can rival complex agentic pipelines.

entry.title: Scope Before You Persist: Preventing Cross-Family Interference in Agent Memory

author.name: Yezhou Cheng, Runjia Du, Zeming Liu, Qibai Chen, Hang Lyu, Yankai Zeng, Yilan Wei, Bojun Lin

entry.summary: The paper studies persistent memory for frozen-model agents and shows that restricting retrieval of stored skills to their originating task family prevents harmful interference across task types. On a 12-round code-repair stream with an execution-grounded gate called Orthogonal Regression Control, scoped retrieval raises mean trajectory utility from 0.713 to 0.816 and eliminates harmful deployments.

entry.title: Evaluation of Multi-Turn Consistency in LLM Agents: Survival Analysis and Failure-Rationale Taxonomy

author.name: Igor Bogdanov, Olga Manakina, Chung-Horng Lung

entry.summary: This study evaluates temporal consistency of LLM agents in a controlled 20-step delayed-gratification setting, running 84,540 trajectories across 8 model families with full-factorial manipulation of social visibility, persona stressors, and deliberation policy. It treats first reward-claim as a time-to-event outcome, applying Kaplan-Meier survival curves and discrete-time hazard regression to quantify how factors shift failure risk over time, plus a failure-rationale taxonomy. The survival-analysis framing is a rigorous, time-resolved way to study long-horizon agent degradation.

entry.title: Safe Skill Retirement for Physical Agents

author.name: Zhonghao Zhan, Xiao Ma, Hamed Haddadi

entry.summary: The paper addresses a subtle safety risk when pruning agent skills: maintenance tests on authorized benchmark tasks can leave dormant safety conditions (governing authority, user consent, environment state) untested, creating an unmeasured support gap for physical and privacy-sensitive effects. It introduces matched authority counterfactuals that vary a single governing predicate while holding the action fixed, formalized via a two-gate retirement certificate. This provides a principled procedure for safely removing instructions as model capabilities advance.

entry.title: To Think or Not to Think: Allocating Reasoning Where It Helps

author.name: Zhengdong He, Yunfan Zhou, Jianguo Yao, Haibing Guan, Xijun Li

entry.summary: The paper identifies systematic length misallocation in RL-trained reasoning LLMs, which over-reason on simple questions and terminate prematurely on hard ones, and challenges the assumption that harder questions benefit monotonically from extended reasoning. It finds reasoning-length effects on accuracy are concentrated on partially difficult questions, motivating allocation based on where reasoning actually helps rather than raw difficulty. This informs efficient test-time compute allocation.

entry.title: AI-based detection of worsening heart failure from low-resolution telemonitoring data

author.name: Erik Aerts, Yinan Yu, Annika Rosengren, Michael Fu, Martin Lindgren, Falk Dippel, Martin Adiels, Helen Sj\"oland

entry.summary: Introduces TRACER, a Transformer with contrastive event representation and time-aware biomarker embeddings, to predict hospitalization timelines from low-resolution, irregularly sampled heart failure telemonitoring data. It targets early autonomous detection of patient deterioration to reduce clinical workload.

entry.title: Augur: A Synthetic Decision Lab for Rehearsing Reactions to Product and Policy Changes

author.name: Rahul Khedar, Mayank Malhotra, Avinash Karn

entry.summary: Augur rehearses reactions to product and policy changes offline using a typed knowledge graph, a grounded persona market, and simulated interaction, outputting auditable decision memos scored against Gold-50, fifty real episodes with known outcomes. Its central finding is negative: gaps between frontier cloud and fine-tuned open-weight models were mostly due to under-specified evaluation rather than capability.

entry.title: SciWalker: Synthesizing Scientific Coding Problems with Operator Graphs and Execution Feedback

author.name: Chenxi Li, Wenxuan Zeng, Yun Luo, Fangchen Yu, Peng Ye, Yu Cheng, Jun Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces SciWalker, a framework that synthesizes scientific coding training problems by sampling operator chains from operator graphs built from scientific library interfaces, then uses LLMs with execution feedback to generate scientifically grounded problems and solutions. It addresses scarcity of high-quality scientific coding data.

entry.title: SAGE: Mitigating Long-Horizon Reasoning Biases via Topological Guidance

author.name: Xinyue Zeng, Jiawei Zhang, Yujun Yan, Dawei Zhou

entry.summary: The paper attributes long-horizon LLM reasoning failures under sparse rewards to exploration bias (attraction to locally plausible but unstable branches) and compounding bias (accumulating small deviations). It introduces Symbolic Closure Analysis as a theoretical lens and derives SAGE, a method providing structural priors to mitigate these biases.

entry.title: A Harness for Synthesizing Diverse Naturalistic Full-Duplex Conversations

author.name: Matthew Sun, Vinay Kothapally, Meng Yu, Chao Huang, Hao Zhang, Yixuan Zhang, Steve Yves

entry.summary: Presents a pipeline for synthesizing intent-labeled, two-channel conversational speech with fine-grained control over turn-taking events like interruptions, backchannels, and pauses. An LLM authors relational event lists without absolute timestamps, which are then aligned and rendered on a shared clock, addressing a major data bottleneck for full-duplex dialogue systems.

entry.title: Robots That Take Initiative: A Framework for Building and Evaluating Proactive Robots

author.name: Maithili Patel, Sonia Chernova

entry.summary: Introduces a unified formalism for proactive robot assistance organized into three levels, plus a framework for the hardest case of unprompted proactivity. It shows that offline evaluation with static human models overstates performance and contributes a closed-loop evaluation with a human model that captures how robot actions change user behavior.

entry.title: Empath: Tracing Multi-Level Emotion Dynamics in Crisis Counseling Dialogues

author.name: Ziwei Gong, Yuchen Huang, Wen Liang, Nicholas Deas, Melanie Subbiah, Kathleen McKeown, Julia Hirschberg

entry.summary: Introduces EMPATH, a framework analyzing affect in crisis conversations at three granularities: turn-level labels, transition probabilities, and global conversation archetypes. Applied to text-based crisis conversations from self-identified Black texters discussing grief, it reveals persistent negative affect, gradual hope-ward transitions, and distinct texter-volunteer emotional roles.

entry.title: FB-GDM: Fully-Bayesian Guided Diffusion Models for High-Dimensional Linear Inverse Problems via Unsupervised Variational Inference

author.name: Gatien S\'eguy (SATIE), Thomas Rodet (SATIE)

entry.summary: FB-GDM removes per-task hyperparameter tuning from guided diffusion inverse problems by deriving a closed-form conditional score with two precision parameters treated as latent variables inferred via variational inference at each reverse step. This eliminates calibration against ground truth, a practical weakness of DPS and PiGDM guidance methods.

entry.title: TP-CRIV: A Framework for Third-Party Challenge-Response Identity Verification of AI Models

author.name: Teruki Sano, Minoru Kuribayashi, Masao Sakai, Shuji Isobe, Eisuke Koizumi, Zhang Zhang, Satoru Matsumoto

entry.summary: TP-CRIV proposes a challenge-response protocol for verifying whether a deployed service actually possesses and uses a claimed AI model, in a third-party setting where the verifier has neither white-box nor API access to the claimant model. This addresses growing model misappropriation concerns beyond watermarking and fingerprinting, with relevance to AI governance and provenance.

entry.title: GeoRefer-Bench: A Benchmark from Referring Pixels to Verifiable Geospatial Reasoning

author.name: Shuaishuai Cao, Min Huang, Meng Tang, Xuan Liu, Youjin Wang, Hui Lin

entry.summary: Introduces GeoRefer-Bench, which evaluates referring segmentation in overhead imagery using executable logical forms over metric scene graphs and an Exact Query Success metric that only credits predictions matching the exact referent set of relational queries like buildings north of a road. It contains 700 full 2048x2048 scenes and verifies whether spatial relations were actually resolved rather than scoring mask overlap.

entry.title: When Agents Act Unwatched: The Reduced-Supervision Paradox in Agentic AI

author.name: Hanjing Shi, Dominic DiFranzo

entry.summary: Argues that agentic AI creates an accountability inversion: as stepwise human supervision recedes, verification shifts into runtime infrastructure that defines authority, records actions, and supports repair, a dynamic the authors call the reduced-supervision paradox. A 63-artifact audit across 46 research papers and 17 engineering and governance sources finds action surfaces are easy to reconstruct while accountability mechanisms are far less visible.

entry.title: Do World Models Make Better Robots? A Survey of Evaluation Benchmarks for Predictive Embodied Intelligence

author.name: Gaytri Jena, Kapil Wanaskar, Vinija Jain, Aman Chadha, Vasu Sharma, Amitava Das

entry.summary: A survey arguing that the field cannot yet answer whether world models yield closed-loop task advantages over direct VLA policies, because evaluation is fragmented: world-model benchmarks score open-loop prediction without execution while task-success suites test only policies. It maps this measurement gap and outlines what unified evaluation would require.

entry.title: Era by Eon: Benchmarking Enterprise Agents on Hidden Knowledge

author.name: Benjamin Gruenbaum, Doron Porat, Assaf Natanzon, Roy Zavida, Chen Dinachi, Or Itzahary

entry.summary: The Era by Eon benchmark evaluates enterprise agents with code execution, where questions' answers are computed from generated company data; strong models with code access nearly saturate the original 27 questions. The authors add eight templates depending on hidden facts that are never stated explicitly but implied by other data, such as a recorded call contradicting the official sales explanation, and evaluate 12 model-plus-prompting agent pairs. This creates a much harder, more realistic test of enterprise agent reasoning over implicit information.

entry.title: Reachability-Based Formal Verification of Graph Neural Networks with Node and Edge Features

author.name: Anne M. Tumlin, Ben Wooding, Zhenxuan Shao, Diego Manzanas Lopez, Tyler Derr, Taylor T. Johnson

entry.summary: This work extends the neural network verification framework to graph-structured inputs via GraphStar sets, a generalization of Star sets capturing uncertainty over both node and edge features, enabling sound propagation of linear message-passing operations and ReLU approximation for GNNs including graph convolutions. It targets safety-critical power-system applications such as power flow, optimal power flow, and cascading failure analysis. This fills a real gap in formal verification for GNN surrogates in infrastructure.

entry.title: Coding Agents for Generalized Task and Motion Planning Problems

author.name: Matteo Merler, Bowen Li, Josh Roy, Yichao Liang, Qianwei Wang, Yixuan Huang, Tom Silver

entry.summary: This work investigates whether coding agents can automate generalized task and motion planning by synthesizing programs that exploit regularities across problem instances, given a task description and simulator access within a fixed synthesis budget. The frozen program is then evaluated on new instances, reducing the need for TAMP-specific engineering.

entry.title: The Mechanics of Delta Learning: Target Design for Generalizable Scientific Machine Learning

author.name: Kareem M. Gameel, Ihor Neporozhnii, Sjoerd Hoogland, Oleksandr Voznyy

entry.summary: The paper challenges the assumption in delta learning that smaller residual targets from more accurate baselines are easier to learn, showing that some accurate-baseline residuals are disproportionately rough and hard to learn. It introduces scale-normalized geometry metrics for target learnability and demonstrates improved in-domain and out-of-domain prediction on molecular energy prediction.

entry.title: On the second-order optimization for spiking neural networks

author.name: Ngoc Phu Doan, Ihsen Alouani

entry.summary: SpiKFAX introduces a tractable second-order optimization method for spiking neural networks using a Kronecker-factored approximation of the Fisher information matrix, motivated by the sharp loss landscape created by spiking activations that Adam-family optimizers handle poorly. This addresses a genuine training bottleneck in energy-efficient SNNs. Better SNN optimization could accelerate neuromorphic and event-driven computing research.

entry.title: An Analytical Theory of Auxiliary Learning

author.name: Federico Milanesio, Alessandro Ingrosso, Matteo Osella

entry.summary: Derives an analytical theory of auxiliary learning using a teacher-student framework, obtaining a closed system of differential equations for online SGD dynamics and closed-form generalization error for linear networks, showing how task correlations and label noise determine the benefit of joint training. For non-linear activations it develops a fluctuation-dissipation theory connecting auxiliary tasks to noise reduction. This provides principled explanations for a widely used but poorly understood training paradigm.

entry.title: Aim Short to Reach Far: Your Frozen World Model Can Plan Better Than You Think

author.name: Xvyuan Liu, Jianjie Fang, Chen Gao, Yong Li

entry.summary: Shows that scoring predicted outcomes of visual world models purely by distance to the encoded goal image limits control, since reaching a goal may require initially moving away from it, and demonstrates that intermediate targets substantially improve action synthesis and ranking with frozen LeWM world models on Cube, PushT, Reacher, and TwoRoom. It introduces Anchored Planning, which retrieves a recorded segment resembling current and goal observations and aims at an observation shortly after its start. This is a simple, model-free intervention that extracts much better planning from frozen world models.

entry.title: Beyond Compression: Training Latent Representations for Stable Long-Horizon Rollout in Neural Surrogate Solvers

author.name: Andreas E. Robertson, Ashley T. Lenau, John D. Shimanek, Benjamin A. Jasperson, Vivek Oommen, David L. Damm, Krishna Garikipati, Remi Dingreville

entry.summary: Shows that instability in latent neural surrogate solvers during long autoregressive rollouts does not stem from the latent representation itself but from training it solely for reconstruction, and systematically evaluates training-level interventions (including Koopman operator learning) that align latent representations with long-horizon forecasting. This reframes a known failure mode of latent dynamics models as a training-objective problem with actionable fixes. It is significant for scientific ML, where surrogate stability limits practical use.

entry.title: Don't Read the Log: Execution Traces Contaminate Verifiers in Video-Generation Agents

author.name: Jian Xu

entry.summary: In agentic video-generation loops where an LLM plans shots, calls a text-to-video model, and a multimodal judge verifies the result, recent harnesses show the judge the agent's execution trace and plans alongside the video. The paper shows on a manually labeled benchmark of 109 two-event clips that traces reporting successful tool calls bias open-weight Qwen-VL judges (7B, 8B, 32B) on purely visual requirements, even when frames are held fixed. The finding that auxiliary text contaminates verifier verdicts has direct implications for the design of generator-verifier agentic systems.

entry.title: UltraBench 2: Towards Robust Evaluation of Vision Foundation Models on Ultrasound

author.name: Ashwath Radhachandran, Adam Tupper, Christian Gagn\'e, William Speier

entry.summary: This paper introduces UltraBench 2, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating ultrasound vision foundation models with wide anatomical and task coverage, emphasizing standardization, reproducibility, and ease of use. The authors benchmark existing ultrasound foundation models and find fragmented, inconsistent progress in prior evaluations. It matters because rigorous benchmarking infrastructure is essential for measuring real clinical progress in medical imaging AI.

entry.title: A Corpus of Real Scam- and Spam-Call Conversations from an Active Voice-Agent Honeypot

author.name: Ethan Traister, Dennis Tsang Ng, Siyu Zhang, Huaiyu Guo, Tommy Duong, Tyler Wu, Yuchen Zhou, Xingyu Shen, Jiaqi Wu, Simiao Ren

entry.summary: The paper presents a dataset of real scam-call conversations collected by an active voice-agent honeypot that seeds phone numbers into lead-generation channels and sustains interactions with a plausible target persona, recording and auto-labeling every call. Over an initial 53-day window it captures dialogue data that passive honeypots and metadata studies have largely missed.

entry.title: On Growth and Form, and Function: Reusable Regulatory Handles Control Phenotypic Variation

author.name: Benedikt Hartl, Milton L. Montero, Marcello Barylli, Sebastian Risi, Michael Levin

entry.summary: Uses low-rank adaptation (LoRA) of pretrained neural cellular automata to show that large-scale morphological transformations can be encoded as low-dimensional modulations of a fixed developmental regulatory scaffold. Inspired by D'Arcy Thompson, this suggests reusable regulatory handles controlling phenotypic variation in self-organizing development models.

entry.title: EAGER: Enhancing Generative Event Extraction via Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Omar Adjali, Siting Liang, Omair Shahzad Bhatti, Daniel Sonntag

entry.summary: This paper introduces EAGER, a reinforcement learning framework for generative event extraction that pairs fine-grained verifiable rewards with Schema-Contrastive Advantage Estimation to avoid advantage collapse under sparse binary rewards. The reward design targets structural validity, extraction accuracy, groundedness, coverage, over-generation, and span precision. Across seven benchmark datasets, EAGER consistently outperforms prompting, supervised fine-tuning, and prior RL baselines for end-to-end event extraction.

entry.title: Parts-of-Speech as Emergent Categories in SAE Latent Space

author.name: Alessandro Bondielli, Lucia Passaro, Serena Auriemma, Alessandro Lenci

entry.summary: Uses part-of-speech categories as a controlled test case to study whether sparse autoencoder latents encode morpho-syntactic structure individually or in groups. It finds PoS distinctions are highly recoverable from SAE activations but via compact, stable groups of latents rather than one-to-one mappings, with open and closed classes behaving differently.

entry.title: Baseline Shape Decides the Verdict: A Controlled Re-Examination of Ternary Language Models at 60K Parameters

author.name: Gautam Veldanda

entry.summary: Re-examines a prominent claim that a routed ternary architecture (convolution, diagonal SSM, sparse attention) beats a parameter-matched full-precision transformer by 22% at 60K parameters. Under a fixed recipe with three seeds per cell and 98 byte-level runs, baseline depth/width shape alone spans 22.6% in validation loss, and the best-shaped transformer ties the routed ternary model, overturning the inductive-bias conclusion.

entry.title: VietPrism: A large-scale Vietnamese speech and deepfake corpus with diverse dialects and code-switching

author.name: Minh Hoang, Thai Le

entry.summary: VietPrism is an open multi-domain Vietnamese speech corpus of 993.4 hours and 403,941 bona fide utterances from 1,262 verified speakers, uniquely combining transcripts, speaker identities, five dialect groups, and natural Vietnamese-English code-switching (nearly half the corpus). It also includes over 3.1K hours of spoof speech from four synthesis systems for deepfake research. It is the first large-scale Vietnamese resource to unite ASR, speaker, dialect, code-switching, and deepfake dimensions.

entry.title: Accent Analogy Guidance: More Speaker Similarity at Equal Accent in Cross-Lingual Voice Cloning

author.name: Yoomee Cho, Jisun Lee

entry.summary: The paper introduces Accent Analogy Guidance (AAG), a training-free sampler term for cross-lingual zero-shot TTS that subtracts an estimated accent direction from model predictions so speaker voice can be disentangled from reference-accent leakage. The authors also propose a principled evaluation metric (Delta SIM) measuring speaker similarity above an identity-accent trade-off curve, validated with a blind LLM accent judge. AAG improves speaker similarity across four open TTS models, e.g., +0.11 to +0.27 on OmniVoice.

entry.title: MoVISA: Multi-Token Reasoning for Video Object Segmentation

author.name: Ruining Zhao, Ho Kei Cheng, Alexander G Schwing

entry.summary: MoVISA extends MLLM-based video object segmentation by replacing the single SEG token with multiple segmentation tokens (e.g., SEG0, SEG1) to represent an object across frames. This enables finer-grained alignment between language prompts and spatio-temporal mask predictions, improving localization of multiple objects over time.

entry.title: Seeing Is Not Measuring: Tool-Augmented Metric Spatial Reasoning for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Kai Glantz, Clemens Grange

entry.summary: This paper shows that small vision-language models reason poorly about metric 3D structure like distances, sizes, and directions, and proposes a modular tool-augmented framework that pairs a Qwen3.5-4B VLM with 3D detection, metric depth estimation, and deterministic geometric solvers lifted into a shared world frame. Moving metric computation out of model weights into explicit tools yields large gains on three of four ReVSI-Bench tasks.

entry.title: Visual Representation and History Modeling for Navigation World Models

author.name: Guangfu Guo, Xiaoqian Lu, Rui Liu, Yutong Chen, Kunpeng Liu, Long Cheng

entry.summary: The paper studies two design bottlenecks in Navigation World Models: choice of frozen visual representation and efficient modeling of observation history for repeated planning queries. It introduces Cached-Linear, a hybrid architecture combining local attention with cached history processing to reduce redundant computation in long-context, multi-query planning within a conditional flow-transformer framework.

entry.title: AgenticCADedit: A Stateful, Tool-Mediated Agentic Approach to Multimodal 3D CAD Editing

author.name: Saptarshi Neil Sinha, Mika Silvan Goschke, Paul Julius K\"uhn, Arjan Kuijper, Michael Weinmann

entry.summary: This paper addresses limitations in neural CAD editing by proposing a stateful, tool-mediated agentic approach for editing 3D models from multimodal requests (speech, sketches, and model interaction). Unlike prior stateless methods that discard partial progress and re-execute edits from scratch each attempt, the proposed system accumulates incremental changes and allows the agent to inspect the geometry it produces, which matters for industrial design workflows where most effort goes into modifying existing models rather than generating new ones.

entry.title: EgoSpeedUp: Transferring Human Manipulation Tempo to Robot Policies

author.name: Hanbit Oh, Yukiyasu Domae, Takuma Yagi

entry.summary: EgoSpeedUp uses egocentric human manipulation videos as temporal supervision so robot imitation policies can execute faster than their slow demonstrations, extracting task-appropriate, phase-wise tempo references from human behavior rather than robot-side heuristics or fixed speedup factors. It transfers human manipulation tempo to robot policies. This matters because imitation learning inherits conservative demo pacing that limits real-world productivity.

entry.title: MoSign: Challenge-Response Motion-Watermark Authentication for Anonymous Virtual-Reality Users

author.name: Xujun Che, Thomas Carr, Depeng Xu, Aidong Lu, Shuhan Yuan

entry.summary: MoSign recasts digital watermarking as a challenge-response authentication protocol on the motion channel in social VR, embedding a keyed time-varying message into a motion VAE style latent via keystream-whitened Gaussian-Shading, with provable indistinguishability of watermarked motion. It addresses the paradox that motion biometrics enable re-identification (over 94 percent among tens of thousands) yet users may need selective identity proof within anonymity. This is a novel intersection of privacy, biometrics, and watermarking.

entry.title: FlyCNS: Connectome-Grounded Information Organization for Communication-Constrained Embodied Control

author.name: Jinchang Zhang, Jiakai Lin, Guoyu Lu

entry.summary: FlyCNS is an embodied control framework inspired by the Drosophila brain-nerve-cord connectome that keeps sensorimotor computation local within limbs and routes selective long-range messages through ascending and descending pathways. It extracts directional structural complexity from a real connectome to decide which computations stay local and which information is worth transmitting under communication constraints.

entry.title: ADM-Planner: LLM-Guided Long-Horizon Planning for Mobile Manipulators with Attention-Enhanced Dynamic Memory

author.name: Jiaping Xiao, Pingyuan Ji, Mir Feroskhan

entry.summary: ADM-Planner is an LLM-guided planning framework for mobile manipulation that maintains an attention-enhanced dynamic memory separating persistent workspace knowledge from object-centric state. Asynchronous observations and action outcomes update the state, and a bounded retriever surfaces only decision-relevant entries to the LLM, which replans when updates invalidate the current plan. This addresses stale-context and unbounded-history problems in LLM planning.

entry.title: RACaP: Agentic Reasoning, Acting, and Coding as Policies for Evolvable Robot Learning

author.name: Zexi Li, Yehang Zhang, Haojian Huang, Bohan Zhou, Wenqian Li, Chenxu Wang, Yifan Chang, Yangkai Wei, Tianyi Zhang, Ying-Cong Chen, Kaiwen Zhou, Yinchuan Li, James Cheng

entry.summary: RACaP moves program generation out of the deployment loop: an agentic framework evolves typed Policy APIs offline while a frozen ReAct loop calls them at runtime, reducing latency compared to Code-as-Policies methods. A two-phase strategy combines capability curriculum learning with autonomous self-evolution that improves the APIs, the ReAct harness, and experience memory. The APIs encode reusable physical mechanisms with arguments for runtime adaptation.

entry.title: PolyUMI: Accessible Visual-Tactile-Audio Data Collection for Object Inference and Manipulation

author.name: Conor W. Hayes, Rickmer Krohn, Aravind Ramaswami, Anunth Ramaswami, Nils Dengler, Kevin M. Lynch, J. Edward Colgate, Georgia Chalvatzaki, Matthew L. Elwin

entry.summary: PolyUMI is an open-source platform for scalable visual-tactile-audio demonstration collection and robot deployment built around a lightweight wireless handheld gripper that records synchronized wrist-camera, optical tactile, contact-audio, and proprioceptive data without a tether. This fills a gap in imitation learning systems, which usually rely only on vision and proprioception and thus miss contact-rich information. The platform supports object inference and manipulation research with accessible hardware.

entry.title: Increasing Skill Level Recruits Deeper Attention Layers in a Frozen Chess Transformer

author.name: David Litman

entry.summary: The post reports interpretability experiments on Maia-3, a chess transformer conditioned on Elo, showing that turning the Elo dial from 700 to 2500 monotonically pushes causal computation deeper into later attention layers for every measured piece and move type. The depth migration is strongest for specific tactics like knight forks and appears to involve later heads being recruited for specialized computations while earlier heads keep constant contributions. The author discusses why this contradicts an initial expectation that features would migrate shallower with skill.

entry.title: Abliterated models are now served cheaply and conveniently via a chat interface - how dangerous are they?

author.name: Alice Rutte

entry.summary: A case study of Abliteration.ai, a startup serving uncensored/abliterated models (identified as GLM 5.2 and Qwen 3.6) through a no-code chat interface, extending the FAR.AI Safety Gap toolkit to measure how much such services could assist a low-skill bad actor. The post argues that operational barriers to harmful model access have collapsed from GPU-rental engineering work to a few clicks.

entry.title: Pistis Technical Report

author.name: Heyun Chen, Xiaohan Lan, Jiaxi Li, Zhilin Lu, Qi She, Weiwen Xu, Fei Yu, Yujie Zhong, Jinghuan Chen, Zijian Feng, Siyu Jiao, Yiheng Lin, Xinhao Wang, Sihan Yang, Jieyu You, Changbin Zhang, Hengyu Zhang, Xudong Zhang, Yunqing Zhao, Shuai Zheng

entry.summary: Pistis introduces 27B and 9B multimodal LLMs built on Qwen3.6 and Qwen3.5 bases via a scalable post-training framework featuring Interleaved Distillation and Reinforcement Learning (IDRL), which alternates on-policy distillation with RL in a single loop instead of using static joint losses. The authors claim better knowledge transfer and improved performance from this tightly coupled paradigm. It is relevant as an example of advanced post-training recipe engineering at mid-scale.

entry.title: PFArena: Benchmarking Language Models for Protein Modification

author.name: Yawen Ouyang, Xinbo Zhang, Ziyuan Ma, Yixin Wu, Wenbin Liao, Feiran Zhang, Wenjie Li, Lihao Wang, Hao Wang, Xiaoqing Zheng, Xuefeng Yan, Lei Bai, Ya-Qin Zhang, Shuyi Zhang, Wei-Ying Ma, Dahua Lin, Bowen Zhou, Hao Zhou

entry.summary: PFArena is a benchmark with four controlled task interfaces covering single-mutant generation and multi-mutant ranking, providing varying levels of mutation fitness data to mirror realistic experimental decision-making scenarios. It evaluates six protein language models, LLMs, and LLM-based agents to clarify their relative efficacy in protein modification. This addresses a genuine gap in comparing computational paradigms for protein engineering.

entry.title: Sequential knowledge editing breaks a model's ability to tell good evidence from bad, without costing it accuracy

author.name: Atul Anand

entry.summary: The paper shows that sequential knowledge editing can degrade a model's ability to arbitrate between its remembered answer and an injected passage on never-edited facts, even when standard editing metrics all pass.
