entry.summary: The paper identifies a methodological flaw in longitudinal clinical AI evaluation: event-based metrics can conflate recognition-mediated care-process signals with genuine pre-recognition early detection, inflating apparent lead time. It defines an interval-censored pre-recognition transition and an independent as-of reference standard to make detection-before-recognition claims testable.

entry.title: Prompt Breadth and Rollout Refresh Interact in On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Lingxiang Hu, Tianle Xia, Ming Xu, Yiding Sun, Linfang Shang

entry.summary: Runs a controlled 3x3 study of on-policy distillation varying prompt bank size and the number of response-generating policy snapshots at fixed trajectory budget, finding a strong interaction: prompt breadth helps only under per-update refresh (23.61% to 25.57%) but hurts with frozen initial-policy rollouts (21.16% to 19.05%). Eight prompts with ten snapshots nearly match 14,080 distinct prompts.

entry.title: Trains but Doesn't Learn: A Post-Training Delivery Benchmark for LLM Agents as Forward-Deployed Engineers

author.name: Weihang Ding, Junfei Zhan

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmark evaluating whether LLM agents can be trusted to deliver complete post-training-as-a-service engagements, driving ten governed stages scored by an oracle from platform-recorded facts. Its central finding is the silent TBDL failure mode: runs where loss falls and all signals stay green but the delivered model is no better than the base.

entry.title: Beyond Natural Language: An Agent-Native Language for Autonomous Science

author.name: Yifeng He, Jiachen Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Lara, a machine-checkable language and protocol that turns research arguments into executable, auditable artifacts, enabling automated validation pipelines for autonomous research agents and cross-paper claim bridges. It argues that natural-language prose is too informal a medium for scientific output that exceeds human review capacity.

entry.title: AkasicMEM: Governed Enterprise Memory for Agents

author.name: Jeongmin Bae, Yongjae Kim, Kyoung Hur, Donghyoung Han, Min-Soo Kim

entry.summary: Proposes an enterprise agent memory system that integrates organizational sources with persistent shared memory while enforcing governance policies throughout the memory lifecycle. The key contribution is addressing information leakage that occurs when source restrictions are bypassed as memory entries are repeatedly derived and reused under changing principals and policies.

entry.title: Risk-Aware Online Conformal State Probing

author.name: Pietro Talli, Petar Popovski, Osvaldo Simeone

entry.summary: This paper addresses safety-critical control of autonomous agents that must acquire state information from robots or edge devices under uncertainty. It introduces online conformal state probing (OCSP), a policy that jointly decides when to act and when to probe an arbitrary state prediction model, providing distribution-free worst-case reliability guarantees by provably controlling the missed query error rate. This fills a gap left by average-case uncertainty methods that are insufficient for safety-critical settings.

entry.title: Policy-Backed Selective Regeneration under Tainted Inter-Agent Communication

author.name: Jinghan Xu, Longze Fan, Zeyuan Wang, Xinjin Li, Hankai Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces ESC-CR, a framework for securing inter-agent communication in multi-agent language-model systems, separating message claims from authorization and enforcing executable semantic commitments at an external release boundary rather than relying on prompt-based defenses. When a violation occurs, it taints the responsible message and rejected artifacts, then performs clean-room recovery to selectively regenerate only what was compromised, avoiding both blind removal and unenforced trust.

entry.title: When Recursive Models Finish Computing

author.name: Hare Krishna, Shubham Singh, Stephen Ebert, Hao-Yu Sun

entry.summary: Studies completion dynamics in Tiny Recursive Models on 1,000 hard Sudoku puzzles, showing that extending recurrence from 16 to 512 steps lifts exact-solve accuracy from 59.2% to 87.5% (attention) and 74.4% to 91.9% (MLP), and that latent-state motion drops sharply after the first correct solution. It distinguishes unfinished computation from persistently unsuccessful regimes.

entry.title: Marginally Correct Tool Caches Can Reverse Group-Normalized Policy Updates

author.name: Shivam Gupta

entry.summary: This theory paper shows that tool-result caching in agent training couples rollout randomness: even when shared execution preserves each rollout's marginal reward distribution, sharing one stochastic result per group can reverse the expected group-normalized policy update. The author derives an exact finite-group expression, identifies a wrong-direction region for Bernoulli rewards, and shows a non-vanishing update-variance floor.

entry.title: On Preference Coverage Collapse from Hindsight Relabeling in Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Baptiste Bonin, Caro Strickland, Audrey Durand

entry.summary: The authors show that a natural extension of hindsight relabeling to preference-conditioned multi-objective RL — relabeling transitions with the achieved rather than requested preference — is frequently harmful. Across four off-policy algorithms and the MO-Gymnasium suite, the technique degrades 19 of 36 settings by up to four standard deviations while improving only one. The paper provides a rigorous negative result with analysis of the underlying coverage collapse mechanism.

entry.title: Forecast Workflow Bench: Evaluating Language-Model Decisions with Budgeted Forecast Tools

author.name: Shunya Nagashima

entry.summary: FWBench evaluates language-model agents on decision quality and forecast cost using 1,251 electricity and cycle-hire cases with fixed forecast tools and simulated capacity contracts, where agents choose models, histories, and horizons to minimize a loss-cost objective. Testing ten configurations including the existing GPT-6 Astra, the study found that model selectively bought inexpensive short-horizon forecasts using 2.5 percent of the budget and outperformed fixed policies in certain savings regimes. The benchmark shifts time-series evaluation from accuracy alone toward budgeted decision-making.

entry.title: Private Decentralized Optimization with Noise Reduction and Bias Correction

author.name: Yizhao Fan, Wenjian Luo, Jiaojiao Zhang

entry.summary: Presents PRDO, a private recursive decentralized optimization algorithm that reduces errors from sampling and privacy noise via recursive estimation with same-batch gradient differences, while an Exact Diffusion component corrects bias from data heterogeneity. The paper establishes nonconvex convergence bounds without assuming uniformly bounded heterogeneity and gives conditions under which gradient differencing strictly lowers query sensitivity.

entry.title: Backdoors Leave Structural Traces: FedMAST for Backdoor Detection and Containment in Federated Learning

author.name: Srinivasan Subramanian, Kazi Aminul Islam, Md. Abdullah Al Hafiz Khan

entry.summary: Shows that stealthy backdoor poisoning in federated learning can suppress isolated anomaly signals but still leaves residual structural traces, and proposes FedMAST, a multi-axis defense that scores client updates using complementary structural, spectral, and historical evidence with tiered containment. This addresses adaptive attackers that evade single-signal defenses.

entry.title: Evaluation Choices Decide the Forecasting Leaderboard: Evidence from a Production Marketplace Panel

author.name: Md Rezwanul Islam, Wael Mohammed

entry.summary: Benchmarks 24 forecasting methods, including six 2025-era time series foundation models, on a production panel of 1,887 customers over 67 months and shows that varying only evaluation design choices (unit of analysis, error aggregation) reverses or dissolves headline leaderboard conclusions. For example, changing from market totals to individual customers drops the production baseline from second place to twenty-third of twenty-five.

entry.title: CS-WCP: Robust Conformal Sets for LLM-Judge Traffic Shifts with Uncertain Group Proportions

author.name: Ibne Farabi Shihab, Fariya Afrin

entry.summary: This paper introduces CS-WCP, a confidence-set weighted conformal prediction method that maintains valid coverage for LLM-judge prediction sets when deployment traffic shifts the proportions of task or policy groups. It constructs simultaneous intervals for source and target group masses and unions weighted conformal sets over all compatible ratio vectors, with theoretical coverage guarantees accounting for covariate and conditional shift.

entry.title: Minimal-Norm Univariate Two-Layer ReLU Classification: Exact Solutions and Global Optimality with Skip Connections

author.name: Karolina Drabik, Ben Lewis, Antoni Puch, Etienne Boursier, Piotr Hofman, Matthias Englert, Ranko Lazi\'c

entry.summary: Provides complete geometric characterizations of minimal-norm interpolators and L2-regularized logistic-loss solutions for univariate two-layer ReLU classifiers, distinguishing cases where hidden biases are penalized or not. It also analyzes how skip connections affect the optimizer, yielding exact global-optimality statements in function space.

entry.title: Artificial intelligence surrogates for treatment effect estimation with before-and-after data

author.name: Frances Dean, Anna Neufeld, Joshua Barrios, Geoffrey H Tison, Ahmed Alaa

entry.summary: This work develops a causal inference framework that uses pretrained AI model predictions on before-and-after patient measurements as surrogate outcomes for estimating treatment effects when clinical outcomes are costly or slow to measure. It provides a principled route to leverage clinical AI models for downstream causal questions.

entry.title: DeltaS: Reading the Gated Linear Attention State for KV Cache Eviction in Streaming Video

author.name: Taeyoun Kwon, Seungjin Kim, Hyeonyu Kim, Moon Hwan Kim

entry.summary: DeltaS uses the recurrent state of gated linear attention layers in hybrid video-language backbones to decide KV cache eviction for full attention layers, enabling question-agnostic eviction decisions in streaming video. This avoids proxy queries and extra computation required by attention-score-based eviction methods.

entry.title: Robustness of Diffusion Models under Distribution Shift

author.name: Wei Luo, Neil K. Chada, Shijie Zhang, Lu Yu

entry.summary: Provides minimax-optimal theory for robust score estimation in score-based diffusion models when the test distribution is Wasserstein-perturbed relative to training data. For the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck diffusion, it decomposes robustness cost into statistical learning cost plus an intrinsic shift cost scaling quadratically with the Wasserstein radius, and constructs a finite-sample estimator attaining the rate.

entry.title: Quantum score matching with applications to learning thermal states

author.name: Yulong Dong, Jiaqi Leng

entry.summary: The authors establish a general quantum score-matching framework with end-to-end theoretical guarantees, extending classical score matching to noncommuting density operators, and apply it to Gibbs-state (thermal state) learning with efficient circuit implementations. This bridges a foundational gap between classical generative learning and quantum state learning.

entry.title: The Illinois Social Attitudes Aggregate Corpus (ISAAC): An Open Tool and Reproducible Pipeline for Analyzing Social Group Discourse at Scale

author.name: Babak Hemmatian, Sarah Hadjarab, Jessica Chen, Benedek Kurdi

entry.summary: ISAAC is an open corpus of 527M+ Reddit posts (2007-2023) filtered for relevance to six social-group distinctions (race, sexuality, age, ability, weight, skin tone), with region annotations and semantic labels such as moralization and sentiment. A human-audited pipeline keeps irrelevant content below 10%, enabling reproducible large-scale studies of social-group discourse.

entry.title: When Parallel Drafter Meets Parallel Speculative Decoding

author.name: Fuliang Liu, Xue Li, Kun Qian, Zhibin Wang, Wanchun Dou, Wenyuan Yu, Chen Tian

entry.summary: This paper introduces DPara, a parallel speculative decoding (PSD) framework that combines parallel drafters with overlap between drafting and verification. Unlike prior PSD methods that guess the accepted prefix and bonus token in advance and fall back to serial drafting on error, DPara precomputes draft representations for every possible acceptance boundary with a diffusion backbone, guaranteeing overlap in every round and improving inference throughput.

entry.title: Computation Over Geometry: Meaning Identity Is Computed, Not Shipped in the Embeddings

author.name: Jiaqi Deng

entry.summary: This arXiv paper challenges the common assumption in retrieval and RAG that semantic equivalence between paraphrases is a fixed property of independently encoded embedding vectors. The authors show empirically that off-the-shelf sentence encoders (BGE, E5, GTE, MiniLM, E5-Mistral-7B) and last-token states of Llama 3, Mistral, and Qwen achieve only weak paraphrase-identity discrimination (AUC roughly 0.55-0.70) on overlap-matched PAWS-X, and that late fusion of two independently encoded vectors stays near chance. In contrast, a joint forward pass over both sentences reaches AUC 0.90-0.96 across model scales from 1.5B to 32B, indicating that meaning identity is computed during shared processing rather than shipped in static embedding geometry.

entry.title: Text Scores Can Miss Waveform Use: A Qwen2-Audio Quantization Case Study

author.name: Mengzhe Geng, Jinxi Jin, Junhao Xu

entry.summary: This paper introduces an evaluation protocol for quantized speech language models that separately tests lexical output, a transcript-insufficient endpoint, and a measured packed implementation, arguing that text-output scores and nominal bit widths alone do not capture behavior that depends on non-transcript information. In a Qwen2-Audio case study, a translation-selected 6-bit allocation improves chrF by 2.36 on an English-to-German task but loses 3.91 percentage points on speaker-disjoint emotion recognition, while a uniform structural control at the same 6-bit budget reaches higher emotion accuracy.

entry.title: EnSIMem: Entity-Structured Indexing for Long-Term Agent Memory

author.name: Xuanyu Meng, Xing Fan, Xinyi Fan, Chenlei Guo, Yixuan Xie, Jiawei Han

entry.summary: EnSIMem proposes an entity-structured long-term memory architecture for agents that organizes interaction history into theme-coherent episodes and indexes facts as entity-type-property-value entries preserving source turns, temporal information, and multimodal fields. This aims to let agents correctly identify the relevant entity, property, and supporting evidence during online retrieval.

entry.title: Lessons learned from deploying imaging AI with the open PACS-AI platform

author.name: Samuel Kadoury, Julie G. Hussin, Pascal Th\'eriault-Lauzier, Laurent L\'etourneau-Guillon, Rob Lewis, Adam McArthur, Gordon J. Harris, Houda Bahig, Pierre-Luc D\'eziel, Jay Kshirsagar, Jacob L. Jaremko, Julien Cohen-Adad, Jacques Delfrate, Robert Avram

entry.summary: This deployment study reports on imaging AI across six hospitals via PACS-AI, an open self-hosted platform, finding that infrastructure for study routing, result display, feedback capture, and auditing, rather than model accuracy, is the binding constraint. Honest publication of per-model readiness levels is framed as a governance practice.

entry.title: Latent evolving World Action Model

author.name: Xueji Fang, Boqiang Duan, Hua Wu, Jingdong Wang, Guo-Jun Qi

entry.summary: Shows that JEPA predictive embeddings better support action generation than VAE latents from video diffusion backbones, enabling a World Action Model that decouples action modeling from expensive large-scale video generation pretraining. Provides both theoretical and empirical analysis of how visual representations affect action generation in world models.

entry.title: Frozen Flows Forget: Diagnosing and Restoring Lost Motion in a Latent-flow World Model

author.name: Xiwen Chen, Rigaudiere Z. Li, Zhiruo Zhou, Xiaojun Zhu, Houde Liu

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses why latent world models with flows in frozen self-supervised latent spaces silently lose motion: anchor-sparse, latent-only supervision never specifies when along the horizon change occurs. The proposed DART (decode-augmented rollout training) repairs this by retraining only the flow with decode-path supervision while keeping the representation frozen, restoring temporal structure and outperforming its latent-only parent. This is a crisp diagnosis-and-fix for a fundamental failure mode in world models.

entry.title: HOTICE: Whole-Body Humanoid Object Transportation in Cluttered Environments

author.name: Toan Nguyen, Weiduo Yuan, Siheng Zhao, Yue Wang, Daniel Seita

entry.summary: Presents HOTICE, a whole-body humanoid learning framework for carrying objects through clutter, using Humanoid-Object Decoupled Potential Fields to jointly guide collision avoidance for robot and payload, and a dual-agent RL architecture that decouples upper- and lower-body control to tame the large whole-body action space. This targets realistic human-centric environments where existing transport methods fail.

entry.title: RoboMP-DINOv2: Prompts, Not Filters for Robust Robot Manipulation

author.name: Han Qi, Heng Yang

entry.summary: RoboMP-DINOv2 is a full-scene vision encoder for robot manipulation that treats segmentation masks as spatial prompts rather than hard visibility filters, injecting learned region embeddings into dense DINOv2 features and jointly contextualizing prompted and unprompted tokens. Masked-region color randomization further improves appearance robustness across visual shifts.

entry.title: Deploying Foundation Models for Embodied Navigation

author.name: Vishnu Sashank Dorbala, Dinesh Manocha

entry.summary: This paper identifies two practical obstacles to using foundation models for embodied navigation: training bias that hurts personalization in unseen environments, and limited context length on long-horizon tasks. The authors propose Transit-Aware Planning (TAP), which primes the model with human-habit data mined from the scene, and MemCtrl, a memory-head augmentation for active memory management, alongside a taxonomy of FM-based navigation literature. Real-world results demonstrate the approaches.

entry.title: RouteRLT: Learning When and Which RL Specialist Should Control a Vision-Language-Action Policy

author.name: Chongyu Zhu, Jaden Hinds, Hyegang Kim, Juan Sebastian Rojas, Ramy Elmallah, Chi-Guhn Lee

entry.summary: Presents RouteRLT, a routing framework that learns when to hand control from a generalist VLA policy to RL-trained specialists for precision-critical phases of contact-rich industrial tasks such as connector insertion and cable management. A phase selector preserves generalist behavior while enabling task-specific RL refinement, addressing the open question of when and which specialist should act.

entry.title: Conditional Tensor Diffusion: Distributional Counterfactual Learning and Inference

author.name: Xinbing Kong, Zeyu Li, Junfan Mao, Bin Wu

entry.summary: This work develops Counterfactual Tucker Diffusion, a method that integrates treatment masks and latent Tucker structure into conditional diffusion models to recover the joint conditional distribution of missing control outcomes in high-dimensional panel/tensor causal inference. By performing nonlinear score learning in a low-dimensional core, it preserves cross-mode dependence while drastically reducing dimensionality, with high-probability error guarantees.

entry.title: Optimal Sequential Annotations for Off-Policy Evaluation

author.name: Woojin Chae, Ezinne Nwankwo, Haitong Qin, Angela Zhou

entry.summary: The authors study off-policy evaluation when state and reward information exists as text or images that can be labeled cheaply by LLM-as-a-judge with unknown bias or expensively by experts, formulating annotation allocation under a limited ground-truth budget. They derive variance-optimal annotation probabilities for doubly-robust sequential off-policy evaluation with missing rewards.

entry.title: From Offline Proxies to Online Decisions: A Layered Engagement Evaluation Framework for Conversational AI

author.name: Xuanyi Li, Vaskar Nath, Hossein Amirkhani, Jay Li, Alex Deng

entry.summary: This paper provides a reusable framework for validating offline engagement proxies against online A/B experiments in conversational AI, modeling the proxy as a chain of three alignments: behavioral label to product outcome, classifier to assistant behavior, and offline signal to experiment effect. It contributes an interval-aware decision-agreement protocol that compares confidence intervals rather than point estimates, with wit........ness-based auditing of the composite.

entry.title: Neurosymbolic Action Model Learning under Partial Observability

author.name: Adem Kikaj, Lennert De Smet, Giuseppe Marra, Luc De Raedt

entry.summary: Proposes NeSyAM, a neurosymbolic paradigm for learning planning action models when observed images are missing or only partially informative, relaxing the complete fully-observable-trace assumption of prior work. This extends action-model learning to realistic partially observable settings.

entry.title: FusionMMT: A Unified Multimodal and Multitask Learning Framework for Nuclear Fusion

author.name: Qiang Chen, Xiao Wang, Qingquan Yang, Hao Si, Zikang Yan, Meiwen Chen, Guosheng Xu, Jin Tang

entry.summary: FusionMMT provides a unified multimodal multitask learning framework for tokamak plasma diagnosis, contributing EAST-VTD640, a dataset spanning 640 EAST shots with vision and time-series diagnostics for disruption prediction, edge-localized mode recognition, and confinement-quality estimation. It addresses the gap between multimodal-single-task and unimodal-multitask approaches in fusion science.

entry.title: SWE-Serve: Benchmarking Agentic Engineering For Production Inference Serving

author.name: Jennifer Williams, Dave Farris, Jeff Farris, Jiantao Jiao

entry.summary: SWE-Serve is a benchmark of 53 repository-grounded tasks evaluating coding agents on production inference-serving engineering, spanning model support, runtime execution, and public APIs. It fills a gap between repository-level SWE benchmarks that ignore inference and narrow kernel-optimization benchmarks.

entry.title: Mitigating Sequential Reappearance in Diffusion Data-Point Unlearning

author.name: Donghyun Kim, Taehyuk Lee, Jinyeong Kim, Youngmin Oh, Dohyeong Kim, Jaehyuk Ryu, Sangwoo Hong

entry.summary: Identifies sequential reappearance, a failure mode in diffusion model data-point unlearning where an instance judged forgotten initially returns to the memorized regime after subsequent deletion requests, without data reuse or adversarial fine-tuning. It introduces a target-level evaluation protocol tracking immediate forgetting, persistence, and reappearance, and finds reappearance correlates with sharper local denoising-loss geometry after deletion.

entry.title: VLAQuantBench: Closed-Loop Evaluation of Post-Training Quantization for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Jiuyi Xu, Qing Jin, Meida Chen, Song Wang, Yang Sui, Yangming Shi

entry.summary: Provides a controlled closed-loop evaluation of post-training quantization for vision-language-action models across 409 runs and 94,574 simulation episodes, showing that precision selection must jointly account for layer scope, numerical format, and calibration. Striking results include success jumping from 7.0% to 70.5% when expanding a quantized action-head subset, and two-episode calibration removing severe joint failures.

entry.title: Terminal Shrinkage Averaging Reveals a Schedule-Estimator Interaction in LLM Pretraining

author.name: Adam Ousherovitch, Yixin Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Terminal Shrinkage Averaging (TSA), which decouples the learning-rate schedule from the estimator used to construct the deployed model by interpolating between the raw final iterate and an average of recent checkpoints, balancing late-training optimization progress against terminal variation in the returned model.

entry.title: From Experts to Sub-experts: Fine-grained Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for MoE LLMs

author.name: Zhentao Tan, Chang Liu, Yao Liu, Yue Wu, Jieping Ye

entry.summary: Observes that activated experts in MoE LLMs are internally sparse, with only a small fraction of intermediate channels responding to downstream tasks, making expert-level PEFT too coarse. Proposes NSFT (Neural Sub-expert Fine-Tuning), which selects and updates parameters at sub-expert granularity for more efficient adaptation.

entry.title: WatchPoint: Executable User Feedback for Real-World Agentic Web Development

author.name: Guanqun Yang, Wei Yang, Xueqing Liu

entry.summary: WatchPoint is a simulated-user system for coding agents that mimics professional developer debugging behavior by generating and executing diagnostic scripts against the running web application, producing structured observations that guide the model's retry. This contrasts with existing feedback mechanisms based on screenshots, LLM-as-judge scoring, or natural-language corrections that rarely interact with the live application.

entry.title: Learning Risk Scores Robust to Unobserved Confounders

author.name: Ryan Edmonds, Yingxiao Ye, Sina Aghaei, Andr\'es G\'omez, \c{C}a\u{g}{\i}l Ko\c{c}yi\u{g}it, Phebe Vayanos

entry.summary: This work addresses learning risk scores from observational data when historical allocation decisions depend on unobserved confounders, a setting where standard inverse propensity weighting fails. The authors develop optimization-based methods producing scores robust to unobserved confounding for prioritizing individuals for scarce resources. This is directly relevant to equitable resource allocation in healthcare and social policy.

entry.title: The Capability Manifold and ML Scaling Laws

author.name: Syed Ali Raza Zaidi, Maryam Hafeez

entry.summary: The paper proposes a capability manifold framework that maps downstream capabilities such as reasoning, retrieval, planning, and adaptation to pre-training, post-training, and test-time resources via bounded scaling functions, extending beyond loss-centric scaling laws. Analytical Jacobians quantify how sensitive each capability is to resource changes across the ML lifecycle. It responds to the observation that similar-loss models can differ sharply in agentic performance.

entry.title: Reliable Fusion of Conflicting Experts

author.name: Pranuthi Tenali, Sahil Sidheekh, Saurabh Mathur, Vijayalakshmi Saravanan, Erik Blasch, Kristian Kersting, Sriraam Natarajan

entry.summary: Proposes a probabilistic-circuit-based framework for fusing opinions from multiple black-box experts, using context-specific credibility estimates to handle noisy, conflict-prone settings where reliability varies per input. The method is agnostic to expert internals and requires no retraining, and is validated on multiple-choice QA using multiple LLMs as experts.

entry.title: EvoAudio: Recursive Self-Improvement for Audio Understanding

author.name: Yuxiang Wang, Shengbo Cai, Yingda Shen, Ming-Hao Hsu, Qinke Ni, Liqiang Zhang, Teddy Sun, Steve Yevs, Zhizheng Wu

entry.summary: EvoAudio is a recursive self-improvement system for audio understanding that jointly evolves the model, waveforms, questions, and difficulty in a closed loop, using a library of audio tools to construct questions with answers derivable from how the audio was made. This provides verifiable supervision without new human annotation and uses RL for improvement.

entry.title: LEAP-CBF: A Safety Filter for Uncertain Systems with Least-Effort Adversarial Potentials

author.name: Oswin So, Eric Yu, Chuchu Fan

entry.summary: The paper introduces Least-Effort Adversarial Potentials (LEAP), a certificate quantifying robustness of a state against disturbances by the effort needed to cause failure, and shows LEAP is a control barrier function for the undisturbed system that can also build a safety filter robust to uncertainty. This reduces the conservativeness of robust CBFs, especially in high dimensions with input constraints.

entry.title: Pro-Bench: Prompt-Robust Open-Vocabulary Visual Grounding Across Real-World Heterogeneous Environments

author.name: Linus Nwankwo, Muslim Alaran, Christian Rauch, Stanley Chukwuebuka Obilikpa, Elmar Rueckert

entry.summary: Pro-Bench is a prompt-conditioned benchmark for open-vocabulary visual grounding with over 13k RGB frames from robotic domains including subterranean, industrial, indoor, outdoor, and urban environments, featuring 74.5k manual annotations and 515 diverse query types. It tests whether open-vocabulary grounding models generalize beyond web-scraped imagery and short labels.

entry.title: Capability-Aware Arbitration for Semantic Intent-Based Shared Control

author.name: Zhaoda Du, Michael Bowman, Xiaoli Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a shared-control framework in which a VLM infers human intent with semantic confidence and a vision-language-action policy provides autonomous actions whose capability confidence is estimated online from the dispersion and instability of stochastic action trajectories; a nonlinear Bayesian-filtered arbitration policy combines the two to set robot authority. This prevents over-helping when intent confidence is high but autonomous execution is unreliable.

entry.title: PAKT: Physically-Aligned Kinesthetic Teaching for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Lars Johannsmeier, Yashraj Narang

entry.summary: PAKT is a framework for kinesthetic teaching in real-world reinforcement learning that lets operators physically guide robots while respecting the physical system's constraints and policy limits, addressing the lack of an intuitive interface for demonstrations and interventions in contact-rich industrial manipulation. It targets micrometer-level precision, above-99 percent success rates, and human-level cycle times.

entry.title: PLAT: Sparse Timed Keyframe Motion Tracking for Humanoid Control via Privileged Latent Transition Learning

author.name: Zepeng Wang, Jiangxing Wang, Chao Ma, Xiaochuan Shi, Zongqing Lu

entry.summary: PLAT studies sparse timed keyframe motion tracking, where a humanoid policy receives only sparse future keyframes with arrival times instead of dense references. Its three-stage framework uses dense goal sequences as privileged supervision during training while requiring only sparse keyframes at deployment, bridging dense motion tracking and goal-conditioned control.

entry.title: What Does Chain-of-Thought Entropy Measure? A Channel Audit of Scaffolding, Routing, and Content

author.name: Marios Papamichalis, Regina Ruane

entry.summary: This paper shows that entropy over chain-of-thought tokens conflates three distinct choices: whether to emit connective scaffolding, which connective to use, and what substantive content to continue with. It introduces an exact decomposition of entropy, KL divergence, and entropy velocity into channels via a designated scaffold vocabulary, proves raw and content conventions can disagree about which position is the larger fork, and validates across twenty-three configurations.

entry.title: Attention as a Routing Graph: Live Circuit Extraction from a Single Forward Pass

author.name: Ash Manvi, Samreena Tajreen

entry.summary: The authors propose a cheap interpretability method that treats attention as a routing graph from a single forward pass, keeping a small set of edges pointing toward the answer, then verifies these extracted circuits by ablation. On induction and IOI tasks, ablating extracted edges hurts GPT-2 and Pythia models far more than random ablations, at roughly two orders of magnitude lower cost than head-by-head patch sweeps.

entry.title: Weakly Supervised Quantum Error Mitigation

author.name: Seyed Mohamad Ali Tousi, G. N. DeSouza

entry.summary: This paper replaces expensive noiseless classical simulation labels in quantum error mitigation with sixteen cheap, individually unreliable heuristic labeling functions derived from circuit structure and hardware calibration. It reconciles their disagreements with a probabilistic label model, a weak-supervision strategy borrowed from machine learning.

entry.title: Gaze responses to false-positive computer-aided detection prompts during colonoscopy: a paired-video and real-time eye-tracking study

author.name: Te Luo, Yan Zhu, Peiyao Fu, Ruijie Yang, Xian Yang, Quanlin Li, Pinghong Zhou, Shuo Wang

entry.summary: Uses event-locked eye tracking in retrospective paired-video experiments and 42 real-time CADe-assisted colonoscopies to quantify how false-positive AI detection prompts attract and occupy endoscopists' attention. False-positive prompts drew gaze in roughly half of retrospective cases, providing evidence that CADe false alarms impose real attentional costs.

entry.title: Testing-Driven Reliability Audit of Trajectory-Based Early Outcome Prediction for LLM Agents: Target-Specific Calibration Transfer Persists Within a Single Benchmark

author.name: YanZe Cao

entry.summary: Audits a frozen dual-head early-outcome prediction pipeline on public SWE-bench Verified trajectories using leave-one-agent-out and leave-two-agents-out calibration tests. It finds that calibration transfer failures persist even within a single benchmark, concentrated in specific target agent/head combinations, undermining the expense-saving premise of early termination.

entry.title: The Architect, the Adversary, and the Judge: Closed-Loop Generation of Standards-Aligned Assessment Items at Scale

author.name: Wenhui Chen, Ziyao Lin, Jianlin Chen, Peiji Long, Chi Man Vong

entry.summary: CLAIM is a production pipeline for K-12 assessment-item generation combining a generate-then-attack protocol, bidirectional few-shot conditioning on accepted and rejected items, and a knowledge dictionary of 44,844 error-correction rules mined from evaluator feedback. Across 43,227 scored items over 755 Common Core ELA standards and ten LLMs, a 9,074-item production run achieved a 97.8% expert pass rate, and the paper critically examines what that rate certifies.

entry.title: EADC: Evaluation of Advanced and Deep-level Compliance in Large Language Models

author.name: Yan Zhang, Ruien Li, Yaoyao Peng, Wanxin Ren, Yijia Zhang, Wusheng Zhang, Guangwen Yang

entry.summary: EADC is a new evaluation framework for assessing LLM compliance with laws and regulatory frameworks, addressing limitations of static benchmarks. It targets implicit and covert compliance risks and tracks risk propagation along logical dependency chains in context-rich real-world scenarios.

entry.title: Brain-Inspired Hierarchical Modularity for General Continual Learning

author.name: Hongwei Yan, Kanglei Zhou, Qi Cheng, Weiyi Dong, Chunyan Lan, Guanglong Sun, Jun Zhou, Qian Li, Yi Zhong, Liyuan Wang

entry.summary: Identifies a hierarchical modular principle inspired by the Drosophila learning and memory system that separates conflicting experience to reduce interference while integrating compatible experience for generalization, targeting general continual learning under online, uncertain, evolving data streams rather than offline task-boundary settings. The design coordinates both functions through expert specialization.

entry.title: Passes Alone, Fails Together: Benchmarking Semantic Coordination in Parallel LLM-Agent Development

author.name: Haocheng Xia, Eugene Wu, Yongjoo Park

entry.summary: Introduces stale, a benchmark for semantic coordination failures in parallel coding agents, where patches that pass tests individually fail when merged because one agent changed an interface another relies on. Using three task tiers including 417 mined Django pull-request pairs and constructed tasks with 12 real Django helpers, it finds interference in 97% of constructed-task runs but almost none in naturally mined pairs.

entry.title: Interpretable AI plus Handheld, Portable Retinal Photographs: A Low-Cost Glaucoma Screening Solution for West Africa

author.name: Charis Y. N. Chiang, Tarela Sarimiye, Adeyinka Ashaye, Martin Buist, Michael A. Hauser, Olusola Olawoye, Micha\"el J. A. Girard

entry.summary: Develops an interpretable AI glaucoma screening framework using low-cost handheld retinal cameras, evaluated on a community-based study of 681 participants in Nigeria with per-device fine-tuned component models for vessel and optic-disc segmentation. The work compares handheld versus tabletop imaging performance toward equitable, deployable screening in West Africa.

entry.title: EMERGE: Resolution-Agnostic Point Cloud Generation with Equivariant Graph-Based Diffusion

author.name: Ilias Mitsouras, Nikolaos Chaidos, Giorgos Stamou, Athanasios Voulodimos

entry.summary: EMERGE introduces the first fully SE(3)-equivariant graph-based diffusion backbone for point cloud generation, addressing the gap that 3D generative modeling has largely ignored continuous, non-grid topologies despite their success in discriminative vision tasks. The model aims for resolution-agnostic generation, contrasting with transformer- and VAE-based approaches that do not respect 3D geometric structure.

entry.title: TTTIR: Unlocking Instance-Specific State Evolution via Test-Time Training for Image Restoration

author.name: Kaihang Zheng, Jun Li, Hang Guo, Hongyu Chi, Zimo Liu, Tao Dai, Jinpeng Wang, Yaowei Wang

entry.summary: TTTIR reformulates image restoration as instance-specific state evolution using test-time training, addressing the limitation that static globally shared parameters struggle with diverse, input-dependent degradations. The framework augments the standard self-supervised TTT inner loop with explicit guidance to transition degraded features toward clean structures, aiming to generate data-dependent operators per instance.

entry.title: Receptiveness, Not Sycophancy: Distinguishing Engagement from Deference in Language Models

author.name: Calvin Isley, Johann Gaebler, Max Lamparth, Julia Minson, Sharad Goel

entry.summary: Identifies a construct-validity problem in social sycophancy evaluations: markers of sycophancy overlap with conversational receptiveness, a construct shown to improve interactions across disagreement. Using a moral-advice dataset, the authors show responses classified as more sycophantic are also more receptive, arguing evaluations must distinguish engagement from inappropriate deference.

entry.title: GeoRVQ: Decoder-aware geometry for residual-token prediction in physiological signals

author.name: Bo Cui, Yaowen Zhang

entry.summary: GeoRVQ is a coarse-to-fine masked token model for residual-vector-quantized physiological waveforms whose training objective reflects the local response of a frozen waveform decoder, producing geometry-aware soft targets and expected-distortion losses. Across MIMIC-IV Waveform, VitalDB, and CODE-15 percent, it improves exact token accuracy, reduces decoded distance, and boosts R-peak F1 from 0.784 to 0.837. The key insight is that token errors should be weighted by decoder sensitivity rather than treated uniformly.

entry.title: Discover, Falsify, Revise: Auditing Input-Use Claims from Source Code to Predictive Contribution in Agent-Discovered Cell Models

author.name: Mengran Li, Bo Li, Chengyang Zhang, Yang Yan, Jinfeng Xu, Zhenchao Tang

entry.summary: CELLAUDIT audits whether AI-discovered virtual cell models actually use the perturbation inputs they claim to, checking whether an input can enter the computation, whether predictions depend on it, and whether that dependence improves prediction. On a paired morphology-transcriptomics benchmark (BBBC047), an agent-selected predictor achieves modest held-out correlation while overstating input use. This targets the prediction-claim gap in agentic scientific model discovery.

entry.title: PhyMo: A Physical-Field Modality for Multimodal AI4Physics

author.name: Henan Sun, Haitao Hu, Jin Liu, Jianfeng Zhang, Lujia Pan, Nuo Chen, Jia Li

entry.summary: PhyMo introduces a physical-field modality for multimodal AI-for-physics, organizing heterogeneous measurements through PDE-associated operators rather than treating physical quantities as generic numerical or text tokens. A three-stage learning procedure first pretrains a physical-field encoder before later stages. This is a step toward physics-grounded multimodal models that respect spatiotemporal constraints of governing equations.

entry.title: Safety Nudges: User-Facing Interventions for Real-Time AI Risk Awareness

author.name: Varshini Elangovan, James Wedgwood, Chhavi Yadav, William Agnew, Sauvik Das, Virginia Smith

entry.summary: Introduces Safety Nudges, a browser tool that flags potentially risky chatbot behaviors such as hallucination, sycophancy, and anthropomorphism in real time. A two-week field study with 45 frequent chatbot users found the tool useful and awareness-raising, though improved awareness alone did not reliably translate into safer user behavior.

entry.title: MolDesignBench: Evaluating LLM-based Agent for Scenario-grounded Molecular Design

author.name: Yongjun Jeong, Hanbum Ko, Ye Rin Kim, Chanhui Lee, Rodrigo Hormazabal, Jaewan Lee, Sehui Han, Sungbin Lim, Sungwoong Kim

entry.summary: MolDesignBench is a scenario-grounded benchmark of 2K generation and optimization tasks for tool-augmented LLM agents in molecular design, combining implicit requirements in design narratives with explicit property and functional constraints. It covers infeasible specifications and multi-step tool reasoning that existing benchmarks lack.

entry.title: The Recall Ceiling of LLM Recommendation Reranking

author.name: Zhaohui Wang

entry.summary: Shows that oracle evaluation protocols used for LLM-based recommendation rerankers, which guarantee the ground-truth item is in the candidate set, overestimate realistic NDCG@10 by 92-95% across three Amazon datasets. It derives a deterministic recall ceiling on closed-candidate reranker performance and finds realistic retrieval covers only 2-19% of relevant items at K=100.

entry.title: Tensor Decomposition of Transformer Key-Value Caches: Spectral Structure and Format Comparison

author.name: Rahul Krishnan, Volker Schulz

entry.summary: This paper views the transformer KV cache as a fourth-order tensor and measures singular-value spectra across attention heads, tokens, features, and layers on Mistral-7B-v0.3 and LLaMA-2-13B, comparing Tucker, CP, tensor train, and t-SVD decompositions at matched storage. It finds token and feature modes are low-rank while head and layer modes resist compression, with Tucker achieving the lowest reconstruction error at 2x-5x compression ratios.

entry.title: LOCKR: A Hidden-State Trajectory-Guided Planner for Detecting and Repairing Stable-but-Wrong Lock-In in Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Guoshenghui Zhao, Tan Yu, Weijie Zhao

entry.summary: LOCKR targets a newly identified failure mode in diffusion language models: stable-but-wrong lock-in, where an incorrect answer stabilizes early during denoising. It formulates selective repair as test-time planning guided by hidden-state trajectories, allocating extra compute and expanding targeted repair branches, since surface signals like confidence and entropy cannot distinguish correct from erroneous lock-in.

entry.title: MWE-ECL: Recoverable Long-Range Context Does Not Always Override Local Lexical Priors

author.name: Wei He, Aline Villavicencio, Rodrigo Wilkens, Zhenyun Deng

entry.summary: This paper introduces MWE-ECL, a bilingual diagnostic showing that long-context models can explicitly recover distant discourse anchors yet fail to let them override locally preferred readings of multiword expressions. Across eighteen models, failures concentrate when the no-anchor default conflicts with the anchor, challenging the assumption that recoverable context guarantees behavioral influence.

entry.title: TEMPS: Temporal Sentence Embeddings for Temporal Information Retrieval

author.name: Mourad Hassani, Julien Romero, Amel Bouzeghoub, Christian Jacquelinet

entry.summary: The paper defines Temporal Textual Similarity (TTS), a task measuring time alignment between anchored texts independent of topic, and presents TEMPS, a modular temporal branch attaching to a frozen semantic retriever that trains on this signal. It addresses the common failure of dense retrieval and RAG systems to surface temporally correct content in clinical, journalistic, and legal search.

entry.title: What Looks Like a Capability Limit in Vision-Language Models Is a Readout Limit

author.name: Alfredo F. Frontera Del Valle

entry.summary: This paper shows that benchmark answer-format conventions can masquerade as capability limits in vision-language models: Qwen3-VL-4B picks correct object locations 68.5% of the time with English word options but only 20.0% with pixel-coordinate options, well above chance. The gap persists across grid sizes and quantization settings, indicating the reported limits belong to the readout format rather than the model.

entry.title: HYDRO: Towards Non-Reversible Face De-Identification Using a High-Fidelity Hybrid Diffusion and Target-Oriented Approach

author.name: Felix Rosberg, Vitomir \v{S}truc, Cristofer Englund, Eren Erdal Aksoy, Fernando Alonso-Fernandez

entry.summary: HYDRO proposes a hybrid diffusion, target-oriented face de-identification method designed to be non-reversible, addressing the risk that generative de-identification preserves subtle identity cues that enable reconstruction attacks. It aims to balance high visual fidelity and attribute retention with robust identity removal.

entry.title: Learning Spectral Allocation: A Fractional Diffusion Framework for Adaptive Volumetric Segmentation

author.name: Yi-Hui Shen, Tie-Qiang Li

entry.summary: FHEAT derives a two-parameter operator family from the DCT solution of a fractional heat equation for 3D medical segmentation, letting optimization decide per-stage spectral mixing; a reparametrization via semigroup time enables exact composition across same-resolution stages. The identity limit at zero diffusion lets each layer learn whether global mixing is needed.

entry.title: Groundbench: Multi-Resolution Polygon Grounding Exposes the Geometry Gap in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zhonghan Bian, Zhenran Wang, Jinsong Li, Zhangyang Qi

entry.summary: GroundingBench re-targets 1,500 image-expression-referent grounding triples from bounding boxes to exact-N polygons at five vertex budgets, using a fixed-denominator harness that separately audits filled-region IoU and legal-polygon completion. Results show frontier configurations reach 88.2 box IoU but drop sharply for direct polygon prediction, exposing a geometry gap in vision-language models. This provides a sharper diagnostic than RefCOCO-style box grounding.

entry.title: VIVAS: Vitalizing Visual Perception in VLM Pre-training via Vision-language Unified Autoregressive Supervision

author.name: Zhehan Kan, Yubo Zhu, Xinghua Jiang, Zhixiang Wei, Shifeng Liu, Wei Tong, Sheng Zhong, Qingmin Liao, Wenming Yang, Xin Li, Yinsong Liu, Deqiang Jiang, Xing Sun

entry.summary: VIVAS is a companion work to UVU arguing that VLM fine-grained perception is limited by text-dominant pre-training optimization, and that overcoming this requires a unified token space for stable training plus modality-aligned dense visual supervision. It applies unified autoregressive visual supervision during pre-training to strengthen perceptual representations. This reinforces the case for visually-grounded pre-training objectives in multimodal models.

entry.title: VLMs Can Describe, But Not Measure: Object-Centric Scene Understanding for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Enrico Saccon, Tommaso Faraci, I\~{n}igo De La Ossa Zarzuelo, Luigi Palopoli, Marco Roveri, Matteo Saveriano

entry.summary: Shows empirically that vision-language models provide good semantic descriptions but unreliable geometric measurements, and proposes a modular framework that segments RGB-D scenes into object regions, annotates them with a VLM, and grounds them with depth to build a task-independent object-centric representation. Across 151 tabletop scenes, the decomposition preserves semantic performance while substantially improving localization and depth accuracy.

entry.title: Norm2Tex: Augmenting Visuo-Tactile Simulations with Texture

author.name: Seongjin Bien, D\'ebora Oliveira Makowski, Roberto Calandra, Florian Walter, Wolfram Burgard

entry.summary: Norm2Tex is a plug-in method that injects high-frequency surface texture into vision-based tactile simulators by modifying target-object depth maps with normal-map textures before rendering, reducing the sim-to-real gap in tactile data. The authors evaluate sim-to-real transfer, addressing the domain shift caused by simulators that capture only coarse contact geometry.

entry.title: CODA: Depth-Aligned Scene Completion and Object Decomposition from a Single RGB-D Image

author.name: Dongwon Son, Junhyek Han, Yoontae Cho, Minseok Lee, Hong-seok Choi, Jiwook Choi, Hyungjin Kim, Beomjoon Kim

entry.summary: CODA is a generative model that reconstructs complete scene geometry from a single unsegmented RGB-D image and then decomposes the surface into environment and movable objects, using depth alignment to keep generated geometry consistent with the observed partial point cloud. It avoids failure modes of detect-then-reconstruct pipelines in cluttered scenes, such as missed objects and fused or overlapping meshes.

entry.title: MotionForge: A Data Generation Pipeline and Large-Scale Benchmark for Long-Horizon Manipulation of Dynamic Objects with Domain Shifts

author.name: Mohan Liu, Dengchen Mei, Haotian Xian, Ruyang Han, Jiayi Sun, Xuanyu Chen, Haitian Zhang, Luxi Li, Kaimin Mao, Lin Wang

entry.summary: MotionForge is a large-scale simulation benchmark and data-generation pipeline for dynamic object manipulation that jointly evaluates long-horizon interaction and robustness under domain shifts, with model-agnostic real-time execution protocols. It addresses the gap left by existing benchmarks that focus on static scenes or short-horizon reactive tasks.

entry.title: Dr-LiSA: Direct Radar-Lidar Scan Alignment for $SE(3)$ Localization

author.name: Alex Zhang, Daniil Lisus, Cedric Le Gentil, Timothy D. Barfoot

entry.summary: Introduces Dr-LiSA, the first direct method for localizing 2D spinning radar intensity measurements in SE(3) against 3D lidar maps, combining radar's weather robustness with lidar's map fidelity. It bridges the substantial sensing-modality gap between radar and lidar, extending prior radar-lidar localization beyond planar SE(2) and approaching lidar-lidar accuracy.

entry.title: SuperPCA: subspace analysis and an efficient algorithm for high-dimensional PCA

author.name: Irina-Beatrice Haas, Maike Meier, Yuji Nakatsukasa, Taejun Park

entry.summary: The authors show that in the spiked covariance model, the subspace spanned by several leading sample eigenvectors contains substantial information about the true signals well before individual eigenvectors converge, and they exploit this to build a more efficient high-dimensional PCA algorithm. This insight enables earlier and more reliable signal estimation in high-dimensional settings.

entry.title: DTOC: Dynamic Tool Output Compression for Adaptive Context Management in AI Agents

author.name: Abhay Chaturvedi, Shreya Bhattacharya, Rashmika Gopalkrishnan, Peter van der Putten

entry.summary: DTOC is a context-management framework for LLM agents that models context updates as explicit, reversible operations: full tool outputs are retained in external memory while compact placeholders occupy the active context, enabling selective reconstruction. Integrated into a ReAct-style agent, it avoids the information loss and hallucination risks of truncation, aging, and lossy summarization.

entry.title: AIBuildAI-2.5: Efficient Autonomous AI Model Development Through LLM-Guided Tree Search

author.name: Peijia Qin, Ruiyi Zhang, Qi Cao, Han Guo, Li Zhang, Pengtao Xie

entry.summary: Presents an autonomous agent that builds AI models by framing the task as code search over a program tree, addressing three efficiency weaknesses of existing LLM-guided tree-search agents such as reliance on few, noisy executed rewards for node ranking. The system approaches experienced-AI-engineer capability on realistic benchmarks with improved efficiency.

entry.title: Dynamic Deep Prompt Optimization for Defending Against Jailbreak Attacks on LLMs

author.name: Doniyorkhon Obidov, Honggang Yu, Xiaolong Guo, Kaichen Yang

entry.summary: DDPO is proposed as the first jailbreak defense based on deep prompt optimization: it uses the target LLM's own intermediate layers as feature extractors to dynamically generate defensive embeddings, adapting to diverse and evolving attacks unlike static prefix/suffix defenses. The approach aims to avoid the cost and catastrophic forgetting of safety fine-tuning while providing adaptive protection.

entry.title: TriWorldBench: A Tri-View Consistency Perspective on Embodied World Models

author.name: Xuanyi Liu, Haofeng Wang, Ruiqi Li, Danni Yu, Rui Wan, Ruixu Zhang, Siyu Tao, Xue Yang, Shaofeng Zhang, Zicheng Zhang, Jiaqi Zhang, Siwei Ma

entry.summary: Presents a benchmark for evaluating embodied world models using synchronized head, left-wrist, and right-wrist camera videos across 500 episodes of 50 bimanual manipulation tasks, with 19 metrics covering tri-view consistency, physical and 3D coherence, and temporal quality. It enables assessment of whether multiple views describe the same action and object state.

entry.title: From Alignment to Access Control: A Framework for GenAI Policy Enforcement

author.name: Nathalie Baracaldo

entry.summary: This position-style paper surveys how policy means different things across GenAI security, safety, and alignment practices, leading to fragmented and inadequate compliance solutions. The author proposes a unifying framework for policy definition and enforcement spanning alignment, safety, and access control for LLM applications and agents.

entry.title: ChipMEM: Verification-Grounded Memory for EDA Agents

author.name: Abdulrahman AlRabah, Joshua Mabry, Dilek Hakkani-T\"ur, Abdussalam Alawini, Hamid Shojaei, Kartik Hegde, Sandesh Adhikary

entry.summary: ChipMEM adds a verification-grounded memory layer for LLM-based EDA agents that generate and revise RTL designs, combining cross-task procedural memory distilled from verification feedback with within-trajectory statistical guidance. It addresses the problem that prior methods are evaluated on the same tasks that produced their experience, rewarding task-specific revision over transferable knowledge. This is a step toward reusable agentic skills in hardware design.

entry.title: DCRL: Decoupling and Coupling Reinforcement Learning via Policy-Reward Manifold Alignment

author.name: Henan Sun, Zehua Li, Haitao Hu, Qifan Zhang, Jianfeng Zhang, Nuo Chen, Jia Li

entry.summary: DCRL revisits RL for LLM reasoning from a geometric perspective, modeling reasoning as a coupled manifold of logical deduction, evaluation, and representation sub-manifolds, and interprets generation and reward estimation as decoupling processes. The framework aims to mitigate unstable optimization and reward hacking found in rule-based and reward-model-based systems. A companion paper by overlapping authors (PhyMo) suggests a shared research program.

entry.title: FLEET: From Logits Entropy to Enhanced Trajectories in Text Generation

author.name: Oleksii Streltsov, Oleksandra Vitko

entry.summary: FLEET adds a memory mechanism to LLM sampling: generations are represented as sparse trajectories through high-entropy token states, from which per-token utility scores are inferred to avoid the semantically duplicate answers that accumulate under temperature sampling. This directly targets the diminishing returns of best-of-N style aggregation used widely in LLM inference.

entry.title: Global tree forecasters collapse at the hierarchical aggregate: a five-panel failure characterization

author.name: Md Rezwanul Islam, Wael Mohammed

entry.summary: Documents and characterizes a previously undocumented failure of global gradient-boosted tree forecasters: asked for a hierarchical aggregate far outside training range, tree models predict a constant and under-predict totals by 30-50x in production and up to 496x on an M5 reconstruction. The paper shows the known out-of-range behavior of trees surfaces acutely at aggregates and that per-series scaling largely cures it.

entry.title: WhatWorkedBench: Benchmarking Experimental Understanding in AI Agents

author.name: Jingjie Ning, Xueqi Li, Yibo Kong, Dongting Li

entry.summary: WhatWorkedBench measures whether AI research agents understand how experimental component changes affect outcomes: agents inspect code, select measurements, and submit a response surface predicting scores for every configuration. Reference effects come from exhaustive CPU execution across 36 tasks, 30 data sources, and 8 workflow types, with over 4200 numerical-control records.

entry.title: Non-Commutative State Tracking with Input-Dependent Low-Rank Updates in Mamba-3

author.name: Hiroki Fujii, Masaki Yamakita

entry.summary: The authors extend Mamba-3's diagonal state transition with an input-dependent low-rank reflection term enabling non-commutative state tracking where operation order matters, while preserving the model's discretization, RoPE, and readout. They adapt chunkwise parallel computation for training and evaluate on group word problems and shell game tasks.

entry.title: Distilling Sequential Computation in Transformer Language Models

author.name: Zixuan Lan, Jessica Yang, Yanhong Li, Karen Livescu, Jiawei Zhou

entry.summary: The paper introduces a method to compress predictable token spans into single surrogate embeddings computed on the fly by a lightweight merge module, letting pretrained transformers operate on compressed inputs without architectural changes or retraining. This distills sequential computation and reduces the cost of growing contexts.

entry.title: Damnatio Memoriae: Adversarially and Selectively Forgetting Identities in the Embedding Space of Face Recognition Models

author.name: \"Unsal \"Ozt\"urk, Vedrana Krivoku\'ca Hahn, Sushil Bhattacharjee, S\'ebastien Marcel

entry.summary: The paper introduces open-set adversarial forgetting: modifying a face recognition model's embedding space so chosen identities become unlinkable across occasions while the model keeps serving the rest of the population. Three loss functions disperse or map target embeddings toward near-orthogonal targets, addressing a limitation of delete-and-retrain approaches.

entry.title: Gender Bias in Vision-Language In-Context Learning

author.name: Tong Xiang, Noa Garcia, Yuta Nakashima

entry.summary: Systematically investigates how gendered in-context demonstrations influence bias in large vision-language models through VL-BICLE, spanning six ICL settings, three tasks, and six LVLMs. Finds that gendered demonstrations act as a directional force via a cross-gender mechanism that disproportionately degrades performance on the opposite gender, with effects in captioning and pronoun prediction but not VQA.

entry.title: LiAM-SAM: Lifecycle-Aware Memory for Robust SAM2-Based MOT

author.name: Gr\'egoire Francisco, Alessandro D'Amico, Samuele Costantini, Gianpiero Francesca, Lorenzo Garattoni

entry.summary: LiAM-SAM reframes detector-prompted SAM2 multi-object tracking as a lifecycle memory integrity problem, adding targeted mechanisms for three failure modes: erroneous track initiation, memory drift during close interactions, and unreliable re-identification after long occlusions. This addresses error accumulation that destabilizes long-horizon tracking in crowded scenes. Extending foundation video models with structured memory is a broadly relevant theme.

entry.title: Bend the Clock: Predicting Ahead to Beat Latency in Event-Based Object Detection

author.name: Biswadeep Sen, Benoit R. Cottereau, Nicolas Cuperlier, Terence Sim

entry.summary: The paper studies the observation-availability mismatch in event-based multi-object detection, showing that state-of-the-art event detectors degrade substantially when evaluated at prediction availability time rather than observation time. The proposed method predicts ahead to compensate for detection latency, countering staleness in low-latency robotic perception. This reframes evaluation methodology and improves practical usefulness for high-speed robotics.

entry.title: Relative Contact Velocity-Controlled Hand-Object Mechanism for Dexterous Tool Manipulation

author.name: Sunyu Wang, Jean Oh, Nancy S. Pollard

entry.summary: The paper models the hand and tool as a unified hand-object mechanism whose motions are expressed via a common set of Cartesian-space relative contact velocities, independent of the hand's kinematics and geometry, enabling multi-finger hands to perform the full tool manipulation process from pickup to wielding. Sub-assemblies are defined through relative contact velocity and force constraints inspired by human tool use.

entry.title: Beyond Reconstruction Error: Analytical and Data-Driven Action Tokenization for Autoregressive Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Yuxin Yang, Gaohan He, Changxue Guan, Hangming Liu

entry.summary: This study asks which properties of discrete action tokenizations actually matter for closed-loop control in autoregressive VLA models, comparing fixed analytical, linear, and nonlinear representations under a unified interface. Across rate-distortion analysis, sequence-modeling diagnostics, and 3,500 LIBERO rollouts, representation rankings change with the criterion; PCA lowers reconstruction error but yields less predictable token sequences and lower task success.

entry.title: Statistical Gains from Looped Estimation under Parameter Budgets

author.name: Xinyu Tian, Xiaotong Shen

entry.summary: The paper analyzes looped estimators that repeatedly apply a single operator with shared (tied) parameters, comparing their statistical accuracy against untied counterparts with separate parameters per iteration. For general likelihood models, it derives Hellinger risk upper bounds and minimax lower bounds that expose a parameter-iteration-accuracy tradeoff, showing repeated computation can substitute for extra parameters.

entry.title: Rollout Efficiency in Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning Large Language Models: A Taxonomy and Future Directions

author.name: Niloofar Gholipour, Marcos Assuncao, Gursimran Singh, Timothy Yu, Rajkumar Buyya, Julien Gascon-Samson, Zhenan Fan, Yong Zhang, Xiaojie Xu, Yaqiang Yao, Xiaolong Bai

entry.summary: This survey systematizes research on rollout efficiency for reasoning-oriented RL fine-tuning of LLMs, where trajectory generation dominates training cost. It classifies approaches along mechanism and bottleneck dimensions, analyzes how technique families address distinct sources of rollout inefficiency, and outlines open directions while maintaining data freshness, consistency, and statistical validity.

entry.title: Selection-Invariant Communication Compilers for Privacy-Aware Multi-Agent LLM Workflows

author.name: Jinghan Xu, Longze Fan, Zeyuan Wang, Xinjin Li, Hankai Liu

entry.summary: The paper identifies selection-channel leakage in multi-agent LLM workflows: even after authorization, a private-state-aware choice among semantically equivalent message realizations can leak information. It proposes selection-invariant communication compilers that constrain the post-authorization representation kernel, with a proven compositional guarantee combining authorization, publication, and invariant layers.

entry.title: Type-Safe Is Not Error-Free: A Constrained Decision Head Follows the Option Name, Not the Rubric Bound to It

author.name: Yu Sun, Junhao Xu

entry.summary: The paper studies Jev and two Jev-like open-weight typed decision models, showing that schema-constrained outputs do not guarantee semantic correctness. By swapping which option name is bound to each rubric while holding everything else fixed, the authors demonstrate on 1200 workflow decisions that models follow option names rather than their bound rubrics.

entry.title: Magnitude Profile Pruning: Calibration-Free Structured Attention Head Removal for Transformer Compression

author.name: Kasun Dewage, Marianna Pensky, Heranga K. Rathnasekara, Suranadi De Silva

entry.summary: Magnitude Profile (MP) scoring is a training-free, calibration-free criterion for structured attention head pruning that identifies dispensable heads via statistical outlier detection on weight row norms, preserving outlier heads that carry disproportionate representational capacity. This avoids the calibration data, gradients, and Hessian estimation required by existing head-importance methods, and an MP-G variant extends the approach to grouped settings.

entry.title: Metrics Failure in LLM-Based Code Vulnerability Repair: An Empirical Study and a Change-Aware Screen

author.name: Om Nepal, Sushant Aryal, Oluseyi Olukola, Nick Rahimi

entry.summary: The authors show compile rate is an unreliable progress metric for LLM-based C/C++ vulnerability repair: across 203 Big-Vul functions and three small code LLMs, compile rate barely responds to interventions that improve code, and about 64% of compile failures stem from harness and dataset artifacts rather than model quality. They propose a change-aware screening metric as a better alternative.

entry.title: Full-Covariance Smoothing of Bayesian Neural Networks for Online Adaptation

author.name: Oren Wright, Haoming Jing, Qiaoan Shen, Koichiro Niinuma, Yorie Nakahira, Jos\'e M. F. Moura

entry.summary: The authors treat neural network layers as time steps of a state-space model, turning Bayesian training into a smoothing problem, and introduce a cross-covariance identity enabling full-covariance propagation where prior methods were restricted to diagonal covariances. A backward Rauch-Tung-Striebel pass updates weight posteriors in closed form, enabling single-pass, uncertainty-aware online adaptation without gradient iterations or replay. This is relevant to data-efficient continual learning.

entry.title: NGN: Learning Neural Network Size as a Differentiable Count

author.name: Lixing Li

entry.summary: The Neurogenesis Network (NGN) is a differentiable parameterization in which a learnable boundary selects an active prefix of ordered structural components, letting model size emerge during training rather than being fixed beforehand. Deployed models simply discard components beyond the learned boundary. Experiments cover boundary convergence, deployed prefix performance, and comparisons with fixed-size models and other capacity-learning approaches.

entry.title: VCMM: Variance-Calibrated Momentum for Multimodal Learning

author.name: Zhongjing Gu, Chenyang Huang, Yufa Feng, Chong He, Qinxu Ding, Yiming Cui

entry.summary: VCMM tackles modality imbalance in multimodal joint training by adapting gradient memory in momentum-based optimizers to modality-specific gradient dynamics, estimating minibatch noise variance and calibrating momentum accordingly. This addresses the gap that prior modality-balancing methods modulate only the current update while momentum optimizers also carry accumulated gradient history. It is an optimizer-level fix for a persistent multimodal training pathology.

entry.title: Limiting-Kernel Q($\lambda$): Bridging Short and Long Horizons

author.name: Tolga Ok, Arman Sharifi Kolarijani, Peyman Mohajerin Esfahani, Mohamad Amin Sharifi Kolarijani

entry.summary: Introduces LKQL, an off-policy value estimator for RL that combines n-step truncation with a long-horizon approximation based on limiting kernels of transition dynamics, bridging short-horizon efficiency with long-horizon accuracy. The goal is to improve policy evaluation accuracy without the prohibitive memory and compute of global transition-structure methods in large or continuous state spaces.

entry.title: Experts Rise Where LLMs Disagree: Using Cross-Model Disagreement to Target Expert Effort in LLM Codebook Revision for Large-Scale Annotation

author.name: Zeyu He, Zhuqian Zhou, Kirk Vanacore, Rene F. Kizilcec, Ting-Hao 'Kenneth' Huang

entry.summary: Explores using cross-LLM disagreement to identify cases needing expert attention when revising annotation codebooks at scale, comparing three expert feedback modes: verifying LLM revisions, answering disagreement questions, and labeling with rationales. Experiments on thousands of tutoring transcripts inform how to make large-scale AI-assisted annotation efficient.

entry.title: Beyond the Illusion of Power: Calibrating Quasi-Experiments in Observational IS

author.name: Spandan Ghose Chowdhury

entry.summary: A large Monte Carlo study (9837 parameter conditions, ~9.8 million datasets) decomposes the planned-versus-achieved power gap in quasi-experimental designs like DiD and IV used in information systems research. It shows serial correlation is recoverable by AR(1)-aware calculators, but attrition, staggered adoption bias, and parallel-trends pretesting distort power in ways standard calculators miss.

entry.title: COMED: The Missing Middle Between Routing and Collaboration in Multi-LLM Inference

author.name: Norah Alballa, Wenxuan Zhang, Salma Kharrat, Fares Fourati, Zafar Ayyub Qazi, Mohamed Elhoseiny, Marco Canini

entry.summary: COMED is a post-anchor controller for selective cross-model LLM collaboration, showing that collaboration is non-monotonic since peers can recover unsolvable failures but also corrupt initially correct answers. Using anchor self-consistency, router margin, and a lightweight peer probe, it accepts confident answers and escalates only when collaboration is likely to help, positioning itself between pure routing and dense collaboration.

entry.title: LEGO: Synergizing Expert GraphRAG and Expert Chain-of-Thought for Legal Reasoning

author.name: Qingjing Chen, Junkai Zhang, Shaochun Wang, Jiahao Ding, Siyuan Zheng, Yukun Yan, Zhi Zheng, Antonino Rotolo, Yun Liu, Weixing Shen

entry.summary: LEGO couples an expert-annotated civil code graph encoding normative legal relations with expert Chain-of-Thought prompting to structure legal reasoning in LLM pipelines. It targets two weaknesses: similarity-only GraphRAG and rationales that ignore the normative structure of legal argument.

entry.title: Adversarial Attacks and Identity Leakage in De-Identification Systems: An Empirical Study

author.name: Felix Rosberg, Cristofer Englund, Eren Erdal Aksoy, Fernando Alonso-Fernandez

entry.summary: This empirical study shows that adversarial attacks on identity encoders transfer from surrogate models like CosFace to system models like ArcFace, causing identity leakage in face de-identification frameworks. The authors propose mitigations including fine-tuning on adversarial examples for weather-style distortions and low-pass filtering against adversarial noise.

entry.title: GaussPDE: Graph-Based Partial Differential Equation-Driven Rendering for 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Haoyuan Yue, Fengyuan Ye, Ziyin Li

entry.summary: GaussPDE injects PDE dynamics into pretrained 3D Gaussian splatting scenes without mesh extraction or retraining, using camera-aware regularization during reconstruction and an active Gaussian graph with covariance- and appearance-aware conductance for mass-weighted graph Laplacian PDE evolution directly on primitives.

entry.title: Information Capacity of Generative Video Compression: Quantifying the Rate-Compute Exchange at Identical Quality

author.name: Cheng Yuan, Jiawei Shao, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: Models reconstruction quality in generative video compression as a two-factor power law in transmitted data rate and decoder compute, fitting measured results within 3% error, and defines an information capacity metric quantifying how much bandwidth a unit of decoder compute can replace. Grounded in the AI Flow framework of distributing intelligence across devices, edge, and cloud.

entry.title: BronchoTop: Bronchoscopy Navigation via RGB-Only Topological Localization

author.name: Clara Tomasini, Ana Cristina Murillo, Luis Riazuelo

entry.summary: BronchoTop is a real-time, RGB-only framework for topological bronchoscope localization that removes the need for patient-specific CT scans or external sensors. It estimates scope position relative to a generic airway model through lumen detection and tracking, lumen-branch association, and probabilistic localization modules. This reduces cost, setup time, and radiation exposure in a clinically meaningful procedure.

entry.title: VGM-VS: Rethinking Visual Geometry Model for High-Precision Visual Servoing

author.name: Yimin Pan, Sen Wang, You Zhou, Jianfeng Gao, Pengbo Sun, Ahmed M. Naguib, Zoltan-Csaba Marton

entry.summary: Presents VGM-VS, which uses a pretrained feed-forward visual geometry model inside a closed-loop pose-based visual servoing scheme, estimating relative camera pose between current and target views and applying it iteratively as a pose increment. A metric-scale estimation module resolves the scale ambiguity inherent to such models, with reliability under occlusion, weak texture, and small target size.

entry.title: REDACT: Robust Perceptive Locomotion under Unseen Visual Corruption

author.name: Natapat Kirdwichai, Tobias Driskell-Poole, Andrei Sontea, Jadu Dash, Muhammad Burhan Hafez, Danesh Tarapore

entry.summary: REDACT is a teacher-student framework for depth-conditioned legged locomotion that stays robust under visual corruptions unseen during training, combining an improved visual encoder, persistent feature masking, and a consensus-gating algorithm. It addresses the out-of-distribution failure modes of perceptive locomotion policies caused by occlusion, noise, and distractors.

entry.title: PhyVisGen: Physically and Visually High-Fidelity Robotic Manipulation Data Generation

author.name: Yu Zheng, Qiyu Feng, Yixin Wu, Baoquan Yang, Yixuan Zhou, Bingyang Hu, Kemeng Huang, Guansheng Yang, Hesheng Wang

entry.summary: PhyVisGen is a framework for scalable generation of manipulation training data combining high-fidelity physics via an Incremental Potential Contact-based arm-gripper coupling method for soft contact, with visual fidelity from real-scene reconstruction and real-time path-tracing. It targets the sim-to-real transfer bottleneck for visuomotor policies, especially with soft grippers.

entry.title: The Cartesian Hand: In-Hand Manipulation with All-Linear Fingers

author.name: Boxi Xia, Bokuan Li, Ryan Shin, Zijiang Yang, Jiaxun Liu, Boyuan Chen

entry.summary: The Cartesian Hand is a 7-DoF end-effector that uses only linear finger motion to combine independent grasping and relative in-hand manipulation, positioned between complex dexterous hands and simple parallel grippers. It targets manipulation of articulated objects like threaded containers and tools that normally require a second gripper or coordinated arm motion.

entry.title: Learning Air-Ground Motion Control with Temporal Mode Switching and Cross-Terrain Tracking

author.name: Ruitian Pang, Mingrui Li, Xuanting Liu, Tiancheng Lai, Juncheng Chen, Xiangyu Li, Ruibin Zhang, Qishao Wang, Jin Yu, Haiyin Piao, Fei Gao, Chao Xu, Yanjun Cao

entry.summary: This paper presents a learning-based control framework for passive-wheeled terrestrial-aerial bimodal vehicles (TABVs), combining a learned mode selector that uses ToF sensor history for autonomous air-ground switching with a reinforcement learning policy for cross-terrain trajectory tracking. It targets real-world deployment under limited onboard perception.

entry.title: MATES: Learning Multi-Agent Interactions by Transforming Observations for Frozen Single-Agent Policies

author.name: Elie Abboud, Oren Gal

entry.summary: MATES is an input-side adaptation framework for multi-agent reinforcement learning that learns a small adapter mapping multi-agent observations into the format expected by a frozen single-agent policy, avoiding training decentralized policies from scratch. This lets agents reuse solo-task competence learned in isolation while inducing coordinated behavior via observation transformation.

entry.title: When LLM Agents Fail to Read the Room: ReAdapt for Relational Social Reasoning

author.name: Jianzhe Lin, Xiaolin Li, Yunda Liu, Fei Wang, Jubin Chheda

entry.summary: This paper identifies a failure mode where LLM agents base social decisions on content salience rather than latent relational structure like tie strength and reciprocity. The authors formalize the problem with a benchmark of 500 synthetic social worlds yielding 1,000 queries over reaction selection and warm introductions, and propose ReAdapt to explicitly model how new relational evidence should revise social hypotheses.

entry.title: LingLan: An Advancing Traditional Chinese Medicine Diagnosis LLM with Multimodal Data

author.name: Zheng Chen, Zhicheng Du, Haoxuan Li, Yingshan Liang, Peiwu Qin

entry.summary: Proposes a Unification Framework for Multimodal Data that converts tongue and pulse images into structured clinical descriptions to digitize the I-AOI-P diagnostic process of TCM, then trains LingLan-14B, a TCM-specific language model on this structured multimodal record. It addresses the slow AI integration into TCM caused by subjective, holistic diagnostics.

entry.title: AgenticSizing: A Large Language Model-based Multi-Agent Framework for Analog Circuit Sizing

author.name: Yijia Hao, Pratibha Verma, Dongxu Guo, Cristian Sestito, Michael O'Boyle, Christos-Savvas Bouganis, Themis Prodromakis

entry.summary: AgenticSizing is a multi-agent LLM framework for analog circuit sizing that analyzes circuit topology, decomposes netlists into functional blocks, and reuses extracted design knowledge, addressing the lack of topology understanding in prior LLM-based sizing methods. It targets complex circuits beyond the simple analog building blocks used in earlier evaluations.

entry.title: VACS: Value-Aligned Compositional Shielding for Multi-Agent Reasoning

author.name: Yiyao Zhang, Diksha Goel, Hussain Ahmad, Shixun Huang, Jun Shen

entry.summary: VACS is a four-layer framework for safe multi-agent reasoning that infers each agent's implicit value priorities (via Bradley-Terry modeling and deep MaxEnt IRL), encodes compositional formal safety guarantees, and performs value-aware conflict resolution with faithful explanations. It targets high-stakes domains where heterogeneous agent values cause conflicting recommendations.

entry.title: Decoupling Is Not Identification: Supervised Evidential Learning in Next-Token Prediction

author.name: Ge Wang

entry.summary: This paper proposes an Evidential Next-Token Prediction (ENTOP) framework auditing whether Dirichlet-head concentration parameters in language models carry meaningful lexical support signals. Using exact 8-gram counts on character-level Moby-Dick as reproducible ground truth, it finds implicit evidential training carries essentially no count signal (Spearman rho near zero) while explicit supervision generalizes, showing decoupling does not equal identification.
