entry.summary: RewardVerse introduces a rubric-based video reward framework for RL optimization of video generation models, inserting a dynamic rubric as an intermediate representation between evaluation query and scorer. This addresses scalar drift, where unconstrained scalar scoring collapses or shifts scales across prompts, making rewards unreliable for policy optimization.

entry.title: Algebraic Consistency Alone Does Not Certify Temporal Structure in Latent Action Models

author.name: Di Wen, Ruodi Zhang, Kailun Yang, Kunyu Peng

entry.summary: The paper challenges a claimed label-free certificate in latent action model research, showing that additive composition and antisymmetric reversal properties of the transition code hold trivially for any frame pairing under reconstruction, and thus cannot demonstrate genuine temporal structure. Across five source domains, an unconstrained trained counterpart already achieves 83-97% of the reported error reduction, indicating the metric conflates encoding of nuisance state or coordinate conventions with temporal understanding.

entry.title: OnlineWM: Causality-Aware Active Online Learning for Effective World Modeling

author.name: Yikun Miao, Fangqi Zhu, Quanxin Shou, Xiaoyi Pang, Zhengyang Yan, Junhao Li, Haodong Wang, Zicong Hong, Song Guo

entry.summary: OnlineWM improves generative world models by addressing two failure modes: distribution misalignment from static offline data collection, and spurious correlations encouraged by purely observational discrepancy objectives. It introduces a causality-aware active online learning pipeline that targets unreliable long-tail dynamics and encourages capturing true action-effect causality.

entry.title: Look Where It Counts: A Free, Label-Free Visual Evidence Signal for Fine-Grained Vision-Language Reasoning

author.name: Santi Ram Tiwari, Nihal Naik, Devbrat Pandey, Nishant Sinha

entry.summary: The paper formalizes the contrastive evidence gap: the per-token log-likelihood ratio a multimodal model assigns to its output when conditioned on a question-relevant versus irrelevant image region, showing this label-free signal can substitute for expensive SFT, RLVR, or distillation on fine-grained visual questions. It studies the signal across Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Qwen3-VL-8B, and Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B on V*Bench, where high-resolution evidence is lost to downsampling.

entry.title: Preoperative Prediction of Microvascular Invasion in Hepatocellular Carcinoma by Integrating Multimodal Ultrasound and Clinical Data: A Multicenter Study

author.name: Jun Cheng, Yuanyuan Kong, Qing Huang, Xiaotong Tan, Licong Dong, Yulong Han, Wufeng Xue, Ruobing Huang, Dong Ni, Qi Yang, Jie Yu, Ping Liang

entry.summary: This multicenter clinical study develops and validates a model predicting microvascular invasion in hepatocellular carcinoma preoperatively by fusing B-mode ultrasound, color Doppler, contrast-enhanced ultrasound, and clinical data from 489 patients across eight centers with independent external validation. MVI currently requires postoperative histopathology, so reliable preoperative prediction could directly affect surgical planning and prognosis. Rigorous design with external validation strengthens clinical credibility.

entry.title: Beyond Uniform Subspaces: Spectrum-Aware and Depth-Adaptive Fusion for Multi-Task Model Merging

author.name: Ruxi Gu, Zilei Wang, Wei Wang

entry.summary: SADA-Merging improves data-free multi-task model merging by accounting for task-specific subspace capacity, spectral transformation tolerance, and depth-dependent distortion introduced by subspace projection. The framework allocates subspace capacity by spectral complexity and adapts spectral preservation across layers, addressing a uniform-treatment limitation of prior subspace methods.

entry.title: ZVeC: A Zero-Shot Framework for Instance-Level Vehicle Extraction and Generative Point Cloud Completion

author.name: Daisy Li, Kyle Gao, Quanyun Wu, Boris Jutzi, John S. Zelek, Jonathan Li

entry.summary: ZVeC reformulates LiDAR scene-level point cloud completion as compositional object-level reconstruction, decomposing cluttered underground scenes into vehicle instances completed independently via a depth- and 3D Gaussian-conditioned diffusion model. The zero-shot design removes the need for scenario-specific supervised training, addressing severe geometric incompleteness from occlusions.

entry.title: GameHorizon Suite: Multi-Horizon Data and Evaluation in Gameplay

author.name: Yiran Wang, Xingyilang Yin, Junfu Pu, Guangzhi Wang, Kaifeng Li, Mingyu Ouyang, Huiqiang Sun, Lingen Li, Cheng Cheng, Wangbo Yu, Honghao Chen, Xiaodong Cun, Chi-Man Pun, Zhiguo Cao, Ying Shan

entry.summary: GameHorizon is a unified data and evaluation suite measuring gameplay AI capabilities across temporal horizons, comprising an automated multi-horizon instruction annotation pipeline, a constructed dataset, and evaluation covering visual understanding, instruction decomposition, planning, and action control. It addresses narrow game coverage, missing language instructions, and high-variance online rollouts in prior benchmarks.

entry.title: Omni2Web: Benchmarking Audiovisual Website Development

author.name: Minghao Han, Zhenghao Xing, Xize Cheng, Yuxuan Wang, Junming Lin, Ling Wang, Yinsong Yan, Yunfei Chu, Qize Yang, Jin Xu

entry.summary: Introduces Omni2Web, a bilingual benchmark of 918 instances and 13,907 edit steps for webpage editing from screen-recorded requests containing weak deictic expressions, with three tracks covering direct editing, instruction recovery, and instruction utility. Evaluating 17 open- and closed-source models reveals best Edit Fidelity scores around 51, indicating substantial headroom.

entry.title: Unsupervised Brain Anomaly Detection as a Bayesian Inverse Problem with Diffusion Prior

author.name: Hugues Roy, Reuben Dorent, Ninon Burgos

entry.summary: The paper reformulates unsupervised brain anomaly detection as a Bayesian inverse problem under a diffusion prior, introducing a latent spatial anomaly mask that models consistency between a test image and a pseudo-healthy reconstruction. This replaces the heuristic noise schedules and synthetic corruptions used in prior diffusion-based UAD methods with a principled probabilistic formulation. A theoretically cleaner approach to annotation-free medical anomaly localization.

entry.title: REDACT: Robust Perceptive Locomotion under Unseen Visual Corruption

author.name: Natapat Kirdwichai, Tobias Driskell-Poole, Andrei Sontea, Jadu Dash, Muhammad Burhan Hafez, Danesh Tarapore

entry.summary: REDACT is a teacher-student framework for depth-conditioned quadruped/legged locomotion that remains stable under visual corruptions unseen during training. It combines an improved visual encoder, persistent feature masking, and a consensus-gating algorithm to retain evidence despite occlusion, noise, and invalid depth returns.

entry.title: Contact-Stable Deformable Tissue Simulation Using Implicit Integration and Live-Pose Grasp Constraints for Laparoscopic Surgery Robot Policy Evaluation

author.name: Juahn Oh, Dongho Yee, Jinseok Lee, Jiyul Lee, Yechan Seo, Seong Jeong, Minsung Kim, Seonho Shim, Younghoon Noh, Hyuk Choi, Youngbin Kong, Hyoun-Joong Kon

entry.summary: A surgical simulation pipeline reconstructs deformable tissue from fixed-view RGB-D recordings of the surgical field, composites out instruments, and produces stable tetrahedralized volumes (13 organs, ~146k tetrahedra, no inverted elements) placed in a bimanual cell with two Franka FR3 arms operating through trocars. Core contributions are the implicit integration and live-pose grasp constraint design enabling stable grasping and lifting.

entry.title: Sample, Simulate, Select: Physics-in-the-Loop Text-to-Motion for Humanoids Without Training

author.name: Raphael Memmesheimer, Sven Behnke

entry.summary: S3 measures how much of the gap between text-to-motion models and humanoid robots can be closed with no training: it draws N candidate motions per prompt from a frozen text-to-motion model, retargets each to a Unitree G1 via inverse kinematics, rolls them out in simulation with a pretrained tracking policy, and selects the best-executed candidate. Putting the deployment controller in the loop as the verifier enables zero-training language-to-humanoid motion.

entry.title: Auditing Proxy-Based Validation Across Text Spans

author.name: Daein Weon, Dong Ho Kang

entry.summary: This paper exposes a subtle flaw in how evaluation metrics are validated against cheap proxy labels: when the score and proxy are computed over the same text span, agreement can reflect shared surface evidence rather than the intended semantic construct. The authors formalize a validation contract and re-evaluate proxies strictly outside the scored span, showing in a controlled HotpotQA experiment that score-proxy agreement far exceeds score-correctness agreement (+0.184 gap) when spans overlap, collapsing to +0.045 from 120 characters onward. This has broad implications for how LLM evaluation pipelines are trusted.

entry.title: Conditional Tensor Diffusion: Distributional Counterfactual Learning and Inference

author.name: Xinbing Kong, Zeyu Li, Junfan Mao, Bin Wu

entry.summary: The paper develops CFTDiff, a conditional diffusion model with masked Tucker structure for counterfactual distribution recovery in high-dimensional panel/tensor causal settings. By preserving dependence across tensor modes and reducing nonlinear score learning from the product of mode dimensions to the product of Tucker ranks, it derives high-probability error bounds for distributional treatment-effect estimation.

entry.title: Understanding Reliability in LLM-based Human Behavior Simulation

author.name: Pei Wang, Lei Wang, Yuanzi Li, Xu Chen

entry.summary: ReliMap decomposes LLM-based human behavior simulation into three structured layers and evaluates reliability at individual and population levels across model capacity, profile completeness, and population coverage, tested on four tasks and eleven LLMs. The study finds that all models exhibit substantial distributional problems, clarifying how configuration choices interact to determine simulation trustworthiness.

entry.title: Cognitive Action Reasoning for Proactive Robots from Human-Centered Multimodal Observations

author.name: Zhihao Gu, Kechao Zhu, Yuanfeng Wu, Mohan Liu, Ankit Kumar Shaw, ChenDong Hong, Xuanyu Chen, Dengchen Mei, Xu Tianyi, Lin Wang

entry.summary: Formulates ProRobo, an upstream cognitive decision problem where robots must proactively decide what action to take from multimodal human and environmental cues without explicit instructions. Introduces ProAction, a resource of human-centered multimodal observations supporting this underexplored setting of proactive embodied assistance.

entry.title: Beyond End-Task Success: How to Audit Visual Experience Retrieval in Robotics

author.name: Eshika Pathak, Leela Krishna

entry.summary: This paper argues that end-task success rates mislead evaluations of robot experience-reuse systems, since a retrieval rule can score well by exploiting one broadly transferable experience or poorly because its preferred experience is weak. The authors contribute an audit methodology that executes every stored experience in every query scene across two manipulation tasks, three reuse mechanisms, and multiple library sizes, exposing library-level confounds.

entry.title: Rollout Efficiency in Reinforcement Learning for Reasoning Large Language Models: A Taxonomy and Future Directions

author.name: Niloofar Gholipour, Marcos Assuncao, Gursimran Singh, Timothy Yu, Rajkumar Buyya, Julien Gascon-Samson, Zhenan Fan, Yong Zhang, Xiaojie Xu, Yaqiang Yao, Xiaolong Bai

entry.summary: A survey providing a systematic taxonomy of rollout efficiency methods for reasoning-oriented RLHF/RL on LLMs, classified from both mechanism and bottleneck perspectives. It analyzes how technique families address sources of rollout inefficiency while preserving data freshness, consistency, and statistical validity, and outlines future directions.

entry.title: Queer inclusion in speech datasets: An audit and taxonomy of practical tensions

author.name: Brooklyn Sheppard, Anaelia Ovalle, Adina Williams, Levent Sagun

entry.summary: This paper audits six major speech datasets for LGBTQIA+ representation, finding measurable queer speaker representation between 0 and 1.4 percent, too low for robust disparity measurement. The authors develop a taxonomy of tensions explaining why marginalized voices are underrepresented and compare against two community-built speech science datasets.

entry.title: Identifying Intelligent Processes via Online Sequential Testing

author.name: Aritra Das, Debayan Gupta

entry.summary: The paper formalizes the problem of identifying which LLM from a known set is being interacted with as a two-level active sequential hypothesis testing problem: an outer probe-design stage and an inner identification stage. It provides a principled framework for choosing which evaluations to construct and how to deploy them sequentially.

entry.title: Mitigating Sequential Reappearance in Diffusion Data-Point Unlearning

author.name: Donghyun Kim, Taehyuk Lee, Jinyeong Kim, Youngmin Oh, Dohyeong Kim, Jaehyuk Ryu, Sangwoo Hong

entry.summary: Identifies sequential reappearance, a previously unreported failure mode in diffusion model unlearning where an instance initially judged forgotten later returns to the memorized regime after subsequent unrelated deletion requests, without data reuse or adversarial fine-tuning. The paper introduces a target-level evaluation protocol tracking immediate, sustained, and reappearing forgetting, and links reappearance to sharper local denoising-loss geometry.

entry.title: Transformer-Informed Trajectory Optimization for Relative Motion in Cislunar Orbits

author.name: Walter J. Manuel, Yuji Takubo, Simone D'Amico

entry.summary: Extends the Autonomous Rendezvous Transformer (ART) to cislunar rendezvous, proximity operations, and docking for the first time, using transformer warm-starts to accelerate non-convex trajectory optimization in severely nonlinear perilune dynamics. Relevant to autonomous spacecraft guidance where Earth-orbit methods break down.

entry.title: Risk-Aware Online Conformal State Probing

author.name: Pietro Talli, Petar Popovski, Osvaldo Simeone

entry.summary: The paper proposes online conformal state probing (OCSP), a sequential policy for autonomous agents that jointly decides which control actions to take and when to probe edge devices for state information, certifying worst-case reliability without distributional assumptions. It provably controls the missed query error fraction, addressing safety-critical settings where average-case guarantees are insufficient.

entry.title: The Uncontrolled Variable: Vision-Language Model Refusal Responds to Image Presence in Ways Risk Cannot Explain

author.name: Haoyu Zhang, Yi Feng, Shibo Zheng, Zhuoxi Wang, Xiao Luo, Haowen Xu, Xiangchen Guan, Mohammad Zandsalimy, Shanu Sushmita

entry.summary: This paper shows that safety-aligned vision-language models key refusal partly on whether an image is attached, independent of request content: attaching a blank canvas shifts refusal by tens of percentage points. The effect is not blanket caution — neutral prompts are barely affected while borderline-benign questions about privacy, self-harm and violence move sharply, so benign sensitivity-adjacent traffic bears the cost. Image properties modulate the size of the shift.

entry.title: TriWorldBench: A Tri-View Consistency Perspective on Embodied World Models

author.name: Xuanyi Liu, Haofeng Wang, Ruiqi Li, Danni Yu, Rui Wan, Ruixu Zhang, Siyu Tao, Xue Yang, Shaofeng Zhang, Zicheng Zhang, Jiaqi Zhang, Siwei Ma

entry.summary: Presents a benchmark evaluating embodied world models via synchronized head, left-wrist, and right-wrist camera videos, with 500 episodes across 50 bimanual manipulation tasks and 19 metrics covering tri-view consistency, physical and 3D coherence, motion quality, and more. It argues independent per-view evaluation cannot verify that views describe the same action and object state.

entry.title: The Sirens' Song: When Proximal Background Context Overshadows Distant Evidence

author.name: Xiaoyu Yang, Jie Lu, Wei Duan, En Yu

entry.summary: The paper identifies the Proximity Trap: long-context LLMs underuse distant evidence not primarily because of distance itself but due to competition with abundant task-irrelevant proximal background. It introduces LYRA, a t-distributed directional matching mechanism that reshapes context retrieval distributions to direct more attention mass toward task-relevant evidence, showing gains on LongBench-v2, RULER, and LongBench.

entry.title: Fully Byzantine-Resilient Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haejoon Lee, Dimitra Panagou

entry.summary: FRAC-MARL proposes a decentralized actor-critic method for multi-agent RL in which each agent exploits redundancy in two-hop messages to identify reliable communication under Byzantine edge attacks. Under linear function approximation, the authors prove parameters converge almost surely to the same limit points as the attack-free setting, unlike prior methods that converge only to a degraded neighborhood. This is a meaningful theoretical advance for robust distributed multi-agent learning.

entry.title: Protocol before progress: leakage-aware evaluation of AIS trajectory prediction

author.name: Zobeir Raisi, Vali Mohammad Nazarzehi Had

entry.summary: This paper audits reported progress in vessel-trajectory prediction from AIS data, showing that evaluation protocol choices, not architectures, drive much of the apparent error reduction. Using vessel-, time-, and region-disjoint splits across two real traffic corpora, the authors find TrAISformer's oracle best-of-16 decoding inflates gains by a factor of 2.1-3.2 and vessel-sharing splits lower error substantially. The work is a valuable cautionary study on benchmark hygiene with actionable protocol recommendations.

entry.title: Block-Level Weight-Space Structure Persists Under Post-Training: An Empirical Study Across LLM Families

author.name: Zhaohui Wang

entry.summary: This empirical study across eight configurations from Qwen2.5, Llama-3.1/3.2, Mistral, and Gemma-2 shows that post-training changes every tensor (defeating hash-based deduplication entirely) yet preserves block-level weight geometry, with cosine similarities above 0.99 and relative Frobenius distances below 0.13 versus base weights. Post-training thus acts as a structured perturbation rather than a rewrite of weight-space geometry. This has implications for model deduplication, distillation, and interpreting what instruction tuning actually changes.

entry.title: OMatG-flash: An All-Atom Flow Map with Reinforce Adjoint Matching for Scalable Materials Discovery

author.name: Thomas Egg, Harry Winston Sullivan, Ellad B. Tadmor, Stefano Martiniani

entry.summary: OMatG-flash is an all-atom flow matching model for inorganic crystal structure prediction and de novo generation that achieves Pareto-optimal inference, sampling candidate materials with an order of magnitude fewer inference steps and less wall-clock time than existing flow and diffusion baselines. Benchmark performance remains on par with the state of the art, accelerating the materials discovery pipeline.

entry.title: Bridge of $\Psi$'s: Quantum Circuit Optimization with Schr\"odinger Bridges

author.name: Lino S. Hofstetter, Lia Yeh, Prakash Murali

entry.summary: BOPS is a generative model based on Schrödinger bridges with a custom denoiser that learns to transform unoptimized quantum circuits into equivalent lower-cost circuits directly from examples. Training data is synthesized by applying rewrite rules backwards so each input has a known cheaper target, and the model is evaluated on held-out 8-qubit, 64-depth Clifford+T circuits.

entry.title: Learning to Fluctuate: Statistical Foundations for Causal Tabular Pretraining

author.name: Zhiheng Zhang

entry.summary: The paper argues that causal tabular foundation models trained with latent-effect supervision reward posterior shrinkage rather than encoding the repeated-sample response needed in a fixed deployment population. It proposes fluctuation-supervised pretraining, labeling each synthetic table with its average treatment effect plus an efficient influence-function fluctuation, and proves an endpoint transition showing full fluctuation makes the Gaussian label observable and improves finite-sample causal label recovery.

entry.title: On the Lexical Superstition of Large Language Models for Code Comprehension: Re-evaluation on Code of Low Lexical Quality

author.name: Xin Shen (Nanjing University, Nanjing, China), San-Zhuo Xi (Nanjing University, Nanjing, China), Yali Du (Nanjing University, Nanjing, China), Ming Li (Nanjing University, Nanjing, China)

entry.summary: Using Face/Off, a semantics-preserving identifier-renaming framework, the paper shows that LLMs assign disproportionate weight to identifier names when comprehending code: performance drops as identifier information is removed or made misleading, even though program structure is preserved. This reveals over-reliance on statistically informative but unreliable lexical cues across evaluated models and tasks.

entry.title: Training a Language Model End-to-End in Rust: An Experience Report

author.name: Arif Adito

entry.summary: A solo author pretrained a language model end-to-end in Rust without PyTorch or Python in the training path for 164 dollars of rented GPU time, and reports a measured failure taxonomy of the Candle and Burn Rust ML frameworks as training backends. The documented defects include silently gradient-free fused kernels, a backward pass at roughly 3 percent of theoretical GPU throughput, and mid-training segfaults, all of which passed ordinary loss-curve inspection.

entry.title: PACE-dLLM: Elastic Block Decoding via Confidence Cliff Estimation for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Xiaocheng Lu, Shuhan Guo, Ziyue Ma, Jie Zhang, Jian Liu, Jingcai Guo, Haoxuan Che, Song Guo

entry.summary: PACE-dLLM accelerates diffusion LLM decoding by decoupling look-ahead horizon from commit count in block decoding, using the model's own per-step confidence which follows a context-dependent cliff. This replaces indirect heuristics like volatility tracking with a direct signal. It builds on competitive dLLMs such as LLaDA and Dream and targets faster parallel text generation.

entry.title: Transcribe, Translate, and Optimize: Joint Reward Learning for Speech Translation

author.name: Yanghe Dong, Wanting Huang, Weiran Wang

entry.summary: Addresses exposure-bias-style mismatch in LLM-based speech translation by jointly fine-tuning recognition and translation with GRPO, scoring transcripts and translations conditioned on model-generated transcripts, and comparing three token advantage strategies. Using Qwen2.5-Omni-3B across four languages, CoT GRPO beats Direct ST GRPO by 1.77 and 0.83 average BLEU on CoVoST 2 and FLEURS.

entry.title: Rethinking Streaming Video Diffusion Model: Context, Execution, and Training

author.name: Hongchen Zhang (University of Chinese Academy of Sciences)

entry.summary: The paper develops a unified analytical framework for streaming video diffusion covering model/sampler choices, historical conditioning, execution scheduling, and training strategies, making computational dependencies and training-inference alignment explicit. It compares context-selection policies (clean, same-level, progressive history) on the full VBench set, with progressive history achieving the best aggregate score of 85.60.

entry.title: Planning-Aligned Pretraining of BEV Representations with Sparse Action-Conditioned Targets for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jaeha Song, Soonmin Hwang

entry.summary: PAVER pretrains bird's-eye-view encoders for end-to-end driving using sparse risk and unknown targets derived from rule-based ego motions on a single LiDAR sweep, with a tiny 10K-parameter action-conditioned prediction head. Pretraining requires no driving-task annotations or dense reconstruction, and only the BEV encoder transfers, preserving camera-only downstream inference.

entry.title: MM-ContextFold: Context Folding for Multimodal Agentic Retrieval

author.name: Yang Tian, Fan Liu, Jingyuan Zhang, Zhenyang Li, Yupeng Hu, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: The paper addresses context explosion in multimodal agentic retrieval, where agents iteratively invoke tools and accumulate ever-growing multimodal interaction histories. Based on a systematic study of about 10,000 trajectories showing raw images become redundant as visual cues are textualized, MM-ContextFold folds visual content out of the context to keep token usage manageable while preserving task performance.

entry.title: PREM: Prefix-Steered Recurrent Memory for Long-Video Understanding

author.name: Siru Zhong, Qiongyan Wang, Xiaohui Lv, Yuzheng Zhuang, Shuai Tao, Wulong Liu, Haohuan Fu, Yuxuan Liang

entry.summary: PREM is a memory-token-free framework for long-video understanding with frozen vision-language models that separates video ingestion from query answering: a recurrent writer distills the visual stream into a compact 256 KiB multi-slot associative state, and a question-conditioned readout adds memory-derived K/V steering to non-visual prompt prefixes during prefill. This enables write-once, query-many inference without extra prompt tokens or decoding recurrence, evaluated across six long-video benchmarks.

entry.title: BindCLIP: One Balanced Coupling For Compositional Vision Language Scoring

author.name: Liuyang Song, Yi Zhang, Zhongyi Deng, Daqian Yang, Hongbo Zhang

entry.summary: BindCLIP tackles compositional reasoning failures in CLIP-style models by building a pairwise scorer from a balanced token-patch-depth optimal transport coupling that places candidate captions and multiple visual depths in a single plan. It reads semantic, entity, order, and spatial evidence as energies of this transport state while keeping the encoder frozen, arguing the association structure should be read out rather than rebuilt.

entry.title: Hierarchical Prompt Learning for Hyperbolic Vision-Language Models

author.name: Andro Erdelez, Pascal Mettes, Behzad Bozorgtabar

entry.summary: This paper introduces a plug-in for hierarchical prompt learning on frozen hyperbolic vision-language models, adding parent-class prompt learners, hyperbolic entailment regularization, and parent-feedback logit fusion. It instantiates the approach with CoOp, CoCoOp, and MaPLe, yielding HyPLO, CoHyPLO, and MaHyPLO, evaluated across standard benchmarks. It matters because it exploits taxonomic label structure that flat prompt-learning methods ignore, in a geometry naturally suited to hierarchies.

entry.title: Dynamic Thermal Gaussians: Multimodal 4D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Rongfeng Lu, Lifeng Lin, Xiaobao Wei, Quan Chen, Ming Lu, Yitian Xue, Yaoqi Sun, Yuhan Gao, Anke Xue, Chenggang Yan

entry.summary: This paper presents the first dynamic RGB-thermal reconstruction framework using 4D Gaussian splatting, jointly modeling color, thermal observations, and scene geometry over time. It anchors both modalities to a shared geometric substrate to capture heat-transfer dynamics rather than assuming static temperature distributions, with applications in military and thermal analysis.

entry.title: MiTHras: Task-specific Hierarchical Semi-supervised Contrastive Masked Autoencoder for Mitotic Figure Analysis

author.name: Trinh T. L. Vuong, Simon Graham, Quoc Dang Vu, Phat T. H. Ho, Jeewoo Lim, Mostafa Jahanifar, Nasir Rajpoot, Jin T. Kwak

entry.summary: MiTHras is a task-specific pretraining framework combining pseudo-label-guided image- and token-level contrastive learning with masked reconstruction for mitotic figure analysis in pathology. The authors release TCGA-MF-Pseudo, a 1.8 million image corpus across 14 TCGA cohorts, and achieve the best mean F1 on all three MF classification and both subtype benchmarks.

entry.title: When Wider Views Fail: Stress-Testing Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Daisy Li, Kyle Gao, Quanyun Wu, Hanna Chomko, John S. Zelek, Jonathan Li

entry.summary: This paper systematically stress-tests feed-forward 3D reconstruction models by varying the angular span of sparse input views while holding the input budget fixed, treating viewpoint span as a controlled distribution shift. It finds substantial degradation at wide spans, producing incomplete surfaces and hallucinated geometry, revealing a key failure mode of pretrained reconstruction models.

entry.title: Anatomy-Decomposed Chest Computed Tomography (CT) Projections as Scalable Supervision for Bone Suppression in Chest Radiographs

author.name: Mrunmay Angaitkar, Piyush Kumar, Aarjav Satia, Pranav Rao, Ashish Mittal, Manoj Tadepalli, Preetham Putha

entry.summary: The authors build a digitally reconstructed radiograph framework that decomposes chest CT into bone, non-lung soft-tissue, and lung components, projecting each separately so weighted combinations sum exactly to the full radiograph. This yields pixel-registered synthetic training data enabling models to suppress bone or lung components and recover them by subtraction, transferring to real X-rays.

entry.title: AWR-Net: Decoupling Anatomy and Appearance for 3D Fetal Brain Ultrasound Synthesis

author.name: Yuhuan Lu, Sergio Valencia, Yuanji Zhang, Yuhao Huang, Camilo Jaimes, P. Ellen Grant, Davood Karimi

entry.summary: Proposes AWR-Net, which decouples anatomical correspondence learning from ultrasound appearance modeling to synthesize 3D fetal brain ultrasound from anatomical label maps, using fetal MRI as a knowledge-transfer bridge. This addresses the data and annotation scarcity that limits fetal ultrasound development.

entry.title: SPeaR: Test-Time Adaptation with Steering Primitives for Realigning Representations

author.name: Muhammad Sudipto Siam Dip, Ali Etemad

entry.summary: SPeaR proposes a test-time adaptation approach that keeps a pretrained network frozen and instead inserts lightweight learnable steering modules at stage boundaries, optimizing them directly from unlabeled test data without source data or supervised warm-up. A gated objective adapts only when it reduces uncertainty, with a diversity regularizer to prevent collapse. This is a meaningful alternative to parameter-updating TTA methods and could reduce adaptation cost and risk of catastrophic drift.

entry.title: Online Automated Algorithm Design with Large Language Models

author.name: Zhiyao Zhang, Yichen Li, Xingyu Wu, Liang Feng, Kay Chen Tan

entry.summary: The paper introduces online LLM-based automated algorithm design, a paradigm that treats the algorithm itself as a state-dependent decision variable: at each optimization stage, LLM agents synthesize a new algorithm with fresh behavior logic from the current optimization state, and executing it advances the search. This bridges LLM-driven algorithm synthesis and conventional adaptive optimizers, which can only adjust predefined parameters or operators. A conceptual contribution at the intersection of LLMs, meta-learning, and evolutionary computation.

entry.title: PARTE: Plane-Assisted Robust Transformation Estimation for Point Cloud Registration

author.name: Abolfazl Babanazari, Carson Cramer, Tyler Summers, Carlos Nieto, Kaveh Fathian

entry.summary: PARTE is a global point-cloud registration method that treats planar structure as complementary evidence rather than discarding it. It introduces a Plane Context Histogram descriptor for planar patches and a two-level matching procedure to identify reliable plane correspondences, targeting scenarios with limited overlap, repetitive geometry, and noisy correspondences.

entry.title: Deploying Foundation Models for Embodied Navigation

author.name: Vishnu Sashank Dorbala, Dinesh Manocha

entry.summary: The paper tackles two deployment problems for foundation models on embodied navigation agents: training bias causing poor personalization in unseen environments, and limited context length on long-horizon tasks. It proposes Transit-Aware Planning (TAP), which primes FMs with human-habit data mined from scenes, and MemCtrl, an active memory management scheme with a novel memory head augmentation, alongside a taxonomy of FM-based navigation.

entry.title: An Action Is Worth One Patch: Unified World-Action Modeling with PatchWAM

author.name: Tianheng Wang, Zhou Xie, Heng Jia, Jianhua Xu, Tong Zhang, Kaicheng Yu

entry.summary: PatchWAM explores whether a generative visual backbone's existing capacity can support continuous control without separate action heads or action experts, by expressing continuous actions as patches via a fixed Action-as-Patch mapping. This unifies world modeling and action generation in a single architecture, questioning whether visual prediction and action generation require separate computational pathways. The answer has implications for how generative world models are extended to control.

entry.title: SparseNav: Instruction-conditioned Sparse Semantic Perception for Training-Free Vision-Language Navigation

author.name: Quanhua Chen, Juhan Kang, Runfeng Lin, ZiFei Zhang, Enquang Feng, Chunran Zheng, Xiwang Dong, Jiarong Lin

entry.summary: SparseNav is a training-free framework for map-based vision-language navigation that maintains only a lightweight geometric BEV map plus a sparse landmark memory, acquiring new semantics on demand rather than persistently tracking all objects. This less-is-more approach reduces perception cost and avoids cluttering the VLM planner's visual-spatial input with irrelevant annotations. It connects language understanding with geometric planning more efficiently than conventional semantics-heavy VLN pipelines.

entry.title: Dr-LiSA: Direct Radar-Lidar Scan Alignment for $SE(3)$ Localization

author.name: Alex Zhang, Daniil Lisus, Cedric Le Gentil, Timothy D. Barfoot

entry.summary: Dr-LiSA is a first-of-its-kind direct method for localizing 2D spinning radar intensity measurements in SE(3) against 3D lidar maps, combining radar's weather robustness with lidar's map fidelity. It overcomes the modality gap that previously restricted radar-lidar localization to planar SE(2) with lower accuracy than like-for-like systems.

entry.title: ShowTellArena: Evaluating Business Workflow Understanding from Demonstrations

author.name: David Garg, Ritobrata Sarkar, Ehsan Azarnasab, Siddhartha Borah

entry.summary: ShowTellArena is a benchmark protocol and public dataset testing what agents comprehend from narrated business demonstrations, with 50 workflow tasks across finance, hiring, procurement, and logistics and 502 questions testing rules, boundaries, exceptions, and errors in proposed automations. It holds the scenario and quiz fixed while allowing different products to teach through their own interfaces, analyzing 218 selected episodes.

entry.title: RGSQ: Riemannian Geometry-Sensitive Quantization for Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Zhiping Wu, Dongdong Ren, Yangchengyu Zhou, Zhengjie Zhang, Wenbin Li, Hongbing Pan, Yang Gao

entry.summary: Proposes RGSQ, which formulates post-training quantization of large VLMs as reconstruction under Riemannian geometry rather than isotropic Euclidean perturbations, addressing uneven bit-width distribution and inconsistent low-bit performance of unimodal PTQ methods. Targets efficient deployment under memory and latency constraints.

entry.title: Latest Exact Match Attention

author.name: Moritz Br\"osamle

entry.summary: This paper introduces Latest Exact Match Attention (LEMA), a hard-attention transformer variant where binarized queries attend only to the latest exactly matching key. It proves LEMA transformers with chain of thought can simulate word-RAMs, and crucially shows the converse: word-RAMs can simulate LEMA transformers with per-token cost independent of context length, yielding a tight two-way computational correspondence. The author also proposes a training method for LEMA transformers beyond the theory.

entry.title: Optimizing Denoising Trajectories in dLLMs: A Lightweight Evolutionary Heuristic Approach

author.name: Zijian Zhao, Dian Jin, Xialiang Tong, Sen Li, Mingxuan Yuan

entry.summary: The paper analyzes failure modes (EOS Overflow and Proximal Bias) in confidence-based denoising schedulers for diffusion large language models, attributing them to disproportionate attention at certain positions. It proposes a lightweight evolutionary heuristic scheduler that improves generation quality at inference time without retraining.

entry.title: MemoryAthena: Adaptive Routing over Latent and Generated Memories

author.name: Mingyuan Li, Guangsheng Yu, Juyuan Zhang, Xu Wang, Zhibo Man, Haonan Zhang, Shaoxiong Ji

entry.summary: MemoryAthena studies learned-memory systems where memory can be generated rather than only retrieved, using three pathways: direct Engram retrieval, generation from retrieved cues, and generation from backbone states. It finds generated memory is conditionally useful and trains a lightweight causal router over frozen components to decide when generated representations should intervene. This contributes to more flexible memory architectures for LLMs.

entry.title: The Right Future for Action: Learning Action-Relevant Predictive States in World Action Models

author.name: Qiwen Gu, Jifan Li, Bingjie Gao, Rui Chen, Jing Tang, Xiangxiang Chu, Junqiao Zhao

entry.summary: This paper studies generation-free world action models (WAMs) that keep future-video prediction during training but act from internal video features at inference, showing via representation diagnostics that predictability of future changes does not imply easier linear action decoding. It proposes Action-Relevant Predictive States (ARPS), a compact horizon-conditioned predictive interface between video and action experts.

entry.title: Pay More Attention To Text In High-Resolution MLLMs

author.name: Zhongkuan Mao, Wenzhuo Zhao, Xianjie Liu, Yidong Wang, Zhao Gao, Ronghao Xian, Yao Jiang, Yi Zhang, Liangjian Wen, Keren Fu

entry.summary: This paper argues that failures of high-resolution multimodal LLMs are partly a linguistic bottleneck rather than purely a visual one: questions formulated for answering do not necessarily specify the visual evidence needed for localization. It introduces EviSpec, a training-free compiler that derives complementary evidence-oriented specifications to guide visual search, building on evidence that relevant visual cues already exist in intermediate representations.

entry.title: MaskVLA: Visual Masking Against Trajectory Overfitting of Vision-Language-Action Model

author.name: Yuxuan Jiang, Jiaying Huang, Ge Wang, Shenhao Yan, Jiahao Yang, Chengsi Yao, Qi Liu, Qing Zhao, Shuguang Cui, Yiming Zhao, Yatong Han, Zhen Li

entry.summary: MaskVLA is a masking-based fine-tuning strategy for vision-language-action (VLA) models that combats severe trajectory overfitting observed when finetuning on limited datasets. By randomly masking a small portion of the main camera's visual input, the model is pushed to learn more fine-grained, task-relevant features and to use wrist camera information, yielding more robust policies for complex manipulation tasks.

entry.title: Mira-Scene: Pixel-Aligned Layouts for Generative 3D Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Yang-Tian Sun, Tianjia Liu, Zehuan Huang, Yi-Hua Huang, Xiaoyang Lyu, Ziyi Yang, Zi-Xin Zou, Yuan-Chen Guo, Yan-Pei Cao, Xiaojuan Qi

entry.summary: Mira-Scene is a compositional 3D scene reconstruction framework that replaces sparse unbounded pose regression with dense bounded correspondence recovery via a Canonical Canonical correspondence representation, enabling single-image placement of high-fidelity generated objects into coherent scene layouts. This addresses the generalization problems of compositional methods under scarce scene-level supervision.

entry.title: PrismGPT: Proxy-Guided Learning for Region-Aware Photo Editing with Self-Synthesized Reasoning

author.name: Ke Zhao, Hue Nguyen, Abhijith Punnappurath, Zhongling Wang, Iqbal Mohomed, Michael S. Brown

entry.summary: PrismGPT is a VLM framework that produces structured, region-aware photo editing plans from a single image without commercial black-box tools, trained via proxy-guided learning with operation decomposition and region-aware aesthetic ranking as auxiliary tasks. This addresses the vast combinatorial space of global and local editing parameter prediction, with self-synthesized reasoning data.

entry.title: PhyVisGen: Physically and Visually High-Fidelity Robotic Manipulation Data Generation

author.name: Yu Zheng, Qiyu Feng, Yixin Wu, Baoquan Yang, Yixuan Zhou, Bingyang Hu, Kemeng Huang, Guansheng Yang, Hesheng Wang

entry.summary: PhyVisGen is a framework for scalable manipulation data generation combining physically accurate soft-gripper contact via an arm-gripper coupling method based on Incremental Potential Contact, with visually faithful scenes from real-scene reconstruction and real-time path rendering. It targets the physical and visual fidelity needed for sim-to-real transfer of visuomotor policies.

entry.title: Generalizing Manipulation Skills with a Local Coding Agent

author.name: Raman Talwar, Elias Nijs, Andreas Verleysen, Francis wyffels

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether a local open-weight VLM (Qwen3.8-27B) can control a UR3e arm through a coding-agent harness that writes and executes its own code above services for kinematics, safety limits, and classic computer vision, enabling one-shot generalization to task variations without new programming or training. It leverages fully local, open-weight models on a single workstation.

entry.title: When LLM Agents Fail to Read the Room: ReAdapt for Relational Social Reasoning

author.name: Jianzhe Lin, Xiaolin Li, Yunda Liu, Fei Wang, Jubin Chheda

entry.summary: The paper formalizes a failure mode where LLM agents choose actions based on surface content rather than latent social relationships like tie strength and reciprocity. It introduces a relationship-reasoning benchmark with 500 synthetic social worlds and 1,000 queries, plus ReAdapt, a method for revising social hypotheses with new relational evidence.

entry.title: SMTB: Fast Structure-Mapping with Tight Bounds

author.name: Daniel Weitekamp, Christopher MacLellan

entry.summary: Introduces SMTB, a structure-mapping algorithm for analogical reasoning that is 5-15x faster than the classic Structure-Mapping Engine and about 50 percent better at finding mappings in large nested domains. It is part of the Cognitive Rule Engine, an open framework with Python interfaces to optimized C++ implementations of core cognitive-system algorithms.

entry.title: Seeing Is Not Perceiving: When Synthetic Consumers Can and Cannot Pretest Visual Marketing

author.name: Yi-Lin Tsai (Arvin), Yung-Hsiu (Arvin), Lai

entry.summary: Stress-tests whether generative AI synthetic consumers can reproduce human effects in visual marketing experiments, varying model (GPT-4o-mini vs. GPT-5.4-mini) and input format across six canonical experiments. All configurations passed manipulation checks but none reproduced more than two of six human effects, with one significant reversal of a human finding.

entry.title: Toolcompass: Guiding Tool Trialing, Not Suppressing It

author.name: Junlin Fang, Chong Zhang, Do Nguyen-Thanh, Xiaogang Xu, Zhen Fang, Sean Du

entry.summary: Introduces ToolCompass, a post-training framework for LLM agents that structures tool-call representations by shared function using von Mises-Fisher distributions, guiding selective tool trialing without suppressing necessary exploration of unseen tools. It jointly reduces intra-function variation and increases inter-function separation.

entry.title: Towards Omni-dimensional GUI Agent Navigation with Masked Trajectory Prediction

author.name: Yan Zhang, Pei Fu, Daiqing Wu, Huawen Shen, Ruoceng Zhang, Shaojie Zhang, Jiahui Yang, Yu Zhou, Can Ma, Zhenbo Luo, Jian Luan

entry.summary: Proposes MaP, a unified masked trajectory prediction framework that harmonizes divergent GUI navigation tasks (step-wise decision-making, state-action alignment, long-horizon planning) despite inconsistent objectives and heterogeneous data. Targets omni-dimensional GUI agent navigation capability.

entry.title: Improved Multiplayer Bandit Algorithm for Bernoulli Rewards

author.name: Khang Nguyen, Ricardo Parada, William Chang

entry.summary: The paper studies multiplayer multi-armed bandits with information asymmetry under Bernoulli rewards across three information structures, replacing Hoeffding-style confidence bounds with KL-divergence-based ones. The proposed mKL-UCB variants yield strictly tighter regret guarantees, with at least a two-fold improvement by Pinsker's inequality.

entry.title: JEV-as-a-Judge: Accept When Confident, Escalate When Unsure

author.name: Yubo Li, Yidi Miao, Ramayya Krishnan, Rema Padman

entry.summary: The paper studies whether a decision-only judge (JEV) can serve as an economical first-pass evaluator that escalates uncertain cases to stronger judges. Compared against sixteen generative and reward-model judges with blinded human adjudication, JEV stays within three percentage points of the strongest LLM judge on ordinary preferences and factuality at 0.36% of the cost, with gaps concentrated in derivations and adversarially written wrong answers.

entry.title: A Practical Recipe for Semi-Supervised Federated ASR: Online Pseudo-Labels with Server Update Stabilization

author.name: Wonho Bae, Zakaria Aldeneh, Martin Pelikan, Jan "Honza" Silovsky, Tatiana Likhomanenko, Sheikh Shams Azam

entry.summary: Studies two coupled design axes in semi-supervised federated ASR, the teacher generating pseudo-labels and the server-side anchor updates stabilizing training, showing that a stabilized per-client online teacher matches or beats broadcast global teachers. Provides a practical recipe for closing the gap to fully-supervised federated ASR.

entry.title: Compressing Long Context into Answer-Aligned Memory Embeddings for LLM Inference

author.name: Md Mostafizer Rahman, Md Faizul Ibne Amin, Md Shahajada Mia, Yutaka Watanobe, Fang Liu

entry.summary: Proposes CMC, a framework compressing long contexts into compact Context Memory Embeddings aligned to any frozen decoder's embedding space with a two-tier KV cache combining question guidance and answer-targeted supervision, reducing inference cost without modifying decoder weights. Targets quadratic attention and linear KV-cache scaling limits.

entry.title: TimeInteract: Towards Real-Time Interactive Intelligence for Streaming Time Series

author.name: Sheng Pan, Yongli Gu, Yiqing Guo, Warren Jin, Bo Du, Shirui Pan, Ming Jin

entry.summary: Defines a new Time-Series Interaction regime where a model continuously perceives streaming observations and user intent, autonomously deciding when to speak or stay silent while continuing to ingest data during response generation. TimeInteract realizes this with a dual-view streaming encoder and related designs, moving beyond static offline time-series language models.

entry.title: Targeted Review for AI-Assisted Biodiversity Surveys: Active Continuous-Score Occupancy Modeling

author.name: Timm Haucke, Lauren Harrell, Justin Kay, Mary Clapp, Sara Beery

entry.summary: The paper addresses how ecologists should allocate human review effort to verify ML-generated wildlife-monitoring labels, focusing on occupancy modeling where systematically biased errors can distort scientific conclusions. It proposes active review strategies for continuous-score occupancy estimation that prioritize which labels to check given scientific goals. This tackles the important and widely applicable problem of human verification budgets for AI-labeled scientific data.

entry.title: GeoPair: Geometry-Preserving Cross-Layer Factorization for Training-Free Transformer Compression

author.name: Baher Mohammad, Ammar Ali, Stamatios Lefkimmiatis

entry.summary: GeoPair is a training-free post-training compression framework that jointly optimizes cross-layer weight pairings and shared-dictionary factorizations while preserving each layer's activation calibration geometry, unlike pipelines that compress layers in isolation. Combined with structured sparsity, it produces efficient weight decompositions without quality loss. This matters because cross-layer redundancy is a largely untapped compression lever for large transformers.

entry.title: Mode Collapse Is Cheap to Detect: A Ground-Truth-Free Pre-Flight Check for Neural Samplers

author.name: Jian Xu

entry.summary: The paper shows that self-diagnostics computed from a sampler's own draws cannot detect missing target mass, exhibiting a sampler with self-normalized effective sample size 0.99 that still misses 87% of the target. It argues detecting missing mass is strictly easier than sampling it, requiring only one point per missed basin plus local curvature, and builds a pre-flight check that consumes a few percent of the training budget to flag mode collapse without ground-truth samples. This is a valuable quality gate for training neural samplers against unnormalized targets.

entry.title: Visual Jev: Accurate and Efficient Decisions from Shared Visual Context

author.name: Guanxu Yu, Yuhang Yao

entry.summary: Visual Jev encodes an image and shared context once and executes many independent forced-choice question suffixes as a batch, reading candidate probabilities from the language-model head, achieving an 8.9x warm amortized speedup at 32 questions per image versus serial execution. Answer-supervised post-training raises macro accuracy from 70.6% to 76.1%, though gains concentrate on task families represented in training.

entry.title: One Domain, Many Tongues: Composing Domain and Language LoRAs for Cross-Lingual Remote-Sensing MLLMs without Paired Data

author.name: Xuechen Li

entry.summary: MODL adds new languages to an English remote-sensing multimodal LLM using no multilingual RS examples: a domain LoRA trained on English RS imagery and a language LoRA trained on text alone are learned jointly under a mutual-orthogonality constraint at every layer. Without this constraint, the model answers RS questions in English, erodes the base model's multilingual ability, and can diverge on some seeds.

entry.title: Peerify: Benchmarking Peer-Review Claim Verification

author.name: Alireza Daghighfarsoodeh, Sajad Ebrahimi, Ali Ghorbanpour, Soroush Sadeghian, Radin Cheraghi, Negar Arabzadeh, Ebrahim Bagheri

entry.summary: Peerify is a pipeline that decomposes peer-review comments into atomic claims, retrieves relevant manuscript evidence, and judges whether each claim is supported by the paper. It contributes a benchmark of 800 claims from authentic NeurIPS 2024 and ICLR 2024 reviews, including a 300-claim hand-labeled subset used to audit automated supervision.

entry.title: FineWeb-CLaR: Culture, Language, and Region Annotations for Benchmark-Aligned Corpus Auditing

author.name: Yusser Al Ghussin, Eva Gavaller, Cristina Espa\~na-Bonet, Josef van Genabith, Simon Ostermann

entry.summary: FineWeb-CLaR is a large-scale annotated dataset derived from FineWeb and FineWeb-2 that indexes web documents along a shared culture-language-region axis, aligning pretraining corpora with culturally situated benchmarks. This enables audits of whether a target cultural phenomenon is represented in pretraining data, in benchmarks, or both.

entry.title: Modality-Gated Deep Adapters: Adding a Modality to a Frozen Embedding Model with Exact Preservation

author.name: Abdul Basit Tonmoy, Kazi Fardinul Hoque, Md. Shahrier Islam Arham, Arman Luthra

entry.summary: The paper shows LoRA-style adaptation silently changes a deployed multimodal embedding model's text outputs, invalidating stored retrieval indices and audits, and proposes modality-gated deep adapters: per-modality bottleneck adapter packs attached to every decoder layer that execute only when their modality is encoded. This yields exact output preservation for existing inputs while adding a new modality. It addresses a real deployment problem at scale.

entry.title: AdaMerge: Tuning-Free Patch Compression for Multi-Vector Visual Document Retrieval

author.name: Jianxin You, Kun Ni

entry.summary: AdaMerge removes the per-dataset grid-searched cluster budget required by the state-of-the-art Prune-then-Merge method for compressing multi-vector document retrieval embeddings like ColPali, exploiting a sharp cliff in the merge-cosine sequence that separates redundant from salient patches. This yields tuning-free compression while retaining accuracy at high compression ratios.

entry.title: Scout: Open-World Species Recognition on the Edge

author.name: Mohammad Mehdi Rastikerdar, Hui Guan, Deepak Ganesan

entry.summary: Scout is an autonomous system for open-world wildlife species recognition that intermittently invokes a cloud VLM to teach new classes to a compact edge model, operating within tight compute, energy, and bandwidth budgets. It leverages deployment location information to decide when cloud consultation is worthwhile for camera-trap monitoring.

entry.title: CLEAR: Complex Learned Explicit Analytical Regularization for Ultra-Accelerated 4D Flow CMR Reconstruction

author.name: German Sh\^ama Wache, Sebastian Neumayer

entry.summary: CLEAR combines the interpretability of compressed-sensing variational objectives with the flexibility of learned models for ultra-accelerated (10x-50x) 4D Flow cardiac MRI reconstruction, claimed as the first learned regularizer for a 4D reconstruction task. It outperforms compressed sensing and implicit unrolled approaches in the CMRx4DFlow2026 challenge setting.

entry.title: RegVGGT: Sustainable Visual Geometry Grounding for Streaming via Regulated Memory

author.name: Hongbo Mao (Harbin Institute of Technology), Junjun Jiang (Harbin Institute of Technology), Youyu Chen (Harbin Institute of Technology), Jiaxin Zhang (Harbin Institute of Technology), Zhemeng Dong (Harbin Institute of Technology), Xianming Liu (Harbin Institute of Technology)

entry.summary: RegVGGT tackles 3D reconstruction from long video streams where whole-stream inference context exceeds GPU memory, using a training-free token regulation method that admits at most 1% of tokens per frame to update the context. It relies on the observation that a token's initial saliency reliably predicts its long-term importance across the stream, avoiding both memory inflation and context degradation.

entry.title: GAPS: Generative Active Pseudo-view Selection for Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Hongfei Zhu, Haochen Deng, Sitao Zhang, Ling Zhou

entry.summary: The authors propose an alternating optimization framework for novel view synthesis from sparse views, where a pre-trained image diffusion model generates geometrically consistent pseudo-views to supervise 3D Gaussian Splatting. Constraints via depth-conditioned ControlNet, IP-Adapter, LoRA scene adaptation, and img2img anchoring are combined with a Generative Active Pseudo-view Selection (GAPS) scheme that balances reconstruction informativeness against generative reliability, using an annealing schedule.

entry.title: GeoBalance: Geometry-Aware Monitoring and Reconstruction with Asymmetric Optimization for Balanced Multimodal Learning

author.name: Zechang Xiong, Da Li, Rong Yin, Kexin Tang, Biao Yang, Pengyuan Li, Wenkang Kong, Yulan Hu, Shengyu Zhu, Hao Peng

entry.summary: The paper identifies that persistent modality dominance in multimodal classifiers can cause representation-level collapse of the weak modality, termed manifold modality collapse, in which weak-modality representations degrade geometrically across classes. It proposes geometry-aware monitoring and an asymmetric optimization approach (GeoBalance) to detect and repair this collapse, moving beyond loss- and gradient-level balancing methods.

entry.title: Collapse, Not Complexity: Failure-Conditioned Decomposition Repair for End-to-End Document Parsing

author.name: Xingyu Lin, Dehui Du

entry.summary: Using a 180-page entropy-stratified sample and a frozen 4B checkpoint, the paper shows that page complexity is the wrong decision variable for enabling reasoning mode in document parsers: reasoning lowers mean quality at higher token cost, and its benefit concentrates on pages whose ordinary pass has already collapsed into degenerate repetition. The authors instead build collapse detection with a decomposition-repair strategy, noting mode switching rarely repairs collapsed pages.

entry.title: Colon3R: Cross-Domain 3D Reconstruction from Monocular Colonoscopic Video

author.name: Zhihao Xing, Yingyu Wang, Liang Zhao, Shoudong Huang

entry.summary: Colon3R is a semi-supervised framework built on the pretrained VGGT geometry foundation model that transfers coupled camera, depth, and pointmap estimation from labeled phantom and simulated data to unlabeled in-vivo colonoscopy, where weak texture, specular reflections, and non-rigid tissue defeat conventional multi-view reconstruction. It targets surgical robotic colonoscopy applications.

entry.title: HDND: Hierarchical Dynamic Neural Decoding for Multilingual Word/Character Retrieval from Non-Invasive Brain Recordings

author.name: Yueyang Li, Shuran Chen, Wai Ting Siok, Nizhuan Wang

entry.summary: HDND treats word decoding from non-invasive brain recordings as structured hierarchical refinement rather than flat label retrieval, preserving acoustic, lexical, and semantic information at multiple temporal scales. It targets the difficult problem of multilingual word and character retrieval from noisy, weak word-level neural evidence.

entry.title: CoaG: Cylinders on a Grid: Coarse 3D Layout Control for Video Generation

author.name: Zhangsihao Yang, Mengyi Shan

entry.summary: CoaG lets users control video generation with minimal geometry: a ground-plane grid plus one cylinder per person, whose placement and motion over 81 frames determine where people stand and how the camera moves, while appearance comes from text and a background reference. Since no dataset pairs this signal with video, the authors synthesize training pairs automatically with generated captions and renders.

entry.title: NeuIDO: Neural Intrinsic Dynamics Operator for Physics-Informed 4D World Models

author.name: Jiajing Lin, Xin Zhang, Jianhua Sun

entry.summary: NeuIDO proposes learning a unified intrinsic dynamics representation from visual observations via neural operator learning, aiming to internalize world dynamics rather than imposing manual physical assumptions in physics-informed 4D generation. This bridges a gap between physics-based simulation and genuine learned world models for embodied intelligence. The framing as neural operator learning for world dynamics is a meaningful conceptual step.

entry.title: VPRune: Efficient Training-free Pre-LLM Visual Token Pruning

author.name: Guangchuan Lv, Dianxing Shi, Dingjie Fu

entry.summary: VPRune identifies three causes of performance degradation in visual token pruning for large vision-language models: text-guided selection bias, information loss from discarded tokens, and positional distortion from sequence compaction. Its training-free pre-LLM framework uses visual-only diversity selection, similarity-guided token recycling, and position-preserving restoration. Experiments on FastVLM-1.5B show a favorable accuracy-compression trade-off.

entry.title: Relationally Grounded Latent World Models for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Fabian Schmidt, Markus Enzweiler, Abhinav Valada

entry.summary: Building on LAW, this paper uses actor-centric traffic scene graphs from nuScenes 3D annotations as privileged semantic supervision for latent world models, aligning visual latents with serialized relational structure encoded by a frozen text embedding model. The supervision branch is removed at inference, adding no test-time cost, and reduces average trajectory L2 error from 0.661 to 0.622 on nuScenes.

entry.title: PRQuant: Permutation Residual Quantization for Low-Overhead Inference

author.name: Peiran Wang, Anqi Wang, Jiaying Zhao, Huiwen Yang, Zhenyu Ming, Rongqian Wang, Yiwu Yao, Kun Tian, Xin Yao, Gong Zhang, Fan Yang, Zhongyi Huang

entry.summary: PRQuant is a training-free, low-overhead low-bit quantization framework that combines channel reorganization with static weight-side residual compensation after AWQ-style scaling. It permutes channels contributing most to weight quantization error, avoiding the online runtime overhead of rotation and smoothing baselines.

entry.title: WildfireSpreadBench: The Metric Decides the Model in Wildfire Spread Prediction

author.name: Arin Gopakumar, Marco Pannozzo

entry.summary: Benchmarking five discriminative architectures and one generative model on WildfireSpreadTS with a shared pipeline, the authors show that wildfire spread model rankings flip depending on whether average precision or threshold-dependent metrics like F1 and IoU are used, with the highest-AP model over-flagging burned area four- to five-fold. The paper argues that threshold-dependent metrics should guide operational model choice since acting on forecasts requires one threshold.

entry.title: Forecasting Intrathecal Tracer Enhancement from Pre-Contrast Brain MRI: Direct Regression versus Flow Matching

author.name: Qinghui Liu, Jon Andr\'e Ottesen, Thu Nguyen, Geir Ringstad, Ingrid Mossige, Siri Fl{\o}gstad Svensson, Atle Bj{\o}rnerud, Per Kristian Eide, Kyrre Eeg Emblem

entry.summary: Compares direct image-to-image regression against conditional flow matching for forecasting cerebrospinal-fluid tracer enhancement from a single pre-contrast brain MRI, potentially replacing repeated 24-48 hour scans. Trained on 104 patients with external validation on 51 patients with normal pressure hydrocephalus, with a copy-baseline comparison.

entry.title: Graded-Relevance Composed Multimodal Retrieval for E-commerce Visual Search at Scale

author.name: Anubhav Gupta, Hrushikesh Mohapatra, Prijith Chandra, Asish Mohapatra, Anuj Garg, Arvind Maan, Sudip Datta, Venkat Bulusu, Sitesh Kumar Jalan

entry.summary: This paper tackles composed image retrieval (image plus text modifier queries) in large-scale e-commerce visual search, replacing binary-relevance triplet training with a graded-relevance methodology. It uses a VLM to curate training queries and data, better matching the reality that many catalog candidates partially satisfy a query. Deployed-at-scale relevance training is a practical improvement for industrial visual search systems.

entry.title: What do VLM-Based Vision-Language Navigation Models Rely on: Interpreting and Steering Policy Behavior

author.name: D\'ebora Oliveira Makowski, Samiran Gode, Abhijeet Nayak, Marco Hutter, Cordelia Schmid, Lukas Rosenberger Schmid, Wolfram Burgard

entry.summary: This work studies interpretability and steerability of VLM-based vision-language navigation models using intervention-based metrics that measure how visual observations, instructions, and visual memory causally influence navigation decisions. Results indicate these policies are sensitive to certain cues but it remains unclear whether they ground predictions in relevant semantics or track task progress. Valuable behavioral-science-style analysis of an increasingly deployed model class.

entry.title: Acoustic Ellipses: Bio-Inspired Omnidirectional Echolocation in Cooperative Multi-Agent Systems using Frequency Sweeps

author.name: Petras Swissler, Lindsay Burke, Julia Hyland Bruno

entry.summary: Inspired by bird song and flight, the paper enables cooperative agents to localize obstacles using a stationary source emitting frequency-modulated chirps while moving listeners observe direct and reflected signals. A novel frequency-gap mapping defines reflection ellipses combined with a 2D accumulation filter, demonstrated in a bespoke audio simulator.

entry.title: RouteRLT: Learning When and Which RL Specialist Should Control a Vision-Language-Action Policy

author.name: Chongyu Zhu, Jaden Hinds, Hyegang Kim, Juan Sebastian Rojas, Ramy Elmallah, Chi-Guhn Lee

entry.summary: RouteRLT is a routing framework that learns when control of a generalist VLA policy should transfer to an RL specialist trained for a single precision-critical phase of contact-rich industrial tasks such as connector insertion. A phase selector identifies the task phase and orchestrates handoffs, aiming to preserve generalist competence while enabling precision.

entry.title: MATE: Multi-Agent Virtual Teleoperation Platform for Humanoid Collaboration Data Collection

author.name: Yichuan Yu, Youzhuo Wang, Yiming Ren, Di Feng, Yexuan Yang, Bingxi Yang, Shengxiao Gong, Yujing Sun, Yuexin Ma

entry.summary: MATE is a multi-agent virtual teleoperation platform enabling multiple geographically distributed operators to simultaneously control whole-body humanoids in a shared physics-based environment for collaborative skill data collection. It removes the need for multiple physical robots and co-located operation while preserving physically coupled interactions among humanoids, objects, and the environment.

entry.title: Three Routes to One Answer: Reconciling AIPW, TMLE, and Double Machine Learning for Applied Researchers

author.name: M. Ehsan Karim

entry.summary: This tutorial reconciles AIPW, TMLE, and double machine learning as three estimators of the same efficient influence function for average treatment effects, building all three by hand on the NHEFS smoking-cessation dataset with shared nuisance libraries and identical cross-fitting folds. It explains in practical terms what a practitioner must match across software packages for the routes to agree.

entry.title: Lost in the Slop: Can AI Find the Plot in the Log?

author.name: jennz

entry.summary: A team tested whether AI monitors can reconstruct ground-truth history (roles, relationships, events) from long multi-agent interaction traces generated from human-authored murder-mystery seeds. The best monitor recovered under half of rubric facts, with GPT-6 Astra high-reasoning performing best, Gemini worst, and Claude Opus 5 reporting zero reasoning tokens.

entry.title: ZeroGate: Trust-Preserving Fast Paths for Governed AI Agent Runtimes

author.name: Zexun Wang

entry.summary: ZeroGate separates exact-action approval from durable local admission in governed agent runtimes: issuers sign short-lived ActionPasses, and a trusted runtime adapter reconstructs and locally gates actions with nonce consumption, quota updates, and admission receipts in a SQLite transaction. It states a conditional decision-preservation proposition linking local admission to synchronous policy authorization.

entry.title: A Behavioral Trait Leaks into Preferences: Diagnosing Trait Interference in LLM User Simulators

author.name: Chaehyun Kim, Sein Kim, Hongseok Kang, Chanyoung Park

entry.summary: Shows that trait independence in LLM-based user simulators for recommender evaluation collapses in practice: amplified browsing activity distorts preference boundaries and inflates satisfaction scores, biasing evaluations. Proposes PQA, a mitigation to decouple behavioral and preference traits.

entry.title: Neurosymbolic Action Model Learning under Partial Observability

author.name: Adem Kikaj, Lennert De Smet, Giuseppe Marra, Luc De Raedt

entry.summary: Proposes NeSyAM, a neurosymbolic paradigm for learning action models from partially observable image traces, extending prior approaches that required complete, fully observable sequences. This enables agents to learn when actions apply and how they change the world from incomplete visual data.

entry.title: Optimizing the Score, Losing Sight of the Task: Reward Hacking Across Weights, Selection, and Prompts

author.name: Vansh Wahi

entry.summary: This work builds a comparative framework for reward hacking across three optimization substrates: weight updates, selection among generated outputs, and persistent prompt revisions. It builds on the Proxy Compression Hypothesis and formalizes a distance-dependent upper bound on evaluator disagreement. The paper is a useful conceptual contribution to AI safety by unifying hacking phenomena that are usually studied separately.

entry.title: DTOC: Dynamic Tool Output Compression for Adaptive Context Management in AI Agents

author.name: Abhay Chaturvedi, Shreya Bhattacharya, Rashmika Gopalkrishnan, Peter van der Putten

entry.summary: DTOC addresses context-window constraints in LLM agents by modeling context updates as explicit, reversible operations: full tool outputs are retained in external memory while compact placeholders occupy the active context, enabling selective reconstruction. It integrates into a ReAct-style agent loop, avoiding the information loss and hallucination risk of truncation or lossy summarization. This is a practical contribution to the increasingly central problem of agent context management.

entry.title: TREND-10K: A Comprehensive Dataset for Next-Generation Video Quality Assessment Based on Preference-Driven Media

author.name: Ziheng Jia, Zicheng Zhang, Junqi Zhang, Jiaying Qian, Jiarui Wang, Yushuo Zheng, Xiongkuo Min

entry.summary: TREND-10K is a 10,000-video dataset for video quality assessment covering shifting media consumption toward short dramas and AIGC entertainment, organized into trend-driven and static parts. It aims to provide a unified evaluation framework for contemporary, diverse video content.

entry.title: REFLEX with Jev for Efficient Selective Control in LLM Agents

author.name: Tiantong Wu, Wei Yang Bryan Lim

entry.summary: REFLEX is an agent architecture using Jev, a fast typed decision layer, that calls a strong LLM only when confidence is low or generation is required, achieving 95% task success on a frozen 100-task benchmark with 72.7% fewer strong-model calls. Controlled interventions show reliability depends on action-set size and near-valid alternatives, and external evaluations show limited advantages over a cheap generative cascade in some settings.

entry.title: Predictive Uncertainty for Neural CAE Surrogates

author.name: Kaustubh Tangsali, Mohammad Amin Nabian, Kelvin Lee, Carmelo Gonzales, Sanjay Choudhry

entry.summary: Evaluates three uncertainty quantification approaches (GP-based, MC dropout, deep ensembles) for geometry-conditioned neural surrogates in computer-aided engineering across three industry datasets for aerodynamics and crash dynamics. Assesses whether predicted uncertainties have credible magnitudes, localize issues, and support design decisions.

entry.title: Evaluating Accuracy and Probabilistic Reliability of Zero-Shot Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Panagiotis Michael, Moysis Symeonides, Demetris Trihinas

entry.summary: This benchmark study evaluates six time series foundation models on energy, traffic, and financial datasets against statistical baselines and a supervised deep model, examining both point accuracy and probabilistic calibration. It finds TSFMs generally outperform baselines but face a fundamental trade-off between point accuracy and probabilistic reliability, with xLSTM architectures calibrating better and patch-based transformers favoring point accuracy.

entry.title: Certified Mechanistic Interpretability: Lifting Single-Input Findings to Bounded Neighbourhoods

author.name: Zhen Zhang, Yanliang Huang, Peng Xie, Wenyuan Wu, Amr Alanwar

entry.summary: This work adds formal guarantees to mechanistic interpretability by lifting single-input circuit observations to certified statements over bounded sets of perturbations, using constrained polynomial-zonotope propagation. The authors formulate internal-attention queries (top-k stability, evidence mass, attention entropy) as tractable programs and show the propagation preserves softmax simplex and LayerNorm identities exactly. This addresses the fragility of one-input-at-a-time interpretability findings.

entry.title: Refusal without Discrimination: What Encoded Prompts Do to Safety-Trained Models

author.name: Haoyu Zhang, Haowen Xu, Xiao Luo, Mohammad Zandsalimy, Shanu Sushmita

entry.summary: The authors show that encoded-prompt attack benchmarks measure almost nothing about the model under test: across four post-trained 7-8B models, refusal of homoglyph-encoded harmful prompts sits inside the range sampling noise alone produces, while plaintext refusal varies widely. What encoding destroys is not refusal but discrimination — one model refuses benign and harmful requests identically at 0.99 under encoding, erasing a +0.82 harmful/benign gap. This reframes encoded-prompt robustness evaluation.

entry.title: When Recursive Models Finish Computing

author.name: Hare Krishna, Shubham Singh, Stephen Ebert, Hao-Yu Sun

entry.summary: Studies completion dynamics of Tiny Recursive Models on 1,000 hard Sudoku puzzles, showing that extending recurrence from 16 to 512 steps raises accuracy from 59.2% to 87.5% (attention) and 74.4% to 91.9% (MLP), solving most puzzles unsolved at the nominal budget. Latent-state motion drops sharply after the first exact solution, offering a signal for detecting genuine completion versus persistent failure.

entry.title: Spectral Tail Interventions in Decoder-Only Language Models: Reasoning-Sensitive Weight Structure from Controlled Surgery

author.name: Ibne Farabi Shihab, Sanjida Akhter, Md Najmus Swaqeeb, Abu Sa-Adat Mohamed Moon-Im Al Ahsan, Anuj Sharma

entry.summary: The paper moves from correlational weight-space observations to causal claims by performing controlled surgical interventions on concentrated upper spectral tails in decoder-only transformers, deriving a finite-width bound linking the inverse participation ratio of squared singular values to logit kurtosis. Comparing independent factor surgery against a product-targeted factorization that preserves native attention computation across three base checkpoints and five reasoning benchmarks, the learned-tail edits reveal reasoning-sensitive weight structure. This establishes that specific spectral structure is computationally involved in reasoning, not merely correlated with behavior.

entry.title: Component Type, Not Reconstruction Error, Predicts Attention Quantization Sensitivity

author.name: Kasun Dewage, Marianna Pensky, Suranadi De Silva

entry.summary: Through 3,808 measurements quantizing one attention projection at a time across nine open-weight models (1.3B-8B parameters, including OPT, GPT-J, LLaMA-1/2/3, Mistral, Qwen 2.5) at 3 and 4 bits under RTN and GPTQ, the authors show that layer-wise reconstruction error does not predict downstream functional impact of quantization. Instead, component type is the dominant predictor of attention quantization sensitivity. This challenges the objective design of widely used post-training quantization methods.

entry.title: MAGIC: Mixed-Granularity Agent Graphs via Incremental Construction with Dense-Reward Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Kairui Yang, Ziheng Yi, Xunkai Li, Minghao An, Zhanke Liu, Zekai Chen, Rong-Hua Li

entry.summary: MAGIC is a framework for LLM-based multi-agent systems that selects collaboration granularity locally for each functional role, mixing individual agents and predefined groups within one organization, learned via incremental construction with dense-reward reinforcement learning. The approach targets the combinatorial search over collaboration topologies with limited intermediate feedback, aiming to improve both performance and execution cost.

entry.title: MIND the Gap: A Geographic Implicit Neural Representation with Adjustable Spatial Scale

author.name: Isaac Corley, Arjun Rao, Esther Rolf, Konstantin Klemmer, Evan Shelhamer, Nils Lehmann, Marc Ru{\ss}wurm, Gengchen Mai, Nathan Jacobs, Hannah Kerner

entry.summary: MIND (Matryoshka Implicit Neural Distillation) distills embeddings from specialist pretrained geospatial models into a single generalist coordinate embedding with adjustable spatial granularity, enabling prediction at unsampled locations from sparse geographic labels without satellite imagery at inference. The work directly tackles the underexplored problem of cross-region generalization in geographic implicit neural representations. It has strong implications for remote sensing and geospatial ML where labels are sparse and unevenly distributed.

entry.title: Damage Predicts Recovery: When Calibration Data Matters in Compressing Financial LLMs

author.name: Junyi Ye, Mengjia Yu, Debapriya Hazra, Guiling Wang

entry.summary: The paper tests whether finance-specific LLMs need domain-matched calibration data for quantization and pruning, across two model families, six compression configurations, three token-matched calibration corpora, and ten financial tasks. Its hypothesis: calibration-corpus choice matters little when compression preserves the target capability, but task-formatted calibration can recover part of the loss when compression causes large damage.

entry.title: SuperPCA: subspace analysis and an efficient algorithm for high-dimensional PCA

author.name: Irina-Beatrice Haas, Maike Meier, Yuji Nakatsukasa, Taejun Park

entry.summary: In the spiked covariance model, the paper proves that the subspace spanned by several leading eigenvectors of the sample covariance contains significant information about the signal directions long before individual eigenvectors converge to population principal components. Building on this, it derives an efficient algorithm for estimating leading signals in high-dimensional PCA.

entry.title: Optimal Sequential Annotations for Off-Policy Evaluation

author.name: Woojin Chae, Ezinne Nwankwo, Haitong Qin, Angela Zhou

entry.summary: This paper studies off-policy evaluation in settings where states and rewards are complex text or images that must be labeled, for example by LLM-as-a-judge with unknown bias or by costly expert annotators. It develops methods to allocate a limited ground-truth annotation budget optimally, deriving variance-optimal annotation probabilities for doubly-robust OPE with missing rewards in the sequential setting. This is significant because it directly addresses a practical reliability problem as LLM-generated labels increasingly replace ground-truth annotation in RL and evaluation pipelines.

entry.title: TopoCompress: Topology Aware Token Compression Algorithm for Distributed Edge MoE Inference

author.name: Ning Li, Xinyu Wang, Xin Yuan, Wenchao Xu, Athanasios V. Vasilakos, Song Guo, Haijun Zhang

entry.summary: TopoCompress is a deployment- and topology-aware token compression framework for distributed edge inference with mixture-of-experts models, jointly optimizing token compression, expert placement, and routing costs across heterogeneous servers. It addresses the inefficiency of optimizing compression and expert placement independently.

entry.title: Hierarchical Aggregation of Semantic Uncertainty in 3D Scene Graphs

author.name: Carlos Cueto Zumaya, Iacopo Catalano, Wallace Moreira Bessa, Julio A. Placed

entry.summary: The authors propose a framework that converts detector confidence and stored vision-language embeddings in open-vocabulary 3D scene graphs into correctness probabilities, propagating them through the containment hierarchy into beliefs about room-level queries. This lets deployed robots distinguish reliable map entries without requiring model resampling or training data at query time.
