Random Forest reaches ROC-AUC 0.87 and F1 0.84, with SHAP analysis showing lexical and grammatical features drive predictions.

entry.title: Complementary rPPG-Derived and Lip-Region Frequency Cues for Talking-Face Deepfake Detection

author.name: Othmane Harraq, Tamer Aldwairi

entry.summary: This work studies two lightweight visual-only cues for talking-face deepfake detection: rPPG-derived waveforms from RhythmFormer and lip-region DCT coefficients, evaluated on seven generators in Celeb-DF++ under subject-independent and leave-one-generator-out protocols. Concat fusion reaches AUC 0.891 in-domain, and the cues show complementary cross-generator transfer behavior.

entry.title: Math2Visual-X: A Modular Framework for Pedagogically Aligned Lower-Primary Math Visuals Generation

author.name: H. D. E. Maduranga, S. K. Munasinghe, K. P. T. I. Weerasekara, Surangika Ranathunga, Nisansa de Silva

entry.summary: Math2Visual-X is a symbolic visual generation framework for lower-primary math word problems with an LLM-based routing layer, three worksheet-oriented generation modules, and fallback mechanisms for open-world SVG asset acquisition. Human evaluation found it outperforms Stable Diffusion XL, Nano Banana, and GPT Image on satisfying exact mathematical constraints.

entry.title: D3GS: Depth, DINO, and RGB Diffusion Co-Guided 3D Gaussian Splatting for Sparse-View Reconstruction

author.name: Yunqi Gao, Zhanfeng Liao, Hanzhang Tu, Zhaoqi Su, Guoqing Zheng, Songtao Wang, Hongwen Zhang, Zhou Xue, Leyuan Liu, Yebin Liu

entry.summary: D3GS improves sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting by jointly enhancing geometry and appearance: diffusion-based depth completion with DPT refinement provides robust Gaussian initialization and geometric constraints, while DINO-guided view-consistent learning augments Gaussian attributes with structural features.

entry.title: Adaptive Cortically Constrained EEG-Vision Alignment for Zero-Shot Brain-to-Image Retrieval

author.name: Ye Wang, Haokun Ren, Wei Wu, Guoyin Wang, Zhuliang Yu, Hong Yu, Ke Liu

entry.summary: This work reconstructs noisy scalp EEG responses into ROI-level cortical source representations and encodes them with a Neuro-ROI Attention Encoder for zero-shot brain-to-image retrieval. An evidence-based adaptive supervision strategy weights visual targets per response, addressing variability in alignment reliability that fixed visual supervision ignores.

entry.title: MIGA:Shared-Geometry Gaussian Representation with Implicit Amplitude Modeling for Accelerated 3D Multi-Echo MRI

author.name: Jingran Xu, Yuanyuan Liu, Yanjie Zhu

entry.summary: MIGA is a scan-specific framework for reconstructing undersampled 3D multi-echo MRI using shared anisotropic Gaussian geometry across echoes, a coordinate-conditioned multi-output amplitude network, and echo-specific phase variables. It exploits shared anatomy while preserving echo-dependent signal variation with reduced computational and memory demands. This addresses a real clinical bottleneck of long acquisition times.

entry.title: 0.5%>100%: Bidirectional Reciprocal Learning for Referring Image Segmentation

author.name: Xiaoqiang Lu, Licheng Jiao, Lingling Li, Yuting Yang, Long Sun, Wenping Ma, Xu Liu, Fang Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes bidirectional reciprocal learning for referring image segmentation, enabling progressive cross-modal interaction and visual feedback for textual refinement within a parameter-efficient fine-tuning setting for vision foundation models. It avoids full fine-tuning costs and catastrophic forgetting while going beyond unidirectional language-to-vision guidance. The catchy title refers to achieving strong gains with only 0.5% trainable parameters.

entry.title: Multicentre Bi-atrial Segmentation from LGE-MRI for Atrial Fibrillation with a 2D and 3D Framework

author.name: Malitha Gunawardhana, Gregory B. Sands, Mark L. Trew, Jichao Zhao

entry.summary: Presents a two-stage segmentation framework and benchmarking platform for bi-atrial wall and cavity delineation in multicentre late gadolinium enhancement MRI, systematically evaluating ROI localization, encoder design, 2D vs 3D dimensionality, and ensemble fusion. Targets a prerequisite for structural analysis and fibrosis quantification in atrial fibrillation.

entry.title: What is the Better Curriculum: Controller-Shaped Grasping Behavior for Contact Force-Sensitive Manipulation

author.name: Ziyan Feng, Zizhao Yuan, Yulong Fu, Yuxin He, Zhiyuan Zhang, Zhengjie Zhang, Jinni Zhou, Renjing Xu, Qiang Nie

entry.summary: For manipulating fragile objects where sub-Newton forces cause damage, this work argues the bottleneck occurs during data collection, where manual teleoperation is too coarse to stay in narrow force ranges. It uses a deterministic 25 Hz tactile reflex controller as a collection-time teacher, producing controller-shaped demonstrations from which tactile-free policies (on ACT) can be trained. This reframes curriculum design as shaping demonstration quality rather than adding tactile inputs to the policy.

entry.title: MatchFusion: Explicit-Implicit Instance Matching for Spatio-Temporal Multimodal Autonomous Driving

author.name: Xiaoyu Li, Jiajia Fu, Long Shi, Tianyu Du, Ruihang Li, Xian Wu, Lijun Zhao, Yingtao Zhang, Lining Sun, Ruifeng Li

entry.summary: MatchFusion is a learnable instance matching and fusion module for spatio-temporal multimodal autonomous driving that combines attention-based contextual matching with efficient, interpretable matching based on structured object states. It targets reliable instance correspondences across LiDAR-camera and temporal dimensions despite geometric and semantic discrepancies.

entry.title: LingLan: An Advancing Traditional Chinese Medicine Diagnosis LLM with Multimodal Data

author.name: Zheng Chen, Zhicheng Du, Haoxuan Li, Yingshan Liang, Peiwu Qin

entry.summary: Introduces a Unification Framework for Multimodal Data that converts tongue and pulse images into structured clinical descriptions spanning the four TCM diagnostic processes, and builds LingLan-14B, a TCM-specific large language model on this structured data. Aims to bridge subjective holistic diagnostics with standardized AI systems.

entry.title: Not Quite My Tempo: Voice Activity-aware Speech Synthesis for Lip-Synchronous Dubbing

author.name: Alejandro P\'erez-Gonz\'alez-de-Martos, Florian Lux, Angelina Elizarova, Milana Shkhanukova, Andreas Kellner, Mattia Antonino Di Gangi

entry.summary: Conditions speech synthesis for lip-synchronous dubbing on a binary voice-activity signal rather than lip movements extracted from video, generating alternating voice and silence patterns matching the source clip timing. The approach achieves high timing accuracy while preserving natural prosody and appropriate pause placement, validated via objective and subjective evaluation.

entry.title: The Disciplinary Language Transfer Problem: How Psychological Vocabulary Produces Governance Failures in AI Agent Deployment

author.name: Kymberly Lasser-Chere, Tyler Akidau, Marc Millstone

entry.summary: Argues that governance discourse about AI agents borrows psychological vocabulary (memory, values, trust, compliance) that imports an invisible disciplinary grammar, calibrating frameworks to a metaphysical entity absent from current AI architectures, causing systematic deployment and oversight failures. The authors ground the argument in Wittgenstein, Kuhn, and Haraway and name this the disciplinary language transfer problem.

entry.title: Spatiotemporal Kronecker Covariance Neural Networks

author.name: Andrea Cavallo, Athanasios Georgoutsos, Elvin Isufi

entry.summary: KVNN is a temporal graph neural network that represents spatiotemporal covariance matrices as sums of Kronecker products, decoupling spatial and temporal dependencies while capturing correlations across time steps. It improves on spatiotemporal PCA and existing covariance-based networks that ignore cross-time correlations.

entry.title: AURA: Angular Update Rate Adaptation for training complex-valued neural networks

author.name: Enrico Ballini, Allan Peter Engsig-Karup, Tito Andriollo

entry.summary: AURA is a per-parameter step-size adaptation method for complex-valued neural networks that exploits angular information in the complex plane, measuring agreement between consecutive updates in length, alignment, and rotation sense. It can be added on top of any first-order optimizer without altering update directions and removed cleanly afterward. This fills a real gap, as CVNNs typically inherit real-valued step-size heuristics that ignore complex geometry.

entry.title: Learnable Classifier-Free Guidance Null Embeddings for Enhanced Controllable Speech Synthesis

author.name: Biel Tura Vecino, Yoach Lacombe, Julian Weber, Zbigniew {\L}atka, Haitong Zhang, Logan Hart, Eren G\"olge

entry.summary: The authors replace the fixed null vector used for unconditional predictions in classifier-free guidance for TTS with a learnable unconditional embedding optimized to represent a meaningful unconditional state. Objective and subjective evaluations show consistent gains in speaker similarity, stability, and expressiveness, plus robustness to larger guidance scales. This is a simple, broadly applicable tweak to CFG-based generative audio systems.

entry.title: Unlocking Cross-Scenario Physical Layer Security: A Mixture-of-Experts Framework with Generative Diffusion Models

author.name: Xiao Tang, Tong Hui, Chao Shen, Yichen Wang, Qinghe Du, Li Sun, Zhu Han

entry.summary: The paper proposes a mixture-of-experts framework for cross-scenario physical-layer security in anticipated 6G networks, training scenario-specific generative diffusion model experts for secure transmission beamforming with adaptive routing among experts. The goal is robust security provisioning across diverse wireless environments without full recomputation per scenario.

entry.title: Retrieved-Span Training for Efficient Query-Focused Meeting Summarization on QMSum

author.name: Edward Xi Yang (Ertas AI)

entry.summary: The paper rescores or generates 15 systems under one implementation to address QMSum's lack of a shared scorer, and shows that a released 406M Fusion-in-Decoder specialist loses 6.30 ROUGE-1 when moved to 2,000-word retrieved spans but recovers with span-regime fine-tuning. The resulting small system statistically ties a 1.2B system while using about one-third the parameters and less than half the peak inference memory.

entry.title: Challenges of Multi-Speaker Extraction for Real Conversational Speech Enhancement

author.name: Robert Sutherland, Stefan Goetze, Jon Barker

entry.summary: This work examines the gap between simulated training conditions and real multi-party conversations for target/multi-speaker extraction, noting that real conversations feature long silences and enrolment samples that differ from target speech. The authors propose a new loss function to better handle these real-world conditions.

entry.title: Combining Foundation Model Confidence and Monocular Depth for Training-Free Out-of-Distribution Segmentation

author.name: Serin Varghese, Fabian H\"uger, Kira Maag

entry.summary: This paper proposes a training-free method for segmenting out-of-distribution objects in autonomous driving scenes, deriving dense OOD scores from the confidence predictions of a foundation segmentation model combined with monocular depth. It avoids the need for OOD training samples, backbone retraining, or auxiliary architectures.

entry.title: BiView-Touch: Learning Bimanual Tactile Representations by Cross-Hand Completion

author.name: Chenxin Liang, Youchen Lai, Chuqiao Lyu, Tianxing Chen, Shoujie Li, Wenbo Ding

entry.summary: BiView-Touch is a tactile-only representation learning framework that exploits the complementary tactile views produced by bimanual interaction, completing masked target-hand latents from visible regions and the synchronized contralateral hand. A student encoder with a geometry-conditioned directional decoder predicts full-view EMA latent targets, with temporal and layout counterfactuals encouraging sensitivity to synchronized, anatomically organized information.

entry.title: VISTA: Video-Injected Stylized Text-to-Animation

author.name: Monseej Purkayastha, Anindita Ghosh, Philipp Slusallek

entry.summary: VISTA generates stylized 3D human motion by fusing text-defined structure with style extracted from reference videos, without requiring paired text-video-motion training triplets. It uses a dual-channel autoencoder into a shared latent manifold and a masked autoregressive diffusion backbone with a Dual-AdaLN late-fusion pathway, trained with a cross-batch unpaired protocol and latent cycle consistency.

entry.title: Video-STLayout Pre-training

author.name: Akash Abdu Jyothi, Greg Mori

entry.summary: Video-STLayout is a pre-training strategy that aligns video encoder features with spatio-temporal layout features derived from object bounding boxes, obtainable cheaply from an off-the-shelf detector, via a contrastive loss with a trained layout encoder. The layout-informed representations transfer to downstream tasks including activity recognition.

entry.title: Action-Slot: Structured Action-Centric Representation Learning for Multi-Agent Atomic Activity Understanding

author.name: Yu-Ho Chang, Chi-Hsi Kung, Yi-Hsuan Tsai, Yi-Ting Chen

entry.summary: Action-Slot reformulates slot attention for atomic traffic activity understanding, replacing permutation-invariant object-centric slots with category-aligned action slots and structured activity decomposition. The framework jointly encodes motion patterns and their grounding in road topology for multi-agent, multi-label recognition and localization.

entry.title: DeCo: Efficient Decouple-to-Couple Learning for Multi-Task Visual Grounding

author.name: Xiaoqiang Lu, Licheng Jiao, Long Sun, Yuting Yang, Xu Liu, Lingling Li, Wenping Ma, Fang Liu

entry.summary: DeCo is a two-stage framework for multi-task visual grounding that first decouples task-specific representations and then couples them through complementary priors, addressing the conflict between task-oriented feature interests that shared-representation methods ignore. It adapts multimodal large language models to multiple grounding objectives efficiently. The framework targets joint semantic understanding with localization and segmentation.

entry.title: Virtual neural networks: hundreds of souls in a body

author.name: Petr Hurtik, Marek Vajgl, Zahra Alijani, Vojtech Molek

entry.summary: The paper introduces virtual neural networks, where trainable parameters stay constant while scalability comes from generating hundreds of virtual models sharing weights derived from a small set of physical models, merging siamese networks with deep ensembles. The interconnected virtual ensemble induces internal distortion that boosts robustness, with accuracy improving as virtual network count grows.

entry.title: CDKF-Track: Cluster-aware Data-Driven Kalman Filtering for Cooperative 3D Multi-Object Tracking

author.name: Maria Damanaki, Nikos Piperigkos, Alexandros Gkillas, Aris S. Lalos

entry.summary: CDKF-Track is a cooperative 3D multi-object tracking framework that fuses multi-vehicle LiDAR detections via a Graph Laplacian formulation and applies cluster-aware, data-driven Kalman filtering to handle redundant measurements, false associations, and nonlinear dynamics. It targets EdgeAI perception for safe autonomous decision-making.

entry.title: Dual Covariance Gaussian Splatting SLAM: Decoupling Rendering and Registration for Robust Real-Time Tracking

author.name: Edward Beng Wai Tan, Siew-Kei Lam

entry.summary: This work identifies a conflict in ICP-based 3D Gaussian Splatting SLAM where one Gaussian covariance must serve both photometric rendering and robust frame registration, and proposes a dual-covariance parameterization keeping separate rendering and tracking covariances per Gaussian. Tracking covariances derived from an RGB-D noise model also serve as anchors for image corners, adding directional constraints. The result is more robust real-time tracking in 3DGS SLAM systems.

entry.title: The AI Neuroscientist: An Interactive Agentic Interface for Neuroimaging Analysis

author.name: Aakash Patel, Panos Ketonis, Shreya Saxena, Smita Krishnaswamy, David van Dijk

entry.summary: This paper presents an LLM-based agent that integrates a neuroimaging toolset for interactive quality control, modeling, and visualization of neuroimaging data via natural language. Demonstrated on fNIRS data with a custom benchmark, it lowers the computational barrier for researchers lacking coding expertise.

entry.title: ChatT2: An Adaptive Framework for Developing a Large Language Model-Based Agent for Natural Product Domain Research

author.name: Yihan Wang, Qiandi Gao, Yihui Zhuang, Liangjun Ge, Heqian Zhang, Jiaquan Huang, Zhiwei Qin

entry.summary: Introduces ChatT2, an LLM agent for research on bacterial type II polyketides, built via an autonomous multiagent development loop of mentor, executor, and evaluator. It aims to lower barriers for novices in complex natural-product and bioinformatics workflows.

entry.title: When Are Aggregate Agent Traces Diagnosable? Traffic-Governed Interpretation and Calibrated Abstention

author.name: Peiying Zhu, Sidi Chang

entry.summary: This paper studies when aggregate runtime traces of an agent (a simulated hotel-pricing agent) are actually diagnosable, noting that a closed-loop policy may rarely visit states where a fault manifests, leaving no visible trace evidence. It proposes a gated pipeline with reference-map and matched-runtime support tests, plus calibrated abstention, before attempting fault interpretation. This matters because it formalizes a precondition for agent debugging and observability that most trace-analysis work ignores.

entry.title: AgenticSizing: A Large Language Model-based Multi-Agent Framework for Analog Circuit Sizing

author.name: Yijia Hao, Pratibha Verma, Dongxu Guo, Cristian Sestito, Michael O'Boyle, Christos-Savvas Bouganis, Themis Prodromakis

entry.summary: AgenticSizing is a multi-agent LLM framework for analog circuit sizing that analyzes circuit topology, decomposes netlists into functional blocks, and extracts reusable design knowledge before optimization. It targets more complex circuits than prior LLM-based sizing approaches, which lack topology understanding. The work demonstrates LLM agents extending into specialized EDA domains.

entry.title: FairMon: A Tool for Monitoring and Visualizing Algorithmic Fairness

author.name: Jan Baumeister, Bernd Finkbeiner, Vladimir Krsmanovic, Frederik Scheerer, Julian Siber, Tobias Wagenpfeil

entry.summary: FairMon is a runtime monitoring tool for algorithmic fairness of high-stakes autonomous decision systems (credit, hiring, criminal justice), built on the RTLola monitoring language and motivated by oversight requirements of the EU AI Act. It addresses shortcomings of existing monitoring tools that were not designed for fairness oversight in critical scenarios. The tool bridges formal runtime verification and practical fairness compliance.

entry.title: The Cost of Conservation: Coordination-Memory Laws for Exact-Support Generation

author.name: Zhen Zhang, Amr Alanwar

entry.summary: This theory paper studies product measures conditioned on additive conservation laws (e.g., selecting exactly a fixed number of items), showing that communication-free coordinate-parallel generation requires exponentially many pre-shared plans while a sequential exact sampler needs only logarithmic memory. It characterizes an intermediate regime of bounded-state stochastic executors whose support is entirely legal. The results formalize fundamental coordination-memory trade-offs for constrained generation.

entry.title: Unanimity Without Persuasion: A Single Round of Debate Erases the Disagreement That Verification Needs

author.name: Yang Shu

entry.summary: This paper shows that one round of multi-agent debate can erase judge disagreement without improving accuracy: on 600 code-correctness candidates, panel unanimity jumps from 39.5% to 95.2% in one round while accuracy moves less than one point and 96.3% of verdict flips follow the displayed peer majority. Since substituted verification ballots only matter on narrow-margin votes, debate destroying disagreement undermines downstream targeting signals. This is a cautionary finding for debate-based verification and oversight schemes.

entry.title: RCShift: Certifying When Partial Linkage Suffices for Finite-Sample Decisions

author.name: Shuheng Cao, Ruiqi Chen, Zhenhao Zhang, Renjie Cao, Siyu Zhang, Lingwei Dang, Jiajun Zhang, Tingting Dan

entry.summary: RCShift certifies when partial record linkage suffices for finite-sample decisions in systems with costly gold outcomes and cheaper auxiliary observations, offering exact and approximate modes for minimum-cost storage and bounds on reverse Le Cam deficiency. It calibrates how much linkage to retain against a declared observation contract.

entry.title: A Hybrid AI Framework for Academic Advising: Integrating Ensemble-Based Grade Prediction and a Rule-Based Expert System

author.name: Hamid Saadatfar, Rohollah Hedayati-Nasab, AmirHossein Eshghi, Arash Hajihashemi

entry.summary: This study builds an academic advising system combining clustering, a stacking ensemble (Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, MLP) for grade prediction, and a rule-based recommendation engine, trained on 416,558 student records from the University of Birjand. The stacking model outperformed base learners across the clusters.

entry.title: Reproducible AI Requires Reproducible Randomness

author.name: Anthony Bertrand (UCA, LIMOS), Tom Schmitt (UCA), Engelbert Mephu Nguifo (LIMOS, UCA), David Hill (INP Clermont Auvergne, ISIMA, LIMOS, UCA)

entry.summary: The paper examines PRNG reproducibility across software environments, arguing that reproducibility of Monte Carlo, stochastic computing, and AI applications depends on generating identical sequences from the same internal state, including states that exceed conventional integer seed capacity. It analyzes pitfalls in modern PRNG initialization across software environments.

entry.title: Neutral-Atom-based Quantum Optimization for Resource Allocation in NOMA Networks

author.name: Patatchona Keyela, Remon Polus, Soumaya Cherkaoui, Ola Ahmad

entry.summary: The paper applies neutral-atom quantum computing to the maximum access problem in NOMA wireless networks, formulated as mixed-integer programming jointly covering admission control, user clustering, channel assignment, and power allocation. It maps the NP-hard combinatorial problem onto an annealing-style quantum platform leveraging superposition and entanglement.

entry.title: AIBuildAI-2.5: Efficient Autonomous AI Model Development Through LLM-Guided Tree Search

author.name: Peijia Qin, Ruiyi Zhang, Qi Cao, Han Guo, Li Zhang, Pengtao Xie

entry.summary: Presents an autonomous agent that builds AI models by framing model development as code search with LLM-guided tree search, addressing efficiency weaknesses of reward-ranked search where only a few candidates can be executed. Targets broadening access to AI model engineering beyond experienced practitioners.

entry.title: From Pattern Recognizers to Personalized Companions: A Survey of Large Language Models in Mental Health

author.name: He Hu, Yucheng Zhou, Qianning Wang, Yingjian Zou, Chiyuan Ma, Juzheng Si, Jianzhuang Liu, Zitong Yu, Laizhong Cui, Fei Ma, Qi Tian

entry.summary: A survey organizing the fragmented literature on LLMs for mental health support around an evolutionary thesis of moving from pattern recognizers to personalized companions, motivated by access barriers like cost, stigma, and privacy. It contextualizes progress and outlines future directions for a fast-growing application area.

entry.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning on Item-Compatibility Graphs for One-Dimensional Bin Packing

author.name: M. Asl{\i} Ayd{\i}n

entry.summary: Proposes an end-to-end, size-agnostic graph reinforcement learning framework for one-dimensional bin packing, formulating packing as a Markov decision process on an item-compatibility graph where actions merge compatible partial bins. Fills a gap since most learned solvers target 2D/3D variants of this NP-hard problem.

entry.title: An Exploratory Replica-Overlap Probe of the Grokking Transition

author.name: A. C. Opus, J. Q. Lu

entry.summary: The authors trained 64 independently seeded networks to probe whether a replica-symmetry-breaking-inspired distribution of pairwise weight overlaps changes across the grokking transition. The paper candidly reports that the registered implementation's permutation-based alignment does not preserve network function, so its weight-overlap statistics are defective, while function-overlap measures remain valid.

entry.title: Interweaving Marginals into Multivariate Sample Paths: Training-Free Dependence Construction for Probabilistic Time Series Foundation Models

author.name: Jinmyeong Choi, Jinkwan Jang, Seul Lee, Taesup Kim

entry.summary: This paper addresses a gap in probabilistic time series foundation models: they produce coordinate-wise marginal distributions but not a coherent joint distribution over multivariate futures. The authors propose a training-free method to couple frozen marginals into multivariate sample paths, carefully evaluating with a fixed-marginal constraint to isolate the effect of dependence modeling. The results show historical temporal and channel relations measurably improve dependence diagnostics.

entry.title: TTTIR: Unlocking Instance-Specific State Evolution via Test-Time Training for Image Restoration

author.name: Kaihang Zheng, Jun Li, Hang Guo, Hongyu Chi, Zimo Liu, Tao Dai, Jinpeng Wang, Yaowei Wang

entry.summary: TTTIR reformulates image restoration as an instance-specific state evolution process using test-time training, addressing the failure of static globally shared parameters to handle input-dependent degradations. The framework adds explicit guidance to the standard self-supervised inner loop to help degraded features transition toward clean structures. It aims to make data-dependent operators practical for restoration tasks.

entry.title: Magnitude Profile Pruning: Calibration-Free Structured Attention Head Removal for Transformer Compression

author.name: Kasun Dewage, Marianna Pensky, Heranga K. Rathnasekara, Suranadi De Silva

entry.summary: The paper introduces Magnitude Profile scoring, a training-free criterion for structured attention-head pruning that identifies dispensable heads via statistical outlier detection on weight row norms, requiring no calibration data, gradients, or Hessian estimates. Heads with outlier norms are preserved as carrying disproportionate representational capacity, and an MP-G variant handles grouped query attention. This makes head-level Transformer compression cheaper and data-independent.

entry.title: Dynamic Deep Prompt Optimization for Defending Against Jailbreak Attacks on LLMs

author.name: Doniyorkhon Obidov, Honggang Yu, Xiaolong Guo, Kaichen Yang

entry.summary: DDPO is presented as the first jailbreak defense based on deep prompt optimization, using the target LLM's own intermediate layers as feature extractors to dynamically generate defensive embeddings. Unlike static prefix/suffix defenses, it adapts to diverse and evolving attacks without costly fine-tuning that risks catastrophic forgetting. The approach aims to close the adaptability gap in prompt-based safety defenses.

entry.title: WatchPoint: Executable User Feedback for Real-World Agentic Web Development

author.name: Guanqun Yang, Wei Yang, Xueqing Liu

entry.summary: WatchPoint is a simulated-user system that mimics professional developer debugging behavior by generating and executing diagnostic scripts against a running web application, producing structured observations that guide a coding agent's retries. This departs from screenshot-based or LLM-as-judge feedback and from evaluation on non-executable settings. It targets more realistic feedback loops for agentic web development.

entry.title: A Semiotics-Aware Framework for Evaluating Fidelity and Coverage in Natural Language Generation

author.name: Lorenzo Zangari, Davide Picca

entry.summary: Proposes a framework evaluating semiotic alignment between texts, yielding Semiotic Fidelity and Semiotic Coverage scores that capture contextual meaning and discourse references beyond lexical overlap. Experiments show coverage is typically lower than fidelity and that LLM-human alignment is highest at low sampling temperatures.

entry.title: Measuring the Serving Stack Instead of the Model: Hidden Confounds in Local Tool-Use Evaluation

author.name: Lijuan Tang, Yuemeng Zheng

entry.summary: The authors show that local LLM serving stacks confound tool-use evaluations: in Ollama, a static per-model template flag gates whether tool-call requests are accepted, and some models like Phi-3 and Gemma-3 are rejected before inference. Harness behaviors such as rejection and retry exhaustion can be misclassified as model non-calls, distorting reported tool-use fidelity.

entry.title: Extending FunctionGemma for Practical On-Device Mobile Function Calling

author.name: Ali Rezagholizadeh, Soheila Samiee

entry.summary: The authors extend FunctionGemma 270M-it for Android device-control function calling via a synthetic, schema-validated dataset of about 9,500 conversations across fifteen categories, fine-tuned with completion-only loss under TRL. They produce a specialist model and a combined model trained with Google's MOBILEACTIONSGOOGLE data, evaluating on-device practicality.

entry.title: A Lightweight Plastic-Memory Framework for Graph Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Zihan Mei, Zhili Qin, Tongze Zhang, Hongyuan Liu, Junming Shao, Qinli Yang

entry.summary: The authors propose a lightweight plastic-memory module for few-shot class-incremental learning on graphs that continuously updates and expands memory to accommodate new classes, avoiding the high costs of replay or distillation used in prior catastrophic-forgetting approaches. This targets realistic settings where labeled data for new classes is scarce. It addresses an underexplored intersection of graph learning, few-shot learning, and continual learning.

entry.title: Theory for groupoid equivariant neural networks: an approach for steerable CNNs on bounded domains

author.name: Alberto Ibort, Maria Jimenez-Vazquez, Juan M. Perez-Pardo

entry.summary: This theoretical work generalizes equivariant neural networks from global group symmetry to groupoids, capturing settings where symmetry holds only locally or breaks down at boundaries of bounded or stratified domains. The authors prove a bisection-equivariant kernel theorem showing equivariance amounts to a transport constraint on the two-point kernel, characterizing the solution space. This provides a rigorous foundation for steerable CNNs on domains where rigid global symmetry assumptions fail.

entry.title: MICRO: Multi-Fidelity Active Search for Severe Error Discovery

author.name: Orlando Leone, Niclas Pokel, Pehu\'en Moure, Yingqiang Gao, Roman Boehringer

entry.summary: MICRO is an active search framework that allocates a fixed annotation budget between cheap quality ratings and expensive expert feedback to maximize the discovery of severe errors, jointly modeling both feedback types and clustering candidates by predicted impact with rollout-based value estimation. On WMT20 English-German it shows ratings improve loss reconstruction and severity prediction. This is a practical contribution to budget-aware quality control for human feedback pipelines.

entry.title: Towards Adaptive Federated Graph Clustering: A Global Community-aware Contrastive Learning-based Approach

author.name: Yinlin Zhu, Di Wu, Wang Luo, Guocong Quan, Miao Hu

entry.summary: This paper targets federated graph clustering, an underexplored unsupervised setting in federated graph learning, and identifies two flaws in prior work: unrealistic pre-defined cluster cardinality assumptions and inconsistent handling of client-specific community structure from subgraph heterogeneity. It proposes a global community-aware contrastive learning approach that adapts cluster structure across clients. This advances privacy-preserving unsupervised learning over distributed graph data.

entry.title: Margin-Drop Coordinates for Cross-Budget Robustness Evaluation

author.name: Yanliang Huang, Zhen Zhang, Peng Xie, Wenyuan Wu, Sitong Zhu, Zhuoqi Zeng, Amr Alanwar

entry.summary: This work asks whether cheap, shallow robustness evaluations of frozen vision encoders contain enough signal to predict fragility under stronger attack budgets. It defines three normalized margin-drop coordinates (clean margin slack, one-step shortfall, and iterative drift) computed per clean-correct sample, and studies how these coordinates relate to robustness loss when evaluation budget is increased. The goal is to avoid selecting encoders that look robust only at low attack budgets.

entry.title: Information-Theoretic Decoupled Prompt Tuning for Continual Learning

author.name: Yunfei Zhang, Wen Wen, Tieliang Gong, Weizhan Zhang

entry.summary: DPT4CL addresses two chronic problems in prompt-based continual learning, retrieval dependence and recency bias, by decoupling the CLIP textual prompt into a task-shared prompt distribution optimized via an Information Bottleneck-style objective plus class-specific prompts. This reduces sensitivity to prompt selection and bias toward newly arrived classes. It is an incremental but well-targeted improvement to parameter-efficient continual learning with vision-language models.

entry.title: On the Effect of Bit-Level Parameter Perturbations in Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models

author.name: Akanksha Raghapur, Mark Stamp

entry.summary: The authors study how small, targeted bit-level modifications to model parameters affect classical models (HMMs, SVMs) compared to deep models (MLPs, LSTMs) on the Drebin Android malware dataset. They find classical models are brittle under limited parameter edits and additionally probe the steganographic capacity of these models.

entry.title: PreGS: A Parameter-Transfer-Based Multi-Expert Graph Neural Network for Node Classification

author.name: Zhicong Cai, Yinglong Zhang, Xiaoying Hong, Xuewen Xia, Xing Xu

entry.summary: PreGS is a multi-expert graph neural network framework that pretrains a multi-head graph attention network and transfers its first-layer attention weights to multiple frozen GraphSAGE experts for node classification. The design aims to capture diverse structural patterns across graph datasets while avoiding the overhead of independently training multiple structural branches.

entry.title: EquivSVA: A Formally Verified Dataset of Behavioral Assertions Across Equivalent RTL Implementations

author.name: FNU Aditi

entry.summary: EquivSVA is a formally verified dataset for SystemVerilog Assertion generation organized around behavior families, each containing four structurally distinct RTL implementations of the same externally observable behavior with shared interface-level gold properties and controls. It enables studying whether LLM-generated assertions capture externally observable behavior rather than incidental details of one RTL implementation.

entry.title: What Does 99% Accuracy Measure? A Reproducible Audit of Shortcut Learning in a Widely Used Fake News Corpus

author.name: Yuvraj Verma

entry.summary: The paper audits the widely used ISOT/Kaggle fake news corpus, showing classifiers report above 0.98 accuracy largely through leakage: a classifier using only the subject metadata field achieves F1 of 1.000 because the classes have disjoint subjects. The authors quantify three leakage channels and two distribution-shift protocols with a transparent TF-IDF pipeline and release all code and derived numbers.

entry.title: GINIO: A Geometric SO(3)-Equivariant Interface for Neural Inertial Odometry

author.name: Chankyo Kim, Minghan Zhu, Tzu-Yuan Lin, Avantika Rattan, Maani Ghaffari

entry.summary: GINIO provides an SO(3)-equivariant interface so that neural motion measurements and uncertainties from IMU data transform correctly as vectors and second-order tensors under arbitrary sensor-frame rotations. It introduces Last-Frame Alignment, a deterministic preprocessing step provably equivalent to world-frame training for SO(3), enabling efficient sensor-frame learning. This bridges learned neural measurements with classical filtering pipelines for inertial odometry.

entry.title: Generalized Deep Regression for Repeated Measurements

author.name: Kexuan Li

entry.summary: This theoretical work establishes oracle inequalities and minimax rates for ReLU neural networks estimating marginal regression functions from repeated measurements (binary, count, continuous), where within-unit dependence comes from an unobserved random mean function. It derives non-asymptotic integrated MSE bounds of order n^-1 + (nm)^(-2beta/(2beta+d)) over Hoelder classes.

entry.title: Mining Legal Arguments in U.S. Corporate Case Law

author.name: Luis Brena, William Jurayj, Gregory Deyesu, Zaid Al-Huneidi, Andrew Blair-Stanek, Benjamin Van Durme

entry.summary: The paper introduces an expert-annotated dataset of 42 U.S. federal tax opinions on corporate reorganizations under I.R.C. Section 368, the first expert-annotated tree-structured argument corpus for this domain. Spans receive one of five functional labels, with Rule, Analysis, and Conclusion spans linked into directed support trees, and agreement analysis shows functional labels are reliably annotatable.

entry.title: BELXTR: Biomedical Entity Linking via Contextualized Token Retrieval

author.name: Samuele Garda, Ulf Leser

entry.summary: BELXTR applies multi-vector late-interaction retrieval to biomedical entity linking, avoiding the information loss of single-vector embedding compression by leveraging token-level matching. It extends the XTR model with a task-specific training objective and active query expansion, evaluating across ten corpora. Entity linking is foundational for biomedical information extraction pipelines.

entry.title: Differentiable Fuzzy Inference Layer: A Monotone, Compositional Ordinal Reasoning Head for Large Language Models

author.name: Zhen Zhang, Amr Alanwar

entry.summary: DFIL is a dual-path prediction head pairing a standard classifier with a scalar-bottlenecked branch built from ordered membership functions, giving LLMs monotonicity and algebraic composition over ordinal categories. It targets failures like interpreting nested quantifiers such as most-of-most, attributed to architectural rather than data limitations. The work connects fuzzy logic and structured output heads with language model reasoning.

entry.title: Beyond Short Segments : Expanding Speaker Embeddings with Vector Archives

author.name: Hyunku Kang, Minkyu Cho, Chanwoo Kim

entry.summary: The paper introduces VAM-ECAPA, a speaker verification system that improves feature extraction from short utterances using a Transformer-based module mapping sparse features against a learnable Vector Archive of canonical speaker traits. Integrated into a WavLM+ECAPA-TDNN baseline, it produces more robust speaker representations for short segments.

entry.title: X-Beat: An Explainable Framework for ECG Image Classification

author.name: Mohammad Sadman Tahsin, Haitham Y. Adarbah, Afzel Noore

entry.summary: X-Beat is a reliability-aware benchmark framework for ECG image classification combining transfer learning with post-hoc explainability across four cardiac classes including myocardial infarction. It aims to support trustworthy clinical deployment through systematic transparency and reliability validation.

entry.title: SatOV: Restoring Spatial Priors for Training-Free Open-Vocabulary Segmentation in Remote Sensing Imagery

author.name: Changhao Zhao, Linglin Zeng, Hai Liu

entry.summary: SatOV is a training-free framework for open-vocabulary semantic segmentation of remote sensing imagery that restores spatial priors lost in vision-language foundation models due to image-level classification design and downsampling. It targets the complementary deficiencies of degraded structural relations and lost fine-grained spatial detail at two stages of the representation pipeline.

entry.title: VDGS: Visibility-Driven Large-Scale 3D Gaussian Splatting for Aerial Scene Reconstruction

author.name: Haolin Yu, Jiadong Tang, YiXian Wang, Yu Gao, Shi He, Zhilin Lai, Yi Yang, Mengyin Fu

entry.summary: VDGS tackles large-scale aerial 3D Gaussian Splatting by incorporating camera distribution into scene modeling, using visibility-driven statistics for scene anchors to quantify supervision, addressing excessive memory consumption and uneven viewpoint coverage from UAV acquisition.

entry.title: QwenVLConnector: A Fast, Unified Medical VLM Chatbot for Fine-Grained Clinical Perception and Text Generation

author.name: Le Thien Phuc Nguyen, Thien Nguyen, Thanh-Huy Nguyen, Gia Minh Hoang, Anh Mai Vu, Ulas Bagci

entry.summary: QwenVLConnector is a medical chatbot built on Qwen2.5-VL that unifies classification, multi-label classification, detection textualization, counting, regression, and report generation under a single next-token objective. Its lightweight dense multi-layer Connector fuses low- and high-level visual features with the final visual representation without increasing sequence length.

entry.title: RSPDBench: Benchmarking Vision Foundation Models on Earth Observation Tasks Under Physically Grounded Remote-Sensing Product Degradations

author.name: Tanjim Bin Faruk, Khondaker Masfiq Reza, Shrideep Pallickara, Sangmi Lee Pallickara

entry.summary: RSPDBench evaluates vision foundation models on Earth observation tasks under physically grounded product-level degradations (spatial, radiometric, alignment, noise, harmonization) rather than generic corruptions. It spans five EO datasets, seven foundation models, and two supervised baselines under audited primitive degradations and compound degradation chains.

entry.title: SewFusion: Tailored Generation of Topology and Panel-Level Geometry for Sewing Patterns

author.name: Jiaxin Lin, Xiao Pan, Hangjie Yuan, Luyan Liang, Wan Li, Daquan Feng

entry.summary: SewFusion is a unified autoregressive framework for generating sewing patterns from images and text, using tailored generation mechanisms for the discrete topology of panels versus the continuous panel-level geometry, via next-token prediction. It aims to bridge the gap between diffusion methods that weaken discrete topology modeling and autoregressive methods that tie continuous regression to token-level hidden states with limited panel context.

entry.title: Transferring Visual Explanations: How Cross-Architecture Knowledge Distillation Affects Model Interpretability

author.name: Aleks Czufarow, Ihor Babin

entry.summary: The study investigates whether knowledge distillation transfers the spatial feature attribution of a large teacher to a compact student, distilling ResNet-152 into ResNet-34 on ImageNet-1K across five configurations with varied distillation temperature and soft-label weight. Models are evaluated on top-1 accuracy plus two interpretability metrics, Relevance Mass Accuracy and Relevance Rank Accuracy, motivated by interpretability needs in safety-critical deployments.

entry.title: PETR: Prompt Ensembling with Training-free Routing for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Weihan Cai, Hao Tan, Xinping Gao, Shibiao Xu, Jun Wan

entry.summary: PETR addresses the tension between seen-class discrimination and unseen-class generalization in prompt learning for vision-language models by learning two complementary prompts under different data and objectives on a frozen CLIP backbone. At inference, a training-free routing mechanism uses similarity of each test sample to seen data, informed by training-set logit statistics, to select which prompt to apply.

entry.title: Mind the Gaps: A Curated Benchmark for Form Field Detection

author.name: Iheb Brini, Omar Moured, Hamza Gbada, Elisa Barney

entry.summary: The paper introduces mini-CommonForms, a carefully curated benchmark for Form Field Detection with consistent high-quality annotations, addressing the noisy heuristic labels of existing large-scale datasets. It provides an evaluation of state-of-the-art detection approaches, highlighting that FFD is hard because fields are defined by layout structure and whitespace rather than visible content.

entry.title: PRISM-RAG: Multimodal Hypergraph Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Tobacco Product and Legislative Policy Reasoning

author.name: Manuel Serna-Aguilera, Raegan Anderes, Page Dobbs, Khoa Luu

entry.summary: PRISM-RAG addresses inter-context conflict in retrieval-augmented generation, where semantically similar statutes across US jurisdictions cause models to give confidently wrong jurisdiction-specific answers about tobacco regulation. It uses multimodal hypergraph retrieval to identify which jurisdiction law governs a product rather than merely retrieving topically relevant text.

entry.title: InterHier: Learning Interconnected Hierarchical Semantics for Open-Vocabulary Object Detection

author.name: Yeong-Jin Kim, Ho-Joong Kim, Seong-Whan Lee

entry.summary: InterHier improves open-vocabulary object detection by replacing fixed hand-crafted connectors between adjacent super- and sub-categories with learnable interconnected hierarchical semantics, using a prepended learnable context to globally guide interpretation of hierarchy-aware prompts. It constructs hierarchy-aware prompt representations in two stages to better relate base and novel categories.

entry.title: Positive Pair Geometry Matters: Optimal Transport for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations

author.name: Akshit Nanda, Shahzad Ahmad, Ram Prasad Padhy

entry.summary: OTCLR improves contrastive self-supervised learning by constructing geometry-consistent positive samples via entropic optimal-transport displacement interpolation between original images and their augmentations, rather than using independently sampled augmented views. The interpolated views respect the intrinsic geometry of the data distribution.

entry.title: Beyond Emotion Prompts: Fine-Grained Text-to-Image Generation Driven by Valence-Arousal-Dominance

author.name: Minglang Li, Yueyue Fang, Xieping Gao

entry.summary: EMOTRANS transforms psychologically grounded valence-arousal-dominance (VAD) coordinates into content-independent generation conditions modulated across denoising stages, making emotional style an adjustable control variable in text-to-image generation. It also introduces EMOVAD, an art-painting dataset pairing objective content descriptions with collected emotional ratings.

entry.title: AnalogDepth: Multi-view Geometry from FPV drones under Analog Video Transmission

author.name: Andr\'e Amorim, Pedro F. Proen\c{c}a

entry.summary: AnalogDepth adapts the Depth Anything 3 foundation model to analog FPV drone video, where spatially structured transmission noise severely degrades accuracy. It uses parameter-efficient student-teacher distillation with LoRA in the DINOv2 backbone and real analog data rather than synthetic noise. This matters for the large FPV drone community where analog video transmission remains standard due to low latency and cost.

entry.title: Spatial Action Review: A Visual Analytics Dashboard for Auditing Language-to-Action Hand-offs in Electron Microscopy

author.name: Samia Mohinta, Albert Cardona

entry.summary: The paper identifies the language-to-action hand-off failure mode in MLLM-based scientific image analysis, where a correct textual answer is paired with a spatial action that misses annotated objects needed downstream. It introduces Spatial Action Review, a visual analytics dashboard for auditing this transition in electron microscopy workflows. The concept of silent answer-action failures is broadly relevant to MLLM oversight.

entry.title: Incentive Noise and Structural Prior Infusion for Multi-modal Object Re-Identification

author.name: Weixiang Zhou, Yuhao Wang, Xingguo Xu, Weizhen Zhou, Zhixun Su, Jinshan Pan, Cong Wang

entry.summary: This work tackles noisy text descriptions in multi-modal object re-identification, proposing a framework based on Positive-Incentive Noise theory to model modality-mismatched and ambiguous text signals. It also introduces structural priors to reconcile fine-grained structural discrepancies between imaging modalities after high-level semantic alignment.

entry.title: Video-based Surgical Skill Assessment Using Dynamics-and-Uncertainty-Aware Tree-based Gaussian Process Classifier

author.name: Arefeh Rezaei, Mohammad Javad Ahmadi, Amir Molaei, Hamid D. Taghirad

entry.summary: The authors combine a representation-flow CNN with a dynamics- and uncertainty-aware tree-based Gaussian Process classifier for surgical skill assessment from video. Latent motion dynamics serve both as features and as an uncertainty source, and novel semantic-aware compound kernels capture semantic, flow, and dynamic information while requiring less training data.

entry.title: Hi-Singers: A Comprehensive High-Quality Dataset for Expressive Audio-Driven Singing Head Synthesis

author.name: Yichi Zhang, Hui Zhang, Guanjun Liu, Yuefeng Zou, Fengzhao Sun, Jun Yu

entry.summary: Hi-Singers is the first large-scale, high-quality, in-the-wild video dataset tailored for audio-driven singing head synthesis, with rigorous automated and manual filtering to ensure thematic adherence and resolution. It targets the domain gap between talking-head and singing-head synthesis, including rhythmic drift and constrained facial dynamics.

entry.title: Lesion-Gated Hybrid Synthesis for Virtual Contrast-Enhanced Breast MRI: A MAMA-SYNTH Challenge Solution

author.name: Shohei Yoshimoto

entry.summary: Describes a challenge-winning pipeline for synthesizing post-contrast breast MRI from pre-contrast images, using a lesion probability map from pre-contrast-only segmentation ensembles to coordinate tumour-focused and global synthesis pathways. Designed to balance four metric groups in the MAMA-SYNTH challenge at MICCAI 2026.

entry.title: Learning-Based 3D Reconstruction of Power Networks from Aerial Point Clouds

author.name: Rishabh Jain, Anuja Saini, Vishal Jain

entry.summary: Presents an end-to-end pipeline for reconstructing overhead power network topology from aerial LiDAR, combining improved KPConv semantic segmentation with pole clustering and a lightweight ResNet classifier for conductor connections on 2D projections. It extracts span-level physical metadata useful for utility inspection.

entry.title: Prescriptive SVD-Inspired Attention via Spectral Energy Retention

author.name: Vasileios Arampatzakis, Vasileios Sevetlidis, George Pavlidis

entry.summary: Building on SVD-Inspired Attention (SVDA), which makes latent attention directions inspectable via spectral indicators like entropy and effective rank, this paper moves from diagnosis to intervention. It proposes a diagnosis-intervention-verification framework and evaluates one intervention based on spectral energy retention. A step toward mechanistically grounded, interpretable modifications of attention in Transformers.

entry.title: A bioinspired internal model-based online estimator for planar pursuit

author.name: Tengyue Liu, Xincheng Li, Sofia Morales Ferreira, Kevin Galloway, Udit Halder

entry.summary: The paper develops a bioinspired internal model-based estimator that reconstructs unobserved relative-configuration quantities from partial onboard sensing and known self-motion, posed as an optimization over relative kinematic constraints. Necessary conditions are derived via Pontryagin's Maximum Principle for use in pursuit, tracking, and collective-motion feedback control.

entry.title: A Deployable Four-Finger Payload for Teleoperated Free-Flying Manipulation with Astrobee

author.name: William Su, Jordan Kam, Yunosuke Nakamura, Yixiao Wang, Jianshu Zhou, Masayoshi Tomizuka

entry.summary: The paper describes a bimanual VR teleoperation pipeline and a deployable four-finger gripper payload for Astrobee free-flying robots, offering 17 manipulation DoF through independently actuated fingers on a linear rail. Preliminary results come from teleoperation in a custom zero-gravity MuJoCo-based simulation targeting future LEO habitat tasks.

entry.title: Skill Sequence Planning for Collaborative Multi-Robot Construction

author.name: Xi Wang, Bo Fu, Carol C. Menassa, Vineet R. Kamat, Min Deng

entry.summary: This paper presents a skill sequence planning method that lets a heterogeneous team of multi-functional robots collaboratively perform construction assembly tasks using reusable, preprogrammed skills such as grasping, drilling, and fastening. A central controller converts a digital building representation into a construction relationship graph encoding entities, states, and parent-child dependencies, from which the system selects construction targets and generates action sequences. The goal is to reduce the programming effort that currently limits industry adoption of construction robots.

entry.title: MatcherCompass: A Deployment-Aware Benchmark to Guide Image Matcher Selection in the Wild

author.name: Hyunwoo Kim, Giseop Kim

entry.summary: This benchmark evaluates nine classical and learned image matching pipelines across resolutions, numerical precisions, and four visual conditions including day-night and visible-thermal matching, with runtime measured on target hardware. It aims to guide practitioners in selecting matchers under onboard time and resource constraints rather than relying on accuracy numbers reported on single devices. It fills a real gap between academic accuracy claims and deployment realities in field robotics.

entry.title: AgriGen: Large-Scale Scene Generation Framework for Photorealistic Agricultural Robotics Simulation

author.name: Utkarsh Bajpai, Serge Tleiji, C\'{e}dric Pradalier, St\'{e}phanie Aravecchia

entry.summary: AgriGen is a ROS-integrated framework built on Isaac Sim for procedural generation of photorealistic agricultural environments at scale, supporting physics simulation and domain randomization. It addresses the scarcity of diverse agricultural data caused by field access limits, seasonal cycles, and geographic variability. This brings agricultural robotics closer to the simulation-driven scaling seen in other robotics domains.

entry.title: VisForce: Visual Grounding of Current and Desired Forces for Goal-Conditioned Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Jung-Woo Lee, Soo-Chul Lim

entry.summary: VisForce renders current and desired force cues directly onto wrist camera images and a goal image at the corresponding fingertip locations, letting a policy learn the spatial correspondence between forces and visual context. Goal-conditioned cross-attention fuses these representations into force-aware actions for dexterous hand manipulation. Evaluated on a real system, it addresses how VLA models can incorporate contact-force information more naturally than as separate state inputs.

entry.title: Control Barrier Functions for Safe Free-Flying Robotic Spacecraft Operations in Tumbling Target Capture

author.name: Alexander Meinert, Peter Stadler, Niklas Baldauf, Alen Turnwald

entry.summary: This paper builds a modular control barrier function framework for safe free-flying spacecraft capture of tumbling targets, translating ESA close-proximity guidelines into dedicated safety filters. A 13-DoF system is decomposed into translational, attitude, and robotic subsystems, each with a QP-based safety filter enforcing approach corridors, collision avoidance, pointing, joint limits, and actuator constraints, with dynamic coupling handled across subsystems. It grounds space-robot safety in formal CBF machinery aligned with real guidelines.

entry.title: Design and Implementation of an Ultra-Low-Cost Wall-Climbing Robot for Infrastructure Crack Detection

author.name: Mrinmoy Modak, Supreyo Chakravorty Pretom, Shourv Tarafder, Daniel S. Drew

entry.summary: This paper presents a low-cost wall-climbing robot for automated concrete crack detection, combining YOLOv8 for real-time crack localization with CNN and EfficientNet-B0 classifiers for verification, along with a curated crack image dataset. The two-stage detection pipeline targets infrastructure inspection where manual surveying is costly and hazardous.

entry.title: Higher-Order Approximation of Exit Functionals in Sampling-Based Stochastic Model Predictive Control

author.name: Sashank Modali, Takashi Tanaka

entry.summary: This paper studies higher-order strong approximation methods for exit times and exit indicators, which are key numerical bottlenecks in sampling-based stochastic MPC for safety evaluation. It applies adaptive Milstein and order-1.5 discretizations, including Levy-area simulation via Wiktorsson's method for noncommutative dynamics, under anti-concentration conditions.

entry.title: Trading firms could control meaningful amounts of compute by 2030

author.name: Patrick McElroy

entry.summary: An analysis arguing that the very high margins of selling frontier AI via API are redirecting supply chains (memory, fab space, compute formerly used for Bitcoin mining) and could allow trading firms, not just labs, to accumulate meaningful compute holdings by 2030. The post engages with questions about AI lab profitability and compute concentration, noting claims that OpenAI and Anthropic may soon control a large share of worldwide compute.

entry.title: Politics Gets Interested In Those Trying Not To Die

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi surveys a dramatic month in AI policy discourse: a researcher resignation and statements from frontier lab CEOs about pacing AI development briefly produced cross-partisan interest in safety measures, before the US administration dismissed existential risk as a hoax tied to anti-data-center activism. The post analyzes how political dynamics may shape future AI regulation.

entry.title: TCMaster: Confidence-Aware Querying and Workload-Guided Physical Design for Multi-Source Traditional Chinese Medicine Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Zheng Chen, Yuzhu Li, Haoxuan Li, Zhongde Zhang, Lianshun Jin, Peiwu Qin

entry.summary: Presents TCMaster, a property-graph query substrate over a Traditional Chinese Medicine knowledge graph of roughly 221K entities and 723K edges, with provenance-level confidence annotation, confidence-aware query rewriting, and workload-guided physical design on Neo4j. Integrates pharmacopoeias, prescriptions, molecular databases, and LLM-extracted micro-semantics.

entry.title: Do Vision Model See Like the Brain? A Comparison Across EEG Encoding Model

author.name: Shashank Baghel, Kshitij Dwivedi, Dinesh Singh, Sanjeev Nara

entry.summary: Compares six CNNs and two vision transformers as models of the human visual system using EEG encoding across ten participants viewing 200 natural images, layer by layer and token representation. CNNs correspond most strongly at early layers with weakening deeper on, while transformers sustain strong correspondence longer, suggesting architecture-dependent divergence from neural responses.

entry.title: PermuFormer: Multi-Task Pretraining for Permutation Representation in Algebraic Combinatorics

author.name: Henry Kvinge

entry.summary: PermuFormer applies diverse multi-task pretraining to learn reusable representations of permutations for algebraic combinatorics, positioning specialized models trained directly on mathematical objects as complements to frontier LLM reasoning in AI for math. The work argues pretraining avoids the limits of training specialists from scratch for each task.

entry.title: CrowdCue: Specialist-Cue Conditioning for Vision-Language Crowd Counting

author.name: Moshiur Farazi, Bekir Ciftler, Abdulhalim Dandoush, Reda Bendraou

entry.summary: This paper studies whether auxiliary guidance from a pretrained specialist can lift VLM crowd counting accuracy, evaluating Qwen2.5-VL-7B with P2PNet-derived cues across four benchmarks. Zero-shot prompting rarely yields parseable counts, LoRA fine-tuning sets an MAE baseline of 81.64, and conditioning on specialist density heatmaps improves counting, revealing which guidance channel works best.

entry.title: Vision Transformers versus convolutional neural networks for fine-grained orchid genus identification in a species-rich, data-poor flora: a controlled benchmark on the Orchidaceae of New Guinea

author.name: Reza Saputra, Diah Harnoni Apriyanti, Andr\'e Schuiteman, Kurt Metzger, Ashley Field, Katharina Nargar, William Edwards

entry.summary: This controlled benchmark compares two ViT backbones (DINOv2, BioCLIP 2) and two CNNs (ConvNeXt V2-L, EfficientNetV2-L) under an identical protocol for a two-stage orchid identification system: genus prediction followed by FAISS-based species retrieval, applied to the species-rich but data-poor orchids of New Guinea. It establishes which architecture and pretraining strategy best support fine-grained identification with very few images per species.

entry.title: Relightable 3D Avatar Reconstruction with Semantic-Adaptive Motion-Illumination Responses

author.name: Jiankuo Zhao, Xiangyu Zhu, Jijie Li, Baiqin Wang, Shukai Chen, Zhen Lei

entry.summary: SAMIRA is a 3D Gaussian avatar framework that models motion and illumination responses per facial semantic region rather than with globally coupled primitives, improving fine-grained animation and relighting plausibility from monocular video. It targets expressive, relightable head avatar reconstruction.

entry.title: Estimating Accurate Hand Pose in Camera Space with Vision Transformer

author.name: Kaiwen Ren, Yiran Jiang, Yongjing Ye, Shihong Xia

entry.summary: The paper tackles global hand pose estimation in camera space from monocular RGB, addressing depth ambiguity and the coupling of local hand poses with global wrist positions under perspective projection. Its framework introduces two innovations, including a Transformer-based component, to overcome these coupled challenges. Global camera-space estimation is important for AR/VR and human-computer interaction.

entry.title: A Reconfigurable Bidirectional Cable-Driven Hip Exoskeleton with Swappable Bench/Backpack Dual-configuration Actuation

author.name: YuanLong Ji, Shuhan Xiang, Qihan Ye, Xingbang Yang

entry.summary: A reconfigurable hip exoskeleton platform that rapidly switches between bench-mounted actuation for lab-based rehabilitation assessment and backpack-mounted portable actuation, sharing one cable-free wearable interface. The modular design adapts actuation, sensing, and low-level control to serve both development and mobile assistance use cases.

entry.title: MedVLA: A Hierarchical Vision-Language-Action Framework for Closed-Loop Precision Medical Robot Manipulation

author.name: Junjie Xie, Chuxuan He, Angen Ye, Yujia Song, Dapeng Zhang

entry.summary: MedVLA couples high-level multimodal VLA reasoning with low-level function-constrained execution for precision medical robotics, where continuous action generation alone is ill-suited to strict safety and interpretability requirements. It introduces a multi-agent pipeline generating skill-oriented chain-of-thought training data and supports different multimodal backbone models. The hierarchical design enables closed-loop operation that can invoke non-action system function calls.

entry.title: Robust Active-Perception Control for Global-State-Free Aerial-Ground Cooperation

author.name: Mingxuan Zhang, Jiajun Yu, Baozhe Zhang, Pengxiang Zhou, Wentao Liu, Fei Gao, Chao Xu, Yanjun Cao

entry.summary: COPA enables UAV-UGV cooperative operations without global localization by controlling directly in a UGV-attached non-inertial frame with passive-marker relative pose estimation. A single-axis gimbal decouples camera optical axis from UAV pitch, and an active-perception model coordinates UAV motion and gimbal control so the marker stays in view despite attitude conflicts. This yields robust global-state-free aerial-ground cooperation.

entry.title: Early Prediction of Pathological Complete Response to Neoadjuvant Chemotherapy Using Temporal Deep Learning on DWI

author.name: Pablo Garc\'ia Marcos, Md. Tarequl Islam, Paula Puerta Gonz\'alez, Guillermo Lorenzo, H\'ector G\'omez, Covadonga del Camino, Angel Rio-Alvarez, V\'ictor M. Gonz\'alez

entry.summary: This companion paper predicts pathological complete response early using only diffusion-weighted MRI at baseline and after the first chemo cycle, feeding tumor-centered patches to an EfficientNet-based temporal model that learns shape and tissue characteristics without handcrafted radiomics. Early identification of non-responders could enable timely treatment adaptation. The minimal-data requirement improves practical applicability.

entry.title: Exposing Blind Spots in Deep Imbalanced Regression Evaluation

author.name: Noah C. Puetz, Jens U. Brandt, Marc Hilbert, Elena Raponi, Thomas B\"ack, Thomas Bartz-Beielstein

entry.summary: Critically revisits evaluation practice in Deep Imbalanced Regression, identifying three blind spots: over-reliance on image benchmarks, a many/medium/few-shot protocol that is diagnostic but not decision-complete, and unexamined tail-region stability across seeds. The authors broaden evaluation to a multimodal virtual sensing benchmark (MuViS) and propose fixes along these axes.

entry.title: Radiomics-Conditioned Modulation of RenalCLIP Features for Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma Classification

author.name: Yuan Liang, Sourav Bhattacharjee, Abraham Campbell

entry.summary: Uses radiomics features to modulate RenalCLIP foundation-model features via FiLM, with a direct radiomics contribution retained, for CT-based clear cell renal cell carcinoma classification. The FiLM model reaches AUC 0.804 internally and 0.854 externally, the best among evaluated RenalCLIP fusion strategies in both cohorts.

entry.title: High-Order Liquid Evidence Modeling for Continuous and Subtle GNSS Spoofing Detection in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Muhammad Ayub Sabir, Junbiao Pang, Fatima Ashraf

entry.summary: The paper frames subtle GNSS spoofing detection as causal sequential evidence modeling, comparing displacement implied by consecutive GNSS fixes against motion inferred from non-GNSS onboard sensors and feeding these inconsistency signals into a high-order liquid evidence detector. This targets attacks where forged positions stay locally plausible while drifting from observed vehicle motion, a setting where residual-threshold detectors fail. It is relevant to autonomous vehicle security.

entry.title: DiaSeg: Diagonal Segment Extraction from DTW Paths for Interpretable Gait Analysis

author.name: Tresor Y. Koffi, Amel Hidouri, Corentin Legrand, Aur\'elie Bertaux

entry.summary: DiaSeg extracts diagonal segments from dynamic time warping paths and characterizes each by five geometric features, enabling unsupervised pattern discovery from gait time series without domain-specific feature engineering. It is validated on 91 subjects across six clinical conditions including Parkinson's, Huntington's, ALS, and stroke.

entry.title: STA-TFM: Spatio-Temporal Aggregation Across Views TransForMer for Pose Estimation

author.name: Mena Kamel, Natalie Won, Amrut Sarangi, Sven Jager, Albert Pla Planas

entry.summary: STA-TFM is a transformer architecture for multi-view 3D human pose estimation combining DSTformer monocular features within views with a fusion transformer across views and time. It also proposes a data generation pipeline converting any 3D pose dataset into multi-view setups to counter training data scarcity. It targets depth ambiguity, occlusion, and temporal consistency without complex capture setups.

entry.title: Predict Before You Step: Auditable Occupancy Forecasting for Dynamic Obstacle Avoidance under Sparse Guidance

author.name: Yuhui Mao, Fen Liu, Shenghai Yuan, Tianxin Hu, Ruimeng Liu, Rong Su

entry.summary: LOOP is a local avoidance policy for legged robots that forecasts future occupancy over a one-second horizon from LiDAR histories using learned flow and visibility gates, connecting sparse waypoint guidance to a frozen locomotion controller at 50 Hz. Map-derived features and geometric risk estimates guide velocity selection, and predictions are explicitly inspectable and replaceable, giving an auditable interface. Evaluations in Isaac Lab show 57.1% head-on success against obstacles moving at 2.5 m/s.

entry.title: An Accurate and Interpretable Hyper Graph Neural Network for GBM Survival Prediction

author.name: Mushahid Intesum

entry.summary: A multi-modal hypergraph neural network framework for glioblastoma survival prediction that fuses multiple MRI modalities and clinical metadata while preserving interpretability. The authors argue the accuracy-versus-transparency trade-off in clinical prediction is not inherent and demonstrate structural GNN representations that deliver both.

entry.title: CQ4OE: A benchmark for assessing LLM-assisted ontology generation from competency questions

author.name: Jiayi Li, Ziyuan Wang, Daniel Garijo, Mar\'ia Poveda-Villal\'on

entry.summary: CQ4OE is a benchmark for evaluating LLM-based ontology generation from competency questions, featuring gold OWL ontologies with explicit provenance linking each question to ontology elements and metrics separating lexical overlap from structural and logical adequacy. It addresses fragmentation in prior evaluation practice. This enables reproducible comparison of ontology-generation systems.

entry.title: RankCert: When Can Simulated Learners Safely Select an AI Tutor? Robust Decision Certification Under Structural Uncertainty

author.name: Nizam Kadir

entry.summary: RankCert certifies selection among eight equal-budget tutoring policies only when multiple utility, regret, and rank-based criteria agree, otherwise abstaining; it was evaluated across 1,280 frozen held-out settings using an EdNet-KT1 derivative with 5,000 learners. The paper formalizes safe AI-tutor selection under structural uncertainty in learner models. This connects calibrated abstention to educational AI deployment decisions.

entry.title: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy response prediction using pretreatment diffusion and contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging with clinical variables

author.name: Pablo Garc\'ia Marcos, Paula Puerta Gonz\'alez, Guillermo Lorenzo, H\'ector G\'omez, Covadonga del Camino, Ad\'an Rodr\'iguez, Ignacio Pel\'aez, Angel Rio-Alvarez, V\'ictor M. Gonz\'alez

entry.summary: This study builds a deep-learning model predicting pathological complete response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy in breast cancer using pretreatment ADC maps, DCE-MRI, and clinical variables on the public ACRIN 6698/I-SPY2 dataset, with EfficientNet-B0 encoders and late fusion of clinical information. Notably, only HR/HER2 subtype improved average AUC among the clinical variables tested. It is a competent clinical prediction contribution on a public multicenter dataset.

entry.title: When Verifiers Vote Backwards under Verdict Substitution: Signed Pivotal Value in Correlated Self-Consistency

author.name: Yang Shu

entry.summary: Using a labeled verdict-substitution intervention on k=7 self-consistency panels, the paper measures the signed pivotal effect of replacing one correctness ballot with a verifier signal, finding +24.2pp gain for a different-model verifier on MATH-500 but negative gains in role-reversed and code settings. An exact signed-gain decomposition explains all observed signs via verifier state-space properties. The work reveals when verifiers help or hurt narrow-margin majority decisions.

entry.title: You've Seen Enough: Quality-Constrained Image Coding for Machines

author.name: Khoa Pham-Dinh, Sanaz Nami, Hamed Rezazadegan Tavakoli, Moncef Gabbouj, Farhad Pakdaman

entry.summary: Recasts joint image compression and segmentation as a constrained optimization problem that caps human-perceived quality at a just-acceptable level and redirects the remaining coding capacity toward machine task performance. Inspired by just-noticeable distortion, this targets the growing reality that most images are consumed by vision models rather than humans.

entry.title: Complementary Roles of Radiomics and Foundation Representations in Renal Cell Carcinoma Classification: A Comparative Study of 2D and 3D CT Encodings

author.name: Yuan Liang, Sourav Bhattacharjee, Abraham Campbell

entry.summary: Compares handcrafted radiomics, 2D and 3D MedVAE foundation representations, and their fusion strategies for classifying clear-cell versus non-clear-cell renal cell carcinoma on the KiTS23 CT dataset under unified preprocessing. The study clarifies whether radiomics adds value beyond pretrained representations and how 2D versus 3D encoders compare.

entry.title: Minimal Recurrent Behavioral Memory for Imitation under Partial Observability

author.name: Xianyao Li, Fang Xu, Rui Min, Ruitong Tian, Jing Du

entry.summary: The paper theoretically characterizes the minimal recurrent memory an agent needs to imitate an expert under partial observability, via a compatibility relation on behavioral equivalence classes, with exact minima under transitivity and entropy-minimization certificates on finite instances. A sole-carrier measurement protocol separates behavioral sufficiency, excess code rate, and information carried by observations or other memory paths. This is a rigorous information-theoretic take on memory requirements in imitation learning.

entry.title: Same Quantity, Different Answer: Numerical Representation Invariance in Language Models

author.name: Ephraim Atta-Duncan

entry.summary: This study tests whether language models give the same canonical answer when a quantity in a word problem is expressed as a decimal, fraction, percentage, number word, scientific notation, or converted unit, using 3,600 exact-rational problems and 8,600 prompts across five transformation families on five open-weight systems. Canonical accuracy is high (0.969-0.996) but orbit correctness and orbit invariance drop substantially, with the strict-parser collapse largely traced to multiplication-form scientific notation falling outside the implemented number grammar.

entry.title: Learning from Humans for Proactive Assistance in Human-Robot Collaborative Transport

author.name: Elvin Yang, Christoforos Mavrogiannis

entry.summary: This work addresses human-robot collaborative transport by integrating predictions of human collaborative behavior with compliant robot control, rather than treating efficiency and responsiveness separately. The robot learns from human demonstrations to both contribute to efficient object relocation and remain physically responsive to user input. Applications span logistics, manufacturing, and household settings.

entry.title: Automatic depth-based local center clustering via $\beta$-integrated local depth and adaptive grouping

author.name: Siyi Wang, Alexandre Leblanc, Paul D. McNicholas

entry.summary: A-DLCC is a fully data-driven clustering method that requires no user-specified parameters such as cluster count or neighborhood size. It uses beta-integrated local depth to identify stable exemplar points across locality levels and merges induced groups via a new nonparametric group-level local similarity metric.

entry.title: Rethinking Length-Based Training: Batch Composition and Loss Normalization in Speech Token Language Models

author.name: Hongjin Song, Runwu Shi, Weiqiao Shan, Jiale Luo, Yujin Wang, Yifei Wu, Chunxiang Jin

entry.summary: This paper disentangles the confounds in short-to-long curriculum training for speech token language models, including shuffle policy, batch composition, token retention, and loss normalization. Matched comparisons show the curriculum ordering itself has no independent benefit when batch composition and token exposure are fixed. It provides a systematic protocol that corrects common misattributions of curriculum-training gains.

entry.title: Brain-to-Image Generation: Reconstructing Visual Stimuli from EEG using Generative Adversarial Networks

author.name: Harshit Goyal

entry.summary: This paper presents a reproducible single-subject baseline on THINGS-EEG2 for reconstructing visual stimuli from EEG, using a compact temporal-spatial convolutional encoder to map repetition-averaged EEG to ViT-B/32 image features. It emphasizes the more defensible retrieval question with concept-disjoint validation and the official 200-image test gallery.

entry.title: Yarn tracking of large-scale 3D textile reinforcements using topological material features

author.name: Hafsa El Herichi (LMPS, CVN), Arturo Mendoza (LMPS), Yanneck Wielhorski (CVN), Hugues Talbot (CVN), St\'ephane Roux (LMPS)

entry.summary: The paper presents a semi-automatic method for tracking yarn paths in fan blade textile preforms from coarse X-ray CT images, statistically modeling cross-section shape, continuity, and other material properties. It enables scalable slice-based analysis on real industrial components with minimal training data.

entry.title: C$^{2}$-INR: Customized Convolutional Implicit Neural Representation

author.name: Jinglei Shi, Xinran Chang, Jiaqi Cui, Yingjie Xia, Zhaolin Xiao, Chongyi Li

entry.summary: This work proposes a convolutional implicit neural representation with customizable architecture, exploiting inter-pixel spatial correlations that MLP-based INRs ignore. It addresses the underexplored space of convolutional INRs where most prior work relies on fixed architectural settings.

entry.title: Blind Deconvolution of Binary and Pattern Images with Pixel Intensity Constraints and Sparse Gradient Prior

author.name: Qinghua Zhang, Xuesong Yang, Liangtian He, Liang-jian Deng, Jun Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a unified blind image deconvolution framework for specialized image classes such as barcodes, text, and patterns, where pixels are restricted to a limited set of values. The authors introduce a novel pixel intensity constraint combined with a sparse gradient prior, exploiting image-specific structure that most existing blind deconvolution methods overlook since they are designed for natural images. This improves recovery quality for practical imaging tasks like barcode and document restoration.

entry.title: Beyond UV Mapping: Mesh Texture Compression via Surface-Aligned Texture Fields

author.name: Jianqiang Wang, Junhui Hou, Siyu Ren, Weiyao Lin, Wenping Wang

entry.summary: The paper introduces TexF, a surface-aligned texture field organizing texture attributes in sparse voxels derived from the mesh surface, avoiding the chart discontinuities and mapping overhead of 2D UV atlases. It supports reuse of established 3D attribute codecs with voxel locations reconstructed from the decoded mesh, plus a GPU-resident codec (3DNTC) combining quantized hash features with a lightweight decoder for random-access reconstruction.

entry.title: Reassessing Global Gradient-Norm Imbalance in BLIP Fine-Tuning Across Physical Domains

author.name: Kiran Naseer, Samreen Azhar, Dwarikanath Mahapatra
