It replaces costly high-fidelity simulator roll-outs during reinforcement learning policy optimization. This is significant because data collection for vehicle-terrain interaction is a well-known bottleneck in off-road autonomy.

entry.title: HEARTH: An Object-Centric RGB-Thermal-3D Dataset for Temperature-Aware Robot Manipulation

author.name: Yuning Su, Borui Li, Yonghao Shi, Bofei Liu, Xing-Dong Yang

entry.summary: Releases HEARTH, a dataset of 90 physical objects across 18 categories with RGB-thermal-3D captures (145 object states), mapping surface temperatures onto reconstructed meshes via calibration and pose transfer, plus 1,200 demonstrations on LIBERO-derived tasks for temperature-aware finetuning. Temperature is a physical property invisible to RGB that matters for manipulation. Filling the thermal-modality gap in manipulation datasets is a genuinely useful resource contribution.

entry.title: STRIDER: Stepping-Enabled Multi-Gait Hierarchical 3D Loco-Manipulation Framework for Humanoid Robots

author.name: Yuanzhuo Li, Wen Zhao, Zhe Yong, Xiang Meng, Gang Han, Hengle Ren, Xiaoyang Zheng, Zhen Wang, Yijie Guo

entry.summary: Introduces STRIDER, a hierarchical multi-gait humanoid loco-manipulation framework combining terrain-aware 3D stepping logic with foothold selection in the stance-foot frame, AMP-based natural walking, and Cartesian upper-body control, addressing the tension between continuous velocity commands and precise foothold regulation. It also improves imitation distillation to encourage shared representations of heterogeneous skills. Humanoid loco-manipulation with precise foothold control is an active industrial-relevance topic.

entry.title: HapticWAM: Distilling Imagined Touch into a World-Action Model without Inference-Time Tactile Sensing

author.name: Mikhail Sannikov, Ilya Mikhalchuk, Konstantin Gubernatorov, Petr Kovalev, Ogunwoye Faith Oluwatobi, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: HapticWAM is a world-action model whose teacher encodes gel images plus deformation, shear, distributed forces, and contact state into a frozen video backbone, then distills imagined touch into a student policy requiring no fingertip tactile sensing at deployment. Combines heterogeneous tactile encoding, structured contact prediction, and teacher-student distillation. Tackles contact-rich manipulation without tactile hardware costs.

entry.title: Opt2VLA: Force-Aware Vision-Language-Action for Contact-Rich Humanoid Whole-Body Manipulation

author.name: Fukang Liu, Yipu Chen, Jaehwi Jang, Danfei Xu, Zsolt Kira, Ye Zhao

entry.summary: Opt2VLA brings explicit force awareness into humanoid whole-body VLA control, since existing humanoid systems use geometric motion goals with motion-tracking controllers and limited force reasoning. Targets contact-rich tasks where similar motions need different force regimes and vision becomes unreliable after contact. Part of an emerging wave of force-aware VLAs for humanoids.

entry.title: Zeva-Ego: Egocentric Mid-Training with In-Context Causal Learning for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Bingjia Huang, Xin Ding, Fu Chen, Kun Li, Wei Sun, Hao Wu, Yunxin Liu, Ting Cao

entry.summary: Zeva-Ego is a unified framework converting egocentric human video into action-centered supervision for VLA mid-training via an Action-Centric Encoder, plus parameter-free in-context adaptation from action-effect feedback at deployment. Scaling egocentric data to 10K hours improves RoboTwin success from 63.8% to 75.3%, matching 2K hours of robot demonstrations, implying an empirical egocentric-to-robot data ratio of roughly 4-5:1. This provides concrete evidence on how cheap human video substitutes for expensive robot data.

entry.title: TACIT: Tactile Contact Supervision for Spatial Attention in Dexterous Manipulation

author.name: Yanhou Lai, Fucai Zhu, Ruiqiang Wang, Koichi Hashimoto

entry.summary: TACIT uses measured tactile contacts from teleoperated demonstrations to supervise spatial attention heads in visuomotor policies, removing the need for human point annotation or visual prior models. Gaussian targets over camera point clouds train an attention head whose pooled output conditions a visuotactile diffusion policy, showing improved object-position tracking with only ten demonstrations on real robots.

entry.title: HE-Guardrail: A Homomorphic Guardrail Against Jailbreak Attacks for Encrypted Large Language Model Inference

author.name: Byeongseo Min, Yongwoo Lee, Young-Sik Kim, Yongjune Kim

entry.summary: The paper identifies a security vulnerability in homomorphic-encryption-based LLM inference: confidentiality prevents servers from inspecting encrypted prompts, so malicious clients can submit jailbreak attacks undetected. It proposes HE-Guardrail, a guardrail mechanism that operates directly over encrypted data to detect adversarial prompts while preserving client privacy. This closes a genuine gap at the intersection of privacy-preserving ML and LLM safety.

entry.title: Are Coreset Selection Methods Worth Their Cost?

author.name: Yangze Liu, Zhongyi Han

entry.summary: Introduces an end-to-end benchmark that charges coreset selection and downstream training to the same auditable wall-clock budget across 4 datasets, 11 selectors, 5 fractions, and 3 seeds with over 1,500 released runs. Tests whether budget-aware evaluation favors simple random selection even when each selector gets its most favorable training recipe.

entry.title: Misaligned Clinical Risk Classification and Cost Asymmetry in Open-Weight Large Language Models

author.name: Star S. D. Liu, Xiyu Ding, Robert B. Barrett, Alberto Santamaria-Pang, Nic Dobbins, Harold P. Lehmann

entry.summary: Using a public diabetes dataset, the authors probe how four open-weight LLMs (Qwen-2.5-7B/32B and Llama-3.1-8B/70B) internally represent false-negative versus false-positive cost tradeoffs in clinical risk classification, varying 11 cost ratios across three phrasings. Patient risk is linearly recoverable with AUC around 0.83 and cost direction is recoverable in every model, yet representational shifts in cost direction fail to translate into correspondingly shifted behavioral decisions. This reveals a representational-behavioral misalignment with direct patient-safety implications for clinical LLM use.

entry.title: Fairness Beyond Anonymization? Demographic Leakage in German LLM-Generated Resumes

author.name: Charlotte Leininger, Helena Veit, Matthias A{\ss}enmacher, Andreas Bender

entry.summary: This two-stage audit examines whether LLM-generated German resumes encode recoverable demographic information, using GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite, and Qwen 3 models (4B-14B) to generate resumes from real anonymized job-matching data. It addresses a gap under the EU AI Act, where hiring is high-risk, by showing fairness concerns extend beyond explicit decisions to the generated documents themselves.

entry.title: Detecting Agitation Before Behavioral Escalation in Autistic Youth Through Multimodal Wearable Sensing

author.name: Nibraas Khan, Abigale Plunk, John Staubitz, Ingrid Shragge, Jordan Brooks, Suzanne Wright, Alec Brewer, James Dieffenderfer, Alper Bozkurt, Amy Weitlauf, Nilanjan Sarkar

entry.summary: The study collects multimodal wearable data from 15 autistic youth across 30 clinician-annotated sessions, combining inertial, physiological, and vocal signals to predict agitation before behavioral escalation. Four pretrained foundation models, one per modality, are projected into a shared representation for early warning.

entry.title: PixelART: Image-to-Layer Decomposition without Latents or Text-to-Image Pretraining

author.name: Zelin Jia, Zhao Zhang, Zhicong Tang, Yuhui Yuan, Shixia Liu

entry.summary: PixelART is a pixel-space rectified-flow Transformer trained from scratch for image-to-layer decomposition into editable RGBA layers, avoiding RGBA-VAEs, pretrained T2I backbones, and layer-specific decoders used by prior diffusion systems. The authors identify a key training property that makes this lighter-weight approach work.

entry.title: RopeFormer: Cross-Trial Adaptation from Interaction History for Dynamic Rope Manipulation

author.name: Menglin Wu, Kaixiang Yao, Shangbo Luan, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Yuxin Chen

entry.summary: Presents RopeFormer, a history-conditioned policy for dynamic rope manipulation that retains cross-trial action-response history as context while keeping weights frozen, requiring no explicit online rope-parameter estimation. In matched simulation across rotation, bimanual, and whipping tasks, retained context improves control versus resetting the same checkpoint, with benefits varying across rope dynamics. Implicit in-context adaptation from interaction history is an emerging and important robot-learning theme.

entry.title: Attention-Aware Routing: Coupling Routing and Attention in MoEs

author.name: Despoina Kosmopoulou, Anastasios Tsetsilas, Efthymios Georgiou, Giannis Karamanolakis, Swastik Roy, Alexandros Potamianos

entry.summary: The paper proposes Attention-Aware Routing (AAR), which augments Mixture-of-Experts routers with temporal and spectral features from attention-weight windows, training only routing parameters while freezing the base transformer. AAR improves GSM8K by 3.37 points over a routing-only SFT baseline on OLMoE and demonstrates that routing and attention form a coupled circuit whose changes propagate across layers.

entry.title: Implicit Rule Induction with Test-Time Task Embeddings in ARC-like Tasks

author.name: Adrien Deli\`ege, Claas Beger, Marc Van Droogenbroeck, Melanie Mitchell

entry.summary: The authors study test-time task embeddings in Vision ARC, introducing a two-step test-time training protocol that first finetunes only the task embedding and then the backbone. They evaluate on ARC-AGI-1, ConceptARC, and controlled datasets with known rules to determine whether success reflects genuine rule induction versus shortcuts. This addresses a fundamental question about abstract reasoning evaluation.

entry.title: PolyBridgeBench: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs for Physics-Grounded Bridge Design

author.name: Zicheng Zhao, Dongyin Chen, Rui Xu, Yinghui Xu

entry.summary: PolyBridgeBench is an executable benchmark requiring multimodal LLMs to design complete load-bearing bridge structures from visual scenes and engineering constraints, with deterministic legality checks gating execution in a dynamic physics simulation. It uniquely tests whether models can repair structures after simulator execution exposes failures, going beyond static validity checks.

entry.title: AutoRecLab: Describe the Experiment, Get the Code!

author.name: Moritz Baumgart, Philipp Meister, Justus Krell, Michael Schmidt, Bela Gipp, Joeran Beel

entry.summary: AutoRecLab is an autonomous recommender-systems lab that turns natural-language experiment descriptions into executable code, deriving requirements, building and validating prototypes, and expanding them into full experiments using RAG documentation lookup, static type verification, and execution-steered tree search. It demonstrates autonomous implementation of an explicit-to-implicit feedback conversion study with baseline comparisons.

entry.title: Making Latent Evolution Explicit: Operator-Structured Transitions for World Action Models

author.name: Xiaoxiao Lu, Yunlong Dong, Jiahao Shi, Ye Yuan

entry.summary: This work critiques the default use of Transformer predictors for latent dynamics in World Action Models for robotics and proposes LEON, a Latent Evolution Operator Network that models transitions in a learned observable space via context-modulated operators. It reframes transition realization as an independent architectural design choice.

entry.title: Verify, Don't Trust: Agentic Model Development for Video Discovery Retrieval at Scale

author.name: Hao Fu, Baiting Zhu, Minglei Chen, Yinjie Huang, Shuai Ding

entry.summary: The paper presents EvoPilot, a human-gated autoresearch method for long-horizon online model development in asynchronous production systems, using role-specific agents with versioned domain skills, durable experiment records, and deterministic verification to guard against no-op changes, data leakage, evaluator drift, and funnel mismatches. It targets video discovery retrieval at product scale.

entry.title: Beyond Exact Match: Task-Aware GRPO for Cross-Domain PCBA Visual Question Answering

author.name: Jia Li, Li Dai, Peng Jia, Zhenzhen Hu, Chee Seng Chan, Bingkun Bao, Richang Hong

entry.summary: This paper presents a multimodal reasoning framework for cross-domain visual question answering in printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) inspection, unifying standards-derived, real-world production-line, and auxiliary PCB data into a single instruction format. It uses a task-aware GRPO (reinforcement learning) reward that goes beyond exact match to handle heterogeneous output spaces such as multiple-choice and numerical counting tasks. This matters because domain shift between standards documents and factory imagery is a real barrier to deploying VLMs in industrial inspection.

entry.title: Samsone: A Family of Open Small Audio Language Models for On-Device Inference

author.name: Piotr Masztalski, Micha{\l} K. Grzeszczyk, Olaf Sikorski

entry.summary: Samsone is a family of open small audio language models (35M-356M parameters) designed for privacy-preserving, low-latency on-device inference, with the 134M core model claiming state-of-the-art results for its size class. The family also enables scaling-law analysis for SALMs, with performance competitive with much larger models.

entry.title: Value-Sensitive Delegation in Everyday AI Agent Use: Evidence from OpenClaw

author.name: Renkai Ma, Ruyuan Wan, Xuan Lu, Fan Yang, Chen Chen, Lingyao Li

entry.summary: Using Value Sensitive Design, the authors analyzed 73,093 first-person Reddit posts about the OpenClaw agent, coding each for human values, agent aspects, value fulfillment, and outcomes, yielding 21 values in six groups such as Dependable Operation, Bounded Reach, and Reviewability. Values clustered around operating conditions users set around agent runs rather than agent outputs, and were mostly unmet in certain groups.

entry.title: Success Leaves Detours: Learning Executable Walkthroughs for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Kaijie Chen, Chenyu Fang, Liang Yan, Bo Li, Bo Zhang, Peng Ye

entry.summary: The paper studies how self-evolving agents can reuse sparse-reward trajectories, proposing Trace, a credit-guided framework that compiles noisy experience into executable Walkthrough Memory: compact, state-conditioned, verifiable procedures. It detects progress anchors from rewards and persistent state changes, propagates credit, and grounds action dependencies so future agents can execute rather than merely summarize past successes.

entry.title: Multiple latent orderings better predict language model preferences

author.name: Aviral Chawla, William H. W. Thompson, Jean-Gabriel Young

entry.summary: The authors show that LLM preference intransitivities cannot be explained by a single latent ordering under any monotone link function, and propose a noise-augmented mixture Bradley-Terry model that treats inconsistencies as aggregation of multiple internally consistent latent orderings. This reframing could improve how model preference data is modeled for alignment and evaluation.

entry.title: Teacher Should Think Ahead: Adaptive Continuations for Reliable On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Jingang Zhou, Yuyi Zhou, Haiyang Guo, Xukai Wang, Shuai Feng, Sirui Gao, Jian Xu, Qingpei Guo, Xu-Yao Zhang

entry.summary: The paper identifies Teacher Uncertainty Contraction (TUC), a phenomenon where a teacher's predictive uncertainty systematically decreases when continuing from a student-generated prefix in on-policy distillation, creating a variance-bias trade-off between uncertainty contraction and teacher-student path divergence. The authors theoretically characterize this and propose adaptive teacher continuation lengths guided by the analysis.

entry.title: Classification with Abstention Under Class-Conditional Error Constraints

author.name: Mohammadreza M. Kalan, Yuyang Deng, Sanaz Hamidi

entry.summary: Studies binary classification with abstention under separate per-class error constraints, minimizing abstention rate while capping both class errors. Derives distribution-free minimax excess-abstention rates, surrogate-loss formulations with finite-sample guarantees for neural models, and computational-complexity characterizations in the convex setting.

entry.title: Merge++: Universal Merge Refinement Through Data-Free Checkpoint Inversion

author.name: Aditya Pola, Vineeth N. Balasubramanian

entry.summary: Proposes Merge++, a data-free post-hoc model-merging refinement that inverts expert checkpoints to synthesize task-representative images, then distills expert behavior into the merged model using those synthesized inputs. Applies universally across merging algorithms without requiring any external data beyond the checkpoints.

entry.title: WaveFront Decoding: Parallelized Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Language Models

author.name: Hyeongju Ha, Jae-Joon Kim

entry.summary: Introduces WFD, a training-free self-speculative decoding method for looped language models that batches token states at different recurrence depths in a single weight-shared block call, arranged as a diagonal wavefront. It exploits intermediate recurrence outputs as drafts to cut the latency cost of sequential recurrent calls.

entry.title: ValueDiff: Value-Geometric KV Cache Eviction for Sink-Suppressed LLMs

author.name: Junyoung Park, Jungwook Choi, Mingu Lee

entry.summary: Observes that modern LLM architectures with QK-normalization, gated attention, and learned attention sinks have weaker persistent attention sinks that break existing KV cache eviction heuristics. ValueDiff ranks tokens for eviction by the L2 deviation of their value vectors from the cache mean, derived as the minimal-disturbance eviction under a max-entropy assumption, and evaluates it under fixed cache budgets.

entry.title: GenVoid: Uncertainty-Aware Learning of Subsurface Material Defects with an Experimentally Validated Physics-Informed Generative Model

author.name: Trishit Mondal, Prajwal Bharadwaj, Nikhil Karanjgaokar, Ameya D. Jagtap

entry.summary: GenVoid is a physics-informed generative framework for identifying hidden internal voids in 2D and 3D solids using only surface displacement measurements. It handles linear elastic, hyperelastic, and plastic material behaviors, and explicitly quantifies uncertainty in the inferred defect geometry, with experimental validation. This matters because non-destructive defect characterization is a persistent industrial challenge, and the combination of generative inference with governing physics plus uncertainty awareness is a meaningful methodological step.

entry.title: H-Spec: Parallel Speculative Decoding Without a Drafter-Side KV Cache

author.name: Weifan Jiang, Krishna Teja Chitty-Venkata, Megan Flynn, Reed Meyerson, Zhenting Qi, Tianyu Wu, Eldar Kurtic, Minlan Yu, Alexandre Marques

entry.summary: H-Spec removes the drafter-side KV cache from block-diffusion speculative decoding by reusing target model KVs in place, complemented by hybrid injection of target hidden states only at the last input position to sustain draft quality across the block. This eliminates per-request memory and KV-write overhead that grows with serving concurrency.

entry.title: ARM: Attention with Routed-Memory for Learnable Sparse Control

author.name: Qiuhao Zeng, Jerry Huang, Peng Lu, Ruiyi Fang, Gezheng Xu, Zihao Jing, Yufei Cui, Charles Ling, Gang Niu, Boyu Wang

entry.summary: ARM introduces a differentiable, fixed-size KV-cache memory organized as a hierarchical router, using Gumbel-Softmax slot selection and sigmoid-gated updates to softly combine new and stored information instead of hard token eviction. This reduces information loss in long-context LLM inference, with a policy trained on top of the memory structure.

entry.title: When Tomorrow Becomes Today: Self-Evolving Policies for Agentic Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Yifan Hu, Xilin Dai, Zhiyuan Qu, Yiding Liu, Zewei Dong, Jiang-ming Yang, Qiang Xu

entry.summary: The paper frames agentic time-series forecasting as a system that must adapt both its forecasts and the orchestration policy over which components to trust, as the underlying mechanisms drift. By committing all candidate expert forecasts and agent paths before targets are observed, realized outcomes provide delayed feedback enabling self-evolution without extra annotation.

entry.title: Beyond Raw Context Transfer: Representation-based Federated Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Can Peng, Yu Liu, Yingyu Yang, Anjie Le, Yuyuan Liu, Qianye Yang, J. Alison Noble

entry.summary: FedRepRAG is a decentralized RAG framework that exchanges representations rather than raw retrieved content, addressing privacy in sensitive domains like healthcare where corpora are distributed across institutions. It reduces inference-time overhead and avoids direct exposure of retrieved information compared to prompt-based federated RAG.

entry.title: Strategic Classification Has a Missing Lever: Audit Risk

author.name: Raman Ebrahimi, Massimo Franceschetti

entry.summary: This paper extends strategic classification by letting the decision maker jointly design a linear classifier and an audit profile that assigns detection probabilities and penalties to fakeable features, mirroring real practices like income verification and tax audits. This fills a gap in existing models where the classifier is the only instrument. The framework yields new design levers beyond down-weighting or discarding gameable features.

entry.title: SPIBER: Reconstructing Free Energy Landscapes from Short, Unconverged Trajectories with Generative Flow Networks

author.name: Venkata Sai Sreyas Adury (Chemical Physics Program and Institute for Physical Science and Technology, University of Maryland), Pratyush Tiwary (Biophysics Program and Institute for Physical Science and Technology, University of Maryland, Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry and Institute for Physical Science and Technology, University of Maryland, University of Maryland Institute for Health Computing, Bethesda, USA)

entry.summary: SPIBER combines the State Predictive Information Bottleneck with Generative Flow Networks to identify collective variables and reconstruct free energy landscapes from short, unconverged molecular simulation trajectories that sample different metastable states. This addresses a key limitation of histogram reweighting, which cannot correct population imbalances across unbiased trajectories. It is a meaningful methodological advance for molecular simulation and biophysics.

entry.title: CLEAR: Complex Learned Explicit Analytical Regularization for Ultra-Accelerated 4D Flow CMR Reconstruction

author.name: German Sh\^ama Wache, Sebastian Neumayer

entry.summary: Proposes CLEAR, the first learned regularizer for 4D cardiac MRI flow reconstruction, combining the interpretability of compressed-sensing variational objectives with the flexibility of learned models. It outperforms compressed sensing baselines in the ultra-accelerated 10x-50x regime of the CMRx4DFlow2026 challenge.

entry.title: Conformal Robustness in Prediction-Driven Decision-Making

author.name: Lingjie Zhao, Hansheng Jiang, Wei Qi

entry.summary: Builds a score-calibrated robustness framework that converts any fixed black-box point predictor into decision-relevant uncertainty representations via distribution-free conformal calibration. The conformal score serves as the primitive unit of robustness, powering coverage-calibrated uncertainty sets for robust optimization and a Conformal Robust Satisficing formulation with an induced fragility measure.

entry.title: Stochastic Flow Map for Count Data

author.name: Ganchao Wei

entry.summary: Proposes Count Flow Map, a generative model that learns finite-time stochastic transitions directly over count data using Poisson births and Binomial deaths, enabling one- or few-step generation of high-dimensional nonnegative integer data. This addresses the gap where diffusion and flow models are designed for continuous or categorical data and require many sequential evaluations.

entry.title: The Exponential Price of Determinism in Nonsmooth Nonconvex Optimization

author.name: Guy Kornowski

entry.summary: Resolves an open question in nonsmooth nonconvex optimization by proving that deterministic first-order algorithms require (1/epsilon)^Omega(d) oracle complexity to find Goldstein stationary points of Lipschitz functions. This closes the previously known exponential gap between randomized (dimension-free) and deterministic (dimension-dependent) complexity.

entry.title: Cost-Accuracy Trade-offs: Neural Operator vs Classical Numerical Solver

author.name: Daniel Zhengyu Huang, Andrew M. Stuart

entry.summary: Analyzes when and why neural operator surrogates outperform classical numerical PDE solvers in terms of cost for a given accuracy, focusing on the post-training many-query regime where training costs are amortized. Even in this deliberately favorable setting, the paper delineates conditions under which classical solvers retain advantages.

entry.title: Adversarially Robust PAC Learning with Optimal VC Rates

author.name: Steve Hanneke, Amirreza Shaeiri

entry.summary: Determines the optimal perturbation-map-independent sample complexity of adversarially robust PAC learning in both realizable and agnostic settings, characterizing rates in terms of the VC dimension of the concept class. This settles fundamental statistical limits of learning classifiers robust to every allowed perturbation of test points.

entry.title: Topographic Training Concentrates Causal Circuits Without Improving Neuron Monosemanticity

author.name: Gautam Ranka, Shubham Santosh Pandere, Aiden Dsouza

entry.summary: The paper tests whether a spatial-locality training loss (TopoLoss) can improve mechanistic interpretability of vision transformers at training time rather than post hoc. Across ImageNet-100 experiments, topographic training concentrated causally relevant circuits as measured by activation patching, but sparse autoencoder analysis showed no improvement in neuron monosemanticity.

entry.title: onPanda: Efficient Annotation of On-Policy Alignment Data for LLMs and Agents via Token-Level Correction

author.name: Lei Yang, Mengyin Liu, Jia Wang, Hangyu Guo, Liang Zhao, Zheng Ge, Kang An, Binxing Jiao, Qi Han, Daxin Jiang, Siqi Shen, Xiangyu Zhang

entry.summary: onPanda is an interactive annotation tool for LLM alignment data and agent trajectories built around token-level correction: the annotator edits the first bad token, the system truncates and regenerates from the corrected prefix in a locate-correct-continue loop. A controlled study reports a 52% reduction in median annotation time versus manual post-editing.

entry.title: Type-Driven Tokenization for Brahmic Scripts

author.name: Sai Hemanth Kapila, Rakshika Bagavathy

entry.summary: The paper shows that standard tokenizers produce malformed text for Brahmic abugida scripts (Devanagari, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada) because English-style orthography forms a semigroup under concatenation while Brahmic orthography forms only a partial semigroup. The authors formalize this distinction in Agda, model valid tokens as chains in a transition system, and derive type-driven tokenization rules.

entry.title: Team DArgk at the 2026 ELOQUENT lab for evaluating generative language model quality: Residuals of Humanity: AI Detection Evasion via GRPO Fine-Tuning

author.name: Antonela Tommasel, Juan Manuel Rodriguez

entry.summary: Introduces SHADE, a reinforcement learning framework that fine-tunes an instruction-tuned LLaMA model with Group Relative Policy Optimization to evade AI-generated text detectors, using a surrogate detector (PAN 2025 mdok) as feedback signal rather than post-hoc perturbations or prompt rewriting. It highlights the fragility of current AI-text detectors under adversarial generation and was developed for the ELOQUENT shared task.

entry.title: Pretrained Persona Mixture Models and Tandem Models for Human Simulation

author.name: Minwoo Kang, T\'ea Wright, Seun Eisape, Ayush Raj, Suhong Moon, Joseph Suh, Alane Suhr, David M. Chan, John Canny

entry.summary: Argues that the dominant practice of prompting instruction-tuned assistants to role-play personas produces inaccurate, stereotyped human simulations, and shows instead that binding models to specific people via short naturalistic dialog samples yields well-calibrated Persona Mixture Models realized as pretrained base models. PMMs produce more accurate predictions than instruction-tuned alternatives, and demographics can be added later by querying without harm.

entry.title: Directing large language models to follow the letter or spirit of the law

author.name: Peng Qian, Andrew Li, Sam Chen, Sonia K. Murthy, Yonatan Belinkov, Tomer D. Ullman

entry.summary: Uses targeted adaptation to make LLMs prioritize either the spirit or the letter of the law, showing that minimal modifications significantly shift behavior across novel vignettes, real-world scenarios, and legal cases. Analysis of model internals reveals a low-dimensional, three-axis interpretable space matching a pre-specified framework for the geometry of legal concepts.

entry.title: Judging a Review by its Cover: A Reliability Analysis of LLM-based Peer Review Evaluation Metrics

author.name: Shakiba Amirshahi, Sajad Ebrahimi, Hai Son Le, Negar Arabzadeh, Ebrahim Bagheri

entry.summary: Proposes a statistical framework testing whether LLM-as-a-judge peer-review metrics measure substantive review quality versus surface linguistic polish, using faithful LLM rewrites that preserve evaluative content while changing form. This is directly relevant as reviewers increasingly use LLMs to polish reviews.

entry.title: Efficient Reasoning Exploration via State-Conditioned Latent Steering with Progress Guidance

author.name: Hengyuan Zhang, Chenming Shang, Zunhai Su, Xiao Liang, Hui Shen, Jing Xiong, Dawei Li, Shiping Yang, Kailai Yang, Wei Zhang, Ruobing Xie, Hayden Kwok-Hay So, Ngai Wong

entry.summary: The paper identifies exploration collapse in post-trained reasoning models, where Best-of-N rollouts follow near-identical paths and waste inference budget. It proposes SPS, a training-free latent steering method with progress guidance that pushes sampled continuations toward diverse paths that make meaningful progress. This improves the efficiency of inference-time reasoning without additional training.

entry.title: SocioVerse2: A Longitudinal Dynamic Social Simulation Framework under a Human-AI Co-evolutionary Paradigm

author.name: Xinnong Zhang, Jiayu Lin, Jia Wang, Yixu Huang, Xinyi Mou, Yingqian Wu, Jingcong Liang, Shijun Lei, Jianing Shi, Guanying Li, Siyuan Wang, Hanjia Lyu, Zhenfei Yin, Yunlu Yin, Siming Chen, Yulan He, Jiebo Luo, Xuanjing Huang, Liyin Jin, Baohua Zhou, Hanqi Yan, Zhongyu Wei

entry.summary: This paper introduces SocioVerse2, an extension of the SocioVerse 1.0 social simulation platform into a human-AI co-evolutionary paradigm built around two feedback loops and shared infrastructure. It targets two gaps in existing agent-based social simulation tools: allowing researchers to intervene in simulation content and to control the process that generates it, while supporting longitudinal (long-horizon) dynamics rather than static cross-sectional snapshots. The work matters because credible social simulation with generative agents is increasingly used as a stand-in for costly real-world experiments, and systematic researcher control plus temporal evolution addresses key validity concerns.

entry.title: AURA: Uncertainty-Routed Activation Editing for Acoustic Grounding in Speech Foundation Models

author.name: Natarajan Balaji Shankar, Zilai Wang, Zihan Wang, Mohan Shi, Kaiyuan Zhang, Abeer Alwan

entry.summary: Proposes AURA, an ultra-efficient representation-editing method that freezes a pretrained AED speech foundation model and applies sparse scale-and-shift edits to decoder cross-attention heads, routed by cross-attention uncertainty features that capture over-concentration, diffuse attention, and abrupt frame shifts. It targets non-speech hallucination and acoustic grounding failures across four datasets including imperfect-label child speech.

entry.title: UK-PRBENCH: A Paragraph-Level Precedent Retrieval Benchmark for United Kingdom Case Law

author.name: Damith Premasiri, Tharindu Ranasinghe

entry.summary: UK-PRBENCH is a new benchmark for paragraph-level prior case retrieval in UK law, built from judgments in the UK National Archives and spanning many courts and tribunals. It moves beyond document-level relevance, evaluating state-of-the-art retrieval models and establishing baselines showing current methods are suboptimal at paragraph granularity.

entry.title: Authority-Preserving Evaluation of Medical Vision-Language Assistants

author.name: Flint Xiaofeng Fan, Cheston Tan, Yew-Soon Ong, Roger Wattenhofer

entry.summary: AuthEval is a logging and evaluation framework that distinguishes proposal quality from selected-action quality for medical vision-language assistants, recording both the model's proposal and the local service's accepted action and scoring them under declared local criteria. It quantifies an authority gap only when the record supports it, reflecting that local services retain referral authority under policy and capacity constraints.

entry.title: Rethinking Vision Architectures with Gated Linear Attention and KAN

author.name: Ali Mehizel, Oussama Khaldi

entry.summary: LKAT introduces an isotropic ViT encoder that pairs chunkwise Gated Linear Attention with a two-layer Kolmogorov-Arnold Network feed-forward block, replacing both quadratic MHSA and fixed-activation MLPs, plus a fused RBF-KAN kernel for efficiency. It is evaluated under a shared DeiT-style recipe to isolate architectural effects.

entry.title: An Evolutionary Agentic Approach for Open-ended Image Quality Perception

author.name: Zhenchen Tang, Bo Peng, Zichuan Wang, Songlin Yang, Leilei Cao, Fengjie Zhu, Jing Dong

entry.summary: Introduces PACE, a training-free multi-agent framework that formulates open-ended image quality assessment as explicit protocol construction, addressing holistic bias where models reuse generic quality priors on unseen perceptual dimensions such as physical plausibility and text rendering. This matters because generative models are creating new quality dimensions that fixed IQA models cannot handle.

entry.title: ScaleBlind: Point Cloud Completion under Unknown Scale

author.name: Shenghui Wu, Chen Wang, Yuan Feng, Guangshun Wei, Yuanfeng Zhou, Changjian Li

entry.summary: ScaleBlind identifies a hidden assumption in learning-based point cloud completion: reliance on ground-truth scale normalization at both train and test time, which causes severe artifacts (over/under-completion, nested shells) when that oracle cue is unavailable. The method leverages foundation image generation models, which understand object scale, to enable completion under unknown scale. A sharp problem identification with a creative solution direction.

entry.title: Evaluating the Generalization of Neuroimaging Foundation Models on African Brain MRI

author.name: Oluwatobi Iyanuoluwa Akinmuleya, Olatokun Shamsudeen Akano, Samuel Danquah Ankapong, Olamide Lawal, Toufiq Musah

entry.summary: The paper evaluates four neuroimaging foundation models (BrainIAC, Neuro-JEPA, NeuroVFM, Primus) on a three-way diagnostic task using 88 Nigerian brain MRI subjects across four modality configurations, comparing against a trained ViT3D baseline. Frozen backbones collapse to majority-class predictions, revealing serious generalization failures on underrepresented populations.

entry.title: All-in-One Multilingual Scene Text Recognition with Script-aware Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Xingsong Ye, Yongkun Du, Jiaxin Zhang, Zhixian Li, Chong Sun, Chen Li, Jing Lyu, Lianwen Jin, Zhineng Chen

entry.summary: The authors build a single multilingual scene text recognizer using a script-aware mixture-of-experts design, supported by TextMuSS-10M, a large synthetic dataset spanning 10 scripts and 229 languages. The approach aims to be simpler and cheaper than per-language recognizers and smaller VLMs while being more accurate on many scripts. This addresses a real practical gap in multilingual OCR.

entry.title: CoaG: Cylinders on a Grid: Coarse 3D Layout Control for Video Generation

author.name: Zhangsihao Yang, Mengyi Shan

entry.summary: CoaG enables controlling person placement and camera motion in generated videos with minimal geometric input: a ground-plane grid and one cylinder per person, animated over 81 frames, rendered photorealistically with appearance from a text prompt and background reference. Since no dataset pairs this signal with video, the authors generate their own via an automatic captioning and synthesis pipeline. This offers an accessible, coarse control scheme for video generation.

entry.title: IMPLICIT-Bench: Measuring Implicit Bias in Text-to-Image Models under Neutral Prompts

author.name: Yue Dai, Ziyang Liu, Marc Cheong, Caren Han

entry.summary: IMPLICIT-Bench measures implicit bias in text-to-image models that emerges when stereotype-relevant attributes are left unspecified in natural prompts, going beyond template-based explicit attribute probes. It builds controlled prompt triplets (neutral, stereotype, anti-stereotype) via a structured knowledge graph so scene semantics are held constant while a single bias dimension varies.

entry.title: Revisiting Multi-View Stereo: A Sequence-to-Sequence Formulation

author.name: Aoxiang Fan, Corentin Dumery, Nicolas Talabot, Pascal Fua

entry.summary: The paper reformulates multi-view stereo with known cameras as a sequence-to-sequence task that jointly predicts geometry for all input views, bridging conventional MVS and modern feed-forward methods. It introduces a global transformer-based architecture to mitigate the reconstruction ambiguity and geometry distortion that afflict feed-forward models.

entry.title: Omni2Web: Benchmarking Audiovisual Website Development

author.name: Minghao Han, Zhenghao Xing, Xize Cheng, Yuxuan Wang, Junming Lin, Ling Wang, Yinsong Yan, Yunfei Chu, Qize Yang, Jin Xu

entry.summary: Omni2Web is a bilingual benchmark of 918 instances spanning 13,907 edit steps for evaluating models on web-editing requests from screen recordings, where weak deictic expressions like this and there require recovering intent from speech, cursor trajectories, page state, and edit history. It defines three tracks (Direct Editing, Instruction Recovery, Instruction Utility) and evaluates 17 open- and closed-source models, with the best achieving only 51.17 on the Edit Fidelity Score. This matters because it exposes a substantial gap in multimodal agentic web-editing capabilities that existing web-editing benchmarks miss.

entry.title: MoSAT: Human Motion Generation from Spatial Audio and Textual Description

author.name: Shuyang Xu, Zhiyang Dou, Yiduo Hao, Zekun Li, Liang Pan, Jingbo Wang, Cheng Lin, Yuan Liu, Wenping Wang, Mingmin Zhao, Taku Komura

entry.summary: Introduces the novel task of full-body human motion synthesis jointly conditioned on spatial audio and natural language, releasing STAM, a dataset pairing motion sequences with spatial audio and detailed text. Proposes MoSAT, a latent flow-matching framework for this joint audio-text conditioning.

entry.title: CHOREO: Every Humanoid Skill as a Trajectory

author.name: Ziyi Sun, Jingwen Chen, Yuxi Wang, Xiuze Xia, Long Cheng, Zhaoxiang Zhang, Yujun Dong

entry.summary: Presents CHOREO, a training-free framework for composing heterogeneous humanoid skills by converting every learned capability into a unified SkillMotion representation of motion states, contacts, semantics, and boundary conditions, then composing skills via continuation, cubic Hermite blending, or variational methods.

entry.title: ReliCAD: From Uncertain LLM Generation to Reliable Parametric CAD Modeling

author.name: Peng Zheng, Xintong Dong, Chuanyang Li, Jiaxin Jing, Chuqi Han, Hailong Shen, Yanzhi Song, Zhouwang Yang

entry.summary: Presents ReliCAD, a framework that converts uncertain natural-language LLM generation into reliable parametric CAD modeling by explicitly modeling design intent and leveraging the deterministic capabilities of CAD kernels. The approach addresses the mismatch between probabilistic language models and the deterministic, validity-critical requirements of CAD.

entry.title: Expert-Play Contouring Control: Faster-than-Demonstration Planning from Slow Expert and Fast Play

author.name: Seunghoon Cho, Wonsuhk Jung, Sundhar Vinodh Sangeetha, Shreyas Kousik

entry.summary: EPCC tackles faster-than-demonstration execution by combining slow expert demonstrations with fast, non-expert play data: demonstrations train a latent trajectory generator reparameterized into a time-independent contour of task progression, while play data trains a world model of fast-action outcomes. At deployment a planner uses the world model to optimize accelerated actions safely.

entry.title: Selective Commitment for Language-Guided Object Retrieval under Partial Observability

author.name: Wonhee Koh, Sushil Samuel Dinesh, Hansol Ko, Shinkyu Park, Eungjoo Lee

entry.summary: Presents a closed-loop framework for language-guided object retrieval that decides whether to gather evidence, interact, grasp, or abstain, maintaining a persistent joint belief over target identity, container relation, and absence hypotheses. Conformal grasp eligibility and finite-horizon belief-space planning govern commitment decisions under partial observability. It matters because calibrated abstention under uncertainty is essential for reliable robots in unstructured environments.

entry.title: TaskAnchor: Grounding Task State in Reactive VLAs for Long-Horizon Manipulation

author.name: Hengyan Liu, Wenlve Zhou, Bo Yue, Yongyi Su, Ruixiang Wang, Zhanqi Zhang, Dekun Lu, Wei Gao, Xiaofen Xing, Kui Jia

entry.summary: Introduces TaskAnchor, a lightweight adapter that fixes task-state aliasing in reactive VLA models by injecting execution history via history-conditioned visual refinement and a milestone-supervised task-state scalar. Plugs into native visual and language interfaces without a planner or changes to action generation. Reports roughly 4.9-point improvements on RMBench for long-horizon manipulation.

entry.title: BarrierFormer: Transformer-Guided Predictive Barrier Enforcement for Safe Robot Control

author.name: Anandsingh Chauhan, Kunal Garg

entry.summary: BarrierFormer trains a transformer on barrier functions to provide predictive, receding-horizon-like safety enforcement without solving the constrained optimization MPC requires each step. Addresses the myopia of standard control barrier functions that only enforce safety at the current timestep. Targets real-time safe control for safety-critical robotics.

entry.title: Dexterous Robot Manipulation from Human Demonstrations via Contact-Anchored Retargeting and Residual Policy Learning

author.name: Zihao Yang, Chengyuan Liu, Yu Zhou, Runze Lv, Tianyu Cui, Sheng Yi, Haohua Zhu, Irvine Lu, JieQ Sun

entry.summary: This paper tackles the data bottleneck in dexterous manipulation by retargeting human demonstrations based on contact structure—what touches the object and in what order—rather than joint motion, since contact forces are absent from scalable human data sources. A single residual RL policy, trained once across diverse demonstrations, repairs kinematic recordings into physically consistent, contact-annotated trajectories. This offers a scalable path to converting cheap human video data into usable robot training data.

entry.title: SPARSER: Sparse Variable Projection by Exploiting Separable Structure in Robotic Perception

author.name: Nikolas R. Sanderson, Andrew Fishberg, Haoyu Han, Heng Yang, Jonathan P. How, Hanumant Singh, Michael Everett, Alan Papalia

entry.summary: SPARSER exploits separability in nonlinear least-squares problems of robotic perception via variable projection, analytically eliminating linearly appearing variables such as landmarks conditioned on poses. It addresses the gauge symmetry challenges (global translation and rotation invariance) that limited prior VarPro use, yielding faster solvers for large perception problems.

entry.title: KerColle: Unlocking Fine-Grained GPU Concurrency in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Anna Li, Christina Giannoula, Nandita Vijaykumar

entry.summary: Characterizes GPU underutilization in VLA model inference across four state-of-the-art VLAs, attributing inefficiency to head-of-line blocking in the hardware thread-block dispatcher when the decoupled VLM and action-head phases fail to overlap. Proposes KerColle to unlock fine-grained GPU concurrency and improve inference throughput toward robot control-rate requirements.

entry.title: DENSE: Distilling Agent Trajectories into Evidence-Grounded Shortcut Trees for Self-Refinement

author.name: Siyuan Liu (Fudan University, Meituan Longcat Team), Fan Yu (Fudan University, Meituan Longcat Team), Dongyu Ru (Meituan Longcat Team), Yizhu Liu (Meituan Longcat Team), Yifan Yang (Meituan Longcat Team), Xuezhi Cao (Meituan Longcat Team), Xunliang Cai (Meituan Longcat Team), Yixin Cao (Fudan University)

entry.summary: DENSE distills abundant online agent execution traces into evidence-grounded nested shortcut trees that capture local progress, recovery, and unfinished requirements without post-hoc outcome labels. It introduces REFIT, a source-paired protocol for comparing feedback quality, and links reusable progress to remaining obligations for agent self-refinement. This turns cheap deployment byproducts into scalable agent improvement signal.

entry.title: Designer-RSI: Evolving Procedural Memory from User Traffic for Agentic Graphic Design

author.name: Hongyang Du, Lan Yan, Christian Flores, Asim Kadav

entry.summary: Designer-RSI is a continual adaptation framework where a frozen frontier model operates professional design software through more than 230 tools, while an external natural-language procedural memory accumulates and refines reusable design skills from user traffic. The memory widens by acquiring procedures for uncovered subtasks and deepens by revising procedures against success/failure feedback, with a replay gate admitting only non-regressive changes.

entry.title: Potential-Field Action Representation for Reinforcement Learning in Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Xinyu Liu, G\"okhan Solak, Arash Ajoudani

entry.summary: PA-RL is a reinforcement learning framework for contact-rich manipulation that uses artificial potential fields as the action representation, so the policy modulates attractor/repulsor parameters rather than issuing direct Cartesian motion commands each step. This decouples task-level adaptation from low-level motion generation, easing exploration and physical execution. The design could make model-free RL more practical for real-world contact tasks.

entry.title: UniGIO: Unified Generative Global In-situ Weather Modeling from Spatiotemporal Incomplete Observations

author.name: Songru Yang, Zili Liu, Tao Han, Ben Fei, Lei Bai, Chang Liu, Zhengxia Zou, Xiangyang Ji, Wanli Ouyang, Zhenwei Shi

entry.summary: UniGIO is a generative framework for modeling global in-situ weather dynamics directly from sparse, incomplete station observations, generating missing values rather than waiting for error-prone AI-ready completed datasets. It targets fine-scale, localized weather dynamics critical for numerical weather prediction, disaster prevention, and agriculture.

entry.title: Didactic knowledge or Clinical Cases? How Data Types Shape Medical Large Language Models

author.name: Yuzheng Fan, Haochun Wang, Sendong Zhao, Xiao Han, Ming Ma, Bing Qin

entry.summary: The paper uses token-matched experiments varying the didactic-to-clinical data ratio to show asymmetric transfer in medical LLM training: clinical data improves clinic-oriented tasks while staying competitive on knowledge tasks, whereas textbook data mainly helps knowledge-intensive tasks. Error analysis reveals a knowing-doing gap between knowledge and clinical application.

entry.title: StateMem: Single-State Residual Memory with Adaptive Inference for Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Wenzhuo Li, Qiongfeng Shi, Yi Zhou

entry.summary: StateMem proposes a single-state residual memory framework for vision-language-action robotic policies, using prediction error to update a persistent memory token via low-rank residuals and to adaptively route cached prefixes. A training-free online controller adjusts routing thresholds, and fast correction compensates for stale prefix features. It improves on external memory banks like MemoryVLA by avoiding explicit storage and retrieval.

entry.title: Stealing profits: Spread-based temporal hierarchy forecasting for day-ahead electricity markets

author.name: Arkadiusz Lipiecki, Nikolaos Kourentzes, Rafal Weron

entry.summary: Shows that a temporal hierarchy forecasting framework jointly reconciling hourly electricity prices and all intraday price spreads improves performance across German and Spanish markets and three forecasting architectures, with accuracy gains up to 19.7% and battery-arbitrage profit gains up to 10.4% on five years of out-of-sample data. Gains persist even against a highly accurate pretrained TabPFN foundation model.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy and Surface Fluency: Risk-Sensitive Evaluation of LLMs for Legal Clause Generation

author.name: Devansh Singh, Sundaraparipurnan Narayanan

entry.summary: The paper proposes a risk-sensitive evaluation framework for LLM-drafted contract clauses, combining the CLAUSE classifier taxonomy with 34 legally-motivated failure modes across 22 clause categories. It evaluates four small/fast models (Claude Haiku 4.5, Gemini 2.5 Flash Lite, GPT 5.4 Nano, Qwen 3.5 Flash) and shows that fluent clauses can still carry severe legal risk such as omitted carve-outs or unenforceable risk allocation.

entry.title: Vox-Infinity: Benchmarking the Limits of Long-Context Spoken Language Models

author.name: Xize Cheng, Wenxu Jia, Chenyuhao Wen, Dongjie Fu, Zehan Wang, Xinyu Zhang, Tao Jin

entry.summary: Introduces Vox-Infinity, the first benchmark for long-context understanding in spoken language models, systematically extending audio history along turn count and turn duration dimensions across diverse interaction structures and semantic complexities. It targets the amplified forgetting problem in speech, where audio requires far more embeddings than text to preserve semantics and acoustic cues.

entry.title: Time-Incremental Continued Pretraining of LLMs: Knowledge Updates Without Catastrophic Forgetting

author.name: F{\i}rat \"Oncel, Salman Hussain Ali, Mirco Ravanelli, Cem Subakan, \c{C}a\u{g}atay Y{\i}ld{\i}z

entry.summary: Studies time-incremental continued pretraining in the realistic regime where successive FineWeb-Edu snapshots share substantial URL overlap, evaluating six open-weight models across three families and four scales (1B-8B) on data strictly after each model's knowledge cutoff. It organizes findings on updating knowledge without catastrophic forgetting under realistic overlapping-crawl conditions.

entry.title: ZIL: Zero-shot Image-to-LiDAR Registration

author.name: Zijun Li, Xiaotian Sun, Xuelun Shen, Yao Dai, Sheng Ao, Yangyang Shi, Jakob Engel, Zhipeng Cai, Cheng Wang

entry.summary: ZIL is presented as the first foundation model for zero-shot, non-synchronized image-to-LiDAR registration, using Vision and Point Transformers to encode inputs and jointly regressing relative pose with 3D coordinate prediction. It addresses two persistent limitations of prior work: distant-frame inputs and lack of generalization to unseen scenarios.

entry.title: Mira-Scene: Pixel-Aligned Layouts for Generative 3D Scene

author.name: Yang-Tian Sun, Tianjia Liu, Zehuan Huang, Yi-Hua Huang, Xiaoyang Lyu, Ziyi Yang, Zi-Xin Zou, Yuan-Chen Guo, Yan-Pei Cao, Xiaojuan Qi

entry.summary: Mira-Scene is a compositional 3D scene reconstruction framework that replaces sparse pose regression with dense, bounded correspondence recovery via Canonical Coordinate fields, enabling single-image object generation to be accurately placed into coherent scenes. This improves layout generalization under scarce scene-level supervision while preserving object fidelity.

entry.title: What Makes a Good Medical Image Tokenizer? Rethinking Reconstruction and Generation in Medical Image Tokenization

author.name: Niklas Bubeck, Yundi Zhang, Vasiliki Sideri-Lampretsa, Julian McGinnis, Jiancheng Yang, Daniel Rueckert, Jiazhen Pan

entry.summary: This systematic study evaluates around thirty tokenizers for medical latent diffusion pipelines, testing the unexamined assumption that natural-image tokenizers transfer to medical imaging where datasets are smaller and inter-sample variance is lower. It examines how tokenizer choice bounds reconstruction fidelity, generation quality, and downstream representations. The findings provide practical guidance for building medical generative models.

entry.title: ForceRFT: Refining VLA Actions through Force-Guided Residual Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yichen Wang, Chaoyang Zhang, Xuqi Su, Jun Ma, Haiyue Zhu, Xiaocong Li

entry.summary: ForceRFT improves force-conditioned vision-language-action policies with a residual RL framework: a frozen demonstration-trained SmolVLA prior generates force-conditioned action chunks while a lightweight residual actor refines end-effector commands using wrist force feedback, learning from both human corrections and autonomous task outcomes. This enables contact-dependent recovery beyond demonstration coverage.

entry.title: SCULPT-VLA: Learning Structured Control through Staged Action Grounding

author.name: Wenbo Li, Yiteng Chen, Wei Zhang, Wenhao Li, Jun Yang, Qingyao Wu

entry.summary: Introduces SCULPT-VLA, a vision-language-action policy that learns structured control via staged action grounding: an action-conditioning state is composed of factors for task progression, scene dynamics, and spatial grounding, first formed with teacher scaffolds and then grounded through their composition as scaffolds are withdrawn, with direct perception restored for continuous refinement. This tackles the open question of what intermediate representations VLA actions should depend on. It contributes to the trend of structured supervision in robot policies.

entry.title: RiverVLN: Phase-Grounded Temporal Vision--Language Navigation for Unmanned Surface Vehicles

author.name: Jieling Wu, Yuehao Huang, Jiajun Lv, Tao Huang, Yong Liu, Weiwei Liu

entry.summary: Introduces RiverVLN, claimed as the first benchmark for long-horizon vision-language navigation of unmanned surface vehicles under continuous riverine motion, plus PGT-NAV, a phase-grounded temporal navigation framework that converts instructions into phase-based motion rather than mapping whole instructions to discrete actions. Indoor-centric VLN assumptions break down on water due to inertia and sparse ambiguous landmarks. This extends VLN to an underexplored continuous-motion maritime domain.

entry.title: ContactDP: Contact-Guided Diffusion Policy for Tight Insertion Tasks

author.name: Chengyi Xing, Shaoxiong Yao, Diego Romeres, Devesh K. Jha

entry.summary: ContactDP is a multimodal diffusion policy for high-precision connector insertion that fuses wrist RGB, fingertip tactile sensing, and wrist force-torque measurements to infer contact state and generate temporally extended corrective actions. Targets tight mechanical tolerances, partial observability, and multimodal contact ambiguity. Industrial insertion is a strong practical testbed for diffusion policies.

entry.title: CaLR: Causal Latent Revision for Robust Diffusion Reasoning

author.name: Wei Cai, Jian Zhao, Yuchen Yuan, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: CaLR combines autoregressive and diffusion language model strengths by reformulating reasoning as constrained latent optimization. It uses a causal topology matrix from an expert model with implicit differentiation to perform gradient-guided thought revision during parallel generation. It reports SOTA diffusion language model performance on complex benchmarks, surpassing strong AR baselines.

entry.title: PlaceReasoner-Beta: Reasoning-Driven Macro Placement and Benchmarking

author.name: Qiufeng Li, Chengxuan Wang, Rongqian Chen, Quan Cheng, Yihui Ren, Chia-Tung Ho, David Z. Pan, Tian Lan, Weidong Cao

entry.summary: PlaceReasoner-Beta reformulates VLSI macro placement as a closed-loop reasoning problem using a verifier-guided multi-agent framework, with a vision-language model planner generating candidate placements from floorplan images and design specifications. It incorporates visual context, design expertise, and downstream physical-design feedback in one loop, contrasting with one-shot numerical optimization on proxy objectives. It also contributes benchmarking infrastructure.

entry.title: One Prompt Does Not Fit All: Self-Meta-Evolve for Personalized Information Extraction

author.name: Hongliang Li, Lu Wang, Yong Xu, Hanyang Chen, Zhitao Hou, Xiaoting Qin, Song Ge, Qingwei Lin, Dongmei Zhang

entry.summary: Self-Meta-Evolve formulates enterprise information extraction as per-user prompt adaptation under interaction feedback, maintaining a dedicated prompt for each user refined through a dual-loop process. An inner loop edits structured prompts based on persona-conditioned feedback while an outer loop evolves the meta-prompt itself by distilling successful adaptation patterns.

entry.title: MIST: Multimodal Survival Prediction with Genomic-Guided Histology Attention

author.name: Muhammet Sami Yavuz, Sabri Mustafa Kahya, Richard R. Chen, Jana Lipkova, Benedikt Wiestler

entry.summary: MIST fuses whole-slide histology images and genomic profiles for survival prediction by representing genomic features as tokens that query compact foundation-model-derived histology context tokens before prediction, rather than late-fusing separately encoded modalities. Training combines discrete-time survival objectives with genomic masking, WSI dropout, and modality alignment losses, targeting robustness under cohort shift.

entry.title: Hallucination-R1: Robustness-Oriented Paraphrase Generation for Factual Consistency

author.name: Wenhan Yu, Wenxin Wu, Hao Wang, Lei Sha

entry.summary: The paper studies paraphrase-induced hallucination, where models answer correctly in original form but fail under semantically equivalent paraphrases, and proposes HALLUCINATION-R1, a framework that learns to generate semantically faithful yet robustness-challenging paraphrases to train and evaluate factual consistency. It balances the weak-signal near-copy and equivalence-breaking extremes of generic paraphrasers.

entry.title: CESBench: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Cryptographic Engineering Security for IoT Devices

author.name: Wenquan Zhou, An Wang, Jing Liang, Peien Feng, Jingqi Zhang, Yaoling Ding, Liehuang Zhu

entry.summary: CESBench is a benchmark of 380 expert-written items covering six sub-domains of cryptographic engineering security for IoT devices, including side-channel analysis, fault injection, implementation, countermeasures, evaluation, and integration. It uses four task types (multiple choice, judgment, and others) to test recall and deeper security verdicts. This fills a gap between cryptography and general cybersecurity LLM benchmarks.

entry.title: OneBid: A Unified Auto-Bidding Foundation Model for Diverse oCPX Advertising Scenarios

author.name: Yewen Li, Peng Jiang, Yitian Li, Pengfei Lv, Xialong Liu, Peng Jiang, Qingpeng Cai

entry.summary: OneBid is a unified auto-bidding foundation model that consolidates heterogeneous oCPX advertising scenarios (registration, purchase, etc.) that are currently served by fragmented per-scenario models. It tackles multi-objective control, scalable capacity under strict latency constraints, and safe offline policy improvement. Applying foundation-model thinking to computational advertising could reduce pipeline fragmentation and enable cross-scenario transfer.

entry.title: Outcome-Conditioned End-Effector Geometry Across Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Xingyu Lin, Zhuang Li, Zhongrun Wu, Shouquan Zhou, Dehui Du

entry.summary: Analyzing 15,000 closed-loop LIBERO rollouts from four VLA policies in 3,600 configuration-matched pairs, this study shows successful executions across different policies share much more similar end-effector geometry (median normalized DTW distance 0.0120 m) than executions where only one policy succeeds (0.0380 m). The finding suggests convergent physical solutions underlying task success, though the ratio varies across representations.

entry.title: Detecting Pretraining Data in Large Language Models from a Free-Energy Perspective

author.name: Chenye Ke, Zirui Liu, Qi Liu, Yan Zhuang, Jintao Zhang, Zhenya Huang, Shijin Wang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a membership-inference detector for LLM pretraining data that uses an inclined boundary in the joint space of prediction loss and predictive entropy, showing entropy correction preserves the membership signal while reducing variance and improving member-nonmember separation. It extends the mean-variance analysis to settings with a nonzero mean entropy gap.

entry.title: Correcting Learning-based Perception for Safety

author.name: Yan Miao, Hussein Darir, Sayan Mitra

entry.summary: The authors propose a two-step runtime correction strategy for ML-based state estimation in autonomous systems: offline characterization of perception uncertainty via preimages of perception contracts, and runtime selection of conservative states using a risk heuristic to drive safe control decisions. Extensive simulations demonstrate reduced unsafe and overtly conservative control actions.

entry.title: SafeTune: A Unified Faithful Library for Auditing and Repairing Safety Drift in Fine-Tuned LLMs

author.name: Pratinav Seth, Saisab Sadhu, Anshul Kaushal, Vinay Kumar Sankarapu

entry.summary: SafeTune is a source-available library unifying four intervention paradigms for safety drift in fine-tuned LLMs: post-hoc weight recovery, safety-constrained fine-tuning, gradient-based unlearning, and inference-time steering, with shared interpretability, evaluation, and deployment utilities. A configuration-driven workflow and modular registry make methods comparable and extensible without reimplementation.

entry.title: Contrastive World Models

author.name: Bonnie Li

entry.summary: Building on Dreamer, this work replaces pixel reconstruction in the world model objective with a Deep InfoMax-like mutual information lower bound between state-action sequences and local patch features of future observations. This encourages latent dynamics models to retain planning-relevant information while ignoring visually irrelevant detail in complex environments.

entry.title: FIRM-WM: State-factorized factual-interventional recurrent modeling for reward-free visual planning

author.name: Yilun Wu, Yunjian Zhang, Aobo Li, Mujiangshan Wang, Haitao Wu, Aqiang Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces FIRM-WM, a pixel world model for reward-free visual planning that factorizes its recurrent state to make coordinates goal-comparable while retaining history-dependent dynamics like velocity and contact, and addresses the factual-versus-interventional mismatch of offline training against sampling-based planners. Designed for learning from offline video and solving new image-goal tasks.

entry.title: Leveraging Inference-Time Compute for Diffusion Models via Global Scheduling of Denoising Trajectories

author.name: Yuan Cao, Yifu Tang, Hangqi Li, Zeyu Zheng

entry.summary: Formulates inference-time compute scaling for diffusion models as a budget-allocation problem: given a fixed count of verifier-scored candidate noise draws, how to distribute search effort across denoising steps. Provides principled global scheduling strategies that improve sample quality without retraining.

entry.title: Discovering Physical Representation Languages

author.name: Linzhe Zhang, Changming Xu

entry.summary: Introduces the problem of recovering a hidden physical ontology (cell structure, intensive/extensive measurement types, duality sectors, gauge distinctions) directly from anonymous controlled experiments. Provides an identifiability theory and a constructive polynomial-time procedure that recovers carriers, differential sequences, Maxwell diagrams, and residual unbreakable equivalences.

entry.title: Belted Engression: Sufficient Dimension Reduction for Generative Distributional Regression

author.name: Wenxi Tan, Bing Li, Lingzhou Xue

entry.summary: Belted Engression bridges sufficient dimension reduction and conditional generative modeling via a compress-then-generate paradigm that embeds a structural bottleneck in the generative architecture. The authors prove that the standard SDR condition is equivalent to a law-preserving generative factorization, giving theoretical grounding for the approach. This addresses a real weakness of modern conditional generative models: learning complex covariate dependencies efficiently with parameter-light architectures.

entry.title: The Neural Forcing for Three-Dimensional Incompressible Navier-Stokes finite time blowup

author.name: Beibei Li

entry.summary: The paper presents a two-part framework for forced 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes: a physics-informed neural system that generates and screens structured external-force trajectories via differentiable PDE rollouts or PPO-Clip, and a mathematical certification layer deriving reciprocal-vorticity criteria implying Riccati-type growth and finite-time blowup. It deliberately separates neural candidate discovery from rigorous continuum analysis with a validated transfer strategy. This connects deep learning to deep open problems in PDE theory.

entry.title: Acceptance-Aware Draft Model Training for Speculative Decoding

author.name: Tianhua Xia, Mugilan Ganesan, Yifei Feng, Haiyu Wang, Maximilian Egger, Sai Qian Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes training losses for speculative decoding draft models that directly optimize the expected number of accepted tokens in a speculative window, rather than cross-entropy or KL-divergence proxies that only encourage distribution matching. It also handles the differing acceptance mechanisms between greedy and sampling-based verification.

entry.title: 1% of Tokens Can Be Enough: On Gradient Estimation in On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Huanxin Sheng, Zhiling Ye, Haonan Wang, Jian Wang, Jinjie Gu, Jian Kang

entry.summary: The paper studies gradient estimation noise in sparse on-policy distillation, proposing an information-efficiency ratio (IER) derived from a signal-to-noise decomposition in information geometry to select which tokens receive teacher supervision. Adding IER-based token selection improves existing OPD methods on math and medical reasoning while retaining the sampled reverse-KL objective.

entry.title: AdaMem: Adaptive Memory Token Allocation for Soft Compression in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Artem Sakhno, Grigorii Davydenko, Omar Zoloev, Julia Belikova, Andrey Savchenko, Maksim Makarenko

entry.summary: AdaMem allocates a fixed memory-token budget across retrieved passages in a query-dependent way, mapping learned relevance estimates to the number of continuous memory embeddings each passage receives under a shared query-conditioned compressor. This relevance-guided soft compression aims to cut RAG cost while reducing distraction from irrelevant evidence.

entry.title: Does the Truthfulness Signal Survive Code-Mixing? Probing Hidden States for Hallucination Detection in Hinglish

author.name: Tanveer Singh (Plaksha University)

entry.summary: The paper tests whether hidden-state hallucination probes trained on clean-language activations transfer to Hindi-English code-mixed (Hinglish) input, building a 5,674-item trilingual QA benchmark with 17,022 labeled responses from open-weight models. It addresses a real gap, since a large user population writes code-mixed text that existing probing work has never evaluated.

entry.title: StyleAT: Defending Face Recognition Against Semantic Attacks

author.name: Ben Shapira, Roi Cohen, Shang-Tse Chen, Mahmood Sharif

entry.summary: Introduces BoundStyle, a fast semantic adversarial attack in StyleGAN's latent space that is roughly 9.5x faster than prior attacks while achieving high success rates, enabling practical adversarial training. Builds StyleAT, a defense that trains face recognition models against realistic semantic edits like aging or pose changes that induce misclassification.

entry.title: Adapting Boltz-2 with limited experimental activity data improves early enrichment in virtual screening

author.name: Kairi Furui, Masahito Ohue

entry.summary: The authors fine-tune the affinity prediction heads of Boltz-2 with small numbers of binary activity labels to improve hit prioritization in virtual screening. On retrospective evaluations across eight MF-PCBA targets, fine-tuning with 300 labels increased actives in the top 1% by a geometric mean of 1.77-fold.

entry.title: DeepInstructor: An Agentic AI Instructor for Experience-Driven Idea Evaluation

author.name: Rongcan Pei, Fang Guo, Qinglin Qi, Qi Zhu, Yun Luo, Jianhao Yan, Minjun Zhu, Qiujie Xie, Dehong Zheng, Yue Zhang

entry.summary: DeepInstructor frames research-idea evaluation as reasoning over structured scholarly experience, building an Experience Graph from 58,607 peer reviews and using a ReAct-based agent to retrieve dimension-specific evidence for traceable judgments. It also contributes DeepInstruct, a controlled dataset for idea-evaluation research.

entry.title: H2LooP Telecom Model v1: From Telecom Comprehension to Autonomous Issue and PR Resolution

author.name: Amit Singh, Vedant Nipane, Mayank Goel, Pulkit Agrawal, Sairanjan Mishra

entry.summary: This paper introduces H2LooP Telecom Model v1, a domain-specialized LLM for telecommunications released in two variants: a comprehension model for telecom question answering and an agentic model for autonomous telecom code generation, PR resolution, and commits on production repositories. The authors report strong results on the GSMA Open Telecom Lite benchmark and a proprietary code-generation benchmark, claiming to outperform frontier closed-source models like GPT-5 and Claude Opus on independent leaderboard evaluation while preserving general capabilities. Domain-specific fine-tuning for vertical industries matters because it demonstrates that smaller specialized models can beat general frontier models in narrow but economically important domains.

entry.title: Do Chess Explanations Reflect Model Decisions? Behavioral and Token-Level Tests of LLM Reasoning Faithfulness

author.name: Angelina Parfenova

entry.summary: Tests whether LLM explanations for chess moves are faithful to the underlying decision using 200 Lichess endgame puzzles, where ground truth is objectively evaluable. Using move recoverability, decoder-side controls, and token-level scoring, it finds explanations provide only small, decoder-dependent gains under strict masking, suggesting plausible explanations may not reflect actual decision drivers.

entry.title: LLMs Anchor on Chief Complaint and Fail to Integrate Evidence in Sequential Clinical Triage

author.name: Dipankar Srirag, Haokai Zhao, Ashutosh Kumar, Eleanor Hopper, Michael Dalton, Quoc Dung Nguyen, Aditya Joshi, Salil S. Kanhere, Padmanesan Narasimhan

entry.summary: Evaluates six LLMs on sequential emergency-department triage, predicting acuity from a growing prefix of nurse-patient conversations rather than completed retrospective records. All models degrade substantially in the sequential setting, anchoring on the chief complaint and failing to integrate later evidence, contradicting optimistic prior evaluations.

entry.title: Paragraph Boundaries Are Not White Space:Compression Depth as the Signature of Hierarchical Structure

author.name: Shuyang Xiang

entry.summary: Uses hierarchical rotary positional encoding with separate paragraph/sentence/token channels to intervene on the paragraph coordinate and measure cross-paragraph attention with a token-distance-exact estimator. It finds attention compression alone is not diagnostic of structure; the depth of compression distinguishes genuine hierarchical structure from density-matched random labels.

entry.title: Re:CAP - Auditing Retrieval Coverage in Production RAG Pipelines

author.name: Aviral Joshi, Hanoz Bhathena, Max Nelson, Saket Sharma

entry.summary: Re:CAP is a reference-free audit loop for deployed RAG pipelines that probes for evidence of missing documents rather than exhaustively labeling relevance over huge, non-stationary corpora. It inspects the initial answer and retrieved context, identifies covered topics, generates probing questions for plausibly missing topics, and retrieves candidate documents to estimate coverage gaps. This addresses a genuine production monitoring gap where retrieval quality is usually ignored in favor of generation metrics.

entry.title: Written as a Record, Read as an Address: What a Forward Pass Leaves in an Operation's KV Cache

author.name: Lingfeng Wu, Behzad Shomali

entry.summary: The paper investigates what language models write into the KV cache when reading an operation such as swapping box contents, splitting a forward pass into a frozen writer and an isolated reader trained to recover state from the cache alone. On a synthetic boxes task, the reader recovers information from the cache, showing that operation spans leave recoverable latent records even though prior entity-tracking work suggested bindings are resolved only at query time. This refines understanding of how entity state is represented across the forward pass.

entry.title: Initial Evaluation of Potential Bias in Coverage of Humans in Wikidata

author.name: Clair Kronk

entry.summary: Presents an open-source auditing platform that ingests over 10 million statement bindings for more than 6 million humans on Wikidata via QLever and evaluates representation across gender, orientation, geography, ethnicity, multilingual coverage, occupation, and intersectional pairs using statistical tests. Because Wikidata increasingly grounds agentic AI and language models, systematic equity auditing of knowledge graphs is timely.

entry.title: LLM-Based FORM Code Generation with Verification-Driven Fine-Tuning

author.name: Bakar Chargeishvili

entry.summary: Shows that frontier LLMs achieve zero-percent execution pass rate on FORM, a symbolic manipulation language central to particle physics calculations, without documentation, establishing FORM as a genuine zero-shot language for LLMs. It then presents a verification-driven fine-tuning approach to teach LLMs to write FORM code. This opens AI tooling for a scientifically important but neglected DSL.

entry.title: Moonworks Lunara: Modeling Artistic Intelligence

author.name: Yan Wang, Yanzu Wang, Maitreyee Joshi, Samiha Sadeka, Partho Hassan, Reza Jarral, Sayeef Abdullah, Sabit Hassan

entry.summary: Moonworks Lunara is a text-to-image model built on a Diffusion Mixture Transformer architecture with a training algorithm that iteratively evolves the data distribution via informative sample acquisition and targeted injection of human-created art, framed around a concept called Artistic Intelligence. Benchmarked against seven models including FLUX.2-Klein-4B, Qwen-Image, and GPT-Image-1-Mini, it ranks first in aesthetic quality under GPT-5.6 Sol as evaluator.

entry.title: Seeing is not Enough: Vision-Language Models Perceive Evidence but Fail to Act

author.name: Yuyang Dai, Bofei Huang, Hongbo Zhang, Haoran Xie

entry.summary: This paper distinguishes perceptual failure from process failure in VLMs, showing models often correctly identify visual evidence yet fail to let it constrain their final decisions. It introduces VPAC-Bench spanning nine real-image process families and SRT, a structured intervention requiring models to link evidence to process state before answering, finding process failure widespread across VLMs.

entry.title: BrainIAC: Interactive 3D Brain Lesion Segmentation across Heterogeneous MRI Modalities with Online Adaptation

author.name: Wentian Xu, Anthony P Addison, Ziyun Liang, Harry Anthony, Guang Yang, Konstantinos Kamnitsas

entry.summary: Presents BrainIAC, a unified 3D segmentation framework combining a multi-modal backbone that handles heterogeneous MRI modality sets via zero-filling and random modality dropping, interactive segmentation, and online adaptation to distribution shifts from scanner, protocol, and pathology differences. Aimed at making lesion segmentation practical for real clinical deployment.

entry.title: BindCLIP: One Balanced Coupling For Compositional Vision Language Scoring

author.name: Liuyang Song, Yi Zhang, Zhongyi Deng, Daqian Yang, Hongbo Zhang

entry.summary: BindCLIP addresses compositional caption scoring by showing a frozen CLIP encoder retains word-region association structure that can be read out rather than rebuilt. It introduces a balanced token-patch-depth optimal-transport coupling placing candidate captions and multiple visual depths in a single plan, from which semantic, entity, order, and spatial evidence are read as energies.

entry.title: A$^2$Safe: Counterfactual Evidence-Aligned Adaptive Agent Collaboration for Safe and Effective Visual Question Answering

author.name: Quanxing Xu, Ling Zhou, Xian Zhong, Jinyu Tian, Xiaohua Huang, Rubing Huang, Chia-Wen Lin

entry.summary: A2Safe is an agent-collaboration framework for safe VQA with MLLMs that grounds safety decisions in multimodal evidence, using counterfactual analysis to detect risks arising from interactions between individually benign image and question content. It organizes localized visual observations, textual intent, and cross-modal risk relations to decide when to refuse or answer. The work improves on superficial correlation-based safety alignment.

entry.title: SAFe: Segment-guided Aggregation of Feature Densities for Anomaly-aware Segmentation

author.name: Anja Deli\'c, Jurica Runtas, Marin Or\v{s}i\'c, Ivan Markovi\'c, Ivan Petrovi\'c

entry.summary: SAFe is a generative anomaly-aware segmentation method using class-conditional density estimation over self-supervised foundation model features, training lightweight normalizing flows that produce class-conditional normalized likelihoods with segment-guided aggregation. It improves feature semantics and spatial consistency over prior density-based approaches. The work targets reliable scene parsing for deployed autonomous systems encountering out-of-distribution objects.

entry.title: VPRune: Efficient Training-free Pre-LLM Visual Token Pruning

author.name: Guangchuan Lv, Dianxing Shi, Dingjie FU

entry.summary: VPRune is a training-free framework for pruning visual tokens before the LLM stage of large vision-language models, identifying three degradation sources: text-guided selection bias, information loss, and positional distortion from sequence compaction.
