It combines visual-only diversity selection, similarity-guided token recycling, and position-preserving restoration, showing favorable accuracy-compression trade-offs on FastVLM-1.5B.

entry.title: Unsupervised Brain Anomaly Detection as a Bayesian Inverse Problem with Diffusion Prior

author.name: Hugues Roy, Reuben Dorent, Ninon Burgos

entry.summary: Reformulates unsupervised brain anomaly detection as a Bayesian inverse problem under a diffusion prior, introducing a latent spatial anomaly mask modeling pixel-wise consistency between a test image and its pseudo-healthy counterpart. Provides a principled alternative to heuristic noise schedules and synthetic corruptions used in diffusion-based UAD.

entry.title: ORDER: A Fictitious-World Benchmark for Domain-Adaptive Embodied AI

author.name: Sai Krishna Reddy Sathi, Anuj Tiwari

entry.summary: Introduces ORDER, a benchmark built on a 342,069-token synthetic corpus defining a fictitious world with proprietary, safety-critical rules, designed to cleanly measure genuine domain adaptation in knowledge-intensive, task-light robot deployments (e.g., pharmaceutical dispensing, hazmat handling) where live testing is costly or unsafe.

entry.title: Becoming a Fruit Ninja: Real-Time Probabilistic Kinodynamic Planning for Manipulator Projectile Interception

author.name: Lucas Chen, Austin Garrett, Andrew Niu, Zachary Kingston

entry.summary: Presents FRUITNINJA, an anytime sampling-based planner for intercepting and slicing thrown objects, growing a tree in parallel on the GPU toward the interception manifold. Each edge is an exact cubic satisfying actuator limits, with travel times found via parallel dynamics search and plans ranked by risk-aware criteria.

entry.title: AquaWorld: Structure-Consistent Underwater World Generation for Robot Simulation

author.name: Bin Peng, Tiandong Zhang, Ruidong Wang, Min Luo, Shuo Wang

entry.summary: Presents AquaWorld, a world-generation framework for underwater robot simulation that keeps terrain, asset placement, task definitions, and current fields mutually consistent through shared terrain structure. It uses language-conditioned planning, over 10,000 underwater-compatible assets, and a CFD-supervised residual model for reusable terrain-conditioned mean-flow fields, supporting conventional vehicles and bio-inspired robotic fish.

entry.title: Commonsense-Grounded Path Planning from Abstract Instructions

author.name: Masafumi Endo, Kohei Honda, Ryo Yonetani

entry.summary: The paper introduces commonsense ranked search (CoRS), a path planner that uses LLMs and VLMs as commonsense knowledge to honor unstated considerations in abstract instructions, e.g. detouring around a wet floor when told to move carefully. It derives region-specific considerations from visual observations and compiles them into planning constraints.

entry.title: Transferring the Intelligence of VLMs to Robotic Control

author.name: Meng-Hao Guo, Zhe-Han Mo, Jia-Jun Wang, Yi Zhang, Kejin Wang, Yi-Xuan Deng, Jia-Peng Zhang, Yongming Rao, Shi-Min Hu

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether VLM intelligence can transfer from the digital to the physical world for robot control via RoboDawn, an interface exposing closed-loop robotic control to an agentic VLM through a compact set of discrete translation, rotation, and gripper commands. The VLM observes the visual state, reasons about the next action, executes it, and adapts based on outcomes.

entry.title: Splat-CBF: Safe Next-Best-View Control in 3D Gaussian-Splat Maps

author.name: Amirhossein Mollaei Khass, Athanasios Cosse, Nader Motee

entry.summary: Splat-CBF resolves the tension between active perception and collision safety in unmapped environments using an active-perception control barrier function over 3D Gaussian-splat maps. A risk-aware CBF turns Average Value-at-Risk of the Gaussian field into a smooth hard constraint, while a second barrier rewards camera orientations with high expected Fisher information for next-best-view selection.

entry.title: AquaCap: A Training-Free Underwater Embodied Agent with Code-as-Policy

author.name: Xiaoshi Li, Yule Xu, Chunghiu Kong, Yizhou Zhou, Yang Liu, Hao Yang, Zihao Huang, Yunxiao Shan

entry.summary: Presents AquaCap, a training-free Code-as-Policy framework for underwater navigation and manipulation that uses a dual-layer agent to translate instructions and observations into condition-aware plans and executable control programs, with reliability-aware perception under degraded underwater conditions and failure-aware memory for diagnosis. It sidesteps the need for costly underwater interaction data that limits VLA models. This is valuable because underwater data scarcity is a major barrier to embodied AI in marine settings.

entry.title: Shared Execution-Clock Drifting Policy for Dynamic Precision Manipulation

author.name: Zhenchen Dong, Qingran Wu, Jinna Fu, Jiaming Wu, Fulin Chen, Hongyu Yu, Yide Liu

entry.summary: Proposes SECD, which makes execution rhythm an explicit part of one-step action generation by jointly predicting a progress-indexed action curve and a shared monotone clock mapping control times to curve locations, anchored by demonstration-derived alignment. This addresses the implicit temporal allocation in directly predicted action sequences for time-constrained tasks like intercepting moving objects. It is a novel angle on temporal structure in robot policies.

entry.title: Receding-Horizon Pushing with Composable Object-Centric Policies

author.name: Zhiyi Yuan, Tianrun Hu, Anxing Xiao, Yuhong Deng, David Hsu, Hanbo Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes an object-centric pushing policy within a feedback-guided hierarchical framework: a learned policy predicts contact actions from pose- and scale-normalized point clouds, a quasi-static sliding-versus-tipping stability score filters contacts, and BIT* search handles long-horizon planning. This decomposes the coupled problems of where to push, push stability, and downstream feasibility for non-prehensile manipulation of arbitrary 3D objects. Non-prehensile manipulation of heavy or ungraspable objects has broad practical relevance.

entry.title: FeasibleFlow: One-Step Joint Transport of Configuration Feasibility and Trajectories for End-to-End Driving

author.name: Xiang Li, Bikun Wang, Qing Xu, Jianjun Wang

entry.summary: Proposes FeasibleFlow, a one-step end-to-end generative driving framework that jointly transports a configuration-space feasibility field and multimodal ego trajectories using an Asymmetric Joint MeanFlow with pathwise Jacobian-vector products, so safety feedback directly shapes trajectory generation rather than only auxiliary supervision. It addresses temporal mismatch between observation-time trajectories and evolving scenes. Flow-based planning with explicit feasibility fields is a technically interesting direction for autonomous driving.

entry.title: WOLF: World Model Guided LiDAR Exploration with Predictive Frontiers

author.name: Yuyang Tian, Penghui Yang, Pengyuan Wu, Haoran Yang, Chenhui Li, Pengfei Han, Dong Wang, Zhigang Wang, Bin Zhao, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: WOLF uses a recurrent world model trained on exploration trajectories to predict future LiDAR observations behind occlusions, guiding UAV frontier selection beyond the measured map. The model combines observation history with candidate motions to predict local outcomes, giving exploration foresight. Extends world-model ideas from control into the mapping/exploration domain.

entry.title: Object-Centered Reconstruction for Vision-Based 3D Force Estimation

author.name: Zhonghao Zhang, Mingyeung Wu, Hao Yang, Ayberk Acar, Alan Kuntz, Jie Ying Wu

entry.summary: Presents a vision-based pipeline estimating 3D interaction forces from soft-tissue deformation in stereo endoscopic video, using object-centered dynamic point-cloud reconstruction, constrained tissue tracking, and a neural force predictor. Evaluated progressively on phantoms, ex vivo porcine colons, and in vivo colorectal surgery video. Enables force sensing on surgical robots lacking the da Vinci 5's integrated sensing.

entry.title: RoboTalk: Learning Multi-Robot Communication and Coordination from Multimodal Demonstrations

author.name: Dorian Benhamou Goldfajn, Mason Nakamura, Saaduddin Mahmud, Justin Svegliato, Kyle H. Wray, Shlomo Zilberstein

entry.summary: RoboTalk provides a synthetic data-generation pipeline and a dataset of 7,950 multimodal trajectories across 53 mobile-manipulation kitchen tasks, training small on-device VLMs to jointly learn inter-robot communication and skill-level action selection from demonstrations. Targets decentralized multi-robot manipulation under partial observability via natural-language communication. From Shlomo Zilberstein's group (UMass).

entry.title: ActiveArena: Benchmarking and Understanding Active Perception in Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yibo Li, Enshen Zhou, Rui Chen, Yanjun Ding, Mengzhen Liu, Yi Han, Jiabo Zhan, Lipeng Wang, Shanghang Zhang, Lu Sheng

entry.summary: ActiveArena introduces an active-perception simulator with controllable viewpoints and large workspaces, plus a benchmark of 35 tasks across 5 categories requiring multi-round evidence acquisition and memory-based reasoning rather than passive observation. It provides rich memory annotations and standardized training data. This fills a gap because existing manipulation benchmarks rarely evaluate how robots actively acquire and maintain information.

entry.title: Feasibility Distance Fields for Heterogeneous Constraints in Robot Configuration Space

author.name: Xijing Cui, Huayan Pu, Jun Luo, Gang Wang

entry.summary: The paper defines feasibility distance fields (FDF): under a fixed positive-definite joint-space metric, the distance to the union of infeasible configuration sets, providing a common comparable measure across heterogeneous constraint types with incompatible units and gradient scales. It derives 1-Lipschitz continuity and a.e. differentiability properties from distance-to-set theory, provides admissibility analysis for collision, joint limit, and other practical constraints, and derives admissible formulations.

entry.title: Learning to Drive on Mars: Visual Multimodal Traversability Estimation for Off-World Navigation

author.name: Darren Chiu, Cole Wilson, Andrei Tumbar, Gaurav S. Sukhatme, Steven Myint

entry.summary: Releases a large-scale dataset from the Mars 2020 Perseverance rover spanning 500 sols and 45km of trajectories, including stereo imagery, poses, accelerometer readings, rocker-bogie angles, and tilt/slip estimates, to enable learning-based traversability estimation. Builds on it a multimodal traversability estimation model for off-world autonomous navigation.

entry.title: Efficient Benchmarking in Production: A Study of an Evolving LLM Agent

author.name: Yining She, Lei Lin

entry.summary: The paper studies how to efficiently re-evaluate a production analytics agent (tens of thousands of monthly users) as it evolves, comparing random sampling, caching, fixed subsets, and IRT-based adaptive testing over 574 historical runs. Multidimensional 2PL adaptive testing gave the best score fidelity at 38.5% of full cost, though the authors deployed difficulty-stratified fixed subsets for practical reasons. It offers rare first-hand production deployment experience with agent evaluation.

entry.title: FOCAL-VLA: Subtask-Guided Geometry Distillation and Implicit World Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Zhiyuan Gao, Di Wen, Yanxiang Zhan, Mohammad Khoshnazar, Jeroen Sch\"afer, Kunyu Peng, Michael Beetz

entry.summary: FOCAL-VLA improves vision-language-action models for precise long-horizon manipulation by combining subtask-guided geometry distillation with implicit world modeling, focusing supervision on geometry and dynamics relevant to the current interaction rather than redundant whole-scene prediction. It targets limitations of direct 2D-observation-to-action VLA pipelines.

entry.title: GameLogicBench: Evaluating Coding Agents on Runtime Game Logic with Tick-Level State Assertions

author.name: Xinyu Che, Yunfei Ge, Shihao Li, Yanchen Liu, Hang Yan, Xinping Lei, Yanghai Wang, Zixuan Dong, Yifan Yao, Qianqian Xie, Letian Zhu, Jiaheng Liu

entry.summary: GameLogicBench is a benchmark of 72 gameplay-logic tasks in Godot projects, evaluated by an automated checker that verifies game rules at every simulation tick across 403 hand-designed scenarios and 1,451 seeded test cases. Unlike benchmarks that replay examples or use model judges, it ensures exactly reproducible verdicts about runtime rule compliance. This gives a rigorous way to assess whether coding agents implement game logic correctly, not just plausibly.

entry.title: Matrix AdaGrad: Row-wise and Column-wise Adaptive Subgradient Methods

author.name: Wenpeng Zhang, Runsheng Yu, Peilin Zhao

entry.summary: This paper develops a general Online Mirror Descent framework with adaptive proximal functions for matrix-valued parameters, deriving row-wise and column-wise matrix-aware adaptivity as a principled generalization of AdaGrad. It provides regret-minimization theory for structured adaptive optimization beyond vector-parameter methods.

entry.title: StepKV: Step-Aware KV Cache Compression for LLM Agents

author.name: Boyu Feng, Jiahong Liu, Yifan Li, Wenhao Yu, Zexuan Qiu, Yuliang Sun, Ming Shen, Xiang Li, Quanyu Dai, Irwin King

entry.summary: StepKV addresses KV-cache compression for multi-step LLM agents by arguing that token-level recency or attention-saliency pruning mismatches the unit of reasoning in agentic workflows, where queries expand into trajectories of reasoning, tool calls, and observations. It compresses at the granularity of reasoning steps, preserving the information structure agents need across trajectory stages.

entry.title: CleanScore: Black-Box Benchmark Audits with Negative Controls and Sensitivity Bounds

author.name: Jeffery Opoku, David Banahene

entry.summary: CleanScore is a black-box audit method for detecting benchmark contamination using only scored outputs: each question is paired with independently written fresh forms preserving numbers, facts, and answer, plus a private negative-control bank that separates memorization exposure from ordinary form mismatch. It reports intervals rather than verdicts and includes registered audits of five open models on GSM8K and ARC-Challenge items.

entry.title: Connected Content Retriever: Dense Graph Edge Features Powering Pre-Ranking at LinkedIn

author.name: Akhilesh Gupta, Sudarshan Srinivasa Ramanujam, Chirag Bhanuprasad Mehta, Reshma Asharaf Beena, Dhritiman Das, Birjodh Singh Tiwana, Bhargavkumar Kanubhai Patel, Mack Lee, Renyi Tang

entry.summary: LinkedIn describes its Connected Content Retriever, a pre-ranking system that uses dense graph edge features from the professional knowledge graph to select the best few hundred candidates from an index exceeding one billion activities, leveraging both first-degree network signals and stranger-viral second-degree engagement. It powers selection of the network-generated content that accounts for over 70 percent of Feed impressions.

entry.title: Improved Private Sparse Covariance Estimation with Multiscale Threshold Tests

author.name: Zihan Zhang

entry.summary: Develops a differentially private sparse covariance estimation algorithm in operator norm using multiscale random thresholds, improving the privacy-dependent sample complexity term by a factor of sqrt(k) over prior work and matching known lower bounds in the applicable regime.

entry.title: Ask for Any Appliance: A Prompt-Programmable Foundation Model for Non-Intrusive Load Monitoring

author.name: Xudong Wang, Jiacheng Cui, Junyu Xue, Tongxin Li, Guoming Tang

entry.summary: Presents FM4NILM, a single prompt-programmable foundation model that estimates any requested appliance's power trajectory from aggregate meter readings, a natural-language description, and optional exemplars, replacing per-appliance models. It is pretrained via masked reconstruction on 645k sequences from seven public corpora at varied sampling rates.

entry.title: VISTA: An Attention-Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Architecture for Space Situational Awareness Sensor Tasking

author.name: Miguel Leiva-V\'elez, Adalberto Claudio Quiros, Nicolas Gaston Rozado, Hodei Urrutxua, V\'ictor Rodr\'iguez-Fern\'andez

entry.summary: VISTA is a scalable deep multi-agent RL architecture for tasking heterogeneous, distributed space-surveillance sensors to maintain uncertainty over large, dynamic catalogues of space objects. Unlike prior deep RL approaches with fixed-dimensional state and action spaces, it handles variable object populations and sensor configurations via attention. This is relevant as the population of resident space objects grows and classical optimization becomes intractable.

entry.title: Lifted Bellman Linear Programming for Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Hyukjun Yang, Jongchan Park, Narim Jeong, Donghwan Lee

entry.summary: LBLP replaces regression-based critic training in offline RL with in-sample Bellman optimality enforced via inequality constraints, lifting the linear programming characterization of Bellman optimality to joint (Q,V) space so constraints only involve dataset state-action pairs. The unique minimizer is the in-sample optimal pair, avoiding off-policy correction and EMA target networks.

entry.title: Learning Prognostic Variables for AI Convective Parameterizations via Symbolic Distillation

author.name: Jurij Sch\"onfeld, Tom Beucler, Julien Savre, Steven Sherwood, Veronika Eyring

entry.summary: For hybrid AI-physics climate models, this work moves beyond local-in-time diagnostic convection parameterizations by learning prognostic variables that carry memory of past states. Past information is compressed into a low-dimensional autoencoder latent space and distilled into symbolic form for tractable use in coarse Earth-system models.

entry.title: Schematize: An Agentic System for Generating and Refining Information-Extraction Schemas for Legal Research

author.name: Albert Sawczyn, Jakub Binkowski, Kamil Tagowski, {\L}ukasz Augustyniak, Berenika Kaczmarek-Templin, Tomasz Kajdanowicz

entry.summary: Presents an open-source multi-agent system that converts a legal researcher's problem statement into a validated information-extraction schema through clarification dialogue, iterative generation, data-grounded refinement, and chat-based post-editing. It targets the manual, expertise-heavy bottleneck in empirical legal research. Human evaluation with legal professionals demonstrates practical utility.

entry.title: Scalable Incremental Robustness Analysis of Neural Network Feedback Systems

author.name: Zichen Wang, Peter Seiler, Geir Dullerud, Bin Hu

entry.summary: This work develops a unified framework for robust stability and performance analysis of feedback loops containing high-dimensional neural networks, combining structured decomposition of full-order SDP conditions with scalable Lipschitz estimation. The resulting reduced verification conditions certify incremental convergence and incremental l2-gain bounds, with LMI dimensions reduced relative to neuron-count scaling. It bridges the gap between conservative but scalable small-gain tests and exact but intractable SDP certificates.

entry.title: Event Signature Transfer: Model-Agnostic Forecast Scenario Construction from Historical Events

author.name: Karthik Sridhar, Aaditya Jain, Murari Mandal, Saurabh Deshpande

entry.summary: Introduces EST, a training-free, model-agnostic operator that transforms a completed past event into an explicit forecast scenario by removing the source event's trend and seasonality, then scaling and retiming its signature onto a native forecast. Tested on Chronos-2, TimesFM-2.5, and Toto-2.0 across twelve real episodes and ten synthetic scenarios, it reduces forecast error relative to baselines.

entry.title: Distill What You Trust: Reliability-Aware Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Jie Sun, Mao Zheng, Mingyang Song, Zeyuan Liu, Gengsheng Li, Houcheng Jiang, Yilin Cheng, Bichuan Feng, Yuchen Cai, Junfeng Fang, Xiang Wang

entry.summary: Proposes TrustMOPD, which replaces example-level teacher selection in multi-teacher on-policy distillation with label-free, token-level supervision allocation. It uses each specialist's RL-induced displacement from a shared pre-RL reference as a proxy for local reliability, calibrates scores across teachers, and builds weighted distributions at each student-generated prefix.

entry.title: Is Imagination Derived from Hallucination? A Cross-Taxonomy Evaluation of Imagination and Hallucination in Large Language Models

author.name: Zixuan Tang, Hongzong Li, Shuxin Zhuang, Dapeng Wu, Zi Liang

entry.summary: The paper introduces Whiteboard, a benchmark that evaluates LLM imagination while checking whether departures from common answers are licensed by the prompt, and jointly evaluates hallucination in the same pipeline for the first time. This makes the influential claim that imagination and hallucination share a generative mechanism directly testable via a cross-taxonomy design.

entry.title: Euston: Training Away Mathematical Sycophancy Without Losing the Mathematics

author.name: Zehua Cheng, Wei Dai, Jiahao Sun

entry.summary: Presents Euston, an 8B mathematical claim-verification model trained to refuse corrupted theorems rather than confidently proving them. Using GraphSynth, a factor-graph generator producing 3,026 matched true/corrupted statement pairs from arXiv papers, the authors fine-tune DeepSeek-R1-8B with GRPO under rule-based zero-API rewards, targeting sycophancy while preserving mathematical capability.

entry.title: When Residualization Helps an Audit: Format Effects, Slice Gains, and Their Limits

author.name: Daein Weon, Dongho Kang

entry.summary: This paper examines whether subtracting predictable surface components from LLM evaluation scores (for reward models, rerankers, and LLM judges) improves measurement validity. It shows that a public preference reward model barely beats chance (0.507) when choosing a terse correct solution over a commented buggy one, and demonstrates that residualization alone cannot distinguish construct-irrelevant format bias from construct-relevant signal. Using designed interventions with unit-test labels and comment-only edits, the authors characterize when residualization attenuates format effects and where it helps or fails.

entry.title: Retrieval Geometry Shapes Cache-Based Clip Adaptation

author.name: Mahir Shahriar Tamim, Md. Samiul Alim, Azmine Toushik Wasi, Shahriyar Zaman Ridoy, Meharun Nesa, Mohammad Abu Yousuf, Alex Lamb, Mohammad Ali Moni

entry.summary: This study shows that cache-based test-time adaptation of CLIP depends heavily on the retrieval geometry: with the memory fixed and only the retrieval encoder changed, ImageNet-A cache gains range from +0.44 to +19.7 points across sixteen retrieval spaces, and label-free retrieval-space selection retains 98% of oracle gain on ImageNet-V2. The finding that memory quality hinges on retrieval space, not just which examples enter it, offers practical guidance for training-free CLIP adaptation.

entry.title: Colon3R: Cross-Domain 3D Reconstruction from Monocular Colonoscopic Video

author.name: Zhihao Xing, Yingyu Wang, Liang Zhao, Shoudong Huang

entry.summary: Colon3R is a cross-domain semi-supervised framework built on the pretrained VGGT geometry foundation model that transfers coupled camera, depth, and pointmap geometry from labeled phantom and simulated data to unlabeled in-vivo colonoscopy. It tackles weak texture, specular reflections, limited overlap, and non-rigid tissue motion that break conventional multi-view reconstruction.

entry.title: GameHorizon Suite: Multi-Horizon Data and Evaluation in Gameplay

author.name: Yiran Wang, Xingyilang Yin, Junfu Pu, Guangzhi Wang, Kaifeng Li, Mingyu Ouyang, Huiqiang Sun, Lingen Li, Cheng Cheng, Wangbo Yu, Honghao Chen, Xiaodong Cun, Chi-Man Pun, Zhiguo Cao, Ying Shan

entry.summary: GameHorizon is a unified data and evaluation suite measuring gameplay capabilities across multiple temporal horizons, comprising an automated annotation pipeline, a dataset of multi-horizon game instructions, and evaluations spanning visual understanding, instruction decomposition, planning, and action control across diverse model families.

entry.title: What do VLM-Based Vision-Language Navigation Models Rely on: Interpreting and Steering Policy Behavior

author.name: D\'ebora Oliveira Makowski, Samiran Gode, Abhijeet Nayak, Marco Hutter, Cordelia Schmid, Lukas Rosenberger Schmid, Wolfram Burgard

entry.summary: Studies interpretability and steerability of VLM-based Vision-Language Navigation models using intervention-based metrics that causally measure how visual observations, instructions, and visual memory influence navigation decisions. Reveals whether these policies ground predictions in relevant semantic cues or can track task progress.

entry.title: H-VLA: Hierarchical Vision-Language-Action Model with Key-Action Reasoning and Motion Planning in a Unified Action Space

author.name: Xiongfeng Peng, Lu Xu, Yandong Wang, Jiaqian Yu, Zirui Zheng, Yamin Mao, Weiming Li, Inseop Chung, Hyun-woong Cho, Jaewook Yoo, Dongwook Lee, Daehyun Ji, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: H-VLA is a hierarchical VLA framework that decouples high-level key-action reasoning from low-level motion generation, combining a Key-Action Model with motion planning in a unified action space. This preserves the semantic reasoning of pretrained VLMs and improves robustness to spatial variations in object positions, layouts, embodiments, and viewpoints.

entry.title: DiagGen: Agentic Generation of Deformable Assets with Sim-based Diagnostics for Robotic Simulation

author.name: Guanxiong Chen, Yiduo Qu, Qianjun Xia, Pengyu Jing, Yixian Cheng, Bole Ma, Pengzhi Yang, Bingyang Zhou, Ziming Li, Shashwat Suri, Gongbo Sun, Chao Liu, Peter Yichen Chen, Ziqiu Zeng, Fan Shi

entry.summary: DiagGen is an agentic framework that converts a single in-the-wild image into a simulation-ready deformable asset through a generate-simulate-diagnose-refine loop, using a VLM-based agent to probe material responses in a physics simulator and route evidence-backed repair cues to the responsible generation stage. Existing frameworks typically check plausibility only after generation, without using simulation feedback for repair.

entry.title: Scenario MPC with STL Specifications and Pareto-Based Feasibility Repair

author.name: Tianhao Wu, Yiwei Lyu

entry.summary: Proposes a scenario-based model predictive control framework that enforces signal temporal logic specifications in multi-agent settings with stochastic, uncontrollable agents, adding a Pareto-based feasibility repair mechanism for infeasible constraint sets. It addresses limitations of prior robust STL control, which either certifies strict satisfaction without recovering feasibility or relaxes constraints ego-centrically. Relevant to autonomous driving and other stochastic multi-agent domains.

entry.title: UniPoint: Unified Point-Level Sensor Fusion for Humanoid Locomotion Across Challenging Terrains

author.name: Sicen Li, Zhen Chu, Chao Li, Qiuguo Zhu, Jun Wu

entry.summary: UniPoint early-fuses 360-degree LiDAR and two depth cameras into a single base-frame point set with voxelization for humanoid whole-body locomotion over heterogeneous terrain. Aims to jointly achieve wide coverage, local accuracy, and sensor redundancy that existing depth-only or elevation-map approaches lack. Targets open-world deployment robustness.

entry.title: Topology-Informed Visual Prompting For Vision Language Action Policies

author.name: Haoyang Wu, Abhinav Kumar, Dmitry Berenson

entry.summary: Introduces a topology-guided visual-prompting framework for VLA policies, using topological signatures to disambiguate similar observations requiring different actions in complex obstacle geometries. Simulation-based planning augments demonstration data, and a Gaussian-splatting-based visual prompt provides guidance at deployment. Bridges motion-planning reasoning and learned policies.

entry.title: MimicAgent: Quadruped Skills via Prompt-to-Trajectory Generation

author.name: Lucky Kant Nayak, Narayanan Palghat Parameswaran, Neehar Peri, Deva Ramanan

entry.summary: MimicAgent learns dynamic quadruped skills by generating reference trajectories from prompts rather than shaping reward functions, observing that it is much easier for humans and LLMs to produce reference motions than rewards, and that LLM-based reward design (Eureka) generalizes poorly across skills and morphologies. It builds on the success of example-guided RL for humanoids and applies it to quadrupeds. This reframes skill specification from reward design to motion demonstration generation.

entry.title: Decoupling Internal Representational Changes and Causal Importance in Fine-Tuned Large Language Models

author.name: Lingfang Li, Procheta Sen, Shubham Das, Danushka Bollegala

entry.summary: The authors study how fine-tuning reshapes attention patterns and layer-wise activations in LLMs, and whether these changes correspond to task-relevant components identified by EAP. They find EAP-identified components are functionally localized in specific layers, with distributions largely unchanged. This contributes mechanistic understanding of what fine-tuning actually modifies inside models.

entry.title: Visual Navigation Transformer with Pose Attention

author.name: Beiming Li, Jaime Romero, Jonathan Diller, Vijay Kumar, Alejandro Ribeiro

entry.summary: VNT-PA is a transformer navigation planner whose context is a set of depth keyframes indexed by camera pose, using pose differences as attentional positional encoding instead of temporal order. Trained to imitate a shortest-path planner, it lets policies reuse experience from earlier traversals without constructing explicit maps or topological graphs.

entry.title: Co-Evolving Zero-Day Jamming: Adaptive Attack Synthesis and Graph Attention-Based Online Detection

author.name: Ghilas Aissou, R\'emi A. Chou, Taejoon Kim

entry.summary: The paper proposes a two-pronged wireless security framework: adaptive synthesis of zero-day jamming attacks (avoiding unrealistic assumptions of prior receiver knowledge) and an online detector combining graph attention networks for temporal-spectral representation with Dirichlet process clustering that both classifies known strategies and discovers zero-day ones. This co-evolving attack-detection setup provides more rigorous benchmarks for jamming defense.

entry.title: Steering LLMs Responses Towards Moral Foundations on the Norwegian MFQ-30

author.name: Hans Andersen, David Dichas

entry.summary: This study administers the Norwegian Moral Foundations Questionnaire to six open-weight LLMs and compares their profiles to 1,282 Norwegian respondents, testing prompt-level persona steering and activation-level ActAdd interventions. Notably, half the models fail attention checks or produce flat, central-tendency outputs that look near-human on average without tracking item content. The paper questions whether psychometric instruments measure anything stable in LLMs at all.

entry.title: When Should a Failing Robot Ask? Initiating Corrective Human-Robot Dialogue from Audited Sensor Evidence

author.name: Eshika Pathak, Leela Krishna

entry.summary: This work builds a simulation benchmark with injected, known failure causes to measure what robot sensors reveal about failures, finding force data highly diagnostic (0.99) while image methods stay below 0.55. Testing six open VLMs, it shows their dialogue-initiation decisions track the surface of the prompt rather than the audited sensor evidence.

entry.title: Weak Ties, Strong Signals: Efficient Training Data Detection in Diffusion LLMs via Independent Token Sampling

author.name: Hongyao Yu, Tianqu Zhuang, Ziyuan Xu, Hao Fang, Jiaxin Hong, Bin Chen, Shu-Tao Xia

entry.summary: This paper tackles training-data (memorization) detection in diffusion LLMs, which lack the one-pass probability decomposition of causal models. It theoretically shows that random-masking approximations incur a non-negative structural error characterized by cumulative conditional mutual information among masked tokens, and proposes independent token sampling to expose subtle memorization signals efficiently under query budgets.

entry.title: Improving Parameter Utilization by Sharing Neural Experts Across Layers in Transformers

author.name: Dian Jiao, Jiaxin Duan, Shuai Zhao, Jiabing Leng, Yiran Zhang, Feng Huang

entry.summary: CS-MoE is a Transformer architecture featuring cross-layer expert sharing: it combines layer-independent experts with concurrent access to a centralized, globally shared expert pool, enabling elastic control over token-level parameter activation and FLOPs. Experiments show lower perplexity than layer-isolated MoE baselines, addressing inter-layer parameter redundancy in LLMs.

entry.title: Not All Ranks Are Equal: Budget-Aware LoRA Merging Across Tasks

author.name: Avinash Amballa, Yashas Malur Saidutta, Wenbo Li, Lazar Valkov, Srinivas Chappidi

entry.summary: The paper shows that assuming uniform rank budgets across layers and tasks is a major source of the performance gap between merged and per-task LoRA adapters at inference time. It introduces Net Utility, a data-free SVD-based metric scoring singular directions by task utility and cross-task interference, enabling globally pooled budget allocation for merging (an otherwise NP-hard rank selection problem).

entry.title: Personalized Federated Reinforcement Learning via Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning: Convergence of Exact and Hessian-Free Meta-Policy Gradients

author.name: Ali Beikmohammadi, Sarit Khirirat, Sindri Magn\'usson

entry.summary: Proposes Per-FedAvg-PG for personalized federated RL, where n agents in distinct MDPs learn a shared MAML-style initialization adapted by a single local policy-gradient step. Provides convergence guarantees to epsilon-stationary points in O(eps^{-3/2}) rounds with Hessian-free meta-policy gradients, exploiting structural features of the RL setting.

entry.title: On attention heads and bilinear forms

author.name: Andrew O'Desky

entry.summary: A mathematical study of the symmetric and antisymmetric parts of bilinear forms in trained attention heads, introducing an orthogonally invariant profile map to a 3D simplex. Proves that trained profiles accumulate near rank-one forms and characterizes symmetric parts as hyperbolic-plus-zero forms for a Zariski-dense set of query-key matrices.

entry.title: A discrete generative model of neuronal spiking activity on microelectrode arrays

author.name: Md Sayed Tanveer, Mohammed A. Mostajo-Radji, Ge Wang

entry.summary: The authors introduce a discrete generative model for sparse, array-wide binary spike volumes from high-density microelectrode arrays, using a shared vocabulary of spatiotemporal motifs learned by a residual vector-quantized autoencoder and a factorized masked transformer that predicts activity location and timing. Unlike prior work assuming a fixed sorted-neuron set, it handles the varying electrode subsets across assays. Such models could support disease studies, drug-response analysis, and closed-loop experimentation.

entry.title: KV-COBRA: KV Cache Compression via Co-Optimized Bit-Rank Allocation

author.name: Sihyeon Ha, Jaeho Lee, Yo-Seb Jeon

entry.summary: KV-COBRA argues that the key limit on extreme-rate KV cache compression is budget allocation rather than the compression scheme itself, showing that co-optimizing low-rank truncation and bit-width per attention head dominates uniform allocation, with the largest gains at low bit-rates. It formalizes this as a resource-allocation problem that redistributes budget across heads to minimize total distortion.

entry.title: iSDFT: Information-Proximal Self-Distillation for Continual Learning in LLMs

author.name: Ahmed Khaled Khamis, Xiaotong Ji, Hassan Jaber, Rasul Tutunov, Matthieu Zimmer, Jun Wang, Haitham Bou-Ammar

entry.summary: iSDFT treats the demonstration-conditioned teacher in self-distillation fine-tuning as a budgeted information source, selecting at each token the distribution closest to the student satisfying a prescribed teacher-information constraint via a closed-form exponential target. Anchoring the student to its frozen pre-trained state controls cumulative drift, reducing forgetting in continual learning.

entry.title: One to More, More to One: Category-Aware Iterative Expert Training for Software Engineering Agents

author.name: Jie Zhao, Ziyu Jiang, Suhang Zheng, Minghui Shan, Xiaoxiao Xu, Lin Qu

entry.summary: Addresses uneven progress across task categories in pooled agentic RL for repository-level software engineering, proposing a category-aware expert-training and policy-integration framework with executable task construction and an evidence-grounded multi-axis labeling system (SWE Labeler). Category-specific experts are iteratively trained and consolidated to avoid the category see-saw where gains in some areas mask regressions in others.

entry.title: MECAIL: Communication-Aware Incremental Learning for Object Detection with 14.6 KB Spatiotemporal Experts

author.name: Matthias Neuwirth-Trapp, Maarten Bieshaar, Danda Paudel, Konrad Schindler, Luc Van Gool, Christos Sakaridis

entry.summary: MECAIL addresses on-device incremental learning for intelligent transportation systems by shipping tiny, context-specialized detection modules, capped at 14.6 KB to fit within a single TCP window over V2X and cellular links. The system adapts a fixed base model to diverse spatiotemporal contexts such as parking lots and construction sites.

entry.title: Auditing Political Alignment in LLM Assistants: Engagement, Stance, and User Identity

author.name: Joan C. Timoneda

entry.summary: Argues that LLM political behavior should be understood as a speech regime, a set of policies over whether to engage, what stance to take, and how to respond conditional on topic and user identity. The author derives a five-regime typology from engagement and stance dimensions and tests six major AI systems (OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, Google, Mistral, DeepSeek) in a preregistered experiment.

entry.title: Evaluating Decision Models for Text Annotation in Computational Social Science

author.name: Hazem Ibrahim, Yasir Zaki

entry.summary: The paper evaluates a new class of decision models built for categorical question answering, which return typed choices with probability distributions and confidence scores at a fraction of frontier inference cost, against the Ziems et al. (2024) suite of 18 computational social science classification tasks (7,977 items). It tests whether these models' answers are accurate on social science constructs and whether their stated confidence is trustworthy. This is one of the first systematic validations of decision models for social science annotation.

entry.title: Hierarchical Aggregation of Semantic Uncertainty in 3D Scene Graphs

author.name: Carlos Cueto Zumaya, Iacopo Catalano, Wallace Moreira Bessa, Julio A. Placed

entry.summary: The paper presents a framework that converts detector confidence and stored vision-language embeddings in open-vocabulary 3D scene graphs into probabilities that entries are correct, then propagates them through the containment hierarchy into beliefs about whether a room contains a queried class. This gives deployed robots query-time uncertainty signals without repeated sampling, training, or held-out labels.

entry.title: Towards robust multimodal 3D object detection via visual foundation models

author.name: Ziying Song, Lin Liu, Hongyu Pan, Shaoqing Xu, Lei Yang, Mingzhe Guo, Caiyan Jia

entry.summary: RoboDistill improves robustness of LiDAR-camera 3D object detection under out-of-distribution corruptions (noise, weather, environment changes) by distilling from visual foundation models. It introduces SAM-AD, a domain-specific SAM fine-tuning strategy on driving imagery, and a distillation design transferring robust semantic features to the detection model. Well-motivated robustness work for autonomous driving.

entry.title: STAR: Scene- and Task-Aware 4D Radar Preprocessing Towards End-to-End Cognitive Radar

author.name: Seung-Hyun Song, Dong-Hee Paek, Seung-Hyun Kong

entry.summary: STAR makes 4D radar preprocessing scene- and task-aware, replacing signal-level CFAR detection that can discard useful information with preprocessing guided directly by downstream perception objectives. The approach moves toward end-to-end cognitive radar pipelines for robust environmental perception in adverse weather and lighting. It connects a traditionally hand-tuned radar front-end to task learning.

entry.title: ChartJudgeBench: Evaluating LMM Judges for Chart-to-Code Generation

author.name: Lijian Wu, Henry Hengyuan Zhao, Zijian Zhang, Jiahao Tang, Jiajun Wu, Alex Jinpeng Wang

entry.summary: ChartJudgeBench is a diagnostic benchmark assessing whether large multimodal models can reliably judge chart-to-code generation, with 1,003 pairwise Chart Perception Alignment instances and 650 binary accept/reject Chart Reasoning Judgment instances. It probes LMM reliability as visual critics and reward models, a role increasingly central to RL training of chart systems. The benchmark addresses an underexplored judge-reliability question.

entry.title: Dissecting Agentic Forensics: The Role of Triage, Prompting, and Evidence Arbitration in Open-World Fake Image Detection

author.name: Xianlong Li (IMT School for Advanced Studies Lucca, Italy), Pietro Bongini (University of Siena, Italy), Niccol\'o Pancino (University of Siena, Italy), Marco Blanchini (IMT School for Advanced Studies Lucca, Italy), Benedetta Tondi (University of Siena, Italy), Mauro Barni (University of Siena, Italy)

entry.summary: This paper dissects a training-free agentic framework for open-world image forensics built on specialist detectors, per-detector triage, and conflict-aware evidence arbitration, asking which components actually drive performance and whether benefits survive distribution shift. It uses six configurations to isolate the contribution of each design choice.

entry.title: Relationally Grounded Latent World Models for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Fabian Schmidt, Markus Enzweiler, Abhinav Valada

entry.summary: The authors supervise latent world model representations for autonomous driving with actor-centric traffic scene graphs built from nuScenes annotations, encoded via a frozen text embedding model. The supervision branch is removed at inference, adding no test-time cost, and reduces average trajectory L2 error from 0.661 to 0.622 on nuScenes. It demonstrates that privileged relational semantics improve learned world representations.

entry.title: From Documented Strengths to Force Limits: Material-Informed Robotic Insertion for Construction Assembly

author.name: Lin He, Yanyi Chen, Haofei Sun, Lingyao Li, Min Deng

entry.summary: Introduces SAGE, a system that converts documented material evidence from construction documents into capacity estimates for robotic insertion. It constrains an LLM to extract tensile and compressive strengths from retrieved passages and tables while recording sources, and uses these to gate contact forces so insertion completes without exceeding assembly capacity.

entry.title: ARCGym: Benchmarking Deep Reinforcement Learning in Autonomous Robotic Colonoscopy

author.name: Guanglin Ji, Martina Finocchiaro, Kenny Erleben, Hang Yin

entry.summary: ARCGym is an open-source RL environment and benchmark for image-based navigation of flexible endoscopes, including magnetic-driven and proximally actuated colonoscopes, built on CT-reconstructed deformable colon anatomies. It fills a gap left by prior capsule-robot simulations that ignore contact-rich navigation of real clinical instruments.

entry.title: An Empirical Study and Open Testbed for Federated Fine-Tuning of Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Zhekai Duan, Kevin Ziyang Xie, Xinyu Tan, Shikai Geng, Chengxu Zhou, Ramana Kompella, Gaowen Liu, Chris Xiaoxuan Lu

entry.summary: This paper provides a systematic empirical study and open testbed for federated fine-tuning of three modern pretrained VLA policies across 40 LIBERO simulation tasks and six real-robot tasks, exploiting locally collected and otherwise discarded demonstrations. It addresses whether federated learning can adapt large pretrained VLAs and offers reproducible benchmarks and reusable training frameworks.

entry.title: Manipulation Feasible Navigation Among Movable Obstacles with Discrete Contact Pushing

author.name: Shaohu Wang, Aiguo Song, Yulong Yuan, Zhongyu Sun, Tianyuan Miao, Qinjie Ji

entry.summary: Presents a hierarchical navigation-among-movable-obstacles framework for mobile manipulators where a high-level planner identifies blocking obstacles and searches for relocations satisfying geometric, manipulation, and navigation constraints, invoking an LLM selectively to infer auxiliary manipulation dependencies that are then verified deterministically. This combines LLM commonsense with formal verification for cluttered environments. It matters because detour-only navigation is often infeasible with large movable obstacles.

entry.title: ReVeal: A Reconstruction-Aware Real-to-Sim Framework for VLA Policy Evaluation

author.name: Xinyi Wang, Heng Hao, Wenjun Hu, Anna Enyu Li, Dizhi Ma, Karthik Ramani, Hankyu Moon, Yeong-Dae Kwon

entry.summary: ReVeal is a real-to-sim assessment framework for VLA policy evaluation combining workspace reconstruction, reconstruction-fidelity metrics (Novel-View Mesh Fidelity, Annotated Planar Geometry Fidelity), and matched closed-loop policy evaluation. Includes PGSR-D, a reconstruction pipeline with monocular depth supervision. Addresses when simulated evaluation results can be trusted relative to real-world performance.

entry.title: Advancing AI for biology: Teaching models to design and characterize antibodies

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Amazon Bio Discovery summarizes three papers tackling core bottlenecks in computational antibody design: predicting binding sites on unfamiliar targets, ranking binding candidates, and predicting manufacturability and clinical viability, with emphasis on closing the out-of-distribution generalization gap that in-distribution benchmarks have obscured.

entry.title: Clinician-Grounded Quality Assurance for AI-Assisted Psychiatric Intake

author.name: King Shi, Amanda Li, Jonathan Ivey, Synthia Qia Wang, Guan Gui, Hyunseo Kim, Peter Zandi, Jason Straub, Jacob Taylor, Ananya Joshi

entry.summary: InterviewPlayground is a clinician-grounded evaluation platform for AI-assisted psychiatric intake built around a memory-augmented patient simulator supporting open-ended AI interviewing. It enables comparison across different clinician interviewing styles while minimizing clinician evaluation burden. This matters for safe, standardized deployment of clinical AI intake tools in health systems.

entry.title: LLM-Generated Feature Pools for Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Youssef Attia El Hili, Malik Tiomoko, Corinne Ancourt

entry.summary: The paper shows a simple statistical pipeline using a small pool of sliding-window statistics with transductive robust scoring and per-domain feature selection can beat neural leaderboard entries on TSB-AD-U, reaching 0.529 VUS-PR versus 0.45 for the best neural entry. Ablations attribute performance to the feature pool design, with LLM-generated features highlighted as part of the pool construction story.

entry.title: AutoViewMem: Self-Configuring Orthogonal Views for Conversational Long-Term Memory

author.name: Zijie Cao, Xijun Qu, Zhicheng Gu, Xiaoshu Chen, Duanyang Yuan, Yanning Hou, Sihang Zhou, Jianxing Gong, Jian Huang, Yang Mei

entry.summary: AutoViewMem organizes long-term conversational memory for LLM agents into self-configuring, low-overlap semantic views discovered from interaction traces before indexing, addressing semantic interference that makes top-K retrieval noisy in fixed-granularity memory schemas. The data-driven view selection targets heterogeneous information like preferences, events, constraints, and temporal updates.

entry.title: Geometry of Values: Task Vector Composition for Ethical Preference Alignment in Language Models

author.name: Utkarsh Agarwal, Monojit Choudhury

entry.summary: The paper introduces a 12,000-instance bilingual dataset of two-option moral dilemmas (Honesty vs Justice, Justice vs Autonomy, Autonomy vs Honesty) in five languages to probe ethical preferences in LLMs. It finds hidden value biases such as GPT-5-mini consistently favoring Honesty and Llama-3.2 models showing first-option bias, and explores task-vector composition for controllable ethical preference steering.

entry.title: VLA-Scope: Shift-Aware Failure Prediction for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Kaiwen Zhu, Dongfang Liu, Liangkai Liu

entry.summary: VLA-Scope is a two-stage framework for predicting execution failure of VLA policies under distribution shift: it first detects and categorizes OOD inputs from pooled image/language representations, then combines shift category, action-prefix features, and execution progress to predict failure during OOD rollouts. It notes OOD detection alone is insufficient since models can still succeed out of distribution.

entry.title: Knowledge-Graph-Augmented Chronos-2 for HEC-RAS Surrogate Forecasting

author.name: Edward Holmberg, Elias Ioup, Mahdi Abdelguerfi

entry.summary: KG-Chronos-2 couples a frozen Chronos-2 time-series foundation model with hydraulic project knowledge (graph-conditioned retrieval, exact-state residual decoding, input-aligned correction) to forecast water-surface elevations as surrogates for HEC-RAS hydrodynamic simulations. It outperforms persistence, residual LSTM, GeoFNO, DCRNN-style, and vanilla Chronos-2 baselines across 64 evaluation windows over 4,675 cross sections. This shows foundation models plus domain knowledge graphs can serve as effective physics-simulation surrogates.

entry.title: VidOmni-Bench: A Benchmark for Fine-Grained Video Understanding via Spatio-Temporal Event Verification across Complexity and Duration

author.name: Changbeen Kim, Junwon Chang, Kipyo Kim, Risa Shinoda, Kuniaki Saito, Donghyun Kim

entry.summary: VidOmni-Bench evaluates fine-grained video understanding by requiring models to verify whether each event in dense video captions is supported by the video, avoiding superficial QA cues and incomplete annotations. It spans 500 videos across five complexity types and durations from 4 seconds to 90 minutes, with human-verified sentence-level annotations generated by diverse Video-LLMs. This offers a stricter, claim-verification-style evaluation for Video-LLMs.

entry.title: TERMon: Detecting Persistent Behavioral Threats in Edge AI via Hardware-Native Ternary Runtime Monitor

author.name: Arish Sateesan, Edlira Dushku

entry.summary: TERMon is a lightweight hardware runtime monitor for edge AI accelerators that detects anomalies from corrupted models, distribution shift, and adversarial inputs by matching thermometer-encoded fingerprints against trusted ternary behavioral patterns. It observes inference behavior without re-execution or formal verification, targeting safety-critical deployments.

entry.title: Bayesian Belief Layer for Controllable Opinion Dynamics in LLM Agents

author.name: Hafsa Akbar, Daniel Platnick, Marjan Alirezaie, Hossein Rahnama

entry.summary: The paper introduces Bayesian Chronicle Agents, a belief layer that separates what an LLM agent believes from how it speaks, representing each stance as a probability updated by one Bayesian step per utterance heard. A prior-strength parameter encodes stubbornness and allows on-demand generation of canonical opinion-dynamics regimes including consensus, persistent disagreement, and committed-minority influence.

entry.title: The Limits of Speculation: Bounding Speculative Decoding in Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Aidar Amankulov, Denis Mamatin

entry.summary: The paper studies unstable verification costs in speculative decoding for MoE models caused by input-dependent expert loading, formulating speculation-budget selection as a Stochastic Shortest Path problem and building a counterfactual-simulation Oracle diagnostic. Analysis of Qwen3-Coder with EAGLE-3 shows rejected candidates form a strict linear boundary in delta space, revealing a simple local necessary condition balancing marginal cost against expected benefit.

entry.title: The Effect of Quantization on Clinical Benchmarks: Accuracy and Safety Across Model Families

author.name: Leonard Twagirayezu, Prasenjit Mitra

entry.summary: The authors evaluate five 7-8B models at FP16, INT8, and INT4 GPTQ precision across MedQA, MedMCQA, Med-HALT, HealthBench, and MedSafetyBench with risk stratification. INT8 is universally safe while INT4 degradation is substantial and model-dependent, with clinically fine-tuned BioMistral-7B losing 19.7% on MedMCQA, suggesting clinical fine-tuning does not protect against aggressive quantization.

entry.title: D-IMPL: A Diffusion-based Solver for Parameterized BBOs

author.name: Yang Hu, Na Li

entry.summary: Proposes a diffusion-based universal solver for parameterized black-box optimization, learning optimization policies as a generative modeling task over a new minimization-policy solution concept. At inference, the model amortizes optimization across BBO instances while capturing multi-modal non-convex landscapes.

entry.title: K-TRAIL: Simulator-Guided Generative Design of EM/RF Circuits

author.name: Piyush Saha, Evan Newell, Hanna O'Leary, Arun Natarajan, Alireza Aghasi

entry.summary: Combines diffusion-based layout generation with derivative-free ensemble Kalman guidance from a black-box EM simulator to synthesize RF/EM circuit layouts from prescribed S-parameter responses or performance constraints. Avoids the need for adjoint sensitivities or differentiable solvers and is demonstrated on multi-layer RFIC structures.

entry.title: Blind Thermodynamic Ontology Discovery from Anonymous Experiments

author.name: Linzhe Zhang, Changming Xu

entry.summary: Formulates discovering a hidden thermodynamic ontology (extensive versus intensive channels, conjugate pairings, governing potentials) from sensors that expose only an unknown linear mixture, using anonymous controlled experiments. Delivers an operational identifiability theory and a polynomial-time algorithm extracting scaling sectors from replication contrasts.

entry.title: Simpler Methods Work Better for L1 Penalized Logistic Models and Large Datasets

author.name: Edward Raff, James Holt

entry.summary: The authors benchmark several proposed state-of-the-art solvers for L1-penalized logistic regression on very high-dimensional (d > 1,000,000) industrial-scale tasks and find that older, simpler methods are far superior for general use. They also offer recommendations for avoiding erroneously overconfident empirical claims in solver research. The paper is a valuable empirical corrective for a workhorse model still ubiquitous in industry MLOps pipelines.

entry.title: Opinion Leader Dynamics: How Sparse Attention Shapes Token Clustering

author.name: Jingkun Liu, Yue Song

entry.summary: The paper introduces opinion leader dynamics, modeling tokens as particles on the unit sphere to explain how sparse attention causes token groups to converge internally while maintaining distinct limiting directions. Both explicit and implicit models are formulated as reverse Wasserstein gradient flows with established existence/behavior guarantees, giving a theoretical account of representation evolution under sparse attention.

entry.title: G-NAC: Graph Neural Automata Clustering via Emergent Domain Formation

author.name: Keith Miller, Tristan Crawford

entry.summary: G-NAC is an unsupervised clustering method where observations interact as cells on a graph under a shared recurrent neural cellular rule, with emergent domain states converted to spectral affinities for partitioning. It matches the strong Genie baseline across 73 tasks, scales near-linearly to 100k nodes, and its learned rules transfer across graph sizes.

entry.title: Using Composition Operators to Linearize LLM Semantic Transformations

author.name: Afjal Chowdhury, James Chen, Alan Edelman

entry.summary: The paper applies Koopman-operator theory from dynamical systems to LLMs, introducing composition operators that map between distinct spaces and viewing LLM transformations as rectangular infinite-dimensional operators. Under natural distributional assumptions the LLM operator is an isometry, and misalignment manifests as spectral pollution, offering a new mathematical lens on representation structure.

entry.title: When Does Test-Time Physical Diagnosis Pay? A Frozen Policy Buys Evidence It Never Reads

author.name: Zhengshu Zhang

entry.summary: Decomposes test-time physical diagnosis for robots into six ordered empirical conditions and tests the chain in controlled and public environments. While the chain holds in controlled settings, after transfer to unseen mechanisms it breaks at evidence use: the frozen decoder ignores the collected evidence, though a linear model on trace increments recovers correct choices. This is a valuable caution about diagnosis-driven adaptation in robotics.

entry.title: Replication Without Persistence in Hosted LLMs: Measurement Sensitivity in Action-Time Belief Evaluation

author.name: Bhushan Kashinath Joshi

entry.summary: This paper disentangles three distinct validation questions for behavioral evaluations of hosted LLMs: replication on fresh data, measurement sensitivity when an evaluation configuration is rebuilt, and persistence across model identifiers. It introduces Regent Chess, a sequential environment with exactly recorded hidden state that lets stated beliefs be scored against ground truth at action time. The work matters because it exposes how fragile conclusions about hosted-model behavior can be when service-side or instrument-side changes are conflated.

entry.title: Beyond Final-Token Classification: Heterogeneous Readouts for Evidence-Grounded Suicide Risk Detection

author.name: Zirui Li, Yanling Li, Kaolanglang Gao

entry.summary: The paper proposes heterogeneous readout decomposition for the IEEE BigData Cup benchmark, separating semantic verification from output realization across ordinal risk classification, multi-label factor detection, and phrase extraction. It uses a locally deployed Qwen3.8-27B model, an established open-weight release, adapted with QLoRA adapters, leveraging token margins and layer-63 internal states for calibrated, evidence-grounded predictions. The approach shows how internal model states can support structured clinical-risk outputs.

entry.title: Per-Query Gating of LLM Rerankers for Multi-Hop Retrieval

author.name: Andre Bacellar

entry.summary: This paper measures the cost of LLM rerankers atop a graph-augmented dense retrieval pipeline and learns a per-query gate that skips the reranker where it will not help, using only pre-call features such as score statistics and a query-embedding PCA, with an executable fallback. On three multi-hop benchmarks, reranking helps in 7 of 9 (dataset, K) cells, and the gate avoids harmful skips with all tuning confined to training folds. It is a pragmatic cost-quality tradeoff study for production RAG systems.

entry.title: Leveraging Industrial Foundation Models at the Edge of Particle Physics Detectors via Distillation Learning and Hardware Co-design

author.name: Gia Ancone, Qibin Liu, Liangyu Wu, Julia Gonski

entry.summary: Demonstrates the first fine-tuning of an industrial time-series foundation model (Google Research's TimesFM backbone) for particle physics data acquisition, targeting real-time regression for drift chamber trackers and dual-readout calorimeters. The fine-tuned model is distilled into a student and co-designed with FPGA implementation for on-detector deployment.

entry.title: XSQ-AST: An Explainable Audio Spectrogram Transformer Framework for Localising Synthetic Speech Artifacts

author.name: Ben Heritage, Luca Resti, M\'onica Villanueva Aylagas, Timothy Mehlenbacher, Konrad Tollmar, James Alfred Walker

entry.summary: XSQ-AST combines a speech quality transformer with WhisperX phoneme alignment and saliency methods to produce temporally localized diagnostics of artifacts in synthetic speech without retraining, validated by a 40-participant listening test. Saliency maps are projected onto phoneme boundaries via kernel density estimation and phoneme-discretized saliency.

entry.title: Knowledge Graph-Augmented Ambient AI for Clinical Note Generation

author.name: Jakir Hossain, Yi-Fei Zhao, Hongjian Wang, Minmei Shih, Katie Leigh Mullen, Ahmad P. Tafti, Leming Zhou, Manoj Purohit, William Hogan, Jay Zeng, Elizabeth Skidmore, Yanshan Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Coverage-Directed Revision (CDR), a model-agnostic framework that builds a knowledge graph from patient-clinician encounter transcripts and uses it to identify clinically relevant information missing from AI-generated ambient clinical notes, then revises the notes. It targets the patient-safety problem of information gaps in automated clinical documentation.

entry.title: Used, Mentioned, or Condemned? A Controlled Contrast-Set Diagnostic for the Use-Mention Distinction in Code-Mixed Hinglish Misogyny Detection

author.name: Ashanvi Yadav, Shubham Bhardwaj

entry.summary: This paper examines whether misogyny detectors can distinguish a slur used against a woman from the same slur mentioned in counter-speech, a distinction that determines whether moderation protects or silences people discussing abuse, in code-mixed Hinglish. The authors diagnose serious evaluation artifacts in a public redacted corpus: anonymization placeholders that leak category labels (a no-learning rule scoring a perfect 1.000) and lexically disjoint registers that let bag-of-words reach near-perfect F1 under random cross-validation while collapsing under templated evaluation. They contribute a controlled contrast-set diagnostic for the use-mention distinction.

entry.title: When Cosine Similarity Fails to Reflect Linearly Accessible Structure in Dialogue Models

author.name: Yu Sun, Mengyin Lu, Cong Feng, Guangming Lu, Huimin Han

entry.summary: Shows that ambient cosine similarity substantially underestimates linearly decodable persona structure in dialogue-conditioned LLMs: across three 7-8B chat models, linear probe AUC reaches 0.73-0.97 while cosine kNN only 0.56-0.77 on a 30-class task. A low-dimensional supervised subspace recovers the gap while matched-rank PCA does not, and the mismatch is regime-dependent, absent in single-sentence sentiment classification.

entry.title: Memory vs. Context? Influential Factors of Factual Recall in Language Models

author.name: Guilhem Fouilh\'e, Nicholas Asher, Philippe Muller

entry.summary: The authors reproduce and stress-test Yu et al. (2023) on how language models arbitrate between memorized knowledge and contradictory in-context statements, replicating world-capitals experiments across 31 models from Pythia, GPT-2, Qwen3, and Ministral families and extending to five more relation types. They confirm that larger models and higher-frequency entities favor memorized answers, but find several conclusions do not generalize cleanly, such as entity-frequency effects vanishing on Qwen3-14B and 32B and post-training shifting the balance. The paper provides a valuable replication check on a widely cited finding.

entry.title: On The Robustness-Resolution Tradeoff In Temporal Quantization Of Event Streams

author.name: Sayeed Shafayet Chowdhury, Ruhi Sharmin

entry.summary: The paper proves that hard temporal binning of event-camera streams is discontinuous and establishes a lower bound of 2/Delta on global L1 sensitivity for a class of nonnegative, mass-preserving continuous encoders, with two-bin linear interpolation attaining the limit uniquely. Experiments on SHD, N-MNIST, and DVS128 Gesture support the theory.

entry.title: PanoSeg3R: Feed-Forward 3D Semantic Segmentation for Panoramic Images with an Automatic Data Curation Pipeline

author.name: Heechan Yoon, Dongki Jung, Phuc Nguyen, Ming Lin, Dinesh Manocha

entry.summary: PanoSeg3R performs feed-forward 3D panoramic semantic segmentation, jointly predicting 3D geometry and multi-view semantics in a single pass using a pretrained panoramic reconstruction backbone plus a query-based mask decoder. An automatic data curation pipeline using off-the-shelf foundation models generates pseudo-annotations, expanding training data and improving zero-shot generalization to SOTA on panoramic benchmarks.

entry.title: MixiMotion: One-Step Text-to-Motion Generation via Asymmetric Set Distillation

author.name: Hung Dinh, Binh Mai, Tran Quoc Bao Le, Lam Nguyen, Cong Tran

entry.summary: Introduces MixiMotion, a strict one-step text-to-motion generator built on offline set distillation: instead of matching a single teacher trajectory, it aligns banks of teacher and student motion samples via asymmetric bidirectional matching that promotes coverage while suppressing unsupported generations. This removes the latency of iterative diffusion-style sampling.

entry.title: RegVGGT: Sustainable Visual Geometry Grounding for Streaming via Regulated Memory

author.name: Hongbo Mao (Harbin Institute of Technology), Junjun Jiang (Harbin Institute of Technology), Youyu Chen (Harbin Institute of Technology), Jiaxin Zhang (Harbin Institute of Technology), Zhemeng Dong (Harbin Institute of Technology), Xianming Liu (Harbin Institute of Technology)

entry.summary: Proposes RegVGGT, a training-free token regulation method for feed-forward reconstruction models processing lengthy video streams: based on the observation that initial token saliency predicts long-term importance, it admits at most 1% of tokens per frame to update the stream context, avoiding both memory inflation and artificially capped context. Targets sustainable 3D reconstruction from streaming video.

entry.title: GARO: Geometry-Aware Redundancy Optimization for Real-Time and High-Fidelity Dynamic Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Huiwen Xue (School of Software, Northwestern Polytechnical University), Kaixing Zhao (School of Software, Northwestern Polytechnical University), Zuheng Ming (L2TI, Universit\'e Sorbonne Paris Nord, EmboMind Research), Tingcheng Li (School of Electronic Information, Engineering, Suzhou University of Science, Technology)

entry.summary: GARO tackles the memory and rendering efficiency limitations of deformable Gaussian Splatting for dynamic scene reconstruction by introducing a unified redundancy measurement framework applied during adaptive density control. The method selects low-gradient candidates via an optimization activity assessment and evaluates geometric complexity through curvature analysis to prune redundant Gaussians. The goal is enabling real-time, high-fidelity rendering relevant for VR applications.

entry.title: Layer-Aware Position Embeddings for Visual Token Pruning in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Yahong Wang, Zhangkai Ni, Juncheng Wu, Yuyin Zhou, Ying Wen, Lianghua He

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how position embedding reassignment after visual token pruning in MLLMs degrades either perception (sparse embeddings) or grounding (continuous embeddings), and proposes layer-aware position embeddings that mitigate both failure modes. This reduces the computational overhead of hundreds of visual tokens while preserving MLLM capabilities.

entry.title: Patch-to-Global: Random Patch Diffusion for Globally Consistent Megapixel Artifact Inpainting in Whole Slide Images

author.name: Hyeseong Lee, Eunsu Kim, D M Bappy, Ho Heon Kim, Youngsuk Lee, Se Young Chun, Jang-Hwan Choi, Sung Hak Lee, Sangjeong Ahn

entry.summary: RestorePath performs globally consistent megapixel-scale inpainting of tissue artifacts (bubbles, folds) in whole slide pathology images using a latent diffusion model conditioned on pathology foundation model embeddings with large kernel attention. It prevents silent diagnostic failures caused by artifacts concealing tissue morphology. The framework addresses the gap of patch-only restoration methods that lose global structural coherence.

entry.title: LegendBench: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Legend Understanding with Counterfactual Interventions

author.name: Xinnuo Zhang, Zhike Tang, Jing Xu, Haoyuan Zhao, Weikai Yang

entry.summary: LegendBench is a parametric benchmark and generation pipeline that produces targeted legend-centric test cases for chart understanding, spanning legend parsing, grounding, legend-conditioned reasoning, and abstention. It uses counterfactual interventions to separate legend-specific failures from other reasoning errors in VLMs. This enables fine-grained diagnosis beyond aggregate accuracy metrics.

entry.title: LiAuto-MindViT: A Hybrid Vision Backbone with Adaptive Bidirectional Mamba

author.name: Lifu Mu, Shuai Chen, Wen Zheng, Haoyi Sun, Xueyang Fu, Pengfei Yu, Ning Mao, Tao Wei, Zhou Pan

entry.summary: LiAuto-MindViT is a hybrid vision backbone combining CNNs, Mamba, and Transformers, centered on an Adaptive Bidirectional Mamba module that removes unidirectional SSM directional bias via learnable alpha blending. It also includes a deployment-friendly reparameterization for faster inference, from Li Auto researchers.

entry.title: HyperCLIP++: Fine-tuning CLIP forOpen-vocabulary Semantic Segmentation in Hyperbolic Space

author.name: Zelin Peng, Zhengqin Xu, Changsong Wen, Yu Huang, Yaoming Wang, Xiaokang Yang, Wei Shen

entry.summary: HyperCLIP++ explains why jointly fine-tuning CLIP text and image encoders improves open-vocabulary segmentation via hierarchy alignment, observing that image embeddings shift from image-level to pixel-level hierarchies during fine-tuning. The method leverages hyperbolic space, which naturally encodes hierarchy, tracking hyperbolic radius changes in CLIP embeddings. It offers both a theoretical explanation and a practical segmentation improvement.

entry.title: Characterizing Wildlife Response to Biomimetic and Conventional Underwater Vehicles

author.name: Huy Pham, Levi Cai, Yogesh Girdhar, Daniela Rus, Zach J. Patterson

entry.summary: Presents the first dataset comparing fish disturbance responses to a conventional thruster-driven AUV, a sea-turtle-inspired flipper-driven AUV, and a human diver at a Caribbean reef biodiversity hotspot, analyzed from scene imagery. The work assesses whether biomimetic vehicle design reduces behavioral disruption during ocean ecology data collection.

entry.title: Kinematic Interface for the Wild: Modular Bimanual Loco-Manipulation Capture from 360$^{\circ}$ Cameras Alone

author.name: Benjamin Yang, Weiying Wang, Shenggao Li, Keming Yan, Sasha Wilkinson, Zelin Wang, Yip Fun Yeung, Lingfeng Sun

entry.summary: KIWI is a data-collection kit that uses only off-the-shelf 360-degree cameras for room-scale bimanual loco-manipulation capture, splitting roles across lenses: the rear lens builds a shared metric map registering both hands and an optional head camera, while the front lens records manipulation. This removes the need for instrumenting the operator or scene with tracking hardware.

entry.title: "Dear LLaVA, Please Drive": A Depth-Aware Vision-Language Agent for Closed-Loop Robotic Control

author.name: Sebastian Berger, Katharina Winter, Fabian B. Flohr

entry.summary: The paper fine-tunes a pretrained VLM (LLaVA-based) for autonomous navigation using imperative learning, optimizing against differentiable geometric cost fields from stereoscopic depth instead of labeled trajectories. The result is a parameter-efficient, closed-loop navigation agent that learns collision-free path generation from depth observations alone.

entry.title: Tip Manipulation in Soft Everting Robots via Wall Retraction and Deployable Fingers

author.name: Nelson Badillo Perez, Niccolo Pagliarani, Matteo Cianchetti, Robert D. Howe

entry.summary: Introduces a tip-manipulation and multi-tool deployment strategy for soft everting (vine-like growing) robots based on wall retraction, using a roller assembly and tail spool to decouple robot length from membrane-material position. This enables membrane-mounted tools to be transported, exposed, and repositioned near the distal tip. The work addresses a key limitation of everting robots, which previously supported only a single fixed tip tool.

entry.title: Imagine then Verify: Affordance-Targeted Active Perception for Task-Oriented Grasping in Cluttered Scenes

author.name: Jingzhi Cui, Xuefeng Liu, Feng Han, Xinyu Liu, Wei Chen, Jianwei Niu

entry.summary: Proposes ATAP, an affordance-targeted active perception framework for task-oriented grasping that directs next-best-view planning at task-relevant object parts rather than whole objects, avoiding wasted viewpoint budget on irrelevant surfaces in cluttered scenes. An imagine-then-verify mechanism resolves occlusions of affordance regions such as a mug handle. This is a targeted improvement to NBV planning for functional grasping.

entry.title: PRIMO: Prior-Informed Odometry from Human-Motion Tracking for Humanoid Robots

author.name: Xu Han, Angsong Li, Shaopeng Zhang, Enyu Li, Peiwen Lin, Chuang Wang, Yuan Zhuang, Haiyu Lan

entry.summary: Tackles sim-to-real transfer for humanoid proprioceptive odometry by generating supervision from humanoid tracking of diverse retargeted human motions in simulation, decoupling training data from deployment policies. A prior-informed estimator uses physics and symmetry priors to structure velocity and rotation prediction. Broadens training motion distribution while improving robustness to sim-to-real mismatch.

entry.title: CARE: Experience-Guided Atomic Corrective Execution for Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Junlan Xiao, Junwei Jiang, Zaibin Zhang, Yifan Wang, Zhongbo Zhang, Huchuan Lu, Lijun Wang

entry.summary: CARE improves failure recovery for VLA manipulation policies by learning from failures encountered during execution: it collects failed rollouts, models stage-conditioned post-failure deviation distributions, and synthesizes representative failure states and corrective demonstrations from them. At inference it combines stage-wise planning with physically grounded 3D monitoring to trigger atomic corrective adjustments while preserving the base policy. This addresses the brittleness of VLA policies once execution deviates from nominal trajectories.

entry.title: Smoothness as a Constraint for Stable Humanoid Locomotion

author.name: Utsav Panchal, Denis Kleyko, Unal Artan, Amy Loutfi

entry.summary: DeCap is a constrained reinforcement learning algorithm for humanoid whole-body control that decouples smoothness requirements between the reactive lower body and tightly regulated upper body, imposing smoothness as explicit constraints on physical quantities rather than competing auxiliary reward terms. The approach improves locomotion stability where prior RL treats the body uniformly.

entry.title: Turbulence & Fragility: Prompting-Based Experiments are Sensitive to Stray Details (And other lessons for new researchers.)

author.name: Czynski

entry.summary: The author stress-tests prompting-dependent AI risk experiments, using the ICML 2026 paper on peer preservation in frontier models as a case study and varying framing in content-neutral and blunt ways. Results support the hypothesis that many elicited behaviors are highly sensitive to stray prompt details, echoing lessons from the 2025 Palisade shutdown-resistance and instruction-ambiguity controversy.

entry.title: RBS-Attention: Radius-Bounded Sparse Prefill for Long-Context Large Language Models

author.name: Chuxu Song, Jiuqi Wei, Zhencan Peng

entry.summary: This paper identifies a failure mode in sparse-attention prefill called mean dilution, where block centroids hide highly relevant tokens. It proposes RBS-Attention, a training-free method with a centroid branch plus a rescue branch using maximum key-block radius to catch underestimated blocks, with independent thresholding and mask combination. This targets the prefill bottleneck for long-context LLM inference.

entry.title: TinyCeNN-LM: Quality-Gated Conversion of Pretrained Attention with CeNN-Inspired Cellular-Recurrent Layers

author.name: Kabeh Mohsenzadegan, Vahid Tavakkoli, Kyandoghere Kyamakya

entry.summary: This arXiv paper proposes TinyCeNN-LM, a post-training framework for replacing attention layers in a pretrained language model with cellular neural network (CeNN)-inspired cellular-recurrent layers that use bounded local processing and compact recurrent memory. The key mechanism is a quality gate: a converted layer is accepted only if representation-similarity and negative log-likelihood criteria pass fixed thresholds, otherwise the conversion is rolled back. Experiments on SmolLM2-135M show the first three layers can be converted with a tiny cumulative NLL degradation (+0.012) while a deeper layer is rejected because representation drift exceeds thresholds despite acceptable NLL.

entry.title: A Fully Differentiable Neuro-Soft-Symbolic Framework for Perceptual Task Planning

author.name: Hongyan Wei, Wael AbdAlmageed

entry.summary: The authors introduce a fully differentiable framework connecting visual perception and task planning in a single computational graph, maintaining continuous soft-symbolic states and a differentiable transition operator. Planning gradients flow back to update perception parameters, preserving perceptual uncertainty instead of discarding it via discretization. This advances neuro-symbolic integration for embodied or visual planning tasks.

entry.title: Accelerating Dense LLMs via L0-regularized Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Zhenyu Zhang, Jiudong Yang, Zhaowen Tao, Meng Chen

entry.summary: L0-MoE is a lightweight MoE approach that accelerates dense LLMs using L0-regularization, claiming up to 2.5x speedup with competitive performance. It adds a cluster confusion matrix for domain-aware dataset curation and dynamic batching for efficient training, outperforming existing LLM acceleration baselines.

entry.title: What Should We Ask Next? Retrieval-Aware Question Learning under Partial Evidence

author.name: Lyucheng Qian, John Yuehan Zhang, Pingyu Wang

entry.summary: RAVEL frames interactive retrieval under partial evidence as sequential information acquisition and shows that imitating offline question orderings gives weak supervision for the true objective. It introduces a retrieval-aware online RL framework for interactive person re-identification that observes current top candidates and optimizes for the downstream effect of each question on retrieval updates.

entry.title: dSTAR: Straggler Tolerant and Byzantine Resilient Distributed SGD

author.name: Jiahe Yan, Pratik Chaudhari, Leonard Kleinrock

entry.summary: This paper introduces dSTAR, a lightweight method for distributed SGD that handles slow workers (stragglers) and malicious gradient updates (Byzantine attacks). It aggregates only the first k responding workers and filters updates using an ensemble-median deviation measure, improving robustness and convergence guarantees.

entry.title: KnowDemo: Knowledge-Guided Robot Demonstration Generation from Human Videos
