entry.summary: Investigates bias against Sa'idi Egyptian Arabic (SEA), a non-prestigious dialect underrepresented relative to Cairene Arabic, using targeted syntactic evaluations to show significant upstream preference bias across multiple LLMs, then links those same features to worse downstream MMLU performance. Demonstrates a concrete upstream-bias to downstream-degradation chain.

entry.title: LLJ Cards: Best practices for the Use of LLMs as Judges

author.name: Khaoula Chehbouni, Melina Medjdoub, Florian Carichon, Golnoosh Farnadi, Jackie Chi Kit Cheung

entry.summary: This paper addresses validity and reliability concerns with LLM-as-judge (LLJ) evaluation, arguing that existing bias-mitigation techniques and prompting fixes leave a more fundamental gap: systematic documentation of how judges are constructed and used. It proposes LLJ Cards, a documentation framework akin to model cards for reporting the design and use of LLM judges. The work reframes judge reliability as an accountability and transparency problem rather than purely a technical one.

entry.title: Contributions to the hierarchy of probabilistic languages

author.name: Lothar Sebastian Krapp, Remo Nitschke

entry.summary: Establishes results in the theory of probabilistic formal languages: every probabilistic language generated by an n-gram model is generated by some PCFG, while some PCFG languages cannot be generated by any n-gram model. It introduces fully connected PCFGs and proves that n-gram probabilistic languages always differ from those of fully connected PCFGs, clarifying the strict hierarchy between the formalisms.

entry.title: Extracting Arguments, Not Just Classifying Them: Instruction-Tuned LLMs for Generative Component Detection

author.name: Sofiane Elguendouze (UniCA, I3S, MARIANNE), Erwan Hain (UniCA, MARIANNE), Elena Cabrio (MARIANNE, UniCA), Serena Villata (CNRS, MARIANNE)

entry.summary: The paper proposes ITFACD, which reformulates argumentative component detection as a generation task using instruction-tuned LLMs with compact prompts, jointly identifying and classifying argument spans instead of using sequence labeling or segmentation-then-classification pipelines. This directly targets a challenging and underexplored argument mining subtask.

entry.title: MarsRecon: Self-Supervised and Multimodal Surface Representations for Mars

author.name: Akshay Naik, Marius F. R. Juston, Jay Mahajan

entry.summary: MarsRecon is a geospatially aware pipeline that calibrates NASA PDS HiRISE observations of Olympus Mons, trains a masked autoencoder on unlabeled imagery, and then aligns the frozen visual encoder with observation text, coordinates, and local-global image context for multimodal Martian surface representations. Increasing resolution and filtering invalid tokens reduced held-out reconstruction loss from 0.1751 to 0.1342.

entry.title: AdaMerge: Tuning-Free Patch Compression for Multi-Vector Visual Document Retrieval

author.name: Jianxin You, Kun Ni

entry.summary: AdaMerge improves multi-vector visual document retrieval (e.g., ColPali-style systems) by removing the need to grid-search per-dataset cluster budgets. It observes a sharp cliff in the merge-cosine sequence from hierarchical clustering that separates redundant from salient patches, and exploits this concentration to set compression automatically.

entry.title: Compressing 3D Gaussian Splatting via Cross-Representation Priors

author.name: Yezheng Zhang, Huanxiong Liang, Chuqin Zhou, Guo Lu, Wenjun Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes CRP-GS, a rate-distortion optimized compression framework for 3D Gaussian Splatting that exploits redundancy across anchors using cross-representation priors, with a correspondence-oriented hierarchical structure that conditions some anchors on others for better entropy modeling. Addresses the high storage and transmission costs of dense Gaussian primitives.

entry.title: GrapeSplat: Geometry-Grounded Reconstruction via Amalgamated Pose-Free Encoding for Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Si-Yu Lu, Yung-Yao Chen, Yi Jan Chen, Shang-Lin Li, Ching-Chan Liao, Wen-Huang Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes GrapeSplat, a feed-forward pose-free 3DGS method that amalgamates multi-view cues into a voxel-aligned scene representation and decodes Gaussians from the learned grid without per-scene optimization, using an Atlas Encoder for pixel-wise geometry-appearance features and PEACH-Vox to map unbounded scenes into a bounded sparse grid with a closed-form inverse. Addresses fragile global structure and resolution-tied primitive counts in pixel-wise prediction.

entry.title: GAPS: Generative Active Pseudo-view Selection for Sparse-View 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Hongfei Zhu, Haochen Deng, Sitao Zhang, Ling Zhou

entry.summary: GAPS improves sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting by alternately using a pre-trained image diffusion model, constrained via depth-conditioned ControlNet, IP-Adapter, LoRA, and img2img anchoring, to generate geometrically consistent pseudo-views for supervision. Its active pseudo-view selection balances reconstruction informativeness against generative reliability with an annealing schedule. Combines two hot areas (3DGS and diffusion guidance) in a principled way.

entry.title: An Efficient and Effective Watermarking Scheme for the Protection of the Intellectual Property Rights of Video Generative Models

author.name: Wenhong Huang, Jianwei Fei, Benedetta Tondi, Bin Ma, Fangjun Huang

entry.summary: The authors propose VidMark, an in-generation watermarking network using two-scale DWT decomposition, designed to support both synthetic video verification and model ownership verification for video generative models. This addresses largely unaddressed forensic tasks for protecting video-generation IP.

entry.title: Which Terrain Is Better? Preference Learning with VLM Prototypes for Off-Road Traversability Ranking

author.name: Ji-Hoon Hwang, Jisung Bae, E-In Son, Dong-Wook Kim, Jung-Taak Kim, Seung-Woo Seo

entry.summary: TravPro reframes off-road traversability as visual terrain ranking supervised by pairwise comparisons implied by existing annotations, rather than predefined per-class scores. Using VLM prototypes, it learns an ordering of visible terrain reflecting which region a robot should prefer, addressing the lack of universal traversability ground truth.

entry.title: Video-STLayout Pre-training

author.name: Akash Abdu Jyothi, Greg Mori

entry.summary: The authors introduce a pre-training strategy that aligns video encoder features with spatio-temporal layout features derived from object bounding boxes obtained by an off-the-shelf detector, using a contrastive loss. This yields richer video representations that transfer well to downstream tasks such as activity recognition. It is a simple, data-efficient way to inject structural layout knowledge into video models.

entry.title: Positive Pair Geometry Matters: Optimal Transport for Contrastive Learning of Visual Representations

author.name: Akshit Nanda, Shahzad Ahmad, Ram Prasad Padhy

entry.summary: OTCLR uses entropic optimal-transport displacement interpolation to construct intermediate, geometry-consistent views between an image and its augmentations, replacing independently sampled positive pairs in contrastive learning. These transport-interpolated positives respect the intrinsic geometry of the data distribution. The method aims to improve representation quality without changing the overall contrastive framework.

entry.title: Beyond Emotion Prompts: Fine-Grained Text-to-Image Generation Driven by Valence-Arousal-Dominance

author.name: Minglang Li, Yueyue Fang, Xieping Gao

entry.summary: EMOTRANS converts psychologically grounded valence-arousal-dominance (VAD) coordinates into generation conditions independent of content text and modulated across denoising stages, making emotional style a finely adjustable variable in text-to-image generation. The authors also build EMOVAD, an art-painting dataset pairing objective content descriptions with separately collected multi-annotator emotional ratings. This enables ordered, scale-based emotion control beyond ad-hoc prompts.

entry.title: Document Retrieval-Aware Chunking (D-RAC): Universal Retrieval-Aware Ingestion of Enterprise Documents via PDF Normalization and Multimodal Markdown Conversion

author.name: Uday Allu (AI Research Team Yellow.ai), Abhivanth Sivaprakash (AI Research Team Yellow.ai), Pratik Singh (AI Research Team Yellow.ai), Aman Manocha (AI Research Team Yellow.ai)

entry.summary: D-RAC extends retrieval-aware chunking to arbitrary enterprise document formats by first normalizing inputs to PDF, then performing multimodal Markdown conversion that preserves reading order, tables, and heading hierarchy, avoiding the losses of rule-based OCR and the cost of fully agentic chunking. This improves RAG ingestion over heterogeneous knowledge bases. It is a practical systems contribution from an industry research team.

entry.title: AnalogDepth: Multi-view Geometry from FPV drones under Analog Video Transmission

author.name: Andr\'e Amorim, Pedro F. Proen\c{c}a

entry.summary: AnalogDepth shows that spatially structured analog video transmission noise severely degrades Depth Anything 3, a state-of-the-art feed-forward geometry model, and adapts it to FPV drone imagery via LoRA-based student-teacher distillation using a hardware noise dataset rather than analytic noise synthesis. This enables reliable multi-view depth for low-latency analog drone links.

entry.title: MIRAGE: Full-Body Bystander Privacy for Smart Glasses with Consent-Based Restoration

author.name: Muhammad Umair, Muhammad Danial Maqbool, Fatima Arshad Cheema, Kapal Dev, Muhammad Hamad Alizai, Muhammad Ali Siddiqi, Naveed Anwar Bhatti

entry.summary: MIRAGE is a three-tier privacy architecture for smart glasses that addresses full-body re-identification risks beyond face blurring, covering gait, posture, and silhouette biometrics. It performs full-body detection and synthetic replacement while storing encrypted recovery material enabling consent-based restoration, implemented on a Raspberry Pi 5 with companion phones and a cloud backend. It reports strong detection performance (0.948 AP).

entry.title: Anatomically Faithful Artifact Suppression in SENSE Accelerated Brain MRI

author.name: Changjing Chai, Bin Huang, Libo Xu, Jian Zhou, Boyang Pan, Kristen W Yeom, Qiyong Gong, Nan-Jie Gong

entry.summary: In a prospective paired study of 80 participants, the authors develop ART-Net, an anatomy-aware residual attention network that refines 4x-accelerated SENSE brain MRI reconstructions using generalized self-attention and correlation-based residual artifact regularization while preserving anatomy for quantitative measurements.

entry.title: Behavior Trees for Robotic Systems: An Empirical Study on Practices and Experiences

author.name: Razan Ghzouli, Jennifer Horkoff, Daniel Str\"uber, Rebekka Wohlrab

entry.summary: A mixed-methods empirical study of how behavior trees are actually used in robotics, combining technical action research at an automotive company with a survey of 34 robotics practitioners. It documents real-world adoption practices, gaps between academic guidelines and industrial challenges, and issues around software reuse, maintenance, and evolution.

entry.title: PileBelief: Persistent Physical State for Interaction-Driven World Modeling

author.name: Hongyi Lin, Song Zhang, Haiquan Liu, Yang Liu, Jinhua Zhao, Xiaobo Qu

entry.summary: PileBelief is an interaction-driven persistent world model for partially observed excavation that maintains physical evidence beyond the visible surface using world-addressed deformation and physical-response memory. Observation-conditioned priors, gated residual corrections, and action-aligned reads refine terrain-change predictions as the robot interacts with the pile.

entry.title: Towards Reliable Underwater Diver-Robot Interaction: Gesture Design, Interaction Logic, and Real-World Evaluation

author.name: Yingqi Liu, Kanzhong Yao, Zimeng Peng, Yuanbo Bi, Anran Li, Zhe Sun, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: Evaluates a closed-loop diver-robot interaction framework with a compact seven-gesture vocabulary, lightweight landmark-based recognition, and command-level interaction logic, tested through a user study and underwater experiments in a tank and pool. Findings connect visual similarity to gesture confusion and identify temporal ambiguity from intermediate poses. Real-world human-robot interaction evaluations are rare, especially underwater.

entry.title: Smartphone GNSS Booster: Centimeter-Level Pedestrian Positioning Using a Portable Signal Re-Radiator

author.name: Taro Suzuki

entry.summary: Proposes an external GNSS signal re-radiation system that boosts smartphone observation quality—connecting an active helical antenna and passive patch re-radiator—while still using the phone's built-in receiver and antenna, achieving centimeter-level pedestrian positioning versus the usual meter level. It targets sidewalk-level navigation and pinpoint location applications. The hardware-plus-algorithm approach to smartphone positioning is practically notable.

entry.title: FlockDiffusion: Assignment-Conditioned Diffusion for Multi-Drone Task Allocation and Completion

author.name: Iana Zhura, Satenik Akopyan, Roohan Ahmed Khan, Miguel Altamirano Cabrera, Aleksey Fedoseev, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: FlockDiffusion unifies multi-drone task bundling, allocation, and trajectory generation with a scene graph encoder, explicit allocation head, assignment-conditioned diffusion transformer, and closed-form trajectory decoder, supervised by an autoregressive teacher. Shows bundling raises task completion from 50% in cluttered environments under tight compute budgets. Replaces separate cost-estimation, assignment, and execution solvers.

entry.title: When Does Touch Matter? Charting the Vision-Interaction Gap in Cluttered Dexterous Grasping

author.name: Hao Jiang, Luis Dominguez, Daniel Seita

entry.summary: This is a controlled real-world study quantifying when tactile measurements and external wrench estimates improve over visual geometry for dexterous grasping in clutter, holding demonstrations, observations, action space, and control fixed across five scene conditions. The combined visuo-tactile-wrench policy achieves 24/25 success versus 14/25 for vision-only in one condition and 15/15 versus 6/15 in another. It provides clear empirical guidance on when multimodal interaction sensing pays off.

entry.title: ME-Brain-1.0: Memory, Cognition and Action for Evolving Embodied Intelligence

author.name: Wei He, Hengtao Li, Zhongrui Yu, Xuhan Zhu, Maokui He, Zide Liu, Xiyue Zhang, Xianwei Mao, Chunpeng Zhou, Jia Shi, Yanze Xin, Jingwen Li, Jingxie Zheng, Sijie Zeng, Chenfeng Wang, Fan Lu, Zeyu Zhang, Shuai Guo, Hengxuan Zhang, Pengfei Yu, Jia Shi, Yu Liu, Kun Zhan, Yan Xie

entry.summary: ME-Brain is a self-evolving embodied system organized around a closed loop of action execution, experience acquisition, experience evolution, and improved execution, with an Evolvable Memory consolidating multimodal trajectories into hierarchical reusable experience, a Cognitive Core turning experience into transferable skills, and an Action Model using event-driven keyframes and event-cell local-world prediction. It aims to let embodied systems keep learning from physical interaction after deployment instead of relying on fixed pretrained capabilities. This is an ambitious systems-level proposal for continual embodied learning.

entry.title: InsertAnything: Generalizable Contact-Rich Precision Insertion from Simulation to Reality

author.name: Zhenghua Ma, Xinpan Meng, Zeyu Liu, Muyuan Ma, Hengdi Zhang, Houcheng Li, Long Cheng

entry.summary: This RL framework trains contact-rich insertion policies entirely in simulation for direct zero-shot real deployment, combining target poses with fingertip force feedback so the policy can search for alignment under hole-position estimation errors. A decoupled gated reward coordinates alignment and insertion phases, with force-signal smoothing supporting generalization across varied part geometries and clearances without real-world demonstrations or fine-tuning.

entry.title: Learning Beyond What Humans Can Demonstrate

author.name: Yuchen Song, Aditya Mittal, Unnat Jain

entry.summary: Introduces GLIDE, a framework for the infeasible-demonstration regime where human teleoperation data cannot be collected for dynamic, contact-timing, or dexterous tasks. GLIDE infers task-specific failure modes and converts them into executable guardrails that filter teleoperation and policy commands, constrain failure-prone actions, and iteratively improve from trajectory feedback.

entry.title: The current balance of power in open models

author.name: Nathan Lambert

entry.summary: Nathan Lambert shares prepared remarks from a Congressional briefing assessing the state of open-weight models through a US-China competition lens, clarifying open-weight versus open-source versus closed model distinctions and situating Llama, Qwen, Gemma, and DeepSeek in the strategic landscape.

entry.title: DiaVLo: Diagnosing Behaviours of Vision-Language Models

author.name: Lorenzo Corti, Jie Yang

entry.summary: DiaVLo is a diagnostic framework for VLMs that combines human curation with VLM generation to specify desired versus observed behaviors and surface misalignments, additionally providing causal estimates of concepts steering VLM behavior. It is evaluated on several open-source VLMs in both classification and generation settings.

entry.title: List Counting Failures Are Not One Phenomenon

author.name: Iyad Ait Hou, Saad Mankarious, Aya Zirikly, Rebecca Hwa

entry.summary: Studying list-counting failures across seven open-weight instruct models on identical prompts, the authors find distinct, model-specific error modes: Qwen and Gemma 27B flip odd lengths to nearby even integers, OLMo concentrates on mid-sized integers, and Llama under-counts. These modes are not a stable family law and heavier subword fragmentation does not make counting harder, contradicting popular input-bottleneck explanations.

entry.title: CTRL: Control-Based Time Series Forecasting with LLM-Guided Residual Learning

author.name: Minkyoung Kim, Daeun Ji, Yohan Lee, Beomsoo Kim, Beakcheol Jang

entry.summary: Introduces CTRL, which decouples semantic reasoning from quantitative prediction in LLM-based time series forecasting: a frozen backbone generates base forecasts while LLM agents act as controllers analyzing decomposed error components (trend, seasonal, irregular) and outputting corrective commands for residual learning.

entry.title: TRACE: Tractable Routing Autoencoder for Clinical ECG

author.name: Shunbo Jia, Runze Ma, Haonan Lyu, Haijin Zhang, Qiang Yang, Caizhi Liao

entry.summary: Proposes a tractable routing autoencoder for ECG diagnosis whose 32-dimensional latent space is specified in advance from cardiology knowledge, partitioned into perfusion, structure, and conduction subspaces routed to dedicated diagnostic heads. This makes diagnoses traceable to physiological pathways and enables clinician intervention, unlike auditable black-box ECG foundation models.

entry.title: One Patch, Three Roles: What Is Actually Coupled in Autoregressive Time-Series Forecasting?

author.name: Ziang Li, Yue Huang, Guoxu Zhou, Na Han, Jie Wen, Lunke Fei, Xiaozhao Fang

entry.summary: Disentangles the three roles a single patch length plays in patch-based autoregressive forecasting (input representation, learned transitions, recursive execution) and shows a frozen parent's recursive trajectory is easier to fit than the observed future via lightweight parallel exits. Autoregressive Trajectory Distillation enables selectable execution depths, with ATD-8 achieving 5.54x end-to-end speedup at stable quality.

entry.title: Identifying Representational Biases in Datasets Using PCA: A Max-Disparity Partition Framework

author.name: Arjun KM, Shashi Jain

entry.summary: The paper formalizes the max-disparity partition problem: finding, without group labels, the binary data partition that suffers the greatest representational disparity under a shared PCA projection. A greedy local-search algorithm based on Fiduccia-Mattheyses bipartitioning is proposed and benchmarked against alternatives.

entry.title: CultureMINE: Datasets and Methods for Improving the Cultural Capabilities of NLP Systems

author.name: Tania Chakraborty, Eylon Caplan, Zhaoqing Wu, Kevin Cushing, Han Qin, Shreya Havaldar, Dan Goldwasser

entry.summary: A meta-analysis of over 375 papers in Cultural NLP answering three questions: which cultural capabilities are targeted, how cultural data resources are created, and what methods improve them. It identifies research gaps and releases an interactive interface with the full analyzed paper list to facilitate future research.

entry.title: Adapting Tree-Structured Speculative Decoding to DeepSeek-V4 for Efficient Inference

author.name: Changxu Liu, Zhaogeng Li

entry.summary: The paper integrates tree-structured speculative decoding into the DeepSeek-V4-Flash pipeline, an existing model released in April 2026, addressing the technical challenge that its CSA/HCA online compressed attention breaks cross-branch state consistency when branches diverge from shared prefixes. The solution combines branch-aware causal verification, temporary state isolation, and related mechanisms. Tree speculation retains multiple branches under the same budget, improving acceptance rates and inference efficiency over linear chains.

entry.title: Planning and Rendering in Concert: DeepFusion of Autoregressive Layouts and Diffusion for Visual Text Generation

author.name: Guanqiao Chen, Jingru Tan, Dongxing Mao, Catherine Chen, Zijian Du, Libo Qin, Hu Jian Guo, Alex Jinpeng Wang

entry.summary: DuetGen jointly learns autoregressive layout planning and continuous diffusion rendering for text-rich image generation, conditioning a diffusion transformer on the planner's prompt and bbox-conditioned representations so planner and renderer adapt together rather than being optimized separately. It builds on a DeepFusion architecture to improve textual fidelity and integration.

entry.title: BiView-Touch: Learning Bimanual Tactile Representations by Cross-Hand Completion

author.name: Chenxin Liang, Youchen Lai, Chuqiao Lyu, Tianxing Chen, Shoujie Li, Wenbo Ding

entry.summary: Introduces BiView-Touch, a tactile-only representation-learning framework exploiting the complementary views two hands produce of the same physical process: a student encoder completes masked target-hand latents using visible target-hand regions and the synchronized contralateral hand, with temporal and layout counterfactuals for sensitivity to synchronized, anatomically organized information.

entry.title: PrismGPT: Proxy-Guided Learning for Region-Aware Photo Editing with Self-Synthesized Reasoning

author.name: Ke Zhao, Hue Nguyen, Abhijith Punnappurath, Zhongling Wang, Iqbal Mohomed, Michael S. Brown

entry.summary: PrismGPT is a VLM framework producing structured, region-aware photo editing plans combining global adjustments and semantic-mask-guided local edits without commercial black-box tools. Proxy-guided learning uses two simpler proxy tasks, operation decomposition and region-aware aesthetic ranking, to teach skills needed for the large combinatorial decision space. It targets automating professional photo-finishing workflows.

entry.title: A Reconfigurable Dual-Opposition Architecture for Single-Hand Assembly and Manipulation

author.name: William Su, Yunosuke Nakamura, Yixiao Wang, Yitong Li, Mingrui Yu, Huanan Qi, Boyuan Liang, Masayoshi Tomizuka, Jianshu Zhou

entry.summary: The paper presents a reconfigurable dual-opposition hand architecture with four independently actuated fingers organized into two virtual-finger oppositions and a reconfigurable palm, enabling simultaneous grasping of two parts and coordinated in-hand assembly. It includes a kinematic model, object-size-conditioned workspace formulation, and motion/assembly evaluation.

entry.title: MR-SPITE: Accelerating Multi-Robot Conflict Scans via Hierarchical Swept-Volume Approximations

author.name: Marta Markowicz, James Motes, Marco Morales, Nancy Amato

entry.summary: MR-SPITE is a conservative filter that partitions synchronized multi-robot paths into temporal segments with conservative swept-volume bounds, certifying conflict-free windows before invoking exact collision checking. Integrated into ARC with VAMP collision checking, it dramatically accelerates conflict scans (demonstrated on 16 Fetch robots). A systems contribution to multi-robot coordination efficiency.

entry.title: Tactile-JEPA: Topology-Aware Self-Supervised Representation Learning for Distributed Tactile Sensors

author.name: Elizaveta Kovtun, Matvey Konovalov, Andrey Sakhovskiy, Semen Budennyy

entry.summary: Tactile-JEPA is an efficient self-supervised pretraining method for distributed electronic skins, whose sparse and irregularly arranged sensing elements make direct reuse of visual SSL methods suboptimal. It adapts the JEPA predictive-representation framework in a topology-aware way for tactile data, filling a gap since prior tactile SSL focused on vision-based sensors. Better tactile encoders could improve contact-rich manipulation under visual occlusion.

entry.title: Risk-Aware Occupancy for Safety-Oriented End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jiaxing Chen, Hengduo Zou, Yiren Zhao, Bolin Gao

entry.summary: ROIDrive introduces risk-aware occupancy, a dense BEV representation that jointly encodes scene occupancy, map-derived traffic constraints, and future dynamic agent occupancy for safety-oriented end-to-end driving. This gives the planner explicit, spatiotemporally aligned risk evidence in crowded and occluded scenes where sparse object representations fall short. It matters for improving safety in end-to-end autonomous driving stacks.

entry.title: Learning-to-Optimize as the Missing Architectural Layer of AI-Native Networks

author.name: Giambattista Amati, Federica Mangiatordi, Pierpaolo Salvo, Emiliano Pallotti, Simone Angelini

entry.summary: A position-style paper arguing that Learning-to-Optimize (L2O) should serve as the missing architectural layer between classical optimization and AI-native communication networks. It reframes optimization algorithms as offline knowledge generators that produce transferable knowledge for AI models rather than merely online decision engines, enabling autonomous resource management and zero-touch network operation.

entry.title: Calibrating Teacher--Student Discrepancy for On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Qiangqiang He, Jin Li, MingCai Chen

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces Calibrated On-Policy Distillation (Cal-OPD), a method that improves reasoning-model distillation by separating the true teacher-student capability gap from noise caused by the teacher's own deviations. The authors show that standard on-policy distillation indiscriminately learns these teacher-side likelihood shifts, a problem amplified in privileged OPD, and propose calibrating the discrepancy signal before training.

entry.title: Listen Before You Speak: Response Planning from Listener Facial Reactions for Conversational Speech Generation

author.name: Yunji Chu

entry.summary: ReACT-TTS is a two-stage framework that uses a one-second pre-response listener facial sequence to plan the emotion and prosody of the next spoken utterance. Experiments on a strict dyadic MELD protocol show temporal conditioning improves macro-F1 and VAD concordance, and 76% of speech researchers judged the contextual appropriateness favorably.

entry.title: SpaceDiffusion: Over-the-Orbit Diffusion for Space Generate-and-Forward Communications

author.name: Jianhao Huang, Zhanwei Wang, Khaled B. Letaief, Kaibin Huang

entry.summary: The paper proposes generate-and-forward (GF) satellite relaying, where satellites run on-orbit generative AI (SpaceDiffusion, a diffusion model with a character-level codec) to reconstruct corrupted image transmissions before forwarding to ground stations. This targets the uplink bottleneck in 6G satellite networks caused by low device power and aperture.

entry.title: From Memory to Behavior: A Behavior-Aware Role-Playing Framework for Social Media Influencers

author.name: Ji-Lun Peng, Yi-Zhen Zhang, Chun-Nan Chou, Yun-Nung Chen

entry.summary: This paper proposes the Situation-Internal state-Behavior Persona method for LLM role-playing agents, capturing how individuals react differently depending on the situation rather than relying solely on in-context examples. It also designs an LLM evaluation protocol that supplies evaluators with references about the impersonated person, evaluated on a new social media reply dataset. This improves fidelity of impersonation and evaluation of less famous individuals.

entry.title: CityLearn v3: A Configurable Simulation and Evaluation Framework for Realistic Control Studies of Renewable Energy Communities

author.name: Tiago Fonseca, Luis Lino Ferreira, Armando Sousa, Ava Mohammadi, Zoltan Nagy

entry.summary: CityLearn v3 is a configurable simulation and evaluation framework for control studies of renewable energy communities, modeling changing membership, equipment availability, flexible-load deadlines, demand-response requests, local energy sharing, and data or equipment failures. Unlike simplified controller studies that can hide missed services or infeasible power requests, it enforces building and phase power limits. This enables more realistic evaluation of energy-control and RL policies.

entry.title: CIBuzzBench: A Benchmark for Cross-Lingual Understanding of Chinese Internet Buzzwords

author.name: Yifan Wang, Junyu Lu, Qifan Wang, Shun Zhang, Chaozhuo Li, Jiahao Liu, Zhijun Cao, Lingbin Bu, Fanliang Bu

entry.summary: CIBuzzBench evaluates whether advanced LLMs can understand Chinese internet buzzwords and transfer their culturally grounded, often non-literal meanings into English, a capability tied to safety because offensive content may hide behind homophony, euphemism, and coded language. The benchmark probes cross-lingual knowledge transfer on an evolving, culture-specific lexicon.

entry.title: Generalized Multimodal Foundation Model

author.name: Huizi Cui, Zongbo Han, Chenggong Ding, Naichuan Xiao, Jialong Yang, Jingdong Chen, Guangyu Wang, Qinghua Hu, Changqing Zhang

entry.summary: This paper asks whether a single multimodal fusion model can handle arbitrary modality combinations and arbitrary prediction tasks, rather than being locked to predefined modalities. The authors propose a learning paradigm that trains on the generation of large-scale multimodal correlation patterns, aiming to encode transferable fusion skills instead of modality-specific representations.

entry.title: Correlation-Guided Flow Matching with Annealed Masking for Spatial Transcriptomics Generation

author.name: Yupei Zhang, Hao Chen, Li Pan, Chao Li, Xiaohan Xing

entry.summary: The paper targets predicting spatial transcriptomics gene expression from histology images, arguing that gene-gene interactions must be preserved rather than treating genes independently. It introduces a correlation-guided flow matching model with annealed masking to capture co-expression structure in the generative process.

entry.title: Toollery: Scaling LLM Agents to Thousands of Skills and Tools

author.name: Xiangxi Tian, Ran Guan

entry.summary: Toollery is a training-free candidate-compression framework for scalable LLM skill and tool selection: it generates user-intent queries from each skill/tool specification and builds a retrieval index mapping real requests to compact candidate sets before final LLM decision-making. This addresses the cost, latency, and distraction problems of full-library prompting when agents face thousands of capabilities.

entry.title: SCALE: Simulation-Calibrated Amortized Learning for Energy Materials (A hybrid architecture connecting deterministic modeling, real-world data, and transformer-scale inference for accelerated energy-materials discovery)

author.name: Kuan Huang, Bo Bai

entry.summary: SCALE is a physics-grounded, real-world-data-calibrated architecture that links deterministic scientific operators, experimental calibration, and transformer-scale inference to accelerate energy-materials discovery. It converts expensive mechanistic computations and measured evidence into reusable models supporting rapid screening, ranking, inverse design, and active learning, demonstrated on solid-state materials applications.

entry.title: CAMFT: Conflict-Aware Mergeable Fine-Tuning for Large Language Models

author.name: Jingang Zhou, Haiyang Guo, Yuan Ma, Han Zhu, Xu-Yao Zhang

entry.summary: This paper proposes CAMFT, a fine-tuning method that treats model mergeability as a property shaped during the training phase rather than resolved afterward. By steering each task to update sparse parameter coordinates with low cross-task conflict, it aims to reduce the parameter clashes that make post-hoc model merging sub-optimal. The work matters because model merging is an increasingly practical way to combine multiple task capabilities into a single LLM without retraining.

entry.title: The Ups and Downs of Backprop Weights

author.name: Giuseppe Chindemi, Benjamin F. Grewe

entry.summary: The paper introduces weight entanglement: the problem that overlapping parameter sets across functions (e.g., object recognition and motion prediction) resist selective reuse and adaptation, even in modern architectures with dynamic selection like gating, attention, and mixture-of-experts. It analyzes how backpropagation organizes parameters and proposes approaches to reduce entanglement.

entry.title: Autonomous Model Lifecycle Management for Digital Twin-Based Manufacturing Control

author.name: Zhengyang (Cissy), Gu, Thomas Cook, Fredaljohn Rohrbaugh, Joseph E. Hernandez, Chris Couch

entry.summary: Describes a closed-loop cyber-physical system deployed since 2023 in automotive manufacturing that autonomously manages model lifecycles under distributional shift, pairing a physics-based digital twin with an RL control policy. Multiple model variants compete each retraining cycle and only the best candidate advances, with safeguards and operator-trust mechanisms.

entry.title: Robust Market Making with Hawkes Order Flow and Price Impact via Adversarial Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Hao Yang, Zhenguo Xu

entry.summary: Extends adversarial RL for market making beyond Poisson order arrivals by incorporating Hawkes self-exciting order flow and trade-induced price impact in a zero-sum market-maker-versus-adversary formulation. Aims to improve robustness to regime shifts and capture high-frequency microstructure effects missing from prior approaches.

entry.title: Beyond Similarity: Coverage-Aware Prompt Selection for Time Series Forecasting with LLMs

author.name: Daeun Ji, Minkyoung Kim, Dongkuk Kim, Yohan Lee, Beomsoo Kim, Beakcheol Jang

entry.summary: Shows that similarity-based prompt retrieval for LLM-based time series forecasting biases predictions toward dominant temporal patterns and misses rare informative events. Proposes CASP-LLM, a coverage-aware semantic prompt selection method that controls redundancy in the retrieved prompt pool.

entry.title: Optimal Multi-way Decision Trees for Stratified Sampling in Online Controlled Experiments

author.name: Tomoka Takei, Shunnosuke Ikeda, Yuichi Takano

entry.summary: Proposes OMST, a framework that formulates stratification for A/B test variance reduction as a path-selection problem over a feature graph, solved with an exact optimizer to produce interpretable multi-way decision tree strata. This improves statistical power in online controlled experiments without increasing sample size.

entry.title: Predicting Out-of-Distribution Generalization of Neural Operators via Observable Spectral Error Decomposition

author.name: Hang-Cheng Dong, Pengcheng Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes a structure-preserving framework that parameterizes a learned PDE solution operator as a spectral filter over the eigenvalues of the underlying elliptic operator, using Chebyshev expansions and weak-form training. This observable spectral error decomposition makes OOD generalization of neural operators predictable and auditable rather than black-box.

entry.title: ETH-TraceBench: A Large-Scale Event-Stream Benchmark for Ethereum DeFi under Temporal, Protocol, and Contract Shift

author.name: Kemal Kirtac, Carsten Maple

entry.summary: Introduces a large-scale Ethereum DeFi benchmark covering 1.35 billion transactions (2021-2025) with a fixed 911k-instance supervised split designed to expose shortcut learning under temporal, protocol, and contract shift. Simple models like TraceStats-GB reach 0.953 macro-F1 on aggregate temporal tests, highlighting how public symbols create ML shortcuts.

entry.title: PROSE: A Theory of Optimal Stopping with Perishable Evidence for Peer Selection in Intermittently Connected Decentralised Learning

author.name: Christos Anagnostopoulos

entry.summary: The paper develops a self-contained theory of optimal stopping for peer selection in decentralized federated learning over intermittently connected mobile systems, where evidence about a peer is perishable because links expire and peer models drift. It formalizes within-contact decisions as finite-horizon Markov optimal-stopping problems with costly information acquisition and an outside option, proving the optimal policy has a particular structure. This addresses an underexplored aspect of serverless federated learning.

entry.title: GLR-MM: Graph-Based Global-Local Reconstruction for Robust Multimodal Chest X-ray and EHR Representation Learning under Missing Modalities

author.name: Surbhi Sharma, Nikhil Manali, Devesh Maheshwari

entry.summary: GLR-MM reconstructs missing chest X-ray and EHR embeddings for early ICU mortality prediction using complementary local cross-modal and global graph-attention branches, jointly trained with class-balanced prediction, reconstruction, and contrastive objectives. Evaluated on 9,620 MIMIC-derived ICU stays, it exploits both within-patient and clinically similar inter-patient evidence, which prior missing-modality methods ignore. Handling missing modalities is a practical necessity for clinical deployment.

entry.title: CLOOPD: Closing the Learner Loop in On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Keye Zheng, Hanyu Li, Zhan Cheng, Yuan Gao

entry.summary: CLOOPD reframes on-policy distillation as a closed loop that separates teacher-signal acquisition from student-side realization: it freezes scored batches with adaptive KL-envelope waypoints, re-forwards the student after each actor pass to measure how much of the teacher signal was realized, and allocates actor compute under a token budget. It includes deterministic multi-pass variants and budget-matched controls.

entry.title: TTSE: A Two-Track Online Self-Evolution Framework

author.name: Ruimin Pei, Yongkang Wu, Shangyi Zheng, Yaqing Zhang, Deyang Li, Jianjun Tao, Xinyu Zhang, Xiang Zhang

entry.summary: TTSE is a dual-track online self-evolution framework for LLM agents in continuously interactive environments, separating evolving knowledge into FACT (environmental facts verified through interaction evidence) and TIP (task-specific guidance), treating environmental knowledge as part of agent evolution rather than a fixed input. This aims at long-term autonomy beyond fixed task distributions.

entry.title: Credit Access is Associated with Improved Food Security in the Horn of Africa

author.name: Jordi Cerd\`a-Bautista, Vasileios Sitokonstantinou, Jos\'e Manuel Veiga L\'opez-Pe\~na, Duccio Piovani, Jos\'e Mar\'ia T\'arraga, Gustau Camps-Valls

entry.summary: This observational machine-learning study estimates the causal association between credit access and acute food insecurity in Somalia and the Horn of Africa using a harmonized 2015-2022 dataset of environmental, socioeconomic, and conflict factors. It finds credit access is associated with roughly a 2% population-level reduction in acute food insecurity, a meaningful shift given 16% average crisis prevalence.

entry.title: Corrective Forcing: Unified Post-Training for Diffusions and Flows in Generative Speech Enhancement

author.name: Qing Yao, Lijian Gao, Qirong Mao

entry.summary: CoF is a post-training paradigm that addresses the training-inference mismatch in diffusion and flow models for speech enhancement by forcing models to learn from self-generated rollouts and correct predictions under dynamic sampling schedules. It applies uniformly to both diffusion and flow generative paradigms and regularizes local evolution.

entry.title: Enhancing Transformer Representations of Symbolic ODE Expressions

author.name: Xiyue Fan, Adam Prugel-Bennett, Stuart E. Middleton

entry.summary: This work improves transformer representations of symbolic differential equations by designing embeddings suited to expression trees rather than flat sequences, preserving commutative structure. The aim is to support structured mathematical reasoning rather than purely numerical approximation or blind symbolic search.

entry.title: Exactness at Inference: A Representational Criterion for Out-of-Distribution Generalization

author.name: Filipe Marinho Rocha, In\^es Dutra, V\'itor Santos Costa, Lu\'is Paulo Reis

entry.summary: The paper argues that out-of-distribution generalization requires a representation structurally equivalent to the data-generating mechanism rather than a fitted approximation, using Tensor Logic's zero-temperature contractions as a case study equivalent to discrete logic. It derives what this criterion implies, noting the approach reaches Datalog-level exactness but needs external memory to bind novel entities.

entry.title: Learning Dynamic Neural Evidence Representations for Time-Adaptive Brain-Computer Interfaces

author.name: Beining Cao, Ziyi Zhao, Xiaowei Jiang, Daniel Leong, Yingtao Ren, Thomas Do, Yu-Cheng Fred Chang, Chin-Teng Lin

entry.summary: The paper proposes ProtoTrigger, a two-stage framework for adaptive temporal decision-making in BCIs, producing encoder representations that remain reliable under variable observation lengths rather than fixed windows. It targets the accuracy-time trade-off in EEG decoding and aims for cross-paradigm applicability across BCI tasks.

entry.title: Comparative Analysis of State-of-the-Art Foundation Models for Sleep Analysis Under Channel Reduction

author.name: Hassan Mehdi, Riku Klen, Ayse Kosal Bulbul, Suzanne Timmons, Abdulhamit Subasi, Wei Chen, Zou Zhu, Muhammad Irfan

entry.summary: This paper evaluates six sleep-staging foundation models on the MESA polysomnography dataset under three signal conditions: EEG-only, ECG-only, and EEG+ECG. The motivation is edge-cloud deployment, since ECG is available from consumer wearables while scalp EEG requires clinical equipment, making the results relevant to at-home sleep monitoring.

entry.title: Forecasting Intrathecal Tracer Enhancement from Pre-Contrast Brain MRI: Direct Regression versus Flow Matching

author.name: Qinghui Liu, Jon Andr\'e Ottesen, Thu Nguyen, Geir Ringstad, Ingrid Mossige, Siri Fl{\o}gstad Svensson, Atle Bj{\o}rnerud, Per Kristian Eide, Kyrre Eeg Emblem

entry.summary: Compares direct image-to-image regression with conditional flow matching for forecasting cerebrospinal-fluid tracer enhancement in the brain from a pre-contrast MRI, trained on 104 patients and tested on 23 held-out plus 51 external patients with normal pressure hydrocephalus. I2I removes about 60% of the error relative to copying the pre-contrast scan, with all models measured against that trivial baseline. This could eventually aid patient selection for intrathecal drug treatment.

entry.title: Connectivity-Aware Exploration of Robotic Grasp Spaces

author.name: Maksim A Kazanskii

entry.summary: Analyzes the multiscale connectivity structure of viable robotic grasps in SE(3) across objects and shows successful grasp sets exhibit heterogeneous, reproducible connectivity patterns. It introduces a connectivity-aware sampling strategy that prioritizes structural bridges, frontiers, and boundary extensions for more efficient grasp-space exploration.

entry.title: Silent Failures at the $2^{32}$ Boundary: A Technical Report on Large-Tensor Matrix Multiplication in PyTorch's Apple MPS Backend

author.name: Junichiro Niimi

entry.summary: This technical report documents a silent numerical correctness bug in PyTorch's Metal Performance Shaders (MPS) backend on Apple Silicon: batched matrix multiplication returns incorrect results (relative errors above 1) when tensors exceed the 2^32 element boundary, without any exception or warning. The author validates this across multiple PyTorch releases (2.4.1 to 2.14.0) with a systematic sweep over dtypes, memory layouts, shapes, and batch sizes, benchmarked against float64 CPU baselines. It matters because increasingly large unified-memory machines make such tensor sizes routine, and silent wrong results can corrupt training and inference unnoticed.

entry.title: Toscani-Fourier Distance on Probability Measures: Wasserstein Control, Topological Equivalence on Model Classes, and Duality

author.name: Mehrdad Mohammadi

entry.summary: Provides a rigorous theoretical study of the Toscani-Fourier family of discrepancies on probability measures, establishing the exact parameter window in which the distance is finite on Wasserstein-type spaces, plus metric, embedding, compactness, and duality structure. The work positions this cheap Fourier-side alternative against Wasserstein distances and kernel discrepancies.

entry.title: STEVE: Stabilizing Textual Gradient-Based Prompt Optimization via Error-Driven Refinement and Regularized Verification

author.name: Yifan Xu, Yixuan Li, Xinzhuo Li, Yixin Gu, Yifan Shen, Lijun Yu, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: Identifies two instability sources in textual-gradient prompt optimization: noisy gradients from already-correct examples and over-specialization to hard cases. STEVE generates gradients only from failures and treats every update as provisional, accepting it only when hard-case improvements do not cause unacceptable regression on a preservation set, showing consistent gains across ten reasoning benchmarks.

entry.title: Horizon-Aware Early Event Prediction for Tokamak Disruption Alarms

author.name: Takeshi Koshizuka, Takaharu Yaguchi

entry.summary: The authors adapt Early Event Prediction objectives, including Temporal Label Smoothing and survTLS, to tokamak disruption prediction, aligning survival-model training with finite operational warning horizons. Using Deep Survival Machines as a baseline, the work improves disruption alarm performance on fusion device data.

entry.title: Beyond Point Prediction: Artificial Representative Trees with Uncertainty

author.name: Lea L. Mairh\"ofer, Silke Szymczak, Bj\"orn-Hergen Laabs, Tuwe L\"ofstr\"om-Cavallin

entry.summary: This work combines artificial representative trees, interpretable surrogates for random forests, with Mondrian conformal predictive systems so a single tree provides point predictions, intervals, and threshold probabilities. It evaluates against several baselines across simulations, 21 benchmark datasets, and NHANES data.

entry.title: JAREX: An Acquisition Function for Multi-Objective Algorithmic Process Characterization

author.name: Xinyang Li, Kevin Stone, Ajit Vikram

entry.summary: JAREX is a Bayesian active-learning acquisition function for multi-objective pharmaceutical process characterization, replacing inefficient factorial design of experiments for resolving multivariate pass/fail boundaries. It targets defining proven acceptable ranges in Quality by Design manufacturing workflows.

entry.title: SALSA: Semi-Autonomous Literature Summarization Assistant

author.name: William Schertzer, Sonakshi Gupta, Rampi Ramprasad

entry.summary: SALSA is an open-source human-in-the-loop platform for extracting structured scientific data from multimodal literature, combining document parsing, LLMs, OCR, computer vision, figure digitization, and user-guided correction with configurable schemas and export of verified data. It automates repetitive curation while preserving expert oversight where judgment is needed.

entry.title: Deep Persona: A Psychologically Grounded Architecture and Evaluation Framework for Role-Playing Agents and Simulations

author.name: Rotem Dror, Zohar Elyoseph, Yuval Haber, Elad Refoua, Oshrat Ayalon, Adir Solomon

entry.summary: Deep Persona addresses the problem that LLM persona simulation typically relies on shallow character descriptions that fail to sustain coherent behavior over long interactions. The authors propose a psychologically grounded three-layered architecture separating observable expression, latent beliefs, and core motivational drives, governed by scripted determinism and bounded agency principles, plus a reference-free evaluation framework benchmarking dialogue naturalness against empirical human distributions. This matters for role-playing agents, social simulations, and applications where persona consistency over extended dialogues is essential.

entry.title: MIS-Bench: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs for Psychotherapeutic Interpersonal Skills Assessment

author.name: Yuhan Lu, Yi Yao, Hua Shen, Katie Aafjes-van Doorn, Zhaonan Wang

entry.summary: Introduces MIS-Bench, a benchmark of 996 psychotherapy response videos annotated across eight dimensions of Facilitative Interpersonal Skills, to test whether multimodal LLMs can perform expert-level professional assessment. Across nine MLLMs, models show only modest agreement with human experts, and the authors propose MIS-RAFT, a regression-augmented approach to narrow the gap.

entry.title: Measuring Behavioural Signatures of Large Language Models through Psychometric Profiling

author.name: Yu Sha, Junqi Tao, Dixin Zhou, Yansheng Tu, Mingyang Chen, Xiang Fan, Yang Liu, Mengquan Yang, Jie Lin, Jiahui Fu, Hua Zheng, Benwei Zhang, Zhou Kai

entry.summary: Develops a cross-linguistic psychometric profiling framework evaluating nine LLMs with seven psychological instruments, five repeated administrations each, in Chinese and English, retaining unresolved items as NA to capture response tendencies. LLMs show structured, model-specific profiles alongside a shared alignment-shaped pattern of higher prosociality and self-regulation and lower dominance and harmful tendencies.

entry.title: Constrained Decoding Eliminates Structural Failures in Small LLMs but Reveals a Scale-Dependent Semantic Gap

author.name: Akash Chavan

entry.summary: Benchmarks five small open-source LLMs (0.6B-4B) across 14 structured-output tasks under native, Outlines, and XGrammar decoding with a two-axis evaluation separating structural from semantic correctness. Constrained decoding eliminates all schema failures (to 100%) but exposes a persistent, scale-dependent semantic gap in content accuracy.

entry.title: LoopCD: Loop-wise Contrastive Decoding for Improving Reasoning in Looped Language Models

author.name: Byeongho Yu, Junhyuk So, Eunhyeok Park

entry.summary: The paper identifies loop instability in Looped Language Models, where recursive refinement of latent representations produces localized uncertain tokens tied to reasoning errors. It proposes LoopCD, an inference-time loop-wise contrastive decoding method that contrasts logits from earlier iterations with those from the final refined iteration. This exploits LoopLM internal dynamics to improve latent reasoning without retraining.

entry.title: Toward a Unified Mathematics of Concepts

author.name: Chen Shani

entry.summary: This position paper proposes an operation-based view for evaluating mathematical frameworks of concepts, identifying thirteen recurring operations (similarity, composition, generalization, grounding, and others) across cognition, psychology, and AI. It analyzes how ten frameworks, from vectors to symbols to graphs, embody distinct commitments on these operations, arguing they should be seen as partial solutions to a shared problem rather than competitors. The goal is a shared mathematical language for concepts across disciplines.

entry.title: Beyond Linear Context: Graph-Guided Evidence Navigation for Long-Novel Reasoning with a Local 9B Language Model

author.name: Wenji Fu

entry.summary: Tests whether a frozen knowledge graph can help a small local model (qwen3.5:9b, an existing open-weight model) perform long-novel reasoning by navigating evidence non-linearly rather than reading sequentially. Across thirty detective novels and 234 multiple-choice questions under nine conditions, the strongest graph route reaches 53.85% accuracy. It offers an efficiency-oriented alternative to long-context attention.

entry.title: Circuit Hypernetworks for Quantum-Augmented Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Xiaoqiang Wang, Mengyang Xiong, Jun Dai, Bang Liu

entry.summary: HyperQ adds token-conditioned quantum residual branches to a frozen masked-diffusion language model: a hypernetwork in each transformer block emits token-specific quantum circuit parameters, executes the circuit, and injects measured values via residual connections. Only the added branches are trained while the backbone stays frozen.

entry.title: Enabling Vision and Cross-Modal Learning for Multimodal Stroke Recurrence Prediction: An Interpretable Two-Step Framework

author.name: Christian Gapp, Elias Tappeiner, Martin Welk, Karl Fritscher, Stephanie Mangesius, Constantin Eisenschink, Philipp Deisl, Michael Knoflach, Astrid E. Grams, Elke R. Gizewski, Rainer Schubert

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether image pretraining on 3D CTA scans reduces modality imbalance in multimodal stroke recurrence prediction, examining how self-supervised pretraining and selective parameter freezing affect modality contributions and cross-modal behavior. It proposes an interpretable two-step framework integrating heterogeneous clinical and imaging data.

entry.title: Vision2CAD: A Visual Agent Harness for Explicit Geometry Referencing and Localization in Parametric CAD Modeling

author.name: Xi Cheng, Chenxi Zhai, Hang Cheng, Mingyu Fan, Pingfa Feng, Long Zeng

entry.summary: Vision2CAD combines VLM reasoning with deterministic CAD kernel operations to generate parametric CAD models, addressing geometry reference selection, sketch-plane local coordinates, and constraints to projected external geometry. It introduces an ID-based geometry selection interface, a local-coordinate bridge, and projected-edge localization, plus a new benchmark.

entry.title: D3GS: Depth, DINO, and RGB Diffusion Co-Guided 3D Gaussian Splatting for Sparse-View Reconstruction

author.name: Yunqi Gao, Zhanfeng Liao, Hanzhang Tu, Zhaoqi Su, Guoqing Zheng, Songtao Wang, Hongwen Zhang, Zhou Xue, Leyuan Liu, Yebin Liu

entry.summary: D3GS jointly enhances geometry and appearance for sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting by recovering high-resolution metric depth via diffusion-based completion and DPT refinement for Gaussian initialization, then adding DINO-guided view-consistent learning with RGB diffusion guidance to stabilize reconstruction in under-constrained regions.

entry.title: CrowdCue: Specialist-Cue Conditioning for Vision-Language Crowd Counting

author.name: Moshiur Farazi, Bekir Ciftler, Abdulhalim Dandoush, Reda Bendraou

entry.summary: Systematically studies whether conditioning Qwen2.5-VL-7B on auxiliary specialist signals (e.g., a P2PNet density heatmap) lifts its crowd counting beyond sub-million-parameter regressor accuracy on four standard benchmarks, comparing LoRA fine-tuning baselines and different guidance channels. Zero-shot prompting alone rarely yields parseable counts.

entry.title: QwenVLConnector: A Fast, Unified Medical VLM Chatbot for Fine-Grained Clinical Perception and Text Generation

author.name: Le Thien Phuc Nguyen, Thien Nguyen, Thanh-Huy Nguyen, Gia Minh Hoang, Anh Mai Vu, Ulas Bagci

entry.summary: Presents QwenVLConnector, a Qwen2.5-VL-based medical chatbot unifying classification, multi-label classification, textualized detection, counting, regression, and report generation under a single next-token objective, using a lightweight dense multi-layer Connector that fuses low- and high-level visual features without increasing sequence length. Aims at structured, fine-grained clinical perception in one interface.

entry.title: Semi-automated reconstruction of indoor geometry from 360-degree video for CFD-based airflow analysis in classrooms

author.name: Dhruv Gamdha, James Afful, Shambhavi Joshi, Ulrike Passe, Adarsh Krishnamurthy, Baskar Ganapathysubramanian

entry.summary: The authors present a semi-automated pipeline converting a single 360-degree room video into editable, simulation-ready geometry for computational fluid dynamics analysis of ventilation. It uses NeRF-based dense reconstruction plus text-prompted SAM 3 segmentation lifted to 3D via multi-view consensus, addressing geometry capture, object decomposition, and layout reconfiguration. A strong interdisciplinary application connecting 3D vision with building science.

entry.title: PhysReflect: Geometry and Perception Guided Diffusion for Physically-Plausible Mirror Reflections

author.name: Shuheng Ge, Hongwei Ren, Li Zhang, Xiangqian Wu

entry.summary: PhysReflect targets a persistent failure of diffusion generators: mirror reflections that violate physical laws through positional offsets, misalignment, and structural distortion. The framework directly enforces reflection-specific geometric and perceptual constraints rather than relying on latent-space reconstruction losses or synthetic data scaling. A focused, physics-grounded fix for a recognized generative failure mode.

entry.title: G6D: Geometric Learning-Free RGB-D 6D Pose Solver for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yixuan Liang (Tsinghua University), William Chen (Sapient Intelligence), Yunan Wang (Tsinghua University), Jizhou Yan (Tsinghua University), Zhao Jin (Tsinghua University), Changling Liu (Sapient Intelligence), Chuxiong Hu (Tsinghua University)

entry.summary: G6D is a learning-free, geometry-driven RGB-D 6D pose solver that generates pose hypotheses from an RGB-D observation, instance mask, camera intrinsics, and CAD model, avoiding large pretrained models. This makes zero-shot pose estimation deployable on robots with limited shared compute while retaining geometric interpretability.

entry.title: Confidence-Aware Teacher-Student Distillation for 3D Medical Segmentation

author.name: Georgios Triantafyllou, Dimitris K. Iakovidis

entry.summary: This work proposes an annotation-efficient student-teacher framework for 3D medical segmentation needing only point prompts on a single 2D slice per volume: a foundation-model teacher produces full-volume pseudo-annotations with spatial confidence scores, which are used to suppress noisy pseudo-label propagation during student training. This addresses extreme annotation sparsity.

entry.title: InterHier: Learning Interconnected Hierarchical Semantics for Open-Vocabulary Object Detection

author.name: Yeong-Jin Kim, Ho-Joong Kim, Seong-Whan Lee

entry.summary: This paper replaces fixed, hand-crafted connectors between super- and sub-category hierarchies in open-vocabulary object detection with a learnable, prepended context that globally guides interpretation of hierarchical prompts. It builds a hierarchy-aware prompt structure that better models relationships between base and novel categories. The work could improve detection generalization to unseen classes.

entry.title: Relightable 3D Avatar Reconstruction with Semantic-Adaptive Motion-Illumination Responses

author.name: Jiankuo Zhao, Xiangyu Zhu, Jijie Li, Baiqin Wang, Shukai Chen, Zhen Lei

entry.summary: SAMIRA is a 3D Gaussian avatar framework that models per-semantic-region motion and illumination responses rather than globally coupled primitives, enabling more accurate facial animation and more plausible relighting from monocular video. It assigns region-specific material and reflectance handling to facial areas. The work targets expressive, relightable head avatar reconstruction.

entry.title: Hierarchical Prompt Learning for Hyperbolic Vision-Language Models

author.name: Andro Erdelez, Pascal Mettes, Behzad Bozorgtabar

entry.summary: The paper proposes a plug-in for frozen hyperbolic vision-language models that exploits taxonomic class structure via parent prompt learners, parent-level supervision, hyperbolic entailment regularization, and parent-feedback logit fusion. Instantiated with CoOp, CoCoOp, and MaPLe, it improves few-shot adaptation across the standard 11-dataset benchmark suite.

entry.title: Spatial Action Review: A Visual Analytics Dashboard for Auditing Language-to-Action Hand-offs in Electron Microscopy

author.name: Samia Mohinta, Albert Cardona

entry.summary: The paper identifies the language-to-action hand-off failure mode in MLLM-assisted scientific image analysis, where a correct textual answer is paired with an unreliable spatial action that downstream workflows consume. It presents Spatial Action Review, a visual analytics dashboard for auditing this transition in electron microscopy workflows.

entry.title: Dynamic Thermal Gaussians: Multimodal 4D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Rongfeng Lu, Lifeng Lin, Xiaobao Wei, Quan Chen, Ming Lu, Yitian Xue, Yaoqi Sun, Yuhan Gao, Anke Xue, Chenggang Yan

entry.summary: The authors propose the first dynamic RGB-thermal 4D Gaussian splatting framework that jointly models appearance, thermal observations, and geometry over time, anchoring both modalities to a shared geometric substrate. This extends thermal reconstruction from static 3D to dynamic scenes, capturing heat transfer dynamics. Applications include military and broader thermal analysis.

entry.title: ReSTI: A Source-Grounded Audit and Repair of STI-Bench

author.name: Pengzhan Sun, Ramanathan Rajaraman, Shiu-Hong Kao, Junbin Xiao, Angela Yao

entry.summary: The authors audit the STI-Bench spatial-temporal benchmark against its official ScanNet, Waymo, and Omni6DPose sources, finding systematic coordinate-system and timestamp errors, under-specified targets, and answer-key inconsistencies. They release ReSTI, a source-backed revision reconstructing every recoverable answer under explicit target, time, coordinate system, quantity, and unit specifications. The work exposes task-level geometric failures in the original benchmark.

entry.title: Brain Metastases Segmentation for BraTS 2026 Task 1: A Multi-Architecture Comparison

author.name: Mahdi Islam, Musarrat Tabassum

entry.summary: The authors compare several segmentation approaches for brain metastases — plain nnU-Net, a Residual Encoder Large variant, region-based training, and the Primus transformer — for the BraTS-METS 2026 Task 1 challenge, using patient-grouped cross-validation to avoid leakage from longitudinal data. Primus with label-based training is their strongest model, with aggregate Dice/Normalized Surface Dice scores around 0.68-0.74 depending on tumor subregion. The work addresses the clinically important challenge of segmenting small, numerous, heterogeneous metastatic lesions.

entry.title: Anatomy-Decomposed Chest Computed Tomography (CT) Projections as Scalable Supervision for Bone Suppression in Chest Radiographs

author.name: Mrunmay Angaitkar, Piyush Kumar, Aarjav Satia, Pranav Rao, Ashish Mittal, Manoj Tadepalli, Preetham Putha

entry.summary: The authors create a digitally reconstructed radiograph framework that decomposes chest CT into bone, soft-tissue, and lung components projected separately to generate pixel-registered paired supervision for bone suppression in chest radiographs. Models trained on this synthetic data suppress bone or lung components and transfer to real radiographs, sidestepping scarce paired data.

entry.title: DeViGrasp: Robust Visual Mobile Grasping for Quadruped Manipulators under Degraded Perception

author.name: Liang Zhou, Jiaming Su, Yancong Wei, Kangkang Dong, Houde Liu

entry.summary: Introduces DeViGrasp-Bench, a benchmark for mobile grasping with quadruped manipulators under degraded vision (occlusion, mask dropout, depth noise, localization jitter) across terrains, difficulty levels, and seen/unseen objects, evaluating success, efficiency, and action smoothness. Also proposes DeViGrasp-Net, a policy targeting robustness to these degradations.

entry.title: Density-Driven Area Coverage for Nonholonomic Multi-Robot Systems with Safety Guarantee

author.name: Julian Martinez, Kooktae Lee

entry.summary: Extends density-driven optimal control to nonholonomic multi-robot systems by enforcing safety constraints directly on physical robot inputs rather than reference motions. The framework combines D2OC with a control barrier function safety filter via a feedback-linearizing look-ahead point and derives a safety margin accounting for that transformation.

entry.title: Distributed Infrastructure Sensors and Cues for Robotic Fire-Fighting and Safety System on a Lunar Base

author.name: Alexis Munguia, Eryc Rodriguez, Drake Russ, Jekan Thangavelautham

entry.summary: This paper presents a prototype emergency-response system for crewed lunar habitats that embeds intelligence in the environment itself, using ceramic QR-code plates carrying local maps, sensor limits, and hazard-response procedures, decoded by a low-power rover. It addresses the gap where suited astronauts and Earth-side radio delays cannot guarantee rapid fire or toxic-leak response.

entry.title: Embodied Snap: Octopus-Inspired Distributed Reach-and-Attach with a Speed-Limited Soft Arm

author.name: Linxin Hou, Zhihang Qin, Heyang Zou, Qirui Wu, Peiyi Wang, Muhammad Sunny Nazeer, Yongxin Guo, Cecilia Laschi

entry.summary: This paper presents an embodied snap controller for soft robotic arms with passive suction that separates slow servo-driven preloading from rapid elastic release, letting a compliant arm exceed its tendon-driven speed limit. Motivated by octopus biology, a learned policy shared across three sections selects preloads, aim, tendon slack, and release timing, optimized offline.

entry.title: A Horizon-slicing Approach to Minimum Obstacle Displacement Planning for Robot Navigation

author.name: Antony Thomas, Giulio Ferro, Fulvio Mastrogiovanni, Michela Robba, Marco Baglietto

entry.summary: The paper formalizes Minimum Obstacle Displacement Planning, proving it NP-hard for polygonal obstacles in the plane, and provides both an exact formulation generalizing prior problems and an approximate horizon-slicing algorithm with bounded suboptimality. The method finds feasible paths by moving obstacles when no collision-free path initially exists.

entry.title: Steering Through Contact: A Finite-Support Motion Model for Single-Track Center-Articulated Robots

author.name: Mohamed Dhia Ounally, Nicolas Samson, Mathis Turgeon-Roy, Veronica Vannini, Johann Laconte, Fran\c{c}ois Pomerleau

entry.summary: Proposes a finite-support quadratic (FSQ) model for single-track center-articulated vehicles that accounts for rotational resistance distributed along contact points under slip, generalizing the point-contact kinematic model. An exact reduction of the quadratic slip cost yields a compact closed-form solution for real-time prediction of lateral velocity and yaw effects. This improves trajectory planning and control for articulated field robots.

entry.title: Design and Control of a Cable-Driven Switchable Actuator with Torque/Tension Dual Modes for Exoskeletons

author.name: YuanLong Ji, Xu Liu, Xinyuan Cai, Qihan Ye, Xiangyu Xie, Ruizhe Jiang, Shuhan Xiang, Wenjing Liu, Qijun Wang, Yang Chen, Xingbang Yang

entry.summary: Presents a cable-driven switchable actuator (CDSA) for exoskeletons that rapidly switches between joint-torque and limb-traction tension modes, using a coupled movable pulley mechanism for distal tension amplification and a bidirectional ratchet for mode switching and preload, with multi-sensor estimation eliminating distal instrumentation. Dual-mode actuation expands training-scenario adaptability in wearables. A solid mechatronic contribution to rehabilitation robotics.

entry.title: Risk-Aware Motion Planning and Control under Unknown Dynamics with Hybrid Observations

author.name: Zhiquan Zhang, Melkior Ornik

entry.summary: Extends a hierarchical planning framework for systems with unknown dynamics to settings where state observations are only available in parts of the state space. Precomputes open-loop control sequences and nominal dynamics for blind regions, handling unintended exits from unobserved polytopes in a risk-aware way. A theory-driven contribution to planning under partial observability and model uncertainty.

entry.title: Toward Human-in-the-Loop Robot Failure Recovery: Bridging Communication Gaps in Human-Robot Collaboration

author.name: Promise Ekpo, Teju Vijay, Dhruv Mandalik, Tisha Jain, Arman Ibrayeva, Sunishka Sil, Stefanie A. Tellex, Angelique Taylor

entry.summary: This work introduces LD-HRI, a game, dataset, and benchmark for evaluating how robot requests for help account for differences in what human listeners know, addressing a gap in prior inverse-semantics work that assumed a single listener model. The corpus includes 446 human-written requests and 1,302 listener trials, and evaluates LLM speakers and request-selection algorithms under controlled differences in listener information. It matters because human-in-the-loop robot failure recovery depends on communication tailored to the helper's knowledge.

entry.title: Object-Centric Conditioning for Visuomotor Flow Matching

author.name: Jijie Li, Xu Yang, Junhong Zou, Chunhai Zhao, Chaoyang Zhao, Zhen Lei, Xiangyu Zhu

entry.summary: SlotFlow is an object-centric flow matching policy for visuomotor manipulation that decouples observations into semantic what-features and lightweight image-plane where-cues, addressing robustness failures of Action-to-Action flow matching under spatial out-of-distribution shifts and visual distractors. Object-aware conditioning mitigates stale historical motion priors and entangled global visual representations. This improves the robustness of an increasingly popular efficient policy class.

entry.title: From Semantic Decisions to Feasible Trajectories: Self-Evolving LLM-Guided Optimal Control for Narrow-Space Parking

author.name: Zhengbao Yao, Yuanfu Luo, Kehan Xue

entry.summary: SE-LLM-OCP combines LLM semantic reasoning with optimal control for autonomous parking in narrow, nonconvex environments: the LLM proposes sparse high-level maneuver plans that decompose the task into short-horizon trajectory optimizations, while the optimal-control module enforces vehicle dynamics and collision constraints. A self-evolving mechanism improves LLM decision quality online, avoiding feasibility issues from direct dense trajectory generation.

entry.title: Steerable and Reactive Grasping Through Modular Design with a Three-Point Interface

author.name: Andrew Nguyen, Yonghyeon Lee, Sangbae Kim

entry.summary: Proposes a modular grasping framework using a compact three-point contact interface to separate global geometric reasoning from local contact control. Contact triples are sampled from a precomputed grasp-affordance heatmap, a model-based reactive controller handles collision avoidance and tracking, and an RL policy using only proprioceptive finger states stabilizes the final grasp, enabling language-steerable and reactive dexterous grasping.

entry.title: Bridging Local and Population Causal Effects: A Proximal Instrumental Variable Approach

author.name: Zixuan Yao, Guosheng Yin

entry.summary: Develops a proximal instrumental variable framework that uses proxies for latent factors to adjust the compliance weighting in LATE and recover the population average treatment effect when treatment effects and compliance probabilities are heterogeneous and dependent. Identification is established through outcome bridges capturing latent treatment-effect heterogeneity or compliance bridges.

entry.title: CLT Features Support Manifold Steering, but Hold Only Partial Steering Signal

author.name: Anna Marbut

entry.summary: Follow-up interpretability work extending cyclical manifold steering methods to Anthropic's pre-trained CLT feature space on Gemma-2-2B, showing the day-of-the-week manifold can be steered in both activation space and CLT feature space. The finding that CLT features carry only a partial steering signal suggests MLP sublayers hold a portion of the relevant computation.

entry.title: Driving on Registers, Reasoning on Risk: Risk-Aware Occupancy for Register-Based End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jiaxing Chen, Hengduo Zou, YuKai Qin, Yiren Zhao, Lidong Yu, Bolin Gao

entry.summary: This companion paper proposes RRDrive, applying risk-aware occupancy to a register-based end-to-end driving baseline, using globally structured dense representations to guide multimodal trajectory generation and candidate-conditioned risk queries for selection. It reports that on the baseline, bad/poor candidates comprise 19.74% of the set and the oracle-best ranks only 33.9th on average, and contributes the RiskOcc4D-NAVS dataset. It extends the risk-occupancy idea with a new dataset.

entry.title: EnSol: an environment-aware graph neural network for molecular solubility prediction

author.name: Thao Nguyen, Saman Shafaei, Zhengyi Zhang, Huimin Zhao, Heng Ji

entry.summary: EnSol is an environment-aware probabilistic graph neural network for molecular solubility that explicitly models solute-solvent interactions, continuous temperature effects, and experimental uncertainty, overcoming fixed-solvent assumptions of prior models. It targets reaction feasibility, formulation, and solvent selection use cases in chemistry.

entry.title: Balanced Prompt Adaptation against Entropy-Induced Collapse for Test-Time Binary Segmentation

author.name: Zhengshan Wang, Joshua Charles Webster-Ford, Yifei Tian, Xinxin Wang, Long Chen, Weiping Ding

entry.summary: This paper theoretically characterizes entropy-minimization collapse in imbalanced binary segmentation, where the majority predicted class dominates test-time adaptation updates and produces degenerate masks. It proposes BAPA, combining class-balanced anchor selection with equalized loss weighting between foreground and background to stabilize adaptation.

entry.title: Can Coding Agents Reproduce Official Statistics? Metadata, Retry Budget and the Limits of Execution Feedback in a Controlled Eurostat Benchmark

author.name: Sabina-Cristiana Necula

entry.summary: This controlled benchmark of 30 Eurostat tasks tests whether authoritative metadata and execution feedback improve a coding agent's ability to reproduce official statistics, comparing task-only, metadata-card, repair-loop, and no-diagnostics conditions. It uses an existing frontier model and finds execution feedback contributes less than expected, distinguishing successful execution from valid statistical results.

entry.title: Statistical Inference for Adversarial Training: Central Limit Theorems via Optimal Transport

author.name: Kim Jakwang, Kwon Dohyun

entry.summary: The paper establishes central limit theorems for adversarial training classifiers by proving statistical properties of empirical optimal partial transport, including CLTs centered at expected empirical and population values with smoothing. Proofs rely on uniqueness of optimal potentials, shown for binary settings via multi-marginal optimal transport connections and empirical process theory.

entry.title: TWIG: A Time-Causal Wavelet Operator for Autoregressive Forecasting on Irregular Graphs

author.name: Subashree Venkatasubramanian, David A. Barajas-Solano, Chuyang Liu, Daniel M. Tartakovsky, Dipankar Dwivedi

entry.summary: TWIG is a causal-by-construction graph neural operator that transforms node histories into multiscale temporal features separating recent variation from slower memory components, then propagates them through graph-wavelet blocks with gated channel mixing for closed-loop autoregressive forecasting. It is evaluated on three irregular-domain problems including subsurface hydrology and aerodynamic flow with graphs up to substantial size.

entry.title: A Hybrid Attention Model Learning Unified Time-aware Patch Representation for Irregular Multivariate Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Zhihao Lin, Li Lin, Qi Zhang, Kaiwen Xia, Shuai Wang, Jialin Qiao

entry.summary: Proposes a hybrid attention architecture for forecasting irregular multivariate time series, addressing shortcomings of time series foundation models that rely on imputation or index-based positional encodings. Learns unified time-aware patch representations that respect continuous time and asynchronous sampling across variables.

entry.title: AirGC-CD: Gaussian-Circulant Precoding for Exactly Debiasable PAPR Reduction in Over-the-Air Federated Learning

author.name: Jonggyu Jang, Hyeonsu Lyu, Hyun Jong Yang

entry.summary: Tackles the peak-to-average power ratio problem in over-the-air federated learning with Gaussian-circulant precoding that reduces PAPR while keeping the induced clipping bias exactly removable at the receiver, plus compression to cut channel uses. Enables large-model OTA training under realistic amplifier constraints.

entry.title: Rethinking Class Imbalance for Single-Cell Foundation Models: A Systematic Benchmark Across Architectures and Long-Tail Loss Functions

author.name: Zeyu Dong, Jiahui Zhong

entry.summary: Systematically benchmarks six long-tail loss functions across three single-cell foundation model architectures (scGPT, scBERT, Geneformer) and three datasets over 162 controlled runs. Shows that high aggregate accuracy (up to 97.5%) masks systematic failures on rare, disease-relevant cell populations that long-tail losses are assumed to fix.

entry.title: Decoupled Causal Discovery

author.name: Zhengkang Guan, Fei Wu, Kun Kuang

entry.summary: Proposes DCD, which identifies the Markov boundary by decoupling non-target variables with weighting functions so only boundary variables keep dependence with the target, then iteratively builds the CPDAG from structural asymmetries. This avoids reliance on conditional independence tests, structure scores, or restrictive functional assumptions, with supporting theoretical guarantees.

entry.title: MGRD: Compact morphology-gated residual diffusion for variance-aware cross-domain neurite forecasting

author.name: Tsung Yeh Hsieh, Cosmin Anitescu, Chunghwan Kim, Victoria A. Webster-Wood, Yongjie Jessica Zhang

entry.summary: MGRD is a compact stochastic surrogate that forecasts twenty future neurite-morphology frames from ten observed frames, conditioning on morphology features, and unlike deterministic predecessors such as gated spatiotemporal attention models it represents variability among plausible futures. It reduces trajectory error on controlled phase-field trajectories and supports cross-domain neurite forecasting. Long-horizon morphology forecasting can substantially reduce the burden of time-lapse live imaging.

entry.title: Graph Learning for Cross-Subject, Cross-Population EEG Emotion Decoding and Model-Derived Spatial-Spectral Neural Signatures

author.name: Dongyi He, Bin Jiang, Xiangkai Wang, Yun Zhao, Hongjie Yan, Wai Ting Siok, Nizhuan Wang
