entry.summary: Proposes SAGE, an optimal-stopping peer selector for decentralised federated learning under a one-model-bearing-exchange budget, where a receiver scores candidate neighbors on receiver-owned anchor evidence and selects once an advantage is certified, otherwise falling back to random gossip. Provides theoretical guarantees that the stopping problem admits a finite-stage optimal rule and order-optimal anchor scheduling.

entry.title: The Bairong System for MLC-SLM 2026: Dynamic Question-Aware Evidence Routing for Multilingual Conversational Speech Understanding

author.name: Shangkun Huang, Junchao Hu, Huan Shen, Guoji Wang, Yingao Wang, Shaosai Li, Wei Zou, Yunzhang Chen

entry.summary: The Bairong system for the MLC-SLM 2026 challenge couples a diarization-ASR front-end with a dynamic evidence router that infers the required evidence type and context scope from each question, selecting among full transcript context, local audio-text fusion, speaker-linked evidence, and compact global acoustic samples. The transcript-backbone design preserves discourse context while exploiting sparse acoustic cues.

entry.title: Bridging Static and Agentic RAG for Taiwanese Historical Question Answering

author.name: Kai-Hsin Chen, Wei-Yu Chen, Xuanjun Chen, Jyh-Shing Roger Jang

entry.summary: Conducts a controlled comparison of agentic versus static RAG for Taiwanese historical QA under a shared generator and hybrid retrieval backend, finding similar aggregate performance despite the two pipelines differing on 70.83% of questions. An oracle selecting the better response per question substantially outperforms either pipeline, revealing headroom for question-level routing.

entry.title: When Evidence Conflicts: Reliability-aware Meta-review Generation

author.name: Xinzhe Wang, Fei Tao, Jiang Xie, Hong Yu, Ye Wang

entry.summary: Frames meta-review generation as reliability-aware evidence aggregation: extracting aspect-level opinions from peer reviews, identifying conflicts, estimating opinion support and review quality, and weighting evidence accordingly. Addresses the weakness of uniform aggregation in standard multi-document summarization approaches.

entry.title: Dual-Interest Sequential Product Recommendation With Multi-Granular SSM

author.name: Shuiying Liao, P. Y. Mok

entry.summary: DSRec is a dual-interest cross-SSM model for sequential recommendation that disentangles item roles (polysemy) depending on user context and captures dynamic behavior across multiple temporal granularities. It leverages state space models for efficient long-range modeling where transformer-based recommenders are cost-prohibitive.

entry.title: Trustworthy FinAInce: Unpacking How AI-Mediated Financial Advice is Judged

author.name: Aryan Ramchandra Kapadia, Eshwar Chandrasekharan, Koustuv Saha

entry.summary: A randomized vignette experiment with 285 US adults varies advice source labels (AI, expert, online community) across eight financial decisions while holding recommendations constant, measuring how source style and decision context shape trust, safety, and quality judgments. Appraisals explain a large fraction of downstream judgment variance.

entry.title: From Code Archival to Knowledge Graph: Bridging Software Heritage, COAR Notify and Wikidata

author.name: Camillo Carlo Pellizzari di San Girolamo, Francesco Tosoni

entry.summary: This paper presents a pipeline linking scholarly publications to their archived source code by harvesting editorially verified paper-repository pairs from software-focused venues (JOSS, SoftwareX, IPOL, SIGMOD ARI), yielding 4,397 curated DOI-repository pairs. It models these links in the Linked Open Data cloud via Software Heritage, COAR Notify, and Wikidata.

entry.title: ZoAQ: Adaptive Zeroth-Order Querying via Query-Reuse Coupling

author.name: Yangyang Feng, Yao Shu

entry.summary: ZoAQ is an adaptive zeroth-order optimization method that reuses past function evaluations both for the next gradient update and for deciding whether more queries are needed, avoiding the extra validation queries typical adaptive controllers require. The paper provides analysis of when evaluation agreement indicates a descent-supporting update and shows gains on synthetic objectives and further tasks.

entry.title: Helix-FNO: Spectral-Domain Operator Learning Coupled with a High-Fidelity Mechanistic Model for Fast Surrogate Simulation

author.name: Jiabao Zhao, Chuwei Wang, Jinxi Yang

entry.summary: Helix-FNO is a teacher-student surrogate architecture pairing a thirty-two-state mechanistic water-treatment simulation model with a Fourier neural operator student, enabling fast forward evaluations at a 5-minute decision cadence while generalizing across influent profiles, control settings, and plant layouts. The mechanistic teacher supplies high-fidelity training data mapping input fields to solution trajectories.

entry.title: From Latent Biomarkers to Clinical Rules: Embedding-Guided Rule Mining and Attribution-Based Translation for Interpretable Tabular Learning

author.name: Majid Lotfian Delouee, Hamed Ayoobi, Sjors G. J. G. In 't Veld, Martijn C. Schut

entry.summary: The paper presents a four-step pipeline that mines interpretable decision rules in the latent space of an FT-Transformer and translates them back into measurable clinical features, treating consistently separating embedding dimensions as latent biomarkers. Rules are extracted with small decision trees and translated using gradient-input saliency and CLS attention attribution, evaluated on six public clinical datasets.

entry.title: Role-Aware Morgan Fingerprints for Reaction Yield Prediction

author.name: Chinmay Mirji, Prashant Shekhar, Foram Madiyar, Hao Peng

entry.summary: This paper proposes MFP, a reaction yield prediction method based on role-aware Morgan fingerprints, computing count-based circular fingerprints per reaction component and aggregating them by chemical role (reactant, reagent, product) with transformation-sensitive difference features. It aims to avoid the heavy preprocessing and formatting fragility of graph neural network and Transformer approaches, speeding condition screening in synthetic chemistry.

entry.title: CALM: A Calibrated LLM Choice Network Framework for Activity-Based Traveler Simulation

author.name: Yezhou Cheng

entry.summary: CALM is a hybrid framework combining an optional LLM activity planner with calibrated stochastic choice models, network feedback, memory/habit mechanisms, feasibility checks, and deterministic replay for traveler-day simulation. Evaluated on the 2024 NYC Citywide Mobility Survey, training-only alternative-specific constant calibration cuts holdout mode Jensen-Shannon divergence from 0.156 to 0.004.

entry.title: The Role of Coordinates in Pareto Regret for Adversarial Multi-Objective Bandits

author.name: Changkun Guan, Mengfan Xu

entry.summary: Studies adversarial multi-objective bandits where reward is a multidimensional vector and performance is measured by Pareto regret. Shows a negative result: when the learner does not know which coordinate is easier, smaller cumulative loss on a coordinate does not improve worst-case Pareto regret order.

entry.title: Neural Residual Modeling for Scientific Data Compression under Guaranteed Error Bounds

author.name: Surya Majumder, Liangji Zhu, Sanjay Ranka, Anand Rangarajan

entry.summary: Proposes a post-processing pipeline that augments RVQ-based scientific data compressors with a U-Net trained to predict and correct pixel-space residuals, exploiting the finding that such residuals are spatially structured. The approach targets error-bounded lossy compression of simulation data.

entry.title: A Patient World Model for Early Forecasting of Digital Health Campaign Outcomes: Capabilities and Limits

author.name: Yunlong Wang

entry.summary: Reframes in-flight forecasting of DTC health campaign outcomes as a dynamic-system problem with a compact patient world model that maintains per-patient latent states and learns exposure-conditioned dynamics with a weekly conversion hazard. On a 147k-patient US campaign dataset it forecasts remaining new-to-brand prescription volume through week 52 with 2.9% relative error, while honestly documenting limits.

entry.title: Tail-Weight Control and Localized Generalization in Nearly Low-Rank Adversarial Classification

author.name: Kunyu Wang, Dehan Wang, Wenjun Chen

entry.summary: Proves that in a Gaussian linear classification model with a low-dimensional informative subspace and independent noise tail, a principal-space witness with risk below one half forces every near-optimal predictor to have small tail weight under Euclidean adversarial perturbations. Boundary normalization removes attack-penalty terms, yielding localized finite-sample generalization guarantees governed by principal dimension and tail energy.

entry.title: Collaborative Streaming Anomaly Detection with Interactive Explanations and Ensemble Consensus

author.name: Diogo Risca, Afonso Louren\c{c}o, Ricardo Martins, Goreti Marreiros

entry.summary: The paper presents a streaming anomaly detection system that integrates human analysts into the decision loop, combining heterogeneous detectors via a normalization-based weighted consensus with surrogate models exposing human-readable conditions behind anomaly scores. Analysts can review episodes, adjust consensus behavior, and refine surrogate rules, producing a human-adjusted ensemble. It emphasizes the often-neglected human-in-the-loop and interpretability dimensions of operational anomaly detection.

entry.title: High-Dimensional Online Change Point Detection with Adaptive Thresholding and Interpretability

author.name: Sven Jacob, Bardh Prenkaj, Weijia Shao, Gjergji Kasneci

entry.summary: The paper introduces a change point detection framework that uses the Sliced Wasserstein distance to compress multivariate sequential data into one-dimensional scores compatible with existing CPD methods, improving scalability in high-dimensional settings with adaptive thresholding and interpretability of detected changes. Applications span activity recognition, finance, cybersecurity, manufacturing, and autonomous systems.

entry.title: MUSE: Dependency-Aware Adaptation of a Frozen Vision Backbone for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Xinying Cai, Junkai Lu, Yuhan Zhu, Xiaoyun Yu, Xiangfei Qiu, Jilin Hu

entry.summary: MUSE adapts a fully frozen pretrained masked-autoencoder vision model for multivariate time-series forecasting, with a Variable Context Refinement Module that models cross-variable dependencies while preserving independent visual representation spaces. It addresses the mismatch between natural-image priors and temporal semantics of time-series images.

entry.title: Intelligent Degradation Monitoring in Lithium-ion Batteries via Discharge Incremental Capacity Feature Estimation

author.name: Amir Madmolilvand, Farzaneh Abdollahi

entry.summary: The paper proposes a neural network framework that predicts discharge incremental capacity features directly from charging signals, removing the need for slow low-current discharge cycling in battery degradation monitoring. Trained on 53 cells under diverse fast-charging protocols, the model generalizes across conditions. It is a practical advance for real-time battery management in EVs and storage systems.

entry.title: Reconstructed holograms and explanation-aware evaluation for low-cost computational pollen analysis in veterinary cytology

author.name: Swarn Warshaneyan, Joial Danyal, Bla\v{z} Cugmas, Mindaugas Tamo\v{s}i\=unas, Edgars Kviesis-Kipge, Kirishanth Manivannan, Roberts Kadi\c{k}is

entry.summary: Evaluates whether lens-less digital holographic microscopy can substitute for costlier brightfield microscopy in automated veterinary pollen analysis, comparing raw, back-propagation, and iterative phase-retrieval holograms with YOLOv26s detection and MobileNetV4 classification. It also assesses six attribution methods under an AHIR protocol testing explanation reliability under modality change and weak noise.

entry.title: Auditing Bayesian Graph Alignment: Diagnostic Comparisons and Reference Failure

author.name: Melika Gorgi, Kourosh Mirsohi

entry.summary: Audits the gap between convergence of alignment-score traces and accurate correspondence marginals in Bayesian graph alignment, comparing three samplers and five diagnostic families across 240 new exact graph pairs and larger pairs with 20-100 vertices. Findings show marginal disagreement improves error discrimination for the exact informed sampler, but no diagnostic dominates across samplers and endpoints.

entry.title: PACE: Plug-and-Play Contextual Embedding for Feature Screening with Pretrained Tabular Foundation Models

author.name: Qi Qin, Erbo Li, Ting Wei, Zizhou Huang, Zixuan Qin, Wu Wang, Yifan Sun

entry.summary: Introduces PACE, which inserts a frozen tabular foundation model column encoder before an existing feature-scoring rule to expand each feature into higher-dimensional contextual representations, improving screening of nonlinear and distributional structure. Shows downstream gains on TALENT datasets, including a 0.077 binary AUC improvement, at modest encoding cost.

entry.title: AI-inferred expressed well-being and collective-action discourse in climate-change campaigns on X

author.name: Wentao Xu

entry.summary: This study analyzes 364,118 posts across four climate campaign events over 19 occurrence-years, using a weighted lexical model to measure happiness, hope, collective capability, distress, and action language relative to 30-day pre-event baselines. It finds substantially elevated happiness during campaign periods and probes whether positive affect aligns with mobilization language.

entry.title: DIPLOMAT: Dialogue-Span-Aware Direct Preference Optimization for Polite Persuasive Workplace Negotiation Dialogues

author.name: Bibhuti Jha, Rishikant Chigrupaatii, Priyanshu Priya, Asif Ekbal

entry.summary: DIPLOMAT is a dialogue system targeting polite, persuasive workplace negotiation, balancing task goals, relationship preservation, and constructive conflict resolution. The authors contribute PROWESS, a new dataset of multi-turn workplace negotiation dialogues, and apply dialogue-span-aware direct preference optimization to train the system. The work matters because it extends DPO beyond single-turn preferences to longer dialogue spans and addresses an underexplored applied area of socially aware negotiation dialogue.

entry.title: Cross-Dialect NER for Bangla Regional Dialects Using Leave-One-Dialect-Out Cross-Validation and Explainable AI

author.name: Shamim Rahim Refat, Faika Fairuj Preotee, Shuvashis Sarker, Shifat Islam, Bidyarthi Paul, Mohammad Ashraful Hoque

entry.summary: Presents a cross-dialect Bangla NER framework on the ANCHOLIK-NER dataset (17,405 sentences, 101,817 tokens across five regional dialects), using Leave-One-Dialect-Out Cross-Validation to test generalization to unseen dialects and explainable AI techniques to analyze model behavior.

entry.title: Diagnose, Then Repair: A Two-Stage MQM-Guided Post-Editing Framework for Domain-Specific Machine Translation

author.name: Ji Hun Wang, Siyu Wu

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage framework that converts LLM-based MQM translation evaluation into targeted repairs: a retrieval-augmented evaluator produces span-level diagnoses under an explicit edit contract, and a separate post-editor applies minimal edits restricted to those diagnoses. Experiments across seven LLMs from three providers show improved controllability and less paraphrastic drift than one-stage judge-and-refine baselines.

entry.title: ChemCLIR-Bench: Benchmarking Cross-Lingual Information Retrieval in Multilingual Chemical Patents

author.name: Mahdi Astaraki, Mohammad Khodadad, Reza Namazi, Mohammad Arshi Saloot, Amir Reza Behzad Moghadam, Hamidreza Mahyar, Soheila Samiee

entry.summary: Introduces ChemCLIR-Bench, a multilingual cross-lingual retrieval benchmark built from Google Patents and EPO data across five languages in the chemical domain, designed to expose retrieval-depth and recoverability failures that aggregate recall metrics hide. The paper systematically evaluates eight retrieval approaches on this industrial-documentation setting.

entry.title: Perplexity Predicts Protection: Choosing Pretrained Backbones for Worst-Client Fairness in Federated Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning

author.name: Kiran Naseer, Samreen Azhar, Umar Shoaib, Haroon Mahmood, Muhammad Awais

entry.summary: Across 313 federated LoRA fine-tuning experiments on three text-classification datasets and three backbones, the authors show that lower per-word perplexity on target text predicts which pretrained backbone best serves the worst-off client before training starts. This offers a cheap pre-training-time signal for worst-client fairness in federated learning.

entry.title: From Articles to Publishers: Aggregating Language Model Predictions for News Source Reliability Inference

author.name: John Bianchi, Manuel Pratelli, Fabio Pinelli, Marinella Petrocchi

entry.summary: This work reformulates news reliability assessment as a source-level prediction problem, using a two-stage framework where transformer language models estimate per-article reliability and aggregate these predictions to infer the reliability of previously unseen publishers. This mirrors how expert organizations evaluate outlets rather than individual articles. The approach enables reliability inference for publishers not seen during training.

entry.title: Tutoring Large Language Models to be Domain-adaptive, Precise and Safe

author.name: Somnath Banerjee

entry.summary: A thesis proposing a responsible-intelligence framework spanning three areas: domain adaptation via active learning and graph-based knowledge to reduce hallucination, decoding-time alignment that blocks harmful generation in real time, and language-specific steering for cultural and multilingual safety. It serves as a blueprint for contextually knowledgeable, ethically sound LLMs.

entry.title: Beyond the Survey: A Systematic Empirical Study of Detection and Association in Visual MOT

author.name: Linh Van Ma, Juhua Hu, Wei Cheng, Unse Fatima, Moongu Jeon

entry.summary: This work provides a rigorous experimental evaluation of state-of-the-art multi-object tracking algorithms, quantifying the separate contributions of detection and association components to overall performance, with a unified pipeline diagram spanning tracking-by-detection and end-to-end branches. It aims to give practical guidance for method selection and system design.

entry.title: DOA-SORT: Directional Occlusion-Aware Multi-Object Tracking with Distributional Observations

author.name: Hao Wang

entry.summary: DOA-SORT is an online, training-free multi-object tracker that models occlusion directionally rather than as a scalar penalty, inferring front-back ordering and directional occlusion coverage/depth, then constructing a mixture of clean and four directionally occluded observation distributions for identity association.

entry.title: LINGO: Latent Initialization and Gradient Optimization for Sparse-view X-ray Novel View Synthesis and CT Reconstruction with 3D Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Lifeng Xing, Dequan Jin, Kunpeng Bu, Peigeng He, Shihui Ying

entry.summary: LINGO addresses noisy initialization, positional insensitivity, and weak gradients in low-density regions when applying 3D Gaussian Splatting to sparse-view X-ray novel view synthesis and CT reconstruction. It combines latent mask-space initialization with dynamic gradient optimization, building voxel-level 3D filters from X-ray masks.

entry.title: HDMamba-YOLO: Efficient State-Space Perception and Local Spatial Reconstruction for UAV Small Object

author.name: Linduo Wei, Junjie Fan, Yijun Mai, Yong Qi

entry.summary: Proposes HDMamba-YOLO, a stage-wise hybrid SSM-CNN detector for small-object detection in UAV imagery, organizing long-range state-space contextual perception with explicit local 2D spatial reconstruction according to a perception-reconstruction-alignment-interaction rationale. Targets weak visual evidence, dense distributions, and complex backgrounds in aerial imagery.

entry.title: Vision-Wireless Fusion for Multi-User Localization: A Cross-Modal Transformer Approach

author.name: Can Zheng, Jiguang He, Guofa Cai, Henk Wymeersch, Merouane Debbah

entry.summary: The authors propose a cross-modal transformer that fuses pilot-indexed channel state information (CSI) from wireless signals with visual observations for multi-user localization in urban environments. Cross-attention retrieves user-specific information from a spatial visual memory while self-attention among CSI tokens captures inter-user interactions. The work is relevant to 6G sensing and autonomous systems but is a specialized fusion architecture contribution.

entry.title: Detecting Phone-Induced Pedestrian Distraction via a Multimodal Fusion Transformer

author.name: Yuanzhe Li, Hounian Liu, Xiaotong Chang, Yidi Huang

entry.summary: The paper presents a multimodal fusion Transformer (MFT) that detects pedestrians distracted by phone use, combining skeletal dynamics from body pose keypoints with visual appearance features from images. Reliable detection of such distraction supports autonomous vehicle situational awareness, risk assessment, and safe motion planning. The work addresses a real and growing safety problem in traffic scenarios.

entry.title: Beyond UV Mapping: Mesh Texture Compression via Surface-Aligned Texture Fields

author.name: Jianqiang Wang, Junhui Hou, Siyu Ren, Weiyao Lin, Wenping Wang

entry.summary: TexF replaces 2D UV-atlas-based mesh texture compression with surface-aligned texture fields organized in sparse voxels on the mesh surface, reusing existing 3D attribute codecs and enabling GPU-resident compression via a 3D neural texture codec (3DNTC) with quantized hash features. This improves coding efficiency and supports direct surface queries.

entry.title: DFD-Lab: A Modular Audio-Visual Deepfake Detection Pipeline

author.name: Jan Rybarczyk, Mateusz Roszkowski, Jacek Komorowski

entry.summary: DFD-Lab is a modular pipeline for comparing audio-visual deepfake detectors, integrating Xception-based logit fusion, ResNet-LSTM fusion, and an AVFF reimplementation under shared training and evaluation workflows. Experiments on a filtered Deepfake-Eval-2024 subset reveal poor cross-dataset generalization, with JPEG augmentation training substantially raising baseline AUROCs.

entry.title: Lightweight Pedestrian Head-Orientation Recognition Network for Safe Pedestrian-Vehicle Interaction

author.name: Yuanzhe Li, Yidi Huang, Xiaotong Chang, Hounian Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces LRHO-CNN, a lightweight network for recognizing pedestrian head orientation from low-resolution traffic images, along with a new dataset of head images extracted from public datasets and manually annotated into eight orientation classes. Head orientation provides cues for anticipating pedestrian crossing behavior in autonomous driving. Systematic preprocessing and augmentation improve reliability in real-world scenes.

entry.title: Can Spiking Neural Networks play pinball? A neuromorphic motion detector for target tracking

author.name: Mazdak Fatahi, \v{S}\'arka Pryjmakov\'a, Pierre Boulet, Giulia D'Angelo

entry.summary: The paper presents a fully spiking, real-time perception-to-action pipeline for closed-loop pinball gameplay, using a dynamic vision sensor and spiking neural networks for low-latency target tracking under strict energy constraints. Pinball serves as a controlled dynamic testbed requiring precise motion estimation and fast reaction.

entry.title: FedMust: Semi-supervised Multi-task Student-Teacher Federated Learning for Multi-organ CT Segmentation

author.name: Ashkan Moradi, Bendik Skarre Abrahamsen, Mattijs Elschot

entry.summary: FedMust is a semi-supervised federated learning framework combining student-teacher training with multi-task learning for multi-organ CT segmentation, leveraging both labeled and unlabeled data across institutions while respecting privacy constraints. It addresses the realistic scenario where sites have labels for only a small portion of local data. The flexible design aims to improve segmentation without sharing patient data.

entry.title: CIG-MAE: Cross-Modal Information-Guided Masked Autoencoder for Self-Supervised WiFi Sensing

author.name: Gang Liu, Yanling Hao, Yixuan Zou

entry.summary: CIG-MAE is a cross-modal information-guided masked autoencoder for self-supervised human action recognition from WiFi channel state information, avoiding augmentation-based contrastive schemes that conflict with radio signal semantics. It addresses annotation cost and limited CSI dataset scale through masked reconstruction guided by cross-modal information.

entry.title: SHAFT: A Slack-Compensating, Helical-Buckling-Attenuating Flexible-Shaft Transmission for Lightweight Multi-DoF Manipulation

author.name: Tomoya Takahashi, Moses Gladson Selvamuthu, Richiro Tadakuma, Kazutoshi Tanaka

entry.summary: Proposes SHAFT, a flexible-shaft transmission design for lightweight, slim manipulators that compensates for slack and attenuates helical buckling, which otherwise causes increasing angular transmission error at joint bending. The design targets proximal actuation setups that relocate motors near the base to reduce inertia.

entry.title: MIRA-PRM: Mission-Informed Reusable Roadmap Planning for Mobile Gas-Sensing Inspection

author.name: Gongsen Wang, Siyuan Wang, Xinyuan Wang, Yuhan Wen, Feng Yang, Zhen Tian, Hoi Leong Lee

entry.summary: MIRA-PRM is a mission-informed probabilistic roadmap planner for mobile gas-sensing inspection that combines geometry-, mission-flow-, and inspection-conditioned sampling with adaptive connectivity and evidence-gated refinement. Across 142,448 planner runs it maintained 100% success as ordered targets grew to eight and reached 97.67% success under a 40-node budget versus 67.17% for standard PRM.

entry.title: GraspTune: Tactile-Driven Execution Refinement for Robust Grasping

author.name: Juntao Li, Xingke Xia, Sichao Liu, Daqiang Guo

entry.summary: GraspTune refines visual grasp proposals at execution time using tactile-driven bounded residual tool-center-point motions during approach, contact formation, and final grasp, learning contact semantics from depth, tactile signals, state, and history with multi-task supervision. A diffusion-pretrained residual policy aligned with PPO provides closed-loop execution refinement. This targets the underexplored gap between selecting a grasp proposal and physically realizing a stable grasp.

entry.title: Range-Aided SLAM Initialization Exploiting Accurate Heading Information

author.name: Isabel Lougheed, James Richard Forbes

entry.summary: This paper presents a two-step initialization method for range-aided SLAM that exploits highly accurate heading information, typical of AUV navigation, to solve for range transponder and robot positions linearly. It uses a generalized trust region subproblem to solve transponder positions relative to the AUV from nonlinear range measurements, then recovers the full initialization.

entry.title: Riemannian Density-Driven Optimal Control: Tangent-Space LQR for Second-Order Multi-Agent Systems on Curved Manifolds

author.name: Kooktae Lee, Ruchika Singh

entry.summary: Extends Density-Driven Optimal Control to second-order multi-agent systems on Riemannian manifolds, constructing local distribution objectives in tangent spaces via logarithmic maps and using weighted centers as references for finite-horizon LQR. Establishes theoretical guarantees and executes control through intrinsic dynamics with parallel transport in a receding-horizon scheme.

entry.title: Import AI 473: The US's superintelligence strategy; human brain in a mouse skull; and machine hermeneutics

author.name: Jack Clark

entry.summary: Jack Clark's newsletter covers a lengthy RAND paper arguing the US should pursue a Freedom of Action strategy toward superintelligence — investing in AI safety, human-AI ecosystems, AI-security architecture, and benefit-sharing — plus other research items including brain-tissue work and machine hermeneutics.

entry.title: TARGet: Topology-Aware Fusion-based Radio Frequency Circuit Functional Modeling using Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Soroosh Noorzad, Sebastian Bodero, Morteza Fayazi

entry.summary: TARGet is an open-source GNN-based modeling method for analog/RF circuits that leverages circuit topology so models generalize across topologies when components are added or removed, unlike prior ML approaches requiring per-topology retraining with flat fully connected representations. It aims to enable efficient circuit modeling for automatic RF synthesis with less training data.

entry.title: Performance-Preserving Online Adaptation in Social Navigation via Diffusion Steering

author.name: Haruto Nagahisa, Kohei Matsumoto, Yuki Hyodo, Ryo Kurazume

entry.summary: This paper adapts diffusion-based social navigation policies to deployment environments using diffusion steering via RL, training only the noise policy while keeping the diffusion policy frozen to preserve the base model's pedestrian avoidance and goal-reaching performance. This addresses the problem that simulation cannot fully capture deployment-specific dynamics and social conventions. It offers a safe online fine-tuning recipe for diffusion policies in the wild.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: Centroid-Guided Contrastive Loss for Structured Fraudulent Job Posting Detection

author.name: Syed Ali Ahmed (National University of Computer and Emerging Sciences, Karachi, Pakistan), Malaika Raza (National University of Computer and Emerging Sciences, Karachi, Pakistan), Muhammad Shoaib Siddiqui (Islamic University of Madinah, Madinah, Saudi Arabia), Muhammad Rafi (National University of Computer and Emerging Sciences, Karachi, Pakistan)

entry.summary: The paper proposes Centroid-Guided Contrastive Loss (CGCL), a loss function that unifies classification with densely formulated clustering via a centroid-driven top-k push-and-pull mechanism, applied to detecting fraudulent job postings. It aims to simultaneously achieve high accuracy and well-structured latent representations that capture subtleties among fake posts.

entry.title: PlantShade: Predicting Plant Shadows for Lighting-Aware Robotic Agricultural Operation

author.name: Longchao Da, Xiaoou Liu, Xingjian Li, Lirong Xiang, Hua Wei

entry.summary: The paper introduces a plant growth and shade dataset spanning four species (soybean, tomato, sugarbeet, strawberry) with top-down and supplementary-light viewpoints, and develops models to predict plant shadows for lighting-aware robotic agriculture. It argues shade simulation is an underexplored but important factor for crop productivity and robot operation planning.

entry.title: LE4Mob: Towards Inductive, Distance-Aware and General-Purpose Location Embedding for Human Mobility Modelling

author.name: Xinglei Wang, Stephen Law, Zichao Zeng, Junyuan Liu, Guangsheng Dong, Tao Cheng

entry.summary: LE4Mob introduces a location embedding framework for mobility modeling that is inductive (handles unseen locations), distance-aware, and derived from geography rather than mobility observations, extending contrastive language-location pre-training with a distance-preserving regularization objective. This enables reuse across datasets and mobility tasks where prior embeddings fail.

entry.title: A Comparative Framework for Evaluating Foundation Models on Tabular Data: A Case Study in Healthcare

author.name: Majid Lotfian Delouee, Sjors G. J. G. In 't Veld, Martijn C. Schut

entry.summary: The paper introduces a comparative evaluation framework that scores and ranks tabular foundation models across six clinically meaningful dimensions, including generalization to new datasets, to help clinicians and data scientists choose models for specific healthcare tasks. Unlike surveys, it structures comparison against the demands of real applications, with a healthcare case study.

entry.title: Interpretable Multi-Hypersphere Deep Anomaly Detection for Open-set Supervised Anomaly Detection

author.name: Zhiji Yang, Fangyong Wang, Yue Li, Xianli Pan, Jianhua Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes IMHD-AD, which places one hypersphere per known normal class in a shared feature space with learnable acceptance ranges and inter-class boundary constraints for multi-class open-set anomaly detection. Improves on single-hypersphere methods while yielding interpretable per-class decisions.

entry.title: Bilinear Optimization Divergence: Diagnosing Factor-Constrained LoRA Continual Learning

author.name: YongShun Wang, JianLin Su, Yong Ma

entry.summary: Formalizes Bilinear Optimization Divergence, an anchor-relative diagnostic of how effective LoRA updates respond on historical features, distinguishing shared-adapter from fresh-block cases. The analysis yields SFOR, a semi-frozen orthogonal routing scheme for shared adapters in continual learning with LoRA.

entry.title: Multivariate quantile regression via Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks

author.name: Andrew Polar, Michael Poluektov

entry.summary: The paper introduces an algorithm for predicting conditional joint distributions of vector-valued targets in stochastic systems with intrinsic randomness, using ensembles of Kolmogorov-Arnold networks as function approximators. It targets the harder setting beyond standard multivariate quantile regression, identifying regions corresponding to probability levels. KANs are used for their flexibility, though the technique is claimed not to be restricted to them.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning Inspired Black-box Adversarial Attacks for Computer Vision

author.name: Florian Krone, Elena Hoemann, Sven Hallerbach

entry.summary: The paper proposes a black-box adversarial attack for CNN and transformer vision models that uses reinforcement learning to optimize perturbations when gradients are unavailable, targeting the more realistic black-box threat model relevant to safety-critical deployments. RL-based optimization replaces white-box gradient methods requiring full model access.

entry.title: Prescriptive SVD-Inspired Attention via Spectral Energy Retention

author.name: Vasileios Arampatzakis, Vasileios Sevetlidis, George Pavlidis

entry.summary: Building on SVD-Inspired Attention (SVDA), which makes latent attention directions inspectable via spectral indicators such as effective rank and spectral entropy, this paper proposes a diagnosis-intervention-verification framework for moving from interpretability to operational intervention, evaluating spectral energy retention as one intervention on attention structure.

entry.title: Probabilistic Modelling of Operational Design Domains, A New Approach for Testing AI Systems

author.name: Hans-Werner Wiesbrock

entry.summary: The paper proposes probabilistically extended ontologies (PEONs) that describe an ML system's operational design domain augmented with a probability distribution over the induced partitioning, using marginal distributions instead of unmaintainable conditional probability tables. This enables statistically interpretable, representative test sets for systems like vehicle obstacle detection where classical bug fixing is impossible.

entry.title: Beyond the Raw Waveform: Fusing Visual Representations of EDA for Stress Detection

author.name: Stefanos Gkikas, Thomas Kassiotis, Yang Guo, Guangliang Li, Eric Nichols, Houshyar Asadi, Nikolaos Smyrnis, Giorgos Giannakakis

entry.summary: The study derives six image-based representations of electrodermal activity signals (phase spectrograms, PSD, scalograms, recurrence plots, and more) and fuses them as multichannel inputs for stress classification. It evaluates whether these complementary visual views improve recognition over raw-waveform pipelines.

entry.title: When Does Learning Beat Heuristics? A Case Study in Kubernetes Scheduler Score Plugins

author.name: Wang Xuying, Zhibek Sarypbekova

entry.summary: This case study asks whether learned scoring functions, including a random forest and a graph neural network trained on production cluster traces, can beat hand-tuned Kubernetes scheduler heuristics. It finds both models achieve only modest regression fit (R^2 about 0.042) and provides an honest analysis of why learning fails to beat heuristics on the metric that matters in production.

entry.title: Domain-decomposed Evolutional Deep Neural Network with Random Features for Transient Pressure Diffusion with Discontinuous and High-Contrast Coefficients

author.name: Peiqi Li, Jie Chen, Hui Zhang, Simon Hands

entry.summary: Develops a domain-decomposed random-feature evolutional deep neural network for transient pressure diffusion in heterogeneous porous media with discontinuous, high-contrast permeability. It separates spatial approximation from temporal evolution, compressing permeability-informed random features into an orthonormal pressure space with a conservative finite-volume operator, retaining dissipative structure with error quantification.

entry.title: The shape of quark flavors

author.name: Shinsuke Kawai, Nobuchika Okada

entry.summary: This theoretical particle physics paper constructs quark Yukawa couplings as overlap integrals of Gaussian wave functions in extra dimensions, using machine learning numerical optimization to find field configurations consistent with all current experimental constraints. The setup naturally explains the large quark mass hierarchy from localization geometry. It is an interesting demonstration of ML as an optimization tool in flavor model building.

entry.title: An LLM-Assisted AutoML Framework for Intrusion Detection in IoT Networks

author.name: Li Yang

entry.summary: Combines LLM assistance with conventional AutoML to automate ML pipeline construction for IoT intrusion detection systems, covering preprocessing, feature selection, model selection, and hyperparameter tuning. The goal is to reduce the expert burden of building effective ML-based IDS models for expanding IoT attack surfaces.

entry.title: If You Hear It, Help Find It: Orthogonal Knowledge Distillation for Open-Vocabulary Audio-Visual Event Localization

author.name: Yi Xu, Cheng Chen, Wenzhuo Lei

entry.summary: Proposes OV-OrthKD, a reliability-aware asymmetric orthogonal knowledge distillation method for open-vocabulary audio-visual event localization, deciding which teacher signals should shape localization versus remain auxiliary based on setting-specific boundary reliability. Frames the problem as supervision placement rather than a universal ranking of audio versus vision teachers.

entry.title: Fast Graph Laplacian Estimation using Effective Resistance

author.name: Christoffer Kjellson, Claudio Altafini, Emma Tegling

entry.summary: Proposes a non-iterative estimator for graph Laplacians under Laplacian constraints for Gaussian Markov random fields, using effective resistance for regularization in the underdetermined regime with fewer samples than nodes. Avoids the computationally demanding sparsity-regularized maximum-likelihood optimization of prior approaches.

entry.title: Density-Ratio Rescoring for Imbalanced Classification

author.name: Dongha Kim, Seunghwan Park

entry.summary: Proposes Density-Ratio Rescoring, which augments a classifier trained at the original class prior with a survey-raking-derived dual score that reweights majority samples to match minority feature moments, combining the two standardized scores with fixed weight. Provides theory showing the dual recovers the log density ratio under correct specification, plus class-separation analysis and tabular benchmark results.

entry.title: UniK: Universal Knowledge Perception for Digital and Physical AI

author.name: Nirmit Desai, Kunal Sawarkar, Aditya Mahakali, Dongkon Lee, Kevin Park, Eric Song

entry.summary: Proposes UniK, a unified platform serving both digital AI (enterprise agents and chatbots) and physical AI (robots learning from video and telemetry), covering the full knowledge lifecycle of ingestion, enrichment, indexing, retrieval, and continuous evaluation across heterogeneous modalities and private corpora.

entry.title: Jev-Mem: System-One-Controlled Agentic Memory for Efficient AI Agents

author.name: Dongming Jiang, Yi Li, Bingzhe Li

entry.summary: Proposes Jev-Mem, an agentic memory architecture inspired by System-One/System-Two cognition, with a lightweight System-One control plane handling memory typing and organization, a multi-relational memory plane, and a System-Two reasoning plane. The goal is to remove expensive autoregressive LLM generation from the critical path of memory operations for long-horizon agents.

entry.title: Model-Agnostic Feature Selection via LOCO-Guided Adaptive Minipatch Sampling

author.name: Xuhui Liu, Lili Zheng

entry.summary: Introduces LAMPS, a model-agnostic ensemble framework that uses any black-box regression algorithm as a base learner within a minipatch sampling scheme guided by leave-one-covariate-out signals to select features important for prediction. Requires only predictions from the base learner, avoiding model-specific or model-X assumptions.

entry.title: Functional Emotion Without Character: Large Language Models, Aristotelian Disposition, and the Limits of Behavioral Alignment

author.name: Marzieh Zare

entry.summary: A philosophical treatment modeling emotions as context-sensitive trajectories and attractor dynamics in high-dimensional representational state spaces, offering a structural alternative between behavioral equivalence and phenomenal consciousness as criteria for machine emotion. It connects mechanistic interpretability findings on emotion-concept representations to Aristotelian disposition theory and published representation-adequacy standards.

entry.title: Automatic multimodal UX improvement recommendations from LLM agent user simulations

author.name: Anu Chowdhury, Bin Wu, Hossein A. Rahmani, Emine Yilmaz

entry.summary: Formalizes UX improvement recommendation from LLM-agent user simulation data as a structured generation and ranking problem, with an evaluation protocol using expert annotation and LLM-as-a-Judge. The AMUSER framework simulates multimodal user behavior on websites and automatically produces prioritized UX improvement recommendations.

entry.title: Error-Supervised Synthetic Learner Writing for Automated Essay Scoring

author.name: Duy Anh Nguyen

entry.summary: Fine-tunes an LLM generator on error-annotated texts from grammatical error detection to produce synthetic essays containing realistic learner errors, then evaluates automated essay scoring under authentic, conventional-synthetic, and error-supervised-synthetic data conditions. A simple, targeted fix for the unrealistic-error weakness of synthetic training data.

entry.title: Efficient LLM Distillation for Bangladesh Legal Context: A Smartphone-Compatible Retrieval-Augmented Generation Model

author.name: MD. Nafis Kamal, Mahadi Hasan Fahim, Talha Ridwan, Nadifa Zaman, Fariha Roushon Florin, Farig Yousuf Sadeque, Saadat Rafid Ahmed

entry.summary: The authors compress a 9B-parameter Gemma-2 teacher into a 2B-parameter student via two-phase progressive distillation, combined with retrieval augmentation, to deliver offline-capable legal guidance on smartphones in Bangladesh. The system is deliberately scoped to statutory interpretation, excluding case-law reasoning, and is built around quality-gated training data (9,429 accepted pairs from 14,514 generated queries). The work targets the inaccessibility of English-only statutes and unreliable connectivity, where hallucinated legal text causes direct harm.

entry.title: Brain-to-Image Generation: Reconstructing Visual Stimuli from EEG using Generative Adversarial Networks

author.name: Harshit Goyal

entry.summary: The paper presents a reproducible single-subject baseline on THINGS-EEG2 for reconstructing visual stimuli from EEG, using a compact temporal-spatial convolutional encoder mapping repetition-averaged EEG to ViT-B/32 image features, with concept-disjoint validation and the official 200-image test gallery. It prioritizes the more defensible retrieval question given EEG's limited spatial resolution.

entry.title: Image Frame Dynamic Object Segmentation and Ego Motion Estimation using Radar Image Fusion

author.name: Astik Srivastava, Suhani Grover, Avinash Sharma, Madhava Krishna

entry.summary: Radar-Dot couples dynamic object segmentation and ego-motion estimation for autonomous driving by exploiting radar Doppler measurements: a linear Doppler constraint estimates ego velocity, residual-based segmentation separates static from dynamic observations, and motion plus metric depth and optical flow flags regions inconsistent with rigid scene motion.

entry.title: Blind Deconvolution of Binary and Pattern Images with Pixel Intensity Constraints and Sparse Gradient Prior

author.name: Qinghua Zhang, Xuesong Yang, Liangtian He, Liang-jian Deng, Jun Liu

entry.summary: Introduces a unified model-based framework for blind deconvolution of specialized image classes such as barcodes, text, and patterns, exploiting a previously overlooked pixel intensity constraint (pixels limited to few values) combined with a sparse gradient prior to improve blur-kernel and image recovery over natural-image-oriented methods.

entry.title: Mind the Gaps: A Curated Benchmark for Form Field Detection

author.name: Iheb Brini, Omar Moured, Hamza Gbada, Elisa Barney

entry.summary: The paper introduces mini-CommonForms, a carefully curated, high-quality benchmark for form field detection (FFD), where fields are defined by layout structure and whitespace rather than visible content. It exposes noise and inconsistency in existing heuristic-annotated datasets and evaluates state-of-the-art detection methods on the new benchmark.

entry.title: Comparative Performance and Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of DINOv2 for Active Trachoma Classification

author.name: Kibrom Gebremedhin, Hadush Hailu, Bruk Gebregziabher, Yordanos Hailu

entry.summary: This study provides a controlled comparison of six pretrained backbones and four lightweight adaptation mechanisms for binary trachoma (TF vs normal) classification on 1,546 public conjunctival images, using a standardized segmentation and cropping pipeline. It establishes the relative value of modern visual representations and parameter-efficient adaptation for trachoma grading.

entry.title: CMAMBADEPTH: Self-supervised Monocular Depth Estimation with Channel Mamba and Hybrid Attention

author.name: Xuezhi Xiang, Jiayao Liu, Heqi Xiang, Yuqi Hu, Yiming Chen, Shanjun Zhang

entry.summary: CMambaDepth is a self-supervised monocular depth estimation framework using bidirectional and unidirectional Channel Mamba modules for efficient cross-scale feature fusion and fine-grained contextual modeling, addressing the balance between local and global spatial modeling.

entry.title: Active Visual Sampling with a Connectome-Constrained Fly Model for One-Shot Hatch Recognition in Architectural Drawings

author.name: Dmitry Kuklev

entry.summary: This paper repurposes a connectome-constrained fly visual network, pretrained for motion, as a frozen descriptor for one-shot matching of hatch patterns in architectural drawings, using scan trajectories and 57 cell types. On a synthetic benchmark built on CubiCasa5K, the pipeline reaches 0.857-0.910 area-weighted accuracy, outperforming pixel statistics on an equal-brightness condition. It demonstrates neuroscientifically grounded models can be reused for unusual industrial vision tasks without task-specific training.

entry.title: Hi-Singers: A Comprehensive High-Quality Dataset for Expressive Audio-Driven Singing Head Synthesis

author.name: Yichi Zhang, Hui Zhang, Guanjun Liu, Yuefeng Zou, Fengzhao Sun, Jun Yu

entry.summary: Hi-Singers is the first large-scale, high-quality in-the-wild video dataset tailored for audio-driven singing head synthesis, with rigorous automated and manual filtering to address the domain gap between speech and singing, including exaggerated expressions and rhythmic synchronization challenges like rhythmic drift.

entry.title: Multicentre Bi-atrial Segmentation from LGE-MRI for Atrial Fibrillation with a 2D and 3D Framework

author.name: Malitha Gunawardhana, Gregory B. Sands, Mark L. Trew, Jichao Zhao

entry.summary: The paper presents a two-stage segmentation framework and benchmarking platform for bi-atrial wall and cavity delineation from multicentre LGE-MRI, systematically evaluating ROI localization, encoder design, 2D/3D dimensionality, and ensemble fusion. It targets atrial fibrillation structural analysis and future fibrosis quantification.

entry.title: Sensing to Intelligence: Principles for Neuromorphic Circuits and Systems

author.name: Saptarshi Maiti, Chetan Singh Thakur

entry.summary: A perspective arguing that neuromorphic engineering should be defined by computational principles shared with biological systems rather than by resemblance to biological components or particular devices and substrates. Surveys the field's expansion into event-based sensors, spiking processors, memristive devices, and large-scale neural accelerators.

entry.title: Prescribed-Time Contracting-Boundary Control of a Tendon-Driven Flexible Arm

author.name: Yi Lu, Chao Tang, Zhiji Han, Hongdu Wang

entry.summary: The study develops a prescribed-time performance-shaping controller for curvature tracking of a single-segment tendon-driven flexible arm, using a Cartesian curvature representation to avoid undefined bending directions and a contracting cubic performance boundary with dual error transformations. The controller guarantees boundary invariance and prescribed-time convergence.

entry.title: A Topological Representation with Object-Path Graphs for Open-Vocabulary Instance Navigation

author.name: Linwei Zheng, Daojie Peng, Bingtao Wang, Haoang Li, Jun Ma

entry.summary: This paper proposes an object-path graph that unifies open-vocabulary semantic reasoning with topological navigation, jointly supporting semantic grounding, graph-based localization, and navigation in a single lightweight framework, avoiding dependence on dense metric maps. It targets vision-language navigation where scene graph memory is usually decoupled from the navigation policy. The unified representation could make language-guided navigation more scalable.

entry.title: Estimation and Control of Tensegrity Manipulator Kinematics based on Strut Inclination Angles

author.name: Tufail Ahmad Bhat, Shuhei Ikemoto

entry.summary: The paper develops a reduced-order model for shape and posture control of tensegrity-based continuum manipulators, which are networks of rigid struts and tensioned cables not well served by continuous elastic backbone models. It models the manipulator as serially connected parallel-link mechanisms, enabling closed-loop kinematic estimation and control from strut inclination angles.

entry.title: Tensor Completion using Subspace Information

author.name: Jingyang Li, Michael K. Ng

entry.summary: Introduces TCSI, a tensor completion algorithm that incorporates side information through an estimated subspace extracted from available side data, then reformulates the tensor completion problem to exploit it. The work targets the statistical-to-computational gap in highly missing regimes under uniform sampling, with recovery guarantees.

entry.title: Virtual neural networks: hundreds of souls in a body

author.name: Petr Hurtik, Marek Vajgl, Zahra Alijani, Vojtech Molek

entry.summary: The paper introduces virtual neural networks, a framework where trainable parameter count stays fixed while scalability comes purely from computation: many virtual models share weights derived from a small set of physical models, merging siamese networks with deep ensembles. Up to hundreds of virtual networks process the same input, and their interconnected structure induces internal distortion that improves ensemble robustness. Accuracy reportedly grows with the number of virtual networks.

entry.title: Ability-Residual Decoupled Modeling for Affective Cognitive Diagnosis

author.name: Boyuan Zhao, Meng Ye

entry.summary: The paper argues that existing affective cognitive diagnosis methods wrongly assume the diagnosis backbone has fully explained cognitive effects, leaving residual errors attributable to affect. It proposes decoupling stable cognitive-structural residuals from affective factors in student response modeling. This improves the interpretability of models inferring student concept mastery from response logs.

entry.title: A Hybrid Computational Intelligence Framework for scRNA-seq Imputation: Integrating scRecover and Random Forests

author.name: Ali Anaissi, Deshao Liu, Yuanzhe Jia, Weidong Huang, Widad Alyassine, Junaid Akram

entry.summary: The authors present SCR-MF, a two-stage pipeline combining the scRecover dropout-detection method with missForest random-forest imputation for single-cell RNA-seq data. Across real and simulated datasets it matches or beats existing imputation approaches while remaining fast and interpretable for mid-scale datasets.

entry.title: 2nd Place Solution to the HANDS 2026 Workshop Challenge-Dexterous Grasp Motion Track: Single-Shot Trajectory Warping for Grasp Motion Generation

author.name: Muneeb A. Khan, Woojin Kim, Shinwoo Kim, Muhammad Munsif, Binod Bhattarai, Seungryul Baek

entry.summary: This is a competition report describing a 2nd-place solution for dexterous grasp motion generation of a 12-DoF LinkerHand O6 in the HANDS 2026 challenge at ECCV 2026. Instead of generating motions from scratch, the approach edits a single successful GraspM3 demonstration via trajectory warping to produce physically plausible reach-and-lift trajectories for unseen objects. It handles per-step compounding decisions under domain shifts in objects and dynamics.

entry.title: An Agentic Just-in-Time Adaptive Intervention System for Personalized Sleep Support: Proof-of-Concept Study with N of 1 Data

author.name: Nick Rezaee, Chelsea Boccagno

entry.summary: This proof-of-concept study uses an AI agent running in Home Assistant to review 30 days of personal sleep and behavioral data, evaluate and adapt reminders, and log decisions for human review within a just-in-time adaptive intervention framework. Initial runs demonstrated technical feasibility of agentic, personalized sleep support.

entry.title: Modelling daily activity patterns from mobile phone location data via deep representation learning

author.name: Xinglei Wang, Junyuan Liu, Guangsheng Dong, Zichao Zeng, Stephen Law, James Haworth, Tao Cheng

entry.summary: This work presents the Activity Chain Encoder (ACE), a self-supervised Transformer that combines pre-trained urban embeddings with visit timing and duration to infer activity patterns from passive mobile phone location data, treating activity mining as representation, clustering, and interpretation. It uses masked-sequence training to learn the sequential organization of stays in mixed-use urban environments.

entry.title: SolarFlowRefiner: Refinement-Aware Flow Matching for Surface Solar Radiation Downscaling

author.name: Udbhav Srivastava, Antonita Racheal, Yiheng Chen, Runlong Yu, Xinyue Ye

entry.summary: SolarFlowRefiner performs multisource downscaling of surface solar radiation by reconstructing high-resolution SolarCube fields from coarse ERA5 data and satellite channels, using a refinement-aware flow matching approach to handle the spatially sharp and ambiguous corrections caused by sunlit versus cloud-shadowed subregions. It addresses the stage-wise mismatch between one-stage generators and post-hoc refinement.

entry.title: Predictors and Orchestrators: Parsimonious Machine Learning within an Agentic AI Harness for Multi-Horizon Karst Aquifer Forecasting

author.name: Pramod Lekhak, Chetan Sharma, Hakan Ba\c{s}a\u{g}ao\u{g}lu, F. Paul Bertetti, Debaditya Chakraborty

entry.summary: A deployment-aware framework forecasts spring discharge and groundwater levels 1-12 weeks ahead for the Edwards Aquifer using about 79 years of hydroclimatic data, comparing XGBoost, Extra Trees, LSTM, CNN, and Transformer model families under a common temporal evaluation design. Simple predictive models are embedded within an agentic harness for orchestration.

entry.title: When Does Adversarial Refinement Help? A Negative Result and Open Problem in Adapting R3GAN to Time Series Imputation

author.name: Yufeng He

entry.summary: Adapts the stable modern R3GAN to multivariate time series imputation with a coarse-to-fine refinement framework and frequency-domain discriminator, auditing 14 saved configurations across 3 datasets. Reports a negative result: adversarial refinement does not revive GAN-based imputation, despite honest acknowledgment that evidence is descriptive rather than a matched causal ablation.

entry.title: Adaptive Forgetting for Nonstationary Optimization: Towards Robust EEG Decoding

author.name: Hongyu Zhu, Lin Chen, Jing Chen, Yuting Zhou, Mingsheng Shang

entry.summary: The paper targets cross-subject EEG decoding generalization by replacing the fixed second-moment decay coefficient in Adam/AdamW with an adaptive forgetting mechanism suited to nonstationary, low-SNR gradients. This addresses the mismatch between optimizer assumptions and the subject variability that degrades EEG decoder generalization.

entry.title: Artificial Structure Function Search: Preserving Artificial Functional Connectivity for Structured Pruning

author.name: Mindula Illeperuma, Rafael Pina, Charuka Herath, Sharmarke A. Gabayre, Varuna De Silva

entry.summary: ASF-S is a structured pruning framework using Principle Gradient Importance, a prune-candidate selection criterion inspired by structure-function relationships in the brain. By respecting the topographical organization of the output layer, it defines an artificial functional connectivity that pruned models should preserve, offering interpretable structural criteria over opaque heuristics.

entry.title: Quantifying Hidden Salt for Precision Healthcare: Sodium Assessment via Joint-Factor Retrieval and Chain-of-Thought Inference

author.name: Mingyu Huang, Weiqing Min, Yuehui Fang, Yuna He, Shuqiang Jiang

entry.summary: The SALT framework uses RAG with a joint-factor embedding retrieval module and chain-of-thought inference to estimate sodium content in recipes, addressing hidden salt from ambiguously described seasonings like soy sauce and ketchup. It supports dietary monitoring for hypertension and cardiovascular precision healthcare.

entry.title: A Hybrid Quantum Neural Network to Analyse Big Experimental Powder X-ray Diffraction Data

author.name: H. Dong, S. D. M. Jacques, M. Q. Hlatshwayo, E. Papoutsellis, K. Georgopoulos, A. M. Beale, A. Vamvakeros

entry.summary: Introduces a hybrid quantum neural network that extracts quantitative parameters like phase weight fractions directly from 1D powder X-ray diffraction patterns without iterative refinement. It combines noise-aware classical pre-training with QPU fine-tuning and was deployed on an IBM quantum computer for experimental diffraction computed tomography data.

entry.title: Clinical Domain Classification from Medical Transcriptions

author.name: Sravani Pottipati, Lakshmikar R. Polamreddy

entry.summary: This paper presents a comparative study of six traditional ML classifiers, BERT and XLNet transformers, and few-shot LLM prompting for classifying clinical specialties from medical transcription data under severe class imbalance. It benchmarks which approaches best serve underrepresented specialties. The contribution is empirical guidance rather than a new method.

entry.title: Bayesian Deck-of-cards-based Ordinal Regression with Sequential Preference Elicitation

author.name: Marco Grillo, Silvano Zappal\`a

entry.summary: Proposes B-DOR, a Bayesian reformulation of Deck-of-cards ordinal regression in which the number of blank cards between ranked levels is modeled through a cumulative-link likelihood relating card counts to latent value differences. Two Bayesian inference algorithms are introduced, replacing hard-constraint treatments with full probabilistic inference over value functions.

entry.title: Low-Rank Frequency Convolution and Noise-Range Augmentation for Real-Time Pitch Estimation on Edge Devices

author.name: Venkat Suprabath Bitra, Homayoon Beigi

entry.summary: Factors a Frequency Convolution Network into low-rank form, cutting parameters by 35.9% (to 11,397) with no accuracy loss in-domain or on unseen corpora, and shows that the noise range used during training dominates robustness behavior more than architecture. Targets real-time pitch estimation under edge-device compute, latency, and noise constraints.

entry.title: TAC-Time: Texts as Channels For Multimodal Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Jiayi Liang, Xiaotian Gu, Xinyu Xie, Yuanbin Wu, Xiaoling Wang

entry.summary: Proposes TAC-Time, a framework that converts auxiliary textual information into additional temporal channels so text features are modeled jointly with numerical sequences in a shared temporal backbone. This preserves temporal continuity and periodic structure while avoiding costly LLM-based forecasting backbones or static text features.

entry.title: Evaluating Personal Information Output from Conversational Interactions in Generative AI Systems

author.name: Yosuke Seki, Hirotaka Tahara

entry.summary: This pilot study with 15 Japanese participants evaluates how GPT-5.2 Instant and GPT-5.2 Thinking surface personal information during conversations, categorizing outputs as Fact, Inference, or Confidence. It finds model design differences have limited impact, Fact-type outputs are more conservative than Inference-type, and core identifying attributes are treated more conservatively than behavioral or linguistic attributes.

entry.title: Mitigating Entity Type Confusion in Cross-Domain NER via Multidimensional Quantification and Reasoning Enhancement

author.name: Jingyu Wang, Shijie Wu, Fusheng Jin

entry.summary: The paper targets entity type confusion in cross-domain NER, where models detect spans well but misclassify entity types when transferring to a new domain. It proposes MCQM, a model that quantifies confusion across three dimensions including source-target hierarchy and semantic similarity, then uses this quantification to guide reasoning enhancement for type classification. The approach addresses a specific, well-defined failure mode that span-centric improvements miss.

entry.title: Jev for Scientific Decisions: Evaluating Semantic Choices and Their Consequences

author.name: Boyuan Deng, Shuyi Fan, Hongyang Zhang, Xinhong Xie

entry.summary: Evaluates Jev as a semantic decision component in scientific workflows, using a harness that separates semantic selections, downstream outputs, and final claim labels across twelve model configurations, twenty source-grounded choices, and ten scientific cases. Jev matched other configurations at complete semantic correctness while achieving the lowest observed median latency among successful runs.

entry.title: Custom Named Entity Recognition and Topic Classification for Global Health Publications

author.name: Genis Skura, Antoine Geissb\"uhler, Jean-Luc Falcone

entry.summary: This thesis-style work studies how to select and adapt NLP models for global health literature under limited annotation and compute, comparing skip-gram word2vec models against BioWordVec for tag discovery and convolutional spaCy models for entity extraction. A notable finding is that broader vocabulary coverage does not necessarily produce more useful domain-specific associations.

entry.title: C$^{2}$-INR: Customized Convolutional Implicit Neural Representation

author.name: Jinglei Shi, Xinran Chang, Jiaqi Cui, Yingjie Xia, Zhaolin Xiao, Chongyi Li

entry.summary: C2-INR revisits convolutional implicit neural representations for image signals, arguing convolutions are a more natural fit than MLPs because they process pixels in parallel while exploiting inter-pixel dependencies. It proposes customized architectural settings rather than fixed ones to improve INR fitting quality.

entry.title: Accurate Motion Estimation with B\'ezier Control Point for Efficient Frame Interpolation

author.name: Shuhao Han, Chenyang Wu, Chun-Le Guo, Zheng-Peng Duan, Zhen Li, Ming-Ming Cheng, Chongyi Li

entry.summary: ABC-Inter addresses blurry intermediate frames in video frame interpolation caused by motion ambiguity in training data and the uniform-motion assumption at inference. It decouples two-frame features for accurate optical flow estimation and uses computed Bezier control points to model non-uniform motion trajectories. A competent incremental contribution to a mature task area.

entry.title: Compact Low-Cost Hyperspectral Imaging via Angular-to-Spectral Diversity Conversion

author.name: Kazuma Fujiwara, Takuya Funatomi, Kazuya Kitano, Yuki Fujimura, Yasuhiro Mukaigawa

entry.summary: This work presents a snapshot hyperspectral imaging system using a tapered kaleidoscope plus birefringent filter to convert angular diversity into view-dependent spectral transmittances, producing complementary measurements that stabilize single-shot spectral reconstruction. The system uses only off-the-shelf optics and supports fast non-learning reconstruction.

entry.title: Incentive Noise and Structural Prior Infusion for Multi-modal Object Re-Identification

author.name: Weixiang Zhou, Yuhao Wang, Xingguo Xu, Weizhen Zhou, Zhixun Su, Jinshan Pan, Cong Wang

entry.summary: This work tackles noise in text descriptions used as an auxiliary modality in multi-modal object re-identification, proposing Positive-Incentive Noise and structural prior infusion to reconcile fine-grained discrepancies between modalities. It addresses the common assumption that text descriptions are clean deterministic signals. The framework aims to enrich semantic representation across heterogeneous imaging modalities.

entry.title: DTKDP: A Dual Teacher Knowledge Distillation and Pruning Framework for Lightweight Oriented SAR Ship Detection

author.name: Yuming Li, Fan Zhang, Alin M. Achim

entry.summary: DTKDP is a dual-teacher knowledge distillation and pruning framework that compresses two-stage oriented SAR ship detectors, adding learnable gates to convolutional, normalization, and linear layers and using rotated proposal alignment to distill teacher-student predictions. It preserves proposal-level refinement for precise rotated localization while enabling lightweight deployment.

entry.title: Resolution-Flexible Decoding for Hybrid Neural Video Representations

author.name: Taiga Hayami, Masaya Takabe, Hiroshi Watanabe

entry.summary: Proposes a resolution-flexible decoder framework for hybrid neural video representations, decoupling latent spatial sizes and upsampling schedules from the target frame resolution. Uses uniform 2x upsampling stages traced through spatial restructuring to improve parameter allocation for high-resolution video.

entry.title: A Direct Rigid Transmission 2-DoF Wrist Extension for Tendon-Driven Hand

author.name: Yujie Pang, Sadman Sakib, Mohammad Abdullah Al Faruque

entry.summary: Presents CRAFT-Wrist, a concentric 2-DoF wrist extension that mounts between a robot arm and the CRAFT Hand without modifying the hand, enabling local orientation control in confined spaces. The prototype actuates both axes under load with demonstrated workspace ranges and simplifies end-effector paths relative to arm-only orientation control.

entry.title: Spiking Neural Network Actor-Critic Proximal Policy Optimization Control for Autonomous UAV Navigation Through Constrained Openings in Civil Infrastructure and Buildings

author.name: Francis Noah Walugembe, Maciej Wielgosz, Toma\v{z} Gori\v{c}an, Matej Mertik

entry.summary: Applies spiking neural network-based PPO for autonomous UAV navigation through constrained openings in bridges, tunnels, and buildings, targeting the computational cost limits of deep RL on embedded platforms. Explores neuromorphic efficiency for infrastructure inspection. Application-oriented work combining SNNs with policy optimization.

entry.title: AquaOrbit: Sim-to-Real Reinforcement Learning for Underwater Target Orbiting under Intermittent Visual Feedback

author.name: Kanzhong Yao, Jinyi Leng, Hao Zhang, Zhe Sun, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: AquaOrbit is an RL controller with a recovery module for underwater robots orbiting a target when visual feedback is intermittently lost, using latched line-of-sight, roll, and depth references for stabilization and target reacquisition. Trained in Isaac Sim with domain randomization including vision loss, it transfers to Gazebo/ROS2 without retraining and completes 20/20 trials for both static and moving targets. This demonstrates robust sim-to-real transfer for a niche but practically relevant underwater autonomy task.

entry.title: A Monolithic Force-Proprioception Soft Acutuator Enabled by Single-Material 3D printing

author.name: Nan Huang, Lele Liu, Junfeng Lu, Yipan Zhu, Jiansheng Dai, Sicong Liu

entry.summary: The paper introduces the MFPS actuator, integrating an asymmetric origami bending pneumatic chamber with a strain-based force-proprioception sensor in a single conductive-TPU material via one-step FDM printing, avoiding assembly errors and stress concentrations from heterogeneous materials. Parametric sensing analysis and characterization demonstrate integrated actuation-sensing for soft robots.

entry.title: Identity Continuity in Long-Term Embodied AI Relationships: From Agent-Specific Identity Representation to Identity-Continuity Appraisal

author.name: Zijian Ru

entry.summary: A conceptual article proposing a user-side framework for identity continuity in long-term embodied AI relationships, addressing whether a system remains experienced as the same particular agent after model updates, memory compression, hardware repair, or embodiment migration. It synthesizes research on relational particularity, identity migration signals, and relational loss into an identity-continuity appraisal framework.

entry.title: A class of statement between conjecture and theorem

author.name: Jason Fantl

entry.summary: Responding to concerns from mathematicians that LM-generated, Lean-verified but incomprehensible proofs break the traditional link between proof and understanding, the author proposes formally recognizing a new class of statement, provisionally called a compertum: proved but not understood. The goal is to give the mathematical community language to track both verification status and pedagogical value.

entry.title: Interpretable Stress Detection from ECG Signals Using Motif-Based Anomaly Analysis

author.name: Zhanna Balyan, Sachin Kumar

entry.summary: The paper proposes an interpretable, personalized stress-detection framework using ECG motifs discovered via Matrix Profile analysis, detecting stress as deviation from subject-specific baseline cardiac patterns rather than training a classifier. This captures individual variability that black-box models miss.

entry.title: URA-NER: A Unified Retrieval-Augmented Framework with Retrieval Alignment and Uncertainty Reduction for Low-Resource NER

author.name: Jingyu Wang, Shijie Wu, Fusheng Jin

entry.summary: URA-NER is a retrieval-augmented framework for few-shot NER with LLMs, comprising Progressive Granularity Retrieval, Model-aware Representation Enhancement, and Reason-aware Knowledge Verification. It tackles retrieval misalignment and generation uncertainty that make existing ICL-based NER performance heavily dependent on model scale, aiming to help smaller LLMs in low-resource settings. The framework addresses a practical bottleneck where annotated data is scarce.

entry.title: Video-based Surgical Skill Assessment Using Dynamics-and-Uncertainty-Aware Tree-based Gaussian Process Classifier

author.name: Arefeh Rezaei, Mohammad Javad Ahmadi, Amir Molaei, Hamid D. Taghirad

entry.summary: The paper combines a representation-flow CNN with a dynamics- and uncertainty-aware tree-based Gaussian Process classifier for surgical skill assessment from video, using latent motion dynamics as both features and uncertainty sources. It introduces semantic-aware compound kernels and reports lower data requirements and better efficiency than conventional deep learning. Uncertainty quantification supports safer clinical deployment.

entry.title: Adaptive Differential Evolution and Multistart Search for Noisy QAOA Optimization

author.name: Vojt\v{e}ch Nov\'ak, Ivan Zelinka, Swagatam Das, Martin Beseda

entry.summary: Benchmarks ten classical optimizers on a fixed low-depth QAOA ansatz across four Hamiltonian families under exact and noisy objectives, finding multistart BFGS and CMA-ES favored with exact evaluations while adaptive population methods become more competitive under noise, with rankings depending on the performance metric used.

entry.title: Phrase-Level Robotic Guqin Performance: Bimanual Motion Planning and Audio-Tactile Interaction Monitoring

author.name: Zhen Wang, Zhiheng Chen, Tianyuan Bao, Tianwei Zhang

entry.summary: This paper builds a heterogeneous dual-arm robotic system that autonomously performs phrase-level music on the guqin, a seven-string fretless zither with millimetric string spacing, formulating performance as a hybrid discrete-continuous problem with bimanual motion planning and audio-tactile monitoring of contact timing. Musical instrument playing is framed as a demanding manipulation benchmark requiring precise contact timing and acoustic outcomes. It demonstrates impressive precision but on a highly specialized task.

entry.title: Uncertainty and Business-Aware Remaining Useful Life Estimation for Semiconductor Manufacturing

author.name: Davide Frizzo, Francesco Borsatti, Gian Antonio Susto

entry.summary: The paper presents a predictive maintenance framework for semiconductor manufacturing combining deep learning sequence models (including state space model architectures) with simultaneous quantile regression for uncertainty-aware remaining useful life estimation, feeding risk-aware, business-constrained maintenance decisions. It compares several architectures on the 2018 PHM Data Challenge ion-milling data.

entry.title: DPTM-DT: Dual-Pretrained Transformer Multitask Representation Learning for Drug-Target Prediction

author.name: Ge Kong

entry.summary: DPTM-DT combines GROVER molecular graph embeddings, ESM protein language-model embeddings, and CTD physicochemical descriptors in a dual-pretrained Transformer with bidirectional cross-modal attention for drug-target prediction. It jointly handles affinity regression and interaction classification through a shared pair representation, supporting screening, repositioning, and mechanism analysis.

entry.title: Graph-to-Grid (G2G): Continuous-Coordinate Feature Painting for Soccer Pass Surfaces

author.name: Kaan G\"unay, Orhun Gun

entry.summary: G2G evaluates an interpolated form of graph-to-grid feature painting for dense soccer pass surfaces, scattering each player's features bilinearly onto the pitch grid at measured coordinates so that surface loss trains the per-player encoder end to end. On 53,628 passes from the 2022 World Cup, the paper measures this interface borrowed from LiDAR detection, bird's-eye-view perception, and graph weather models. It is an empirical measurement study of an architectural interface in sports analytics.

entry.title: Low resource cross-modal alignment using HGNN to enhance speech representation

author.name: Yannick Yomie Nzeuhang, Marie Tahon, Paulin Melatagia Yonta

entry.summary: Proposes a data-efficient speech-text alignment method based on heterogeneous graph neural networks as a frugal alternative to student/teacher systems like SAMU-XLSR that require large data and compute. The approach maps speech and text into a shared representation space under low-resource constraints.

entry.title: Math2Visual-X: A Modular Framework for Pedagogically Aligned Lower-Primary Math Visuals Generation

author.name: H. D. E. Maduranga, S. K. Munasinghe, K. P. T. I. Weerasekara, Surangika Ranathunga, Nisansa de Silva

entry.summary: Math2Visual-X is a symbolic visual generation framework for lower-primary math word problems, combining an LLM-based routing layer, worksheet-oriented generation modules, and fallback mechanisms for open-world SVG asset acquisition. Human evaluation against Stable Diffusion XL, Nano Banana, and GPT Image shows the symbolic approach better satisfies exact mathematical constraints.

entry.title: Identity-Consistent Analysis of Long-Shot Windsurfing Video: A Domain-Specific Offline Tracking System

author.name: Bertil Braun

entry.summary: An offline system for windsurfing video that detects surfers, forms conservative local tracklets, links them globally with camera-compensated motion and sail-color descriptors, and drives a rider-relative virtual camera from rig pose keypoints. It is evaluated on 21 manually reconstructed videos with 41,004 observations under a fixed-observation protocol prioritizing identity consistency.

entry.title: AI-GRACE: A Use-Case Operationalization Framework for Agentic AI: From Organizational Objectives and Obligations to Deployment Capabilities and Architecture

author.name: John Cuneo, David Chun, Gaurav Khanna

entry.summary: AI-GRACE is a governance framework that connects organizational objectives and obligations to technical validation, control, and observability requirements for agentic AI deployments. It uses design science and situational method engineering to support tailoring to specific use cases. It matters because agentic systems need practical bridges between governance requirements and implementation.

entry.title: Interference-Driven Clustered Optimisation for FM Spectrum Coordination

author.name: Federica Mangiatordi, Emiliano Pallotti

entry.summary: This paper proposes a clustered optimization framework for large-scale cross-border FM spectrum coordination, exploiting the observation that foreign-service protection violations are dominated by a small subset of transmitters. By identifying dominant transmitters, it reduces the dimensionality of the otherwise computationally demanding power-control problem over thousands of transmitters and millions of transmitter-pixel relationships. This is a domain-specific optimization contribution to radio planning.

entry.title: Rank Portability Does Not Imply Feasibility Portability: Target-Specific Evaluation of Joint Hardware Constraints

author.name: Wesley Shu

entry.summary: The paper stress-tests the assumption that architecture rankings transferring across hardware devices imply feasibility portability for joint latency-energy constraints, using NAS-Bench-201 and another architecture family. It shows incomplete feasible-set overlap even with good rank correlation, demonstrates a conformal-analysis evidence bottleneck requiring at least nine calibration observations, and cautions against proxy-device model selection.

entry.title: Clustering-Based Collective Anomaly Detection in IoT Systems: A Graph Neural Network Approach

author.name: Dalila Khettaf, Djamel Djenouri, Zeinab Rezaeifar, Youcef Djenouri

entry.summary: The paper introduces UGCAD, an unsupervised graph-based framework for detecting collective anomalies in IoT network traffic, moving beyond the point-anomaly focus of prior work.
