It uses clustering combined with graph neural networks to identify coordinated malicious activity patterns across interconnected devices.

entry.title: EmbeddGAN: A Novel GAN Framework Using an Embedding Network and Gini Distance Correlation

author.name: MaTais Caldwell, Yixin Chen, Xin Dang, Charles Walter

entry.summary: EmbeddGAN replaces the standard real/fake discriminator with an embedding network trained via a dependence-based Gini distance correlation objective: representations are learned that maximize statistical dependence between samples and their real/fake labels while the generator minimizes it. The aim is to address GAN training instability, mode collapse, and hyperparameter sensitivity with a formally grounded criterion.

entry.title: User-Level Handover Decision Making Based on Machine Learning Approaches

author.name: Jo\~ao Lima, Alvaro Medeiros, Eduardo Aguiar, Vicente Angelo de Sousa Junior, Tarciana Guerra

entry.summary: A comparative study of machine learning methods for cellular handover target selection under adverse propagation conditions, using ns-3 simulations across KNN, SVM, neural networks, fuzzy logic systems, and gradient boosting. SVM and MLP perform best for classification of the handover target, while fuzzy logic (SOFL) matches at lower compute and LightGBM is best for download-time estimation.

entry.title: Feature Suppression and Differential Privacy for Residential Traffic Classification: A Two-Home Federated Study

author.name: M\'arton P\'al Lipcsey-Magyar, Adrian Pekar

entry.summary: Studies the privacy-utility tradeoff in federated residential traffic classification using 1.62 million gateway flows across six categories, comparing feature suppression against DP-SGD under a fixed record-level privacy setting. Finds that mild feature suppression without formal guarantees can beat DP-SGD on macro-F1 and worst-group F1 with size-proportional aggregation.

entry.title: Explainable Neuro-Fuzzy Prediction for Trustworthy Decision-Making in Maritime

author.name: Dionisis Kalogeropoulos, Georgia Sovatzidi, Dimitris K. Iakovidis

entry.summary: The paper proposes an explainable decision-making framework combining a neuro-fuzzy prediction model with a two-stage explainability component: gradient-based saliency maps for feature attribution followed by fuzzy decision trees extracting local rules. The framework is generic and claimed to be the first fuzzy logic-based framework providing both feature-level and local rule-based explanations of black-box models.

entry.title: Machine Learning-Based Prediction of Childhood Stunting in Bangladesh: Fairness and Temporal Robustness Assessment

author.name: Md Ahshanul Haque, Muhammad Ashad Kabir

entry.summary: Using Bangladesh Demographic and Health Survey data from 2007-2022, the authors build ML models to predict childhood stunting at population level, explicitly evaluating temporal robustness on later survey rounds and subgroup fairness. Twelve feature-selection approaches were compared, with KNN among the top performers.

entry.title: GraphToolbox: A Configurable Python Framework for Graph Neural Network Forecasting

author.name: Eloi Campagne (CB), Yvenn Amara-Ouali (LMO, CELESTE), Yannig Goude (EDF R\&D), Argyris Kalogeratos (CB, ENS Paris Saclay)

entry.summary: GraphToolbox is an open-source PyTorch Geometric-based framework unifying graph construction, model selection, training, aggregation, and interpretation for GNN electricity forecasting in one configuration-driven pipeline. It supports instantiating and training 51 of 65 PyTorch Geometric convolutions plus PyTorch Geometric Temporal recurrent cells.

entry.title: Attention-Enhanced Dual-Branch ConvNeXt-BiLSTM Network for Subject-Independent EEG Seizure Detection

author.name: Maimuna Chowdhury, Sk. Imran Hossain

entry.summary: The paper presents a dual-branch network for scalp EEG seizure detection that combines a pretrained ConvNeXt-Tiny on wavelet scalograms with a BiLSTM plus multi-head self-attention on raw signals, classified via a weighted MLP. It targets subject-independent detection despite patient-varying seizure morphology and severe class imbalance.

entry.title: Machine Learning for Underwater Optical Wireless Communication Systems: A Comprehensive Survey

author.name: Shaymaa Mahmoud, Ardimas Purwita, Mohamed-Slim Alouini

entry.summary: A comprehensive survey of machine learning methods for underwater optical wireless communication, covering channel modeling, signal processing, and system adaptation across the full UOWC pipeline. It positions ML against conventional analytical methods for mitigating underwater channel impairments.

entry.title: Signal-Informed Temporal Routing for Vinyl Defect Regime Detection

author.name: Yi-Hung Kan, Homayoon Beigi

entry.summary: Presents a lightweight two-stage audio detector for vinyl restoration that distinguishes clicks, bursts, crackle, and overlapping damage before selecting repair operations, using signal-informed experts and a temporal backend with hierarchical decoding and validation-selected transition penalties. It reports 0.730 pooled performance on a synthetic benchmark of 597 excerpts from 21 recordings.

entry.title: TriFleetRCA: On-Premise LLM Root Cause Analysis for Kubernetes

author.name: Rohit Patel, Susil Kumar Mohanty, Jeenal Chaudhary

entry.summary: Presents TriFleetRCA, a root cause analysis pipeline running entirely on one on-premise GPU for Kubernetes clusters, collecting evidence at pod, namespace, or cluster scope, ranking it via template de-duplication and BM25, filtering tampered runbooks through an ingest guard, and addressing context budget constraints that live-cluster benchmarks have not studied.

entry.title: HumynexSurg-1: A Curated Expert Liposuction Dataset

author.name: Rhea Huang, David L. Matlock, Laurence Reich

entry.summary: Releases the first curated dataset of expert liposuction surgery demonstrations, recorded on porcine tissue with synchronized force/torque, suction pressure, RGB-D video, and narration, addressing the absence of surgery in robot foundation model training corpora. 14 episodes with over 42,000 frames from a master surgeon.

entry.title: Learning-Based 3D Reconstruction of Power Networks from Aerial Point Clouds

author.name: Rishabh Jain, Anuja Saini, Vishal Jain

entry.summary: Presents an end-to-end pipeline for reconstructing overhead power grid topology from aerial LiDAR, using an improved KPConv segmentation model biased toward pole and wire classes plus a two-stage topology inference combining geometric criteria and a ResNet classifier on 2D projections. Extracts span-level physical metadata for utility applications.

entry.title: The Operational Value of Spatial Dependence in Renewable Forecast Scenarios for Single-Period Economic Dispatch: A Controlled Ablation Study

author.name: Jayakumar Manoharan

entry.summary: Uses controlled ablations on real European transmission system data to show that spatial coherence across renewable forecast sites contributes at most 0.64% of dispatch cost savings, statistically indistinguishable from zero in most configurations, when per-zone marginal forecasts are held fixed. Questions the practical value of modeling cross-site dependence in single-period economic dispatch.

entry.title: A framework for recipe data structure with applications for culinary and nutritional insights

author.name: Mansi Goel, Sumit Bhagat, Saloni Srivastava, Malav Patel, Shlok Vinodkumar Mehroliya, Ganesh Bagler

entry.summary: The paper formalizes a structured recipe data schema that decomposes recipes into typed ingredient entities grounded in a nutritional database and annotated with geo-cultural and dietary context, released as RecipeDB2. This enables computable queries linking composition, provenance, and nutrition within a single representation.

entry.title: Replay-Gated Neural Execution: Decoupling Persistent Behavioral Specifications from Neural Realizations in Frozen Language Models

author.name: Xianliang Zeng, Zhanzhan Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces replay-gated neural execution, a runtime framework that separates a persistent behavioral predicate, its certified realization set, a transient action witness, a budget-limited finder, and execution authorization, with isolated FP32/BF16 replay of frozen models and run audits for commitment. Experiments on Qwen3-0.6B and SmolLM2-360M-Instruct reveal distinct failure modes among these objects.

entry.title: Analyzing Public Discourse on Urbanism: Topic Clustering, Sentiment Analysis and Retrieval-Augmented Generation using YouTube Comments

author.name: Jakob Morales, Monica Hegde, Fayeq Jeelani Syed

entry.summary: Presents a pipeline combining geographic entity resolution, topic modeling, sentiment analysis, and RAG over YouTube transcripts and comments about urbanism across 309 North American cities. The contribution is both a conversational system and empirical measurements of how standard NLP components degrade on short, informal, geographically ambiguous text.

entry.title: Assessing Readability with LLMs: The Role of Reasoning and Few-Shot Prompting

author.name: Rapha\"el Thieffry, Matej Martinc

entry.summary: The paper benchmarks diverse open-source LLMs for multilingual readability assessment, systematically studying the impact of reasoning modes and few-shot prompting strategies. It positions LLMs as a scalable, training-free alternative to readability formulas and supervised models, which generalize poorly across genres and languages and depend on scarce annotations. The study clarifies when advanced prompting helps in this task.

entry.title: Long-Tail Rebalancing for Non-Verbal Vocalization-Aware ASR: A Track~1 System for the NVVSpeech Challenge

author.name: Shangyue Jia, Jingru Ma, Yangzhuo Li, Daoping Luo, Bowen Tian, Hanchen Lu, Wenze Ren, Yunxiang Chen, Houdun Liu, Shuo Feng, Lei Xie, Liumeng Xue

entry.summary: This is a challenge-system paper for the ISCSLP NVVSpeech Challenge, presenting an NVV-aware ASR pipeline that jointly transcribes lexical content and 16 categories of non-verbal vocalizations (laughs, sighs, etc.) under limited, highly imbalanced supervision. The approach combines cross-dataset label harmonization into a unified taxonomy with a two-stage sampling schedule (square-root category sampling followed by uniform-category fine-tuning) to handle long-tailed distributions. It matters because paralinguistic cues like non-verbal vocalizations are routinely dropped by conventional ASR despite carrying important conversational information.

entry.title: Yarn tracking of large-scale 3D textile reinforcements using topological material features

author.name: Hafsa El Herichi (LMPS, CVN), Arturo Mendoza (LMPS), Yanneck Wielhorski (CVN), Hugues Talbot (CVN), St\'ephane Roux (LMPS)

entry.summary: The paper presents a semi-automatic method for tracking textile reinforcement yarns in fan blade preforms from coarse X-ray CT images (above 140 micrometers), using slice-based analysis on planes orthogonal to yarn directions and statistically modeling cross-section shape, continuity, and other yarn properties. It targets generating high-fidelity numerical models for industrial simulation with minimal training data.

entry.title: Exact Quotients of Fresnel-Kummer Surfaces and Certified Biaxial Refraction

author.name: Tanush Shaska

entry.summary: A pure mathematics paper identifying the Fresnel wave surface of biaxial crystals exactly as the Kummer surface of the Jacobian of an explicit genus-two curve, with an isogeny decomposing it into two elliptic curves carrying the permittivities and optic-axis angle. The algebraic identification enables certified treatment of biaxial refraction.

entry.title: Rule-Constrained Assignment for Cue-Ball Identification in Broadcast Snooker

author.name: Yuxin Cao, Wei Song, Yuezhong Wu, Jin Song Dong

entry.summary: This paper reformulates cue-ball identification in broadcast snooker video as a rule-constrained assignment problem jointly matching detected candidates to the bounded ball inventory (one cue ball, up to 15 reds, six colors), selecting the cue ball via incremental assignment cost rather than independent appearance thresholds. This handles illumination changes and occlusions that break prototype-matching systems. A niche but neat formulation-driven solution.

entry.title: Scale-Vector Alignment: A Scale-Aware Framework for Spatially Resolved Morphological Similarity in Astronomical Images

author.name: Mengke Zhao, Guang-Xing Li, Keping Qiu, Shanghuo Li

entry.summary: Proposes scale-vector alignment, built on Constrained Diffusion Decomposition, which decomposes astronomical images into localized scale components and defines pixel-wise similarity as normalized alignment of local scale vectors. Enables comparison of maps from different tracers whose morphological differences depend on position and spatial scale.

entry.title: Genetic Programming with Behaviour-based Niching for Learning Guided Local Search in Vehicle Routing Problems

author.name: Saining Liu, Yi Mei, Mengjie Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes BN-GPGLS, augmenting genetic programming guided local search for vehicle routing with behavior-based niching: programs are characterized via six operator-level behavioral descriptors, and an archive selects fitness-competitive representatives from behavior strata, improving diversity management beyond fitness alone.

entry.title: Automatic Labelling for Bimanual Mobile Manipulation

author.name: Yupu Lu, Jia Pan

entry.summary: This paper presents a pipeline that automatically produces semantic subtask labels for bimanual mobile manipulation trajectories by segmenting synchronized kinematic signals into phases and applying phase-localized vision-language reasoning to describe each segment. It was evaluated on 29 real Galaxea bimanual tasks, with repeated VL reasoning used to improve label reliability. Automatic labeling of this kind reduces the annotation cost of building long-horizon robot policies.

entry.title: Minimum Time Trajectories for a Car-Like Mobile Robot Moving with Rigid Wheels Under Non-Sliding Constraints

author.name: Joseph Ben-Asher, Elon Rimon, Leeor Ravina

entry.summary: The paper derives minimum-time trajectory primitives for a car-like mobile robot with bounded front-wheel acceleration and limited steering rate, extending prior kinematic-car results by formulating non-sliding wheel constraints from robot dynamics. It augments time-optimal kinematic path primitives with three new dynamic primitives accounting for wheel slip limits.

entry.title: LoRA Enhanced Contrastive Learning with SAS Vision Transformers

author.name: Dan Zimmerman, Frank E. Bobe III, Amelia L. McCormack, Matthew Cook, Gregory D. Vetaw

entry.summary: This work adapts DINOv3 Vision Transformers to underwater synthetic aperture sonar automatic target recognition using a three-stage parameter-efficient pipeline: LoRA fine-tuning, hard-negative mining against acoustic mimics like rocks, and supervised contrastive learning. It tackles scarce target imagery and background clutter in a naval application.

entry.title: Offline Multimodal Large Language Models for Decision Support in Air Operations

author.name: Joao P. A. Dantas, Jelton A. Cunha, Gabriel Dietzsch

entry.summary: The paper describes a modular retrieval-augmented, offline multimodal LLM architecture for air operations decision support, allowing analysts to query doctrinal manuals (text and images) in fully isolated, low-connectivity environments with traceable sources. It includes a first-step evaluation of the architecture. This is a practical deployment study for secure, offline military/aviation contexts.

entry.title: Hierarchical Bayesian optimization of an aircraft-based multi-agent system-of-systems

author.name: Paul Saves, Thierry Lefebvre, Nathalie Bartoli, Jasper Bussemaker, Nikolaos Kalliatakis, Nabih Naeem, Prajwal Prakasha

entry.summary: The paper introduces a hierarchical Bayesian optimization framework using Gaussian process meta-modeling to optimize expensive, failure-prone system-of-systems simulations in aircraft architecting. It addresses evaluation failures and computational expense that make direct optimization of high-fidelity multiphysics SoS models impractical.

entry.title: Industrial Kinematic Trajectory Model (IKTM): Coordinate-Free Autoregressive Generator

author.name: Max Amiri, David Eyers

entry.summary: IKTM is a coordinate-free trajectory generator for industrial vehicle motion in ports, mines, and airports, representing motion as kinematic sequences (speed and heading change) rather than site-specific coordinates or road tokens. It uses an autoregressive causal transformer with probabilistic mixture heads, extending a prior Markovian model with deep sequence modeling.

entry.title: Cost-Aware Reinforcement Learning with Action Masking and Projection for Battery Energy Storage Dispatch under Suppressed-Spread Market Shifts

author.name: Kuanlin Chen, Chen-Wei Kuo, Cheng-En Ou

entry.summary: Evaluates a PPO controller with action masking and emergency projection for battery energy storage dispatch under declining price spreads, separating feasibility enforcement from a causal forecast-informed economic advisor. Across five seeds, advice-on PPO earns 30.59 and 18.04 USD per window versus 36.77 and 22.94 for proxy-cost MPC, showing PPO still trails the MPC reference.

entry.title: Stagewise Anomaly Detection for E-Transaxle Quality Monitoring Using Wavelet and STFT Features

author.name: Mohammad N. Bisheh, Rajesh Gupta, Qian Wang, Mohammad Babakmehr, Colin Brady, Parinaz Farajiparvar, Saurabh Singh, Kamran Payanabar

entry.summary: The paper presents two interpretable frameworks for electric-vehicle e-transaxle quality screening: a Stagewise Wavelet Isolation Forest and an STFT-based diagnostic framework that analyze vibration signals across operating stages. Both exploit stage-dependent vibration behavior for assembly quality monitoring in manufacturing.

entry.title: Balancing Reasoning and Hardware Constraints in RAG Pipelines for Ukrainian Multi-Domain Document Understanding

author.name: Illya Havrylov

entry.summary: This system paper describes a resource-efficient hybrid RAG pipeline for the UNLP 2026 shared task, extracting answers, document IDs, and page numbers from Ukrainian PDFs under a strict 9-hour offline budget in which OCR consumed 5-7 hours. The design trades reasoning depth against hardware constraints to guarantee pipeline completion within the time limit.

entry.title: Enhancing speech representation learning with cross-modal knowledge transfer with HGNN under low resource settings: the case study of Yemba

author.name: Yannick Yomie Nzeuhang, Paulin Melatagia Yonta, Marie Tahon

entry.summary: Enhances acoustic representation learning for the low-resource language Yemba via heterogeneous graph neural networks, modeling acoustic and linguistic entities as distinct node types so linguistic nodes transfer knowledge to acoustic nodes through message passing. Evaluation uses standard clustering metrics to demonstrate the benefits of structured, interpretable cross-modal flow.

entry.title: HaikuS2S: A Cascaded System For Responding In Verse

author.name: Devangi Sharma, Sophia Judicke, Glenda Tan, Conrad Schaumburg, Shinji Watanabe

entry.summary: A cascaded ASR-LLM-TTS system, HaikuS2S, that responds to speech with haiku, fine-tuning TTS on prose and custom haiku data to capture 5-7-5 syllable structure and line-ending pauses. Evaluations show improved prosody and tonal alignment on emotion similarity, speech quality, and prosody metrics.

entry.title: QLoRA Fine-Tuning of Ministral LLM for Sequence-to-Function Protein Annotation

author.name: Demian Pavlyshenko, Bohdan Pavlyshenko

entry.summary: The paper frames protein functional annotation as sequence-to-text generation rather than fixed-ontology multi-label classification, fine-tuning the 3B Ministral 3 base model with QLoRA (4-bit NF4 quantization) on sequence annotation pairs. Predictions are assessed with an LLM-as-expert protocol where a GPT model prompted as a senior molecular-biology curator scores outputs. This addresses the curation bottleneck as sequencing data outpaces manual annotation capacity.

entry.title: X-Beat: An Explainable Framework for ECG Image Classification

author.name: Mohammad Sadman Tahsin, Haitham Y. Adarbah, Afzel Noore

entry.summary: X-Beat is an explainable, reliability-aware benchmark framework for ECG image classification across four cardiac classes, combining transfer learning with post-hoc explainability and systematic reliability evaluation. It aims to make deep models more deployable in clinical settings through transparency and validation.

entry.title: Trust-Aware Output Management for Physical Neural Network in Cloud-Continuum Systems

author.name: Maliheh Hariri, Stefan Fischer

entry.summary: Proposes a trust-aware output management framework for heterogeneous physical neural networks in cloud-continuum computing, where each output carries quality and context information and lightweight edge-level trust scores decide acceptance, rejection, or fog forwarding, with reliability- and uncertainty-aware fusion at the fog layer.

entry.title: Odometry-Aided Real-Time Mapping for Underwater Robots Using Forward-Looking Sonar

author.name: Siyuan Du, Kanzhong Yao, Youdong Wang, Yingqi Liu, Qingwen Liu, Qunhui Yang, Zhe Sun, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: This paper presents a real-time forward-looking sonar mapping pipeline for underwater robots combining FFT-based denoising, multiscale constant false alarm rate detection, and cascaded feature reconstruction to handle unresolved target elevation, non-uniform noise, and fragmented boundaries. It is odometry-aided and addresses geometric ambiguity during acoustic projection. This matters for underwater perception where optical sensing degrades badly.

entry.title: Gaussian Process Decorrelation for Spatiotemporal Deep Learning-Based Snow Water Equivalent Prediction

author.name: Colin Fenster, Adrienne Marshall, Soutir Bandyopadhyay, Daniel McKenzie

entry.summary: For snow water equivalent forecasting across the SNOTEL network in the Western US, the authors use a Gaussian Process-based linear transformation to decorrelate spatially and temporally correlated measurements before training an LSTM. This lets the network learn cleaner per-station temporal signals, improving water-resource forecasts.

entry.title: COREM: Cosine-Relation Momentum Reshaping with Stateful Writeback

author.name: Yan Wang, Xiaochuan Wang, Yuxiang Sun

entry.summary: COREM introduces a unit-relation-transform abstraction that exploits relational structure within matrix-valued optimizer states, partitioning momentum into update units and reshaping them using cosine relations before writing the transformed state back. This stateful writeback lets the reshaped momentum influence both current and future optimization dynamics. It is evaluated on CIFAR-scale image classification tasks, suggesting early-stage empirical evidence for a new optimizer design direction.

entry.title: Benchmarking Hybrid Deep Learning Architectures for Predictive Maintenance in Industry 4.0

author.name: Zhengyang (Cissy), Gu, Joseph E. Hernandez, Thomas Cook, John Burtenshaw, Sean Scott, Chris Couch

entry.summary: The authors evaluate six deep learning architectures across more than 700 experimental runs to address the gap between lab performance and reliability on real factory data for predictive maintenance, focusing on recurrent networks versus transformers for sequence modeling of industrial sensor data.

entry.title: Experimental Evaluation of a Low-Power Ultra-Wideband Receiver for Spectrum Sensing

author.name: Panagiotis Vlachos, Ioannis A. Bartsiokas, Cedric Dehos, Francois Rivet, George Karachalios

entry.summary: This paper reports hardware measurements of a Walsh-sequence-based ultra-wideband receiver prototype for reconstructing multiple simultaneous RF signals. Using reconstructed spectra, Walsh-lane power spectral densities, and EVM measurements across interference and configuration scenarios, it provides rare experimental validation of Walsh-domain processing under realistic conditions.

entry.title: Physics-Informed Classical and Quantum Neural Networks for One-Dimensional Schrodinger Eigenvalue Problems

author.name: Tariq Mahmood, Waqas Arshad, Bilal Naseer, Alfredo Raya

entry.summary: The paper formulates PINNs and physics-informed quantum neural networks (PIQNNs) for the time-independent Schrodinger equation, applied to the harmonic oscillator, infinite square well, and finite square well using a composite loss encoding the DE residual, normalization, boundary behavior, and eigenstate orthogonality without supervised data. It compares classical and quantum implementations on exactly solvable benchmarks.

entry.title: Vision Transformers versus convolutional neural networks for fine-grained orchid genus identification in a species-rich, data-poor flora: a controlled benchmark on the Orchidaceae of New Guinea

author.name: Reza Saputra, Diah Harnoni Apriyanti, Andr\'e Schuiteman, Kurt Metzger, Ashley Field, Katharina Nargar, William Edwards

entry.summary: Builds a two-stage genus-prediction-then-image-retrieval system for orchid identification in New Guinea, where most of ~2,856 species have few photographs. Compares four pretrained backbones (DINOv2, BioCLIP 2, ConvNeXt V2, EfficientNetV2) under an identical fine-tuning protocol for fine-grained classification in data-poor floras.

entry.title: Taramandal-GPT: Enhancing Astrodynamics Problem-Solving with Knowledge Retrieval and Structured Thinking

author.name: Akhil Sharma, Jatin Gupta, Ali Imam Abidi

entry.summary: Taramandal-GPT is a domain-adapted framework built on the Qwen3-8b backbone with a RAG pipeline and a fallback mechanism, targeting multi-step reasoning and symbolic manipulation in astronomy and astrodynamics. It is evaluated on APBench, a 299-question benchmark spanning foundational to advanced space-science problems, using dual numeric-margin and complementary evaluation methods. The work demonstrates how retrieval plus structured reasoning can improve LLM performance in specialized scientific domains.

entry.title: Dimensionality reduction for AI based hyperspectral image classification based on XAI

author.name: Vladimir Zeljkovi\'c, Branka Stojanovi\'c, Harald Ganster, Aleksandar Ne\v{s}kovi\'c

entry.summary: This work applies CNNs to hyperspectral imaging with over 200 spectral channels for wood recycling classification, using explainable AI methods to guide dimensionality reduction of the feature space for training and inference. It contributes to sustainability in material recycling through more efficient AI pipelines.

entry.title: Enhancing Shrimp Disease Detection via Deep Learning and Data Refinement for Resilient Aquaculture

author.name: Vinh Canh-Thanh Truong, Hai-Binh Pham, Ngoc Hong Tran

entry.summary: This paper applies Vision Transformers and self-supervised learning (SimCLR with a ViT-Small encoder) to shrimp disease classification for the first time, covering Healthy, Black Gill, White Spot Syndrome Virus, and co-infection on a 4,348-image dataset. It pairs supervised transfer learning with a contrastive pipeline to reduce labeling burden. Practically valuable for aquaculture but methodologically a domain application of established techniques.

entry.title: Lesion-Gated Hybrid Synthesis for Virtual Contrast-Enhanced Breast MRI: A MAMA-SYNTH Challenge Solution

author.name: Shohei Yoshimoto

entry.summary: This is a challenge solution for synthesizing post-contrast breast MRI from pre-contrast images, using a lesion probability map from an ensemble of segmentation networks to coordinate a tumour-focused regression pathway within a hybrid pipeline, optimized across four metric groups in the MAMA-SYNTH MICCAI 2026 challenge.

entry.title: DCL-GPGLS: Dynamic Curriculum Learning for Genetic Programming Guided Local Search in Large-Scale Vehicle Routing

author.name: Saining Liu, Yi Mei, Mengjie Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes DCL-GPGLS, which dynamically estimates training-instance difficulty from the current population's solution quality and updates estimates during training, replacing predefined size- or difficulty-ordered curricula in genetic programming guided local search for large-scale vehicle routing. Builds on prior ACL-GPGLS work.

entry.title: D3DWA: Adaptive Weight and Prediction-Horizon for Dynamic Window Approach via Dueling Double Deep Q-Network

author.name: Zahra Jooyandeh, Masato Kobayashi, Yuki Uranishi

entry.summary: Proposes D3DWA, using a Dueling Double Deep Q-Network to adaptively select Dynamic Window Approach evaluation weights and prediction horizon from continuous navigation state at every control step, while retaining DWA's trajectory generation and collision checking. Evaluated in eight simulated environments including unseen layouts.

entry.title: Ask Before It Tells: Benchmark-to-Robot Body-Cue Transfer for a Question-First Bedside Robot

author.name: Dongsik Yoon

entry.summary: This paper presents Nuni, a bedside assistive robot prototype that treats detected distress cues as prompts to ask the person a question rather than to trigger alerts, and studies the gap between benchmark accuracy and robot-viewpoint reliability. A pose-centric hybrid pipeline achieves 0.71 macro recall on robot-camera clips versus 0.25-0.29 for RGB classifiers that scored 94-98% on NTU RGB+D. It highlights a concrete deployment failure mode of benchmark-tuned vision models in embodied settings.

entry.title: Task aware Dynamic Movement Primitives for failure detection and recovery in contact rich manipulation

author.name: Bhavnashri A, Sobia Shafi, Krishnapuram Himavarshini, Anuj Tiwari

entry.summary: Presents a failure detection and recovery framework for contact-rich assembly that integrates DMP-based trajectory generation with real-time stage classification using Quadratic Discriminant Analysis on multimodal sensor data. The framework segments execution into approach, alignment, and other phases to detect deviations and recover from task failures.

entry.title: What if not Circuits?

author.name: CarolusRenniusVitellius

entry.summary: An essay from an Iliad Fellowship reflecting on the mechanistic interpretability community's default ontology of circuits, arguing that representational drift poses obstacles to weights-based circuit approaches, reconsidering how universality should shape explanations of LLM function, and sketching a co-selectionist view of circuits inspired by comparisons with evolution and neuroscience.

entry.title: CogGym: Towards Large-Scale Comparative Evaluation of Human and Machine Cognition

author.name: Lance Ying, Jinzhou Wu, Yingshan Susan Wang, Shivam Aarya, Luca M. Schulze Buschoff, Harry Chen, Katherine M. Collins, Andrea de Varda, Shuhao Fu, Sean Dae Houlihan, Akshay K. Jagadish, Guangyuan Jiang, Samuel Kiegeland, Tetsu Kurumisawa, Rongzhi Liu, Ryan Liu, Ningshan Ma, Kathryn McGregor, Younes Strittmatter, Polina Tsvilodub, Jacob Hoover Vigly, Sarah Wu, Enjie Xu, Yiling Yun, Kelsey Allen, Tyler Brooke-Wilson, Brian Christian, Evelina Fedorenko, Michael C. Frank, Michael Franke, Tao Gao, Samuel J. Gershman, Robert D. Hawkins, Jennifer Hu, Julian Jara-Ettinger, Max Kleiman-Weiner, Sydney Levine, Tal Linzen, Hongjing Lu, Timothy O'Donnell, Desmond C. Ong, Steven T. Piantadosi, Rebecca Saxe, Eric Schulz, Tianmin Shu, Felix A. Sosa, Ilia Sucholutsky, Tan Zhi-Xuan, Tomer Ullman, Fei Xu, Ilker Yildirim, Jian-Qiao Zhu, Thomas L. Griffiths, Tobias Gerstenberg, Kevin Smith, Joshua B. Tenenbaum

entry.summary: As featured yesterday in Research, CogGym is a large-scale framework for systematically comparing model and human behavior on matched cognitive-science experimental trials, using a semi-automated human-in-the-loop pipeline and a task-agnostic Experiment Markup Language. It comes with an unusually broad consortium of well-known cognitive science and AI researchers. This could become a standard infrastructure for rigorous human-model behavioral comparison.

entry.title: CodeMidas: Scaling Agentic Coding RL Environments from Code Itself

author.name: Bowen Ye, Lei Li, Shicheng Li, Zihao Yue, Linghao Zhang, Hanglong Lv, Yuanxin Liu, Wenhan Ma, Hao Tian, Rang Li, Jinhao Dong, Yikai Zhao, Xiangwei Deng, Hailin Zhang, Liang Zhao, Qi Liu, Lingpeng Kong, Tong Yang, Fuli Luo

entry.summary: As featured yesterday in Research, CodeMidas is an agentic pipeline that converts implemented functionality in existing codebases into executable RL environments for coding agents, using only source code as task-specific input rather than development artifacts like issues or commits. Agents explore functionality to formulate behavioral specifications, construct execution-grounded tests, and scale environment construction, addressing the verifier reliability bottleneck for coding-agent RL.

entry.title: Scaling Discovery through Test-Time Communication

author.name: Jongho Park, Vasilis Kontonis, Shivam Garg, Akshay Krishnamurthy, Dimitris Papailiopoulos

entry.summary: As featured yesterday in Research, The paper shows that multi-agent test-time communication, where role-free agents share breakthroughs through a common directory, substantially outperforms independent parallel agents on challenging tasks, evaluated on ARC-AGI-3. A team of k communicating agents matches the success rate of 4k independent agents, with the advantage growing with k.

entry.title: OpenBlock: Constructive and Verified Content Generation for Adaptive Tile-Matching Games

author.name: Jiang Jun

entry.summary: OpenBlock is an open adaptive tile-matching game platform combining a deterministic rule-based generator with an optional learned generator, both gated by an exhaustive sequential-placement verification that guarantees every delivered piece set is fully placeable. It enables open study of adaptive difficulty in a genre where generation algorithms have been proprietary.

entry.title: Towards Robust Classroom Attendance: A Comprehensive Evaluation of Face Detection and Recognition Models

author.name: Himani Trivedi, Hiren Patel, Ridham Patel, Krutika Patel, Nancy Patel

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Visage Face dataset of 16,234 face samples captured in classroom-like conditions with varied angles, lighting, expressions, and partial occlusion, and evaluates face detection and recognition models for robust attendance systems. It addresses the gap between benchmark datasets built for controlled settings and real classroom variability. The work is an applied dataset-and-evaluation contribution.

entry.title: An Unexpected Robot Policy: Early Evaluations of GPT-6 Astra on RoboDojo and Beyond

author.name: Wenbo Zhang, Kaixuan Wang, Yutao Ouyang, Xiaoyu Huang, Liyang Li, Kailun Su, Weiyang Jin, Wenhao Chai, Haotian Liang, Zhiyang Dou, Yue Chen, Tianxing Chen

entry.summary: This paper tests whether a general LLM can serve as a robot manipulation policy without task-specific finetuning, evaluating three LLMs across all 42 RoboDojo tasks against 40 public policies over roughly 2,100 trials. GPT-6 Astra, an existing OpenAI model released in early September 2026, achieves 22.48% average success and ranks above every public policy entry, while GPT-5.5 and DeepSeek-Flash trail. The result suggests frontier multimodal LLMs are becoming surprisingly capable low-level controllers for embodied agents.

entry.title: A Synthetic Multivariate Refrigerator Time-Series Dataset for Predictive Maintenance

author.name: Islam Benamirouche, Feriel Fass, Djemel Ziou

entry.summary: The authors release a physics-inspired synthetic dataset covering 27 refrigerators at one-minute resolution with over 7 million rows, 15-20 sensor outputs per unit, six progressive degradation types, and failure logs, along with the generator and documentation. It supports failure prediction and degradation analysis research including transfer across heterogeneous sensor configurations.

entry.title: Contrastive Siamese Representation Learning for Predictive Maintenance of Electrical Submersible Pumps

author.name: Seshu K. Damarla, Xiuli Zhu

entry.summary: A fault-diagnosis framework for offshore electrical submersible pumps uses Siamese contrastive representation learning with class-imbalance awareness plus prior-corrected k-NN classification, extracting features from vibration-domain indicators and engineered harmonic relationships. It targets nonlinear operating conditions, imbalance, and variability across pump units.

entry.title: Augmenting PID Control with Deep Reinforcement Learning: A Hybrid Approach to the Industrial Benchmark

author.name: Zhengyang (Cissy), Gu, Joseph E. Hernandez, John Burtenshaw, Sean Scott, Thomas Cook, Chris Couch

entry.summary: The paper augments traditional PID controllers with deep reinforcement learning on the Industrial Benchmark, a realistic simulation with high-dimensional states, delayed effects, and conflicting multi-criteria objectives. It explores DRL's ability to discover non-obvious optimal policies while acknowledging the instability of learned policies, combining the reliability of PID with DRL's adaptivity.

entry.title: A multi-temporal dataset for mapping burned areas in the Brazilian Cerrado using time series of remote sensing imagery

author.name: Alisson Cleiton de Oliveira, Thales Sehn K\"orting

entry.summary: Releases a multi-temporal tabular dataset from CBERS-4A, CBERS-4, and AMAZONIA-1 WFI imagery for burned-area mapping in Chapada dos Veadeiros National Park (2020-2022), including spectral bands and indices. Validates Random Forest classifiers under binary and three-class burned/unburned labeling schemes.

entry.title: Explainable Predictive Condition-based Maintenance of Naval-Propulsion Systems using Fuzzy Logic

author.name: Dionisis Kalogeropoulos, Georgia Sovatzidi, Panagiotis G. Kalozoumis, Dimitris K. Iakovidis

entry.summary: The paper presents an explainable predictive maintenance framework for naval propulsion systems that adds explanation of predicted failures to condition-based maintenance, addressing the lack of user-facing interpretability in existing PdM methods. It targets operational availability and safety in the shipping industry.

entry.title: A Temporal Knowledge Graph for Music Festival Lineup Forecasting

author.name: Julia Gastinger, Thilo Dieing, Christian Meilicke, Heiner Stuckenschmidt

entry.summary: The authors release a temporal knowledge graph spanning 380 music festivals over 55 years with over 90K performance quadruples, and formalize festival lineup prediction as temporal link prediction between artists and festivals. They evaluate six TKG forecasting models and compare against LLM approaches on this task.

entry.title: TEMPER: Temporal Encoder-Masked Probabilistic Ensemble Regressor for Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Giancarlo Vercellino

entry.summary: Presents TEMPER, a univariate probabilistic forecasting algorithm combining a temporal autoencoder, differentiable masked neural decision forest, CRPS training, and Gaussian-mixture post-processing, with an R/torch implementation returning full density, distribution, quantile, and sampler functions. Evaluated on synthetic series with trend, periodic, regime-switching, and heteroskedastic components.

entry.title: A Tutorial on Prompt Engineering: From Messy Thoughts to AI Workflows

author.name: Erfan Loweimi, Hadi Daneshvar, Samira Loveymi, Samir Ouelha, Zhengjun Yue, Hajar Mozaffar, Saturnino Luz

entry.summary: This is a tutorial paper that systematizes prompt engineering as a discipline for converting informal human intent into structured AI work specifications. It proposes reusable design moves such as defining the work, curating only task-relevant context, choosing roles or moderated role panels as attention lenses, and stating affirmative quality targets, adapting Occam's razor and Chekhov's gun to keep prompts lean, and adding structured critique (steelmanning, premortems) and agentic operating loops for multi-step tasks. It is primarily educational and methodological rather than presenting new empirical results.

entry.title: NLPCC 2026 Task 10: Citation-Level Faithfulness Verification with DeBERTa Ensembles and Class-Wise Calibration

author.name: Yanling Li, Zirui Li, Mingyu Wan

entry.summary: Describes a shared-task system for citation-level faithfulness verification in AI-assisted scientific writing, ensembling a paragraph-aware cross-encoder with a document-level DeBERTa-large classifier plus class-wise decision calibration, and fusing paragraph scores with BM25 for evidence selection. The system runs fully offline and reports strong official-submission results.

entry.title: End-to-end Jordanian dialect speech-to-text self-supervised learning framework

author.name: Ali A. Safieh, Ibrahim Abu Alhaol, Rawan Ghnemat

entry.summary: The authors present an end-to-end transformer-based speech-to-text framework for Jordanian Arabic dialect, combining self-supervised training with self-training on noisy data to cope with scarce labeled speech. The framework includes customized audio-to-text processing and ingests data from multiple sources. It targets the broader problem of low-resource language and dialect coverage for speech applications.

entry.title: SKstars at SHROOM: Visions Agreement-Guided Ensembling of Zero-Shot and LoRA-Adapted Vision--Language Models

author.name: Ali Athar, Imran Ahsan, Joon-Yong Jung

entry.summary: Describes a shared-task submission for fine-grained hallucination detection in vision-language model outputs at SHROOM-Visions 2026, combining zero-shot predictions from Qwen2.5-VL-72B-Instruct with a LoRA-adapted 7B model via agreement-guided ensembling, span refinement, and confidence adjustment.

entry.title: Audio-based UAV Localization with Adaptive Temporal Correspondence via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Haoxiang Lei, Mingzheng Feng, Daotong Wang, Shenghai Yuan

entry.summary: This paper proposes an audio-based anti-UAV localization framework where an RL controller adaptively determines the audio window size per localization decision, guided by an acoustic state characterizing observation reliability, instead of using a fixed segment length. This resolves the trade-off between gathering sufficient acoustic evidence and localizing quickly. Audio offers a low-cost, illumination-independent sensing modality for UAV early warning.

entry.title: Orientation-Aware Control and Trajectory Design for Aerial RIS-Assisted Wireless Communications

author.name: Abdoul Karim A. H. Saliah, Hajar El Hammouti, Daniel Bonilla Licea, Giuseppe Silano

entry.summary: Proposes an orientation-aware framework for Aerial Reconfigurable Intelligent Surfaces mounted on multi-rotor UAVs, explicitly modeling coupled position-orientation dynamics, actuation limits, and orientation-dependent channels. The combined control and trajectory design avoids the optimistic estimates produced by point-mass or orientation-invariant models.

entry.title: Adaptive Physics-Informed Neural Networks for the Blasius Boundary-Layer Problem

author.name: Mehari Fentahun Endalew, Xiaoming John Zhang

entry.summary: This paper develops an adaptive PINN framework for the Blasius boundary-layer equation, using gradient-norm-based adaptive loss weighting, nonuniform residual-based collocation, and sequential Adam-L-BFGS optimization. It achieves high accuracy (absolute error around 1.9e-5 on f''(0)) against a known benchmark.

entry.title: HFEMCNet: A Compact Hybrid Frequency Enriched Multi Channel Network for Automatic Modulation Classification

author.name: Qamar Ijaz, Nayyer Aafaq

entry.summary: HFEMCNet is a compact deep network for automatic modulation classification that jointly uses raw IQ samples and FFT-derived hierarchical spectral features to capture spatiotemporal and frequency-domain information. It aims to outperform handcrafted-feature methods under complex channel conditions for cognitive radio and interference mitigation.

entry.title: An Iterative LangGraph Agent for Text-to-SQL: Natural Language Access to the Chicago Crime Database

author.name: Vigneshwar Ravi Rao, Rupesh Swarnakar, Fayeq Jeelani Syed{\dag}

entry.summary: Builds a six-node LangGraph agent that validates natural-language questions, fetches live schemas, generates and dry-run-validates PostgreSQL, retries on failure, and narrates results, evaluated on a hand-built 100-question benchmark over the Chicago Crime dataset. The system uses prompt engineering only, with no fine-tuning, and compares two prompt revisions across difficulty tiers.

entry.title: Infectious Bovine Pinkeye Detection Using Computer Vision and Imbalance-Aware Learning

author.name: Michael Abalo, Jameson Brennan, Hossein Moradi Rekabdarkolaee

entry.summary: This applied study compares YOLOv11 and YOLOv26 across five model sizes for automated bovine pinkeye classification on an imbalanced dataset, testing random minority oversampling and an adapted SMOTE variant. It demonstrates how class-balancing strategies affect detection performance for a real agricultural disease-screening task.

entry.title: An Affordable AI-Integrated Smart Cane for Multimodal Mobility Assistance of Visually Impaired Users

author.name: Ali Akarma, Adeel Ahmad, Toqeer Ali Syed

entry.summary: The paper presents an $88 fully offline AI-integrated smart cane on a Raspberry Pi Zero 2W, fusing RGB vision with Time-of-Flight sensing and an INT8-quantized SSD MobileNet model to deliver vibrotactile and audio alerts for visually impaired users. It targets accessibility in resource-constrained settings without cloud connectivity.

entry.title: Artificial Neural Networks as Surrogate Models in Black Box Optimization

author.name: Md Khadimul Islam Zim (Czech Academy of Sciences, Institute of Computer Science, Prague, Czech Republic), Martin Hole\v{n}a (Czech Academy of Sciences, Institute of Computer Science, Prague, Czech Republic)

entry.summary: A survey/tutorial-style treatment of using artificial neural networks as surrogate models in black-box optimization, where analytical objective descriptions are unavailable and evaluations via experiments or simulations are expensive. Covers how surrogates reduce the evaluation burden of metaheuristics and evolutionary methods.

entry.title: LLM-based Conversational AI Knowledge Assistant for MyBuddy Humanoid Robot

author.name: Hanxiao Chen

entry.summary: This work presents an LLM-based conversational knowledge assistant integrated into the MyBuddy humanoid robot, replacing rule-based dialogue systems with natural, context-aware HRI that can understand speech, reason over complex queries, and generate knowledge-rich responses. It is primarily an integration/engineering paper demonstrating LLM-backed dialogue on a humanoid platform.

entry.title: Conflicting Pattern Formation by Teams of Anonymous, Fully Disoriented Robots

author.name: Animesh Maiti, Prakhar Shukla, Subhash Bhagat

entry.summary: Studies distributed pattern formation where two groups of anonymous, oblivious, fully disoriented robots must simultaneously solve conflicting tasks: gathering at an unknown point and forming a circle. Improves on prior work by weakening the required capabilities (direction-only axis agreement and global weak multiplicity detection) for the setting.

entry.title: Campaign spending limits would reduce extinction risk (but spending limits might not accord with Constitutional principles)

author.name: MichaelDickens

entry.summary: A policy analysis arguing that US campaign finance jurisprudence (Buckley v. Valeo, Citizens United, SpeechNow.org v. FEC) enables well-funded AI companies to dominate political spending on super PACs, drowning out popular support for frontier AI regulation. The author contends that restoring contribution caps on independent expenditures would make regulation more likely and thereby reduce extinction risk.

entry.title: Prediction of Nonlinear Oscillations in a Jumping Quarter-Car Model Using Reservoir Computing

author.name: Masahisa Watanabe, Shiva Dixit, Nirmal Punetha, Swati Chauhan, Manish Dev Shirimali

entry.summary: The paper investigates echo state networks for predicting nonlinear dynamics of a jumping quarter-car model, including bifurcations and chaotic motion from intermittent tire-road contact loss. Reservoirs are trained on time-series from a smaller model, addressing smooth nonlinearities and discontinuous switching relevant to autonomous driving and ADAS for off-road vehicles.

entry.title: ResNLS: An Improved Model for Stock Price Forecasting

author.name: Yuanzhe Jia, Ali Anaissi, Basem Suleiman

entry.summary: ResNLS is a hybrid ResNet-LSTM model for stock price forecasting in which ResNet extracts dependencies between adjacent prices that LSTM then combines with residual processing of the initial time series. Experiments with previous 5-day closing prices are used to demonstrate improved prediction.

entry.title: VGG16-MCA UNet: Whole-Tumor Segmentation in 2D FLAIR MRI with Decoder-Side Channel Attention

author.name: Shubham Gajjar, Deep Joshi, Avi Poptani, Vishal Barot

entry.summary: Presents a hybrid segmentation architecture pairing an ImageNet-pretrained VGG16 encoder with a UNet decoder augmented by Multi-Channel Attention modules after skip-connection fusion, trained with Focal Tversky loss. Evaluated as a 2D FLAIR-only whole-tumor segmenter on BraTS 2020 and an LGG dataset with 5-fold cross-validation.

entry.title: Why advance automated scientific labs rather than slow them?

author.name: Master Chief

entry.summary: A LessWrong discussion post questioning whether accelerating automated scientific labs increases catastrophic risk, arguing that if the time to a future AI escape is roughly fixed, faster lab progress means more scientific infrastructure available for a rogue AI to exploit. The author evaluates and rejects common counterarguments including safe-design feasibility, benefits outweighing risk, and warning-shot dynamics, referencing skepticism after the Hugging Face incident.

entry.title: Overlay\_dx - Automating forecasting evaluation

author.name: Long Ngo, Mohammed Amine Chamli, Jonathan Rivalan, Thomas Jaillon

entry.summary: Overlay_dx is a visual evaluation metric for time-series forecasting that measures the percentage of predictions falling within confidence intervals around actual values, computing area under an overlay curve across thresholds. It aims to provide a unified, more interpretable evaluation than scalar metrics.

entry.title: SegTSim: A Big Data Driven Segmented Temporal Simulation Framework for Heterogeneous Multivariate Systems

author.name: Xinhang Li, Chenxi Geng, Yujia Sun

entry.summary: SegTSim is a segmented temporal simulation framework combining elasticity modeling, adaptive min-gating, production relocation optimization, and exchange-rate propagation, validated on US-Japan automotive trade data (about 13,000 annual records) with perturbation scenario analyses.

entry.title: A Lightweight Convolutional Neural Network for Real-Time Recognition of Hand-Drawn Geometric Shapes

author.name: Shahir Abdullah

entry.summary: This paper builds a small three-block CNN for recognizing four hand-drawn geometric shapes, using a newly collected dataset of 2,000 images that is publicly released. The system targets sketch recognition applications in education and human-computer interaction.

entry.title: When is a closed-form RGB->S/P ratio adequate? A hyperspectral characterization on natural scenes for mesopic display

author.name: Naoyuki Uchida

entry.summary: Characterizes when low-cost closed-form estimates of the scotopic-to-photopic luminance ratio from linear RGB are adequate for mesopic display transforms, using per-pixel spectral S/P from hyperspectral imagery as ground truth on natural broadband scenes rather than the narrowband sources previously studied.

entry.title: Amazon launches research initiative with Stanford University to advance AI and science

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Amazon and Stanford announce the Stanford and Amazon Research Initiative, formalizing funding across more than 10 Amazon teams for Stanford research and PhD fellowships spanning robotics, post-quantum cryptography, causal measurement, and AI-driven radiology, with an emphasis on translating breakthroughs into applications.

entry.title: We’re not ready for the e/Acc × Longevity preference cascade

author.name: Jackson Wagner

entry.summary: A speculative forecast that anti-aging sentiment could go mainstream as rapidly as AI safety concerns recently did, using the preference-cascade model to explain why the AI x-risk discourse flipped suddenly. The author argues the longevity movement could be next and that society is unprepared for the policy and social consequences.

entry.title: Monthly Roundup #46: September 2026

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi's monthly survey of AI and world news for September 2026, noting the accelerating news pace of AI coverage and touching on items such as device fingerprinting by Alibaba and various miscellanea alongside AI-focused commentary.

entry.title: Universal Observatory Graphs for Distributed Sky Coverage and Artificial Intelligence Based Interplanetary Routing

author.name: Mohammed Abdel Razek

entry.summary: This proposal models autonomous observatories at Sun-planet L2 Lagrange points as nodes in a weighted graph, with edges characterized by distance, latency, transmission power, and reliability, creating a unified representation for a cooperative interplanetary observatory network. A six-observatory configuration spanning the outer planets is examined for AI-based routing.

entry.title: Comparative Study of Quantum and Classical Machine Learning Models in Binary Classification

author.name: Anand Kumar Mishra, Ramanuj Awasthi

entry.summary: Compares a Variational Quantum Classifier and Quantum Kernel SVM against Logistic Regression, SVM, and an MLP on the Breast Cancer Wisconsin dataset using PennyLane simulation, finding that classical Logistic Regression achieved the best accuracy. A small-scale benchmark of near-term quantum machine learning against classical baselines.

entry.title: Grantmakers: Consider sharing rough probabilities & brief feedback with grantees/applicants

author.name: david reinstein

entry.summary: The author argues grantmakers should share rough funding probabilities and brief feedback with applicants, using an all-pay auction framing to show how application costs can dissipate the value of grant funding, particularly urgent in a fast-moving AI funding ecosystem.

entry.title: Where Do Chatbots Come From? What I Wish Everyone Knew About AI in 2026

author.name: Vaughn Papenhausen

entry.summary: A lay-audience explainer covering baseline knowledge about how LLMs work, why the fancy-autocomplete framing is misleading, and how to interpret AI claims in public discourse, written by a philosopher rather than an AI practitioner.

entry.title: Gratitude and the End of the World

author.name: Ephraiem Sarabamoun

entry.summary: A reflective essay examining the motives driving AGI development despite risk, arguing that a focus on the world's problems can distort what is being risked, and that cultivating gratitude for small valuable things may make people less willing to gamble away the present world.

entry.title: A Brief History of Koinometry

author.name: Benjamin Schneider

entry.summary: A work of fiction imagining the kingdom of Enopolis and its universal measurement system, the Metron, whose unit adapts to context of use until monetary incommensurability causes crisis — an allegory presumably bearing on measurement, standardization, or value commensuration.

entry.title: Will AI wipe out the human race?

author.name: scout1

entry.summary: A personal, informal essay reframing the AI extinction question from whether it can happen to how to prevent it, arguing that humans' difficulty resolving conflicts is the core problem and sketching ideas about problem-solving and curiosity.

entry.title: Cairo University – College EA Meetups Everywhere Fall 2026

author.name: Screwtape

entry.summary: An event announcement for a college Effective Altruism meetup at Cairo University as part of a Fall 2026 series, crossposted by an ACX meetup organizer with location and contact details.

entry.title: Research Summary: September 21, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's highlights span agentic environments, inference efficiency, and safety. CogGym leads with community-built infrastructure comparing human and machine cognition on matched experimental trials — a foundational evaluation step.

  • Agentic systems: MintAct (2B–8B vision-language models) unifies UI grounding and cross-platform navigation. CodeMidas converts codebases into verifiable RL environments; RecreationWorld (Qwen-linked) benchmarks hybrid GUI-plus-coding agents
  • Efficiency: Elastic Threshold Attention predicts query-conditioned sparsity thresholds to cut long-context decoding cost. Rewarding Efficient Reasoning shows reasoning models over-compute on unanswerable tasks, fixed through reward design
  • Safety: A controlled study finds AI reviewers recursively inherit collapsed scientific judgment from LLM peer reviews in training corpora. SafeStage delivers a 97-scenario lifecycle benchmark for vision-language-conditioned manipulation risks
  • Embodied AI and speech: DEXTERA turns a single RGB image into deployable dexterous policies via real-to-sim-to-real. NVIDIA's open NemotronLabs VoiceChat unifies full-duplex speech-to-speech with tool calling
entry.content:
Today's highlights span agentic environments, inference efficiency, and safety. CogGym leads with community-built infrastructure comparing human and machine cognition on matched experimental trials — a foundational evaluation step.

  • Agentic systems: MintAct (2B–8B vision-language models) unifies UI grounding and cross-platform navigation. CodeMidas converts codebases into verifiable RL environments; RecreationWorld (Qwen-linked) benchmarks hybrid GUI-plus-coding agents
  • Efficiency: Elastic Threshold Attention predicts query-conditioned sparsity thresholds to cut long-context decoding cost. Rewarding Efficient Reasoning shows reasoning models over-compute on unanswerable tasks, fixed through reward design
  • Safety: A controlled study finds AI reviewers recursively inherit collapsed scientific judgment from LLM peer reviews in training corpora. SafeStage delivers a 97-scenario lifecycle benchmark for vision-language-conditioned manipulation risks
  • Embodied AI and speech: DEXTERA turns a single RGB image into deployable dexterous policies via real-to-sim-to-real. NVIDIA's open NemotronLabs VoiceChat unifies full-duplex speech-to-speech with tool calling

entry.title: CogGym: Towards Large-Scale Comparative Evaluation of Human and Machine Cognition

author.name: Lance Ying, Jinzhou Wu, Yingshan Susan Wang, Shivam Aarya, Luca M. Schulze Buschoff, Harry Chen, Katherine M. Collins, Andrea de Varda, Shuhao Fu, Sean Dae Houlihan, Akshay K. Jagadish, Guangyuan Jiang, Samuel Kiegeland, Tetsu Kurumisawa, Rongzhi Liu, Ryan Liu, Ningshan Ma, Kathryn McGregor, Younes Strittmatter, Polina Tsvilodub, Jacob Hoover Vigly, Sarah Wu, Enjie Xu, Yiling Yun, Kelsey Allen, Tyler Brooke-Wilson, Brian Christian, Evelina Fedorenko, Michael C. Frank, Michael Franke, Tao Gao, Samuel J. Gershman, Robert D. Hawkins, Jennifer Hu, Julian Jara-Ettinger, Max Kleiman-Weiner, Sydney Levine, Tal Linzen, Hongjing Lu, Timothy O'Donnell, Desmond C. Ong, Steven T. Piantadosi, Rebecca Saxe, Eric Schulz, Tianmin Shu, Felix A. Sosa, Ilia Sucholutsky, Tan Zhi-Xuan, Tomer Ullman, Fei Xu, Ilker Yildirim, Jian-Qiao Zhu, Thomas L. Griffiths, Tobias Gerstenberg, Kevin Smith, Joshua B. Tenenbaum

entry.summary: CogGym is a scalable, unified framework grounded in cognitive science for comparing model and human behavior on matched experimental trials, using a semi-automated human-in-the-loop pipeline and a task-agnostic Experiment Markup Language. The very large, distinguished cross-disciplinary author list spans cognitive science and AI. It enables systematic testing of where LLM responses resemble or diverge from human cognition.

entry.title: Elastic Threshold Attention: Learned Contextual Sparsity for Long-Context Decoding

author.name: Themistoklis Haris, Henry Li, Maryam Karimzadehgan

entry.summary: ETA is an end-to-end trainable sparse attention architecture that predicts dynamic, contextual thresholds from query representations to decide which tokens to load during long-context decoding, avoiding the rigid heuristics of prior KV-cache sparsification. It uses multiplicative suppression to learn the sparsity policy from scratch without representation collapse, aiming for hardware-accelerated speed with dense-model quality. This targets the key memory-bandwidth bottleneck for long-context LLM inference.

entry.title: MintAct: A Unified Visual Agent for Digital Environments

author.name: Mingfei Gao, Rui Tian, Haiming Gang, Bohan Zhai, Le Zhang, Yuanzheng Gong, Di Feng, Ege \"Ozsoy, Kaixin Ma, Vishwesh Kirthivasan, O\u{g}uzhan Fatih Kar, Roman Bachmann, Anders Boesen Lindbo Larsen, Afshin Dehghan

entry.summary: MintAct is a family of vision-language models at 2B, 4B, and 8B scales that unifies UI grounding, multi-step navigation across mobile, desktop, and web, and visual tool use, matching per-domain specialists via careful environment, data, and training design. It is backed by scalable infrastructure hosting hundreds of concurrent environment instances for trajectory collection and asynchronous cross-domain RL training.

entry.title: CodeMidas: Scaling Agentic Coding RL Environments from Code Itself

author.name: Bowen Ye, Lei Li, Shicheng Li, Zihao Yue, Linghao Zhang, Hanglong Lv, Yuanxin Liu, Wenhan Ma, Hao Tian, Rang Li, Jinhao Dong, Yikai Zhao, Xiangwei Deng, Hailin Zhang, Liang Zhao, Qi Liu, Lingpeng Kong, Tong Yang, Fuli Luo

entry.summary: CodeMidas is an agentic pipeline that converts implemented functionality in existing codebases into executable RL environments for coding agents, using source code alone rather than issues or commits. Agents explore code to formulate behavioral specifications, build execution-grounded tests, and allocate agentic compute across all stages of environment construction.

entry.title: When AI Reviews Train AI Reviewers: Scientific-Judgment Collapse and Mitigation

author.name: Sy-Tuyen Ho, Minghui Liu, Furong Huang

entry.summary: This controlled study examines the recursive feedback loop where LLM-generated peer reviews enter training corpora and shape future reviewer models. Fine-tuning from Llama 3.1 8B on official ICLR reviews and then training successors on mixtures of official and synthetic 2024 reviews, the authors show synthetic reviews compress rating distributions and reduce semantic diversity of judgments, with proposed mitigations. It is directly relevant as AI-assisted review proliferates.

entry.title: RecreationWorld: Scalable and Verifiable Environments for Hybrid Computer-Use Agents

author.name: Shuai Bai, Jiayong Deng, Yikun Fu, Chang Gao, Xuhao Hu, Mianqiu Huang, Yizhen Jiang, Yuheng Jing, Dehui Kong, Keliang Li, Ning Li, Wanli Li, Dayiheng Liu, Dunjie Lu, Changwei Luo, Que Shen, Zheyuan Wang, Zijian Wang, Jie Wu, Gao Wu, Zhihui Xie, Rui Xie, Haiyang Xu, An Yang, Jiakang Yuan, Yanming Zhang, Jiajun Zhang, Xi Zhang, Zhenru Zhang, Zhuo Zhen, Mingkang Zhu, Bowen Zhou

entry.summary: This paper introduces RecreationWorld, a benchmark framework for hybrid computer-use agents that must interleave GUI interaction and software development across five platforms (Ubuntu, macOS, Windows, Android, and Web). Agents are given a running reference application and must discover its behavior and build a faithful reimplementation with no prescribed workflow, using a unified harness combining native GUI control and coding tools. This addresses a real gap, as prior CUA evaluation has treated graphical use and coding as separate skills.

entry.title: NemotronLabs VoiceChat: An Open Full-duplex Speech-to-Speech Model with Tool Calling Capabilities

author.name: Jagadeesh Balam, Travis Bartley, Edresson Casanova, Sanjay Chauhan, Chen Chen, Zhehuai Chen, Zijia Chen, Francesco Ciannella, Slyne Deng, Mikyas Desta, Harishchandra Dubey, Slim Essid, Nourchene Ferchichi, Boris Ginsburg, Mariana Graterol Fuenmayor, Negar Habibi, Kevin Hu, Anand Joseph, Viraj Karandikar, Myungjong Kim, Viacheslav Klimkov, Seelan Lakshmi Narasimhan, Lily Lee, Jason Li, Eileen Long, Ameya Mahabaleshwarkar, Aditya Malte, Adi Margolin, Sasha Meister, Valentin Mendelev, Oluwatobi Olabiyi, Ankita Pasad, Yifan Peng, Elena Rastorgueva, Jayda Ritchie, Jason Roche, Nikhil Srihari, Yuanhang Su, Yoshi Suhara, Viet Anh Trinh, Jinhan Wang, Piotr Zelasko, Hui Wang, Puhui Meng, Chaosen Zhang, Yunsheng Liu, Shawn Wang, Wenjing Li, Zhonglei He

entry.summary: Introduces NemotronLabs VoiceChat, an open full-duplex speech-to-speech model from NVIDIA combining a streaming speech encoder, a decoder-only LM with parallel output streams for agent text and function calls, an auxiliary RNN-T transcription branch, and a streaming TTS decoder. It achieves the lowest pause-handling takeover rates among evaluated open-weight systems on Full-Duplex-Bench 1.0 while natively invoking tools mid-conversation.

entry.title: Rewarding Efficient Reasoning Improves Abstention on Underspecified Tasks in Reasoning Models

author.name: Polina Tsvilodub, Max H\"oth, Michael Franke, Bj\"orn Deiseroth, Carina Kauf

entry.summary: Shows that large reasoning models waste compute by generating longer chains of thought on unanswerable tasks than answerable ones, in contrast to human behavior where effort on unanswerable tasks is bounded by answerable tasks. Inspired by resource-rational cognition, the authors introduce a GRPO reward that encourages efficient reasoning about task answerability, improving abstention behavior.

entry.title: DEXTERA: From a Single Image to Deployable Dexterous Manipulation via Real-to-Sim-to-Real

author.name: Jin Wu, Lianjie Yuan, Zeyan Sun, Yuanyuan Lei, Disi A, Bicheng Han, Fangzhou Xia

entry.summary: DEXTERA is an automated real-to-sim-to-real framework that turns a single RGB image into deployable dexterous manipulation policies, factorizing the scene into Gaussian backgrounds and articulated assets with VLM-inferred physical parameters, then performing metric alignment and policy transfer. It avoids costly manual digital-twin construction and real-world data collection.

entry.title: On Repulsive and Attractive Teachers: Separating Correctness from Behavior in Self-Distillation

author.name: Anton Baumann, Akmal Ashirmatov, Leo Schmidt-Traub, Frederike L\"ubeck, Jonas H\"ubotter, Thomas Kleine Buening, Andreas Krause

entry.summary: Studies on-policy self-distillation with privileged information, contrasting attractive distillation (moving toward a privileged teacher) with repulsive distillation (moving away). It finds both induce strong opposing behavioral shifts - attraction suppresses exploration and shortens reasoning - so correctness signals are entangled with unintended behavioral changes.

entry.title: SafeStage: Evaluating Safety Before, During, and After Vision-Language-Conditioned Robot Manipulation

author.name: Jinzhu Luo, Qi Zhang, Wei Wang, Wei Jiang

entry.summary: SafeStage is a lifecycle-structured benchmark with 97 risk scenarios evaluating vision-language-conditioned manipulation safety across three stages: initial-state hazards, execution-time safety (contacts, trajectories, region violations), and post-task consequences. It addresses the gap left by evaluations focused only on task success or isolated constraints.

entry.title: Can Agents Design Better Chips with a Higher Level Abstraction?

author.name: Zijian Ding, Yang Zou, Yizhou Sun, Jason Cong

entry.summary: This paper compares LLM-agent chip design flows operating at RTL versus higher-level HLS abstractions, proposing AHRR, which combines agent-based HLS design with post-HLS RTL refinement. On an 11-task FPGA benchmark suite, AHRR achieves a 2.6x geometric-mean speedup over direct RTL design. It provides evidence that abstraction level choice is a key lever for agentic hardware design.

entry.title: World Modeling in Transformers

author.name: Pierre Beckmann, Matthieu Queloz, Andre Freitas

entry.summary: Using TaxiGPT, a transformer trained on random walks through Manhattan previously interpreted as lacking a coherent internal map, the authors show via mechanistic analysis and causal interventions that the model does represent streets, intersections, position, and a goal compass. Failures are traced to interference between superposed intersection features, and an affordance-packing trick mitigates them.

entry.title: Scaling Discovery through Test-Time Communication

author.name: Jongho Park, Vasilis Kontonis, Shivam Garg, Akshay Krishnamurthy, Dimitris Papailiopoulos

entry.summary: This paper studies whether multi-agent communication at test time improves problem solving, using ARC-AGI-3 as a benchmark requiring novel problem solving. Agents with no predefined roles share findings via a common directory, and the authors show a team of k communicating agents matches the success rate of 4k independent agents — an advantage that grows with team size, because a shared breakthrough can propagate across the group.

entry.title: SWE-Proof: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World Issues with Machine-Checked Proofs?

author.name: George Ma, Benjamin Mikek, Haoyu Li, Ferhat Erata, Yuhao Zhang, Zeren Shui, Behrooz Omidvar Tehrani, Jun Huan, Murali Krishna Ramanathan, Somayeh Sojoudi, Hao Zhou, Anoop Deoras

entry.summary: The paper presents Benchproofer, a pipeline that converts coding tasks with known correct patches into formally verified tasks by writing specifications, summarizing existing functions as axioms, and admitting instances only after machine-checked verification. SWE-Proof thereby benchmarks whether LLMs can resolve real repository issues with proofs, avoiding incomplete test suites and memorization.

entry.title: Authorization Revocation for Long-Running AI Agents: Root-Scoped Quiescence under Delegation and Asynchronous Execution

author.name: Genliang Zhu, Chu Wang

entry.summary: Defines a formal protocol called root-scoped authorization quiescence for revoking agent permissions in long-running AI agent systems, where credentials, delegated tasks, and asynchronous operations outlive the initiating process. The work formalizes how to prove that no stale authority survives a revocation cut while allowing safe rebinding to current support.

entry.title: PhysioBench: A Unified Benchmark for Physiological Signal Question Answering

author.name: Mengxuan Li, Junfa Chen, Jinze Xia, Yundan Chen, Lixin Fan, Ke Liu, Keyue Shi, Haishuai Wang

entry.summary: Introduces PhysioBench, a unified benchmark that harmonizes annotations from 22 public physiological signal datasets into 61.4 million question-answer pairs spanning 30 tasks, with each answer traceable to its source signal segment. It evaluates 21 models on instruction-following across physiological modalities, exposing gaps in current foundation models' ability to handle task-agnostic natural-language interfaces for clinical signal analysis.

entry.title: ServeGuard: Verifiable, Bounded-Residual Confinement of Operator-Invisible Channels Without Revealing the Certified Read Factor

author.name: Dominik Dahlem, Rui Vieira

entry.summary: The paper tackles backdoors in third-party adapters for open-weight language models, arguing detection is provably unsound for payloads hidden in the safety monitor's blind subspace since benign adaptation uses that subspace too. Instead of detecting such channels, ServeGuard constructs adapters that read input only through a certified direction set, making operator-invisible channels structurally absent, with a cryptographic-style proof of confinement that does not reveal the publisher's core asset.

entry.title: Watermarkable Multi-Draft Speculative Sampling via Poisson Processes

author.name: Yanxiao Liu, Sicheng Wan, Zhan Gao, Deniz G\"und\"uz

entry.summary: This work tackles the difficult combination of speculative sampling for efficient LLM inference and watermarking for output provenance, which prior work suggested may be jointly impossible. Using a multi-draft speculative sampling algorithm built on Poisson processes, the authors improve the efficiency-provenance trade-off frontier and embed an unbiased watermark without degrading speculative acceptance.

entry.title: ZYT-World: A Real-Time Controllable World Model for Closed-Loop Autonomous-Driving Simulation

author.name: Boni Hu, Xiong Wei, Haoming Huang, Yong Huang, Chenbo Wang, Yi Yang, Jiancheng Wang, Ruicheng Zhu, Zhimin Yang, Guanglai Liu, Qiaowan Jin, Dongzhuo Wang, Haiwei Kuang, Jiajun Fan, Yue Wu, Jiaxin Wei, Hao Sun, Feihong Yan, Wei Bi, Kaixuan Wang, Zichao Guo, Xiaozhi Chen

entry.summary: ZYT-World is a production-oriented driving world model that natively generates a mixed fisheye-pinhole camera rig (four fisheye views over 180 degrees plus three pinhole views) at native resolutions for closed-loop testing of end-to-end and VLA driving policies. It combines projection-specific Plucker adapters, ego-motion adaptive layer normalization, and pixel-aligned layout conditioning to reconcile causal per-timestep interaction with long-horizon stability and low latency while preserving scene identity on revisits. Addresses three deployment requirements typically ignored in academic world models.

entry.title: Catch Me If You Can: Real-Time Feedback Denoising for Responsive VLAs

author.name: Yiheng Ji, Xingru Zhou, Luis Sentis, Mingyo Seo

entry.summary: VLA-Feedback introduces a two-timescale architecture for vision-language-action models that pairs low-frequency diffusion planning with high-frequency visual feedback by retaining the final denoising step as a lightweight feedback mechanism. This makes open-loop action chunks responsive to objects moving or scenes changing during execution.

entry.title: Hiding in Plain Sight: A Diffusion-based Mitigation of Geolocation Privacy Leakage in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yining Wang, Xi Li, Mi Zhang, Xiaohan Zhang, Xiaoyu You, Zhenxing Qian, Mi Wen

entry.summary: Systematically studies geolocation privacy leakage in multimodal large reasoning models, showing that refusal-based safeguards are critically insufficient since crafted jailbreak prompts can achieve 100% response rates for inferring locations from photos. The paper identifies weaknesses in existing perturbation-based defenses and proposes a diffusion-based mitigation that protects user location privacy in shared images.

entry.title: Demonstration Synthesis from a Single Scan via Gaussian Splatting for Visuomotor Policy Learning

author.name: Beichen Wang, Yuen-Hei Yeung, V. R. Sridhar Devarakonda, Xuesu Xiao

entry.summary: GaussianFactory is a data engine that mass-produces visuomotor demonstrations from a single video scan, reconstructing the scene as an editable 3D Gaussian Splatting replica and planning grasps and trajectories kinematically without a physics engine in the generation loop. This drastically reduces the cost of collecting environment-matched demonstrations.

entry.title: Detecting Hallucination in LLMs: Tracing the Topological Signatures of Impaired Context Sharing

author.name: Amir Jalilifard, Anderson Rocha, Eric Wong, Marcos Medeiros Raimundo

entry.summary: The authors analyze Forman-Ricci curvature in attention graphs to identify information bottlenecks that characterize hallucinated responses, capturing both semi-local and global information-flow patterns. Their single-pass detection method consistently outperforms attention-based and multi-response baselines across two hallucination benchmarks and multiple LLMs. It offers a cheap, internal-signal approach to hallucination detection without multiple sampled generations.

entry.title: How Much of a Real Workload Can LLM-Generated GPU Kernels Actually Reach?

author.name: Gaurav Agarwal, Ashish Garg, Isha Singhal

entry.summary: The paper evaluates five model configurations on KernelBench level 1, finding a frontier model produces correct kernels for 91.1% of problems with verified speedups on 22 of 56 tasks, while open-weights models lag far behind. It then profiles seven real workloads to show the addressable fraction of runtime for such kernels is only 8.9-58.2%, since 80-86% of transformer time is in cuBLAS GEMM and FlashAttention.

entry.title: AtomEgo: Exploring Ego-Robot Integration for Embodied Foundation Model Pretraining

author.name: Di Wu, Dongchen Zheng, Junhe Sheng, Zhongxing Wei, Songxin Zhang, Zejian Xie, Xiaoquan Sun, Junyang Zheng, Zhuoyang Song, Jiaxing Zhang, Jiayu Chen

entry.summary: Presents a systematic study of co-training embodied foundation models on large-scale egocentric human video, supported by a curated corpus of about 2,659 hours and a scalable data pipeline. Across VLA and world-action architectures it compares joint co-training, progressive embodiment-aligned transfer, and other paradigms for bridging the human-robot embodiment gap.

entry.title: Stiefel-AdamW: Geometry-Aware AdamW for Linear Factorization Blocks

author.name: Emanuele Zangrando, Marco Sutti, Francesco Tudisco

entry.summary: Stiefel-AdamW is a near drop-in replacement for AdamW tailored to linear factorization blocks W=BA, which pervade LoRA adapters, low-rank layers, and attention query-key products and suffer from non-unique factorizations that destabilize training. The method constrains one factor to the Stiefel manifold while optimizing the other with Euclidean AdamW, resolving the geometry-induced pathology. This could improve training stability and usable learning rates across many architectures.

entry.title: Recursive Language Models Generalize Out of Domain

author.name: Chenxiao Yang, Zhiyuan Li, David McAllester, Nathan Srebro

entry.summary: The paper theoretically and empirically compares chain-of-thought LLMs, which read the full trace, with recursive language models that solve each subtask in an isolated context. It shows recursion costs little in-distribution but prevents context-based shortcut learning out of domain, since simplicity bias selects the shortcut solution that fails when surrounding tokens change.

entry.title: How Many Humans Is a Judge Panel Worth?

author.name: Chao Li, Yingying Yu, Yunfeng Li

entry.summary: Audits LLM judge panels against empirical human label distributions, retaining disagreement that binary error metrics collapse, using a spectral quantity nu_H (effective human-equivalent panel size) and a separate distributional-error quantity nu_MSE. Across three ChaosNLI tasks, the same 32-judge panels correspond to only about 4-6.5 conditionally independent humans for diversity but 2.3-3.75 for squared error, with a spectral identity separating eigenvalues, member energies, and averaging-direction weights.

entry.title: Safe Real-Time Policy Steering via Noise-Space Trajectory Optimization for One-Step Generative Policies

author.name: Qingyi Chen, Joseph Ruan, Zachary Kingston

entry.summary: INSPO formulates inference-time steering of one-step generative robot policies as trajectory optimization over the policy's input noise space, evaluating constraints on the induced state trajectory without modifying generated actions directly.
