This enables real-time adaptation of pretrained policies to constraints like collision avoidance, avoiding expensive iterative gradient guidance through diffusion or flow processes.

entry.title: Skel-WAM: A Hand-Skeleton-Conditioned World Action Model for Human-to-Robot Manipulation Transfer

author.name: Zetao Cai, Yaping Li, Yiqun Wang, Xinyu Zhan, Yuyin Yang, Haoxiang Ma, Kailin Li, Tao Lu, Jiangmiao Pang, Linning Xu, Dahua Lin

entry.summary: Skel-WAM is a world action model that transfers manipulation knowledge from inexpensive human videos to robots by aligning embodiments through a unified hand-skeleton motion interface. It combines skeleton overlays grounded in the scene with structured 2.5-D keypoints encoding hand kinematics, with Video and Keypoint Experts learning visual and skeletal dynamics via a Mixture-of-Transformers.

entry.title: GVPO++: Group Variance Policy Optimization for LLM Post-Training and On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Kaichen Zhang, Yuzhong Hong, Junwei Bao, Hongfei Jiang, Yang Song, Dingqian Hong, Hui Xiong

entry.summary: GVPO is a post-training method integrating the analytical solution of KL-constrained reward maximization into gradient weighting, avoiding the importance-sampling reliance that causes GRPO training instability. Its gradient has an interpretable meaning as mean squared error between central distances of implicit and actual rewards, and it extends to on-policy distillation. This contributes to the rapidly evolving RL post-training method space.

entry.title: Object Detection Benchmarks are Incomplete: The Role of Label Errors and Annotation Uncertainty

author.name: Sarina Penquitt, Jonathan Klees, Antonia van Betteray, Parssa Jashnieh, Peter Stehr, Matthias Rottmann, Lars Schmarje

entry.summary: Re-annotation of COCO, Pascal VOC, Cityscapes, and KITTI reveals substantial missing annotations, with up to +60% more objects on KITTI and +40% on COCO, mostly small, occluded, or dense instances. The paper shows benchmark quality is limited by annotation incompleteness, that missing labels are the dominant error source across datasets, and introduces a scalable high-recall annotation pipeline. Important audit of the field's foundational evaluation data.

entry.title: Attention-Aware Routing: Coupling Routing and Attention in MoEs

author.name: Despoina Kosmopoulou, Anastasios Tsetsilas, Efthymios Georgiou, Giannis Karamanolakis, Swastik Roy, Alexandros Potamianos

entry.summary: AAR augments Mixture-of-Experts routers with temporal and spectral features from sliding windows of attention weights, giving the router contextual state beyond the hidden state while keeping the base transformer frozen. It improves GSM8K by 3.37 points over a routing-only SFT baseline on OLMoE and reveals a coupled circuit between routing and attention. The finding that routing changes propagate through residual connections is a notable interpretability contribution for MoE design.

entry.title: Information-Gain Rewards over Diversity-Pruned Tests: GT-Anchored Verifier Co-Training for Reliable Code Generation

author.name: Ana Nunez, Peyman Najafirad

entry.summary: CoVer is a single-policy GRPO framework that co-trains a model as coder and test author, addressing permissiveness collapse and concentration bias in self-play test generation. It scores self-generated tests by information gain against a graded ground-truth-anchored correctness signal and diversity-prunes the test pool. This targets a key failure mode of RL for code generation beyond fixed test suites.

entry.title: OmniVChat: Synthesizing, Benchmarking, and Training for Native Audio-Visual Dialogue

author.name: Haolin He, Yunfei Chu, Qi Chen, Wen Huang, Yuan Feng, Muzhi Zhu, Zheqi Dai, Haoning Xu, Dongchao Yang, Chunyat Wu, Zining Liang, Zhengxi Liu, Xiquan Li, Xie Chen, Xize Cheng, Qize Yang, Jin Xu, Qiuqiang Kong

entry.summary: Defines the OmniVChat task where omni models receive raw audio and video directly from a user and respond in text without separate ASR or captioning, reducing latency and preserving perceptual cues. The work contributes a data synthesis pipeline, a benchmark, and training methods to overcome data scarcity and evaluation constraints for native audio-visual dialogue.

entry.title: Micro-Collaborative Poisoning: A Distributed Attack on RAG Systems

author.name: Pedro Pereira, Eva Maia, Isabel Pra\c{c}a

entry.summary: Introduces a distributed RAG poisoning attack in which a false claim is split across multiple locally plausible documents rather than concentrated in one malicious passage, so weak adversarial signals accumulate during retrieval. Evaluation across 108 configurations shows the attack succeeds broadly across retriever architectures, retrieval depths, and generator models.

entry.title: TierKV: Long-Context On-Device LLMs via Predictive Multi-Tier KV Caching

author.name: Zhihao Shu, Md Musfiqur Rahman Sanim, Jie Hu, Kun Yuan, Minghai Qin, Gagan Agrawal, Wei Niu

entry.summary: TierKV is a mobile LLM inference framework with Predictive Multi-Tier Cache Optimization that forecasts future KV-cache demand from prefill hidden states before decoding begins, addressing the KV cache as the dominant memory bottleneck for long contexts on devices. It aims to avoid the reconstruction overhead, irreversible token loss, and I/O stalls of prior compression/eviction/offloading schemes. This supports long-context multimodal LLM workloads on mobile hardware.

entry.title: Optimal Randomized Proper Online Learning

author.name: Zachary Chase, Idan Mehalel

entry.summary: The paper proves that the optimal expected mistake bound for randomized proper online learning of a function class is O(L log T), where L is the Littlestone dimension, improving the prior O(L log^6 T) bound of Daskalakis and Golowich (STOC 2022). The result is optimal up to a universal constant for worst-case classes. This is a clean, significant improvement in a core learning theory problem.

entry.title: BrainWideBench: Benchmarking large-scale pretraining and across-animal transfer in multi-region neural recordings

author.name: Alexandre Andre, Shivashriganesh P. Mahato, Vinam Arora, Keshav Balaji, Divyansha Lachi, Nanda H. Krishna, Jingyun Xiao, Yizi Zhang, Ximeng Mao, Wenrui Ma, Han Yu, International Brain Laboratory, Daniel Birman, Niccol\`o Bonacchi, Gaelle A. Chapuis, Joana A. Catarino, Felicia Davatolhagh, Mayo Faulkner, Laura Freitas-Silva, Fei Hu, Julia M. Huntenburg, Anup Khanal, In\^es Laranjeira, Petrina Lau, Guido T. Meijer, Nathaniel J. Miska, Jean-Paul Noel, Alejandro Pan-Vazquez, Georg Raiser, Cyrille Rossant, Karolina Z. Socha, Anne E. Urai, Miles J. Wells, Steven J. West, Olivier Winter, Blake Richards, Guillaume Lajoie, Cole Hurwitz, Mehdi Azabou, Matthew R. Whiteway, Liam Paninski, Eva L. Dyer

entry.summary: BrainWideBench is a benchmark for across-animal transfer learning on multi-region neural recordings, built on the International Brain Laboratory Brainwide Map dataset covering 276 brain regions from 139 mice in a sensory decision-making task. It standardizes evaluation protocols to test whether large-scale neural data can yield general-purpose, transferable neural representations.

entry.title: Complex Problem Solving in Large Language Models: A Statistical Control Survey and Diagnostic Framework

author.name: Jiazhang Cai, Tao Wang, Ruidong Zhang, Siyuan Li, Terry Ma, Luyang Fang, Haoran Lu, Huimin Cheng, Yingchuan Zhang, Shushan Wu, Rui Xie, Lin Tang, Chao Huang, Rongjie Liu, Ziyu Liu, Meizhi Yu, Yongkai Chen, Yifan Zhou, Zeliang Sun, Chang Liu, Zhen Xiang, Wei Xiao, Zixin Rao, Xinyi Liu, Yutong Hu, Mengrui Zhang, Jing Zhang, Weidi Luo, Jincheng Yu, Zhengliang Liu, Weihang You, Hanqi Jiang, Yi Pan, Junhao Chen, Xinliang Li, Tianming Liu, Wenxuan Zhong, Ping Ma

entry.summary: A large-author survey that reframes LLM complex problem solving as a sequential estimation-and-decision problem over a latent solution state, where a controller maintains beliefs, updates them on noisy intermediate evidence, and decides to commit, verify, branch, roll back, or abstain. It provides a statistical control framework and diagnostic tools to explain early-step error amplification, prompt brittleness, and failure to revise incorrect commitments.

entry.title: From Pretraining to Proficiency: Real-World Subtask RL for Long-Horizon Manipulation with Minimal Human Intervention

author.name: Sichang Su, Benjamin Yang, Zhiyun Deng, Boyuan Liang, Yip Fun Yeung, Zelin Wang, Lingfeng Sun

entry.summary: PARTS is a real-world reinforcement learning framework that fine-tunes pretrained robot foundation policies on the specific subtasks where they fail, rather than collecting full-task demonstrations for supervised fine-tuning. A frozen pretrained policy supplies nominal actions during rollouts, concentrating practice at bottleneck subtasks with minimal human intervention to solve long-horizon manipulation tasks under sparse rewards.

entry.title: CASCADE Against Jailbreaks: Combination Across Stages with Controlled Attack-Defense Evaluation

author.name: Jiale Luo, Eric Han

entry.summary: CASCADE presents the first systematic study of LLM jailbreak defenses combined within and across pipeline stages (input modification, output guards, etc.) under a consistent black-box, single-turn threat model. It standardizes evaluation via a principled attack-success-rate formulation with controlled query budgets and explicit fairness constraints, then derives a decision framework for which defenses to deploy at each stage. This addresses fragmented prior evaluations with inconsistent metrics.

entry.title: DRT: Dense Reasoning Trace for Efficient and Grounded Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Wan Xu, Yuanfan Guo, Kevin Han, LaLa Chen, Wangmeng Zuo

entry.summary: DRT replaces natural-language chain-of-thought in multimodal LLMs with compact structured traces that include symbolic connectors and disentangle visual observations from logical deductions. Dense Trace Initialization internalizes this reasoning mode, substantially improving token efficiency while strengthening visual grounding. Directly targets the information-dilution problem of verbose CoT in MLLMs.

entry.title: A Differentiable Ray-Wave Framework for Hybrid Refractive-Diffractive System Modeling and Optimization

author.name: Jiazhou Cheng, Margaret Gao, Yixuan Shao, Chenkai Mao, Tom D. Milster, Jonathan A. Fan

entry.summary: The paper presents a differentiable ray-wave modeling framework for hybrid refractive-diffractive optical systems that plugs into standard ray tracing pipelines, supporting planar and curvilinear diffractive surfaces with arbitrary scalar holographic profiles. This enables end-to-end optimization of optical systems that were previously hard to model due to mixed ray and wave physics.

entry.title: Noctif3R: Feed-Forward Monocular Real-Time SLAM for Photon-Limited Scenes on Embedded Hardware

author.name: Mihir Chauhan, Aditya Uday Abhang, Kevin Biju Mathew, Aniket Bera

entry.summary: Noctif3R targets real-time monocular SLAM in extremely low light on power-constrained embedded hardware, a regime where existing systems like DROID-SLAM and DPV-SLAM degrade catastrophically. The paper quantifies failure modes (e.g., DROID-SLAM returning uninformative trajectories) and proposes a feed-forward approach for photon-limited scenes.

entry.title: FAN: Foresight Action Normalization for Continual Adaptation of Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Yijun Hong, Jiarun Zhu, Xiaoquan Sun, Le Xu, Qijun He, Xin Jin, Mingqi Yuan, Wenjun Zeng, Jiayu Chen

entry.summary: This paper studies a foundational but overlooked mechanism in continual adaptation of vision-language-action models: action normalization, which determines the coordinate system policies use to perceive and execute actions. The authors systematically evaluate five normalization strategies across four real-world task streams with single-arm and bimanual settings and propose a foresight approach for continual skill acquisition without forgetting.

entry.title: SeeQ: Training Generalist Value Functions for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Saksham Singh, Zheyuan Hu, Max Sobol Mark, Jeffrey Yu, Zackory Erickson, Aviral Kumar

entry.summary: SeeQ addresses brittleness of generalist robot policies on long-horizon tasks by learning Q-values for the currently active subtask rather than the sparse task-level reward, shortening the value-prediction horizon and enabling effective TD learning. Subtask-level annotations during training and active-subtask conditioning at inference allow value functions to rank candidate actions and guide policy improvement. This improves multi-stage and retry-heavy manipulation.

entry.title: SAGE: Safety-Aligned Gradient Enforcement for Human--Robot Collaboration

author.name: Yisen Li, Hao Zhang, Ruize Geng, Yves Tseng, Ding Zhao, H. Eric Tseng

entry.summary: SAGE addresses two learning mismatches in multi-agent RL for human-robot collaboration that combines explainable decision-tree policies with control-barrier-function (CBF) safety filtering. Its shield-annealed internalization layer uses differentiable finite-penalty projections to align independently optimized actors with team-level safety-constrained updates.

entry.title: RAYA: Learning Where and When to Intervene for Robot Recovery

author.name: Ishaan Mahajan, Charles Chen, Frederike D\"umbgen, Brian Plancher

entry.summary: RAYA is a hybrid learned-analytic framework for robot recovery based on the insight that recoverability must inform actions as they are chosen rather than veto them afterward. It places a learned finite-horizon recoverability margin inside a constrained optimal controller and pairs it with a bounded learned scheduler that shifts task weights as recoverability shrinks, enabling recovery when the nominal plan has already spent control authority.

entry.title: RBS-Attention: Radius-Bounded Sparse Prefill for Long-Context Large Language Models

author.name: Chuxu Song, Jiuqi Wei, Zhencan Peng

entry.summary: This paper introduces RBS-Attention, a training-free sparse-prefill method for long-context LLM inference that addresses the mean dilution problem, where block centroids hide highly relevant tokens. It uses a centroid base branch plus a rescue branch based on maximum key-block radius, with independent thresholding to combine masks. This matters because prefill cost is a growing bottleneck for long-context deployment.

entry.title: Implicit Rule Induction with Test-Time Task Embeddings in ARC-like Tasks

author.name: Adrien Deli\`ege, Claas Beger, Marc Van Droogenbroeck, Melanie Mitchell

entry.summary: The paper studies whether success on ARC-like benchmarks reflects genuine rule induction or shortcuts, introducing a two-step test-time training protocol for VARC that first finetunes only the task embedding and then the backbone. Evaluation across ARC-AGI-1, ConceptARC, and controlled datasets with known rules probes the structure of learned solutions. The collaboration with Melanie Mitchell adds credibility to the abstraction-and-reasoning focus.

entry.title: LogicTrack: Auditing Reasoning Trajectories of Large Language Models with Formal Logic Solvers

author.name: Jingyu Hu, Shu Yang, Weiru Liu, Di Wang

entry.summary: LogicTrack is a neuro-symbolic framework that audits chain-of-thought reasoning by converting each intermediate step into symbolic form and verifying it with automated theorem provers. It introduces a Solver-Based Backtracking Reward that scores logical soundness step-by-step and guides backtracking tree search, targeting the common failure where models reach correct answers via flawed reasoning.

entry.title: BI-Agent and BI-Bench: Towards Automating End-to-End Business Intelligence

author.name: Chuxuan Hu, Yeye He, Penny Zhou, Wee Hyong Tok, Daniel Kang, Surajit Chaudhuri

entry.summary: This paper from Microsoft-affiliated researchers introduces BI-Agent and BI-Bench, evaluating whether large language models can handle the full business intelligence workflow end-to-end — identifying relevant tables, performing data transformations, building join relationships, and answering business questions — without manual preparation steps. The benchmark is built from a large collection of real-world BI projects harvested from public sources, grounding the evaluation in authentic enterprise use cases like those seen in Power BI and Tableau.

entry.title: Talking Past the Machine: Morality, Politeness, and Alignment in Human-AI Dialogue

author.name: Marina Mitiaeva, Lu Xiao

entry.summary: Analyzes roughly 26,600 multi-turn dialogues of human-ChatGPT and human-human conversation with mixed-effects models to compare morality, politeness, and alignment in cooperative dialogue. It finds a consistent dissociation: AI reproduces surface features of cooperative communication without the underlying social architecture, raising questions about evaluation and trust.

entry.title: ForceTwin: Physics-informed Digital Twins for Robotic Manipulation from Instrumented Human Interaction

author.name: Tim Engelbracht, Ren\'e Zurbr\"ugg, Mayank Mittal, Marco Hutter, Marc Pollefeys, Hermann Blum, Zuria Bauer

entry.summary: Presents ForceTwin, a system for building physics-informed digital twins of articulated objects by capturing instrumented human interaction to identify state-dependent physical parameters like inertia, friction, springs, and door closers that are invisible to appearance-based pipelines. This enables physically plausible simulation assets for robotic manipulation, going beyond kinematics-only digital twins.

entry.title: Sparse Priors for Efficient Distribution Learning

author.name: Saumya Goyal, Barnab\'as P\'oczos

entry.summary: This paper addresses the pessimistic minimax bounds for distribution learning in high dimensions by introducing a class of sparse priors, with a Sparse Dimension measure quantifying sparsity over distributions. It proves a Bayesian risk lower bound of roughly sqrt(k/n) for k-sparse priors under common distance metrics, matching upper bounds. The work matters because it provides theoretical grounding for why generative modeling succeeds in practice despite poor worst-case guarantees.

entry.title: IntBMoE: Integrating Block-Level Conditioning into Expert Composition for Full-Participation Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Ran Cheng, Longfei Xu, Zheng Liu, Kaikui Liu, Xiangxiang Chu

entry.summary: IntBMoE is a Mixture-of-Experts design that disentangles participation, execution, and materialization for each token, letting a model draw knowledge from many experts while keeping compute and memory costs low. Existing sparse MoE variants each trade one of these quantities against the others, and this block-conditioned scheme restores full participation without the usual cost blowups. Architectural efficiency work of this kind directly informs how large-scale MoE LLMs are built.

entry.title: Abstention and Noise Filtering: Two Missing Primitives of Softmax Attention

author.name: Richard Zhe Wang

entry.summary: The paper argues and experimentally shows that value-pathway gating helps language model pretraining because it supplies two primitives softmax attention lacks: abstention (allowing heads to output nothing via a learned sink logit) and noise filtering (suppressing superposed-feature interference in the residual stream via a value gate). Experiments span matched models from 10M to 350M parameters.

entry.title: Extreme classification: beating chance with one training example from each class

author.name: Kevin Bleakley (LMO, CELESTE), Aaditya Ramdas

entry.summary: Studies a minimal two-sample classification setting: given one labeled observation from each of two unknown distributions, can a target be classified better than chance whenever the distributions differ? The authors show one-nearest-neighbor succeeds for a broad Gaussian family but can fail badly for smooth one-dimensional densities, and construct a randomized kernel rule whose expected accuracy is exactly 1/2 plus one quarter of the squared MMD, with characteristic kernels obtained on general measurable spaces.

entry.title: FootQuery: Future-Touchdown-Guided Retrieval from Depth History for Perceptive Humanoid Locomotion

author.name: Tao Dong, Jia Yu, Yuxuan Fan, Linna Zhao, Jiaqi Gong, Andong Yang, Chao Gao, Guyue Zhou

entry.summary: This paper presents FootQuery, a framework enabling humanoid robots to traverse complex terrain by retrieving terrain information from historical depth-camera frames at the moment a foot touches down, even when that terrain is no longer visible due to occlusion. The policy predicts future touchdown locations and uncertainty from proprioception and uses these to query sparsely sampled depth history, with training supervision projecting realized contacts into historical images. This addresses a real gap in perceptive locomotion where footholds disappear from view before contact.

entry.title: End-to-End Hard-Label Cryptanalytic Model Extraction Using Efficient Sign Recovery

author.name: Akira Ito, Takayuki Miura, Yosuke Todo

entry.summary: The authors improve hard-label model extraction of ReLU networks, building on Carlini et al.'s Eurocrypt 2025 polynomial-time attack, by making the expensive sign-recovery step efficient and black-box implementable. This yields an end-to-end practical extraction attack where the adversary sees only final output labels, underscoring that model parameters remain vulnerable even under strict information constraints.

entry.title: Multiplicative Optimism for Constant Regret in Games

author.name: Ashkan Soleymani, Georgios Piliouras

entry.summary: This paper introduces MORM, an uncoupled learning rule for finite general-sum games where each player achieves external regret of O(sqrt(n) log d) uniformly over all horizons with only one-step optimism. The proof combines potential-based regret matching with multiplicative stability and Hellinger control of strategy movement, plus a safeguard for adversarial utilities.

entry.title: Reviser: Revision-Capable Text Generation via Autoregressive Cursor Actions

author.name: Sean Diab

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces Reviser, a decoder-only Transformer that generates text through cursor-relative actions (INSERT, MOVE, STOP) applied to a mutable canvas, rather than emitting tokens in final text order. By being autoregressive over edit-history actions instead of token sequence, it achieves non-monotonic generation with revision and insertion capability while keeping a simple next-action prediction interface, and it reportedly outperforms SEDD and MDLM in arena-style preference evaluations on a continuation benchmark.

entry.title: ArenaFlow: From Trajectory Ranking to Hierarchical Credit Propagation for Open-Ended Agent RL

author.name: Qiang Zhang, Ruixue Ding, Fanrui Zhang, Xi Chen, Boli Chen, Shihang Wang, Yinfeng Huang, Yi Zheng, Pengjun Xie, Kaipeng Zhang, Jiawei Liu, Zheng-Jun Zha

entry.summary: Introduces ArenaFlow, a hierarchical credit propagation framework for RL training of open-ended LLM agents where scalar rewards are hard to define. It uses tournament-based relative ranking of trajectories and propagates credit down to intermediate steps, aiming to consolidate successful behaviors into reusable skills rather than compressing comparisons into a single trajectory-level reward.

entry.title: Conformal Privacy Auditing: Calibrated Re-identification Attacks with Statistical Guarantees

author.name: Shuo Huang, Gholamreza Haffari, Xingliang Yuan, Ting Yu, Lizhen Qu

entry.summary: This paper introduces Conformal Privacy Auditing (CPA), a distribution-free calibration framework that provides a finite-sample statistical certificate of re-identification risk for each released document against LLM-empowered adversaries. CPA outputs a conformal ambiguity set of candidate identities, bridging the gap between empirical attack success rates and principled release-time privacy decisions. This addresses the growing threat of LLM-plus-auxiliary-knowledge attacks linking documents to individuals.

entry.title: From Retrieval to Recognition:How Vision--Language Models Become OCR Specialists

author.name: Yuanxiang Huangfu, Hanmeng Zhong, Linqing Chen, Jeffrey Tiong Jee Hui

entry.summary: A mechanistic-interpretability study asking whether general VLMs acquire OCR ability via a new reading circuit or by reusing existing mechanisms. Using causal interventions on GLM-OCR, MinerU2.5, and PaddleOCR-VL-1.6, the authors identify sparse stable OCR-head sets and show strong overlap (untuned top-20 intersections of 73.3%) with textual retrieval/copy heads in general VLMs. The findings suggest OCR specialization largely reuses existing retrieval/copy circuitry.

entry.title: Catena: A Comprehensive Software Suite for Large-Scale Connectomics

author.name: Samia Mohinta, Pedro G\'omez-G\'alvez, Shi Yan Lee, Daniel Franco-Barranco, Michael Clayton, Stephan Preibisch, Jan Funke, Albert Cardona

entry.summary: Catena is an open-source, developer-centric software suite integrating segmentation, synapse detection, microtubule tracking, and neurotransmitter inference into composable, chunk-wise pipelines for electron-microscopy connectomics. It addresses a real reproducibility problem, since connectome reconstruction currently depends on fragmented or proprietary tools.

entry.title: SPARROW: Survival-POMCP for Adaptive Robot Routing, Observation, and Waiting

author.name: Hshmat Sahak, Aoran Jiao, Nicholas Rhinehart, Timothy D. Barfoot

entry.summary: SPARROW formulates navigation around temporary obstacles as a partially observable semi-MDP and builds a POMCP-based belief-space planner that decides among waiting, rerouting, and gathering more information. It learns class-conditioned survival models of obstacle clearance times online, including from right-censored encounters where the robot leaves early.

entry.title: Learning Scene-Aware Humanoid Locomotion through 3D Clutter from Immersive Human Demonstrations

author.name: Beichen Wang, Tong Xu, Daniel Kosukhin, Yuen-Hei Yeung, Yuanjie Lu, Xuesu Xiao

entry.summary: MTC is a learning-from-demonstration framework for scene-aware humanoid locomotion in densely cluttered 3D environments, using procedurally generated VR environments for immersive human data collection and converting motions into training-ready humanoid data. It couples whole-body motion with scene geometry for obstacle avoidance.

entry.title: LEMCA: LLM-Guided Synthesis of Efficient Mode-Switching Control Architectures

author.name: Arjun Krishna, Vincent Pacelli, Dinesh Jayaraman

entry.summary: LEMCA uses large language models to automate the design of mode-switching controllers that dynamically vary resource allocation across task phases, replacing wasteful monolithic control structures. The system synthesizes performant mode-switching architectures for physical control tasks such as driving and manipulation without expert-driven per-task design.

entry.title: LIMBO: Learning and Internalizing Model-Free Barrier Objectives for Agile and Safe Whole-Body Control

author.name: Jake Gonzales, Arturo Flores Alvarez, Yu-Ming Chen, Aaron D. Ames, Lillian J. Ratliff, Manikantan Nambi

entry.summary: LIMBO synthesizes a state-action control barrier function from black-box transitions and a state-based failure specification over residual actions around a frozen base controller, then distills its safety structure into a task policy. During synthesis, a learned safety value drives risk-guided sampling near the boundary of recoverability, enabling Q-CBF synthesis in the full control dimension for high-dimensional whole-body dynamics. The goal is reusable safety certificates for agile behaviors balancing collision avoidance and balance.

entry.title: GUARD: Natural Forgetting in Large Reasoning Models via Guided Answer-Reasoning Distillation

author.name: Zeyu Yan, Guanghao Zhou, Minghui Qiu, Ming Gao, Cen Chen

entry.summary: Argues that unlearning in large reasoning models should specify a natural forgetting trajectory — a coherent non-disclosing chain-of-thought followed by a stable refusal answer — rather than merely suppressing content. GUARD uses guided answer-reasoning distillation to avoid hallucinated substitutes, malformed boundaries, and repetitive outputs after forgetting.

entry.title: M2G-LLM: Enhancing Clinical Prediction via Multimodal Graph Reasoning and LLM Context Injection

author.name: Inyoung Choi, Sukwon Yun, Jiayi Xin, Jie Peng, Tianlong Chen, Qi Long

entry.summary: M2G-LLM augments LLMs for clinical prediction by using GNNs to model temporal visit relationships, propagate information across similar patients, and align heterogeneous modalities (notes, labs, imaging) into enriched multimodal representations injected as context. It tackles LLMs' weakness at integrating non-text medical data. The framework targets improved clinical decision support.

entry.title: Programming AMD XDNA NPUs with Open-source Compiler Tools: A FlashAttention Case Study

author.name: Erwei Wang, Ephrem Wu, Victor J. B. Jung, Jiajie Li, Andre Rosti, Joseph Melber, Samuel Bayliss

entry.summary: Reports on mapping FlashAttention onto AMD XDNA spatial NPUs using the open-source IRON and MLIR-AIR compiler flows, comparing four reference designs across XDNA 1 and 2, including a fully fused kernel that keeps attention scores in compute-tile local memory and reduces partials over the cascade interconnect. The work provides practical guidance on data placement decisions for spatial NPUs.

entry.title: GALA: Geometry-Aware Latent Action Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Model Pretraining across Embodiments

author.name: Yichen Liu, Puzhen Yuan, Xiang Zhu, Yanjiang Guo, Jianyu Chen

entry.summary: GALA augments image-based latent action models with 3D end-effector geometric motion so that VLA pretraining across heterogeneous embodiments can capture finger-level articulation in human and dexterous robot hands, addressing the fine-grained action semantics that naive point-cloud incorporation loses. This targets scalable multi-embodiment robot learning from video.

entry.title: Same World, Different Knowledge: When Isolated Audits Misjudge World-Model Repairs

author.name: Rui Min, Xianyao Li, Fang Xu, Sofiane Lachab, Jing Du

entry.summary: The paper introduces an information-interface audit for world models, distinguishing fidelity gaps from availability gaps, and shows that repairs validated under isolated input faults can fail when deployed modules share faulty information. In simulated quadrotor MPC, coupled calibration errors collapse success from 69% to 8%, with uncertainty training restoring 65%.

entry.title: AirSplan: Risk-Aware Motion Planning for Quadrotors in Cluttered 3D Gaussian Splats

author.name: Seth Isaacson, William Hong, Katherine A. Skinner, Ram Vasudevan

entry.summary: AirSplan provides a risk-aware motion planning system for quadrotors navigating cluttered scenes represented as 3D Gaussian splats, addressing both high-fidelity environment reconstruction without ground-truth obstacle data and collision-free planning over that representation. It targets safety-critical applications like inspection and agriculture where even minor collisions lose the vehicle.

entry.title: Robotic Multiphase Interaction: Manipulating Coupled Liquid and Solid Dynamics with a World Model

author.name: Yixuan Feng, Peng Wang

entry.summary: This paper introduces Robotic Multiphase Interaction (RMI), a new manipulation setting where liquid enters a porous material and mechanically interacts with its deforming solid skeleton, changing pore volume, liquid distribution, and grasp stability simultaneously. Using a water-filled sponge as the first example, the authors couple implicit incompressible porous flow with smoothed particle hydrodynamics as a dynamics engine and learn manipulation with a world model.

entry.title: CounterPlay: Counterfactual Post-Training for Self-Play Driving Policies

author.name: Jiarong Wei, Yin Wu, Runkai He, Abhinav Valada

entry.summary: CounterPlay is a counterfactual self-play post-training approach for driving policies that backtracks from failed tasks and retries them under alternate driving styles, rather than only evaluating alternative actions at already-visited states. It combines failure-driven backtracking, alternate driving-style retries, and targeted post-training to overcome diminishing returns from scaling self-play rollouts in high-throughput simulators.

entry.title: CaLR: Causal Latent Revision for Robust Diffusion Reasoning

author.name: Wei Cai, Jian Zhao, Yuchen Yuan, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: CaLR reformulates reasoning in diffusion language models as constrained latent optimization, using a causal topology matrix from an expert model and implicit differentiation to perform gradient-guided thought revision during parallel generation. It reports SOTA DLM performance on complex benchmarks, surpassing strong autoregressive baselines. The work addresses a key weakness of diffusion LMs for reasoning tasks.

entry.title: DENSE: Distilling Agent Trajectories into Evidence-Grounded Shortcut Trees for Self-Refinement

author.name: Siyuan Liu (Fudan University, Meituan Longcat Team), Fan Yu (Fudan University, Meituan Longcat Team), Dongyu Ru (Meituan Longcat Team), Yizhu Liu (Meituan Longcat Team), Yifan Yang (Meituan Longcat Team), Xuezhi Cao (Meituan Longcat Team), Xunliang Cai (Meituan Longcat Team), Yixin Cao (Fudan University)

entry.summary: DENSE distills abundant online agent execution traces into evidence-grounded nested shortcut trees that serve as reusable feedback without post-hoc outcome labels, compressing redundant attempts and linking completed progress to remaining obligations. It also introduces REFIT, a source-paired protocol for comparing feedback sources. From the Meituan Longcat team with Fudan, it targets scaling agent learning from deployment data.

entry.title: The Communication Bottleneck: A Round-Trip Study of Tree-Structured Expression Serialization in Language Models

author.name: Xavier Suau, Alex Ferrando de las Morenas, Luca Zappella, Samy Bengio

entry.summary: A round-trip protocol tests how much tree-structured compositional content survives when a generator model converts an arithmetic expression into a word problem and a separate extractor model recovers it. Evaluating sixteen models pairwise yields a communication matrix separating generation quality from extraction quality, showing the natural-language channel is lossy.

entry.title: A Lie Detector Test for Language Models: Reading Knowledge a Model Won't Reveal

author.name: Hiskias Dingeto

entry.summary: Proposes Probe of Internal Recognition (PIR), adapting the forensic Concealed Information Test to language models: present a question with candidate answers and read internal states to identify which candidate the model recognizes as correct, distinguishing sandbagging or lying from genuine lack of knowledge. The method is reference-free, requiring no honest reference model.

entry.title: AgentVidBench: A Multi-Hop Video Question Answering Benchmark for Evaluating MLLM Agents

author.name: Seoyeon An, Hyeonseo Jang, Minsu Kim, Chanho Lee, Younghan Park, Kangwook Lee

entry.summary: Introduces AgentVidBench, a benchmark for evaluating multimodal LLM agents on multi-hop video question answering requiring spatial, temporal, and cross-clip reasoning that existing single-step scene-level benchmarks cannot measure. It targets agentic capabilities grounded in real-world video dynamics.

entry.title: HE-Guardrail: A Homomorphic Guardrail Against Jailbreak Attacks for Encrypted Large Language Model Inference

author.name: Byeongseo Min, Yongwoo Lee, Young-Sik Kim, Yongjune Kim

entry.summary: Identifies a vulnerability in homomorphic-encryption-based privacy-preserving LLM inference: server-side confidentiality prevents inspecting prompts, enabling malicious clients to submit jailbreak attacks undetected. It proposes HE-Guardrail, a guardrail computable over encrypted data that detects adversarial prompts without decrypting them.

entry.title: Samsone: A Family of Open Small Audio Language Models for On-Device Inference

author.name: Piotr Masztalski, Micha{\l} K. Grzeszczyk, Olaf Sikorski

entry.summary: Introduces Samsone, a family of small audio language models (134M, 99M, 356M parameters) for privacy-preserving on-device execution, with Samsone-134M setting a new state of the art for its size class across multiple benchmarks and competitive with far larger models. The models are released openly to support reproducible edge AI research.

entry.title: The Refutation Gap: Certifying Both Halves of an Optimality Claim

author.name: Rohan Pandey

entry.summary: Analyzes the asymmetry in verifying optimality claims from synthesis pipelines: upper bounds (a program of size m exists) come with re-executable, machine-checkable witnesses, while lower bounds (no smaller program exists) rely on solver UNSAT results without witnesses. Drawing on decades of combinatorial optimization practice and proof logging, it proposes frameworks for certifying both halves of an optimality claim.

entry.title: A Principled Approach to Unsupervised Anomaly Detection

author.name: James Myles, Matthew Baugh, Johanna P. M\"uller, Bernhard Kainz, Yingzhen Li

entry.summary: This paper reformulates unsupervised anomaly detection as a Bayesian inverse problem: inferring the most probable corruption responsible for each observation, with a probabilistic anomaly score given by the energy of inferred corruption parameters. It derives several existing UAD methods as instances of the same energy score under different modeling choices, unifying the field theoretically. Offers a principled recipe for designing new UAD algorithms.

entry.title: Dynamics-Induced Commitment in Learning-Based Robotic Penalty Kicks

author.name: Ruize Geng, Hao E. Zhang, Yisen Li, Yikai Wang, H. Eric Tseng, Ding Zhao

entry.summary: The paper studies a humanoid-quadruped penalty-kick game where game-level self-play policies command fixed whole-body controllers, introducing DIC-Map, a body-grounded analysis that estimates the first persistent loss of a terminal alternative due to dynamics-induced commitment. It tests whether remaining interactions reduce to a smaller zero-sum game once the body can no longer execute certain options.

entry.title: Stochastic Neural Signed Swept Volume for Real-time Chance-Constrained Trajectory Optimization

author.name: Qingyi Chen, Kevin Zhang, Lucas Chen, Zachary Kingston

entry.summary: The paper learns a stochastic neural representation of the robot's signed swept volume to enable continuous collision checking within real-time chance-constrained trajectory optimization, avoiding the discrete-state, single-determinized-model trade-off of standard planners. This treats approximation uncertainty explicitly rather than using the model as a coarse filter.

entry.title: Sandwich-Residuals: Parameter-Efficient Test-time Adaptation of World Models

author.name: Krishnam Soni, Aditya Sehgal, Vedant Dave, Elmar Rueckert

entry.summary: This paper proposes Sandwich-Residuals, a lightweight test-time adaptation method for latent world models that keeps the pretrained model frozen and learns only small residual corrections around the predictor. The residuals are optimized online from self-supervised prediction error without rewards, labels, or source-domain data. Evaluation across 21 conditions on the AdaJEPA benchmark demonstrates improved reliability under distribution shift at a fraction of the parameter updates of prior methods.

entry.title: CommitFlow: Semantic Commitment Verification and Local Correction for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation VLA Execution

author.name: Zixiang Zhao, Yansong Feng, Yang Yang, Chaoyu Wang, Haoran Xiao, Hui Zhang, Chuang Cheng, Jianjun Ma

entry.summary: CommitFlow targets a key failure mode of vision-language-action policies in long-horizon manipulation: advancing to the next task stage before the required physical condition is established. The framework keeps the base policy frozen and adds a Semantic Commitment Monitor that compares stage requirements against the current physical state, coupled with local correction to prevent deviation propagation. This closed-loop execution improves reliability of multi-stage VLA tasks.

entry.title: SkelWAM: A Skeleton-Guided World-Action Model for Zero-Shot Cross-Embodiment Manipulation

author.name: Pengjun Niu, Yujia Xie, Rui Peng, Hang Zhao, Ke Liu

entry.summary: SkelWAM enables zero-shot transfer of manipulation skills across robot embodiments through a shared 25-dimensional geometric state combining arm centerline geometry, tool-center-point pose, and parallel-jaw commands. This single explicit representation underlies canonical third-person and wrist observations as well as future whole-body action targets, training a skeleton-guided world-action model with predictive objectives. It addresses how embodiment changes alter visual appearance, action semantics, and whole-body configuration.

entry.title: GameLogicBench: Evaluating Coding Agents on Runtime Game Logic with Tick-Level State Assertions

author.name: Xinyu Che, Yunfei Ge, Shihao Li, Yanchen Liu, Hang Yan, Xinping Lei, Yanghai Wang, Zixuan Dong, Yifan Yao, Qianqian Xie, Letian Zhu, Jiaheng Liu

entry.summary: Introduces GameLogicBench, a benchmark of 72 gameplay-logic tasks in Godot projects with an automated evaluator checking rules at every simulation tick, producing 1,451 reproducible test cases from 403 scenarios. Unlike video-based or LLM-judged benchmarks, it guarantees exactly reproducible verdicts on whether agents implement correct runtime behavior.

entry.title: ForeTac-VLA: A Forecasting-Based Tactile-Vision-Language-Action Model for Contact-Rich Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Zhengyu Tao, Xin Li, Xin Wang

entry.summary: ForeTac-VLA adds tactile forecasting to VLA models, predicting future tactile states from temporal tactile representations fused with vision-language features so that actions can anticipate how contact will evolve rather than only reacting to observed feedback. This improves robustness in contact-rich manipulation where key physical states are not visible.

entry.title: DPed-VLN: A Benchmark for Socially Compliant Vision-and-Language Navigation in Dynamic Pedestrian Environments

author.name: Haojie Dai, Xiangyi Wang, Liuyi Wang, Kai Sheng, Zongtao He, Chengju Liu, Wei Ye, Qijun Chen

entry.summary: DPed-VLN is a Habitat 3.0 benchmark for vision-and-language navigation among moving pedestrians, with 33,093 episodes pairing global and prior-augmented instructions, ORCA-controlled humanoid pedestrians, socially constrained expert paths, and joint metrics for navigation efficiency and social safety. It also introduces DPet, a dynamic pedestrian model, enabling controlled analysis of how instruction priors expose dynamic-pedestrian cues.

entry.title: SpecOpt: Contact-Diff Reasoning for Agentic Molecule Optimization Toward Binding Specificity

author.name: Thao Nguyen, Heng Ji

entry.summary: SpecOpt defines a molecular design task of making constrained structural modifications to existing drugs that increase binding preference for an intended target over known off-targets while preserving drug-like properties. The authors build a ChEMBL-derived benchmark using curated drug-mechanism annotations. This shifts focus from de novo generation to improving selectivity of well-characterized drugs, relevant to reducing adverse drug effects.

entry.title: PlaceReasoner-Beta: Reasoning-Driven Macro Placement and Benchmarking

author.name: Qiufeng Li, Chengxuan Wang, Rongqian Chen, Quan Cheng, Yihui Ren, Chia-Tung Ho, David Z. Pan, Tian Lan, Weidong Cao

entry.summary: PlaceReasoner-Beta reformulates VLSI macro placement as a closed-loop reasoning problem rather than black-box optimization, using a VLM planner that generates candidate placements from floorplan images and specifications, guided by a verifier. It incorporates visual layout context, codified design expertise, and downstream physical-design feedback in a unified loop. This extends LLM/VLM agents into a longstanding EDA challenge.

entry.title: Physically Based Rendering in the Latent Space

author.name: Vuk Radovanovic, Vishesh Gupta, Adrien Gruson, Binh-Son Hua

entry.summary: This paper bridges physically based rendering and latent diffusion by performing light transport simulation in the latent feature space of VAEs, proposing modified rendering equations paired with a differentiable renderer. This enables physically guided, controllable content generation that classical graphics pipelines and diffusion models each lack alone.

entry.title: Co-Evolving Zero-Day Jamming: Adaptive Attack Synthesis and Graph Attention-Based Online Detection

author.name: Ghilas Aissou, R\'emi A. Chou, Taejoon Kim

entry.summary: Presents a two-pronged framework for wireless jamming: adaptive synthesis of zero-day jamming attacks as realistic evaluation adversaries, and an online detector combining graph attention networks over temporal-spectral structure with Dirichlet process clustering. The detector jointly classifies known jamming strategies and discovers novel zero-day strategies.

entry.title: SynthDemo-RL: Breaking the Zero-Reward Barrier in VLA Adaptation with LLM-Guided Synthetic Demonstrations

author.name: Hiroaki Kingetsu, Hiroaki Kurihara, Kaoru Yokoo, Kenji Fukumizu, Manohar Kaul

entry.summary: Proposes a teacher-student framework where an automated teacher converts simulator state into successful manipulation trajectories, a VLA student is distilled via SFT, and PPO with binary success rewards refines it. The approach addresses the exploration failure of RL on sparse-reward manipulation tasks by guaranteeing reward coverage, and is evaluated on the LIBERO-PRO benchmark.

entry.title: Do Quantum Models Scale Like LLMs?

author.name: David S. Berman, Ying-Jer Kao, Roger G. Melko, Alexander G. Stapleton

entry.summary: The authors study neural scaling laws for RydbergGPT, an autoregressive transformer trained on projective measurement data from Rydberg atom arrays, finding power-law scaling with a loss floor near a quantum critical point but degraded power-law fits away from criticality. They compare the statistical structure of quantum measurement data and language corpora using entropy-normalized mutual-information analysis. This probes whether LLM scaling-law phenomenology transfers to physical systems.

entry.title: An Introduction to Compression-Based Machine Learning

author.name: John Hurwitz, Edward Raff, Charles K. Nicholas

entry.summary: This survey formalizes the deep connection between lossless compression and machine learning, covering how compression algorithms yield learners (via normalized compression distance and minimum description length) and how autoregressive models yield compressors via entropy coding. The authors introduce and validate a design framework, finding compression-based methods competitive with conventional baselines and notably strong on malware detection. It is a timely conceptual unification relevant to understanding sequence models as compressors.

entry.title: ExpBoN: Exponential-Noise Best-of-$n$ for Efficient Test-Time LLM Alignment

author.name: Yanxiao Liu, Sicheng Wan, Deniz G\"und\"uz

entry.summary: The paper proposes ExpBoN, a soft Best-of-n inference-time alignment method for LLMs built on the exponential-noise report-noisy-max mechanism. It admits an exact finite-n decomposition with exponentially fast convergence in total variation, expected reward, and KL divergence, and includes comprehensive theoretical analysis of convergence and regret.

entry.title: Hybrid GPU-CPU Retrieval for Personalized Search at Ultra-Large Scale

author.name: Hao Fu, Jichao Sun, Baiting Zhu, Qiaoling Liu, Yan Shi, Cheng Lu, Liu Liu, Yubo Wang, Xin Yao, Xiangyu Niu, Xu Dong, Wenhan Lyu, Chiyao Shen, Yinjie Huang, Minglei Chen, Shuai Ding, Li Fan, Xiao Kong

entry.summary: Characterizes the personalization-scale paradox in trillion-document embedding retrieval: full GPU hosting is too resource-intensive while CPU paths cannot run interaction-heavy personalization models under latency budgets. The proposed hybrid GPU-CPU co-serving system resolves this through orchestration, fusing retrieval and interaction pre-ranking in a high-depth GPU pathway over a curated pool while a CPU pathway provides broad coverage.

entry.title: Prediction Dynamics in Depth-Recurrent Language Models

author.name: Xinyue Luo, Fei Yu

entry.summary: Analyzes why intermediate answers in depth-recurrent language models can agree with the final answer while their scores keep changing, deriving a sharp margin characterization that decomposes conservatism into translation, direction relative to the winner, and competitor pairing. Experiments on Huginn-3.5B and Ouro-1.4B show that accounting for update direction and competitor pairing reduces mean earliest qualifying depth by a further 22.5-34.4% beyond translation removal, suggesting earlier-exit opportunities.

entry.title: Beyond Benchmark Scores: Auditing Medical Vision-Language Models for Chest X-Ray Tuberculosis Screening

author.name: Mushir Akhtar, M. Tanveer, Mohd. Arshad

entry.summary: This study audits three medical vision-language models (BioMedCLIP, CheXficient, MedSigLIP) and OpenCLIP for chest X-ray tuberculosis screening across 12,200 records from four datasets, testing whether benchmark rankings survive changes in cohort, prompt, prevalence, and threshold. Across 244,000 model-image-prompt scores, no model leads consistently and prompt changes alter AUROC in a large fraction of comparisons, demonstrating fragility of benchmark-based medical claims.

entry.title: RheoSampling: Resolving the One-Hot Dilemma in Stochastic Dynamic-Tree Speculative Decoding

author.name: Qiao Hu, Yepeng Weng, Bo Zhang, Takehisa Yairi

entry.summary: The paper identifies a dilemma in dynamic-tree speculative decoding such as EAGLE-3: under stochastic sampling (temperature greater than zero), deterministic top-K expansion collapses draft distributions to one-hot probabilities and sharply lowers acceptance rates. RheoSampling decouples the distribution roles to preserve both context-aware tree topology and stochastic sampling, improving acceptance rates at temperature.

entry.title: MME-Safety: A Fine-grained Benchmark for Safety Evaluation of MLLMs

author.name: Yueming Lyu, Yilian Shi, Haoxiang Tan, Linzhuang Zou, Qihao Wang, Guihua Yu, Jie Qin, Xin Gao, Chenyang Si, Jing Dong, Caifeng Shan

entry.summary: MME-Safety is a rigorously verified benchmark for multimodal LLM safety with a four-dimensional annotation schema covering risk scenarios, harm severity, and modality-specific stealth levels, plus a hierarchical evaluation framework assessing response reliability, risk exposure, and defensive behavior integrity. It reports extensive zero-shot evaluations showing cross-modal vulnerabilities that bypass unimodal filters.

entry.title: TrialAtlas: Multi-Agent Research Organization for Clinical Trial Design and Optimization

author.name: Jiacheng Lin, Zifeng Wang, Zheng Chen, Erick Scott, Ziwei Yang, Fanyang Yu, Sheng Zhong, Jimeng Sun

entry.summary: Introduces TrialAtlas, a memory-augmented multi-agent system for clinical development planning that coordinates specialized agents for literature synthesis, competitive trial intelligence, regulatory reasoning, and other expert roles. It targets the costly failure of ~90% of drugs in clinical development by making risk and success-probability assessment more systematic.

entry.title: I'll Keep an Ear Out: Teaching AudioLLMs Proactive Audio Assistance

author.name: Amit Kumar Singh Yadav, Ritvik Shrivastava, Xuan Zhang, Seungwhan Moon, Shashank Jain, Pinar Donmez, Babak Damavandi

entry.summary: The paper introduces proactive audio assistance, where an AudioLLM monitors an audio stream and autonomously decides when to alert the user based on a single natural-language intent, motivated by wearable applications for Deaf and Hard of Hearing users. The proposed ISM paradigm is model-agnostic and embeds proactive decisions into LLM decoding via two special tokens covering onset detection, sustained-relevance triggering, irrelevance suppression, and de-duplication. Applied to Qwen2-Audio-7B, it achieves 99.6% interrupt F1 and perfect de-duplication recall on ESC-50.

entry.title: ME-Dex 1.0: Bringing Heterogeneous Tactile Sensing into World Action Modeling

author.name: Xuancheng Zhang, Xuetao Liu, Qianying Tang, Jizhe Wang, Zhijing Cheng, Bochen Lin, Haoran Wen, Ming Li, Kun Zhan, Yu Liu

entry.summary: ME-Dex-1.0 is a unified World Action Tactile Model that jointly predicts future tactile states, visual observations, and actions, treating tactile signals as observations of the evolving world state rather than mere conditioning inputs. It adopts a Mixture-of-Transformers architecture to incorporate heterogeneous tactile sensing into video-model-based robot action generation.

entry.title: Adaptive World Memory 3D Foundation Model for Scalable 3D Mapping, Localization, and Rendering

author.name: Tianchen Deng, Guole Shen, Yilin Shen, Wenhua Wu, Yilin Fang, Ziqi Ma, Tianjun Zhang, Shenghai Yuan, Wolfram Burgard, Hesheng Wang

entry.summary: A memory-centric 3D foundation model for scalable robotic localization, reconstruction, and Gaussian rendering, built on an adaptive world memory mechanism combining transformer gated updates with test-time temporal-spatial regulation. It organizes memory into local submaps and integrates progressive mapping, tracking, and loop closure for large-scale deployment. Bridges generalizable 3D foundation models with persistent, renderable scene memory.

entry.title: Info3R: Information-Adaptive Test-Time Training for 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Sunghyun Baek, Hanna Bae, Minchan Kwon, Junmo Kim

entry.summary: Info3R introduces information-aware test-time training for online 3D reconstruction from long video streams, modulating recurrent state updates by frame redundancy/informativeness and actively restoring state plasticity so the model can keep incorporating new observations. This targets a known failure mode of transformer-based streaming reconstruction where internal states saturate.

entry.title: Project SCOUT: Interceptor Drone for Perimeter Defense

author.name: Azmain Yousuf, Siwei Cai, Knut Peterson, Lifeng Zhou, David Han

entry.summary: SCOUT is a ROS-integrated onboard perception and control framework enabling a defender UAV to detect, track, and intercept unauthorized intruder drones in real time without external sensing infrastructure. It combines TensorRT-accelerated drone detection with ByteTrack-based target association and lightweight track filtering to generate stable control commands fully onboard.

entry.title: MetaPusher: Meta Learning and Planning for Nonprehensile Manipulation of Unseen Objects with Rapid Online Adaption

author.name: Donghyung Lee, Seyedali Golestaneh, Jaskrit Singh, Zhuoyun Zhong, Athanasios Kapoutsis, Constantinos Chamzas

entry.summary: MetaPusher combines meta-learning of object dynamics with adaptive planning for nonprehensile pushing of unseen objects whose latent properties like friction and mass distribution cannot be inferred from perception alone. It handles the coupling between online dynamics refinement and trajectory replanning as the model evolves.

entry.title: Stability-aware Residual Reinforcement Learning Framework for Robotic Manipulator Disturbance Compensation

author.name: Jihong Kim, Joonhyuk Kwon, Hwa Soo Kim, TaeWon Seo, Hyung-Tae Seo

entry.summary: This paper proposes a residual reinforcement learning framework that augments conventional disturbance observers for robotic manipulators. A deterministic analytical baseline handles tracking within a reliable region while an RL policy compensates only for residuals, with an estimator network aligning observation history to privileged disturbance context for fast adaptation, and stability guarantees are provided for the combined controller.

entry.title: PSR: Predictive Sensorimotor Representation Learning for Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Shengbao Li, Peng Xu, Chao Tang, Hao Wei, Jiaheng Wang, Hong Yin, Jiangtao Chen, Jinxuan Zhu, Zhong Zhou, Mengfan Wang, Tingguang Li

entry.summary: PSR introduces a framework that pretrains a multimodal Transformer to learn a hierarchy of predictive representations over contact forces, robot configurations, and interaction histories, then injects these into the action stream of a visuomotor policy. Unlike methods that passively condition on force feedback, the policy actively predicts future contact dynamics for high-precision actions. This targets contact-rich manipulation tasks where vision alone is insufficient.

entry.title: Neural composite likelihood estimation: simulation based inference for time series

author.name: Grace Yan, Mark Beaumont, Dennis Prangle

entry.summary: Presents Neural Composite Likelihood Estimation (NCLE), extending neural simulation-based inference to long time series with complex dependency structure. Instead of estimating a full joint likelihood, it divides sequences into smaller batches and trains neural conditional density estimators on composite targets, addressing the dimensionality limits of standard neural likelihood estimation.

entry.title: Verify, Don't Trust: Agentic Model Development for Video Discovery Retrieval at Scale

author.name: Hao Fu, Baiting Zhu, Minglei Chen, Yinjie Huang, Shuai Ding

entry.summary: EvoPilot is a human-gated method for long-horizon online autoresearch, using role-specific agents with versioned domain skills and typed adapters, durable experiment records, and deterministic verification to guard against no-op changes, data leakage, and evaluator drift. It targets asynchronous, hours-to-weeks-scale model development campaigns such as video discovery retrieval systems, rather than minutes-scale self-contained loops.

entry.title: VidOmni-Bench: A Benchmark for Fine-Grained Video Understanding via Spatio-Temporal Event Verification across Complexity and Duration

author.name: Changbeen Kim, Junwon Chang, Kipyo Kim, Risa Shinoda, Kuniaki Saito, Donghyun Kim

entry.summary: Introduces VidOmni-Bench, which evaluates Video-LLMs by asking whether each event in dense video captions is actually supported by the video, avoiding superficial QA and caption-matching shortcuts. It spans 500 human-verified videos across five complexity types and durations from 4 seconds to 90 minutes.

entry.title: FedeRage: Provably Convergent Agnostic Federated Learning under General Client Drift

author.name: Herlock Rahimi, Dionysis Kalogerias

entry.summary: This paper characterizes what distributionally agnostic FedAvg optimizes when client participation probabilities are unknown and skewed, showing uniform aggregation minimizes a participation-weighted stochastic objective at standard O(1/sqrt(T)) rates. It then proposes FedeRage, a provably convergent method for federated learning under general client drift and unknown participation. The analysis relaxes the unrealistic assumption that servers know participation probabilities.

entry.title: WM-VS: Progress-Aligned World Models for Closed-Loop Visual Servoing

author.name: Guanzhong Sun, Junyi Ma, Yixuan Zhou, Yuxuan Wu, Yanzi Miao, Hesheng Wang

entry.summary: WM-VS addresses the prediction-control mismatch in closed-loop visual servoing by training a world model whose latent transitions are aligned to a signed servo coordinate derived from DINOv2 target correspondences, then training a reactive joint-velocity policy with action imitation, consequence supervision, and imagined rollouts that favor error contraction. Deployment is RGB-only and reactive without online adaptation.

entry.title: MA-LIPP: Cooperative Multi-Agent Load-Aware Informative Path Planning for Heterogeneous Robot Teams

author.name: Hojune Kim, Guangyao Shi, Gaurav S. Sukhatme

entry.summary: MA-LIPP extends load-aware informative path planning to heterogeneous multi-robot teams where high-precision samplers collect while high-capacity carriers transport, solving the coordination of when, where, and to whom to hand off samples. This overcomes the depot-return bottleneck of single-robot LIPP in field sampling missions.

entry.title: NeuRIO: A Streaming Neural Estimator for Zero-Shot Sim-to-Real Multi-Robot Relative Inertial Odometry

author.name: Zhehan Li, Jiadong Lu, Shengwei Ren, Chao Xu, Yanjun Cao

entry.summary: NeuRIO is a streaming neural estimator for anchor-free 6-DoF relative inertial odometry across multiple robots using only inter-robot bearings, ranges, and IMU measurements. It canonicalizes measurements into gravity-aligned coordinates, represents robots and observations as a graph with attention and GRUs, handles varying team sizes and time-varying observation graphs, and achieves zero-shot sim-to-real transfer after training with realistic modeled sensor corruptions.

entry.title: CARF: Contrastive Attraction-Repulsion of Failure-Guided Flow Matching

author.name: Shuqi Zhao, Bang Du, Cheng-En Wu, Yichen Xie, Yixiao Wang, Masayoshi Tomizuka

entry.summary: CARF argues that robot demonstration data contain two asymmetric supervision signals: progressive segments that should be imitated and failure-critical segments that should be explicitly avoided. It introduces a progress-based importance scorer trained only on unlabelled trajectories and uses it within a contrastive attraction-repulsion flow matching framework for learning from imperfect data. This better exploits failed demonstrations than methods that only extract progress segments.

entry.title: Risk-Aware Occupancy for Safety-Oriented End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jiaxing Chen, Hengduo Zou, Yiren Zhao, Bolin Gao

entry.summary: ROIDrive proposes a dense risk-aware occupancy representation for end-to-end autonomous driving that jointly encodes scene occupancy, map-derived traffic constraints, and future dynamic agent occupancy into a unified BEV map for trajectory planning. This addresses safety risks in crowded, occluded scenes with unstructured obstacles that sparse object-based representations miss. The unified spatial-temporal risk evidence supports safer planning.

entry.title: ECG Mirage: Revealing and Mitigating the Underutilisation of ECGs in Vision-Language Models for Clinical Prediction

author.name: Jinning Liang, Mingcheng Zhu, Tingting Zhu

entry.summary: Identifies ECG Mirage in clinical vision-language models: apparent multimodal performance without meaningful dependence on the patient-specific ECG, distinguishing ECG neglect from ECG confusion (where mismatched ECGs work as well as matched ones). The paper proposes evaluation protocols and mitigations for emergency-department clinical prediction.

entry.title: Making Latent Evolution Explicit: Operator-Structured Transitions for World Action Models

author.name: Xiaoxiao Lu, Yunlong Dong, Jiahao Shi, Ye Yuan

entry.summary: This work studies architectural choices for latent state transitions in World Action Models for robotics, proposing LEON, a Latent Evolution Operator Network that models latent evolution via context-modulated operators in a learned observable space. It argues that operator-structured transitions are better suited to temporal evolution than token-interaction Transformer predictors.

entry.title: The Stochastic Shift: A New Evaluation Paradigm for Text-to-SQL with AI Operators

author.name: Tarfah Alrashed, Fatma Ozcan, Per Jacobsson, Tal Neiman, Xianshun Chen

entry.summary: The paper observes that SQL augmented with AI operators produces flexible, non-deterministic outputs that current deterministic text-to-SQL evaluation metrics systematically fail to assess. It formalizes these evaluation failure modes and introduces a Multilayered Evaluation Framework decoupling deterministic database logic from AI semantics, tested on BigQuery and academic settings.

entry.title: CESBench: Benchmarking Large Language Models on Cryptographic Engineering Security for IoT Devices

author.name: Wenquan Zhou, An Wang, Jing Liang, Peien Feng, Jingqi Zhang, Yaoling Ding, Liehuang Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces CESBench, a 380-item expert-written benchmark covering six sub-domains of cryptographic engineering security for IoT devices, including side channels, fault injection, and countermeasures. It spans multiple task types testing recall, security judgment, and implementation analysis, filling a gap between cryptography and general cybersecurity benchmarks.

entry.title: Think Locally, Refine Globally for Memory-Efficient 3D Reconstruction

author.name: Jingke Zhou, Chenhang Ma, Zhizhou Zhong, Mingkai Liu, Zhuang Zhou, Yicheng ji, Binghua Su, Bo Cai, Xianliang Huang

entry.summary: Proposes LoG-VGGT, a memory-efficient framework for long-sequence 3D reconstruction that uses sparse cross-window attention in a subset of transformer blocks plus a global camera consistency module where camera tokens interact with compact register tokens. The design bounds memory while significantly improving long-horizon pose stability.

entry.title: When Steering Fails in Latent Reasoning: A Latent-to-Language Transition Gap

author.name: Gaoxiang Huang, Lei Qi

entry.summary: Shows that activation steering of continuous (latent) chain-of-thought representations produces much weaker effects on downstream language generation than steering explicit CoT, even with comparable representational displacement. The authors identify a latent-to-language transition gap, supported by abrupt output distribution changes at the transition boundary, advancing understanding of latent reasoning models.

entry.title: ASGARD: Action-Space Guard for UAV Resilience via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Mohsen Salehi, Karthik Pattabiraman

entry.summary: ASGARD is a two-phase teacher-student pipeline that makes RL-based UAV controllers resilient to action-space attacks, where commands are overwritten between policy output and actuator execution. A teacher encoder combines physical state with privileged attack information, distilled into a student that operates at runtime without privileged data. Most prior defenses target input-space attacks, so this addresses an underexplored threat model.

entry.title: Trading Depth for Time in Recurrent Transformers

author.name: Zeyi Huang, Xuehai He, Yong Jae Lee, Yelong Shen

entry.summary: Using Latent Recurrent Transformers, which insert latent thought tokens between vocabulary tokens while sharing backbone parameters, the paper asks whether extra computation is better spent on more temporal recurrence steps or greater physical depth. This controlled comparison clarifies the compute-allocation trade-off in recurrent transformer designs. The question bears directly on efficient architecture design for decoding-limited settings.

entry.title: Available Guardrails: Certifying Selective Prediction across ML Systems

author.name: Parivesh Priye, Yufeng Wang, Haibin Ling, Michael Chaykowsky

entry.summary: The paper formulates when finite calibration data can certify selective predictors (safety gates returning outputs only when trustworthy) at a target precision per reporting unit such as a tool, policy label, or patient subgroup. Using exact-binomial inversion and a dynamic program over reporting partitions, it makes certificate availability computable and exposes trade-offs among granularity, safety, and data.

entry.title: Reading Less While Writing: A Closed-Form Bandwidth Dial for Streaming Multimodal Decoders

author.name: Yasir Mehmood, Kashif Javed

entry.summary: Replaces fixed wait-k policies in streaming video/audio-to-text decoding with ZENDAYA, a single-parameter schedule that makes the visible source prefix a closed-form function of generation progress, scaled by predicted input length. This unifies offline decoding and real-time streaming as endpoints of one family, enabling flexible latency-quality tradeoffs for live captioning.

entry.title: From Discharge Notes to Patient Understanding: Persona-Grounded, Open-Ended Simulation of LLMs as Discharge Educators

author.name: Won Seok Jang, Zonghai Yao, Hong Yu

entry.summary: The authors introduce DischargeBench, a persona-grounded benchmark where a candidate LLM conducts multi-turn discharge education with a Virtual Patient, with an Education Monitor Agent preserving patient realism without contaminating the evaluation. The dataset covers 477 MIMIC-IV-derived cases across 24 ICD chapters with persona axes such as health literacy and personality.

entry.title: An Interpretable Memory Decision Controller for LLM Agents Based on Three-Signal Complementarity: Decoupling Confidence and Consistency

author.name: Yiming Zhang, Jinghong Zhang, Haoran Zhao, Yiren Ma, Chunlei Zhao

entry.summary: This paper addresses the underexplored question of whether retrieved memories should be trusted, showing that blind RAG injection of conflicting memories substantially increases hallucination rates in susceptible models. Inspired by prefrontal cortex memory signaling, the authors propose a zero-parameter Memory Decision Layer placed between retrieval and generation that uses a three-signal complementarity mechanism decoupling confidence and consistency. The controller is interpretable and adds no trainable parameters.

entry.title: A Scene Language Model for Open-Vocabulary Scene Mapping

author.name: Adam Lilja, Fabio H\"ubel, Siming He, Junsheng Fu, Claire Tomlin, Lars Hammarstrand, Jitendra Malik, Jonas Frey, Marco Pavone

entry.summary: SceneLM maintains an open-vocabulary 3D scene map purely as structured text: the model reads the current textual scene state from each input image and updates it by adding, editing, or removing object entries, replacing feature-heavy persistent memories of prior mapping systems. Author list includes prominent researchers (Jitendra Malik, Marco Pavone).

entry.title: VideoReloc: Long-Term Indoor Video Relocalization against a Kilobyte-Scale Semantic Scene Graph

author.name: Qianru Li, Xuyang Chen, Xuqin Wang, Zhenghao Zhang, Hongyi Luo, Tao Wu, Daniel Cremers, Lu Liu, Yanfeng Zhang

entry.summary: VideoReloc performs long-term indoor video relocalization against a compact (kilobyte-scale) semantic scene graph that stays robust under lighting and furniture changes. It adaptively gathers spatial evidence across clips using odometry, rechecks conflicting placements with cross-clip evidence, and proposes poses from object triplets with hypothesis-first registration. Extremely compact map representation is the standout feature.

entry.title: PRIME: Perception Feedback with Situational Memory Embeddings in VLA Models

author.name: Erik Deinzer, Naya Baslan, Luca Paparusso, Narunas Vaskevicius, Peter Knott, Luigi Palmieri

entry.summary: PRIME adds a learned feedback loop that conditions perception queries in vision-language-action driving models on a situational memory aggregating past perception, reasoning, navigation goals, and predicted behaviors over an L-step window via cross-attention. This lets early perception prioritize cues relevant to downstream planning rather than processing visual input agnostically.

entry.title: Constraint-Unified MPC for Over-Actuated Surface Vehicles with Post-Detection Fault Reconfiguration

author.name: Sebastian Burmester, Ruiheng Jiang, Noa Sendlhofer, Raffaello D'Andrea, Aswin Ramachandran

entry.summary: A deployed MPC system for autonomous surface vehicles solves trajectory tracking, thrust allocation, and per-thruster force/rate limits in one quadratic program, with fault reconfiguration toggled via per-thruster binary flags from an external detector. It achieved 1.6 cm RMS positioning error in live performances on Lake Zurich and in Venice, including under thruster failure.

entry.title: Learning Distance-Conditioned Object Transport for Humanoid Loco-Manipulation from a Single Motion Clip

author.name: Yuhyeon Hwang, Daniel Sungho Jung, YongHyeok Seo, Mingi Jung, Chang Nho Cho, Jung-Hoon Hwang, Dongin Shin

entry.summary: The paper identifies a termination-versus-passage gap in humanoid loco-manipulation via motion tracking: policies trained on a single clip reproduce only the demonstrated endpoint transport outcome. It proposes Distance-Conditioned Reference Recomposition, which relocates the demonstrated termination segment to intermediate transport states, and uses a frozen tracking teacher with closed-loop replay to learn distance-conditioned transport.

entry.title: Scaling Vision-Language Reward Learning for Robot Manipulation in Parallel Simulation

author.name: Lobna Joualy, Eric Demeester, Nikolaos Tsiogkas

entry.summary: RAPID accelerates preference-based reward learning with vision-language models by coupling GPU-parallel rollout collection with data-aware policy updates, single-request preference labeling, automatic reward stabilization, and representative image sampling. On five Franka Panda manipulation tasks in IsaacLab, parallel rollout with adaptive updates cut mean training time from 9.18 to 3.13 hours, with further reductions when all components are enabled.

entry.title: MAAP: Multi-Agent Active Perception for Collaborative Manipulation

author.name: Bruno N. Y. Chen, Li Kang, Heng Zhou, Xiufeng Song, Zhemeng Zhang, Jiahua Ma, Yiran Qin

entry.summary: MAAP proposes that every arm in a multi-arm manipulation team serve a dual purpose: executing actions while its wrist camera acts as a moving viewpoint for the team. It pairs this with RAIL, a role-aware imitation learning controller that predicts each arm's current role alongside its action chunk and conditions action generation on it, representing role-dependent behavior in a single network. This reframes active perception as an emergent benefit of collaborative manipulation.

entry.title: Decoupling Internal Representational Changes and Causal Importance in Fine-Tuned Large Language Models

author.name: Lingfang Li, Procheta Sen, Shubham Das, Danushka Bollegala

entry.summary: This work studies how fine-tuning reshapes LLM internal mechanisms, examining attention patterns and layer-wise activations and linking them to task-relevant components identified by EAP. It finds EAP-identified components concentrated in specific layers, suggesting functional localization of task-specific behavior. This contributes to understanding what fine-tuning actually changes inside models.

entry.title: PolyBridgeBench: Benchmarking Multimodal LLMs for Physics-Grounded Bridge Design

author.name: Zicheng Zhao, Dongyin Chen, Rui Xu, Yinghui Xu

entry.summary: An executable benchmark where multimodal LLMs must design complete load-bearing bridge structures (node-member-material topology) from a visual scene and engineering constraints, with legality checks gating execution in a dynamic physics simulator. It also tests whether models can repair designs after simulation exposes a structural failure.

entry.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning with Buffered Quantile Objectives

author.name: Mohammad Alipour-vaezi, Sajad Khodadadian

entry.summary: Introduces a model-free deep RL method for risk-sensitive decision-making based on lower-buffered quantiles, which average neighboring quantiles below a target level to obtain a smoother surrogate for the point-quantile objective. This extends prior model-based buffered-quantile approaches to model-free settings.

entry.title: CIPL: A Channel-Aware Framework for Recoverable Privacy Leakage in LLM Agents

author.name: Tao Huang, Guosen Wu, Guolong Zheng, Jiayang Meng, Chen Hou, Xu Yang, Xuechao Yang, Feng Xia

entry.summary: Introduces CIPL, a channel-inversion evaluation framework that measures black-box privacy leakage in LLM agents by modeling the transition from selected sensitive units to attacker-recoverable output across source, selection, assembly, execution, observation, and extraction stages. Experiments cover memory-based, retrieval-mediated, and tool-mediated targets plus a live browser-agent case study.

entry.title: Value-Sensitive Delegation in Everyday AI Agent Use: Evidence from OpenClaw

author.name: Renkai Ma, Ruyuan Wan, Xuan Lu, Fan Yang, Chen Chen, Lingyao Li

entry.summary: Applies Value Sensitive Design with LLM-assisted analysis to 73,093 first-person Reddit posts about using OpenClaw, extracting 21 human values in six groups (e.g., autonomous and dependable operation, bounded reach, reviewability). Values cluster around the operating conditions users set for agent runs rather than agent outputs, and are mostly unmet when users describe constraints rather than deliverables.

entry.title: Efficient Bayes-Adaptive Reinforcement Learning with Temporal Logic Specifications

author.name: Jonathan Hau, Alessandro Abate

entry.summary: The paper presents an end-to-end model-based RL algorithm for policy synthesis under Linear Temporal Logic specifications in unknown environments, synchronizing a Limit-Deterministic Buchi Automaton with a Bayes-Adaptive MDP. A novel BAMCP planner enables approximately Bayes-optimal synthesis with improved exploration-exploitation trade-offs versus non-Bayesian approaches. This advances formally-specified RL with principled uncertainty handling.

entry.title: Benchmarking World Models for Continual Learning on Compositional Tasks

author.name: Haoyu Zhou, Joe Watson, Anson Lei, Ingmar Posner

entry.summary: The authors introduce a compositional continual learning benchmark for world models that isolates knowledge reuse from the speed and capacity to learn unseen tasks, exploiting the compositional structure of physical dynamics. The benchmark separates how much of a new task is genuinely novel versus recurrent, enabling cleaner evaluation of continual adaptation.

entry.title: Triply-Scalable Equivariant Gaussian Process Modeling

author.name: Tim Steinert, David Ginsbourger

entry.summary: Establishes results on the interplay of Gaussian process equivariance and conditioning, enabling equivariant sparse GPs through suitable mean functions and covariance kernels. It instantiates the framework with integration-free equivariant kernels, aiming to combine GP uncertainty quantification with the scalability needed for large scientific problems such as molecular research.

entry.title: Schedule optimization for tau-leaping in masked discrete diffusion

author.name: Cecilia Secchi, Giacomo Zanella

entry.summary: The authors analyze the tau-leaping discretization used to accelerate masked discrete diffusion samplers, quantifying the factorization error introduced when blocks of coordinates are revealed in parallel via a product-distribution approximation. Using an exact integral representation involving a dependence density, they characterize how the error depends on the denoising schedule and optimize schedules to reduce it.

entry.title: Predictable Failure in Multi-Hop Retrieval: Score-Distributional Confidence Scoring and Abstention

author.name: Andre Bacellar

entry.summary: The paper formalizes why multi-hop retrieval failures cluster in structurally predictable query subpopulations, proving that confident-failure reduction is possible only when retrieval features carry mutual information about success. It further shows no single ANN score feature is best across failure regimes, with dominant features differing between datasets like MuSiQue and HoVer.

entry.title: $\mu^2$-Bench: A Multilingual Machine Unlearning Benchmark

author.name: Kyomin Hwang, Hyeonjin Kim, Hyunho Lee, Yearim Kim, Yeji Song, Nojun Kwak
