entry.summary: The paper introduces mu2-Bench, a benchmark simulating the full memorization, unlearning, and evaluation pipeline for multilingual machine unlearning, evaluating on both training and hold-out languages and treating knowledge as dispersed across languages. It shows successful multilingual unlearning requires methods that account for cross-linguistic knowledge spread, not just per-language removal.

entry.title: Shake to Learn: Dynamic Interrogation of Hidden Object Physics for Robotic Manipulation with Physical Reservoir Computing

author.name: Wen Sin Lor, Jun Wang, Suyi Li

entry.summary: The paper shows that dynamically perturbing grasped objects (shaking) can reveal hidden physical properties like center of mass and internal contents, using an origami-inspired soft robotic arm as a physical reservoir computer whose ringdown responses are decoded into object physics. This establishes interaction as a new perceptual modality for robotic manipulation.

entry.title: LOInK: Learned Optimal Inverse Kinematics via Structured Neural Surrogate Models

author.name: Michael Somerfield, Damian Abood, Ruigang Wang, Ian R. Manchester

entry.summary: LOInK learns a bi-Lipschitz invertible mapping from configuration space to a decoupled task/latent space whose origin corresponds to cost-minimizing IK solutions, enabling efficient sampling of approximately optimal solutions via operator-splitting network inversion. It is demonstrated on a 3-DOF manipulator, a quadrupedal climbing robot, and other problems.

entry.title: SABER: Learning Attention-based Semantic Affordance for Legged Locomotion

author.name: Hari Prasanth Palanivelu (Michael), Samuel Sze (Michael), Kennard Garrison Johannes (Michael), Albertus Hendrawan Adiwahono (Michael), Meng Yee (Michael), Chuah

entry.summary: SABER is a planner-free reinforcement-learning policy for legged locomotion that jointly reasons about terrain geometry and semantic contact permission via a unified terrain-affordance map encoding local 3D geometry and semantic contact cost. It uses cross-attention augmentation so that geometrically traversable but semantically inappropriate surfaces (a fragile box, equipment in industrial sites) are avoided.

entry.title: Contact-Rich Motion Planning via GPU-Parallel Mode Evaluation

author.name: Jiayun Li, Georgia Chalvatzaki

entry.summary: CoMET revisits broad evaluation of contact-mode sequences for contact-rich motion planning by exploiting modern GPU hardware, combining GPU-parallel trajectory optimization with greedy contact-mode expansion. On planar pushing benchmarks it matches the full-enumeration reference on nearly all instances and is competitive with optimization-based, sampling, and tree-search baselines in solution quality and planning time. This offers a scalable alternative to heuristic-pruned contact-mode search.

entry.title: A Fully Differentiable Neuro-Soft-Symbolic Framework for Perceptual Task Planning

author.name: Hongyan Wei, Wael AbdAlmageed

entry.summary: The framework connects visual perception and task planning in a single differentiable computational graph, maintaining a continuous soft symbolic state and lifting domain rules into a differentiable transition operator. Gradients from the planning objective can flow back to perception parameters, preserving perceptual uncertainty that discrete-symbol pipelines discard. It targets perceptual planning tasks requiring both scene understanding and rule-following action sequences.

entry.title: Driving on Registers, Reasoning on Risk: Risk-Aware Occupancy for Register-Based End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Jiaxing Chen, Hengduo Zou, YuKai Qin, Yiren Zhao, Lidong Yu, Bolin Gao

entry.summary: RRDrive extends a register-based end-to-end driving baseline with risk-aware occupancy as a dense, temporally aligned, trajectory-queryable representation, improving multimodal candidate generation and ranking where the baseline ranks the oracle-best candidate only 33.9th on average. It also contributes the RiskOcc4D-NAVSIM benchmark. This is a companion work to ROIDrive from the same group.

entry.title: FOCAL-VLA: Subtask-Guided Geometry Distillation and Implicit World Modeling for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Zhiyuan Gao, Di Wen, Yanxiang Zhan, Mohammad Khoshnazar, Jeroen Sch\"afer, Kunyu Peng, Michael Beetz

entry.summary: FOCAL-VLA improves vision-language-action models for precise, long-horizon manipulation by combining subtask-guided geometry distillation with implicit world modeling, focusing supervision on geometry and dynamics relevant to the current interaction rather than the whole scene. This counters redundant scene-level supervision that distracts from task-relevant structure.

entry.title: Potential-Field Action Representation for Reinforcement Learning in Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Xinyu Liu, G\"okhan Solak, Arash Ajoudani

entry.summary: Proposes PA-RL, an RL framework that replaces direct Cartesian motion commands with artificial potential fields as the action representation, letting policies adjust goals rather than commanding motion every step. This decouples task-level adaptation from low-level control, easing exploration and physical execution in contact-rich manipulation.

entry.title: MOSAIC-SR: Transformer-Guided Symbolic Regression for Scientific Equation Recovery

author.name: Peiyi Zheng, Yanming Kang, Hans De Sterck, Giang Tran

entry.summary: MOSAIC-SR combines pretrained Transformer proposals with local search for symbolic regression: the Transformer proposes multiple initial expression sketches that seed searches in promising regions, jointly recovering structure and constants, rather than relying on random initialization or fast-but-error-prone neural generation alone. This hybrid targets interpretable closed-form equation recovery for scientific discovery. It seeks to blend neural speed with search robustness.

entry.title: Understanding LLM Quantization through Activation-Guided Compensation and Orthogonal Residuals

author.name: Yamato Narita, Issei Sato

entry.summary: This work decomposes post-training weight-activation quantization error into an activation-guided weight compensation term and an orthogonal residual, bounding the residual via persistent channel-wise outliers. The decomposition clarifies which error components weight optimization, channel scaling, and orthogonal rotation each address in aggressive W4A4 LLM quantization. Such analysis guides future low-bit inference methods.

entry.title: Intervention Granularity Matters: Coherent Treatment Bundles in Counterfactual Simulation with Clinical World Models

author.name: Fangzhou Wang, Yixuan Yang, Camilla Balzarotti, Rishikesan Kamaleswaran

entry.summary: The authors study counterfactual simulation in clinical world models, showing that treatments are documented as bundles of co-occurring components (audited over 945,707 patient-hours of MIMIC-IV) and that editing single components creates unrealizable scenarios. They introduce Clin-JEPA, a latent world model of patient trajectories, and demonstrate that intervention granularity materially changes model responses.

entry.title: Reconstruction of 4D Mitral Regurgitation Hemodynamics from Sparse Planar Data using Deep Operator Networks with Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Jakob Marcel Hoffmann, Yosuke Hasegawa, Alexander Stroh

entry.summary: Uses a Deep Operator Network pretrained on an experimentally benchmarked URANS simulation database to reconstruct transient 3D transvalvular hemodynamics from a single planar velocity slice and two boundary pressure traces, with test-time adaptation to unseen conditions. The approach could enable quantitative mitral regurgitation assessment beyond the assumptions of clinical flow convergence methods.

entry.title: Chronosphere: Space-Time Tessellation of Local Climate Experts

author.name: Daniel Cher, Eric Xing, Kexing Li, Brian Wei, Isaac Corley, Nathan Jacobs

entry.summary: Chronosphere is a spatio-temporal neural field for climate representation learning that pairs an adaptive learnable tessellation of sites on the spacetime torus with a shared bank of local basis functions, unifying global bases (spherical harmonics), localized bases, and learned tessellations. It adaptively allocates representational capacity where environmental processes are most complex, addressing a core limitation of existing location encoders.

entry.title: When Better Turns Do Not Make Better Agents: Diagnosing the Gap Between Next-Turn Metrics and Workflow Success

author.name: Md Tahmid Rahman Laskar, Xue-Yong Fu, Gundeep Singh, Karol Chang, Kevin Sanders, Shi Zong, Tania Habib, Julien Bouvier Tremblay, Shayna Gardiner, Harsh Saini, Matthias Lee, Elena Khasanova, Quinten McNamara, Shashi Bhushan TN

entry.summary: The paper investigates whether next-turn evaluation with gold interaction history predicts autonomous workflow execution, studying SFT-trained Qwen3 (4B/14B) and Gemma 3 (4B/12B) models on multi-turn customer-support workflows. SFT consistently improves text-turn and overall next-turn success under gold-history evaluation, but these improvements do not transfer to autonomous workflow execution.

entry.title: Classification-oriented adaptive sensing via posterior sampling

author.name: Andriy Enttsel, Maxime Rousselot, Vincent Corlay

entry.summary: The paper extends diffusion-based adaptive compressed sensing from reconstruction-driven probe selection to a classification-driven criterion, decomposing posterior uncertainty into within-class and between-class terms via a class-conditional Gaussian mixture and estimating them from diffusion posterior samples. This selects sensing directions that best reduce classification uncertainty.

entry.title: PIVOT: Physically Informed Vision-Language Off-Road Traversability for Field Robot Navigation

author.name: Aoran Jiao, Wenda Zhao, Hshmat Sahak, Timothy D. Barfoot

entry.summary: PIVOT augments geometry-based off-road planning with VLM-based semantic reasoning for traversability, validating that the VLM-predicted traversal energy cost, vibration, and wheel slip correlate with real-world measurements and combining them into a unified traversability score for field robots. This reduces the over-conservatism of pure geometric terrain assessment.

entry.title: FORTE: Task-Adaptive Force Capability Optimization for Mobile Manipulators

author.name: Xiao Wang, Heng Zhang, Gokhan Solak, Fei Zhao, Arash Ajoudani

entry.summary: FORTE is a task-oriented force capability optimization framework for redundant mobile manipulators in which a VLM infers object physical properties from an RGB image and task description to generate a desired task-force sequence. A signed-distance force capability metric then drives redundancy resolution that meets task-specific force demands without indiscriminately maximizing force and sacrificing dexterity.

entry.title: ZeroTouch: Tactile-Supervised Visual Contact Estimation for Contact-Rich Manipulation

author.name: Dmitriy Kosenkov, Daniia Zinniatullina, Miguel Altamirano Cabrera, Iana Zhura, Mikhail Derevianchenko, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: ZeroTouch is a tactile-supervised framework predicting dense contact deformation, instantaneous six-axis wrench, and a grasp-dependent compression target from wrist RGB observations, gripper state, and gravity direction, with tactile measurements used only as privileged training supervision and not needed at deployment. It reduces normal-force MAE from 2.017 N with a state-only baseline to 0.531 N and shows improvements in physical evaluation.

entry.title: AcousticDiffusion: Semantically Conditioned Audio-Guided Diffusion Policy for Search-and-Rescue Assistance

author.name: Iana Zhura, Didar Seyidov, Dmitrii Plotnikov, Hajira Amjad, Miguel Altamirano Cabrera, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: AcousticDiffusion is a diffusion-based navigation policy guided by audio for rescue robots seeking human callers when vision is degraded or occluded. It combines a frozen pretrained audio recognizer with speech gating and distress-aware prioritization, recursively integrating microphone-array direction-of-arrival measurements into a Bayesian bird's-eye-view belief field with ego-motion compensation. The system enables human-directed navigation toward sound sources in search-and-rescue scenarios.

entry.title: AnyviewMeter: Adapting Robotic Reward Models with Camera Geometry and Multi-View Attention

author.name: Yuang Tu, Runjia Tan, Yujie Yan, Jinghan Hu, Chen Lv

entry.summary: AnyviewMeter is a geometry-conditioned adaptation framework for robotic reward models whose scalar progress predictions otherwise shift with camera viewpoint and occlusion. It combines low-rank fine-tuning with token-aligned Plucker ray conditioning that injects camera geometry into visual features and attention, plus synchronous block attention to fuse synchronized multi-view observations inside the pretrained decoder. This makes reward model adaptation robust to how a task is observed.

entry.title: GameASG-Bench: Benchmarking Autonomous Software Generation for Game Development

author.name: Xiuhui Zhang, Yi Chen, Shusheng Xu, Fan Li, Huan Wang, Tongkai Yang, Binhang Yuan

entry.summary: GameASG-Bench makes behavioral testability part of the autonomous software generation task for game development by declaring evaluation interface specifications before generation, fixing legal scenarios, actions, snapshots, and invariants. It includes static L1 source-level checks and browser-executed L2 semantic checks. This addresses the gap where generated applications run but their components may not satisfy specified behaviors.

entry.title: EnterpriseVal: Quantifying the Efficacy, Reliability and Value of Generative AI in the Enterprise

author.name: Abbas Raza Ali, Muhammad Ajmal Siddiqui, Moona Zahid

entry.summary: Argues that the gap between strong benchmark performance and failed enterprise GenAI deployments is largely a measurement problem, and presents EnterpriseVal, a use-case-level evaluation system specifying the frozen socio-technical configuration, data, and controls needed to judge whether a workflow is fit, reliable, safe, and worth scaling on an organization's own data.

entry.title: Fewer Steps, Better Actions: Rethinking Flow-Matching Inference for VLA Policies

author.name: Zhipeng Tang, Xinda Chen, Weining Rao, Xiao Li, Wenting Tan, Yuning Wang, Xiao Shi, Xiaofang Zhao

entry.summary: The paper proposes Coda, which reallocates flow-matching integration budget for vision-language-action policies toward a single learned endpoint correction: a frozen policy produces a few-step action trajectory, and a lightweight trained Transformer predicts a demonstration-supervised residual. On 50 RoboTwin Easy tasks, five-step Coda raises success from 71.64% to 74.68% while reducing inference cost.

entry.title: OneBid: A Unified Auto-Bidding Foundation Model for Diverse oCPX Advertising Scenarios

author.name: Yewen Li, Peng Jiang, Yitian Li, Pengfei Lv, Xialong Liu, Peng Jiang, Qingpeng Cai

entry.summary: Proposes OneBid, a foundation-model approach unifying heterogeneous oCPX auto-bidding scenarios (registration, purchase, etc.) that previously required separate models, tackling multi-objective control, latency-constrained capacity, and safe offline policy improvement. It targets cross-scenario modeling in computational advertising beyond Decision Transformer baselines.

entry.title: Detecting Pretraining Data in Large Language Models from a Free-Energy Perspective

author.name: Chenye Ke, Zirui Liu, Qi Liu, Yan Zhuang, Jintao Zhang, Zhenya Huang, Shijin Wang

entry.summary: Improves membership inference for pretraining data detection by replacing the horizontal likelihood-only boundary with an inclined boundary that evaluates prediction loss relative to predictive entropy, showing entropy correction preserves membership signal while reducing variance. The mean-variance analysis extends to settings with a nonzero mean entropy gap.

entry.title: On the Limits of Maximal Coding Rate Reduction for Out-of-Distribution Generalisation

author.name: Menghui Zhou, Gaoshan Bi, Vitaveska Lanfranchi, Po Yang

entry.summary: The paper identifies two fundamental limitations of maximal coding rate reduction (MCR2), an information-theoretic objective behind interpretable white-box architectures, showing it can completely fail under distribution shift. The authors theoretically characterize when MCR2 representations generalize out-of-distribution. This tempers enthusiasm for an influential representation-learning framework with concrete failure conditions.

entry.title: Tracing the Evidence Behind Zero-Shot Time-Series Forecasting: A Source-First Taxonomy and Audit Framework

author.name: Delun Kong, Wanyun Ling, Chenxi Liu, Ziyue Li

entry.summary: This paper argues that zero-shot time-series forecasting should be defined by what evidence a system can access, not merely by whether parameters are frozen. It proposes a source-first taxonomy separating frozen LLM prior reuse, time-series pretraining, and retrieval-augmented memory, plus an audit framework for verifying claims. Conceptual clarity here could discipline a fast-growing but fuzzy evaluation area.

entry.title: Beyond Gaussian Worlds: Latent Geometry Matters for JEPAs

author.name: L\'eo Nicollier (CB, ATT), Enric Meinhardt-Llopis (CB), Marc Pic (ATT), Pablo Mus\'e (CB, IFUMI), Gabriele Facciolo (CB)

entry.summary: Building on Klindt et al.'s 2026 result that Gaussian target distributions in JEPAs guarantee recovery of Gaussian latents up to linear transformation, this paper extends the analysis to latents supported on embedded Riemannian manifolds. It derives conditions on latent geometry and positive-pair dynamics under which alignment and exact distribution matching still yield linear recovery. This sharpens the theory behind self-supervised JEPA-style representations.

entry.title: The Weight Is Over - Interactive Diffusion on Consumer GPUs

author.name: Frieder Ganz, Maximilian M\"uller

entry.summary: The authors tackle on-device diffusion image generation on consumer hardware, proposing an embedding translator that maps a small text encoder into a large encoder space, a reproducible recipe for navigating the speed/quality/memory trade-off, and an interactive editor achieving sub-second time-to-first-image. The work aims to bring diffusion pipelines to as many client devices as possible despite their memory and latency demands.

entry.title: Aggregated Posterior Predictive Checks for Generative Modeling

author.name: Shweta Dutta, Gemma E. Moran

entry.summary: Addresses prior-aggregated posterior mismatch in latent variable generative models and the increasingly common two-stage strategy of sampling from the estimated aggregated posterior (as in VAEs and latent diffusion). The paper develops posterior predictive checks adapted to this aggregated-posterior sampling regime, providing a principled goodness-of-fit diagnostic for modern generative models.

entry.title: Adaptive Rollout Truncation Based on Epistemic Uncertainty for Efficient Offline World Model Training

author.name: Nikodem Sebastian Zymla, Laurin Thiele, Johannes Pitz

entry.summary: This work proposes an adaptive strategy for training neural world models in which autoregressive rollout horizons are truncated based on the model's current epistemic uncertainty rather than fixed throughout training. Following an auto-curriculum scheme, rollouts stop where the model is unreliable, reducing compute and avoiding amplification of early training errors. This improves efficiency and stability of offline world-model training for model-based robotics.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Diffusion Guidance via Curvature-Adaptive Tubular Correction

author.name: Enze Jiang, Jinwei He, Zheng Ma

entry.summary: CAT is a training-free plugin for gradient-guided diffusion samplers that regulates both first-order normal departure and second-order tangent-induced departure from learned iso-density surfaces within a shared noise-dependent geometric budget. It improves the reliability of strong guidance in inverse problems and conditional generation.

entry.title: ProTracer: Proprioception-Guided Failure Diagnosis in Robot Manipulation

author.name: Chang Dong, Mehdi Hosseinzadeh, King Hang Wong, Lingqiao Liu, Francois Fraysse, Feras Dayoub, Minh Hoai Nguyen

entry.summary: ProTracer is a training-free framework using existing vision-language models plus proprioceptive signals for manipulation failure analysis, covering detection, categorization, explanation generation, and temporal localization of failure onset by converting robot-state dynamics into structured natural language. This supports more interpretable robot debugging without new training.

entry.title: Towards Effective Visual-Inertial SLAM with Passive-Only Sensors for Low-Cost Autonomous Underwater Vehicles

author.name: Grant Schwidder, David Widhalm, Junaed Sattar

entry.summary: This work shows robust underwater visual-inertial SLAM is achievable on a sub-$10,000 open-source AUV using only stereo cameras, MEMS IMUs, and depth sensors, avoiding expensive DVL/USBL systems. It aims to democratize advanced marine robotics for research and hobbyist applications.

entry.title: MicroHookACT: Monocular Microscopic Vision Guided Visuomotor Policy for Flexible Microelectrode Hooking

author.name: Yitong Chen, Fangbo Qin, Yang Wang, Ruihua Hu, Kui Zhang, Shan Yu

entry.summary: MicroHookACT is an imitation-learning visuomotor policy for automated 3D hooking of flexible microelectrodes under monocular microscopic vision, a critical step in implantation. It combines a defocus-cue-based unidirectional hooking strategy, an action-supervised attention module on a frozen ViT that learns to focus on micro-needle tips from human demonstrations without manual annotations, and dynamic weighting of coarse and fine visual features.

entry.title: CRISP: Contact-Rich Robotic Simulation Platform with Extensive Geometries and Contact Solvers

author.name: Somang Lee, Sunkyung Park, Jinhee Yun, Seoki An, Dongjun Lee

entry.summary: CRISP is a new high-fidelity physics simulation engine designed for tight-tolerance, multi-contact robotic manipulation. It supports diverse geometric representations paired with accurate optimization-based collision detection and contact solvers, addressing limitations of existing simulators that use simplified contact modeling or numerically constrained resolution. The platform aims to enable more physically faithful sim-to-real research.

entry.title: Clinician-Grounded Quality Assurance for AI-Assisted Psychiatric Intake

author.name: King Shi, Amanda Li, Jonathan Ivey, Synthia Qia Wang, Guan Gui, Hyunseo Kim, Peter Zandi, Jason Straub, Jacob Taylor, Ananya Joshi

entry.summary: InterviewPlayground is a clinician-grounded evaluation platform for AI-assisted psychiatric intake built around a memory-augmented patient simulator, enabling evaluation across different clinician interviewing styles with minimal clinician burden. It was developed with expert-authored vignettes and a simulated intake platform. This matters for safe health-system deployment of AI interviewing tools.

entry.title: Efficient Benchmarking in Production: A Study of an Evolving LLM Agent

author.name: Yining She, Lei Lin

entry.summary: This paper studies recurring efficient evaluation of a production analytics agent serving tens of thousands of monthly users, comparing random sampling, caching, fixed subsets, and IRT-based adaptive testing across 574 historical benchmark runs. Multidimensional 2PL adaptive testing achieved best fidelity at 38.5% of full-run cost, yet the authors deployed difficulty-stratified fixed subsets for operational reasons. It offers rare first-hand production evaluation data.

entry.title: Calibrating Teacher--Student Discrepancy for On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Qiangqiang He, Jin Li, MingCai Chen

entry.summary: This arXiv paper identifies a flaw in on-policy distillation (OPD) for reasoning models: the teacher-student token-level discrepancy that standard OPD learns is contaminated by the teacher's own likelihood deviations, not just the genuine capability gap. The problem is amplified in privileged OPD, where privileged information causes larger teacher-side shifts. The authors propose Calibrated On-Policy Distillation (Cal-OPD), which estimates and separates teacher-side deviation so the student learns a cleaner distillation signal.

entry.title: Accelerating Dense LLMs via L0-regularized Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Zhenyu Zhang, Jiudong Yang, Zhaowen Tao, Meng Chen

entry.summary: L0-MoE is a lightweight MoE method that accelerates dense LLM inference using L0-regularization, combined with a cluster confusion matrix for domain-aware dataset curation and dynamic batching. It reportedly achieves up to 2.5x speedup over dense models while keeping performance competitive and beating prior acceleration baselines.

entry.title: dSTAR: Straggler Tolerant and Byzantine Resilient Distributed SGD

author.name: Jiahe Yan, Pratik Chaudhari, Leonard Kleinrock

entry.summary: This paper introduces dSTAR, a lightweight distributed SGD method that aggregates gradients from the first k responding workers and filters them using an ensemble median to handle both slow stragglers and Byzantine attacks. It targets robust and reliable gradient aggregation under network and system failures during distributed model training.

entry.title: VLA-Scope: Shift-Aware Failure Prediction for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Kaiwen Zhu, Dongfang Liu, Liangkai Liu

entry.summary: VLA-Scope is a two-stage framework predicting execution failure of VLA policies under distribution shift: it first detects OOD inputs and classifies shift categories, then combines category, action-prefix, and execution-progress features to predict failure during OOD rollouts. It observes that OOD detection alone is insufficient since models can still succeed under shift.

entry.title: Beyond Exact Match: Task-Aware GRPO for Cross-Domain PCBA Visual Question Answering

author.name: Jia Li, Li Dai, Peng Jia, Zhenzhen Hu, Chee Seng Chan, Bingkun Bao, Richang Hong

entry.summary: Proposes a multimodal reasoning framework for visual question answering in printed circuit board assembly inspection, unifying standards-derived and real production-line imagery in a shared instruction format. It applies a task-aware GRPO reward to handle heterogeneous output spaces such as multiple-choice and counting tasks while addressing domain shift.

entry.title: Chinese Competitive Debating Dataset and Benchmark

author.name: Zongrui Yang, Haoyuan Li, Zhongsheng Wang, Zhirui Zeng, Pengqian Han, Yi Zhou, Yuting Wang, Jiamou Liu

entry.summary: Introduces a dataset and benchmark for evaluating LLM understanding of competitive Chinese-language debate, built from 182 organized matches adjudicated by 120 professional judges under a shared rubric, yielding 148 verified matches and over 20,000 exchange units at match, stage, and speaker levels. It matters because debate adjudication requires tracking argument development through interaction, a capability existing datasets rarely test with professionally ground-truthed judgments.

entry.title: From Switching to Dynamic Regret: A Simple Reduction via Unbiased Random Sequences

author.name: Yibo Wang, Wenhao Yang, Sifan Yang, Yuanyu Wan, Lijun Zhang

entry.summary: The authors give a simple reduction from dynamic regret minimization to switching regret minimization in non-stationary online learning, constructing an unbiased auxiliary random comparator sequence with controlled variance. This lets optimal dynamic regret bounds for strongly convex and exp-concave losses be derived from off-the-shelf switching-regret algorithms. It simplifies what previously required intricate bespoke analyses.

entry.title: Multi-Subject Pretraining Enables Short-Calibration Personalization for Closed-Corpus Surface EMG Speech Decoding

author.name: Chenqian Le, Beatrice Fumagalli, Yasamin Esmaeili, Xupeng Chen, Tianyu He, Nikasadat Emami, Adeen Flinker, Yao Wang

entry.summary: This paper tackles silent speech interfaces based on surface electromyography, which normally require heavy per-user calibration due to cross-user variability. Using a multi-subject pretraining plus short fine-tuning pipeline on 27 participants with under 0.5 hours of data each, the authors achieve 21.7% character error rate in a closed 50-sentence corpus, far better than 49.3% without calibration. This shows personalized neural speech decoding is feasible with minimal calibration data, which matters for assistive communication technology.

entry.title: RACER: Role-Aligned Competence Estimation for Human-AI Routing

author.name: Joshua Strong, Emma Sun, Alexander Capstick, Pramit Saha, Cheng Ouyang, J. Alison Noble

entry.summary: RACER addresses learning-to-defer to unseen human experts by estimating a posterior-predictive, instance-level competence profile for an expert from a small context set. It improves on prior population-adaptive deferral methods that either learn routing shortcuts or provide only class-constant competence estimates, offering role-relative estimation for human-AI routing.

entry.title: VISPATH: Visual-Intent-Guided Path Reasoning for Multimodal Knowledge Graph Question Answering

author.name: Jinke Wu, Zhengpin Li, Mengzhe Jia, Yang Li, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes VISPATH, a framework for multimodal knowledge graph question answering that uses visual intent to guide multi-hop path reasoning rather than only grounding starting entities or retrieving evidence. This keeps multimodal cues active at intermediate reasoning hops, addressing a key weakness of prior MM-KGQA methods that degenerate into text-only graph search.

entry.title: Identifying Security Platform Product Abuse with Machine Learning

author.name: Shaefer Drew, Michael Brautbar, Paul Knight, Edward Raff, Lana Peric-McDermott, Simran Sarin, Nickolas Machado, Hanna Albright, Vitaly Zaytsev

entry.summary: Presents the first whole-system ML study of detecting product abuse of security platforms, where sophisticated threat actors misuse security tools in customer environments or probe the product itself using living-off-the-land techniques. The work addresses multi-database data modalities, cold-start rarity of abuse events, and real-world deployment constraints such as cost and performance.

entry.title: Weighted Quantum Signal Processing: Low-Depth Polynomial Approximation with Applications to Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks

author.name: Rohit Sarma Sarkar, Rupayan Bhattacharjee, Elias F. Combarro, Michele Grossi, Lirand\"e Pira, Carmen G. Almud\'ever, Sergi Abadal, Eduard Alarcon

entry.summary: This paper introduces Weighted Quantum Signal Processing (WQSP), an extension of Quantum Signal Processing that assigns a weight function to the central rotation operator, generalizing QSP as the unit-weight special case. The framework reveals parameter redundancies in standard QSP, enables lower circuit depths, and is applied to quantum implementations of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks.

entry.title: Configurable Multi-Stage Vision Pipeline for Crop Disease and Pest Diagnosis

author.name: Naga Ganesh, Chandrashekar M S, Lakshmi Pedapudi, Aakash Singh, Vineet Singh

entry.summary: This paper describes the engineering and evaluation of a configurable multi-stage vision pipeline for Farmer.Chat, Digital Green's advisory service, where farmers send only a photograph taken on cheap phones under poor conditions. Analyzing about 1.16 million photographs from Ethiopia, India, Kenya, and Nigeria, the authors add adjustable rejection thresholds, extensible crop and problem classes, and confidence cut-offs, addressing real deployment constraints in agricultural AI for development.

entry.title: Boosting Deepresearch and LongContext Ability with Self-Generated Deepresearch Rollouts Traces

author.name: Zihan Wang, Hao Wang, Boyuan Jiang, Yiqun Zhang, Shi Feng, Xiaocui Yang, Yiwen Ye, Jianghang Lin, Xiaozhong Ji, Jinghao Lin, Kai Wu

entry.summary: The authors observe that even after deep-research agentic RL, 61.6% of remaining prediction errors stem from insufficient long-context understanding, including long-context hallucination and cross-document integration failures. They propose DR-to-Long, which repurposes deep-research RL rollout trajectories into long-context QA training data to jointly improve agentic search and long-context ability.

entry.title: MAGIC: Marginal-Guided Compression with Optimal Transport for Efficient Visual Document Retrieval

author.name: Xu Yuan, Hua Liu, Wenqi Fan, Qing Li

entry.summary: MAGIC introduces a training-free post-hoc compression method for multi-vector visual document retrievers like ColPali, using optimal transport with marginal guidance to decide which patch embeddings to merge. This reduces index storage and MaxSim scoring overhead while accounting for the non-uniform patch usage that uniform compression objectives ignore.

entry.title: Quantization-Aware Kalman Estimation for Diffusion Sampling

author.name: Qitan Shi, Cheng Jin, Jiawei Zhang, Yuantao Gu

entry.summary: QuAKE formulates sampling with a quantized diffusion denoiser as an online estimation problem, using the history of quantized outputs in a Kalman framework to recover the underlying full-precision outputs during sampling. This corrects quantization errors that propagate across timesteps, beyond what local correction methods achieve.

entry.title: CompAdapt: Adaptable Composite Motion Modeling for Physics-Consistent Text-to-Video Generation

author.name: Haoran Qin (Harbin Institute of Technology, China), Renlong Wu (Harbin Institute of Technology, China), Tianyu Huang (Harbin Institute of Technology, China), Yukang Ding (Taobao, Alibaba Group, China), Hui Li (Harbin Institute of Technology, China), Wangmeng Zuo (Harbin Institute of Technology, China)

entry.summary: CompAdapt extends physics-constrained text-to-video generation from simple single-type motions to composite physical behaviors such as coupled motions and multi-stage transitions, without manually specified parameters. It aims to make diffusion-based video generation respect fundamental physical dynamics in complex real-world scenarios. This matters because physical plausibility is a major gap in current T2V models.

entry.title: OmniVBench: A Benchmark and Large-Scale Dataset for Omni Reference-to-Video Generation

author.name: Wenxue Li, Peiyan Guan, Haoyang Jiang, Junxian Cai, Hualuo Liu, Chunjie Zhang, Chong Guan, Songlian Li, Taiyi Wu, Yongjian Yu, Xiaotong Zhao, Alan Zhao, Eric Liu, Xi Chen, Yu Liu, Lei Zhu

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces OmniVBench and the Omni-R2V Dataset, a benchmark and large-scale training resource for omni reference-to-video generation, where video models must preserve, disentangle, and route many types of reference inputs. The authors argue existing R2V benchmarks cover too few reference types and evaluate only holistic consistency, so they expand evaluation to test whether individual reference factors are correctly handled. The dataset also addresses the scarcity and high cost of suitable training data for this emerging paradigm.

entry.title: Do Spinning Radar Doppler Velocity Measurements Improve Vehicle Detection and Tracking?

author.name: Eric Xie, Daniil Lisus, Timothy D. Barfoot

entry.summary: The paper empirically investigates whether per-azimuth Doppler velocity from spinning FMCW radars improves vehicle detection and tracking, proposing ego-motion-corrected radar images for detection and per-vehicle Doppler-derived velocity priors for tracking motion models. It gives a direct answer to a practical question for all-weather autonomous vehicle perception.

entry.title: NaViRrator: Robot Navigation from Human-Readable Maps through a Learned Visual Route

author.name: Ayun Lee, Jiseon Kim, Giseop Kim

entry.summary: NaViRRator translates user-specified start and goal locations on human-readable maps into navigation instructions for a pretrained vision-and-language navigation policy. Its RouteScribe method separates route inference from verbalization, using start-goal line conditional flow matching to deform a straight waypoint sequence into a route scaffold that a pretrained VLM converts into natural navigation instructions.

entry.title: AVT-Fabric: Active Visuo-Tactile Perception via Adaptive Evidence Selection for Efficient Robotic Fabric Comparison

author.name: Chang Gao, Zhuo Chen, Suhang Xia, Jihong Zhu, Jiankang Deng, Shan Luo

entry.summary: This paper introduces AVT-Fabric, an RGB-first framework that lets a compact 7B multimodal LLM decide adaptively when to gather additional tactile (GelSight) evidence during robotic fabric comparison, using a dual-scale gate over answer-token confidence and logit separation. With textual memory of executed actions and majority voting, it reaches 98.0% accuracy on 400 held-out comparisons, beating a 90B baseline (94.0%) while using only about 1.6 of five available sensing stages.

entry.title: Towards Fine-Grained Object Manipulation: SAM3-Guided Visuomotor Policy with Persistent Memory Learning and Focused Visual Conditioning

author.name: Haolong Meng, Fangbo Qin, Mengchen Bai, Houwu Wang, Cirong Liu, Shan Yu

entry.summary: This work presents a SAM3-guided visuomotor framework for fine-grained object manipulation that distinguishes a specified object from visually similar distractors. FOM-SAM3 learns reusable memory tokens from limited multi-view registration images while keeping SAM3 frozen, using one-vs-rest learning for persistent target localization, paired with focused visual conditioning of the policy.

entry.title: Visual Proactivity: Enhancing Human-Robot Collaboration Through Intent Communication

author.name: Valerio Bo, Edison Bejarano, Ana\'is Garrell, Alberto Sanfeliu

entry.summary: This paper introduces visual proactivity, a method for robots to communicate their own intentions to humans through visual feedback during collaboration, complementing the better-studied problem of inferring human intent. By taking initiative in signaling intent, robots can guide human behavior and improve transparency and interaction fluency. The approach is developed and evaluated in collaborative task settings.

entry.title: A Sim-to-Real Integration Pipeline for Training and Deployment of Chunk-Based VLA Manipulation Policies

author.name: Mathilde Kappel, Cl\'emence Grislain, Mohamed Chetouani, Olivier Sigaud, Louis Annabi, Fa\"{\i}z Ben Amar, St\'ephane Doncieux, Mahdi Khoramshahi

entry.summary: This paper presents an open-source sim-to-real protocol for training and deploying chunk-based vision-language-action manipulation policies, addressing the bottleneck of expensive real-world teleoperated demonstration collection. The pipeline covers expert data generation, training, evaluation, and real hardware deployment. It aims to make VLA policy development more reproducible and scalable.

entry.title: Repulsive normalizing flow mixtures for adaptive importance sampling: reliability analysis of complex systems

author.name: Sara Helal, Victor Elvira

entry.summary: Introduces FAMIS, a flow-based multiple importance sampling framework for rare-event estimation that learns a nonuniform mixture of normalizing flow proposals without presampled failure data or knowledge of failure mode geometry. It uses a smooth rare-event surrogate, tempered target sequences, and repulsive (diversity-encouraging) mixture components to cover multiple failure modes in reliability analysis of complex systems.

entry.title: From Task Success to Productive Success: Evaluating Human-AI Collaboration by Quality and Cost

author.name: Saki Imai, Mert \.Inan, Malihe Alikhani

entry.summary: The paper proposes a productivity-oriented evaluation framework for human-AI collaboration that measures outcome quality relative to interaction cost rather than task completion alone. Across two datasets and four tasks, it shows sessions with identical quality can differ up to 70x in interaction cost, and that quality-cost relationships and subjective ratings diverge across task types.

entry.title: WS-NeRF: A Mamba-Driven World-State-Aware Adaptive Deblurring Neural Radiance Field

author.name: Hang Jiang, Jinghao Wang, Yiming Zhang, Xinhong Wang, Luwei Ran, Yinfeng Yu

entry.summary: Proposes WS-NeRF, a Mamba-based neural radiance field that adaptively deblurs degraded multi-view images by formulating radiance-field optimization as a dynamic evolution process with temporal memory and multi-dimensional world states. It targets joint handling of image blur and 3D inconsistency during reconstruction.

entry.title: Steering LLMs Responses Towards Moral Foundations on the Norwegian MFQ-30

author.name: Hans Andersen, David Dichas

entry.summary: Administers the Norwegian Moral Foundations Questionnaire to six open-weight LLMs and compares their profiles with 1,282 human respondents, testing persona-level and activation-level steering interventions. A key finding is that about half the models produce flat or central-tendency questionnaire answers that look near-human on average without tracking item content.

entry.title: REFINEPPO: Learning Continuous Control Policies by Iterative Action Refinement

author.name: Sachini Weerasekara, Sagar Kamarthi, Jacqueline Isaacs

entry.summary: REFINEPPO explores policies that iteratively refine actions rather than producing them in a single feed-forward pass, learning a progressive improvement process for continuous control built around PPO-style training. The question is whether iterative refinement during policy learning yields advantages over direct action prediction. This draws on test-time compute/refinement ideas applied to control.

entry.title: OpenMAS-GCom. A Diagnostic Benchmark for Graph-enhanced Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Kairui Yang, Xunkai Li, Kaixiang Zhang, Minghao An, Zekai Chen, Yuxuan Ba, Rong-Hua Li

entry.summary: OpenMAS-GCom is a diagnostic benchmark that attributes performance differences in graph-enhanced multi-agent LLM systems to specific communication structures, role assignments, and information flows via controlled interventions. It addresses the confounding in final-score comparisons that mixes model, topology, and compute-cost effects. This kind of controlled evaluation could meaningfully improve multi-agent systems research methodology.

entry.title: $\lambda$-Controlled GRPO: Turning Flow-Matching Ratio Instability into a Budgeted Resource

author.name: Yufeng Wang, Parivesh Priye, Meeshawn Marathe, Ramit Pahwa

entry.summary: The paper analyzes training instability in Flow-GRPO, a reinforcement learning method for aligning flow-matching image generators, showing that seemingly separate failure modes (importance ratio drift, dispersion, uneven clipping) stem from a single per-step quantity. The authors convert this into a budgeted, controllable resource via lambda control, unifying prior hand-tuned stabilizers.

entry.title: Voice-Light: A Full-Duplex Cascaded Voice Agent with Causal Turn-Taking and Speculative Generation

author.name: Bertil Braun

entry.summary: Voice-Light is a full-duplex cascaded voice agent combining immediate acoustic onset detection, a causal adapter sharing a streaming ASR encoder, reversible playback control, and private speculative response generation. It handles overlapping speech without canceling on every acknowledgment, prepares responses before a turn is certain, and keeps canceled audio out of conversation history. Evaluation on 1,673 real-conversation silence candidates informs timing decisions.

entry.title: Edit-VAR: Taming Visual Autoregressive Model for Precise Video Editing

author.name: Chongbo Zhao, Jiangming Wang, Xilai Wang, Xinyu Wang, Jingyi Tang, Chunjie Hao, Pengjie Song, Yue Ma

entry.summary: Edit-VAR presents the first training-free and inversion-free framework for text-guided video editing built on a pretrained visual autoregressive model, avoiding the trajectory-recovery errors of inversion-based methods and the weak editing strength of inversion-free guidance. It preserves temporal coherence of unedited regions while enabling semantic changes.

entry.title: The Role of Radiometric Features in Cross-Site Leaf-Wood Segmentation of LiDAR Point Clouds

author.name: Roman Kaharlytskyi, Derek T. Robinson, Roberto Guglielmi

entry.summary: The paper shows that geometry-only leaf-wood segmentation methods, including state-of-the-art deep models trained on high-density LiDAR data, fail to generalize from terrestrial scans to sparse aerial RPA scans, and that radiometric features such as intensity and return number substantially help cross-site transfer. This challenges a common design choice made purely for sensor compatibility.

entry.title: Adapting Rigid-Body Dynamics Derivatives for Constraint Embedding Closed-Chain Models

author.name: Daniel J. Volpi, Patrick M. Wensing

entry.summary: The paper extends first-order derivative algorithms for rigid-body dynamics to closed-chain systems modeled via constraint embedding, removing the assumption that joint velocity effects are locally configuration invariant. It compares conventional pin-joint models against more complete actuation models capturing local closed chains.

entry.title: Stabilizing Trajectory Outputs in End-to-End Autonomous Driving via SC-IMM Based Teacher Signals

author.name: Siewoo Kim, Seung-Hyun Kong

entry.summary: This work proposes an offline teacher-signal generation method for stabilizing trajectory outputs in end-to-end autonomous driving, based on a Scene-Conditioned Interacting Multiple Model (SC-IMM). Expert trajectories are converted into path-speed states and IMM updates conditioned on scene cues generate teacher labels that better capture scene-dependent path-speed changes and temporal instability than coordinate-level imitation learning.

entry.title: TinyCeNN-LM: Quality-Gated Conversion of Pretrained Attention with CeNN-Inspired Cellular-Recurrent Layers

author.name: Kabeh Mohsenzadegan, Vahid Tavakkoli, Kyandoghere Kyamakya

entry.summary: TinyCeNN-LM proposes quality-gated post-training conversion that replaces attention layers in a pretrained language model with Cellular Neural Network-inspired cellular-recurrent layers, using accept-or-rollback validation against representation and NLL thresholds. On SmolLM2-135M, early layers convert successfully while a deeper layer is rejected when representations drift. This explores whether attention can be swapped for cheaper local-processing layers in existing models.

entry.title: LEGIT: Credentialing Protocol for Trustworthy AI Agent Marketplaces

author.name: Steve Drew, Jiayu Zhou

entry.summary: LEGIT is a credentialing protocol for agentic marketplaces that binds measured quality and cost per solved task to an agent configuration, task domain, and evaluation budget via signed certification records, with reputation linking outcomes to agent identity. It aims to make agent quality claims verifiable and comparable across tasks and budgets. This addresses trust infrastructure for emerging agent marketplaces.

entry.title: One Prompt Does Not Fit All: Self-Meta-Evolve for Personalized Information Extraction

author.name: Hongliang Li, Lu Wang, Yong Xu, Hanyang Chen, Zhitao Hou, Xiaoting Qin, Song Ge, Qingwei Lin, Dongmei Zhang

entry.summary: Formulates enterprise information extraction as per-user prompt adaptation under interaction feedback and proposes Self-Meta-Evolve, a hierarchical framework maintaining a dedicated prompt per user. An inner loop edits structured prompts from persona-conditioned feedback while an outer loop evolves the meta-prompt by distilling adaptation experience.

entry.title: MIST: Multimodal Survival Prediction with Genomic-Guided Histology Attention

author.name: Muhammet Sami Yavuz, Sabri Mustafa Kahya, Richard R. Chen, Jana Lipkova, Benedikt Wiestler

entry.summary: MIST fuses whole-slide histology images and genomic profiles for survival prediction by letting genomic tokens query compact foundation-model-derived histology context tokens, enriching molecular features with morphological context before prediction. Training combines discrete-time survival objectives with modality masking and dropout for robustness under cohort shift.

entry.title: Geometry of Values: Task Vector Composition for Ethical Preference Alignment in Language Models

author.name: Utkarsh Agarwal, Monojit Choudhury

entry.summary: The paper builds a 12,000-instance dataset of two-option ethical dilemmas across Honesty, Justice, and Autonomy conflicts, translated into five languages, to probe cross-lingual moral behavior. Testing on GPT-5-mini and Llama-3.2 shows default value biases and option-position biases, which plain fine-tuning and DPO can steer using task-vector composition for controllable ethical preference alignment.

entry.title: KnowDemo: Knowledge-Guided Robot Demonstration Generation from Human Videos

author.name: Zhiyuan Gao, Yanxiang Zhan, Mohammad Khoshnazar, Jeroen Sch\"afer, Michael Beetz

entry.summary: KnowDemo uses structured manipulation knowledge extracted from human videos to generate diverse, valid robot demonstrations, addressing limitations of motion-reference adaptation that locks in demonstrated contact strategies and subtask orders. It aims to improve behavioral diversity and efficiency of demonstration generation while reducing invalid candidates.

entry.title: Consistent Relexicalization of Clinical Documents using Graph-Based Approach

author.name: Dipankar Das, Atri Mandal, Sandeep Singh, Tushar Shandhilya

entry.summary: Presents G-RELIC, a graph-based clinical NLP relexicalization method that combines LLMs with graph structures to preserve structural, relational, and temporal consistency when masking sensitive information and synthesizing clinical datasets. It avoids the clinical inconsistencies caused by independent entity replacement in longitudinal records.

entry.title: Outcome-Conditioned End-Effector Geometry Across Vision-Language-Action Policies

author.name: Xingyu Lin, Zhuang Li, Zhongrun Wu, Shouquan Zhou, Dehui Du

entry.summary: Analyzes 15,000 closed-loop LIBERO rollouts from four VLA policies, forming 3,600 configuration-matched pairs to show that trajectories of both-success policy pairs are geometrically far more similar (median DTW distance 0.0120 m) than pairs where only one policy succeeds (0.0380 m). The finding suggests task success masks substantial differences in physical execution behavior across policies.

entry.title: TERMon: Detecting Persistent Behavioral Threats in Edge AI via Hardware-Native Ternary Runtime Monitor

author.name: Arish Sateesan, Edlira Dushku

entry.summary: Proposes TERMon, a lightweight hardware runtime monitor for edge AI accelerators that detects anomalies by matching thermometer-encoded fingerprints of inference behavior against class-conditional trusted ternary patterns, without re-executing or verifying the model. It targets safety-critical settings where corrupted models or adversarial inputs still yield confident, well-formed outputs.

entry.title: Benchmarking the Explanatory Quality of Open-Weight Vision-Language Models in Face Recognition

author.name: Laurent Colbois, S\'ebastien Marcel

entry.summary: Introduces a benchmarking framework for VLM-based face recognition that treats explanation quality as a first-class evaluation axis, proposing relevance (reliance on identity-stable facial features) and faithfulness as criteria for natural-language explanations in forensic contexts. This extends evaluation beyond recognition accuracy toward transparent, auditable decisions.

entry.title: Bayesian Belief Layer for Controllable Opinion Dynamics in LLM Agents

author.name: Hafsa Akbar, Daniel Platnick, Marjan Alirezaie, Hossein Rahnama

entry.summary: Introduces Bayesian Chronicle Agents, a belief layer separating what an LLM agent believes from how it speaks, where each stance is a probability updated by one Bayesian step per utterance heard and a prior-strength parameter encodes stubbornness following Friedkin-Johnsen opinion dynamics. Sweeping the parameter yields canonical opinion-dynamics regimes on demand, including consensus and persistent disagreement.

entry.title: Layerwise Decoupling for Stable Structured Sparsification of Fully Connected Layers

author.name: Charles Kulick, Armenak Petrosyan, Sui Tang

entry.summary: The authors propose a decoupled, layerwise method for structured sparsification of fully connected layers, extracting shallow two-layer subnetworks and applying group penalties sequentially to prune neurons. They prove equivalence at optimality between the decoupled objective and a specific joint penalty for positively homogeneous activations, and find the decoupled reformulation more robust than coupled alternatives. This advances theory-backed structured pruning.

entry.title: Kinks vs. Smoothness: Identifiability of Real Analytic nICA for Laplace-like Sources

author.name: Isaac Manring, Kejun Huang

entry.summary: The authors prove identifiability up to trivial ambiguities for nonlinear Independent Component Analysis with real analytic generating functions when the source densities have finitely many first-derivative discontinuities, with the Laplace distribution as the canonical example. The proof exploits the contrast between kinks in source distributions and the smoothness of analytic mixing functions.

entry.title: A Smoothed Discrepancy Principle for Random Feature Methods and Neural Networks

author.name: Mike Nguyen, Nicole M\"ucke

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-scale, data-driven early-stopping rule for spectral regularization in non-parametric regression that achieves full adaptivity across all smoothness levels in the well-specified case. A random-feature extension reduces computational cost on large datasets while preserving minimax-optimal guarantees, and also yields a fully data-driven choice of the number of random features.

entry.title: Detection is solved, delineation is not: what governs tooth segmentation on panoramic radiographs

author.name: Muhammad Rehan, Moaz Amjad, Syed Danial Ahmed, Mariam Adnan, Haider Ali

entry.summary: The study assembles a large expert-annotated corpus of 1,422 panoramic radiographs with over 42,000 tooth polygons, annotated by 30 practitioners, to systematically isolate what drives tooth segmentation performance. Findings show input resolution dominates gains at high IoU thresholds while architecture and anatomical priors matter differently, refocusing attention from detection (solved) to fine delineation in dental radiography.

entry.title: Near-Optimal Acceleration for Smooth $\ell_p$ / $\ell_q$ Nondual Convex First-Order Oracle Optimization

author.name: David Mart\'inez-Rubio, Brian Bullins, Crist\'obal Guzm\'an, Mathieu Molina

entry.summary: The authors derive near-optimal accelerated first-order oracle rates for convex objectives with Holder-continuous gradients in non-dual lp/lq geometries, yielding polynomial-query error bounds and resolving a COLT 2015 open problem of Guzman up to logarithmic factors. The framework includes connections to convex set chasing and achieves cubic decay in the smooth case.

entry.title: Do small language models know what they don't know?

author.name: Prashant Mudgal

entry.summary: This study tests whether entropy-based confidence signals can improve accuracy of sub-3B-parameter language models running on consumer hardware, evaluating seven approaches across 7 model pairs and 5 NLU benchmarks. The key finding is that token-level entropy is nearly zero regardless of correctness in 91% of dataset-model combinations, making token-based confidence unusable at this scale, while semantic entropy over sampled generations works better.

entry.title: Omni Demand Understanding: A Benchmark for Contextual User-Intent Inference in Multimodal Interaction

author.name: Qi Chen, Yunfei Chu, Haolin He, Yifan Yang, Zihan Liu, Yuxuan Wang, Ziyang Ma, Ruiyang Xu, Meng Gao, Yinsong Yan, Ling Wang, Hui Wang, Wen Huang, Yiheng Chen, Guanrou Yang, Qiuqiang Kong, Jin Xu, Xie Chen

entry.summary: Presents a benchmark testing whether multimodal AI assistants can infer users' underlying demands from speech, vision, and dialogue history, including cases where request-like speech is not actually directed at the assistant. It shifts evaluation from response quality to intent inference under ambiguity, disfluency, and noisy acoustics.

entry.title: 4DGS-Fixer: Generative Sparse-View 4D Gaussian Splatting with Iterative Refinement Guided by Video Diffusion Priors

author.name: Haitao Huang, Shenghao Zhao, Boyuan Tian, Shin-Fang Chng, Songlin Yang, Sheila Lim, Huangying Zhan, Yi Xu, Anyi Rao, Frank Guan

entry.summary: This work tackles dynamic scene synthesis from sparse-view video using 4D Gaussian Splatting, addressing poor geometric initialization from sparse COLMAP point clouds. It iteratively refines scenes with guidance from video diffusion priors, filling in missing regions that geometric priors alone cannot recover.

entry.title: VoxelTTO: Voxel-Aligned Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting with Test-Time Optimization

author.name: Yibin Zhao, Yihan Pan, Yangwen Li, Jun Nan, Jianjun Yi

entry.summary: VoxelTTO is a feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that decodes Gaussians from a global voxel representation instead of pixel-aligned primitives, reducing overlap artifacts and camera-pose misalignment in novel-view synthesis. It uses test-time optimization to exploit known camera parameters while keeping pretrained vision foundation model weights frozen. Works from an arbitrary number of images with optional camera poses.

entry.title: SignGPT: Toward LLM-Mediated Sign Language Interaction through Gloss-Free Translation and Generation

author.name: Ronghui Li, Jun Dong, Zhongyuan Hu, Zunnan Xu, Jun Zhou, Liyuan Chen, Shuoling Liu, Jiangpeng Yan, Jie Guo, Xiu Li, Linchao Bao

entry.summary: SignGPT unifies gloss-free sign language translation and generation in a pose-based framework that integrates part-aware hierarchical body/hand/face motion representations into a shared LLM, using asymmetric multi-token prediction and progressive training for bidirectional modeling. It is evaluated on How2Sign (ASL) and Phoenix-2014T (DGS), including an exploratory study with 12 Deaf ASL signers. Enables sign language as both input and output of one model.

entry.title: Robust Structureless Monocular Visual Inertial Initialization Exploiting Line Features and Vanishing Points

author.name: Junwan Choi, Woongrae Jo, Dong-Uk Seo, Jinwoo Jeon, Hyun Myung

entry.summary: SLIM-init is a structureless monocular VIO initializer that exploits vanishing points from tracked 2D line features as translation-invariant orientation cues, enabling robust initialization under degenerate motions without restrictive excitation or expensive 3D reconstruction. This improves practical deployment of visual-inertial odometry in real-world scenarios.

entry.title: MAPLE-RF: Efficient Probabilistic RF Source Localization in Partially Explored Environments

author.name: Haozhe Lei, Sundeep Rangan

entry.summary: MAPLE-RF studies single-snapshot RF transmitter localization on partially explored maps built during SLAM, comparing an extended digital-twin ray-tracing approach with a learned method that encodes estimated angles of arrival. Both produce posteriors over transmitter locations without a complete environment model.

entry.title: Tilt as a Certified Resource: Preserving Motor Wrench-Rate Authority on Articulated Multirotors

author.name: Giuseppe Silano, Martin Saska

entry.summary: This paper treats servo tilt on articulated multirotors as a geometric resource that breaks a zero-sum degeneracy in which motor-speed redistribution cannot improve disturbance-rejection authority without conceding wrench tracking. It constructs a configuration-dependent formulation that preserves motor wrench-rate authority, or readiness, which classical effort-minimizing allocators ignore and which pure readiness maximization makes physically infeasible.

entry.title: Compact but Moving: Intervention-Relevant Geometry in Recurrent World Models

author.name: Yuming Chen, Yang Liu

entry.summary: This analytical paper studies what happens to low-rank counterfactual interventions in recurrent world models after they enter the model, building on a previously identified rank-4 intervention interface. The correction rapidly leaves the fixed entry subspace during autonomous rollout, yet a low-rank image transported through the factual recurrent Jacobian chain captures most of the nonlinear correction. Restarts with the tangent-predicted correction preserve substantial counterfactual future function.

entry.title: PopNavShift: Stress-Testing Social Navigation under Behavioral Population Shift

author.name: Kaizhen Tan, Diyu Zheng, Tim Guangyu Wu, ChengHe Guan

entry.summary: PopNavShift is a matched simulation framework for stress-testing social navigation algorithms under shifts in pedestrian population behavior. It builds population-conditioned pedestrian motion profiles by prompting the existing Gemini 3.7 Flash model with 600 synthetic persona records from MatrAIx Persona 1M and deterministically mapping responses into bounded motion parameters, then compares reactive avoidance, early yielding, and reciprocal collision avoidance strategies across eight population conditions. The work exposes how navigation performance can degrade when pedestrian distributions shift.

entry.title: Designer-RSI: Evolving Procedural Memory from User Traffic for Agentic Graphic Design

author.name: Hongyang Du, Lan Yan, Christian Flores, Asim Kadav

entry.summary: A continual adaptation framework where a frozen frontier model operates professional design software through more than 230 tools while an external procedural memory of natural-language skills grows in width (new recurring subtasks) and depth (revision from successes and failures), gated by replay so only non-regressive changes are admitted.

entry.title: Hallucination-R1: Robustness-Oriented Paraphrase Generation for Factual Consistency

author.name: Wenhan Yu, Wenxin Wu, Hao Wang, Lei Sha

entry.summary: The paper studies paraphrase-induced hallucination, where a model answers correctly in original form but fails under semantically equivalent paraphrases, and proposes HALLUCINATION-R1. This framework learns to generate paraphrases that are semantically faithful yet robustness-challenging, providing better adversarial supervision for factual consistency than near-copy or overly diverse paraphrases.

entry.title: SpecQuant: Speculative Decoding with Multi-Parent Quantization for Adaptive LLM Inference

author.name: Harish KB, Jagadeeswaran M, Pradheep P, Yuvanesh S, Sivakumar T

entry.summary: SpecQuant is a training-free framework that combines speculative decoding with multi-parent quantization, deriving INT4, FP8, and FP16 variants from a shared base model and routing queries by predicted complexity. Simple or factual tasks use lightweight variants while harder queries use full precision, all without retraining, per-architecture tuning, or draft models. It targets efficient local LLM inference on consumer hardware.

entry.title: Cube-Splat: High-Fidelity 360{\deg} Gaussian Splatting SLAM via Cubemap Factorization and Adjoint-Consistent Optimization

author.name: Xiangfei Guo, Hao Shi, Yufan Zhang, Zhonghua Yi, Yongqi Mao, Xiaoting Yin, Kaiwei Wang

entry.summary: Cube-Splat is described as the first panoramic Gaussian-splatting SLAM framework, factorizing each 360-degree frame into a cubemap of four virtual pinhole views sharing one optical center. An adjoint mapping accumulates gradients from all faces to coherently update a single pose state, while anisotropic Gaussians are densified for dense reconstruction.

entry.title: AeRove: A Compact Bimodal Aerial-Terrestrial Drone with Rapid Bistable Reconfiguration for Close-Range Pipeline Inspection

author.name: Caleb Polillio, Petras Swissler

entry.summary: AeRove is a bimodal robot that rolls along pipelines using its propeller guards as wheels and reconfigures to flight via a spring-loaded bistable mechanism in 200 ms, cutting current draw 14x versus continuous flight while improving thrust efficiency. This directly addresses hovering cost and airflow interference in close-range gas-leak inspection.

entry.title: LoRA Enhanced Contrastive Learning with SAS Vision Transformers

author.name: Dan Zimmerman, Frank E. Bobe III, Amelia L. McCormack, Matthew Cook, Gregory D. Vetaw

entry.summary: This paper adapts DINOv3 Vision Transformers to underwater synthetic aperture sonar automatic target recognition via a three-stage parameter-efficient framework: LoRA-based domain bridging, hard-negative mining against acoustic mimics, and supervised contrastive learning to separate targets from clutter. It targets naval applications constrained by scarce imagery and background clutter. It demonstrates effective transfer of natural-image pretrained models to a niche sensing domain.

entry.title: LLM-Generated Feature Pools for Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Youssef Attia El Hili, Malik Tiomoko, Corinne Ancourt

entry.summary: A simple statistical pipeline with a strict feature-selection protocol for univariate time series anomaly detection, reaching 0.529 VUS-PR on TSB-AD-U — above the best neural and statistical leaderboard entries and close to pretrained foundation models with more supervision. Ablations show the LLM's contribution lies mainly in generating a useful candidate feature pool.

entry.title: SpaceDiffusion: Over-the-Orbit Diffusion for Space Generate-and-Forward Communications

author.name: Jianhao Huang, Zhanwei Wang, Khaled B. Letaief, Kaibin Huang

entry.summary: The paper proposes generate-and-forward (GF) relaying for 6G satellite uplinks, where satellites run generative diffusion models on-orbit to reconstruct corrupted data before forwarding. SpaceDiffusion implements this for satellite-assisted image transmission using a channel-adapted diffusion framework.

entry.title: Aligning with Lived Experience: Heterogeneous Benefits of Fine Tuning in Mental Health Support Generation

author.name: Mohit Chandra, Nabin Kim, Eli Min, Aamogh Sawant, Tanmay Sutar, Munmun De Choudhury

entry.summary: The paper introduces the COPES dataset and a three-axis evaluation framework for assessing how well LLMs generate community-aligned peer support for mental health queries drawn from platforms like Reddit. It evaluates zero-shot and fine-tuned models and finds heterogeneous benefits of fine-tuning for lived-experience-informed support generation.

entry.title: Knowledge-Graph-Augmented Chronos-2 for HEC-RAS Surrogate Forecasting

author.name: Edward Holmberg, Elias Ioup, Mahdi Abdelguerfi

entry.summary: Couples the frozen Chronos-2 time-series foundation model with hydraulic knowledge graphs for surrogate forecasting of water-surface elevation in HEC-RAS hydrologic simulations, adding residual decoding and graph-conditioned retrieval. Evaluation across thousands of cross sections from multiple simulation years shows strong event-balanced accuracy gains over baselines.

entry.title: CityLearn v3: A Configurable Simulation and Evaluation Framework for Realistic Control Studies of Renewable Energy Communities

author.name: Tiago Fonseca, Luis Lino Ferreira, Armando Sousa, Ava Mohammadi, Zoltan Nagy

entry.summary: Presents CityLearn v3, a configurable simulation framework for control studies of renewable energy communities that models changing membership, equipment failures, demand-response requests, load deadlines, and data quality issues that prior simplified environments ignored. This prevents control strategies that look cheap on paper but violate feasibility constraints.

entry.title: CIBuzzBench: A Benchmark for Cross-Lingual Understanding of Chinese Internet Buzzwords

author.name: Yifan Wang, Junyu Lu, Qifan Wang, Shun Zhang, Chaozhuo Li, Jiahao Liu, Zhijun Cao, Lingbin Bu, Fanliang Bu

entry.summary: Presents CIBuzzBench, a benchmark testing whether advanced LLMs can transfer culturally grounded understanding of Chinese internet buzzwords into English, where meanings are non-literal and rooted in local pragmatic contexts. The work is motivated partly by safety, since harmful content can be obscured through homophony, euphemism, and coded language.

entry.title: Matrix AdaGrad: Row-wise and Column-wise Adaptive Subgradient Methods

author.name: Wenpeng Zhang, Runsheng Yu, Peilin Zhao

entry.summary: Develops a general Online Mirror Descent framework with adaptive proximal functions for matrix-valued parameters, deriving row-wise and column-wise adaptive subgradient methods that extend AdaGrad-style adaptivity beyond vector parameters. This provides a principled theoretical basis for matrix-aware optimizers used in neural network training.

entry.title: Touvigation: Embodied Adaptive Object Acquisition for Blind and Low-Vision Users in Unfamiliar Indoor Environments

author.name: George Xi Wang, Xiangyu Li, Shaoyue Wen, Jiaqian Hu, Junan Xie, Yupeng Wang, Ziyue Shi, Qijun Chen, Maaike Bouwmeester, Yuhua Jin, Jing Qian

entry.summary: Presents a hands-free object acquisition system for blind and low-vision users that combines vision-language understanding with persistent local spatial modeling for low-latency, body-relative guidance, adapting spatial references across orienting, walking, reaching, and tactile verification stages. Designed from formative interviews with eight blind and low-vision participants.

entry.title: When Should a Failing Robot Ask? Initiating Corrective Human-Robot Dialogue from Audited Sensor Evidence

author.name: Eshika Pathak, Leela Krishna

entry.summary: Builds a simulated benchmark with known injected failure causes to measure how much robot sensors reveal about failures, finding force data nearly perfectly diagnostic (0.99) where image methods reach at most 0.55, then tests six open VLMs and shows their dialogue-initiation behavior tracks prompt surface features rather than evidence. Highlights a significant gap between VLM evidence sensitivity and prompt sensitivity.

entry.title: DiaVLo: Diagnosing Behaviours of Vision-Language Models

author.name: Lorenzo Corti, Jie Yang

entry.summary: Presents DiaVLo, a diagnostic framework that leverages human curation and VLM generation to construct specifications of desired versus observed VLM behaviors, surfacing misalignments and providing causal estimates of the most influential concepts steering behaviors. Evaluated on several open-source VLMs under classification and generation conditions.

entry.title: Gricea: An Open Science Platform for Conversational AI Research

author.name: Nikhil Sharma, Yunlin Gong, Xinyang Cheng, Ziang Xiao

entry.summary: Presents Gricea, an open-science platform representing conversational AI studies as configurable, deployable research artifacts that can be run, inspected, shared, and reused. A replication study replicated configurations from 93% of eligible CUI 2026 papers while flagging missing replication-critical information in 96% of papers.

entry.title: Generative inversion for early ranking of competing geologic interpretations

author.name: Harun Ur Rashid, Daniel O'Malley

entry.summary: This work presents a workflow for ranking competing geologic interpretations under severe data scarcity by translating interpretations into alternative spatial priors and scoring them against hydraulic-head observations using generative inversion. It offers an early-stage, quantitative alternative to subjective expert judgment before expensive drilling commitments. The method addresses a costly real-world subsurface decision problem.

entry.title: HMB-GAN: Hybrid Multi-B\'ezier GAN for Vector Shape Synthesis

author.name: Elian Hugh Thiele-Evans, Binh Duong Pham, Hani Omar M Alharbi, Liibaan Aaden, Syed Umer Hasnain Zaidi, Prem Prakash Jayaraman, Muhammad Saeed, Boris Eisenbart

entry.summary: This paper introduces HMB-GAN, a hybrid quantum-classical generative adversarial network that synthesizes CAD-ready closed vector shapes using stitched multi-segment Bezier representations with geometric continuity enforced by construction. The authors compare a quantum-enhanced generator against a classical generator within the same architecture, evaluating both on point cloud distribution metrics and geometric shape statistics. The quantum variant shows faster convergence, fewer parameters, and slightly improved point cloud performance, though the abstract suggests tradeoffs elsewhere.

entry.title: Decision-Focused Learning for Mean-Variance Portfolio Optimization via KKT-Based Reformulation

author.name: Kensei Nosaka, Shunnosuke Ikeda, Yuichi Takano

entry.summary: The authors develop a decision-focused learning approach for mean-variance portfolio optimization that avoids the surrogate losses and constraint relaxations used in prior work, via a KKT-based reformulation. This aligns predictive model training directly with downstream portfolio quality instead of prediction error. Results should interest the predict-then-optimize and quantitative finance communities.

entry.title: MACE: Memory-Agent Co-Evolution with Adaptive Memory Graphs for Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Kairui Yang, Minghao An, Xunkai Li, Ziheng Yi, Zekai Chen, Guangyuan He, Rong-Hua Li

entry.summary: MACE introduces adaptive memory graphs that store multi-agent collaboration traces as functional memory units with prerequisite and output dependencies, enabling reuse of planning, verification, and repair procedures across tasks. Empirical findings show that grouping dependencies improves retention, unit combinations vary by instruction format, and updating choices from outcome feedback beats separate scoring. It contributes to persistent, evolving memory for LLM agents.

entry.title: LLMs as Feature Engineers for Text-and-Tabular Prediction

author.name: Merwan Barlier, Blaz Skrlj

entry.summary: This work presents an iterative framework where one LLM proposes interpretable, schema-bound categorical feature definitions, another LLM extracts them, and a downstream tabular model evaluates their usefulness. Model errors such as AUC ranking inversions are translated into natural-language feedback to steer feature discovery, yielding up to 3x faster feature discovery versus unguided search across three public datasets.

entry.title: COMPLEX: A Closed-Form Certified Embedding of Multiparameter Persistence Modules

author.name: Sushovan Majhi, Atish Mitra, \v{Z}iga Virk, Pramita Bagchi

entry.summary: COMPLEX is a training-free, closed-form embedding of multiparameter persistence modules from topological data analysis that supplies a missing lower Lipschitz gauge. By slicing modules along a near-diagonal net and embedding barcodes with certified landmark maps, separated modules provably stay separated, validated on Orbit5k where the coherence condition holds on all audited pairs.

entry.title: Diverse and Adaptable Arm Coordination for Octopus-Crawling via Diffusion-Based Uncertainty-Aware Optimization

author.name: Seung Hyun Kim, Heng-Sheng Chang, Kimia Kazemi, Prashant Mehta, Mattia Gazzola

entry.summary: Introduces DUO, a diffusion-based uncertainty-aware optimization algorithm that learns demonstration-free crawling controllers for a simulated muscle-actuated octopus, representing the first application of diffusion-based control to soft multi-arm robots in contact-rich simulation. Embedding diverse locomotion behaviors in a shared control distribution enables robust adaptation to dynamic physical constraints.

entry.title: Diagonalized Attention for Individualized Regression: Latent-Row Localization and Prediction

author.name: Borui Peng, Liwei Lin, Feifei Wang, Long Feng

entry.summary: Formalizes an individualized sparse regression framework for matrix-valued covariates, such as token or patch representations, where each observation has its own rows of interest but regression effects are shared across the population. A diagonalized attention mechanism uses query-key scores to localize sample-specific signal rows and a value matrix for downstream regression, with theoretical guarantees on parameter recovery.

entry.title: Complete Neural Electronic Initialization Accelerates Materials DFT

author.name: Felix {\AE}rtebjerg, Jonas Elsborg, Arghya Bhowmik

entry.summary: The authors present the first complete machine-learning method for accelerating plane-wave density functional theory under the PAW formalism, formalizing seven criteria a Complete Neural Electronic Initializer must satisfy. They identify two previously missing structure-dependent components, augmentation occupancies and spin initialization, whose omission can eliminate or reverse reported speedups, and supply them to achieve reference-free end-to-end acceleration.

entry.title: TatBLiMP: A Benchmark of Linguistic Minimal Pairs for Tatar

author.name: Ilshat Saetov, Dmitry Gaynullin

entry.summary: TatBLiMP is the first grammaticality evaluation benchmark for Tatar, a Qypchaq Turkic language, covering 16 morphosyntactic phenomena in 1248 minimal sentence pairs that differ by a single morpheme. Scoring requires no generation or parsing since it compares probabilities models already assign, and it can evaluate base models and mid-training checkpoints.

entry.title: COAL-SQL: Coverage-Guided Augmentation and Failure-Driven Learning for Text-to-SQL Post-Training

author.name: Qifeng Cai, Xuanguang Pan, Hao Liang, Chang Xu, Wentao Zhang

entry.summary: COAL-SQL is a unified post-training framework for text-to-SQL that combines coverage-guided data augmentation, which identifies structural gaps in training data, with failure-driven learning that dynamically addresses weaknesses exposed during training rather than relying on SFT or RL alone. It targets complex real-world SQL generation with open-source LLMs.

entry.title: Enhancing Audio Reasoning via Semantic Summary Prediction

author.name: Francesco Bonzi, Pooneh Mousavi, Cem Subakan, Mirco Ravanelli

entry.summary: SPARE addresses a reasoning gap in large audio language models where explicit chain-of-thought can reduce accuracy, hypothesizing that long reasoning shifts attention away from the audio. It introduces a register token aligned with the final conclusion via a cosine-similarity loss with a Sentence-BERT embedding, improving zero-shot reasoning on MMAU and MMAR with SALMONN at no extra inference cost.

entry.title: When Does Reasoning Help in Machine Translation? A Hierarchical Analysis of LRM Reasoning Traces

author.name: Yuxiang Liu, Jiaming Luo, Eleftheria Briakou, Colin Cherry

entry.summary: The paper analyzes reasoning traces of large reasoning models in machine translation across models, languages, and domains, finding the best reasoning language is model-specific, reasoning length relates non-monotonically to quality, and traces share a functional structure of understanding/planning, translating/drafting, and refining/verifying. It introduces Hierarchical Meta-Summarization (HMS), a scalable framework that induces reasoning structures without predefined taxonomies.

entry.title: Rethinking Human-Aligned Evaluation: An Analysis of Semantic Metrics Beyond WER

author.name: Hritika Sharma, Thibault Ba\~neras-Roux, Alessandra Pinto, Petr Motlicek, Hyunggu Jung, Esa\'u Villatoro-Tello, Somang Nam
