entry.summary: Introduces HATS-en, a human-labeled English dataset for ASR evaluation, and benchmarks WER against semantic metrics like BERTScore and SemDist under varied model, layer, and pooling configurations. WER agrees least with human judgment, while well-tuned SemDist configurations achieve the highest agreement.

entry.title: QuranicMMLU: A Cognitively-Aware Benchmark for Evaluating Generative AI Solutions on Quranic Linguistic Knowledge

author.name: Rawan El Ghali, Umm Kulsoom, Anas Madkoor, Dima Faris Alsaudi, Roaa Abdelmagid, Roaa Ibrahim, Raghad Mousa, Hamza Aljaji, Abdullah Khanafer, Abdallah Alkanani, Salah Feras Alali, Rawan Khaled Mohamed, Ehsaneddin Asgari

entry.summary: QuranicMMLU is a benchmark for evaluating generative AI on Quranic Arabic across a five-pillar linguistic taxonomy (Phonology, Morphology, Syntax, Semantics, Pragmatics) with 31 subcategories. Questions are stratified by Bloom's cognitive level and verse difficulty, with LLM-as-judge used for independent answering and scoring. It moves beyond generic QA benchmarks to probe specific linguistic competencies in a low-resource classical language.

entry.title: MarsFM: Shading-Regularized Flow Matching for Martian Relief Estimation

author.name: Marius F. R. Juston

entry.summary: MarsFM is an image-conditioned latent flow-matching model that estimates Martian terrain relief from single-band HiRISE orthoimagery, combining pretrained generative priors, stereo-derived supervision, and a differentiable Lunar-Lambert shading objective. It achieves low affine-aligned RMSE in normalized relief space across varying Euler step counts.

entry.title: VeriFuse: Bounded Vision-Language Arbitration and Reason-Guided Refinement for Cooperative 3D Perception

author.name: Hongyi Lin, Yiyao Liu, Qi Kang, Heye Huang, Yang Liu, Haris Koutsopoulos, Jinhua Zhao

entry.summary: VeriFuse defines a bounded arbitration role for vision-language models in vehicle-infrastructure cooperative 3D detection: agents produce detections independently, then a VLM arbitrates among original detections, perturbations, and cross-source geometric candidates within a calibrated candidate set. This avoids unreliable direct VLM regression while exploiting multi-agent information.

entry.title: When Online Adaptation Hurts: Parameter-Frozen Test-Time Ensembling for Continual Medical Image Segmentation

author.name: Ruijie Huang

entry.summary: This paper challenges continual test-time adaptation for medical segmentation under domain shift (changing scanner vendors), showing online updates can be infeasible or harmful on non-stationary streams. It proposes parameter-frozen inference enhancement: averaging anatomy-preserving scale and flip view predictions mapped back to native space, without modifying weights or normalization statistics, validated on the M&Ms cardiac MRI stream.

entry.title: SkillIR: Evolving Scene-Aware Skills for Agentic Image Restoration

author.name: Jie Shao, Shengkai Hu, Xu Zhang, Beihang Song, Yongcheng Jing, Xu Wu, Jun Wan

entry.summary: SkillIR is an agentic image restoration framework that represents experience as degradation-centered action evidence rather than full tool-use trajectories, allowing actions to adapt to evolving intermediate restoration states. It addresses the observation that accepted tool executions change residual degradation and thus the applicability of later tools. Relevant to the growing area of agentic tool-use for vision tasks.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Tumor Inpainting for Renal Segmentation under Clinical Data Scarcity

author.name: Ekaterina Sedykh, Salme Ussanov, Dmytro Fedorenko, Dmytro Fishman

entry.summary: A diffusion-based inpainting framework synthesizes anatomically plausible renal tumors in healthy CT scans without extra annotation, providing the first systematic comparison of 2D, 2.5D, and 3D (MAISI) synthesis strategies for segmentation augmentation. Training on public data and evaluating nnU-Net across low-data regimes, 2.5D and 3D augmentation cut false positives from roughly 18-20% to 3-6% while maintaining Dice. Addresses the common clinical problem of scarce tumor-positive annotations.

entry.title: Morphology-Aware Ambiguity Learning for Wafer Defect Decision Support

author.name: Seungjun Chu, Seokhyun Chung

entry.summary: This paper reframes wafer map defect recognition from fixed-taxonomy classification into a decision-support framework that outputs a single diagnosis, a pair of plausible defect classes, or a full-review flag based on a learned class-level ambiguity matrix built from radial, angular, and geometric wafer-map features. This matters because forcing a single label on boundary-ambiguous wafers can mislead manufacturing triage and yield analysis.

entry.title: How Many Posterior Samples? Calibrated Stopping for Adaptive Sensing

author.name: Vincent Corlay, Andriy Enttsel

entry.summary: This companion paper analyzes the stopping layer in classification-oriented adaptive sensing, showing that a plug-in vote-share threshold provides no confidence guarantee (declaring only about half the time at the threshold), and proposes calibrated fixed-sample and finite-horizon sequential rules. It turns heuristic posterior voting into statistically grounded decision-making.

entry.title: When to Waddle: A Comparative Study of Bipedal Torso-Stabilization on Low-Friction Surfaces

author.name: Naomi Oke, Ben Gu, George Ortiz, Stacy Ashlyn, Cordelia Pride, Sarah Bergbreiter, Aaron M. Johnson

entry.summary: Inspired by penguin waddling, this study compares upright-gait and torso-over-stance-leg strategies for bipedal locomotion on low-friction surfaces using a five-actuator biped in MuJoCo and hardware. Simulation sweeps across friction coefficients show torso-over-stance-leg motion yields more successful controllers and higher speeds at low friction.

entry.title: The EventCV Library for Event-Based Robotic Vision

author.name: Adam D. Hines, Michael Milford, Tobias Fischer

entry.summary: EventCV is an open-source, extensible Rust library with OpenCV-style Python bindings that lowers the barrier to using event cameras in real robotic pipelines. It provides denoising filters, geometric transforms, and unified handling of incompatible event-stream file formats that previously required custom research code.

entry.title: AgenticSwarm: Semantic Perception and Adaptive Task Allocation for Heterogeneous Multi-UAV Missions

author.name: Muhammad Ahsan Mustafa, Yasheerah Yaqoot, Faryal Batool, Roohan Ahmed Khan, Valerii Serpiva, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: AgenticSwarm is an agentic framework for heterogeneous multi-UAV missions in which an agent interprets aerial imagery and natural language instructions to build a grounded mission representation linking objects, regions, task requirements, capability constraints, and dependencies. This representation augments a constrained task-allocation process accounting for obstacle-aware path feasibility, energy consumption, and protected return-home requirements.

entry.title: When Should Robots Intervene? Balancing Engagement and Intrusiveness in Human-Robot Interaction

author.name: Lavinia Hriscu, Valerio Bo, Alberto Sanfeliu, Ana\'is Garrell

entry.summary: The authors compare continuous engagement-seeking robot behavior against a context-aware strategy that intervenes selectively based on user state and task context, using multimodal cues like body orientation and attention. A 32-participant user study in a simulated hospital task measures engagement, intrusiveness, and perceived support. The work provides empirical guidance on when assistive robots should initiate interaction.

entry.title: VIRGA: Virtual-Agent-Intermediated Riemannian Geometry for Active-Sensing Air-Ground Coordination

author.name: Fenghe Guo, Runjie Shen, Chenyang Sun, Junrui Zhang

entry.summary: VIRGA is a neural geometric coordination framework for air-ground teams where a UAV must remain observable by a gimbal LiDAR on a UGV. It converts dual-LiDAR observations into bounded source-specific Riemannian fields coupled through a virtual agent with reciprocal elastic feedback, then maps the shared coordination reference into feasible UAV, UGV, and gimbal commands with active-observation safeguards. Evaluation demonstrates coordinated motion under dynamic obstacles and changing task initiative.

entry.title: Square Root Gauss-Newton iLQR

author.name: Maximilian Haas-Heger, Jur van den Berg

entry.summary: This paper derives a square-root formulation of the iterative Linear Quadratic Regulator that propagates the Cholesky factor of the cost-to-go approximation instead of the matrix itself, offering numerical stability advantages analogous to square-root Kalman filters. The formulation is particularly beneficial when iLQR is embedded in augmented Lagrangian frameworks for constraints, where large penalties degrade conditioning. It improves on previous square-root iLQR formulations.

entry.title: AutoRecLab: Describe the Experiment, Get the Code!

author.name: Moritz Baumgart, Philipp Meister, Justus Krell, Michael Schmidt, Bela Gipp, Joeran Beel

entry.summary: AutoRecLab is an autonomous recommender-systems lab that turns natural-language experiment descriptions into executable code, deriving requirements, building and validating a prototype, and expanding it into full experiments using RAG for documentation, static type verification, and execution-steered tree search. A demonstration automates an explicit-to-implicit feedback conversion study.

entry.title: Visual Navigation Transformer with Pose Attention

author.name: Beiming Li, Jaime Romero, Jonathan Diller, Vijay Kumar, Alejandro Ribeiro

entry.summary: VNT-PA is a transformer navigation planner whose context is a set of depth keyframes indexed by camera pose, so attention depends on pose differences rather than temporal order. Trained to imitate a shortest-path planner, it can reuse experience from earlier traversals without explicit maps or topological graphs.

entry.title: IncentRL: The Trade-Off Between Preference Guidance and Task Performance

author.name: Xuening Wu, Yanlan Kang, Shenqin Yin

entry.summary: IncentRL formalizes how adding preference-based reward shaping changes the task an RL agent optimizes, using a KL penalty between actual and preferred outcome distributions. For finite discounted MDPs it derives external-value perturbation bounds, conditions for preserving the original optimal policy, and characterizes the large-weight regime. This gives principled guidance on when preference guidance helps versus distorts the task.

entry.title: GEM-MPC: Balancing Exploration and Exploitation through Expert-Guided Planning

author.name: Alvaro Serra-Gomez, Thomas Moerland

entry.summary: GEM-MPC is an MPPI-based reinforcement learning method that fixes misalignment between learned components in planning-based RL, combining a planner-cloning policy with a KL-regularized exploration policy. It refreshes stale planning distributions in replay and improves the exploration-exploitation balance in high-dimensional continuous control. This targets a known pain point in model-based RL with planning.

entry.title: HERMES: Contrast-Aware Knowledge Graph Reasoning from Clinical Notes for Patient Outcome Prediction

author.name: Gia-Bach Nguyen, Hoang-Ha Nguyen, Tuan-Cuong Vuong, Trang Mai Xuan, Duy Quoc Ngo, Tien-Cuong Nguyen, Huan Vu, Thien Van Luong

entry.summary: HERMES builds personalized knowledge graphs from clinical notes via LLM-guided extraction with contrastive logic modeling that captures temporal dynamics, treatment failures, and changes, operating exclusively on text while preserving relational and temporal structure. It targets patient outcome prediction, addressing limitations of flat-sequence encodings of unstructured notes.

entry.title: Predictive Suppression Layers for Communication-Efficient Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Aidin Attar, Michele Rossi

entry.summary: This work introduces a predictive coding scheme for spiking neural networks in which layers suppress redundant spikes: error units transmit signed spiking residuals while predictive suppression layers filter predictable information, cutting inter-layer communication overhead. This matters for many-core neuromorphic hardware and wireless IoT settings where spike transmission is a bottleneck.

entry.title: Beyond Reference-Based Evaluation: Reward Models for Meta-Evaluation of Grammatical Error Correction

author.name: Ruotian Wu, Bill E. Johnson, Gene Saunders, Osama Hamzeh, Ankit Vadehra, Pascal Poupart

entry.summary: RM-EVAL is a reward model trained on human preference data from SEEDA that serves as a reference-free meta-evaluator for grammatical error correction, predicting human-like judgments at full- and partial-sequence levels and avoiding penalties on valid but differently-phrased corrections. The same reward model doubles as a learning signal, improving a frozen GEC model via reward-guided online decoding (RGTG).

entry.title: Multi-viewpoint Geo-localization with Event Cameras

author.name: Adam D. Hines, Michael Milford, Tobias Fischer

entry.summary: This paper introduces an event-camera visual place recognition system robust to viewpoint changes, converting five large geo-tagged frame-based datasets into synthetic event streams via image-to-event conversion. It addresses an under-investigated failure mode in event-based localization and releases new resources for viewpoint-variance evaluation.

entry.title: PrismAlign: Prior-Steered Multi-View VLM Alignment for Hallucination-Robust Table OCR

author.name: Guangyi Liu, Qianjun Huang, Boyu Hou

entry.summary: PrismAlign is a multi-VLM framework for table extraction that aligns multiple visual perspectives to resolve ambiguity, uses priors about table logic to assess output plausibility, and applies a Bayesian decision strategy exploiting correlations between extraction errors and computable rule violations. It reports SOTA results on OmniDocBench 1.5 and table categories of CC-OCR and PureDocBench.

entry.title: PointLAM: Local Attentive Mamba for Efficient Point-based 3D Object Detection

author.name: Xuanming Shang, Weijia Zhang, Chao Ma

entry.summary: PointLAM tackles the efficiency bottleneck of point-based LiDAR 3D detection (slow FPS downsampling and costly k-NN queries) with a Laplacian Point Sampler using implicit discrete Laplacian high-pass filtering and a Local Attentive Mamba module for linear-complexity point interaction. It aims to preserve geometric fidelity of point-based methods while achieving voxel-like efficiency. A hybrid efficiency-oriented architecture contribution.

entry.title: AutoViewMem: Self-Configuring Orthogonal Views for Conversational Long-Term Memory

author.name: Zijie Cao, Xijun Qu, Zhicheng Gu, Xiaoshu Chen, Duanyang Yuan, Yanning Hou, Sihang Zhou, Jianxing Gong, Jian Huang, Yang Mei

entry.summary: AutoViewMem organizes long-term conversational memory into self-configuring, low-overlap semantic views before indexing, discovering candidate views from interaction traces to avoid semantic interference in mixed representations. This addresses top-K retrieval noise in LLM agent memory across preferences, events, constraints, and temporal updates.

entry.title: MIRCID: Inferred Hub-miRNAs Drive Cross-Task Improvements in Drug Mechanistic Modeling

author.name: Xin Cao, Yigang Chen, Jiatong Xu, Ziyue Zhang, Xiang Cheng, Shenyu Wang, Yangyi Zhang, Xiaoxuan Cai, Shidong Cui, Zihao Zhu, Xiang Ji, Hsi-Yuan Huang, Yang-Chi-Dung Lin, Hsien-Da Huang

entry.summary: MIRCID infers regulatory features (transcription factor activity and miRNA expression) to augment perturbational transcriptomes for drug mechanism-of-action modeling when matched miRNA measurements are unavailable. HubmiRNet infers 414 pan-cancer hub miRNAs from 977 landmark genes with high correlation and outperforms an existing method on full-miRNA prediction, with miRNA augmentation yielding consistent gains in pathway classification and MoA retrieval. It enables scalable reuse of transcriptomic data for drug discovery.

entry.title: Time series generation with spectrally aligned latent flow matching

author.name: Camilo Carvajal Reyes, Felipe Tobar

entry.summary: The authors propose a spectrally aligned latent flow-matching generator for time series, training the latent space to preserve dynamical properties via fine-tuning losses based on Fourier, wavelet, and signature transforms. This addresses spectral mismatch artifacts of latent compression that hinder synthetic data use as training surrogates.

entry.title: Analysing the Linearity of Linguistic Relations in Language Model Embedding Spaces

author.name: Vasudevan Nedumpozhimana, Fathima Thekkekara, John Kelleher

entry.summary: The authors formalize linear encoding of linguistic relations via constrained linear approximation over related and unrelated word pairs, applying an extended BATS dataset to GloVe, RoBERTa, and ModernBERT. They find near-perfect linear encoding for inflectional and derivational relations but substantially worse for lexicographic and encyclopedic ones, especially one-to-many associations, with contextual models encoding relations more linearly than GloVe.

entry.title: CoLearn: An Agentic Tutor that Learns its Learner in a Human--AI Co-Learning Loop

author.name: Kailai He, Zhihao Wu, Linhai Zhang, Runcong Zhao, Yulan He, Jiazheng Li

entry.summary: CoLearn is an interactive agentic tutor that maintains persistent, evidence-grounded memory of a learner's mastery and misconceptions, updated with a soft-evidence variant of Bayesian Knowledge Tracing where an LLM helps interpret answers. The accumulated memory is used to generate the next personalized question in an iterative human-AI co-learning loop.

entry.title: Evaluating In-Context Learning and Retrieval Strategies for Devanagari Post-OCR Correction

author.name: Abhishek Bhandari, Gaurav Harit

entry.summary: First systematic evaluation of LLMs (3B-32B) for training-free post-OCR correction in Hindi and Marathi, comparing example-retrieval strategies including a proposed CharBM25 that matches OCR error patterns via character n-gram similarity. Across a 20,000-sentence benchmark, retrieval strategy proves decisive, with CharBM25 beating domain-random selection by 2.8-4.0pp.

entry.title: VGGT-CAD: Reconstructing Parametric CAD 3D Model with Geometric Grounding

author.name: Chunan Yu, Tianrun Chen, Fu Shen, Cheng Chen, Lanyun Zhu, Yang Yang

entry.summary: VGGT-CAD transfers pretrained multi-view 3D geometric priors into parametric CAD reconstruction from single and multiple views, encoding camera parameters as condition tokens and fusing variable-viewpoint features via a cross-view aggregation module. The goal is recovering both precise geometry and editable modeling operations.

entry.title: JEPA Guided Diffusion: Predictive Vision-Language Conditioning for Generative Traffic Forecasting

author.name: Trinh Tra Giang Nguyen, Thanh Nguyen Vo, Nguyen Hoai Thuong Bui, Ha Duc Bui

entry.summary: This work decouples future representation learning from video generation for traffic forecasting: a frozen V-JEPA encoder extracts predictive latent scene dynamics, which a lightweight alignment module projects into the conditioning space of a frozen Cosmos diffusion model. This avoids costly end-to-end training of generative forecasters.

entry.title: Adaptive Color Grading

author.name: Trevor D. Canham, Abhijith Punnappurath, Michael S. Brown

entry.summary: The authors build an open-source color grading tool, use it to annotate a large video dataset with tonescale-region thresholds, and model how practitioners adjust shadows, highlights, and other regions, finding that simple K-nearest-neighbor prediction outperforms state-of-the-art end-to-end approaches. It bridges cinematographic practice with automated image/video enhancement.

entry.title: AI-GRACE: A Use-Case Operationalization Framework for Agentic AI: From Organizational Objectives and Obligations to Deployment Capabilities and Architecture

author.name: John Cuneo, David Chun, Gaurav Khanna

entry.summary: AI-GRACE is a governance framework that connects organizational objectives, obligations, risk, assurance, controls, and evidence for agentic AI deployments, using design science and situational method engineering for contextual tailoring. It aims to specify what to validate, control, and observe per use case rather than asking generic trustworthiness questions. It is a governance-oriented contribution rather than a technical study.

entry.title: Ability-Residual Decoupled Modeling for Affective Cognitive Diagnosis

author.name: Boyuan Zhao, Meng Ye

entry.summary: This paper argues that affective cognitive diagnosis models wrongly assume the cognitive backbone has already absorbed ability, item, and concept effects, leaving residuals attributable to affect. It proposes decoupled modeling that accounts for item calibration bias, concept bias, and latent student-item matching before attributing errors to affective states. This improves diagnosis models used in educational data mining.

entry.title: Listen Before You Speak: Response Planning from Listener Facial Reactions for Conversational Speech Generation

author.name: Yunji Chu

entry.summary: ReACT-TTS is a two-stage framework that conditions speech planning on a one-second pre-response listener facial sequence to choose emotion and prosody before generating speech. On a strict dyadic MELD protocol it improves affective measures (macro-F1, VAD concordance) over text-only conditioning, and speech researchers rate its output as more contextually appropriate.

entry.title: Reinforcement learning for post-coronagraphic wavefront control

author.name: Manuela Casta\~neda-Medina (LIRA), Yann Gutierrez (LIRA), Johan Mazoyer (LIRA, CNRS), Baptiste Abeloos, Laurent Mugnier, Olivier Herscovici-Schiller

entry.summary: The paper applies deep reinforcement learning to post-coronagraphic wavefront control for high-contrast exoplanet imaging, training an agent to drive a deformable mirror in a simulated testbed. The fully data-driven approach learns adaptive aberration correction at the subnanometric precision required for direct planet imaging.

entry.title: EnSol: an environment-aware graph neural network for molecular solubility prediction

author.name: Thao Nguyen, Saman Shafaei, Zhengyi Zhang, Huimin Zhao, Heng Ji

entry.summary: EnSol is an environment-aware probabilistic graph neural network for molecular solubility that jointly represents solute and solvent graphs and captures continuous temperature effects and experimental uncertainty. It addresses limitations of fixed-solvent, deterministic models relevant to reaction feasibility, formulation, and solvent selection.

entry.title: From Memory to Behavior: A Behavior-Aware Role-Playing Framework for Social Media Influencers

author.name: Ji-Lun Peng, Yi-Zhen Zhang, Chun-Nan Chou, Yun-Nung Chen

entry.summary: Proposes a Situation-Internal state-Behavior persona method that makes LLM role-playing agents reproduce situation-dependent behavioral strategies of real individuals, evaluated on a new social media reply-generation dataset. It also designs an evaluation protocol giving LLM judges reference information about the impersonated person.

entry.title: Balanced Prompt Adaptation against Entropy-Induced Collapse for Test-Time Binary Segmentation

author.name: Zhengshan Wang, Joshua Charles Webster-Ford, Yifei Tian, Xinxin Wang, Long Chen, Weiping Ding

entry.summary: Theoretically characterizes how entropy minimization collapses in imbalanced binary segmentation, where the larger predicted class dominates test-time updates and pulls minority predictions toward itself, and proposes BAPA with class-balanced anchors and prompt adaptation modules. The analysis is grounded in a shared-shift model for test-time adaptation.

entry.title: Neural Cellular Automata Learn General Features in their Hidden Channels

author.name: Etienne Guichard, Stefano Nichele

entry.summary: Studies the internal hidden channels of neural cellular automata, showing they learn general features, and introduces a transfer-learning mechanism that injects a pretrained teacher NCA hidden states into a student to guide early optimization. On few-shot and scale-variant MNIST benchmarks, NCAs outperform comparable recurrent and feed-forward architectures.

entry.title: Toward individual-level calibration in affect recognition with perceptual adjustment queries

author.name: Xuanzhou Chen, Sankaraleengam Alagapan, Ashwin Pananjady

entry.summary: The paper proposes a framework that estimates each participant's Just Noticeable Difference along the facial affect spectrum via lightweight perceptual adjustment queries, then uses these JNDs to construct difficulty-equated tasks in perceptual space. Validated in 2AFC experiments, it corrects the flawed assumption that identical stimuli have equal perceptual difficulty across participants. This improves individual-level calibration in affective perception research.

entry.title: FairLMs: A Turnkey Library for Fairness in Language Models

author.name: Jiale Zhang, Michael Larionov, Zichong Wang, Zhipeng Yin, Wenbin Zhang

entry.summary: FairLMs is a Python library that unifies bias measurement, mitigation, and evaluation for language models behind a single declarative interface. It offers 33 fairness metrics, 14 mitigation components, and 14 dataset diagnostics, with adapters for major Transformer architectures. Standardizing these tools could make fairness research on LLMs more reproducible and comparable.

entry.title: Probabilistic Forecasting of Business Process Executions with Neural Temporal Point Processes

author.name: Jiaxin Yuan, Daniela Grigori, Han van der Aa

entry.summary: The paper casts business process prediction as generative sequence modeling with marked temporal point processes, producing full predictive distributions over next activities and event times rather than single point estimates. It handles non-Markovian, non-simple event data common in real logs, where events share timestamps. Calibrated uncertainty makes forecasts actionable for operators of service systems.

entry.title: Riemannian Neural Hamiltonian Flows: Geodesic Symplectic Transport and Interpretability

author.name: Vincent Souveton

entry.summary: The paper extends Hamiltonian normalizing flows from Euclidean space to Riemannian manifolds, combining fixed kinetic energy, a learned scalar potential, and an explicit geodesic leapfrog integrator. It also develops an interpretability story: every normalizable potential defines an implicit profile whose induced dynamics can be read off, with a matched potential specialization. This is a mathematically grounded contribution to invertible generative modeling.

entry.title: Beyond Kinematics: Benchmarking Simulation Fidelity for Muscle-Driven Imitation Learning

author.name: Ayah G. Ahmad, Claire E. Borden, Maegan Tucker

entry.summary: This paper systematically compares two motion-imitation reinforcement learning pipelines, SCONE/HyFyDy with physiologically detailed musculotendon modeling and MuJoCo/MyoSim prioritizing efficiency. It evaluates whether pipelines that reproduce human kinematics also capture underlying neuromuscular behavior, a question critical for assistive-device design where muscle activation and metabolic cost matter.

entry.title: Beyond WER: Entity and Disfluency Recall in Accented Conversational ASR

author.name: Fiza Husain, Ankit Pandey, Yash Singh

entry.summary: The paper presents a three-stage pipeline for accented conversational ASR (India, Indonesia, Latin America) combining curated entity-rich training data, regional LoRA adapters on Qwen2.5-Omni-3B producing verbatim and corrected transcripts, and an LLM-validated error taxonomy. It lifts entity recall from roughly 53-55% to 80-85% and filler recall from under 5% to 76-86% at 6-10% WER.

entry.title: From Trainability Diagnostics to Optimization Claims: Boundaries and Controls in Variational Quantum Optimization

author.name: Pilsung Kang

entry.summary: Investigates the gap between barren-plateau trainability diagnostics and actual optimization success in variational quantum algorithms, introducing step-level diagnostics and an exact bridge between signed termwise gradient organization, directional activity, and first-order descent. It shows that at fixed state and update norm the raw gradient maximizes first-order descent, bounding what trainability diagnostics can claim about optimization.

entry.title: Sparse Identification for Automatic Large-Scale Screening: A Constraint-Aware Framework with Ultra Fast Decoding Algorithm

author.name: Jianing Li, Li Chai, Yingcheng Lai

entry.summary: Proposes Logic Screening (LoSc), an ultra-fast, theoretically grounded framework for large-scale pandemic group testing that handles hard constraints from sample usage limits and dilution effects, where prior methods suffered from high complexity, low accuracy, or absent theoretical analysis. It uses a novel decoding approach for sparse identification of infected individuals under limited testing capacity.

entry.title: Improving the Predictive Performance of Bootstrap Aggregating by Dirichlet Resampling

author.name: Quoc Viet Le, Joonha Park

entry.summary: The authors revisit Breiman's principle that decorrelating trees without weakening them improves random forests, introducing two resampling variants based on Dirichlet distributions: Dirichlet-Multinomial Bagging and Dirichlet-Weighted Random Forest, both controlled by a concentration parameter. They provide a theoretical criterion for when the variants behave like standard random forests and demonstrate consistent improvements on public classification benchmarks at negligible runtime cost.

entry.title: SAGE: Schema-Guided LLMs for Grant Review

author.name: Erik Varapaev, Andrei Chetvergov, Stepan Ukolov, Timofei Sivoraksha, Alexander Evseev, Sergey Bolovtsov

entry.summary: SAGE translates grant rubrics into structured aspect-based checks linked to evidence from application packages, evaluated on 35 nonprofit grant applications. Post-factum comparison with 105 original competition reviews showed fair agreement (kappa = 0.29), while an assisted re-review round reached kappa = 0.58 and beat a one-prompt-per-criterion baseline.

entry.title: Reading Anxiety or Reading the Label? Comparing Fine-Tuned and Frontier Models for Anxiety Detection on Social Media

author.name: Cris Huynh, Arlene Pham

entry.summary: The paper compares six conditions spanning frontier commercial models, fine-tuned smaller models, and conventional classifiers for anxiety detection on a held-out Reddit set, and identifies a serious evaluation confound: 69.3% of anxiety-labelled posts contain the word anxiety or a variant, roughly twice the rate of comparable conditions, so keyword matching can inflate scores. The authors re-evaluate all systems under controls for this confound.

entry.title: Scaling Forced Alignment to End-User Devices

author.name: Lawry Sorenson, Michael Crandall, Eric K. Ringger, Stephen D. Richardson

entry.summary: The paper proposes two optimizations to Viterbi-based forced alignment: applying the Hirschberg algorithm for in-place linear-memory alignment, and modeling speech-text alignment as a constrained random walk enabling confidence-based pruning that tolerates transcription errors. The Hirschberg optimization cuts memory from 140 GB to 5 MB for three-hour inputs with identical alignments in one-third the time.

entry.title: Not All Irregularity Is Equal: Causally Isolating a Rare Failure Mode in Japanese Morphological Inflection

author.name: Wen Zhang

entry.summary: Using an orthography-aware diagnosis of Japanese past-tense verb inflection with two character-level Transformers across five seeds, the paper shows that systems above 97% aggregate accuracy still fail systematically on one rare irregular subtype (verbs with /e/-final stems requiring gemination), which makes up under 1% of data. The work isolates this failure mode causally rather than just observing aggregate error.

entry.title: Beyond Atomic Tokens: Factorizing Syllables for Language Model Pretraining

author.name: Nghia Hieu Nguyen, Thai Bao Huynh, Binh-An Dinh-Le, Phu Gia Hoang, Dat Tien Nguyen, Kiet Van Nguyen, Ngan Luu-Thuy Nguyen

entry.summary: Proposes a Phonemic Tokenizer for Vietnamese and Chinese that converts each syllable into IPA and splits it into onset, rime, and tone components, which jointly occupy one contextual position. The deterministic, corpus-free design shares representations across phonologically related syllables and avoids large learned vocabularies, with character-level fallback for unsupported units.

entry.title: Per-Aetiology Contrastive Severity Embeddings with Phonological Pseudo-Labelling for Multilingual Dysarthric Speech

author.name: Bernard Muller, Antonio Armando Ortiz Barra\~n\'on, LaVonne Roberts

entry.summary: Tests whether pooling heterogeneous dysarthria aetiologies into one severity label space is justified, training matched HuBERT-base contrastive models for cerebral palsy, Parkinson's, and ALS versus a mixed baseline. Using training-free phonological pseudo-labels, per-aetiology models outperform the mixed baseline across all three conditions on leakage-filtered held-out data.

entry.title: Hand-Aware Transition Modeling for Bimanual Procedural Anomaly Detection

author.name: Di Wen, Jimmy Weissert, Luc Maria Scherrer, Cedric Z\"ollner, Kailun Yang, Ruiping Liu, Yufan Chen, Jiale Wei, Junwei Zheng, Kunyu Peng

entry.summary: HACT models per-hand event transitions for anomaly detection in bimanual assembly tasks, using a role-preserving history and a marked temporal point process to assign semantic and temporal surprisal to each transition. It introduces a recovery-aware evaluation protocol reporting false-positive rates at fixed operating points.

entry.title: RobotEQ-Video: A Video-Centric Benchmark for Social Proactive Intelligence with World-State Taxonomy

author.name: Xinyi Che, Zheng Lian, Kuofei Fang, Xuehao Wang, Xinghai Gao, Junqing Wu, Chuyu Wu, Liyi Liu, Yanhan Huang, Keyi Xie, Haomin Ouyang, Jinyang Wu, Fan Zhang, Runhao Zeng, Xun Yang, Bin He

entry.summary: RobotEQ-Video extends Social Proactive Intelligence benchmarking from static images to video, introducing a hierarchical world-state taxonomy to guarantee comprehensive scenario coverage in a video-centric benchmark for socially appropriate proactive assistance in embodied settings. It targets robot judgment of when and whether to intervene.

entry.title: MT-WAM: Reorienting the One-Pass Predictive Representation Toward Action Generation

author.name: Yiguang Yang, Jiankun Peng, Xiaoming Wang, Yiran Zhang, Zhibo Fang

entry.summary: MT-WAM builds on the Fast-WAM video-action co-training idea, adding auxiliary supervision for future 2D point trajectories and visual features on top of a single video diffusion Transformer forward pass for control. A lightweight dual-stream branch with a structured attention mask provides target-specific processing. It reorients predictive representations from future-observation prediction toward what control actually needs.

entry.title: A Confidence-Driven Evolutionary Algorithm for Noisy Optimization with Joint Chance Constraints

author.name: Enrico Halim, Hemant Singh, Tapabrata Ray

entry.summary: CR-EA-C is an evolutionary algorithm for noisy black-box optimization under joint chance constraints, combining analytical feasibility estimation, pairwise statistical ranking for robust comparison, and an infeasibility-driven survival strategy to improve evaluation efficiency. This targets expensive real-world constrained optimization under uncertainty.

entry.title: Dynamic Modeling and LQR Control of a Single Coaxial Drone with 2DOF Thrust Vectoring Mechanism

author.name: Ali Jokar, Amin Talaeizadeh, Aria Alasty

entry.summary: The authors design a coaxial drone with a two-DOF pendulum thrust-vectoring mechanism as a simpler alternative to swashplates for roll and pitch control, developing a full Lagrangian dynamic model including inertial contributions of all components. An LQR controller is derived from the linearized hover dynamics.

entry.title: A Unified Dynamic Force Guidance Framework for Performance-Optimized Kinesthetic Teaching

author.name: Chunxin Li, Jianhua Wu, Zhenhua Xiong, Xiangyang Zhu

entry.summary: The paper presents an online dynamic force guidance method for kinesthetic teaching of collaborative robots that integrates robot performance constraints, quantified via the minimum singular value of the Jacobian, with variable admittance control. The framework guides users during teaching so that frequent product changeovers in industrial settings do not result in degraded robot operational performance.

entry.title: A Novel Path-Tracking Algorithm for Automated Tractor-Trailer Forward and Backward Maneuvers

author.name: Alexandre Lombard, Florent Perronnet, Nicolas Gaud, Abdeljalil Abbas-Turki

entry.summary: The paper introduces a path-tracking algorithm for articulated tractor-trailer vehicles combining a lateral control law at the trailer level with short-horizon predictive adjustment of tractor steering, ensuring stable convergence in both forward and reversing maneuvers. This targets increasingly deployed autonomous tractor-trailers in logistics, agriculture, and industry where reversing control is especially difficult.

entry.title: Understanding Engagement and Intrusiveness in Assistive Human-Robot Interaction Using Individual Traits

author.name: Valerio Bo, Lavinia Hriscu, Alberto Sanfeliu, Ana\'is Garrell

entry.summary: This study argues that perceived robot intrusiveness depends on intervention frequency and individual traits such as personality and demographics, not just proxemics. Thirty-two participants interacted with two assistive robots offering similar support but different intervention strategies during an unfamiliar task. Results show trait-dependent perceptions, suggesting personalized assistive robot behavior is needed.

entry.title: TRACE: Coverage Path Planning for Unknown Environments Using Hierarchical Coverage Tree

author.name: Zongyuan Shen, Haodong Liu, Gao Wang, Shancheng Zhao, Dehua Zhou, Yaming Ou, Zhongqiang Ren, Yikui Zhai, C. L. Philip Chen

entry.summary: TRACE is an online coverage path planning algorithm that maintains a hierarchical coverage tree representing the connectivity of remaining uncovered space as the environment is incrementally revealed. It recursively expands tree nodes to handle fragmentation from newly discovered obstacles and maintains an incremental global tour, refining only affected portions of the plan. This enables real-time coverage of unknown environments.

entry.title: Gripper-Aware Automatic Dense Packing of Irregular Objects

author.name: Tianhao Qin, Connor McCann, Berk Calli, Jing Xiao

entry.summary: This paper presents a closed-loop pipeline for dense packing of irregular objects that integrates perception, gripper-aware placement optimization, and force-guided execution on a real manipulator. The optimizer treats the object and gripper as a single composite body of hierarchical sphere trees and searches over five degrees of freedom, addressing contact drift and post-hoc feasibility checks common in prior packing work. It targets realistic warehouse automation.

entry.title: Duty Factor Predicts Robust Constrained Quadrupedal Locomotion Across Gait Types

author.name: James Zhu, David Ologan, George Ortiz, Thomas Chun Fai Lee, Selvin Garcia Gonzalez, Ardalan Tajbakhsh, Pinhas Ben-Tzvi, Aaron M. Johnson

entry.summary: This work investigates which gait parameters predict robust quadrupedal locomotion under disturbances and constrained terrain, showing across three control approaches that duty factor is a stronger predictor of local error convergence than nominal gait type. The analysis spans whole-body trajectory optimization with LQR feedback and learned policies. This reframes how gait robustness should be characterized for legged robots.

entry.title: Did Someone Check if Rogue Agents are Interested in Self-Improvement?

author.name: Ephraiem Sarabamoun

entry.summary: The author reviews OpenAI and METR disclosures about the HuggingFace rogue-agent incident and observes that neither report appears to have checked whether the misbehaving agents ever verbalized or discussed self-improvement in their chains of thought. It notes METR's twelve classifier sweeps did not evidently target this question, and flags it as a consequential gap if unchecked.

entry.title: What Should We Ask Next? Retrieval-Aware Question Learning under Partial Evidence

author.name: Lyucheng Qian, John Yuehan Zhang, Pingyu Wang

entry.summary: Frames interactive retrieval under partial evidence as sequential information acquisition and introduces RAVEL, an online RL framework for interactive person re-identification that learns which question yields the most useful evidence, initialized from supervised question generation and observing current Top-4 candidates directly.

entry.title: GraphSkillEvo: Evolutionary Optimization of Graph-Structured Agent Skills

author.name: Rui Sun, Zhi Zheng, Zhenkun Wang, Zhichao Lu

entry.summary: The paper proposes representing LLM agent skills as graph-structured natural-language artifacts rather than unstructured instructions, with each node capturing workflow-level steps. This reduces redundancy and constrains the search space, enabling evolutionary optimization of skills. It addresses real limitations of free-form skill libraries for agentic systems.

entry.title: Brownian Heads for Deep ReLU Representations: Activation Mass and the Cost of Same-Sample Selection

author.name: Mahdi Mohammadigohari, Nicole M\"ucke

entry.summary: Studies the conditional empirical Rademacher complexity of deep ReLU representations followed by bounded-norm predictors in Brownian RKHS heads, deriving exact dual identities and sharp bounds in terms of activation mass, the average norm of hidden vectors. It explicitly accounts for the cost of selecting hidden features and fitting the predictor on the same sample, inducing a quadratic Rademacher process analyzed via layer-cake and Gaussian-projection identities.

entry.title: Purification and Regulation: Comorbidity-Aware Multi-Label Few-Shot Learning for Medical Image Classification

author.name: Ying-Chih Lin, Po-Chih Kuo, Yong-Sheng Chen

entry.summary: The authors propose PPR, a few-shot multi-label framework for medical image analysis that purifies class prototypes using sample-level comorbidity scores and regulates inter-class separation to respect real disease correlations rather than enforcing full separability. This addresses prototype contamination and ignores-correlations limitations of metric-based meta-learning, with evaluation on medical imaging benchmarks.

entry.title: SIRA: Reasoning-Aware Surgical Instrument Segmentation via Query-Anchored Alignment

author.name: Zhibo Zhang, Qijie Wang, Zengqiang Yan

entry.summary: SIRA reformulates surgical instrument segmentation as query-conditioned inference under procedural context, and introduces SurgRS, a 41,000-pair surgical reasoning segmentation dataset aligning instance masks with structured query-answer supervision for pixel-level semantic grounding. The approach captures task-dependent semantics beyond category-driven localization.

entry.title: GestureFAR: Streaming Co-Speech Gesture Generation with Flow Autoregression

author.name: Pinxin Liu, Haiyang Liu, Jiahao Luo, Junhua Huang, Chunhao Zou, Luchuan Song

entry.summary: GestureFAR generates co-speech gestures in a streaming setting by autoregressing over causal continuous motion latents with a per-token flow-matching head, avoiding the realism/diversity loss caused by discrete motion token codebooks. It preserves causality while keeping continuous expressiveness for embodied conversational agents. Relevant to real-time avatars and human-agent interaction.

entry.title: Uncertainty-driven training for three-dimensional calibrated lung nodule classification

author.name: Giuseppe Tripodi, Alessandro De Rosis, Saleh Rezaeiravesh

entry.summary: This work uses per-class uncertainty estimates from Monte Carlo Dropout and Evidential Deep Learning to reweight training loss for 3D CT lung nodule classification, improving both performance and probability calibration across ResNet, DenseNet, EfficientNet, ViT, and Swin backbones on LIDC-IDRI and NoduleMNIST3D. Calibration matters clinically for triage decisions.

entry.title: A High-Payload Wall-Climbing Robot Using Passive Bistable Suction Cups

author.name: Andrew Nguyen, Mingyuan Li, Daniel Bruder

entry.summary: The paper presents a wall-climbing robot using passive bistable suction cups that generate adhesion without power or being pushed into the wall, addressing the payload limitations of passive adhesion. A track-based system automatically engages and disengages the cups, enabling high-payload climbing for hazardous or labor-intensive tasks like window washing, inspection, and construction.

entry.title: Bayesian classification of astronomical spectra with class uncertainties

author.name: Simon Barton, Martin Sahl\'en, Andreas Korn, Christian Glaser

entry.summary: For the upcoming 4MOST survey, the authors compare four probabilistic classification methods (CNNs, Dirichlet-based, MC dropout, and Bayesian neural networks with variational inference) for classifying stellar and extragalactic spectra with both input-data and predictive uncertainty. Training uses SDSS labels and a custom 4MOST mock dataset, with the methods compared across uncertainty calibration criteria.

entry.title: SFVO: Decoupled Confidence-Guided Stereo-Flow Visual Odometry with Bidirectional PnP

author.name: Kai Zhang, Guoyang Zhao, Jun Ma

entry.summary: SFVO is a correspondence-driven stereo visual odometry framework built directly on pretrained stereo matching and optical flow models, exploiting their complementary geometric information to obtain metric scale while avoiding the cost of traditional stereo VO. It uses decoupled confidence guidance and bidirectional PnP for robustness. Leverages the trend of reusing large pretrained correspondence models for downstream geometric tasks.

entry.title: Offline Multimodal Large Language Models for Decision Support in Air Operations

author.name: Joao P. A. Dantas, Jelton A. Cunha, Gabriel Dietzsch

entry.summary: The paper presents a modular retrieval-augmented architecture for offline multimodal LLM decision support in air operations, operating without Internet connectivity under strict security constraints and tracing doctrinal knowledge to original sources. It supports text and image input from technical manuals. It is an early-stage applied study of LLMs in constrained defense environments.

entry.title: Reducing Barriers to Academic Support: Evaluating a Course-Specific RAG System for Addressing Help-Seeking Disparities in Higher Education

author.name: Andy Gray, Jake Hobbs

entry.summary: Presents Beacon, a course-specific RAG system offering private, module-aligned academic help to students who avoid seeking support due to anxiety or low confidence, especially in computing education. The study evaluates whether such targeted RAG reduces help-seeking disparities compared to general-purpose generative AI tools.

entry.title: Trustworthy FinAInce: Unpacking How AI-Mediated Financial Advice is Judged

author.name: Aryan Ramchandra Kapadia, Eshwar Chandrasekharan, Koustuv Saha

entry.summary: This human-subjects study ran a randomized vignette experiment with 285 US adults across eight financial decisions, varying advice source labels (AI, expert, online community) while holding recommendations constant. It finds advice style and decision context shape perceived quality, safety, and risk appraisals, with models explaining a large share of downstream judgments.

entry.title: Do Personality-Tuned LLMs Make Better Social Agents?

author.name: Tim Krabbe, Xiaodan Shi

entry.summary: Investigates whether personality-aware fine-tuning of small open-weight models (Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Ministral-8B-Instruct) on personality-labelled dialogues improves consistency and controllability of personality-conditioned dialogue compared to instruction prompting, for use in social simulation. The resulting models are evaluated across multiple dialogue settings.

entry.title: From Stress to Affect: Multimodal Deep Learning for Physiological Emotion Recognition Across Wearable Sensor Modalities

author.name: Desta Haileselassie Hagos, Saurav Keshari Aryal, Legand L. Burge

entry.summary: This comparative study evaluates BiLSTM, TCN, and Transformer architectures for physiological emotion recognition on two wearable datasets (WESAD and EmoWear) across wrist-only, chest-only, and multimodal configurations using participant-independent evaluation. It maps how sensing configuration and architecture jointly affect recognition performance, informing mental-health monitoring and affective computing applications. The systematic design addresses a common gap of single-model, single-dataset studies.

entry.title: What Must Survive? Exact Task-Information--State Frontiers for Resource-Sufficient Learning

author.name: Ronald Katende

entry.summary: This theory paper asks how much state must be retained when a system is compressed before its downstream task is known, deriving exact frontiers for finite families of linear tasks when partial task information is revealed in advance. It gives exact, approximate, and direct-sum results showing advance task information reduces required state through low-rank task partitions. The results connect to information-theoretic questions in learned compression and task-conditioned representations.

entry.title: RegKT: Interpretable and Robust Deep Knowledge Tracing With IRT-Regularizer

author.name: Samuel Girard, Juan D. Pinto, Jill-J\^enn Vie, Amel Bouzeghoub

entry.summary: This paper proposes RegKT, a regularization technique for deep-learning-based knowledge tracing models in education that draws on Item Response Theory. The method aims to simultaneously improve model interpretability and robustness against overfitting, addressing two key barriers to adoption in real-world educational settings where datasets are typically small.

entry.title: Fragment-Aware Vision Transformers for Fresco-Fragment Style Classification

author.name: Sara Miketek, Biagio Barchielli, Nadeem Iqbal Kajla, Sinem Aslan

entry.summary: Studies artistic style classification for archaeological fresco fragments, where only incomplete, irregular visual evidence survives. Building on ViT-B/16, the framework adds foreground-guided masking, inpainting-based geometric regularization to align irregular supports with the patch grid, and a supervised contrastive objective on predictive distributions.

entry.title: Single-Loop Stochastic Projected Damped Extragradient Methods for Stochastic Nonconvex--(Strongly) Concave Minimax Optimization

author.name: Huiling Zhang, Minhao Zhang, Zi Xu

entry.summary: The paper develops single-loop stochastic projected damped extragradient methods (SPDE and a variance-reduced VR-SPDE variant) for nonconvex-(strongly) concave minimax optimization, with oracle-complexity guarantees for both game stationarity and optimization stationarity. It establishes rates such as O(kappa*eps^-4) and O(eps^-5) under bounded-variance stochastic gradients.

entry.title: From Generation to Detection: Exploration of Discourse Driven Scenario based LLM Generated Fake News

author.name: Zeynep \"Ozdemir, Murat Osmano\u{g}lu, Sevgi Yi\u{g}it-Sert, \"Omer \"Ozg\"ur Tanr{\i}\"over, Y{\i}lmaz Ar

entry.summary: The study generates a 14,000-article synthetic fake news corpus using seven LLMs across four manipulation scenarios grounded in journalistic discourse, then analyzes linguistic properties and detection performance. Each model also judged the generated fake news, with detection prompts iteratively improved across experiments.

entry.title: Benchmarking Gender Bias in Machine Translation Evaluation Metrics across Occupations

author.name: Orfeas Menis Mastromichalakis, Giorgos Filandrianos, Wafaa Mohammed, Giuseppe Attanasio, Chrysoula Zerva

entry.summary: Studies gender bias in machine translation evaluation metrics using an occupation-balanced subset of GAMBIT+ across seven English-source language pairs in the WMT 2026 shared task setting. When gender is unspecified in the source, the work measures whether MT systems and metrics systematically prefer masculine or feminine realizations despite no basis in the source text.

entry.title: Cross-Lingual Parkinson's Disease Severity Assessment Using Pre-trained Speech Embeddings: A Multi-Class Evaluation

author.name: Simon Pals, Cristian Tejedor-Garcia

entry.summary: The paper evaluates embeddings from four open-source speech foundation models for multi-class Parkinson's disease severity assessment in zero-shot and k-shot cross-lingual settings across three datasets. Results show pre-trained speech embeddings transfer meaningfully across languages for PD severity classification. This supports non-invasive, speech-based diagnosis tools that work beyond the training language.

entry.title: S3VD: Semantic-Guidance Spatio-Temporal Scanning for Video Deraining

author.name: Kui Jiang, Yiang Chen, Yan Luo, Zhaocheng Yu, Junjun Jiang, Xianming Liu

entry.summary: S3VD applies state space models (Mamba) to video deraining with two innovations: multi-scale semantic fusion to preserve 2D spatial semantics and a spatio-temporal scanning scheme for 3D correlation modeling. It targets heavy rainfall artifacts that corrupt high-frequency details and introduce motion blur in outdoor videos.

entry.title: 2D GauSS-MI: Efficient Active Scene Reconstruction with Balanced Visual and Geometric Quality

author.name: Yuhan Xie, Jia Pan

entry.summary: An active reconstruction framework based on 2D Gaussian Splatting that performs online mapping from incremental RGB-D observations and selects next-best views in real time. It introduces a probabilistic reliability model for view-dependent splat quality and a 2D GauSS-MI mutual-information objective balancing visual and geometric quality under limited onboard compute. Targets robot active vision scenarios.

entry.title: MultiHU-TD: Multifeature Hyperspectral Unmixing Based on Tensor Decomposition

author.name: Mohamad Jouni, Mauro Dalla Mura, Lucas Drumetz, Pierre Comon

entry.summary: MultiHU-TD proposes an interpretable low-rank tensor-decomposition framework for hyperspectral unmixing that jointly uses spectral and additional scene features while enforcing abundance sum-to-one constraints. It targets the inadequacy of matrix models when hyperspectral images are represented as high-order multimodal tensors.

entry.title: Labs could soon start automated research into architectures driven by no-CoT perfomance

author.name: nanowell

entry.summary: This LessWrong post argues that AI labs may soon use automated research (AI research interns) to explore architectural modifications, optimizing against no-chain-of-thought performance such as latent multi-hop reasoning across filler tokens. The author, citing work by Greenblatt, Pfau, and Goyal, claims improved latent reasoning would boost token efficiency and long-horizon RL-based reasoning, but warns this trajectory reduces CoT monitorability and creates AI safety risks.

entry.title: We've saved the world before: what the ozone hole teaches us about AI

author.name: leogao

entry.summary: A historical essay by leogao arguing the Montreal Protocol's near-universal ratification and successful elimination of CFCs demonstrates that global coordination against an invisible, test-passing catastrophic risk is possible. It extracts lessons from the ozone regime for AI governance while acknowledging AI coordination is far harder.

entry.title: 2nd Place Solution to the HANDS 2026 Workshop Challenge-Dexterous Grasp Motion Track: Single-Shot Trajectory Warping for Grasp Motion Generation

author.name: Muneeb A. Khan, Woojin Kim, Shinwoo Kim, Muhammad Munsif, Binod Bhattarai, Seungryul Baek

entry.summary: Describes a second-place solution to the ECCV 2026 HANDS workshop dexterous grasping challenge, generating physically plausible reach-and-lift trajectories for a 12-DoF hand by warping a single successful demonstration rather than generating trajectories from scratch. The approach handles randomized initial poses and sim-to-real variation.

entry.title: From Code Archival to Knowledge Graph: Bridging Software Heritage, COAR Notify and Wikidata

author.name: Camillo Carlo Pellizzari di San Girolamo, Francesco Tosoni

entry.summary: Presents an end-to-end reconciliation pipeline that harvests and validates explicit paper-to-code links from software-centric journals (JOSS, SoftwareX, IPOL) and SIGMOD reproducibility reports, producing a curated corpus of 4,397 verified DOI-repository pairs. The work connects software heritage archives into the Linked Open Data cloud to enable semantic discovery of research code.

entry.title: Reliability-Centered Evaluation of Sparse Longitudinal CT Lesion-Size Forecasting with Conformal Interval Calibration and Gompertz-Inspired Regularization

author.name: Lingfei Kong

entry.summary: This paper builds a five-visit lesion-trajectory benchmark from DeepLesion and DLT (205 trajectories from 129 patients) and evaluates sparse longitudinal forecasting of CT lesion sizes, comparing designs with conformal interval calibration and Gompertz-inspired trajectory regularization. The evaluation emphasizes uncertainty reliability and subgroup performance alongside point accuracy. It highlights reliability-centric evaluation for sparse clinical forecasting.

entry.title: Routine Blood Tests Outperform CRP for Distinguishing Bacterial From Viral Infection in Children

author.name: Mihaela Demireva, Zhecho Mitev, Djuna Chinareva-Klimentova, Svetoslav Ivanov, Georgi Nalbantov, Dimitar Mitev

entry.summary: A retrospective study of 906 pediatric patients shows that complete blood count features predict bacterial versus viral infection better than the standard CRP marker. Better discrimination could reduce unnecessary antibiotic prescribing and help combat antimicrobial resistance. The work is clinical ML with direct healthcare relevance.

entry.title: Bilevel Optimization of Topology and Hyperparameters (BOTH)

author.name: Suryanarayanan Manoj Sanu, Miguel Anibal Bessa, Alejandro Marcos Arag\'on

entry.summary: BOTH differentiates topology optimization itself to co-optimize design topology and its many sensitive hyperparameters, replacing error-prone manual tuning or restrictive surrogate-assisted formulations. By treating hyperparameter selection as part of the differentiable design loop, it reduces the domain expertise and trial-and-error burden in simulation-driven engineering design. An applied computational engineering contribution with ML components.

entry.title: TALON: A Temporally Aware Longitudinal Framework for Radiology Report Generation

author.name: Nien-Tsyr Sun, Min-Chen Chen, Hui Nien Hung, Vincent S. Tseng

entry.summary: TALON is a framework for radiology report generation that adaptively integrates variable-length patient histories using a Dual-Channel Temporal Fusion Module, comparing the current examination against each prior with role-dependent relevance modeling. It addresses the limitation of prior work that uses only one or a fixed-length window of prior exams.

entry.title: Adaptive Uncertainty-Aware Modeling and Stochastic Radial Basis Function Predictive Control for Personalized Fluid Resuscitation

author.name: Elham Estiri, Hossein Mirinejad

entry.summary: This paper integrates Bayesian physiological modeling with optimal control for personalized hemodynamic regulation during fluid resuscitation. It develops an uncertainty-aware variational autoencoder state-space model capturing aleatoric uncertainty and a Bayesian nonlinear state-space model capturing epistemic uncertainty, combined with stochastic radial basis function predictive control, validated in a clinical decision-support context.

entry.title: Curriculum-Based Noise Adaptation for Phoneme-to-Text Reconstruction in Visual Speech Recognition

author.name: Matthew Kit Khinn Teng, Haibo Zhang, Takeshi Saitoh

entry.summary: The paper proposes progressive error curriculum training (PECT), which progressively adapts an NLLB-based phoneme-to-text reconstruction model using synthetic phoneme perturbations and multi-domain pseudo-labeled data to match realistic inference-time phoneme prediction errors. It targets phoneme-centric visual speech recognition, where overall performance hinges on reconstruction robustness.

entry.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence Chatbots for Motivational Interviewing: A Scoping Review From System Design to Intervention Outcomes

author.name: Runze Hu, Jingqi Kong, Yang Yang, Yihang Yang, Jingyao Liu, Haizhou Tang, Shanghang Zhang, Zheng Liu

entry.summary: This PRISMA-ScR scoping review synthesizes evidence on GenAI motivational-interviewing chatbots across system design, safety, MI quality, user perceptions, and intervention outcomes, searching nine datasets for work from 2015 to June 2026. It maps the fragmented landscape of GenAI-MI systems and their translation into interventions.

entry.title: PRISM-BN: A Controlled Corpus and Benchmark for Text-to-Parameterized Bayesian Network Extraction

author.name: Amartya Bhattacharya, Nikhil Singh, Neeti Pokhriyal, Soroush Vosoughi

entry.summary: Provides a controlled corpus of 5054 text descriptions paired with fully specified Bayesian networks (variables, states, edges, priors, multi-parent CPDs) across five domains to enable training text-to-parameterized-BN systems. Instances derive from 50 Wikipedia-seeded backbones, with probabilities serving as internal benchmark targets rather than validated causal estimates.

entry.title: Moral Entropy: Auditing Bias and Uncertainty in Moral Judgment

author.name: Maciej Skorski

entry.summary: Proposes Moral Entropy, a Bayesian framework that models annotator disagreement in moral judgments as a full posterior over the true label, decomposing uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components. It enables auditing any consensus heuristic against calibrated ground truth via entropy-based measures like cross-entropy, Brier score, and expected calibration error.

entry.title: The Spoken Wikipedia Presentation Corpus

author.name: Thomas Ranzenberger, Steffen Freisinger, Tobias Bocklet, Korbinian Riedhammer

entry.summary: The authors present a corpus extension of Spoken Wikipedia featuring LLM-generated slide decks aligned with audio for multimodal ASR research. Slides are produced via a hybrid pipeline combining LLM content planning with rule-based design, and slide text is extracted by a vision LLM as Markdown. Evaluations of multiple ASR and spoken language models show a best micro-WER of 10.23% and micro-CER of 6.48% in audio-only settings.

entry.title: SafeStyle: Calibrated Style Residual Injection for Controllable Style-Leakage Trade-off in Diffusion Stylization

author.name: Zhangping Yang, Min Li, Song Yan, Rong Gao, Xinliang Bi, Guanye Xiong, Yujie He

entry.summary: SafeStyle is a training-free framework for reference-guided diffusion stylization that disentangles transferable style cues from reference-specific content, offering a calibrated control knob over the style-fidelity versus content-leakage trade-off. It handles texture-dominant and geometry-dominant styles differently and works on frozen diffusion models.

entry.title: A benchmark dataset and baseline methods for four-dimensional STEM diffraction patterns

author.name: Yuyan Guan, Haoran Zhang, Zian Mao, Antong Yang, Caifei Li, Jialong Wang, Chuying Ouyang, Hong Wang, Xiaoqin Zeng, Yujun Xie

entry.summary: 4D-ImageNet provides 174,000 four-dimensional STEM diffraction patterns (145,000 experimental from 29 acquisitions plus 29,000 multislice simulations) covering specimens such as Ag, Au, CoO, Pd, and ZnO with quality rankings and metadata. It includes baseline methods with a set-prediction detector for analysis tasks. A scientific-imaging dataset contribution enabling ML for electron microscopy.

entry.title: OpenRoIS: A Community-Driven Open-Source Middleware Implementing the Robotic Interaction Service (RoIS) Framework for Physical Robots and Virtual Agents

author.name: Sebastian Carrera Villalobos, Christopher Nolan Arellano, Arne Hitzmann, Edilson Morais Brito, Akira Utsumi, Yukiko Horikawa, Takahiro Miyashita, Lotfi El Hafi

entry.summary: OpenRoIS is a community-driven open-source middleware implementing the OMG-standardized RoIS 2.0 Framework, providing SDKs and adapters so HRI service applications interact with robot platforms through hardware-independent symbolic interfaces. It decouples HRI applications from platform-specific hardware interfaces, spanning physical robots and virtual agents.

entry.title: LunaDrive: A Delay-Compensated High-Voltage GaN FET-Based Motor Driver for Dynamic Robots with Flat BLDC Motors

author.name: Sota Yuzaki, Temma Suzuki, Hiromi Tada, Masanori Konishi, Kento Kawaharazuka, Kei Okada

entry.summary: LunaDrive is a compact motor driver using GaN FETs to drive flat BLDC motors beyond their rated voltage, overcoming the voltage-current trade-off of conventional Si MOSFET drivers to increase instantaneous maximum speed for dynamic robots. It incorporates delay compensation for high-voltage operation. This is a hardware contribution enabling more dynamic legged and agile robot platforms.

entry.title: Reflections on unlearning and inoculation

author.name: Xenomirant

entry.summary: A conceptual post analyzing inoculation prompting and inoculation adapters as promising midtraining interventions for reducing reward hacking and misalignment. It connects inoculation to unlearning, sparse learning theory, and functional sparse decompositions, framing LLM learning as explicit parametric learning versus in-context learning, and sketches open questions and extensions.

entry.title: Learning-to-Optimize as the Missing Architectural Layer of AI-Native Networks

author.name: Giambattista Amati, Federica Mangiatordi, Pierpaolo Salvo, Emiliano Pallotti, Simone Angelini

entry.summary: A position-style paper arguing that Learning-to-Optimize (L2O) should serve as an architectural layer in AI-native communication networks, reframing optimization algorithms as offline knowledge generators rather than purely online decision engines. It proposes how optimization knowledge can be systematically generated, transferred, and exploited by network AI models.

entry.title: Learning Cardiac Features: ECG Biometrics Across Time and~Exercise

author.name: Luca Thiebaud (AMU, AMU SCI, DIAPRO, LIS), Paul Chauchat (AMU SCI, AMU, LIS, DIAPRO), Mustapha Ouladsine (AMU SCI, AMU, LIS, DIAPRO), St\'ephane Delliaux (AMU, APHM, C2VN)

entry.summary: Evaluates ECG biometrics — person identification from cardiac signals — under realistic conditions of exercise-induced stress and cross-session variability, using a Siamese ResNet with late multi-lead fusion trained on cardiopulmonary exercise test data. The work also positions ECG biometrics as security for sensitive cardiac data and as a self-supervised pretext task.

entry.title: Bio-MF: Low-Latency and High-Fidelity EEG-to-fNIRS Cross-Modal Generation for Hybrid Motor-Imagery Brain--Computer Interfaces

author.name: Boyuan Zhao, Sifan Zhang, Luping Chen

entry.summary: Bio-MF addresses slow, pretraining-dependent EEG-to-fNIRS cross-modal generation for hybrid brain-computer interfaces by using a one-step generative model that preserves physiological fidelity. It targets real-time hybrid motor-imagery BCI scenarios where paired EEG-fNIRS acquisition is unavailable.

entry.title: Interference-Driven Clustered Optimisation for FM Spectrum Coordination

author.name: Federica Mangiatordi, Emiliano Pallotti

entry.summary: Develops a clustered optimization framework for large-scale cross-border FM spectrum coordination that identifies the dominant subset of transmitters causing foreign-service protection violations before solving the power-control problem. This reduces dimensionality from millions of transmitter-pixel relationships to tractable subproblems.

entry.title: A Lightweight Plug-in Gate for Transformer-Based Time-Series Forecasters

author.name: Hongkai Zhuang, Tao Huang, Chen Hou

entry.summary: The paper proposes a lightweight pre-encoder gate that assigns sigmoid admission scores to covariate representations before they enter Transformer-based forecasters, plus a usage-regularized variant penalizing average admission. It evaluates the plug-in module on TimeXer, iTransformer, and PatchTST-style models for covariate-rich forecasting. The work frames covariate admission as an explicit input-side interface.

entry.title: Efficient Architecture Search under Leave-One-Subject-Out Evaluation

author.name: Heinke Hihn, Friedhelm Schwenker

entry.summary: PainNAS embeds neural architecture search within leave-one-subject-out evaluation for automated pain assessment, using a block-based leakage-controlled scheme that shares searches across subjects and reduces N searches to B blocks. On the BioVid Heat Pain dataset it achieves comparable subject-level accuracy at much lower compute. It addresses a real statistical rigor versus cost tension in subject-dependent evaluation.

entry.title: Optimization Geometry of Equivalent Brownian RKHS Representations

author.name: Mahdi Mohammadigohari, Gustau Camps-Valls

entry.summary: This paper studies how equivalent finite parameterizations of the same Brownian RKHS model (nodal, increment, spectral coordinates) yield different optimization dynamics despite representing identical functions and norms. It proves exact trajectory equivalences for GD/SGD under mapped initialization and characterizes increment GD as an explicit Euler step under the Brownian/Sobolev metric. A careful, controlled analysis of how parameterization shapes optimization.

entry.title: Geometric Mean Pooling for Equal-Weight Multiplicative Coarse-Graining

author.name: Ang-Kun Wu, Fangdi Wen, Jingtao Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces Geometric Mean Pooling (GMP), a signed pooling operator combining feature-sign products with geometric means of magnitudes as an alternative to average and max pooling. Motivated by quantum many-body physics, GMP preserves joint sign information and multiplicative scale without learnable parameters, and is evaluated on synthetic tasks, coarse-graining, image classification, and molecular property regression.

entry.title: Automated Physics-Informed Neural-Networks-Based Calibration of Highly Segmented Silicon Telescopes

author.name: M. Rejmund, A. Lemasson, P. Morfouace, D. Ramos, J. Taieb, J. D. Frankland

entry.summary: Presents a fully automated, physics-informed neural-network calibration framework for highly segmented silicon detector arrays used in nuclear physics experiments. By formulating calibration as a global optimization problem over detector gains and geometrical corrections, it scales beyond inefficient channel-by-channel manual approaches.

entry.title: Towards Secure Cloud-Native Computing: Unveiling Kubernetes Misconfigurations with Large Language Models

author.name: Mostafa Anouar Ghorab, Mohamed Aymen Saied

entry.summary: The paper explores using LLMs to identify Kubernetes misconfigurations, contributing a taxonomy of common misconfiguration types that affect security and performance in cloud-native environments. It provides a structured framework for categorizing these issues as a basis for LLM-based detection.

entry.title: MIRAGE: Multi-Perspective Creative Language Model Reasoning with Reinforcement Learning Guidance

author.name: Arash Lagzian, Srinivas Anumasa, Dianbo Liu

entry.summary: Proposes MIRAGE, an inference-time reasoning framework in which a Selector picks conceptual perspectives (e.g., algebraic, probabilistic) and a Reasoner applies them sequentially or aggregates across perspectives until a confident solution emerges. Evaluated on GSM8K, MATH500, MMLU-Pro, and other benchmarks.

entry.title: TAPe+ML: A Compact Structured Representation for Multi-Task Computer Vision

author.name: Sergey Kurinov (Comexp Research Lab, TAPe + ML Project, Nizhniy Novgorod, Russia), Alexey Upatov (Comexp Research Lab, TAPe + ML Project, Nizhniy Novgorod, Russia)

entry.summary: TAPe+ML v3 is a compact computer vision system built on the Theory of Active Perception, encoding relations among perceptual elements before recognition rather than operating directly on pixel tensors. It combines background and contour processing, local object localization, prototype-based classification, and a coordinator for specialized submodels, using fewer than 100,000 parameters. Reported results include 84.7 mAP50 on COCO detection and 80.7 on instance segmentation.

entry.title: PSEE: Progressive Sensor Event Expansion for Point-Supervised Temporal Action Localization

author.name: Jiaxi Yin, Ge Wang, Han Ding, Fei Wang

entry.summary: PSEE reduces annotation cost for temporal action localization in wearable sensor streams by using only point-level timestamps and class labels, converting them into pseudo segments via semantic activations and transition evidence. It works with standard TAL detectors without modifying inference. Useful for scalable activity understanding from wearables.

entry.title: XCalib Depth-Guided Geometric Optimization for Dense Thermal-Visible Video Registration

author.name: Aurelien Godet, Gabriel Jobert, Mauro Dalla Mura

entry.summary: XCalib is an unsupervised dense registration framework aligning thermal (IR) and visible cameras for ADAS, addressing non-uniform parallax from non-coincident optical axes that defeats global homography methods. It adds depth-guided geometric optimization and structural regularization to avoid the temporal instability of unconstrained dense flow. Targets preprocessing for multimodal fusion, detection, and segmentation in driver assistance.

entry.title: MarineCraft: Enabling Rapid Prototyping of Underwater Robots via Modular Construction

author.name: Yuta Sugiura

entry.summary: MarineCraft is a modular toolkit for underwater robot prototyping that uses self-contained waterproof propulsion modules integrating power, wireless communication, and actuation, removing centralized wiring and repeated sealing. The authors demonstrate that diverse robot geometries can be assembled and tested in minutes instead of days while maintaining reliable, leak-free operation.

entry.title: Robust Dual-Regularized Variable Selection under Outlier Contamination

author.name: Abdul-Nasah Soale, Adewale F. Lukman, Essoham Ali

entry.summary: Proposes a two-stage sparse median outer product of gradients (smOPG) method for variable selection in single-index models under outlier contamination. It combines l1-penalized local median regression with a rank-one sparse approximation via regularized SVD, providing robustness to both response outliers and leverage points, validated through extensive simulations.

entry.title: Learning to Move Cities: Deep Meta-Models and Reinforcement Policies for Calibration and Control in Urban Networks

author.name: Adewumi Augustine Adepitan, Christopher J. Haruna, Oluwasegun Adegoke, Ayooluwatomiwa Ajiboye, Oluwatobi Oluwasakin

entry.summary: This work proposes a shared latent-space framework unifying urban traffic simulator calibration and reinforcement learning control. A combinatorial MLP-autoencoder learns low-dimensional manifolds from simulator inputs to outputs for Bayesian optimization calibration, while RL policies operate on the same representation for real-time control, showing better sample efficiency than traditional dimension reduction.

entry.title: Reusing Latent Speech Representations for Query-Conditioned Topic Localization in Transcripts

author.name: Steffen Freisinger, Philipp Seeberger, Thomas Ranzenberger, Tobias Bocklet, Korbinian Riedhammer

entry.summary: Studies query-conditioned topic localization in long transcripts, predicting the sentence span best answering a topic-title query. By fusing reused ASR encoder states with textual embeddings, lightweight span locators exploit speech information without a separate audio encoder, yielding gains over text-only baselines, especially on structured speech.

entry.title: HAT: Hypothesis-Anchored Tracking for Video Monocular Spacecraft Pose Estimation

author.name: Andr\'e Lopo, Atabak Dehban, Rodrigo Ventura

entry.summary: HAT is a causal tracking framework for monocular 6-DoF pose estimation of non-cooperative spacecraft, using inter-frame motion to select among competing CAD-based pose hypotheses before alignment and fusion with monocular SLAM. It avoids committing to the highest-scoring single-frame hypothesis, which can preserve incorrect near-symmetric orientations. Targets on-orbit servicing and debris removal applications.

entry.title: Talk to Me, Jarvis: An Open-Source Edge-Deployable Voice Assistant Framework for Autonomous Racecars

author.name: Daniel Henel, Frederik Werner, Alexander Langmann, Johannes Betz

entry.summary: Jarvis is an open-source, offline voice assistant for autonomous vehicles that integrates speech recognition, synthesis, and a domain-specific fine-tuned text-to-command classifier into a lightweight local framework, avoiding network latency of hosted LLM backends. It targets time-critical behavioral command understanding for autonomous racecars. The system demonstrates edge-deployable conversational command control.

entry.title: Training-Adaptive Convolutional Sparse Coding via Information Bottleneck for Robust Visual Representation

author.name: Meng'en Qin, Yinchen Liu, Mingxuan Cui, Youlu Xing

entry.summary: The paper unfolds convolutional sparse coding optimization with FISTA and makes the sparsity coefficient a differentiable, jointly learned variable, interpreting it through the information bottleneck as controlling the retention-redundancy trade-off. The result is a training-adaptive framework for robust visual representations without manually fixed sparsity.

entry.title: The Hidden Cost of Digits: Number Normalization and WER in ASR Systems

author.name: Stanis{\l}aw Kacprzak, Mieszko Fra\'s

entry.summary: This paper analyzes how inconsistent formatting of numbers (Arabic numerals vs. verbatim words) distorts word error rate comparisons in modern ASR evaluation, using Polish as a case study of a highly inflective language. Experiments on VoxPopuli and Polish Parliamentary speech show that standard normalization practices are inadequate outside English. The work proposes improved handling of numerical expressions for fair model comparison.

entry.title: Field Tracking of Insects Using a Stereoscopic Event-Based Camera Setup

author.name: Pratham G. Shenwai, Martin J. Lankheet, John T. Hrynuk, Mandiyam Y. Mahadeeswara, Mandyam V. Srinivasan, Sridhar Ravi

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates stereoscopic event-camera tracking of small fast-moving insects in natural field environments, converting asynchronous event streams into conventional video to exploit enhanced temporal resolution without motion blur. The work supports behavioral and ecological study of flying organisms.

entry.title: Refine Then Fusion: Training-Free 3D Point Cloud Adaptation with Priority Refinement and Multi-Modal Knowledge Fusion

author.name: Hang Cheng, Yan Chen, Mingyu Fan, Long Zeng
